**Centralised vs decentralised**: one central authority (top-down) vs lower governments or private units within broad policy.

8.s: Perspective planning refers to:
o: A plan revised every month according to market prices
A plan applicable only to public-sector enterprises
Planning limited to the current financial year
Long-term planning over 15–20 years or more, from which shorter plans are carved out
8.x: Perspective planning covers a long period of 15–20 years or more. Five-year and annual plans can be carved out of this broader framework.
8.tq: Identify the time horizon and the relationship between long-term and shorter plans.
xs: Perspective planning is **long-term planning over 15-20 years or more**, from which five-year and annual plans are carved out — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is the opposite of a one-year or month-to-month plan.
xa: A **perspective plan (1985-2000)** accompanied the **Seventh Plan**.
Today: **Viksit Bharat @2047**; AP GSDP **Rs 308.11 lakh cr by 2047-48**.
**DMF five-year perspective plans** are built from baseline surveys.

8.s: A long-term perspective plan covering 1985–2000 accompanied which Five-Year Plan?
8.x: A long-term perspective plan for 1985–2000 accompanied the Seventh Plan.
8.tq: Match the distinctive date range with the relevant plan period.
xs: The **1985-2000** perspective plan accompanied **the Seventh Plan** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The Seventh Plan (**1985-90**) stressed growth, modernisation, self-reliance and social justice.
xa: Perspective planning = long-term, **15-20 years** or more.
Lack of perspective was a standard criticism of Indian planning.

8.s: Which of the following has been identified as a standard criticism of Indian planning?
o: Excessive dependence on annual plans alone
8.x: Lack of a sufficiently developed perspective has been cited as a standard criticism of Indian planning.
8.tq: Select the recognised criticism rather than an absolute description of the planning system.
xs: **Lack of perspective** is a standard criticism of Indian planning — so option **(1)** is correct.
Plans are also criticised for growing **centralised**.
xa: Perspective planning was a **Planning Commission** function.
Plan grants created **overlap and central dominance**.
**NITI Aayog** replaced fixed Five-Year Plans with a bottom-up, think-tank approach.

8.s: Which of the following best describes the revision mechanism of a rolling plan?
o: The plan is revised every year and extended by one year
The plan remains fixed until the perspective plan ends
The plan is revised once at the end of five years
The plan is revised only when the annual budget is rejected
8.x: Under a rolling plan, the plan is revised annually and extended forward by one year. This provides flexibility in targets and implementation.
8.tq: Identify the defining operational feature rather than the associated government or period.
xs: In a **rolling plan**, the plan is **revised every year and extended by one year** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It used **flexible targets** instead of fixed five-year targets.
xa: Three plans ran together: **annual plan** (with the budget), **five-year plan** rolled forward, **perspective plan** of **10-20 years**.
Suggested by **Gunnar Myrdal**; run by the **Janata** government, **April 1978 - March 1980**.
Criticism: yearly revision **weakened commitment** to targets.

8.s: What was a major criticism of the rolling-plan arrangement?
o: Yearly revision weakened commitment to targets
8.x: Frequent yearly revision was criticised because it weakened commitment to the originally stated targets.
8.tq: Find the consequence attached to repeated revision, not the formal definition.
xs: The criticism: **yearly revision weakened commitment to targets** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The plan did not end annual budgeting — the **annual plan** ran with the budget.
xa: It ended with the **fall of the Janata government**; **1979-80** was an annual plan.
Congress **Sixth Plan** from **1 April 1980**.

8.s:
With reference to the 'rolling plan' in India, consider the following statements:
1. The concept was suggested by Gunnar Myrdal for developing countries.
2. It was introduced by the Janata Party government and operated from April 1978 to March 1980.
3. It was introduced by the Congress government after the Plan Holiday of 1966-69.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
8.x: Statement 1 is correct: Gunnar Myrdal suggested the rolling plan for developing countries. Statement 2 is correct: the Janata government, which ended the Fifth Plan a year early, ran the rolling plan from April 1978 to March 1980. Statement 3 is wrong: the period after the Plan Holiday saw the Fourth Plan, not the rolling plan; the Congress returned to a fixed Sixth Plan from 1 April 1980. So B.
8.tq: Rolling plan = Myrdal idea, Janata government, 1978-80.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Gunnar Myrdal** suggested it for developing countries.
Statement 2 correct: the **Janata Party** government ran it from **April 1978 to March 1980**, ending the Fifth Plan a year early.
Statement 3 wrong: it was not a Congress plan; Congress returned to a fixed **Sixth Plan from 1 April 1980**.
xa: ⚠ Janata Sixth Plan **1978-83** (rolling) vs Congress Sixth Plan from **1 April 1980**.
Outlay **Rs 12,177 crore**; stressed **employment**.

8.s: Which of the following correctly represents the institutional arrangement of multi-level planning?
o: Centre—NITI Aayog; State—Planning Boards; District—DPC; Block/Village—GPDP
Centre—DPC; State—NITI Aayog; District—GPDP; Block—Planning Commission
Centre—Planning Boards; State—DPC; District—GPDP; Block—NITI Aayog
Centre—GPDP; State—DPC; District—Planning Commission; Block—Planning Boards
8.x: Multi-level planning operates through NITI Aayog at the Centre, Planning Boards in the States, DPCs at the district level, and block or mandal bodies with Gram Panchayats through GPDPs.
8.tq: Start from the sure institutional pair and eliminate swapped authorities.
xs: Multi-level planning: **Centre—NITI Aayog**, **State—Planning Boards**, **District—DPC**, **Block/Village—GPDP** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The aim is **bottom-up** plans built from local needs.
xa: The **73rd/74th Amendments** restored local bodies' role.
**JP Narayan Committee (1961)** flagged growing centralisation; SFDA, DPAP, ITDP, IADP ran outside panchayats.
AP: **three Economic Regions** — Visakhapatnam (**10** districts), **Amaravati** (**9**), Tirupati (**10**).

8.s: Who flagged the growing centralisation of planning in 1961?
8.x: The JP Narayan Committee drew attention to the increasing centralisation of planning in 1961.
8.tq: Test the committee associated with a specific criticism and year.
xs: The **JP Narayan Committee (1961)** flagged the growing **centralisation** of planning — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **NDC** approved Plans; the **Planning Advisory Board** (1946, **K.C. Neogi**) recommended the Planning Commission.
xa: **SFDA, DPAP, ITDP, IADP** ran outside panchayats — a sign of that centralisation.
The **73rd/74th Amendments** restored local bodies' role.
Multi-level planning: Centre → State Planning Boards → **DPC** → Block/Mandal and **GPDP**.

8.s: Which one of the following groups consisted of programmes that operated outside the panchayats?
o: GPDP, DPC, NITI Aayog and SFDA
DPAP, NDC, IADP and Planning Boards
8.x: The Small Farmers Development Agency (SFDA), Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP), Integrated Tribal Development Programme (ITDP) and Intensive Agricultural District Programme (IADP) operated outside the panchayat framework.
8.tq: Recognise the complete list rather than a partially familiar combination.
xs: **SFDA, DPAP, ITDP and IADP** ran outside the panchayats — so option **(3)** is correct.
The other groups mix in planning bodies like **DPC**, **GPDP**, **NDC** and **NITI Aayog**, which are not such programmes.
xa: The **JP Narayan Committee (1961)** flagged growing centralisation.
The **73rd/74th Amendments** restored local bodies' role.
SFDA and the Drought Prone Area Programme belonged to the **Fourth Plan** target-group approach (**1969**).

8.s: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments are significant in the context of planning because they:
o: Made NITI Aayog a constitutional body
Restored the role of local bodies in development planning
8.x: The 73rd and 74th Amendments strengthened and restored the role of rural and urban local bodies in local development planning.
8.tq: Link a constitutional reform to its planning consequence.
xs: The **73rd/74th Amendments** **restored the role of local bodies** in planning — so option **(4)** is correct.
They did not create the Planning Commission (**15 March 1950**, executive resolution) or make **NITI Aayog** constitutional.
xa: Bottom-up bodies: **DPC** (Art. **243ZD**) and **MPC** (Art. **243ZE**).
Aim of multi-level planning: **bottom-up** plans from local needs.
**NITI Aayog State Support Mission** helps states strengthen Planning Boards.

8.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to the three Economic Regions of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Visakhapatnam—10 districts; Amaravati—9 districts; Tirupati—10 districts
Visakhapatnam—10 districts; Amaravati—10 districts; Tirupati—9 districts
Visakhapatnam—9 districts; Amaravati—10 districts; Tirupati—10 districts
Visakhapatnam—9 districts; Amaravati—9 districts; Tirupati—10 districts
8.x: The Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati Economic Regions comprise 10, 9 and 10 districts respectively.
8.tq: Split the options by comparing the numerical rows of the regional table.
xs: **Visakhapatnam—10**, **Amaravati—9**, **Tirupati—10** districts — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Amaravati is the odd one with **9**; the other two have **10** each.
xa: Visakhapatnam region: **NITI-assisted**, launched **13 Nov 2025**, target **USD 750-800 bn** by **2047**.
Amaravati region: **44,962 sq km**, ~**35.15%** of GSDP; plan by **APCRDA**.
AP also prepares **District, Mandal and Constituency Vision Plans**.

8.s: Which statement correctly reflects the relationship between NITI Aayog and financial powers?
o: NITI Aayog exercises direct control over every State budget.
NITI Aayog replaced the Finance Commission as the constitutional grant-making body.
NITI Aayog possesses exclusive powers to allocate plan grants to States.
NITI Aayog lacks financial powers and is associated with cooperative and competitive federalism.
8.x: NITI Aayog lacks financial powers and represents a shift towards cooperative and competitive federalism rather than centralised plan-grant allocation.
8.tq: Use the authority-and-function trap in an institutional question.
xs: **NITI Aayog lacks financial powers** and marks a shift to **cooperative/competitive federalism** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is a **think tank, not a fund allocator**, and was set up by **government resolution** on **1 January 2015**.
xa: It replaced the Planning Commission, dissolved in **2014**.
⚠ Planning Commission **plan grants** created **overlap and central dominance**.
**NITI Aayog State Support Mission** helps states set up **State Institutions for Transformation**.

9.s: Who authored the Gandhian Plan published in 1944?
9.x: The Gandhian Plan was authored by Shriman Narayan Agarwal in 1944.
9.tq: Match the plan with its author and distinguish it from competing economic plans.
xs: The **Gandhian Plan (1944)** was written by **Shriman Narayan Agarwal** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**J.P. Narayan** wrote the **Sarvodaya Plan (1950)**; **M.N. Roy** the **People's Plan (1945)**; the **8 Bombay industrialists** the **Bombay Plan**.
xa: Gandhian Plan: agriculture, **cottage and village industries**; a **decentralised** economy of self-contained villages.
Its principles: **Swadeshi**, **Sarvodaya**, **Trusteeship**.
Agarwal also wrote **Gandhian Constitution for Free India** (**RPSC 2018**).

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gandhian Constitution for Free India — M.N. Roy
9.x: The *Gandhian Constitution for Free India* was authored by Shriman Narayan Agarwal. M.N. Roy authored the People's Plan.
9.tq: Find the author substituted from a neighbouring plan.
xs: **Gandhian Constitution for Free India — M.N. Roy** is wrongly matched — so option **(4)** is correct.
That book is by **Shriman Narayan Agarwal**; **M.N. Roy** wrote the **People's Plan (1945)**.
The other pairs are right: **Sarvodaya Plan** — **J.P. Narayan**; **Bombay Plan** — **8 Bombay industrialists**.
xa: ⚠ **People's Plan** = **M.N. Roy** (1945); **Sarvodaya Plan** = **Jayaprakash Narayan** (1950).
**Ram Rajya**: rule of pure moral authority and justice for the poorest — not a Hindu state.

9.s: In Gandhian thought, 'Ram Rajya' primarily denotes:
o: A state controlled by religious institutions
A monarchy headed by a hereditary ruler
Rule based on pure moral authority and justice for the poorest
9.x: Ram Rajya refers to rule founded on moral authority and justice for the poorest; it does not mean the establishment of a Hindu state.
9.tq: Separate the ethical-political meaning from the misleading religious-state interpretation.
xs: **Ram Rajya** means rule of **pure moral authority** and **justice for the poorest** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ It is **not a Hindu state**, so a theocracy reading is wrong.
xa: Gandhian Plan principles: **Swadeshi**, **Sarvodaya**, **Trusteeship**.
**Gandhian Constitution for Free India**: **Shriman Narayan Agarwal**.
The **Sarvodaya Plan** (**1950**) built on **Vinoba Bhave's Sarvodaya**.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the Visvesvaraya Plan:
1. It was formulated by M. Visvesvaraya in 1934.
2. It proposed doubling national income within a decade through industrialisation.
3. It aimed to treble national income in 15 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statement 1 is correct: M. Visvesvaraya, the 'Father of Indian Planning', drew up the first blueprint in 1934. Statement 2 is correct: it aimed at industrialisation and doubling national income in a decade. Statement 3 is wrong: trebling national income in 15 years was the aim of the Bombay Plan (1944-45). So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' misses a true statement, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
9.tq: Visvesvaraya = double in 10 years; Bombay Plan = treble in 15 years.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **M. Visvesvaraya** drew up the first blueprint in **1934**.
Statement 2 correct: it sought **industrialisation** and to **double national income in a decade**.
Statement 3 wrong: **trebling national income in 15 years** was the **Bombay Plan**'s aim.
xa: ⚠ **Visvesvaraya** = double in a decade; **Bombay Plan** = treble in **15** years.
Visvesvaraya is the "**Father of Indian Planning**".

9.s: Which one of the following is NOT a central feature of the Bombay Plan?
o: A significant role for the State
9.x: The Bombay Plan favoured a significant State role, public sector development and protection of infant industries; it did not advocate a completely non-interventionist State.
9.tq: Find the option that reverses the plan's stated policy orientation.
xs: The Bombay Plan did **not** want **a completely non-interventionist State** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It sought massive **state intervention**, **public-sector** dominance and **licensing to protect infant industry**.
xa: Authors: **8 Bombay industrialists** incl. **J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla, Kasturbhai Lalbhai** (1944-45).
Aim: **treble national income in 15 years**.
Title: "**A Plan of Economic Development for India**".

9.s: The Bombay Plan was published under the title
o: An Economic Programme for Self-contained Villages
A Plan of Economic Development for India
9.x: The Bombay Plan was titled “A Plan of Economic Development for India.”
9.tq: Use the exact title as the distinguishing factual clue.
xs: The Bombay Plan's title: "**A Plan of Economic Development for India**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
"**Planning for an Expanding Economy**" (**1956**) is the **Vakil-Brahmananda** wage-goods book.
xa: Authors: **8 Bombay industrialists** incl. **J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla, Kasturbhai Lalbhai**.
Aim: **treble national income in 15 years**.
It wanted **state intervention** and licensing to protect infant industry.

9.s: Which one of the following was a feature of the People’s Plan?
o: Marxist socialism and equal weight to agriculture and industry
Public-sector licensing to protect infant industries
A decentralised economy of self-contained villages alone
9.x: The People’s Plan advocated Marxist socialism, stressed basic necessities and gave agriculture and industry equal weight.
9.tq: Match the ideological description with the correct non-official plan.
xs: The **People's Plan** stood for **Marxist socialism** and gave **agriculture and industry equal weight** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Licensing to protect infant industry** was the **Bombay Plan**; **self-contained villages** the **Gandhian Plan**.
xa: It stressed **basic necessities**.
Echoed in the 1990s slogan "**reforms with a human face**".

9.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gandhian Plan — agriculture, cottage and village industries
People’s Plan — self-contained villages and Trusteeship
Bombay Plan — Marxist socialism and basic necessities
Sarvodaya Plan — licensing to protect infant industries
9.x: The Gandhian Plan emphasised agriculture, cottage and village industries, decentralisation, Swadeshi, Sarvodaya and Trusteeship.
9.tq: Match each plan with its characteristic core proposal.
xs: **Gandhian Plan — agriculture, cottage and village industries** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Self-contained villages and Trusteeship** = Gandhian Plan; **Marxist socialism** = People's Plan; **infant-industry licensing** = Bombay Plan.
xa: Gandhian Plan: **Sriman Narayan Agarwal**, **1944**; also **Swadeshi** and **Sarvodaya**.
**Sarvodaya Plan**: Gandhian constructive work and **Vinoba Bhave's Sarvodaya**.

9.s: Which one of the following was NOT an event of 1944 in the history of pre-independence planning?
o: Creation of the Planning and Development Department under Ardeshir Dalal
9.x: The People's Plan was prepared by M.N. Roy in 1945. The Bombay Plan, Gandhian Plan and the Planning and Development Department under Ardeshir Dalal belong to 1944.
9.tq: Separate the same-year events from the immediately succeeding event.
xs: The **People's Plan** is from **1945**, not 1944 — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was drawn up by **M.N. Roy**.
xa: **1944**: Gandhian Plan (**Agarwal**); Bombay Plan of the **8 Bombay industrialists** (1944-45).
⚠ **Sarvodaya Plan** = **1950** (JP).

9.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between savings and growth in the Harrod-Domar model?
o: Growth rises only when the capital-output ratio rises.
Growth falls when the savings rate rises.
Growth rises when the savings rate rises, other factors remaining constant.
9.x: The model states that growth depends positively on the savings rate and negatively on the capital-output ratio.
9.tq: Use the direction of change in the equation to eliminate reversed relationships.
xs: In **g = s / k**, **growth rises when the savings rate rises**, other factors constant — so option **(4)** is correct.
Growth **falls** with a **higher capital-output ratio** (k), so option (1) reverses it.
xa: **k**: extra capital needed for one extra unit of output → measures **productivity of capital**.
Bottleneck: **limited aggregate savings**.
Answer in **APPSC 2022, 2024 and 2025**: Harrod-Domar.

9.s: The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) of India was based on which growth model?
9.x: The First Plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model, in which growth depends on the savings rate and the capital-output ratio (g = s/k) and the bottleneck is limited aggregate savings. The Mahalanobis model underlay the Second Plan, the Dhar model the Fifth Plan, and the wage-goods model of Vakil and Brahmananda was an alternative to Mahalanobis, never a Plan's base.
9.tq: First Plan = Harrod-Domar; Second = Mahalanobis.
xs: The **First Plan (1951-56)** was based on the **Harrod-Domar model** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Mahalanobis** = **Second Plan**; **Dhar model** = **Fifth Plan**; the **wage-goods** model was an alternative, never a Plan's base.
xa: ⚠ **1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 5** = **Harrod-Domar – Mahalanobis – Sandy-Chakravarthy – Manne-Rudra – Dhar**.
⚠ **Solow (Solow-Swan)**: no Indian plan was built on it → distractor.

9.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Mahalanobis strategy?
9.x: The strategy emphasised import substitution, self-reliance and a dominant public sector. Exports and export promotion were neglected rather than depended upon.
9.tq: Find the reversed policy orientation in an excluded component.
xs: **Dependence on export promotion** was not a Mahalanobis feature — so option **(4)** is correct.
It stressed **import substitution**, **self-reliance** and a dominant **public sector**; exports were **neglected**.
xa: It assumed a **closed economy** (no foreign trade).
It also **neglected agriculture**.
Goal: **socialistic pattern of society** (IPR **1956**).

9.s: The Mahalanobis strategy sought to raise the investment rate from:
9.x: The strategy aimed to raise investment from 7 per cent to 11 per cent of national income.
9.tq: Test both endpoints of the investment-rate target.
xs: The strategy sought to raise investment from **7% to 11% of national income** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was the model of the **Second Plan (1956-61)**.
xa: Second Plan growth: target **4.5%**, achieved **4.21%**.
⚠ Some notes: target **7.5%**, achieved **4.1%**.
Bottleneck: **scarcity of capital goods**.

9.s: The Mahalanobis strategy is often described as a strategy of:
o: Balanced growth based equally on all sectors
Unbalanced growth centred on heavy industry
9.x: The strategy is described as unbalanced growth because it gave priority to basic and heavy industries while neglecting agriculture, exports and consumer goods.
9.tq: Use the comparison between included and neglected sectors to identify the strategy's character.
xs: Mahalanobis followed an **unbalanced growth strategy** centred on **heavy industry** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Priority went to the **capital goods sector** (steel, machinery); agriculture and exports were neglected.
xa: Model type: **Feldman-Mahalanobis**; a modified Soviet model.
Legacy: steel plants at **Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela**.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mahalanobis model:
1. It assumed a closed economy.
2. It incorporated foreign trade as a central source of growth.
3. It neglected agriculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: The model assumed a closed economy and neglected agriculture. It did not incorporate foreign trade as a central element.
9.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the model’s omission of foreign trade.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: it **assumed a closed economy**.
Statement 2 wrong: **foreign trade** was excluded, not central.
Statement 3 correct: it **neglected agriculture**.
xa: Exports / export promotion were also neglected.
Consumer goods were left to the **small/cottage sector**.

9.s: The Second Five Year Plan achieved growth of approximately
o: 5.21 per cent against a target of 4.5 per cent
4.5 per cent against a target of 4.21 per cent
3.21 per cent against a target of 4.5 per cent
4.21 per cent against a target of 4.5 per cent
9.x: The Second Five Year Plan achieved 4.21 per cent growth against its target of 4.5 per cent.
9.tq: Compare the achieved figure with the target instead of reversing them.
xs: The Second Plan achieved **4.21 per cent** against a target of **4.5 per cent** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes say target **7.5%**, achieved **4.1%**.
xa: Legacy: steel plants at **Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela**.
Also **Chittaranjan** locomotives, **Perambur** coaches, Atomic Energy Commission.
**Mahalanobis** was its architect (**APPSC 2024**).

9.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the outcome of the Second Five Year Plan?
o: Durgapur, Bhilai and Rourkela — steel plants
Atomic Energy Commission — village industries programme
9.x: The Second Plan left the Durgapur, Bhilai and Rourkela steel plants. It also saw the development of Chittaranjan locomotives, Perambur coaches and the Atomic Energy Commission.
9.tq: Match the named locations with the industrial outcome they represent.
xs: **Durgapur, Bhilai and Rourkela — steel plants** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Chittaranjan** made locomotives and **Perambur** coaches; the **Atomic Energy Commission** was also a Second Plan legacy.
xa: Second Plan goal: **socialistic pattern of society** (Industrial Policy **1956**).
Growth: **4.21%** vs target **4.5%**.

9.s: The Indian Statistical Institute was made an Institution of National Importance by the
9.x: The Indian Statistical Institute was made an Institution of National Importance through the ISI Act of 1959.
9.tq: Identify the correct legislation by separating it from related institutional dates.
xs: The **ISI Act, 1959** made ISI an **Institution of National Importance** — so option **(1)** is correct.
ISI was founded on **17 Dec 1931** at **Kolkata** by Mahalanobis.
xa: **Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026**, introduced on **2 Aug 2026**, would replace the **1959** Act.
The Bill makes ISI a statutory body corporate with an **11-member Board of Governors**; **President as Visitor**.
⚠ ISI founded **1931**; ISI Act **1959**; Statistics Day since **2007**.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding P.C. Mahalanobis:
1. He chaired the National Income Committee in 1949.
2. The National Income Committee recommended the National Sample Survey.
3. The first round of the National Sample Survey was held in 1950–51.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. Mahalanobis chaired the National Income Committee, whose recommendation led to the National Sample Survey; its first round was held in 1950–51.
9.tq: Link the committee, recommendation and first-round dates in sequence.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Mahalanobis** **chaired** the **National Income Committee (1949)**, which recommended the **National Sample Survey**.
The NSS **first round** was in **1950-51**.
xa: He helped create the **NSSO** and **CSO** and the **Sankhya** journal.
He devised the **Mahalanobis distance**.

9.s: National Statistics Day is observed on 29 June because it is the birth anniversary of
9.x: National Statistics Day is observed on 29 June, the birth anniversary of P.C. Mahalanobis, since 2007.
9.tq: Link the observance date with the personality and the start year.
xs: **29 June** is the birth anniversary of **P.C. Mahalanobis** — so option **(4)** is correct.
National Statistics Day has been observed since **2007**.
xa: 2026 theme: "**Unlocking the Potential of Administrative Data**".
He founded **ISI** on **17 Dec 1931**, Kolkata.
He was the **architect of the Second Five Year Plan**.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about P.C. Mahalanobis:
1. He is regarded as the architect of the Second Five Year Plan.
2. He founded the Indian Statistical Institute at Kolkata in 1931.
3. He headed the Advisory Planning Board of 1946 that recommended the Planning Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statement 1 is correct: Mahalanobis was the architect of the Second Plan. Statement 2 is correct: he founded the Indian Statistical Institute at Kolkata on 17 December 1931. Statement 3 is wrong: the Advisory Planning Board of 1946 was headed by K.C. Neogi. So B; A misses statement 2, C and D accept the wrong statement 3.
9.tq: Mahalanobis: Second Plan architect, ISI 1931 Kolkata; Neogi headed the 1946 Board.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: he was the **architect of the Second Five Year Plan** (**APPSC 2024**).
Statement 2 correct: he founded the **ISI** at **Kolkata** on **17 Dec 1931**.
Statement 3 wrong: the notes do not tie him to the Advisory Planning Board; he **chaired** the **National Income Committee (1949)**.
xa: Honours: **Padma Vibhushan (1968)**.
**National Statistics Day**: **29 June**.

9.s: The wage-goods model was put forward by
9.x: The wage-goods model was put forward by C.N. Vakil and P.R. Brahmananda in 1956.
9.tq: Distinguish the authors of the wage-goods model from those of other growth models.
xs: The **wage-goods model** came from **C.N. Vakil and P.R. Brahmananda** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was set out in **1956** in **Planning for an Expanding Economy**, as an alternative to Mahalanobis.
xa: Core idea: the real constraint is supply of **wage goods** (food and essential consumer goods).
Priority: **agriculture and wage goods**.
**Harrod and Domar** gave the First Plan model; **Tata, Birla** signed the Bombay Plan.

9.s: The book associated with the wage-goods model is
o: A Plan of Economic Development for India
9.x: Vakil and Brahmananda put forward the wage-goods model in their 1956 work, Planning for an Expanding Economy.
9.tq: Use the exact work-title association to distinguish the model from plan documents.
xs: The wage-goods model's book is **Planning for an Expanding Economy** (**1956**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
"**A Plan of Economic Development for India**" is the **Bombay Plan**.
xa: Authors: **C.N. Vakil and P.R. Brahmananda**.
It was an alternative to the **Mahalanobis** heavy-industry model.
It stressed **employment** of the disguised unemployed.

9.s: According to the wage-goods model, the principal constraint on economic expansion is the supply of
o: wage goods such as food and essential consumer goods
9.x: The wage-goods model identifies the supply of food and essential consumer goods as the real constraint on expansion, rather than the supply of capital goods.
9.tq: Test the central contrast between wage goods and capital goods.
xs: The real constraint is supply of **wage goods such as food and essential consumer goods** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is **not capital goods** — that is the **Mahalanobis** bottleneck.
xa: ⚠ Bottleneck: Harrod-Domar = **limited savings**; Mahalanobis = **capital goods**; wage-goods = **food**.
Priority: **agriculture and wage goods**.

9.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the wage-goods model from the Mahalanobis model?
o: The wage-goods model prioritised heavy industry, whereas the Mahalanobis model prioritised wage goods.
The wage-goods model prioritised agriculture and wage goods, whereas the Mahalanobis model prioritised heavy industry.
Both models gave identical priority to agriculture and heavy industry.
Neither model considered the availability of goods relevant to growth.
9.x: The wage-goods model favoured agriculture and wage goods, while the Mahalanobis strategy gave priority to heavy industry and capital goods.
9.tq: Compare the contrasting sectoral priorities directly.
xs: The wage-goods model put **agriculture and wage goods** first; **Mahalanobis** put **heavy industry** first — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the two.
xa: Wage-goods bottleneck = **food**; Mahalanobis bottleneck = **capital goods**.
The **Janata** strategy also preferred agriculture, employment and small industries to heavy industry.

9.s:
With reference to the planning strategy of the Janata Government, consider the following statements:
1. The Fifth Five Year Plan was ended one year ahead of schedule.
2. A Rolling Plan was adopted for the period 1978–80.
3. The concept of the Rolling Plan was advocated by Gunnar Myrdal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. The Janata Government ended the Fifth Plan in 1978, adopted a Rolling Plan for 1978–80, and followed a concept advocated by Gunnar Myrdal.
9.tq: Check the year, duration and associated thinker together before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: the Janata government **ended the Fifth Plan a year early (1978)**.
Statement 2: it adopted a **Rolling Plan (1978-80)**.
Statement 3: **Gunnar Myrdal** advocated the Rolling Plan concept.
xa: Janata emphasis: **agriculture and rural development**, **employment**, **small and cottage industries**, minimum needs.
The Janata Party came to power in **1977**, during the Fifth Plan.

9.s: Which one of the following was NOT an emphasis of the alternative strategy adopted by the Janata Government?
9.x: The Janata strategy emphasised agriculture, rural development, employment, small and cottage industries, and minimum needs rather than heavy industry.
9.tq: Find the alternative priority that conflicts with the stated emphasis on rural and employment-oriented development.
xs: **Rapid expansion of heavy industry** was not a Janata emphasis — so option **(2)** is correct.
It stressed **agriculture and rural development**, **employment**, **small and cottage industries** and minimum needs.
xa: The Janata Party came to power in **1977**.
It adopted the **Rolling Plan (1978-80)**.

9.s:
Match List-I (Five Year Plan) with List-II (model it was based on):
List-I
(a) First Plan
(b) Third Plan
(c) Fourth Plan
(d) Fifth Plan
List-II
(i) Dhar model
(ii) Harrod-Domar model
(iii) Allen S. Manne and Ashok Rudra model
(iv) John Sandy and S. Chakravarthy model
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
9.x: The sequence is First = Harrod-Domar, Third = Sandy-Chakravarthy (import substitution), Fourth = Manne-Rudra (Gadgil strategy, growth with stability), Fifth = Dhar model. Option A gives exactly this. B swaps the Third and Fourth Plan models; C and D misplace Harrod-Domar and Dhar.
9.tq: 1-3-4-5 = Harrod-Domar, Sandy-Chakravarthy, Manne-Rudra, Dhar (Second = Mahalanobis).

9.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Second Plan model is also called the Feldman-Mahalanobis model.
2. Its principal bottleneck was identified as the scarcity of capital goods.
3. The Harrod-Domar model identified limited aggregate savings as its bottleneck.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. The Feldman-Mahalanobis model focused on the scarcity of capital goods, while the Harrod-Domar model stressed limited aggregate savings.
9.tq: Split the options by comparing the two models’ different bottlenecks.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1-2: the Second Plan's **Feldman-Mahalanobis** model saw **scarcity of capital goods** as the bottleneck.
Statement 3: **Harrod-Domar**'s bottleneck was **limited aggregate savings**.
xa: ⚠ Bottleneck: Harrod-Domar = savings; Mahalanobis = capital goods; **wage-goods** = **food**.
Mahalanobis is also called the **Nehru-Mahalanobis-Feldman** model — a modified **Soviet** model.
APPSC **2025** key for the Second Plan model: **Mahalanobis** (not wage-goods, Gadgil, CELP or Tendulkar).

9.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Solow-Swan model is correct?
o: It is a neoclassical model based on a Cobb-Douglas production function.
It is another name for the wage-goods model.
It was the model underlying the Second Five Year Plan.
It was the model underlying the First Five Year Plan.
9.x: The Solow-Swan model is a neoclassical growth model built on a Cobb-Douglas production function. No Indian Five Year Plan in the given list was based on it.
9.tq: Identify the distractor model by its defining theoretical feature.
xs: **Solow-Swan** is a **neoclassical** model on a **Cobb-Douglas production function** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ No Indian plan was built on it: the First Plan used **Harrod-Domar**, the Second **Mahalanobis**; the wage-goods model is **Vakil-Brahmananda**'s.
xa: In Solow-Swan, growth comes from **technological progress + capital accumulation**.
**Harrod-Domar**: **g = s / k**.

9.s: Which of the following correctly represents the broad significance of the three major plan models in India’s planning experience?
o: Harrod–Domar—employment; Mahalanobis—minimum needs; wage-goods model—heavy industry
9.x: The Harrod–Domar model focused on savings, the Mahalanobis model on capital goods, and the wage-goods model on food. Together they shaped and also attracted criticism of India’s industry-first development path.
9.tq: Start from the sure conceptual pair and eliminate options that reverse the model–focus relationship.
xs: **Harrod-Domar — savings**; **Mahalanobis — capital goods**; **wage-goods model — food** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Together they defined India's **industry-first** path and its critics.
xa: Harrod-Domar: First Plan (**1951-56**); bottleneck = **limited aggregate savings**.
Mahalanobis: Second Plan (**1956-61**); **unbalanced growth**, priority to **capital goods**.
Wage-goods: **Vakil and Brahmananda** (**1956**); priority to **agriculture and wage goods**.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding planning traditions:
1. Stalin’s USSR began five-year plans in 1928.
2. The planning system initiated in Stalin’s USSR was described as imperative planning.
3. India follows indicative planning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. The Soviet Union under Stalin began five-year plans in 1928 and followed imperative planning, whereas India follows indicative planning.
9.tq: Separate the first-use date from the contrasting types of planning followed by the USSR and India.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1-2: **Stalin's USSR** began five-year plans in **1928** — **imperative** planning.
Statement 3: **India** follows **indicative** planning.
xa: The Second Plan's **Mahalanobis** model was a **modified Soviet** model.
First Indian blueprint: **M. Visvesvaraya** (**1934**), "Father of Indian Planning".
⚠ NPC **1938**: set up under **Bose**, chaired by **Nehru**.

9.s:
Arrange the following planning milestones in chronological order:

A. People's Plan
B. National Planning Committee
C. First Five Year Plan
D. Bombay Plan and Gandhian Plan
9.x: The order is the National Planning Committee (1938), the Bombay and Gandhian Plans (1944), the People's Plan (1945) and the First Plan (1951). The answer is B, D, A, C.
9.tq: Arrange the pre-Plan schemes in time order.
n: The National Planning Committee was established in 1938. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 32-33]
The Bombay Plan was formulated in 1944. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 32-33]
The Gandhian Plan was formulated in 1944. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 32-33]
The People's Plan was formulated in 1945. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 32-33]
The First Five Year Plan began in 1951. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 32-33]

9.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Capital Output Ratio is incorrect?
o: A high COR means that investment produces relatively less output.
A high COR indicates lower capital productivity.
A low COR indicates higher productivity of capital.
A low COR means that more capital is needed for each unit of output.
9.x: Option D is incorrect: a low COR means less capital is needed per unit of output, so capital is more productive. Needing more capital per unit means a high COR.
9.tq: Remember: high COR means low capital productivity.
n: A high Capital Output Ratio (COR) means that more capital is needed for each unit of output. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]
A high Capital Output Ratio (COR) indicates lower capital productivity. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]
A high Capital Output Ratio (COR) means that investment produces relatively less output. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]
A low Capital Output Ratio (COR) indicates higher productivity of capital. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]
A low Capital Output Ratio (COR) means that a given amount of capital produces greater output. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]

9.s:
Assertion (A): A high Capital Output Ratio combined with high savings may still result in slow output growth.
Reason (R): A high Capital Output Ratio means that investment produces relatively less output.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
9.x: Both are true: with a high COR, even high savings may give slow growth, because each unit of investment yields relatively little output. R explains A.
9.tq: Ask whether COR explains slow growth.
n: High COR combined with high savings may still result in slow output growth. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]

9.s:
Assertion (A): A decrease in the Capital-Output Ratio increases the growth potential.
Reason (R): A decrease in COR means that more capital is needed per unit of output.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
9.x: A is true and R is false: a lower COR raises growth potential because less capital is needed per unit of output, not more.
9.tq: Remember: low COR means high capital productivity.
n: A decrease in the Capital-Output Ratio increases growth potential. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 71-72]
An increase in the Capital-Output Ratio means that more capital is needed per unit of output. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 71-72]
A decrease in the Capital-Output Ratio increases the productivity of capital. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 71-72]

10.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ninth Plan — Growth with social justice and equity
Seventh Plan — Food, work and productivity
Fifth Plan — Removal of poverty and self-reliance
10.x: Human resource development was the principal objective of the Eighth Plan, whereas the Tenth Plan targeted 8 per cent GDP growth and doubling of per capita income in ten years.
10.tq: Find the wrong plan-objective pair by eliminating the familiar correct matches.
xs: **Tenth Plan — Human resource development** is wrongly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Human resource development** was the **Eighth Plan (1992-97)**; the **Tenth** aimed at **8% GDP growth** and doubling per capita income in **10** years.
The others are right: **Ninth** — growth with social justice and equity; **Seventh** — food, work and productivity; **Fifth** — removal of poverty and self-reliance.
xa: The Tenth Plan was the first with **monitorable targets**.
The Eighth Plan's slogan: "**reforms with a human face**"; model: **John W. Miller**.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the objective of the Tenth Five Year Plan?
o: Faster, sustainable and more inclusive growth
Growth with stability and progressive self-reliance
8 per cent GDP growth and doubling of per capita income in ten years
Removal of poverty and technological self-reliance
10.x: The Tenth Plan targeted 8 per cent GDP growth and sought to double per capita income within ten years.
10.tq: Direct recall of a numerical target linked with a plan.
xs: The **Tenth Plan (2002-07)** aimed at **8 per cent GDP growth** and **doubling per capita income in ten years** — so option **(3)** is correct.
"**Faster, sustainable and more inclusive**" = **Twelfth**; "**growth with stability**" = **Fourth**; "**poverty eradication and technological self-reliance**" = **Sixth**.
xa: The Tenth Plan was approved by the **NDC** in **Dec 2002**.
It was the first plan with **monitorable targets**; it made **agriculture the prime moving force**.
Achieved growth: **7.7%** vs target **8**.

10.s: Which Five Year Plan was described as the last Five Year Plan of India?
10.x: The Twelfth Five Year Plan, covering 2012–17, was the last Five Year Plan.
10.tq: Direct recall of a terminating institutional phase.
xs: The **Twelfth Plan (2012-17)** was the **last** Five Year Plan — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was launched on **1 April 2012** with the theme "**Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth**".
xa: The plan system ran **1951 to 2017**.
**NITI Aayog** replaced the Planning Commission on **1 Jan 2015**.
AP's **Swarna Andhra Vision 2047** (launched **13 Dec 2024**) replaces five-year plans.

10.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Annual Plans associated with the transition to the Eighth Five Year Plan?
o: They covered 1990–92, after which the Eighth Plan began in 1992.
They covered 1985–90 and preceded the Seventh Plan.
They covered 1966–69 and immediately preceded the Fourth Plan.
They covered 1978–80 and were revised every year.
10.x: Annual Plans were implemented in 1990–91 and 1991–92, and the Eighth Plan began in 1992.
10.tq: Separate Annual Plans from the similarly named Plan Holiday and Rolling Plan.
xs: The **Annual Plans** covered **1990-92**, and the **Eighth Plan** began in **1992** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Eighth Plan was postponed by **1990-91** political instability and the **balance-of-payments crisis**.
**1966-69** was the Plan Holiday before the Fourth Plan; **1978-80** was the Rolling Plan.
xa: The **1990-92** Annual Plans stressed **employment and social transformation**.
Eighth Plan: **human resource development**; **indicative planning**.

10.s: The Third Five Year Plan was adversely affected primarily by which combination of events?
o: The 1966 devaluation and the abolition of the Planning Commission
The 1990–91 balance-of-payments crisis and political instability
The 1971 war and the oil shock of 1973
The 1962 and 1965 wars and the 1965–66 drought
10.x: The Third Plan was derailed by the wars of 1962 and 1965 and the severe drought of 1965–66. This led to the Plan Holiday during 1966–69.
10.tq: Use the cause-effect link and distinguish the events responsible for the Plan Holiday.
xs: The Third Plan was hit by the **1962 and 1965 wars** and the **1965-66 drought** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This led to the **Plan Holiday (1966-69)** of three Annual Plans.
The **1990-91 BoP crisis** and political instability postponed the **Eighth** Plan instead.
xa: Third Plan growth: target **5.6**, achieved **2.2%** — the **biggest shortfall**.
Third Plan objective: a **self-reliant, self-generating economy** ("make the economy independent").

10.s: The postponement of the Eighth Five Year Plan was mainly associated with
o: political instability and the balance-of-payments crisis of 1990–91
the termination of the Fifth Plan by the Janata government
10.x: Political instability and the 1990–91 balance-of-payments crisis postponed the Eighth Plan. Annual Plans were implemented during 1990–92.
10.tq: Match the plan with its specific interruption rather than with a nearby plan crisis.
xs: The Eighth Plan was postponed by **political instability** and the **balance-of-payments crisis of 1990-91** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Annual Plans ran in 1990-92**; the Eighth Plan began in **1992**.
Ending the **Fifth Plan** early was the Janata government's act; the **1965-66 drought** hit the Third Plan.
xa: Eighth Plan: target **5.6**, achieved **6.8%**.
Eighth Plan public outlay was financed mainly by **deficit financing**.

10.s: The Eighth Five Year Plan was based on which of the following models?
10.x: The Eighth Five Year Plan, covering 1992–97, was associated with the John W. Miller model.
10.tq: Use the later plan-year clue to separate it from the earlier models.
xs: The **Eighth Plan (1992-97)** was based on the **John W. Miller model** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Harrod-Domar** = First; **Mahalanobis** = Second; **Dhar** = Fifth.
xa: Third: **Sandy-Chakravarty**; Fourth: **Manne-Rudra**.
Eighth Plan: **human resource development**; "**reforms with a human face**"; **indicative planning**.

10.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Plan Holiday:
1. Only Annual Plans were implemented during this period.
2. The Green Revolution began during 1966–67.
3. The Third Plan recorded growth of 5.6 per cent against a target of 2.2 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the figures: Third Plan growth was 2.2 per cent against a target of 5.6 per cent.
10.tq: Split the actual-growth and target figures before selecting the coded option.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **Plan Holiday (1966-69)** had **three Annual Plans**.
Statement 2 correct: the **Green Revolution** began in **1966-67**.
Statement 3 wrong: the figures are reversed — Third Plan growth was **2.2%** against a target of **5.6%**.
xa: Annual Plans **1966-69** gave agriculture and industry **equal weight**.
Plan Holiday growth: **3.69%**.

10.s:
Match List-I (Plan) with List-II (Main objective):
List-I
a. Third Plan
b. Fourth Plan
c. Sixth Plan
d. Eighth Plan
List-II
i. Human resource development
ii. Growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance
iii. Self-reliant and self-generating economy
iv. Poverty eradication and technological self-reliance
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
10.x: The Third Plan (1961-66) aimed at a self-reliant and self-generating economy ('make the economy independent'); the Fourth (1969-74) at growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance; the Sixth (1980-85) at poverty eradication and technological self-reliance; and the Eighth (1992-97) at human resource development. B swaps the Third and Fourth, C swaps the Fourth and Sixth, D swaps the Third and Sixth.
10.tq: Prime objective of the Nth Plan is asked almost every year - learn the taglines.
xs: Correct match: **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Third (1961-66)**: self-reliant, self-generating economy; **Fourth (1969-74)**: growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance.
**Sixth (1980-85)**: poverty eradication and technological self-reliance; **Eighth (1992-97)**: human resource development.
xa: **APPSC 2024** asked the Third, Sixth and Ninth Plan objectives.
"Prime objective of the Nth plan" is asked almost every year.

10.s: After the Plan Holiday of 1966-69, the Fourth Five Year Plan was finally launched in:
10.x: The Third Plan was followed by three Annual Plans (1966-69); the Fourth Plan was finally launched in 1969 and ran for 1969-74. 1966 and 1967 fall within the Plan Holiday, and 1970 is a year too late.
10.tq: Plan Holiday 1966-69, so Fourth Plan = 1969-74.
xs: The **Fourth Plan** was finally launched in **1969** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It followed the **Plan Holiday (1966-69)**; this was asked in **APPSC 2023**.
xa: Fourth Plan model: **Manne-Rudra**; objective: **growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance**.
**14 banks** nationalised in **1969**; "**Garibi Hatao**" came in the **1971** elections.
Growth: target **5.7**, achieved **3.2%**.

10.s: The Community Development Programme was introduced during which Five Year Plan?
10.x: The Community Development Programme was introduced in 1952 during the First Five Year Plan.
10.tq: Directly link the programme with its introducing plan.
xs: The **Community Development Programme (1952)** came in the **First Plan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The First Plan focused on **agriculture**, irrigation and power.
xa: **Drought Prone Area Programme**: **1973-74**, Fourth Plan.
**Minimum Needs Programme**: **1974**, Fifth Plan.
**SBI** was formed from the Imperial Bank in the First Plan.

10.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Drought Prone Area Programme was introduced during the Fourth Plan.
2. The Minimum Needs Programme was introduced during the Fifth Plan.
3. The Twenty-Point Programme was introduced during the Sixth Plan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Twenty-Point Programme was introduced during the Fifth Plan, making statement 3 false.
10.tq: Find the statement containing the plan swap.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **Drought Prone Area Programme** (**1973-74**) came in the **Fourth Plan**.
Statement 2 correct: the **Minimum Needs Programme** (**1974**) came in the **Fifth Plan**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Twenty-Point Programme** (**1975**) was a **Fifth Plan** measure.
xa: Fifth Plan also brought **Command Area Development** (**1974-75**) and the **first population policy** (**1976**).
**IRDP** and **NREP** belong to the **Sixth Plan**.

10.s: The Women's Component Plan and the seven Basic Minimum Services were associated with the:
10.x: The Women's Component Plan and seven Basic Minimum Services were associated with the Ninth Plan.
10.tq: Discriminate between closely succeeding plan periods.
xs: The **Women's Component Plan** and **7 Basic Minimum Services** belong to the **Ninth Plan** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Ninth Plan (**1997-2002**) aimed at **growth with social justice and equity**.
xa: The **Sixth Plan** was the first to focus on **gender issues**.
**Monitorable targets** came with the **Tenth Plan**.

10.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
10.x: Command Area Development was introduced in 1974–75 during the Fifth Plan. IRDP and NABARD belong to the Sixth Plan, while the Women's Component Plan belongs to the Ninth Plan.
10.tq: Use the year–plan relationship to identify the correct pair.
xs: **Command Area Development — Fifth Plan** is correctly matched — so option **(2)** is correct.
CADA/CADP came in **1974-75**.
**IRDP** and **NABARD** (**1982**) belong to the **Sixth Plan**; the **Women's Component Plan** to the **Ninth**.
xa: IRDP merged **TRYSEM**, **NREP** and other schemes.
**Jawahar Rozgar Yojana** (**1989**): Seventh Plan.

10.s: Which Five Year Plan was the first to focus on gender issues and inter-State as well as intra-State inequalities?
10.x: The Sixth Plan was the first plan to focus on gender issues and inter-State and intra-State inequalities.
10.tq: Directly test the distinctive feature of a plan.
xs: The **Sixth Plan** was the first to focus on **gender issues** and **inter/intra-State inequalities** — so option **(3)** is correct.
In the Sixth Plan, **power** also became significant.
xa: Sixth Plan objective: **poverty eradication and technological self-reliance**.
Programmes: **IRDP**, **NREP** (**1980**); **NABARD** set up **1982**.
Growth: target **5.2**, achieved **5.4%** (UPSC notes **5.7**).

10.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. First Plan — Agriculture and irrigation
b. Second Plan — Heavy industry
c. Sixth Plan — Power
 d. Seventh Plan — Employment
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
10.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Agriculture and irrigation dominated the First Plan, heavy industry the Second, power became significant in the Sixth, and employment was the thrust of the Seventh Plan.
10.tq: Match each plan with its distinctive focus sector.
xs: All four pairs are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**First**: agriculture and irrigation; **Second**: heavy industry.
**Sixth**: **power** became significant; **Seventh**: **employment** thrust.
xa: **Eighth**: human development, from heavy industry to **infrastructure**.
**Tenth**: agriculture the prime moving force; **Eleventh**: **social sector** first.

10.s: Human development was the core of which Five Year Plan, which also shifted emphasis from heavy industry towards infrastructure?
10.x: The Eighth Plan placed human development at the core and shifted emphasis from heavy industry to infrastructure.
10.tq: Use the combined focus and structural shift as identifying clues.
xs: The **Eighth Plan** made **human development** its core and moved from heavy industry to **infrastructure** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its public outlay was financed mainly by **deficit financing**.
xa: Eighth Plan model: **John W. Miller**; began in **1992**.
Per capita national output grew **3.9%** a year.
Agriculture **3.6%** (target **3.5%**); industry **8.5%** (target **8.1%**).

10.s: Which sector was placed first in the Eleventh Plan, with education receiving the highest emphasis?
10.x: The Eleventh Plan placed the social sector first, with education at the top of its priorities.
10.tq: Distinguish the plan’s social-sector priority from industrial priorities.
xs: The **Eleventh Plan** put the **social sector** first, with **education** on top — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its theme: "**Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth**".
xa: AP in the Eleventh Plan also gave the **social sector** first priority, education highest.
Eleventh Plan: **27** national monitorable targets, **13** at state level.
It recorded the **highest GDP growth** (**8.0**) — **APPSC-G1 2023**.

10.s:
Consider the following pairs (programme / feature : Plan):
1. Jawahar Rozgar Yojana : Seventh Plan
2. Setting up of NABARD : Sixth Plan
3. First Plan with monitorable targets : Eleventh Plan
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
10.x: Pair 1 is correct: Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989) came in the Seventh Plan. Pair 2 is correct: NABARD was set up in 1982, during the Sixth Plan. Pair 3 is wrong: the Tenth Plan (2002-07) was the first with monitorable targets; the Eleventh only extended them. So B; A misses pair 2, C and D accept the wrong pair 3.
10.tq: JRY 1989 = Seventh; NABARD 1982 = Sixth; monitorable targets first in Tenth.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Pair 1 correct: **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana** (**1989**) came in the **Seventh Plan**.
Pair 2 correct: **NABARD** was set up in **1982**, in the **Sixth Plan**.
Pair 3 wrong: the **Tenth Plan** was the first with **monitorable targets**.
xa: Eleventh Plan: **27** national monitorable targets; Twelfth: **25**.
**IRDP**: Sixth Plan.

10.s: Which of the following was NOT a reason for pruning the Second Plan’s outlay?
o: A sustained fall in inflation caused by excess food production
10.x: The outlay was pruned because of food and capital shortages, inflation, unrealistic closed-economy assumptions and the 1957–58 foreign-exchange crisis. A sustained fall in inflation was not a reason.
10.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated economic conditions.
xs: **A sustained fall in inflation** was not a reason — so option **(2)** is correct.
The outlay was pruned due to the **closed-economy** assumption, **food and capital shortages**, **inflation** and the **1957-58 foreign-exchange crisis**.
xa: Planned public outlay: **Rs 4,800 crore** (private **Rs 3,100 crore**).
Actual outlay: **Rs 4,600 crore** = **Rs 3,650 crore** investment + **Rs 950 crore** current spending.

10.s: Which one of the following was a major criticism of the Nehru–Mahalanobis strategy?
o: It neglected agriculture and contributed to food shortages and inflation.
It relied excessively on labour-intensive small industries and created too many jobs.
It gave no importance to heavy industry.
10.x: The strategy was criticised for neglecting agriculture, generating food shortages and inflation, and relying on capital-intensive heavy industry that created few jobs.
10.tq: Identify the criticism that combines the sectoral and macroeconomic effects.
xs: The strategy **neglected agriculture**, causing **food shortages** and **inflation** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It relied on **capital-intensive heavy industry**, which created **little employment** — the opposite of options (3) and (4).
xa: It assumed a **closed economy**.
High inflation by the late **1950s**.
It **missed its socialistic-pattern goal**.

10.s: Which of the following was NOT a component of the Eleventh Plan’s inclusive-growth strategy?
o: Complete withdrawal of the private sector
Access to health, education and skills
10.x: The Eleventh Plan envisaged continued reform and a competitive private sector; it did not propose its complete withdrawal. The other three were components of inclusive growth.
10.tq: Reject the extreme statement that reverses the stated strategy.
xs: **Complete withdrawal of the private sector** was not part of it — so option **(1)** is correct.
The strategy wanted **continued reform + a competitive private sector**.
Other parts: more emphasis on **agriculture**; access to **health, education and skills**; **infrastructure**; **disadvantaged groups**; **good governance**.
xa: Investment need: **37%** of GDP → **39%** by plan end.
Theme: "**Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth**".

10.s: How many national monitorable targets and State-level targets were set under the Eleventh Plan?
10.x: The Eleventh Plan set 27 national monitorable targets, including 13 targets at the State level.
10.tq: Separate the national count from the State-level subset.
xs: The Eleventh Plan set **27 national** monitorable targets and **13** at **State** level — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **27** (XI) vs **25** (XII) national targets.
xa: Monitorable targets included **TFR 2.1**, IMR **28**.
The **Tenth Plan** was the first with monitorable targets.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly states the Eleventh Plan’s monitorable targets?
o: GDP growth 9%, agricultural growth 4%, IMR 28 and TFR 2.1
GDP growth 9%, agricultural growth 6%, IMR 30 and TFR 2.1
GDP growth 10%, agricultural growth 4%, IMR 20 and TFR 1.9
GDP growth 8%, agricultural growth 5%, IMR 25 and TFR 2.5
10.x: The Eleventh Plan targeted 9 per cent GDP growth, 4 per cent agricultural growth, an IMR of 28 and a TFR of 2.1. Its MMR target was 1 per 1,000 live births.
10.tq: Split the option into several figures and verify each one.
xs: Eleventh Plan targets: **GDP growth 9%**, **agricultural growth 4%**, **IMR 28**, **TFR 2.1** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**IMR 25** is the **Twelfth** Plan target; agriculture was **4%**, not 5 or 6.
xa: GDP target was to rise to **10%** by plan end.
MMR target: **1 per 1,000 live births**.
The **9%** target was hit by an **infrastructure fund shortfall**.

10.s:
Which of the following measures was associated with the Twelfth Plan?
1. Reduction in the number of Centrally Sponsored Schemes
2. Provision of a flexi-fund
3. Promotion of public-private partnerships in the social sector
4. Review of the plan/non-plan distinction by the Rangarajan Committee
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
10.x: All four measures were associated with the Twelfth Plan. The Plan also increased allocations for health, education and skills and for infrastructure.
10.tq: Check whether each administrative reform belongs to the same plan package.
xs: All four measures belong to the Twelfth Plan — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Fewer Centrally Sponsored Schemes** with a "**flexi-fund**"; **PPP** in the social sector.
The **plan/non-plan** distinction was reviewed by the **Rangarajan Committee**.
xa: Health, education and skills up by **1.2 percentage points of GDP**; infrastructure **+0.7** points.
Twelfth Plan: **25** monitorable targets.

10.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.

List-I (Plan)
a. First Plan
b. Second Plan
c. Third Plan
d. Plan Holiday

List-II (Actual growth rate)
i. 2.2%
ii. 3.6%
iii. 3.69%
iv. 4.21%
10.x: The First Plan achieved 3.6%, the Second Plan 4.21%, the Third Plan 2.2%, and the Plan Holiday 3.69%.
10.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes that misplace the remaining Plan figures.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Third**: **2.2%** (lowest); **Plan Holiday**: **3.69%**.
xa: Targets: First **2.1**, Second **4.5**, Third **5.6**.
⚠ Older UPSC notes give the Second Plan target as **7.5**.

10.s: Which Five Year Plan recorded the highest GDP growth among the plans listed?
10.x: The Eleventh Five Year Plan recorded the highest GDP growth, with actual growth of about 8 per cent.
10.tq: Compare actual growth figures across successive plans.
xs: The **Eleventh Plan** recorded the **highest GDP growth** (**8.0**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
It also had the highest **per-capita** growth (**APPSC-G1 2023**).
xa: ⚠ UPSC notes give **7.9**.
Peak average growth **8.5%** in **2003-08**.

10.s: Which one of the following plans recorded the lowest actual GDP growth?
10.x: The Third Plan recorded actual growth of about 2.2 per cent, the lowest among the listed plans.
10.tq: Identify the extreme value from the plan-wise achievement figures.
xs: The **Third Plan** recorded the lowest growth, **2.2%** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was the **biggest shortfall** (target **5.6**), due to wars and drought.
xa: Fourth Plan: **3.2**; Second: **4.21**; Ninth: **5.4**.
Lowest single year since **1961**: **1979** (**-5.2%**).

10.s: Which group contains only those Five Year Plans that exceeded their GDP growth targets?
o: First, Second, Fifth, Seventh and Eighth
Second, Fifth, Sixth, Eighth and Ninth
First, Third, Sixth, Seventh and Tenth
First, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh and Eighth
10.x: The First, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh and Eighth Plans achieved growth above their respective targets.
10.tq: Identify the complete set by comparing each target with its achievement.
xs: Plans that beat targets: **First, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh and Eighth** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Second** (**4.21** vs **4.5**), **Third** and **Ninth** fell short.
xa: Biggest shortfall: **Third**.

10.s: India's GDP growth rate in 1950-51 was approximately:
10.x: GDP grew about 3.6% in 1950-51. 1.1% was the growth of 1990-91, 2.1% was the First Plan's target, and -5.2% (not +5.2%) was the contraction of 1979.
xs: GDP grew about **3.6 per cent** in **1950-51** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1.1%** was **1990-91**; **2.1%** was the **First Plan target**; **1979** saw **-5.2%**, a contraction, not +5.2.
xa: This was the **APPSC-GS 2021** key.
The **First Plan** also achieved **3.6%** against a **2.1** target.
Peak average growth: **8.5%** in **2003-08**.

10.s: Leaving aside the Covid-19 contraction of 2020-21, in which year did India record its lowest GDP growth since 1961?
10.x: 1979 recorded the lowest growth since 1961, about -5.2%, owing to drought and the second oil shock. 1965-66 and 1972-73 were other negative years but less severe, and 1991-92 grew below 1% but did not contract as sharply. Only the pandemic year 2020-21 (-5.8%) was worse.
10.tq: Lowest since 1961 (pre-Covid) = 1979, -5.2% (APPSC-GS 2018).
xs: The lowest growth since **1961** came in **1979** (**-5.2%**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1965-66** and **1972-73** were other negative years; **1991-92** grew **below 1%**.
xa: This was the **APPSC-GS 2018** key.

10.s: Among the following periods, which recorded the highest average GDP growth in India?
10.x: Of these periods, 2004-05 to 2012-13 had the highest average growth. It covers most of the 2003-08 boom, when growth peaked at an average of about 8.5%. The 1980s averaged only about 5.1-5.2%, and both the 1990s and 2000-04 were below the later high-growth phase.
10.tq: Highest-growth period = 2004-05 to 2012-13 (APPSC-G2 2017).
xs: **2004-05 to 2012-13** had the highest average growth — so option **(4)** is correct.
It covers the **2003-08** boom, when average growth peaked at **8.5%**.
xa: This was the **APPSC-G2 2017** key.
The **Eleventh Plan (2007-12)** recorded the **highest GDP growth** of any plan (**8.0**).
The **Tenth Plan (2002-07)** achieved **7.7%**.

10.s:
Consider the following statements about growth during the planning period (First to Eleventh Plans):
1. Average growth was about 4.5 per cent, against roughly 1 per cent before Independence.
2. Agriculture grew at about 2-3 per cent, against about 0.3 per cent before Independence.
3. Industry grew at only about 2-3 per cent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
10.x: Statement 1 is correct: average growth over Plans I-XI was about 4.5% versus about 1% before Independence. Statement 2 is correct: agriculture grew 2-3% against 0.3% earlier. Statement 3 is wrong: industry grew about 6-8%, not 2-3%. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out a true statement, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
10.tq: Remember the pair: agriculture 2-3%, industry 6-8%; overall ~4.5% vs ~1% pre-1947.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: Plans 1-11 averaged ~**4.5%**, against ~**1%** before Independence.
Statement 2 correct: agriculture grew **2-3%**, against **0.3%** earlier.
Statement 3 wrong: **industry** grew **6-8%**, not 2-3%.
xa: Industrial base: steel plants at **Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela**; Chittaranjan, Perambur, IITs.

10.s: Which of the following groups contains only industrial and scientific institutions associated with the expansion of India’s industrial base during planning?
o: FCI, NABARD, SBI and the Green Revolution
Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela and the IITs
NITI Aayog, Gadgil formula, SBI and FCI
10.x: Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela steel plants, along with Chittaranjan, Perambur and the IITs, formed part of the industrial and scientific base created during planning.
10.tq: Identify the group belonging to the same institutional-industrial category.
xs: **Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela and the IITs** formed the industrial and scientific base — so option **(3)** is correct.
**FCI**, **NABARD**, **SBI** and the **Green Revolution** relate to food and finance, not industry; **Jalayagnam** and **RKVY** are AP/agri schemes.
xa: Other parts of the base: **Chittaranjan**, **Perambur**, **Atomic Energy Commission**.
Food self-sufficiency: Green Revolution (**1966-67**), **FCI (1965)**, National Seeds Corporation.

10.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with India’s achievement of food self-sufficiency during the planning period?
o: Food Corporation of India established in 1965
10.x: The Atomic Energy Commission contributed to scientific and technological capacity, not directly to food self-sufficiency. The Green Revolution, FCI and National Seeds Corporation were associated with food security.
10.tq: Find the institution that belongs to the industrial-scientific group rather than the food-security group.
xs: The **Atomic Energy Commission** was part of the industrial base, not food self-sufficiency — so option **(4)** is correct.
Food self-sufficiency came from the **Green Revolution (1966-67)**, **FCI (1965)** and **National Seeds Corporation**.
xa: Institutions: **SBI** (from the Imperial Bank, First Plan), **NABARD (1982)**.
Agriculture grew **2-3%** in the plan era vs **0.3%** before.

10.s: The State Bank of India originated from which institution during the First Plan period?
10.x: The State Bank of India was created from the Imperial Bank during the First Plan period.
10.tq: Test the institutional predecessor rather than the later development role.
xs: **SBI** was formed from the **Imperial Bank** in the First Plan — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is listed among the planning era's key **institutions**.
xa: **NABARD** was set up in **1982** (Sixth Plan).
**FCI** was set up in **1965**.

10.s:
Consider the following statements about the failures of planning:
1. Poverty and inequality persisted.
2. Employment growth lagged behind targets.
3. Regional imbalance existed both across and within States.
4. Industrial growth exceeded targets in every Plan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because industrial growth remained below target in several Plans, including the Sixth Plan.
10.tq: Find the single absolute statement that overstates a generally uneven planning outcome.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statements 1-3 correct: persistent **poverty and inequality**; **employment** growth lagged targets; **regional imbalance** across and within States.
Statement 4 wrong: **industrial growth** was **below target** in several plans, e.g. the **Sixth**.
xa: ⚠ **Centralisation**: 1960s planning diluted people's participation.
Eighth Plan employment growth: **2%** vs **2.6%** target.

10.s: The expression “the poor became poorer” was used in relation to which Five Year Plan context?
o: The Eighth Plan’s poverty and safety-net outcomes
The Twelfth Plan’s regional planning strategy
10.x: The expression was used to describe persistent poverty and inequality under the Eighth Plan despite the existence of a safety net.
10.tq: Link the quoted evaluative phrase with the correct Plan context.
xs: "**The poor became poorer**" refers to the **Eighth Plan**'s poverty outcome **despite the safety net** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It sits under the failure of persistent **poverty** and inequality.
xa: Eighth Plan public sector share of outlay: **34.3%** vs target **45.2%**.
Employment growth: **2%** vs **2.6%**.
Yet the Eighth Plan beat its growth target: **6.8** vs **5.6**.

10.s: During the Eleventh Five Year Plan period in Andhra Pradesh, which sector received the first priority?
10.x: The social sector received the first priority in Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Plan. Education received the highest priority within the social sector.
10.tq: Identify the broad priority before narrowing it to the highest-priority component.
xs: In AP's **Eleventh Plan**, the **social sector** got first priority — so option **(3)** is correct.
Within it, **education** was highest.
xa: AP targets: GSDP **9.5%** (achieved **5.28%**); industry **10%** (achieved **7.26%**).
AP per capita income at plan end: **₹68,970** (above national).
Agriculture and allied share of GSDP: **21.27%**.

10.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Five Year Plan:
1. The State targeted a GSDP growth rate of 9.5 percent.
2. The State achieved a GSDP growth rate of 5.28 percent.
3. The State achieved an industrial growth rate of 10 percent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The industrial growth target was 10 percent, but the achievement was 7.26 percent, making statement 3 false.
10.tq: Separate targets from achievements and reject the statement that converts a target into an achievement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statements 1-2 correct: AP targeted **9.5%** GSDP growth and achieved **5.28%**.
Statement 3 wrong: **10%** was the **industry target**; industry achieved **7.26%**.
xa: AP per capita income at plan end: **₹68,970**.
Agriculture and allied share of GSDP: **21.27%**.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Jalayagnam in Andhra Pradesh?
o: An irrigation mission launched in 2004 to complete major and medium projects
A financial inclusion scheme launched in 2015
A rural employment programme launched in 1990
An industrial corridor launched in 2007 to promote exports
10.x: Jalayagnam was an irrigation mission launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2004 for completing major and medium irrigation projects.
10.tq: Use the programme-purpose-year combination and reject swapped programme identities.
xs: **Jalayagnam** was AP's **irrigation mission** of **2004** to complete **major and medium projects** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**2007** was **RKVY**, a central scheme — not an industrial corridor.
xa: RKVY got **₹1,862 crore**.
AP was a **General Category** State for plan assistance.

10.s: The Gadgil formula for allocation of Central assistance was introduced in
10.x: The Gadgil formula was introduced in 1969. It was later modified into the Gadgil–Mukherjee formula in 1991.
10.tq: Distinguish the original formula year from the later modified formula year.
xs: The **Gadgil formula** came in **1969** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It became the **Gadgil-Mukherjee formula** in **1991**.
xa: ⚠ Gadgil **1969**; Gadgil-Mukherjee **1991**.
Weights: population **60%**, per capita income **25%**, fiscal performance **7.5%**, special problems **7.5%**.

10.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Gadgil–Mukherjee formula:

List-I (Component)
a. Population
b. Per capita income
c. Fiscal performance
d. Special problems

List-II (Weight)
i. 7.5 percent
 ii. 25 percent
 iii. 60 percent
 iv. 7.5 percent

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
10.x: Population received 60 percent, per capita income 25 percent, and fiscal performance and special problems received 7.5 percent each.
10.tq: Start from the sure pair with the largest numerical weight and eliminate codes.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–ii, c–i, d–iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Population 60%**; **per capita income 25%**.
**Fiscal performance 7.5%**; **special problems 7.5%**.
xa: Gadgil formula **1969** → Gadgil-Mukherjee **1991**.
Special Category = **90%** grant : **10%** loan; General Category = **30%** : **70%**.

10.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the pattern of assistance to States?
o: Special Category States — 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan
General Category States — 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan
Special Category States — 30 percent grant and 70 percent loan
10.x: Special Category States received assistance in the ratio of 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan. General Category States received 30 percent grant and 70 percent loan.
10.tq: Compare the two categories through their grant-loan ratios.
xs: **Special Category States — 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**General Category** got **30%** grant : **70%** loan, so options (2)-(4) are wrong.
xa: **AP** was a **General Category** State.
Allocation followed the **Gadgil-Mukherjee formula (1991)**.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly states the current status of Five Year Plans and plan-style planning?
o: Five Year Plans ended in 2017, but plan-style credit and regional planning continue.
Five Year Plans ended in 2015 and all forms of regional planning also ended.
Five Year Plans continued beyond 2017 under NITI Aayog with unchanged fund allocation powers.
Five Year Plans were replaced by Annual Plans administered by the Planning Commission.
10.x: The Five Year Plan system ended in 2017, but plan-style credit planning and regional planning continue through other institutions and frameworks.
10.tq: Separate the end of a formal planning system from the continuation of planning-like activities.
xs: **Five Year Plans ended in 2017**, but **plan-style credit and regional planning continue** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**NITI Aayog** replaced the Planning Commission on **1 Jan 2015** and has **no fund-allocation role**.
xa: Example: **NABARD AP State Focus Paper 2026-27** credit plan **₹5.11 lakh crore**.
AP's three economic regions: **Visakhapatnam**, **Amaravati**, **Tirupati**.
**Kerala** still makes Annual Plans.

10.s: Under Swarna Andhra @2047, which of the following is NOT one of the three economic regions identified for Andhra Pradesh?
10.x: The three identified economic regions are Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati. Kurnool is not included in this three-region grouping.
10.tq: Find the outsider in a closed list of three named regions.
xs: **Kurnool** is not one of the three economic regions — so option **(4)** is correct.
The three: **Visakhapatnam**, **Amaravati** and **Tirupati**.
xa: Visakhapatnam: **NITI Aayog** help, **USD 750-800 bn** by **2047**.
**Swarna Andhra Vision 2047** launched **13 Dec 2024**, aligned with **Viksit Bharat 2047**.

10.s: Kerala was reported to have ended extreme poverty in
10.x: Kerala was reported to have ended extreme poverty in November 2025.
10.tq: Test the precise month and year of a current development milestone.
