xs: Kerala ended **extreme poverty** in **November 2025** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Kerala still makes **Annual Plans**.
xa: Its **Gender Budget** is over **one-fifth** of plan outlay.
Under planning, India's poverty fell from **48.3% (1977-78)** to **37.4% (1983-84)**.

10.s: Which of the following statements about the First Five Year Plan is incorrect?
o: Its primary priority was heavy industry.
Its major focus included food production, rehabilitation and price stability.
10.x: Option B is incorrect: the First Plan put agriculture first, along with food, rehabilitation after Partition, and price stability. Heavy industry was the Second Plan's priority.

11.s:
Consider the following statements about the Third Five Year Plan:
1. It achieved only 2.2 per cent growth against a target of 5.6 per cent.
2. It was hit by the Sino-Indian War of 1962, the Indo-Pak War of 1965 and the droughts of 1965-66.
3. It was followed by a Plan Holiday during which only Annual Plans were implemented from 1966 to 1969.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
11.x: All three are correct: the Third Plan grew only 2.2% against a 5.6% target; it was derailed by the 1962 and 1965 wars and the 1965-66 droughts; and three Annual Plans (Plan Holiday, 1966-69) followed before the Fourth Plan. A, B and C each leave out a true statement.
11.tq: Third Plan: 5.6% target, 2.2% achieved -> Plan Holiday 1966-69.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Third Plan** grew only **2.2%** against a **5.6%** target.
Statement 2 is correct: it was hit by the **Sino-Indian War (1962)**, the **Indo-Pak War (1965)** and the **1965-66 droughts**.
Statement 3 is correct: the **Plan Holiday (1966 to 1969)** had only **Annual Plans**.
xa: The **Fourth Plan** that followed adopted the **Gadgil strategy** — growth with stability and progress towards **self-reliance**.
⚠ Do not mix the figures: Third **2.2%** vs **5.6%**; Fourth **3.3%** vs **5.7%**.
The Fourth Plan was itself hit by droughts and the **1971** war.

11.s: The Fourth Five-Year Plan followed which strategy in relation to growth and self-reliance?
o: Bombay Plan strategy of abandoning public investment
Mahalanobis strategy of complete import dependence
Green Revolution strategy of zero industrial growth
Gadgil strategy of growth with stability
11.x: The Fourth Plan followed the Gadgil strategy, which emphasised growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance.
11.tq: Match the plan with its named strategy and reject unrelated policy labels.
xs: The Fourth Plan followed the **Gadgil strategy** of **growth with stability** — option **(4)**.
The strategy aimed at growth with stability plus **progress towards self-reliance**.
Background: allies had refused **equipment and raw materials** during the **Indo-Pak war**, pushing India towards self-reliance.
xa: Targets: agriculture **5%** a year, industry **8-10%**, exports about **7% a year**.
It aimed to end concessional **PL-480 food imports by 1971**.
Result: only **3.3%** growth vs a **5.7%** target; positive: **14 banks nationalised (1969)**.

11.s:
Consider the following targets of the Fourth Five Year Plan:
1. Agricultural growth of 5 per cent a year
2. Export growth of about 7 per cent a year
3. Ending concessional PL-480 food imports by 1975
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
11.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Fourth Plan targeted 5% annual agricultural growth (and 8-10% industrial growth). Statement 2 is correct: exports were to grow about 7% a year. Statement 3 is wrong: the target was to end concessional PL-480 food imports by 1971, not 1975. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' misses a true statement, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
11.tq: Fourth Plan: agri 5%, industry 8-10%, exports 7%, PL-480 ends by 1971.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the Fourth Plan targeted **agriculture growth of 5%** a year (industry **8-10%**).
Statement 2 is correct: **exports** were to grow about **7% a year**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the target was to end concessional **PL-480** food imports by **1971**, not 1975.
xa: The Fourth Plan followed the **Gadgil strategy** — growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance.
Achieved only **3.3%** against **5.7%**, hit by droughts and the **1971** war.
Positive outcome: **14 banks nationalised** in **1969**.

11.s: Which major banking-related measure was taken during the Fourth Plan period?

All private banks were abolished in 1971.
11.x: A positive development during the Fourth Plan period was the nationalisation of 14 banks in 1969.
11.tq: Use the action-and-number combination to avoid the nationalisation–privatisation trap.
xs: **Fourteen banks were nationalised in 1969** during the Fourth Plan — option **(1)**.
The notes record **14 banks nationalised (1969)** as the plan's positive achievement, despite growth of only **3.3%** vs **5.7%**.
xa: The Fourth Plan followed the **Gadgil strategy** — growth with stability and self-reliance.
It aimed to end concessional **PL-480 food imports by 1971**.
Before it came the **Plan Holiday (1966 to 1969)** with only Annual Plans.

11.s: Which statement best describes planning after 1991?
o: It ended immediately after the Seventh Plan.
It shifted from directed planning to indicative planning, signalling priority sectors while leaving investment largely to the private sector.
It was made a constitutional requirement for all state governments.
It shifted from indicative planning to complete state direction of private investment.
11.x: After 1991, planning became indicative: it signalled priority sectors while private investment played a larger role. Planning was not a constitutional requirement.
11.tq: Apply the directed-versus-indicative distinction to the role of private investment.
xs: After 1991 planning **shifted from directed planning to indicative planning**: it **signals priority sectors** and leaves **investment** to the **private sector** — option **(2)**.
Planning did not end after the Seventh Plan; the last plan was the **Twelfth Plan (2012-17)**.
⚠ Planning is **not** a **constitutional requirement**, so option (3) is wrong.
xa: After the **Seventh Plan**, public outlay was cut in phases while private investment rose.
**UPSC 1994** answer: Five Year Plans still gave a **long-term perspective** in a market economy.
The plan system ran **1951-2017**; the **Planning Commission** was dissolved in **2014**.

11.s: Why did Five-Year Plans continue to provide value in a market economy after 1991?
o: They legally compelled every private firm to follow state targets.
They provided a long-term perspective for economic development.
They replaced Finance Commission transfers to the states.
11.x: Five-Year Plans continued to provide a long-term perspective even in a market economy. Planning itself was not constitutionally mandatory.
11.tq: Choose the purpose-based explanation rather than an exaggerated legal power.
xs: Plans continued to give a **long-term perspective** for economic development in a market economy — option **(3)**.
This was the **UPSC 1994** answer on the role of Five Year Plans after liberalisation.
Plans did not abolish or compel private investment: planning became **indicative**, signalling priority sectors and leaving the private sector to invest.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** Planning is **not** a constitutional requirement.
Last plan: **Twelfth Plan (2012-17)**; NITI Aayog came on **1 Jan 2015**.
The shift began after the **Seventh Plan**: public outlay cut in phases + private investment rose.

xs: The **NDC** was **established in 1952**; its functions **passed to NITI Aayog's Governing Council**, but a **formal abolition resolution** is still pending — option **(1)**.
Because the abolition resolution is still pending, it was not formally abolished before NITI Aayog — option (3) is wrong.
NITI Aayog has **no financial powers**, so no body replaced it as a fund allocator — option (4) is wrong.
xa: **NITI Aayog** was set up on **1 Jan 2015** by **government resolution**.

11.s: The chief drawback of Indian planning identified in the context of its implementation was:
11.x: The chief drawback was implementation failure, even though planning produced several measurable achievements.
11.tq: Distinguish a structural implementation problem from an exaggerated claim of complete failure.
xs: The chief drawback of Indian planning was **implementation failure** — option **(1)** (APPSC-G2 **2017** key).
Industrialisation did not fail: planning brought **self-sufficiency in basic, capital and consumer-goods industries** and diversified industry.
Public investment was present; the notes list rises in **savings and investment** as achievements.
xa: Average growth over **Plans I-XI** was about **4.5%** vs roughly **1%** before Independence.

11.s: Which of the following was NOT an achievement associated with planning in India?
11.x: Regional disparities persisted and therefore were a failure rather than an achievement. Planning did contribute to savings, investment, food security and scientific manpower.
11.tq: Find the item that belongs to the failures column rather than the achievements column.
xs: **Elimination of regional disparities** was NOT an achievement — **regional disparities persist** — option **(1)**.
**Savings and investment** rose, **scientific manpower** grew and **foodgrain self-sufficiency** with food security was achieved — all achievements.
xa: Other achievements: infrastructure in **transport, irrigation and telecom**; **IT and space**.
Other failures: high **rural poverty**, rising **unemployment**, **income inequality** wider after reforms.
Chief drawback: **implementation failure**.

11.tq: Use the reversed-trend trap in the statement on inequality.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.

12.s: Which of the following sets correctly represents the four principal areas of the mandate of NITI Aayog?
o: Agricultural marketing; customs administration; currency printing; census operations
Knowledge and innovation; NITI for States; driving transformational change; monitoring and evaluation
Fiscal federalism; monetary policy; public debt management; industrial licensing

12.x: The mandate of NITI Aayog covers knowledge and innovation, NITI for States, driving transformational change, and monitoring and evaluation.
12.tq: Match the institution’s mandate with its actual functional areas and reject unrelated governmental functions.
xs: NITI Aayog's four mandate areas are **knowledge and innovation**, **NITI for States**, **driving transformational change** and **monitoring and evaluation** — option **(2)**.
**NITI for States** stands for **cooperative and competitive federalism**.
The other sets list subjects like **monetary policy**, **customs** or **defence** that are not part of its mandate; NITI is a policy **think tank**.
xa: **NITI** = **National Institution for Transforming India**, set up by **Union Cabinet resolution of 1 January 2015**.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog:
1. NITI stands for National Institution for Transforming India.
2. It is a non-constitutional and non-statutory body.
3. Like the Finance Commission and the CAG, it is a constitutional body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: NITI = National Institution for Transforming India. Statement 2 is correct: it is an executive (non-constitutional, non-statutory) think tank. Statement 3 is wrong: the Finance Commission and CAG are constitutional, NITI Aayog is not. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
12.tq: FC, CAG, NCBC constitutional; NITI is executive.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **NITI = National Institution for Transforming India**.
Statement 2 is correct: it is a **non-constitutional and non-statutory** (executive) body.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Finance Commission**, **CAG** and **NCBC** are constitutional, but NITI is not (APPSC-GS 2025).
xa: NITI is India's apex public policy **think tank**.
⚠ **Zonal Councils** are **statutory** bodies under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956** — unlike NITI.
Established by **Union Cabinet resolution of 1 January 2015**.

12.s:
Consider the following with reference to the objectives of NITI Aayog in the Cabinet resolution:
1. Ensuring that national security interests are considered in economic policy
2. Building partnerships with think tanks and supporting knowledge, innovation and entrepreneurship
3. Allocating plan funds and grants to the States
Which of the above is/are among its objectives?
12.x: Item 1 is an objective: national security in economic policy. Item 2 is an objective: partnerships with think tanks and knowledge, innovation and entrepreneurial support. Item 3 is not: NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation power; allocating plan funds was the Planning Commission's role. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out item 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include item 3.
12.tq: Any option giving NITI money-allocating power is the trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are objectives — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **national security in economic policy** is an objective.
Statement 2 is correct: **partnerships with think tanks** and **knowledge, innovation and entrepreneurial support** are objectives.
Statement 3 is wrong: NITI has **no fund-allocation power**; allocating plan funds was the **Planning Commission**'s role.
xa: Other objectives: **resolving inter-sectoral issues**, **monitoring and evaluation**, **capacity building**.
Also: attention to **sections at risk of not benefiting** and a **long-term policy framework**.
Critics note its influence depends on **persuasion**, not fiscal redistribution.

12.s:
Which of the following combinations correctly represents the guiding priorities associated with NITI Aayog?
1. Antyodaya
2. Focus on small enterprises
3. Inclusive and participatory development
4. Exclusive preference for large enterprises
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
12.x: Antyodaya, inclusive and participatory development, and attention to small enterprises are guiding priorities. Exclusive preference for large enterprises is contrary to this approach.
12.tq: Spot the reversed comparison in the statement that substitutes large enterprises for the stated focus on small enterprises.
xs: **Antyodaya**, **focus on small enterprises** and **inclusive and participatory development** are NITI's guiding priorities — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the notes stress **small enterprises**, not an exclusive preference for large ones.
xa: The approach is **bottom-up**, with cooperative (**"marble-cake"**) federalism.
Its mandate includes **NITI for States** — cooperative and competitive federalism.
Objective: **credible plans at the village level**, aggregated upwards.

12.s:
Assertion (A): NITI Aayog is a non-constitutional advisory body.
Reason (R): One of its objectives is to develop mechanisms to formulate credible plans at the village level and aggregate them progressively at higher levels of government.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
12.x: A is true: NITI Aayog was created by an executive Cabinet resolution and is advisory. R is true: village-level planning aggregated upwards is one of its stated objectives. But R does not explain A - its status flows from how it was created, not from its objectives (APPSC-G2 2025 key). So not the first option; the last two are wrong because both statements are true.
12.tq: Objective true, status true, no causal link.
xs: **Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)** (**APPSC-G2 2025** key).
A is true: NITI is a **non-constitutional** advisory body, set up by **Cabinet resolution**.
R is true: **credible plans at the village level** aggregated upwards is one of its objectives — but an objective does not explain its **legal status**.
xa: NITI is **non-constitutional and non-statutory**; the **Finance Commission**, **CAG** and **NCBC** are constitutional.
Its approach is **bottom-up**, unlike the Planning Commission's **top-down** plans.
⚠ **Zonal Councils** are **statutory** (States Reorganisation Act, **1956**).

12.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of NITI Aayog:
1. The Prime Minister is its Chairperson.
2. Its Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the Prime Minister.
3. The resolution fixes the number of full-time members at five.
4. Up to two part-time members may be drawn from universities and research institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: The Prime Minister is the Chairperson, appoints the Vice-Chairperson, and may nominate up to two part-time members from universities and research bodies. The resolution does not prescribe a fixed number of full-time members.
12.tq: Test the fixed-number trap by separating provisions that are flexible from those expressly specified.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 4 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Prime Minister** is **ex officio Chairperson**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Vice-Chairperson** is **appointed by the PM**, with **Cabinet rank**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the number of **full-time members** is **not fixed** (**5** at present); statement 4 is correct — **maximum 2** part-time members from universities/research bodies.
xa: Ex-officio members: **maximum 4** Union Ministers nominated by the PM.
⚠ Older notes say **3 full-time** — that was the **2015** set-up; it varies with each reconstitution.
**VC** and **CEO** are **separate posts**.

12.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Vice-Chairperson from the Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog?
o: The CEO is the ex-officio Chairperson, whereas the Vice-Chairperson is nominated by the Finance Commission.
The Vice-Chairperson and the CEO are separate posts; both are appointed by the Prime Minister, but the CEO has a fixed tenure and the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
The Vice-Chairperson is a constitutional authority, whereas the CEO is a statutory authority.
The Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the President, whereas the CEO is appointed by Parliament.
12.x: The Vice-Chairperson and CEO are distinct offices. The Prime Minister appoints both; the CEO has a fixed tenure and the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
12.tq: Separate two closely associated offices by comparing their appointing authority and service status.
xs: The **VC and CEO are separate posts**, both **appointed by the PM**; the **CEO** has a **fixed tenure** and **rank of Secretary to GoI** — option **(2)**.
The **Vice-Chairperson** holds **Cabinet rank**; the **PM** is the ex officio Chairperson, not the CEO.
NITI is **non-constitutional and non-statutory**, so neither post is constitutional or statutory.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** some notes wrongly write **"Vice-Chairman-cum-CEO"**.
First CEO: **Sindhushree Khullar**; then **Amitabh Kant** (2016-22), **B.V.R. Subrahmanyam**, **Anurag Jain**.
**Anurag Jain** (IAS **1989**, MP cadre) was appointed for an initial **two years**.

12.s: Who was the first Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog?
12.x: Sindhushree Khullar was the first CEO of NITI Aayog. Amitabh Kant and B.V.R. Subrahmanyam served later as CEOs.
12.tq: Identify the inaugural office-holder rather than the better-known subsequent incumbent.
xs: The first CEO of NITI Aayog was **Sindhushree Khullar** — option **(2)**.
**Amitabh Kant** (**2016-22**), **B.V.R. Subrahmanyam** and **Anurag Jain** came later.
xa: **Anurag Jain** (IAS **1989**, MP cadre) succeeded B.V.R. Subrahmanyam for an initial **two years**.
The CEO is appointed by the PM, with a **fixed tenure** and **rank of Secretary to GoI**.
First Vice-Chairperson: **Arvind Panagariya** (**2015**).

12.s:
Arrange the following Vice-Chairpersons of NITI Aayog in chronological order of assumption of office:
A. Suman K. Bery
B. Arvind Panagariya
C. Ashok Kumar Lahiri
D. Rajiv Kumar
12.x: The sequence is Arvind Panagariya, Rajiv Kumar, Suman K. Bery and Ashok Kumar Lahiri. Their respective periods began in 2015, 2017, May 2022 and April 2026.
12.tq: Fix the first and last office-holders, then place the intervening incumbents by year.
xs: Order: **Arvind Panagariya** → **Rajiv Kumar** → **Suman K. Bery** → **Ashok Kumar Lahiri** — option **(1) B, D, A, C**.
Panagariya (**2015**), Rajiv Kumar (**2017**), Bery (from **May 2022**), Lahiri (**25 Apr 2026**).
xa: **Panagariya** later chaired the **16th Finance Commission**.
⚠ **Suman Bery** was the answer in **APPSC 2024** for "present VC" — now outdated.
Lahiri is a former **Chief Economic Adviser** and MLA in **West Bengal**.

12.s: According to the APPSC-GS 2025 answer key, NITI Aayog at present has:
o: Three full-time and two part-time members
Five full-time and two part-time members
Eight full-time members and no part-time members
Five full-time and four part-time members
12.x: The key gives five full-time and two part-time members. 'Three full-time' is the 2015 set-up found in older sources; up to eight full-time and no part-time members described the Planning Commission; and four is the ceiling for ex-officio Union Ministers, not part-time members (maximum 2).
12.tq: NITI: 5 full-time + 2 part-time; PC had up to 8 full-time.
xs: Per the **APPSC-GS 2025** key, NITI has **five full-time and two part-time** members — option **(2)**.
⚠ Older notes give **3 full-time** — that is the **2015** set-up; the number varies with each reconstitution.
**Eight full-time** members with **no part-time** members describes the **Planning Commission**.
xa: Part-time members are capped at **maximum 2**; ex-officio Union Ministers at **maximum 4**.
Full-time members of the **Apr 2026** panel include **K.V. Raju**, **M. Srinivas**, **Abhay Karandikar**, **Gobardhan Das**, **Rajiv Gauba**.

12.s: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog has taken over the work of which body?
12.x: The Governing Council has taken over the work earlier associated with the National Development Council.
12.tq: Identify the predecessor body whose planning-related role was transferred.
xs: The Governing Council has taken over the work of the **National Development Council** — option **(2)**.
The **NDC** is now **inactive**; its role passed to NITI's **Governing Council**.
xa: Under the old system, **Planning Commission** plans went to the **NDC** for approval.
NDC members: PC members, **CMs**, UT administrators, Union Ministers.
The Governing Council was first constituted in **Feb 2015**, reconstituted **Feb 2021**.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about the meetings of the Governing Council:
1. It usually meets once a year.
2. Its frequency is prescribed by a fixed statutory schedule.
3. The 11th meeting was held on 11 June 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: The Governing Council generally meets once a year, and its 11th meeting was held on 11 June 2026. Its frequency is not fixed by statute.
12.tq: Spot the false absolute claim about statutory frequency while retaining the date-based statement.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the Governing Council **usually meets once a year**.
Statement 2 is wrong: there is **no statutory frequency**.
Statement 3 is correct: the **11th meeting** was held on **11 Jun 2026**.
xa: 11th meeting theme: **"Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047"**, with **100% attendance**.
10th meeting (**2025**): **"Viksit Rajya for Viksit Bharat@2047"**.
At the 11th meeting AP CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu** presented **Swarna Andhra @2047**.

12.s: The theme of the 11th meeting of the Governing Council held on 11 June 2026 was:
o: Innovation and Growth for Atmanirbhar Bharat
Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047
12.x: The 11th Governing Council meeting was held under the theme “Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047”.
12.tq: Discriminate between the themes of the 10th and 11th meetings.
xs: The 11th meeting's theme was **"Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047"** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **"Viksit Rajya for Viksit Bharat@2047"** was the theme of the **10th meeting (2025)**.
xa: The 11th meeting had **100% attendance** — **all 28 CMs** came for the first time.
AP presented **Swarna Andhra @2047** there.
The Governing Council usually meets **once a year**; no statutory frequency.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about the Regional Councils of NITI Aayog:
1. They deal with issues affecting more than one State.
2. They are convened by the President for specific tenures.
3. They are jointly headed by a Chief Minister (by rotation in the group) and a Central Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: Regional Councils handle issues affecting more than one State. Statement 2 is wrong: they are convened by the Prime Minister, not the President. Statement 3 is correct: they are jointly headed by a rotational group Chief Minister and a Central Minister, with ministers, secretaries, domain experts and a support cell in NITI. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' misses statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.
12.tq: Everything in NITI is convened or appointed by the PM; spot 'President' as the trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: Regional Councils address **issues affecting more than one State**.
Statement 2 is wrong: they are **convened by the PM**, not the President, for specific tenures.
Statement 3 is correct: they are **headed jointly** by a **rotational group CM** and a **Central Minister**.
xa: Composition: Central/State ministers and secretaries, **domain experts** + a **support cell in NITI**.
⚠ **Zonal Councils** are **statutory** (States Reorganisation Act, **1956**), chaired by the **Union Home Minister**.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO):
1. It is an attached office of NITI Aayog.
2. It was set up in 2015 by merging the PEO and NILERD.
3. It marks a shift from expenditure monitoring to outcome and impact evaluation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: DMEO is an attached office of NITI that monitors and evaluates schemes. Statement 2 is wrong: DMEO was formed in 2015 by merging the PEO and the IEO; NILERD (formerly IAMR) is a separate autonomous institute. Statement 3 is correct: DMEO shifted the focus from expenditure monitoring to outcome and impact evaluation. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' misses statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.
12.tq: DMEO = PEO + IEO (2015), attached office; NILERD = old IAMR, autonomous.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **DMEO** is an **attached office** of NITI.
Statement 2 is wrong: DMEO was set up in **2015** by merging **PEO and IEO**, not NILERD.
Statement 3 is correct: it marks a **shift from expenditure monitoring to outcome and impact evaluation**.
xa: ⚠ **DMEO** = PEO + IEO merged; **NILERD** = formerly **IAMR**, an autonomous institute.
DMEO tracks **ministries' performance** and evaluates schemes.

12.s: AIM 2.0 primarily seeks to:
o: Fill ecosystem gaps and scale innovations
12.x: AIM 2.0 is intended to fill gaps in the innovation ecosystem and scale up innovations.
12.tq: Identify the stated objective rather than the institutional location of the programme.
xs: AIM 2.0 seeks to **fill ecosystem gaps and scale innovations** — option **(1)**.
The **SDG India Index** is a separate NITI programme; NITI has **no fund-allocation power** for plan funds.
xa: AIM 2.0: launched **2024**, **₹2,750 crore**, runs to **March 2028**.
The original **Atal Innovation Mission** was set up in **2016**.
**State Support Mission** is a separate umbrella initiative under which States set up **SETU**.

12.s: NILERD, associated with NITI Aayog, is:
o: An attached office formed by merging PEO and IEO
A regional council chaired by the Prime Minister
An autonomous institute formerly known as IAMR
12.x: NILERD is an autonomous institute under NITI Aayog and was formerly known as the Institute of Applied Manpower Research (IAMR).
12.tq: Separate an autonomous institute from an attached office and a council.
xs: **NILERD** is an **autonomous institute** under NITI, **formerly IAMR** — option **(4)**.
Option (1) describes the **DMEO**, an attached office formed by merging **PEO and IEO**.
xa: ⚠ **DMEO** = PEO + IEO; **NILERD** = formerly IAMR.
DMEO was set up in **2015**; it shifts from expenditure monitoring to **outcome and impact evaluation**.
**Regional Councils** are convened by the **PM** — option (3) is a confusion with them.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about SETU (State Economic and Transformation Units):
1. States set up SETUs under NITI Aayog's State Support Mission.
2. The SETU Steering Committee is chaired by the Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog.
3. Assam's SETU-type body is SITA, while Maharashtra's is MITRA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: SETUs are set up by States under the State Support Mission to draft State Vision@2047. Statement 2 is wrong: the SETU Steering Committee is chaired by the CEO of NITI Aayog, not the Vice-Chairperson. Statement 3 is correct: Assam has SITA and Maharashtra has MITRA. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' misses statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.
12.tq: SETU steering = CEO, not VC; Assam SITA, Maharashtra MITRA.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: States set up **SETU** under NITI's **State Support Mission**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **SETU Steering Committee** is chaired by the **CEO, NITI**, not the Vice-Chairperson.
Statement 3 is correct: **Assam (SITA)** and **Maharashtra (MITRA)** are examples.
xa: SETUs draft **State Vision@2047**, aligned to **Viksit Bharat @2047**.
NITI also runs the **Aspirational Districts Programme** and **SDG India Index**.

12.s: The first Three-Year Action Agenda of NITI Aayog covered which period?
12.x: The first Three-Year Action Agenda covered the period from 2017–18 to 2019–20.
12.tq: Identify the exact coverage period rather than the year in which the framework was requested.
xs: The **Three Year Action Agenda** covered **2017-18 to 2019-20** — option **(2)**.
It was part of the **2016 mandate** from the **PMO** to replace Five-Year Plans.
xa: The mandate: **Fifteen-Year Vision**, **Seven-Year Strategy** and **Three-Year Action Agenda**.
**Strategy for New India @75** was released in **Dec 2018**, with targets for **2022-23**.
States now prepare **State Vision@2047** documents under the **State Support Mission**.

12.s: In 2016, which set of documents was NITI Aayog asked by the Prime Minister’s Office to prepare in place of the Five-Year Plans?
o: Twenty-Year Vision, Ten-Year Strategy and Two-Year Action Plan
Fifteen-Year Vision, Five-Year Strategy and Seven-Year Action Agenda
Fifteen-Year Vision, Seven-Year Strategy and Three-Year Action Agenda
Ten-Year Vision, Five-Year Strategy and Annual Action Plan
12.x: In 2016, NITI Aayog was asked to prepare a Fifteen-Year Vision, a Seven-Year Strategy and a Three-Year Action Agenda to replace the Five-Year Plans.
12.tq: Use the distinctive sequence of 15–7–3 to avoid confusing the planning-document time frames.
xs: In **2016** the **PMO** asked NITI to prepare a **Fifteen-Year Vision, Seven-Year Strategy and Three-Year Action Agenda** — option **(3)**.
These replaced the **Five-Year Plans**; the last was the plan system ending in **2017**.
xa: The **Three Year Action Agenda** covered **2017-18 to 2019-20**.
**Strategy for New India @75**: released **Dec 2018**, targets for **2022-23**.
Approach: **Vision-Strategy-Action Agenda** vs the Planning Commission's top-down plans.

12.s: At the 11th meeting of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog, held on 11 June 2026, which document was presented by the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
12.x: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu presented Swarna Andhra @2047 at the 11th Governing Council meeting on 11 June 2026.
12.tq: Use the event-date and document-name pair to distinguish closely related vision documents.
xs: AP CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu** presented **Swarna Andhra @2047** at the 11th Governing Council (**11 Jun 2026**) — option **(3)**.
The **Visakhapatnam Economic Region** plan is a separate document, launched **13 Nov 2025**.
xa: Goals of Swarna Andhra @2047: **zero poverty**, **jobs**, a **human-capital-driven, globally competitive economy**.
The 11th meeting theme: **"Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047"**.
**All 28 CMs** attended for the first time.

12.s: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region plan was prepared with the assistance of NITI Aayog under which initiative?
o: City and Regional Growth Hubs initiative
12.x: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region plan was prepared under NITI Aayog’s City and Regional Growth Hubs, or G-HUB, initiative.
12.tq: Test the institutional association by matching the project with its specific initiative.
xs: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region plan was prepared under NITI's **City and Regional Growth Hubs (G-HUB)** initiative — option **(4)**.
Visakhapatnam is one of **four pilot cities** under G-HUB.
xa: Launched on **13 Nov 2025**.
It projects a **USD 750-800 billion** economy by **2047** (AP SES 2025-26).
⚠ **State Support Mission** is where States set up **SETU** — a different initiative.

12.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Planning Commission from NITI Aayog with respect to financial powers?
o: NITI Aayog allocates funds, whereas the Planning Commission was only advisory.
The Planning Commission allocated plan funds and grants, whereas NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation power and is advisory.
Both bodies possessed identical powers to allocate plan funds.
Neither body had any role in economic planning.
12.x: The Planning Commission allocated plan funds and grants. NITI Aayog does not have fund-allocation power and functions as an advisory institution.
12.tq: Compare the operative financial power rather than the common planning-related purpose.
xs: The **Planning Commission allocated plan funds and grants**; **NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation power** and is **advisory** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses the roles.
xa: Critics: NITI's influence **depends on persuasion** — political coordination, not fiscal redistribution.
Planning Commission: set up **15 March 1950**; NITI: **1 January 2015** — both by **Cabinet resolution**.
Planning Commission plans went to the **NDC** for approval.

12.s: With reference to the role of States, which statement is correct?
o: NITI Aayog restricts States to annual plan talks.
Under the Planning Commission every Chief Minister was a permanent member of its Governing Council.
Under NITI Aayog every Chief Minister sits on the Governing Council, giving States a direct role.
The Planning Commission gave States a direct role through its Governing Council.
12.x: The Planning Commission limited the role of States largely to the National Development Council and annual plan discussions, whereas NITI Aayog gives every Chief Minister a direct role through its Governing Council.
12.tq: Track the institutional location of State participation and reject the swapped-body statements.
xs: Under NITI Aayog **every CM sits on the Governing Council**, giving States a **direct role** — option **(3)**.
Under the **Planning Commission**, States' role was limited to the **NDC** and **annual plan talks** — so options (1), (2) and (4) are wrong.
xa: The **Governing Council** has taken over the work of the **NDC**.
At the **11th** meeting, **all 28 CMs** attended for the first time.
Critics still point to **central dominance**; some states skip meetings.

12.s: Which of the following correctly compares the top officials of the Planning Commission and NITI Aayog?
o: Planning Commission—Vice-Chairperson and CEO; NITI Aayog—Deputy Chairman and Member-Secretary
Planning Commission—Deputy Chairman and Member-Secretary; NITI Aayog—Vice-Chairperson and CEO
12.x: The Planning Commission had a Deputy Chairman and Member-Secretary, while NITI Aayog has a Vice-Chairperson and a CEO appointed by the Prime Minister.
12.tq: Use the paired office titles to detect an authority and designation swap.
xs: **Planning Commission — Deputy Chairman and Member-Secretary**; **NITI Aayog — Vice-Chairperson and CEO** — option **(2)**.
The Deputy Chairman had **Cabinet rank**; NITI's VC and CEO are both **appointed by the PM**.
xa: Last Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission: **M.S. Ahluwalia**.
NITI's CEO has a **fixed tenure** and the **rank of Secretary to GoI**.
Current NITI VC: **Ashok Kumar Lahiri** (**25 Apr 2026**).

12.s:
Consider the following statements regarding membership of the two institutions:
1. The Planning Commission could have up to eight full-time members.
2. The Planning Commission had no part-time members.
3. NITI Aayog may have full-time members and up to two part-time members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: The Planning Commission had up to eight full-time members and no part-time members. NITI Aayog includes full-time members and may have up to two part-time members.
12.tq: Compare numerical composition details across both institutions before selecting the combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statements 1 and 2: the Planning Commission had **up to 8 full-time** members and **no part-time** members.
Statement 3: NITI has **full-time members** plus **up to 2 part-time** members.
xa: NITI's full-time members: **no fixed ceiling** (**5** at present).
NITI also has up to **4** Union Ministers as ex-officio members.
⚠ APPSC-GS 2025 key: **five full-time and two part-time** members.

12.s: The Planning Commission of India was set up on 15 March 1950 through ______, and its first chairman was ______.
o: an Act of Parliament; Jawaharlal Nehru
12.x: Like NITI Aayog later (1 January 2015), the Planning Commission was created by a Cabinet resolution on 15 March 1950, with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru as its first chairman. It was never statutory (no Act) or constitutional, and neither Patel nor Rajendra Prasad chaired it.
12.tq: Both PC (1950) and NITI (2015) = Cabinet resolutions; PM chairs both.
xs: The Planning Commission was set up on **15 March 1950** by **a Cabinet resolution**; its first chairman was **Jawaharlal Nehru** — option **(1)**.
It was not created by an **Act of Parliament** or a **constitutional provision**.
xa: NITI Aayog too came by **Cabinet resolution**, on **1 January 2015**.
The Planning Commission **allocated plan funds and grants**; NITI is only advisory.
It had up to **8 full-time** members and no part-time members.

12.s: Which one of the following best describes a major criticism of NITI Aayog?
o: It possesses extensive powers to allocate funds directly to States.
It functions as a constitutional court for economic disputes.
Its recommendations are advisory and its influence depends substantially on persuasion.
Its recommendations are legally binding on all States.
12.x: NITI Aayog’s recommendations are advisory. Since it lacks fund-allocation power, its influence depends substantially on persuasion and political coordination.
12.tq: Use the authority-versus-advisory distinction to identify the institutional limitation.
xs: A major criticism: NITI's **recommendations are advisory** and its **influence depends on persuasion** — option **(3)**.
NITI has **no financial / fund-allocation powers** and is **non-constitutional**, so options (1), (2) and (4) are wrong.
xa: It offers **political coordination, not fiscal redistribution**.
Critics also point to **central dominance**; some states skip meetings.
Significance: top-down Planning Commission → **collaborative partnership**.

12.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Zonal Councils and NITI Aayog:
1. Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
2. Zonal Councils are chaired by the Union Home Minister.
3. A representative of NITI Aayog attends as an adviser.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: All three statements are correct. Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, are chaired by the Union Home Minister, and a NITI Aayog representative attends as an adviser.
12.tq: Separate the statutory status and chairperson of Zonal Councils from the advisory role of NITI Aayog.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Zonal Councils** are **statutory** bodies under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**.
Statement 2 is correct: they are **chaired by the Union Home Minister**.
Statement 3 is correct: a **NITI representative attends as adviser**.
xa: ⚠ NITI itself is **non-constitutional and non-statutory**, set up by **Cabinet resolution** on **1 January 2015**.
NITI's **Regional Councils** are convened by the **PM** and jointly headed by a rotational group **CM** and a **Central Minister**.
NITI's **Governing Council** has taken over the work of the **NDC**.

12.s: State rankings issued by NITI Aayog are primarily associated with which form of federal competition?
12.x: NITI Aayog’s State rankings encourage competitive federalism by comparing performance across States and promoting improvement.
12.tq: Link the policy instrument—rankings—to the specific type of federalism it promotes.
xs: NITI's **state rankings** drive **competitive federalism** — option **(3)**.
Its mandate area **NITI for States** covers **cooperative and competitive federalism**.
xa: Significance: from a **top-down Planning Commission** to a **collaborative partnership**.
Its cooperative federalism is called **"marble-cake"** federalism.
NITI also runs the **SDG India Index** and the **Aspirational Districts Programme**.

12.s: The first Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog, who later chaired the 16th Finance Commission, was:
12.x: Arvind Panagariya was the first Vice-Chairperson (2015) and later chaired the 16th Finance Commission. Rajiv Kumar (2017) and Suman K. Bery (2022) were later Vice-Chairpersons, and Ashok Kumar Lahiri is the current one (April 2026).
12.tq: Panagariya: first NITI VC, then 16th FC chair.
xs: The first Vice-Chairperson was **Arvind Panagariya** (**2015**), who later chaired the **16th Finance Commission** — option **(2)**.
**Rajiv Kumar** (**2017**), **Suman K. Bery** (from **May 2022**) and **Ashok Kumar Lahiri** (**25 Apr 2026**) came later.
xa: The VC is **appointed by the PM** and holds **Cabinet rank**.
⚠ **Suman Bery** was the answer in **APPSC 2024** for "present VC" — now outdated.
First CEO: **Sindhushree Khullar**.

12.s:
Assertion (A): NITI Aayog was established to replace the Planning Commission.
Reason (R): NITI Aayog was established through a Cabinet Resolution.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
12.x: Both are true: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission, and it was set up by a Cabinet resolution. How it was created does not explain why it replaced the old body, so R does not explain A.
12.tq: Ask whether the method of creation explains the purpose.
n: NITI Aayog was established through a Cabinet Resolution. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 33-34]
NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 33-34]

12.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Planning Commission was an advisory body.
The Planning Commission was a constitutional body.
NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission.
The Finance Commission is constituted periodically.
12.x: Option B is incorrect: the Planning Commission was a non-constitutional, non-statutory advisory body created by a Cabinet resolution in 1950. NITI Aayog replaced it, and the Finance Commission is set up every five years.
12.tq: Recall which planning-era bodies have a constitutional basis.
n: The Planning Commission served as an advisory body. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 33-34]
The Planning Commission was a permanent body. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 33-34]
The Finance Commission was constituted periodically. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 33-34]
