UR measures only the **unutilised part** of the labour force.
**WPR = LFPR × (1 − UR)**.

34.s: The percentage of employed persons in the total population is known as the
34.x: Worker Population Ratio (WPR) is employed persons as a share of population, and WPR = LFPR x (1 - UR). LFPR counts employed plus unemployed per 100 persons, UR is unemployed as a share of the labour force, and Proportion Unemployed is unemployed as a share of population.
34.tq: Employed / population = WPR (APPSC 2023).
xs: Employed persons as a % of population = **Worker Population Ratio** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2023).
**LFPR** includes the unemployed too; **UR** divides by the labour force; **PU** = unemployed / population.
xa: Identity: **WPR = LFPR × (1 − UR)**.

34.s: Which organisation conducts the Employment–Unemployment Survey and the Quarterly Employment Survey of establishments?
o: Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
Directorate General of Employment and Training alone
34.x: The Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment conducts the Employment–Unemployment Survey and the Quarterly Employment Survey of establishments.
34.tq: Use the survey title to identify the responsible labour institution.
xs: The **Labour Bureau (MoLE)** runs the **Employment-Unemployment Survey** and the **Quarterly Employment Survey** of establishments — so option **(2)** is correct.
**NSO (MoSPI)** runs the **PLFS**; **CMIE** runs **CPHS**; **DGE&T** holds job-seeker **registration** data.
xa: QES covers **establishments**, not households.
CMIE gives a **higher UR** than PLFS.
Census: worker data every **10** years.

34.s: Before the establishment of NITI Aayog, unemployment data were primarily obtained from:
34.x: Before NITI Aayog, unemployment data were primarily obtained from the NSSO. Official unemployment information was also associated with the CSO and NSSO statistical system.
34.tq: Recall the principal historical source rather than a newer private source.
xs: Before **NITI Aayog**, unemployment data came from the **NSSO** — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC 2019).
The **Census** and **Labour Bureau** were not the main source; **CMIE** is a private body.
xa: PYQ: "unemployment data is collected by **CSO & NSSO**" (APPSC 2019).
NSSO ran rounds **27th to 68th**; PLFS since **2017**.
CSO + NSSO merged into **NSO** in **2019**.

34.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey is conducted by:
o: The Census of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs
The National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
The Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy under NITI Aayog
The Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
34.x: PLFS is conducted by the National Statistical Office, which functions under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
34.tq: Apply the 'who conducts the survey?' agency test.
xs: The **PLFS** is conducted by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation** (MoSPI) — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Labour Bureau (MoLE)** runs EUS/QES; **CMIE** is private; the **Census** gives decennial worker data.
xa: Designed by the **SCLFS**, set up on the **National Statistical Commission's** advice.
Launched **April 2017**; first report (**2017-18**) in **May 2019**.
Now the standard NSO mechanism for India's UR (APPSC G2 2025).

34.s: The Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics was set up on the advice of which body and was associated with the design of PLFS?
34.x: The Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics was set up on the advice of the National Statistical Commission and designed the PLFS framework.
34.tq: Match the technical committee with the institution that recommended it.
xs: The **SCLFS** was set up on the advice of the **National Statistical Commission** and designed the **PLFS** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its aim: **more frequent data** than 5-yearly NSS rounds.
xa: PLFS is run by the **NSO**, **MoSPI**.
Launched **April 2017**.
Revamp from **January 2025**: **monthly** CWS estimates.

34.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey was launched in:
34.x: PLFS was launched in April 2017. Its first annual report, relating to 2017–18, was released in May 2019.
34.tq: Distinguish the launch date from the release date of the first report.
xs: The **PLFS** was launched in **April 2017** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**May 2019** is when the first annual report (**2017-18**) came out; **January 2025** is the revamp.
xa: ⚠ Launched April 2017, but the first report only in **May 2019**.
Designed by the **SCLFS**.

34.s:
Which of the following changes was introduced with the PLFS revamp from January 2025?
1. Monthly all-India CWS estimates began to be produced.
2. Quarterly estimates were extended to rural areas.
3. The annual report shifted to the calendar year January–December.
4. The sample was reduced to about one-half of its earlier size.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The sample was raised, not reduced, to about 2,72,304 households.
34.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the direction of a sample-size change.
xs: Statements 1–3 are correct: the **January 2025** revamp added **monthly all-India CWS** estimates, extended **quarterly** estimates to **rural** areas, and moved the annual report to the **calendar year**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the sample was **raised** to about **2,72,304 households** (**2.65 times**), not halved — so option **(1)** 1, 2 and 3 only is correct.
xa: Original design: quarterly estimates for **urban** areas only.
PLFS 2025 (calendar year) UR: **3.1%**.

34.s: The unemployment rates under UPS, CWS and CDS in the NSS 68th Round for 2011–12 were respectively:
34.x: For 2011–12, the NSS 68th Round reported unemployment rates of 2.7% under UPS, 3.7% under CWS and 5.6% under CDS.
34.tq: Recall the ordered numerical series and preserve the approach sequence.
xs: NSS **68th round (2011-12)**: **UPS 2.7%**, **CWS 3.7%**, **CDS 5.6%** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The order rises with shorter reference periods: ⚠ **UPS < CWS < CDS**.
xa: The 68th was the **last quinquennial** round.
The high CDS rate shows **high intermittent** unemployment.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about PLFS unemployment rates (persons aged 15 years and above):
1. PLFS 2022-23 reported an overall unemployment rate of 3.2%, with graduate unemployment at 13%.
2. In PLFS 2023-24 (UPSS), the rural unemployment rate was higher than the urban rate.
3. PLFS 2019-20 reported an unemployment rate of 4.8% under UPSS.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Statement 1 is correct: PLFS 2022-23 gave 3.2% overall and 13% for graduates. Statement 2 is wrong: in PLFS 2023-24 the rural rate (2.5%) was lower than the urban rate (5.1%). Statement 3 is correct: PLFS 2019-20 gave 4.8% under UPSS. Hence '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' omits a true statement, and any option containing 2 is wrong.
34.tq: In PLFS, open unemployment is always higher in urban areas than in rural areas.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **PLFS 2022-23** UR **3.2%**, graduates **13%**.
Statement 2 is wrong: in **PLFS 2023-24** rural UR (**2.5%**) was below urban (**5.1%**).
Statement 3 is correct: **PLFS 2019-20** gave **4.8%** (UPSS) — so option **(2)** 1 and 3 only is correct.
xa: PLFS 2019-20 was asked in **APPSC 2022**.

34.s: As reported by CMIE, approximately how many persons were unemployed in India in December 2021?
34.x: CMIE reported approximately 53 million unemployed persons as of December 2021.
34.tq: Recall the distinctive large-scale numerical estimate associated with a private agency.
xs: **CMIE** reported about **53 million** unemployed as of **Dec 2021** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2021 answer).
CMIE is **private** and runs the monthly household survey **CPHS**.
xa: CMIE UR ~**7.95%** in **Sep 2023**, above official PLFS figures.
**CMIE vs PLFS** divergence: CMIE is monthly, has a larger sample and a different methodology.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about unemployment estimates in India:
1. PLFS 2025 (calendar year) put the unemployment rate (15+) at 3.1%, down from 3.6% in 2022.
2. CWS rates are higher than UPSS rates because the short reference period captures seasonal unemployment.
3. In the January-March 2026 quarter, the rural unemployment rate was higher than the urban rate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: Statement 1 is correct: PLFS 2025 gave 3.1% (from 3.6% in 2022). Statement 2 is correct: the 7-day CWS reference period picks up seasonal unemployment, so CWS exceeds UPSS. Statement 3 is wrong: Jan-Mar 2026 urban was 6.6% against rural 4.3% (overall 5.0%).
34.tq: Short reference period, higher rate: CDS > CWS > UPSS.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **PLFS 2025** UR **3.1%**, down from **3.6%** in 2022.
Statement 2 is correct: **CWS** exceeds **UPSS** because its short (**7-day**) period catches **seasonal** unemployment.
Statement 3 is wrong: in **Jan-Mar 2026**, urban **6.6%** exceeded rural **4.3%** (overall **5.0%**) — so option **(2)** 1 and 2 only is correct.
xa: Quarterly data released **12 May 2026**.
Monthly CWS UR: **5.5%** in May 2026.
PLFS 2025: youth UR falling to **9.9%**.

34.s:
Consider the following statements comparing Andhra Pradesh with India under PLFS 2023-24 (usual status):
1. AP's unemployment rate (4.1%) was higher than India's (3.2%).
2. AP's female LFPR (35.8%) was higher than India's (31.7%).
3. In AP, the rural unemployment rate was higher than the urban rate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: AP UR 4.1% vs India 3.2%, and AP female LFPR 35.8% vs India 31.7%. Statement 3 is wrong: AP rural UR was 3.4% against urban 5.9%.
34.tq: AP: higher UR and higher female LFPR than India; urban > rural.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: AP UR **4.1%** vs India **3.2%**.
Statement 2 is correct: AP female LFPR **35.8%** vs India **31.7%**.
Statement 3 is wrong: AP rural UR **3.4%** was below urban **5.9%** — so option **(2)** 1 and 2 only is correct.
xa: AP male UR **4.3%**, female **3.7%**.
AP informality: about **55%** overall.

34.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the measurement of unemployment in India:
1. Critics argue that the CWS measure may mask underemployment.
2. Critics argue that the CWS measure may fail to capture circular migration adequately.
3. The CWS measure is regarded as free from all measurement-related limitations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct criticisms of the CWS approach. Statement 3 is false because the approach has been criticised for masking underemployment and missing circular migration.
34.tq: Find the false absolute statement and select the combination containing the two supported criticisms.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: critics say **CWS** (**1 hour** a week = employed) **masks underemployment** and misses **circular migration**.
Statement 3 is wrong: CWS is not free from limitations — so option **(1)** 1 and 2 only is correct.
xa: India moved to monthly CWS data from **2025**.
CWS rates exceed **UPSS** because the short period catches seasonal unemployment.
**CMIE vs PLFS** divergence is another debate.

34.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes CMIE data from PLFS data in the measurement of unemployment?
o: CMIE data are monthly, use a larger sample, and differ methodologically from PLFS, contributing to divergence in their estimates.
CMIE and PLFS estimates cannot diverge because both use the same frequency, sample size and methodology.
CMIE data are monthly and based on a larger sample, whereas CMIE and PLFS use identical methodologies.
PLFS data are monthly and use a larger sample, whereas CMIE data are based on the PLFS methodology.
34.x: CMIE data are monthly and based on a larger sample, but CMIE and PLFS use different methodologies. These differences can produce divergence between their unemployment estimates.
34.tq: Split the alternatives by frequency, sample size and methodology to identify the complete comparison.
xs: **CMIE** data are **monthly**, use a **larger sample** and a **different methodology** from PLFS — hence the **divergence** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Options 2–4 wrongly claim identical methods or swap the roles.
xa: CMIE: **53 million** unemployed (**Dec 2021**); UR ~**7.95%** in **Sep 2023**.
CMIE's survey is the **CPHS**; it gives a **higher UR** than PLFS.
PLFS is run by the **NSO**, MoSPI.

34.s:
How many of the following statements are correctly matched?

1. WPR — Employed / Total population
2. LFPR — Labour force / Working-age population
3. Real Sector — Money + Financial Assets
4. Microfinance — Financial services for low-income groups
34.x: Three pairs are correct: WPR is employed over total population, LFPR is labour force over working-age population, and microfinance serves low-income groups. The real sector is goods and services, not money.
34.tq: Check each pair.
n: WPR is employed population divided by total population. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48-2 · pp 72-73]
LFPR is the labour force divided by the working-age population. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48-2 · pp 72-73]
The real sector consists of goods and services. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48-2 · pp 72-73]
The financial sector consists of money and financial assets. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48-2 · pp 72-73]
Microfinance provides financial services to low-income groups. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48-2 · pp 72-73]

35.s:
Consider the following statements about 'jobless growth':
1. It refers to a situation in which unemployment of labour increases even at the height of economic growth.
2. The term was coined by Arthur Lewis in the 1950s.
3. A low or near-zero employment elasticity is a sign of jobless growth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
35.x: Statement 1 is correct: jobless growth means unemployment rises even when growth is high. Statement 2 is wrong: the term was coined by Nick Perna in the early 1990s. Statement 3 is correct: employment elasticity (% change in employment / % change in output) near zero means output grows with little job creation. So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
35.tq: Jobless growth = Nick Perna, early 1990s; low employment elasticity.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **jobless growth** = unemployment of labour **increases even at the height of economic growth** (APPSC 2019).
Statement 2 is wrong: the term was coined by **Nick Perna** in the **early 1990s**, not Arthur Lewis in the 1950s.
Statement 3 is correct: a **low or near-zero employment elasticity** signals jobless growth — so option **(2)** 1 and 3 only is correct.
xa: **Employment elasticity** = % change in employment / % change in output (GDP).
⚠ Nick Perna is **not an Indian economist**.
Post-1991 cause: growth driven by **capital-intensive** sectors (**IT, finance**).

35.s: Employment elasticity is expressed as:
o: Percentage change in employment divided by percentage change in output
Percentage change in output divided by percentage change in employment
Total employment divided by total population
Change in labour force divided by change in unemployment
35.x: Employment elasticity equals the percentage change in employment divided by the percentage change in output or GDP.
35.tq: Recall the numerator and denominator of the formula without reversing them.
xs: **Employment elasticity** = **% change in employment ÷ % change in output (GDP)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option 2 inverts the ratio; employment ÷ population is a different ratio altogether.
xa: A **low or near-zero** value → **jobless growth**.
Jobless growth term: **Nick Perna**, early **1990s**.
Post-1991, GDP grew **6-7%** but **formal job creation lagged**.

35.s: The expression ‘missing middle’ in the context of India’s employment pattern refers to:
o: The gap between rural and urban literacy rates
The shortage of middle-level government officials
The absence of a manufacturing stage between agriculture and services
35.x: India followed a services-led path that largely skipped the manufacturing stage, described as the ‘missing middle’.
35.tq: Discriminate between an economic structural term and literal interpretations of the words.
xs: The "**missing middle**" = India's **services-led path skipping the manufacturing stage** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is not about literacy, consumers or officials.
xa: It is one of the **post-1991** reasons for **jobless growth**.
Services' employment share rose **22.82% (1993-94) → 34.90% (2009-10)**; industry stayed ~**12%**.
Urban employment: services **62.0%** (2025-26).

35.s:
Which of the following best explains the employment problem associated with India’s post-1991 growth?
1. Growth of employment did not keep pace with labour-force growth.
2. Employment generation was concentrated sufficiently in labour-intensive manufacturing.
3. Unemployment increasingly appeared in the unorganised sector.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
35.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because growth was not sufficiently concentrated in labour-intensive manufacturing.
35.tq: Find the reversed statement about the sector generating employment.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **employment growth lagged labour-force growth** after 1991.
Statement 2 is wrong: growth was driven by **capital-intensive** sectors (IT, finance), **not labour-intensive manufacturing**.
Statement 3 is correct: this **creeping unemployment** was mostly in the **unorganised sector** — so option **(3)** 1 and 3 only is correct.
xa: GDP grew **6-7%** but formal job creation lagged.
About **12 million** persons enter the job market each year.
"**Missing middle**": services-led path skipping manufacturing.

35.s: Which of the following correctly describes the rural–urban pattern of employment?
o: Rural employment is dominated by services, while urban employment is dominated by agriculture
Agriculture accounts for 62.0% of urban employment, while services account for 57% of rural employment
Agriculture accounts for 57% of rural employment, while services account for 62.0% of urban employment
Both rural and urban employment are dominated equally by manufacturing
35.x: Agriculture accounted for 57% of rural employment, whereas services accounted for 62.0% of urban employment.
35.tq: Compare the sectoral leaders in rural and urban employment without reversing them.
xs: **Agriculture** = **57%** of **rural** employment; **services** = **62.0%** of **urban** employment — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option 2 swaps the two; options 1 and 4 misstate the pattern.
xa: Rural self-employment: **62.8%**.
Agriculture = **42.4%** of total employment (**Q2 FY26**).
Total employment (Q2 FY26): **56.2 crore** (15+).

35.s: The Labour Bureau Quarterly Employment Survey covers establishments with at least 10 workers in how many sectors?
35.x: The QES covers establishments with 10 or more workers across nine sectors.
35.tq: Recall the survey’s coverage threshold and number of sectors.
xs: The Labour Bureau **QES** covers establishments with **10+ workers** in **9 sectors** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Sectors: manufacturing, construction, trade, transport, accommodation and restaurants, **IT/BPO**, education, health, financial services.
xa: QES is run by the **Labour Bureau**.
Q2 FY26: **8.7 lakh** new jobs over Q1.
Total employment Q2 FY26: **56.2 crore**.

35.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the historical change in agriculture’s workforce share?
35.x: Agriculture’s workforce share declined from 72% in 1951 to 64.75% in 1993–94.
35.tq: Track the direction and dates of a long-term structural change.
xs: Agriculture's workforce share fell from **72% in 1951** to **64.75% in 1993-94** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option 2 reverses it; **34.90%** and **22.82%** are **services** shares.
xa: Industry stayed around ~**12%**.
Agriculture now: **42.4%** (Q2 FY26).

35.s: According to the India Employment Report 2024, what percentage of total employment in India was accounted for by self-employment in 2022?
35.x: Self-employment accounted for 55.8% of total employment in India in 2022, as reported in the India Employment Report 2024 prepared by ILO-IHD.
35.tq: Use the exact employment-share figure and distinguish it from rural and urban employment indicators.
xs: Per the **India Employment Report 2024**, **self-employment** was **55.8%** of total employment in **2022** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**42.4%** = agriculture's share; **49.8%** = urban regular wage jobs; **62.8%** = rural self-employment.
xa: The report is by **ILO + Institute for Human Development**.
ES 2025-26 also gives **55.8%** for **Q2 FY26**.
Casual labour: **18.9%** (Q2 FY26).

35.s: The India Employment Report 2024 was released jointly by:
o: The IMF and the Labour Bureau
The World Bank and NITI Aayog
The ILO and the Institute for Human Development
The UNDP and the National Statistical Office
35.x: The India Employment Report 2024 was released by the International Labour Organization and the Institute for Human Development.
35.tq: Identify the correct institutional partnership rather than a neighbouring international body.
xs: The **India Employment Report 2024** was released by the **ILO** and the **Institute for Human Development** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ It is **ILO + IHD**, not NITI Aayog or the World Bank.
xa: It notes **informal and vulnerable jobs** even among **educated youth**.
Self-employment: **55.8%** (for 2022).
Gen Z: only **14.2%** have a formal job contract.

35.s: The Female LFPR for 2023–24 was:
35.x: The Female LFPR for 2023–24 was 41.7%.
35.tq: Identify the year-specific figure from adjacent PLFS values.
xs: **Female LFPR (15+)** in **2023-24** was **41.7%** — so option **(3)** is correct.
xa: AP female LFPR (15+): **44.8%** vs India **41.7%**.

35.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Female LFPR figures cited for 2025?
35.x: For 2025, the overall Female LFPR was approximately 40%, with 45.9% in rural areas and 27.7% in urban areas.
35.tq: Match the aggregate figure with the correct rural–urban breakdown.
xs: **Female LFPR 2025**: overall ~**40%**, **rural 45.9%**, **urban 27.7%** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Options 1, 2 and 4 swap these figures.
xa: Quarterly CWS female LFPR: **34.7%** (Jan-Mar 2026).

35.s: The widening rural–urban gap in Female LFPR is primarily indicated by which of the following?
o: A much larger increase in rural LFPR than in urban LFPR
A decline in rural LFPR and a rise in urban LFPR
Identical rural and urban LFPR levels by 2025
A larger increase in urban LFPR than in rural LFPR
35.x: Rural LFPR rose substantially more than urban LFPR, widening the rural–urban gap.
35.tq: Infer the trend from the comparative changes rather than from a single level.
xs: The widening gap comes from a **much larger rise in rural LFPR** (**33.0% → 45.9%**) than **urban** (**23.3% → 27.7%**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
Both rose, so options 2 and 4 are wrong; levels are far from identical.
xa: Period: **2019-20 to 2025** (July 2026 PLFS).
Rural women = **80%** of the rise in female workers (**2017-18 to 2023-24**).
⚠ **23.3%** = all-India FLFPR 2017-18 and also urban FLFPR 2019-20.

35.s: According to the U-shaped hypothesis, Female LFPR generally:
o: Falls with early income growth and rises later with education and service-sector opportunities
Rises with early income growth and falls with later education
Remains constant regardless of income and education
Falls continuously as service-sector employment expands
35.x: The U-shaped hypothesis proposes that Female LFPR initially falls with income growth and rises later as education and service-sector opportunities expand.
35.tq: Apply the two-stage movement implied by the U-shaped hypothesis.
xs: **U-shaped hypothesis**: FLFPR **falls with early income growth** and **rises later with education + service jobs** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option 2 describes an inverted U; FLFPR is neither constant nor continuously falling.
xa: Barriers: **social norms**, **unpaid care work**, **unsafe transport**.
AP: urban young women stay out due to **higher education** and **no flexible timings**.

35.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a barrier to women’s labour-force participation?
35.x: Social norms, unpaid care work and unsafe transport are barriers; expansion of service-sector opportunities is associated with increased participation at a later stage.
35.tq: Find the supportive factor among the listed barriers.
xs: **Expansion of service-sector opportunities** is not a barrier — under the **U-shaped hypothesis** it later **raises** FLFPR — so option **(2)** is correct.
The listed barriers are **social norms**, **unpaid care work** and **unsafe transport**.
xa: Urban FLFPR only **27.7%** (2025) vs rural **45.9%**.
AP: urban young women stay out (**higher education**, **no flexible timings**).

35.s: The basic reason for the 'feminisation of agriculture' in India is
o: Reservation for women in Panchayati Raj institutions
Rising urban female labour force participation
35.x: Feminisation of agriculture arises chiefly because men migrate from villages to towns, leaving women to do farm work (APPSC 2018). Mechanisation tends to displace labour, panchayat reservation is a political measure, and urban female LFPR has stayed low (about 27.7% in 2025).
35.tq: Men migrate, women farm.
xs: **Feminisation of agriculture** stems from **growing rural-to-urban migration of men** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC 2018).
Urban female LFPR stays low (**27.7%** in 2025), so it cannot explain women's rising farm role.
xa: Rural women = **80%** of the rise in female workers (2017-18 to 2023-24).
Drivers: **subsistence farming**, **unpaid family work**, **distress employment**.
Rural agriculture's employment share: **57%**.

35.s: Which one of the following best describes the gig economy?
o: Employment of workers exclusively in government departments
Engagement of independent contractors and freelancers instead of permanent workers
Employment based only on hereditary occupations
Permanent employment with guaranteed pension benefits
35.x: The gig economy is based on independent contractors and freelancers rather than permanent workers. Delivery services, ride-sharing and freelancing are common examples.
35.tq: Distinguish the exact meaning of a paired economic term from its misleading permanent-employment alternative.
xs: The **gig economy** uses **independent contractors and freelancers instead of permanent workers** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2019).
Examples: **delivery**, **ride-sharing**, **freelancing**.
xa: NITI Aayog: **77 lakh** gig workers in **2020-21**; **2.35 crore** projected by **2029-30**.
**Code on Social Security 2020** defines gig and platform workers.
Gig workers grew **55%** to about **120 lakh** in **FY25**.

35.s: According to NITI Aayog's report titled ‘India's Booming Gig and Platform Economy’, the estimated number of gig workers in India during 2020-21 was
35.x: NITI Aayog estimated 77 lakh gig workers in 2020-21.
35.tq: Separate the base-year estimate from later actual and projected figures.
xs: NITI Aayog's "**India's Booming Gig and Platform Economy**" (**June 2022**) estimated **77 lakh** gig workers in **2020-21** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**2.35 crore** is the **2029-30** projection; **1.27 crore** the **2024-25** projection; **120 lakh** the **FY25** size.
xa: 2029-30 projection = **6.7%** of the workforce.
**1.43 crore** projected for **2025-26**.
PLFS does not yet capture gig workers as a distinct category.

35.s: NITI Aayog projected that the number of gig workers would reach which of the following levels by 2029-30?
35.x: The NITI Aayog projection was 2.35 crore gig workers by 2029-30, equivalent to about 6.7% of the workforce.
35.tq: Use the time reference to distinguish a long-term projection from current estimates.
xs: NITI Aayog projected **2.35 crore** gig workers by **2029-30** (**6.7%** of workforce) — so option **(3)** is correct.
xa: Report: "India's Booming Gig and Platform Economy", **June 2022**.
FY25 size: about **120 lakh** (up **55%**).
Aggregators contribute **1-2%** of annual turnover under the **Code on Social Security 2020**.

35.s: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, aggregators are required to contribute what proportion of their annual turnover to a fund for the benefit of gig workers?
35.x: Aggregators contribute 1% to 2% of annual turnover to a fund intended to support life and health insurance and pensions for gig workers.
35.tq: Match the statutory contribution range with its stated social-security purpose.
xs: Under the **Code on Social Security 2020**, aggregators contribute **1-2% of annual turnover** to a fund — so option **(2)** 1% to 2% is correct.
The fund pays for **life/health insurance** and **pensions** for gig workers.
xa: The Code **defines gig and platform workers**.
Gig workers: **77 lakh** (2020-21) → about **120 lakh** (FY25).
Data gap: PLFS does not capture them as a distinct category.

35.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the measurement and registration of gig workers is correct?
o: PLFS records only platform workers, while e-Shram excludes migrant workers.
PLFS does not yet capture gig workers as a distinct category, and most remain outside e-Shram registration.
PLFS already records gig workers as a separate category and all are registered on e-Shram.
PLFS excludes all informal workers and e-Shram covers only permanent workers.
35.x: The Periodic Labour Force Survey does not yet identify gig workers as a distinct category, and most gig workers remain outside e-Shram registration.
35.tq: Use the contrast between survey classification and portal registration.
xs: **PLFS does not yet capture gig workers as a distinct category**, and **most remain outside e-Shram** registration — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option 3 states the opposite; options 1 and 4 are not in the notes.
xa: Gig workforce about **120 lakh** in **FY25**; over **2%** of workforce.
**Code on Social Security 2020** defines gig and platform workers.
NITI projection: **2.35 crore** by **2029-30**.

35.s:
With reference to female labour force participation in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. The female LFPR for all ages in Andhra Pradesh is 35.8%.
2. The corresponding all-India figure is 31.7%.
3. Andhra Pradesh has a lower female LFPR than India for all ages.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Andhra Pradesh's all-age female LFPR of 35.8% is higher than India's 31.7%, so statement 3 is false.
35.tq: Check both the figures and the direction of comparison before selecting the code.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: AP **female LFPR (all ages)** = **35.8%**.
Statement 2 is correct: India's = **31.7%**.
Statement 3 is wrong: AP is **higher**, not lower — so option **(1)** 1 and 2 only is correct.
xa: Female LFPR 15+: AP **44.8%** vs India **41.7%**.
AP overall LFPR: **47.5%** (rural **50.1%**, urban **41.3%**).
Yet urban young women in AP stay out (**higher education**, **no flexible timings**).

35.s: The overall informal-sector share of employment in Andhra Pradesh was approximately
35.x: The overall informal-sector share of employment in Andhra Pradesh was approximately 55%.
35.tq: Distinguish the approximate overall figure from the separate rural and urban shares.
xs: AP's overall **informal** share of employment is about **55%** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**62.3%** is the **rural** informal share and **45.6%** the **urban** share (2024-25).
xa: Nationally, Gen Z: only **14.2%** have a **formal job contract**.
Direct factory employment fell **61% to 47%** (2011-2023).

35.s: According to PLFS 2025, the approximate values of India's LFPR, WPR and unemployment rate were respectively
35.x: PLFS 2025 reported an approximate LFPR of 59%, WPR of 57% and unemployment rate of 3%.
35.tq: Preserve the correct order of the three labour-market indicators before matching the figures.
xs: **PLFS 2025**: **LFPR ~59%**, **WPR ~57%**, **UR ~3%** — so option **(2)** is correct.
WPR is below LFPR because the labour force also includes the unemployed; the other options jumble the order.
xa: Workforce: **61.6 crore** (PLFS 2025).
Female LFPR 2025: ~**40%**.
AP overall LFPR: **47.5%**.

36.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. NREP — Wage employment
2. IRDP — Self-employment
3. MGNREGS — Wage employment
4. NRLM — Wage employment
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
36.x: NREP and MGNREGS are wage-employment programmes, while IRDP is a self-employment programme. NRLM belongs to the self-employment group, so pair 4 is incorrect.
36.tq: Classify each programme before checking the coded combination.
xs: Pairs 1–3 are correct: **NREP** and **MGNREGS** are **wage employment**; **IRDP** is **self-employment**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **NRLM** is a **self-employment** programme — so option **(1)** 1, 2 and 3 only is correct.
xa: Other wage programmes: **JRY, EAS, SGRY, NFFWP**.
Other self-employment programmes: **TRYSEM, DWCRA, SGSY, PMEGP**.
⚠ **PMRY** is **not** a wage employment programme (APPSC 2017).

36.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between NFFWP, SGRY and NREGA?
o: NFFWP and SGRY were created after NREGA in 2009.
NFFWP and SGRY were subsumed into NREGA in its districts from 2006.
Only SGRY was subsumed into NFFWP in 2010.
NREGA was subsumed into SGRY in 2004.
36.x: NFFWP and SGRY were subsumed into NREGA in the districts covered by NREGA from 2006. The 2009 event was the addition of the name Mahatma Gandhi, not the merger of NFFWP.
36.tq: Use the sequence of predecessor programmes and avoid the renaming-year trap.
xs: **NFFWP and SGRY** were **subsumed into NREGA in its districts from 2006** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: the **2009** event was only the renaming ("**Mahatma Gandhi**" added on **2 October 2009**), not the merger.
xa: NFFWP launched **14 November 2004**.
NREGA launched **2 February 2006** in **200** districts.
⚠ **2005** Act – **2006** launch – **2008** all districts – **2009** "Mahatma Gandhi" added.

36.s: Which one of the following is NOT a wage employment programme?
36.x: PMRY (1993) was a self-employment programme for educated unemployed youth, later merged into PMEGP (APPSC 2017). JRY, EAS and SGRY were all wage employment programmes in the line that led to NREGA.
36.tq: 'Rozgar' in the name does not make PMRY a wage scheme.
xs: **PMRY** (**1993**) is **not** a wage employment programme — it was **self-employment** for educated unemployed youth — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2017).
**JRY**, **EAS** and **SGRY** are all **wage employment** programmes.
xa: PMRY was later merged with **REGP** into **PMEGP** (**2008**).
SGRY was subsumed into NREGA from **2006**.
Other self-employment programmes: **IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA, SGSY, NRLM**.

36.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the initial implementation of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act?
o: It began in 200 districts on 2 February 2006.
It began in 150 most backward districts in 2004.
It began in all districts on 1 April 2008.
It began in 625 districts on 2 October 2009.
36.x: The Act was launched on 2 February 2006 in 200 districts. The all-district coverage was achieved later, from 1 April 2008.
36.tq: Distinguish the initial coverage from later nationwide expansion.
xs: NREGA began on **2 February 2006** in **200** districts — so option **(1)** is correct.
**150 backward districts (2004)** = **NFFWP**; **all districts from 1 April 2008** was a later phase; **2 October 2009** was the renaming.
xa: **130** more districts were added in **2007-08**.
⚠ Trap: **625** = all-district coverage of **2008**, not the launch.
⚠ **2005** Act – **2006** launch – **2008** all districts – **2009** "Mahatma Gandhi".

36.s: Under MGNREGA, the unit to which the employment guarantee is attached is:
o: Each adult individual in a rural area
Each registered worker in a Gram Panchayat
36.x: The entitlement under MGNREGA is provided to a household, not separately to every individual adult.
36.tq: Discriminate between the household-based entitlement and an individual-based interpretation.
xs: The MGNREGA entitlement attaches to the **household**, not the individual — so option **(2)** the rural household is correct.
APPSC 2017: the mandate is "**100 days** to every **household** whose adult members volunteer", **not** "100 days to every adult".
xa: Eligibility: **rural** households whose **adult** members volunteer for **unskilled manual** work.
Guarantee: at least **100 days** per **financial year**.
VB-G RAM G raises it to **125 days**/household.

36.s: Which provision of the Constitution is associated with the right to work that provides the Directive Principles basis for MGNREGA?
36.x: MGNREGA is anchored in Article 41, which relates to the right to work, education and public assistance in certain cases.
36.tq: Match the policy objective with the relevant constitutional article.
xs: MGNREGA is anchored in **Article 41** (**right to work**, DPSP) — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is **rights-based** and **demand-driven**.
xa: A **Supreme Court** bench (**21 Aug 2026**) weighed placing the right to work on par with **Article 21**.
**Olga Tellis (1985)** tied livelihood to Article 21.
MGNREGA is the **only law built on the right to work**.

36.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the target group and objectives of MGNREGA:
1. It covers rural households whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.
2. It seeks to reduce distress migration.
3. It is primarily intended for urban skilled workers.
4. It includes natural resource management and durable asset creation among its objectives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because MGNREGA targets rural households volunteering for unskilled manual work, not urban skilled workers.
36.tq: Identify the target group first, then test the associated objectives.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: it covers **rural** households whose **adult** members volunteer for **unskilled manual** work.
Statements 2 and 4 are correct: aims include **reducing distress migration**, **natural resource management** and **durable asset creation**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is **not for urban or skilled** workers — so option **(2)** 1, 2 and 4 only is correct.
xa: Main objective: **enhancing livelihood security** of rural households (APPSC 2023).
NRM targets **drought, deforestation, soil erosion**.
Permissible works: **water conservation**, land development, rural connectivity.

36.s: Which Ministry is the nodal Ministry for MGNREGA?
o: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
36.x: MGNREGA is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development.
36.tq: Use the ministry–scheme association and avoid neighbouring ministry substitutions.
xs: MGNREGA's nodal ministry is the **Ministry of Rural Development** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Labour and Employment** runs the **National Career Service**; **Gram Sabhas** only plan, monitor and audit works.
xa: **DDU-GKY** is also under **Rural Development**.
Monitoring: **Bhuvan** (ISRO) for geo-tagging, **NREGASoft** for MIS.
Constitutional anchor: **Article 41**.

36.s:
Consider the following statements about wages under MGNREGA:
1. A single uniform wage rate is notified for the whole country.
2. Wages are to be paid within 15 days of the work done, and delay attracts compensation.
3. Wages are paid by DBT into Aadhaar-linked accounts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
36.x: Statement 1 is wrong: MGNREGA wages are State-specific notified wages, not uniform. Statement 2 is correct: payment within 15 days of work done, with compensation for delay. Statement 3 is correct: payment is by DBT to Aadhaar-linked accounts. So '2 and 3 only'; '2 only' omits a true statement, and options with 1 are wrong.
36.tq: MGNREGA wage = State-specific, paid within 15 days, via DBT.
xs: Statement 1 is wrong: wages are **State-specific notified wages**, not uniform.
Statement 2 is correct: wages are paid **within 15 days of the work done**; delay attracts **compensation**.
Statement 3 is correct: payment is by **DBT to Aadhaar-linked accounts** — so option **(3)** 2 and 3 only is correct.
xa: ⚠ **15 days** twice: wages within 15 days of work; **allowance** if no work within 15 days of application.
VB-G RAM G: wages **weekly** or within a fortnight; floor **₹300/day**.
Unions demand a **₹700** wage.

36.s: The primary objective of MGNREGA is
o: Providing 100 days of employment to every adult in rural and urban areas
Enhancing livelihood security of rural households by providing at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year
Providing skill training and placement to rural youth
Providing collateral-free credit to rural self-help groups
36.x: MGNREGA aims at enhancing livelihood security of rural households through at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment per financial year (APPSC 2023). The guarantee is per household, not per adult, and covers only rural areas. Skilling and placement is DDU-GKY, and SHG credit falls under NRLM.
36.tq: Livelihood security, 100 days, household, rural.
xs: MGNREGA's objective: **enhancing livelihood security** of rural households via at least **100 days** of **guaranteed wage employment** per **financial year** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2023).
The guarantee is per **household**, not every adult, and **rural only**; skilling is **DDU-GKY**; SHG credit is **NRLM**.
xa: Other aims: **durable asset creation**, **natural resource management**, reducing **distress migration**.
Successor **VB-G RAM G** guarantees **125 days**.

36.s: What is the minimum share of women prescribed among MGNREGA beneficiaries?
36.x: At least one-third of MGNREGA beneficiaries must be women, although their actual share has consistently exceeded 50 per cent of person-days.
36.tq: Distinguish the statutory minimum from the actual participation trend.
xs: At least **one-third** of MGNREGA beneficiaries must be **women** — so option **(3)** is correct.
In practice women's share is consistently **above 50%** of person-days.
xa: Unemployment allowance: at least **1/4** of wage for the first **30** days, **1/2** thereafter.
Social audit by the **Gram Sabha** is mandatory.
Scale: **200-250 crore** person-days a year.

36.s: Which pair is correctly matched in the context of MGNREGA monitoring?
o: Bhuvan — GeoMGNREGA geo-tagging platform; NREGASoft — Management Information System
Bhuvan — Wage payment authority; NREGASoft — Social audit forum
GeoMGNREGA — Constitutional provision; NREGASoft — Central Finance Commission
NREGASoft — Satellite launch vehicle; Bhuvan — Unemployment allowance portal
36.x: Bhuvan, developed by ISRO, supports GeoMGNREGA geo-tagging, while NREGASoft is the programme's Management Information System.
36.tq: Start from the sure technology–function pair and reject swapped institutional roles.
xs: **Bhuvan** (**ISRO**) = **GeoMGNREGA** geo-tagging; **NREGASoft** = **MIS** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC 2018).
Social audit is by the **Gram Sabha**, not NREGASoft.
xa: **AwaasSoft-NREGASoft** link gives **90/95 person-days** to **PMAY-G** beneficiaries.
Gram Sabhas **plan and monitor** works.
VB-G RAM G assets sit on the **VB-NRIS** stack.

36.s: Social audit of MGNREGA works is mandatory and is conducted by:
36.x: Social audit is mandatory under MGNREGA and is conducted by the Gram Sabha. Gram Sabhas also plan and monitor works.
36.tq: Identify the local participatory body responsible for the function.
xs: MGNREGA **social audit** is mandatory and done by the **Gram Sabha** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Gram Sabhas also **plan and monitor** works.
xa: Geo-tagging: **Bhuvan** (**ISRO**) — GeoMGNREGA.
MIS: **NREGASoft**.
VB-G RAM G: **no contractors**; Central and State **Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Councils**.

36.s: If employment is not provided within 15 days of an application under MGNREGA, the unemployment allowance is at least:
o: One-fourth of the wage throughout the period
One-fourth of the wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter
One-half of the wage for the first 30 days and one-fourth thereafter
The full wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter
36.x: The unemployment allowance is at least one-fourth of the wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter.
36.tq: Track the change in rate after the first 30-day period.
xs: If work is not given within **15 days** of application, the allowance is at least **1/4 (one-fourth) of the wage for the first 30 days** and **1/2 (one-half) thereafter** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option 3 reverses the fractions.
xa: ⚠ **15 days** also = deadline for paying wages after the work is done.
The allowance is **retained** under **VB-G RAM G**.
Women: at least **one-third** of beneficiaries.

36.s: With effect from 1 July 2026, which legislation replaced the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act?
o: National Food for Work Programme Act, 2004
Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025
36.x: The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, replaced MGNREGA and came into force on 1 July 2026.
36.tq: Identify the exact official title in a scheme-renaming and replacement question.
xs: From **1 July 2026**, MGNREGA was replaced by the **Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025** (**VB-G RAM G**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was passed by Parliament on **18 Dec 2025**.
**Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan (2020)** was a campaign for returnee migrants; **NFFWP (2004)** was a programme, not an Act.
xa: Guarantee: **125 days**/household (operated over **305** days).
Funding **60:40** (**90:10** NE/Himalayan States, UTs).
Job cards → **Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards**.

36.s: Under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, the guaranteed wage employment and the period over which the programme is operated are respectively:
36.x: VB-G RAM G provides 125 days of employment per household and operates over 305 days.
36.tq: Compare the paired numerical features instead of recalling either number in isolation.
xs: **VB-G RAM G** guarantees **125 days**/household, operated over **305 days** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**100 days** was the old **MGNREGA** guarantee.
xa: States may **pause** works up to **60 days** in sowing/harvest.
⚠ **125 – 60 – 9%** = guarantee days – seasonal pause – admin ceiling.
Wage floor **₹300/day**; wages paid **weekly** or within a fortnight.

36.s:
Consider the following statements about the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025:
1. States may pause works for up to 60 days during the sowing and harvest seasons.
2. Funding is shared 60:40 between the Centre and States, and 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and UTs.
3. The administrative cost ceiling has been reduced to 6%.
4. It fixes a statutory wage floor of Rs 300 per day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: a seasonal pause of up to 60 days, 60:40 funding (90:10 for NE/Himalayan States and UTs) and a Rs 300/day wage floor. Statement 3 is wrong: the ceiling was 6% under MGNREGA and is raised to 9% under VB-G RAM G. So '1 and 2 only' omits a true statement, and options containing 3 are wrong.
36.tq: VB-G RAM G: 125 days, 60-day pause, 60:40, 9% admin ceiling, Rs 300 floor.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: States may **pause works up to 60 days** in sowing/harvest.
Statement 2 is correct: funding **60:40** (**90:10** for NE/Himalayan States, UTs).
Statement 3 is wrong: the admin cost ceiling was **6%** under MGNREGA and is **raised to 9%**.
Statement 4 is correct: statutory wage floor **₹300/day** — so option **(2)** 1, 2 and 4 only is correct.
xa: Allocation is **normative State-wise**, not demand-driven as under MGNREGA.
Guarantee **125 days**; assets on **VB-NRIS** stack.

36.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the ministry and implementing agency associated with the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)?
o: Ministry of Skill Development; implemented by NSDC
Ministry of Labour and Employment; implemented by NCS
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises; implemented by KVIC
Ministry of Rural Development; implemented by DRDA
36.x: PMEGP is administered by the Ministry of MSME and implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).
36.tq: Use the ‘who launched or implements it?’ method to distinguish neighbouring ministries and agencies.
xs: **PMEGP** is under the **Ministry of MSME** and **implemented by KVIC** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**DDU-GKY** is under **Rural Development**; **NCS** under **Labour & Employment**.
xa: ⚠ PM-SVANidhi = **Housing & Urban Affairs**, not MSME.
PMEGP (**2008**) = **PMRY + REGP**.
PMEGP met its target of **4.02 lakh** new micro-enterprises; **80%** rural, **40%** women.

36.s: PMEGP was formed by integrating which two earlier programmes?
36.x: PMEGP, launched in 2008, was formed by combining the Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) and the Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP).
36.tq: Identify the predecessor programmes rather than the ministry or beneficiary group.
xs: **PMEGP** (**2008**) merged **PMRY and REGP** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**NRLM** and **MGNREGS** are separate rural programmes; **NCS** and **PMKVY** are job-portal and skilling schemes.
xa: **PMRY** (**1993**): for educated unemployed youth.
PMEGP: margin money **15-35%**.
⚠ PMEGP = **MSME** ministry, implemented by **KVIC**.

36.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. DDU-GKY, under the Ministry of Rural Development, provides placement-linked skilling to rural poor youth.
2. DDU-GKY has its roots in the special projects of PMEGP.
3. PM Vishwakarma, under the Ministry of MSME, covers 18 traditional artisan trades.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
36.x: Statement 1 is correct: DDU-GKY (2014) is a Ministry of Rural Development scheme of placement-linked skilling for rural poor youth. Statement 2 is wrong: its roots are in the special projects of SGSY, not PMEGP. Statement 3 is correct: PM Vishwakarma is under MSME and covers 18 artisan trades. So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
36.tq: DDU-GKY grew out of SGSY special projects; PMEGP is a separate MSME/KVIC scheme.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **DDU-GKY** (**2014**, **Rural Development**) gives **placement-linked skilling** to rural poor youth.
Statement 2 is wrong: its roots are in **SGSY** special projects, not PMEGP.
Statement 3 is correct: **PM Vishwakarma** (**MSME**) covers **18** traditional artisan trades — so option **(2)** 1 and 3 only is correct.
xa: PM Vishwakarma offers **training, toolkits, credit**.
**SGSY** is a self-employment programme.
**Recognition of Prior Learning** certifies skills against **NSQF**.

36.s: PM-SVANidhi primarily provides:
o: Long-term housing loans to rural households
Subsidised loans to traditional artisans only
Collateral-free working-capital loans to street vendors
36.x: PM-SVANidhi provides collateral-free working-capital loans to street vendors. The scheme has covered more than 75 lakh vendors.
36.tq: Use the target occupation—street vendors—to separate PM-SVANidhi from other credit schemes.
xs: **PM-SVANidhi** gives **collateral-free working-capital loans to street vendors** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It has covered **75 lakh+** vendors.
Placement-linked skilling is **DDU-GKY**; artisans are covered by **PM Vishwakarma**.
xa: ⚠ PM-SVANidhi = **Housing & Urban Affairs**, not MSME.
PMEGP supports new **non-farm micro-enterprises**.
National Career Service (**2015**): job-matching portal.

36.s: Recognition of Prior Learning under PMKVY is intended to:
o: Provide working capital to street vendors
Certify existing skills against the National Skills Qualifications Framework
Provide EPF support for new formal jobs
36.x: Recognition of Prior Learning certifies skills that individuals already possess against the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF).
36.tq: Identify the scheme by the action it performs—assessment and certification of existing skills.
xs: **Recognition of Prior Learning** (under **PMKVY**, **2015**) **certifies existing skills** against the **NSQF** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Street-vendor capital = **PM-SVANidhi**; **125 days** = **VB-G RAM G**; **EPF** support = **ABRY**.
xa: RPL falls under **Skill Development**.
**DDU-GKY** gives placement-linked skilling to rural poor youth.
**PM Vishwakarma** covers **18** artisan trades.

36.s: Andhra Pradesh ranked what position nationally under MGNREGS?
36.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked fourth nationally under MGNREGS.
36.tq: Use the exact rank rather than assuming that a major-performing State occupied the first position.
xs: AP ranked **4th** (**fourth**) nationally under **MGNREGS** (AP SES analysis) — so option **(1)** is correct.
The rank comes from the State's socio-economic survey.
xa: AP's new Mission pooled rural development funds for **125 days** in distressed pockets (**Jun 2026**).
VB-G RAM G also guarantees **125 days**/household from **1 July 2026**.
MGNREGA scale: **5-6 crore** households a year nationally.

36.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Supreme Court Bench discussed whether the right to work should be placed on a par with Article 21.
2. Olga Tellis (1985) linked livelihood with Article 21.
3. MGNREGA is described as the only law built on the right to work.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: All three statements are correct: the Supreme Court discussion concerned the relationship between the right to work and Article 21, Olga Tellis linked livelihood to Article 21, and MGNREGA is described as the only law based on the right to work.
36.tq: Test the constitutional case, judicial discussion and broader significance as separate statements.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: a **Supreme Court** bench (**21 Aug 2026**) weighed placing the right to work on par with **Article 21**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Olga Tellis (1985)** tied **livelihood** to Article 21.
Statement 3 is correct: MGNREGA is the **only law built on the right to work** — so option **(4)** 1, 2 and 3 is correct.
xa: MGNREGA's DPSP anchor: **Article 41**.
Unions sought rollback of VB-G RAM G, **200 days** and **₹700** wage.

36.s: Which of the following best expresses the wider significance of MGNREGA?
o: It certifies prior learning under the NSQF.
It is primarily an urban credit programme for informal workers.
It serves as a safety net during agrarian distress and crises such as COVID-19.
36.x: MGNREGA is significant as a safety net during agrarian distress and emergencies such as the COVID-19 crisis, in addition to being associated with the right to work.
36.tq: Apply the scheme’s broader social-protection role to a crisis situation.
xs: MGNREGA is a **safety net** in **agrarian distress** and crises like **COVID-19** — so option **(4)** is correct.
NSQF certification is **RPL**; it is **rural**, not urban credit; it has nothing to do with export manufacturing.
xa: It is the **only law built on the right to work**.
World Development Report **2014**: "**stellar example of rural development**".
Scale: **200-250 crore** person-days a year.

37.s: Antyodaya was first launched in:
37.x: The Antyodaya programme was first launched in Rajasthan in 1977.
37.tq: Recall the launch-place and year combination.
xs: **Antyodaya** was first launched in **Rajasthan** in **1977**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**1982** belongs to **DWCRA** and **RUDSETI** (Ujire, Karnataka), and **1975** is the launch year of the **Twenty Point Programme**, not Antyodaya.
xa: **Community Development Programme** began on **2 Oct 1952**: called the "mother of social development programmes".
**TRYSEM** (Training of Rural Youth for Self Employment) began on **15 Aug 1979**.
Strategy shift: **direct-attack** (target-group) programmes replaced reliance on **trickle-down** from the **5th-6th Plans**.

37.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Twenty Point Programme is correct?
37.x: The Twenty Point Programme was launched in 1975 and restructured in 1982, 1986 and 2006.
37.tq: Separate the original launch year from the successive restructuring years.
xs: The **Twenty Point Programme** was **launched in 1975** and **restructured in 1982, 1986 and 2006**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**1977** is the year of **Antyodaya** (Rajasthan) and **1952** is the **Community Development Programme**, so options built on them are wrong.
xa: ⚠ **1982** is a triple date: Twenty Point restructuring, **DWCRA** and **RUDSETI**.
**Antyodaya** was first launched in **Rajasthan** in **1977**.
**IRDP** covered **all blocks** from **2 Oct 1980** (6th Plan).

37.s: Which of the following statements about RUDSETI is correct?
o: It was established at Ujire in Karnataka in 1982 and trains rural youth for self-employment.
It was established in Rajasthan in 1977 to provide micro-credit to women.
It was established in Andhra Pradesh in 1992 to refinance banks.
It was established in Delhi in 1975 to restructure the Twenty Point Programme.
37.x: RUDSETI was established at Ujire in Karnataka in 1982 and trains rural youth for self-employment. It became a model for the present RSETIs.
37.tq: Combine location, year and function while rejecting swapped institutional roles.
xs: **RUDSETI** (Rural Development and Self Employment Training Institute) was established at **Ujire** in **Karnataka** in **1982** and trains **rural youth for self-employment**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Rajasthan 1977** is **Antyodaya**; **refinancing banks** is **NABARD**'s role; **1975** is the Twenty Point Programme launch.
xa: RUDSETI became the **model for today's RSETIs**.
⚠ **DWCRA** (group approach for women, forerunner of women's SHGs) also began in **1982**.
**TRYSEM** (**15 Aug 1979**) was the earlier rural-youth self-employment training programme.

37.s: The Community Development Programme, described as the ‘mother of social development programmes’, was launched on:
37.x: The Community Development Programme was launched on 2 October 1952 and is described as the mother of social development programmes.
37.tq: Use the exact commemorative date associated with the programme.
xs: The **Community Development Programme**, the "mother of social development programmes", was launched on **2 October 1952**, so option **(3)** is correct.
The other dates are not linked to this programme in the notes.
xa: **Twenty Point Programme**: launched **1975**; restructured **1982**, **1986**, **2006**.
**Antyodaya**: first launched in **Rajasthan**, **1977**.
**IRDP** extended to **all blocks** on **2 Oct 1980** (another 2 October date).

37.s: Which of the following correctly describes the change from IRDP to SGSY?
o: Rural poverty programmes were replaced by urban street-vendor programmes.
Individual beneficiary approach was replaced by an SHG or group approach.
Bank credit was replaced entirely by government grants.
Training programmes were replaced by crop insurance.
37.x: IRDP followed an individual family or beneficiary approach, whereas SGSY adopted an SHG-based group approach.
37.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap to distinguish two successive poverty programmes.
xs: The move from **IRDP to SGSY** replaced the **individual family (beneficiary) approach** with an **SHG/group approach**, so option **(2)** is correct.
SGSY stayed a **rural** programme with **group financing** through bank credit; street vendors (**SUSV**) belong to urban **DAY-NULM**.
xa: **SGSY** (**1 April 1999**) merged **IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA, SITRA, Ganga Kalyan Yojana** and the **Million Wells Scheme**.
SGSY aimed to bring assisted poor families above the poverty line by organising them into **SHGs** (APPSC 2023, 2019).
SGSY → **NRLM "Aajeevika"** (restructured 2010, launched **2011**) → **DAY-NRLM** (2016).

37.s:
Which of the following correctly describes IRDP?
1. It combined subsidy with bank credit.
2. It aimed to help poor rural families cross the poverty line.
3. It was implemented in all blocks from 2 October 1980.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: IRDP combined subsidy and bank credit, aimed at taking poor rural families above the poverty line, and covered all blocks from 2 October 1980.
37.tq: Verify a scheme through its financing pattern, objective and expansion date.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **IRDP** combined **subsidy + bank credit**.
Statement 2 is correct: its aim was that **poor rural families cross the poverty line**.
Statement 3 is correct: it covered **all blocks from 2 Oct 1980**, so **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)**.
xa: IRDP: **1978-79**, part of the **6th Plan** (1980).
APPSC 2025 quoted IRDP as envisaging "assistance to poor rural families to come above the poverty line".
IRDP was merged into **SGSY** on **1 April 1999**; IRDP used an **individual family** approach.

37.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: SITRA — Supply of Improved Toolkits to Rural Artisans
TRYSEM — Training of Rural Youth for Self Employment
DWCRA — Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas
Ganga Kalyan Yojana — General urban employment guarantee
37.x: Ganga Kalyan Yojana concerned bore-well and tube-well irrigation for small and marginal farmers, not urban employment guarantee. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
37.tq: Find the mismatched aim while the other pairs use exact official expansions.
xs: **Ganga Kalyan Yojana** was for **bore-well/tube-well irrigation for small and marginal farmers**, not urban employment, so option **(4)** is the wrong pair.
**SITRA** = Supply of Improved Toolkits to Rural Artisans; **TRYSEM** = Training of Rural Youth for Self Employment; **DWCRA** = Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas — all correct.
xa: Years: **TRYSEM 1979**, **DWCRA 1982**, **SITRA 1992**, **Ganga Kalyan Yojana 1997**.
All four were merged into **SGSY** on **1 April 1999**, along with IRDP and the **Million Wells Scheme**.
**DWCRA** used a group approach for women and was the forerunner of women's **SHGs**.

37.s:
Arrange the following schemes in chronological order of their commencement:
A. SITRA
B. TRYSEM
C. DWCRA
D. Ganga Kalyan Yojana
37.x: TRYSEM began in 1979, DWCRA in 1982, SITRA in 1992 and Ganga Kalyan Yojana in 1997.
37.tq: Arrange programmes by their starting years, using the earliest and latest items first.
xs: Correct order is **B, C, A, D**: **TRYSEM (1979)** → **DWCRA (1982)** → **SITRA (1992)** → **Ganga Kalyan Yojana (1997)**, option **(1)**.
TRYSEM began on **15 Aug 1979**; DWCRA is also dated **1982-83**.
xa: All four were absorbed into **SGSY** on **1 April 1999**.
**RUDSETI** (Ujire, Karnataka) also dates to **1982**, like DWCRA.
**SITRA** = Supply of Improved Toolkits to Rural Artisans; **Ganga Kalyan Yojana** = irrigation wells for small and marginal farmers.

37.s: Which one of the following combinations consists entirely of direct-attack poverty programmes?
37.x: IRDP, NREP, RLEGP and JRY are listed as direct-attack or target-group poverty programmes.
37.tq: Identify the common programme family rather than matching only one item.
xs: **IRDP, NREP, RLEGP and JRY** are the **direct-attack** (target-group) poverty programmes, so option **(3)** is correct.
**PAISA** and **SUSV** are **DAY-NULM** components, **SVEP** is a DAY-NRLM initiative, and **RSETIs** are training institutes — not in the direct-attack list.
xa: Direct attack replaced reliance on **trickle-down** from the **5th-6th Plans**.
⚠ Odd-one-out questions slip a non-poverty programme (crop insurance, a statistics body) beside IRDP/NREP/RLEGP/JRY.

37.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
37.x: JRY was associated with the Seventh Plan and began in 1989, not the Sixth Plan in 1980. The other matches are correct.
37.tq: Catch the wrong plan-year association in a list of closely related programmes.
xs: **JRY** belongs to the **7th Plan** and **1989**, not the Sixth Plan, 1980 — so option **(4)** is the wrong pair.
**RLEGP — 1983**, **IRDP — 1978-79 / 6th Plan** and **NREP — 6th Plan, 1980** are all correct.
xa: All four are **direct-attack** poverty programmes.
IRDP was extended to **all blocks** on **2 Oct 1980**.
**TRYSEM** (**15 Aug 1979**) gave rural youth self-employment training.

37.s: The direct-attack strategy in poverty alleviation replaced reliance on
o: trickle-down from the Fifth and Sixth Plans
37.x: Target-group programmes under the direct-attack strategy replaced reliance on the trickle-down approach associated with the Fifth and Sixth Plans.
37.tq: Distinguish a change in poverty-alleviation strategy from changes in individual schemes.
xs: The **direct-attack** strategy (target-group programmes) replaced reliance on **trickle-down from the 5th-6th Plans**, so option **(2)** is correct.
SHG group financing (**SGSY**, 1999) and Gram Sabha vetting (**PIP** under DAY-NRLM) came much later; urban street-vendor support is **DAY-NULM**.
xa: Direct-attack programmes: **IRDP**, **NREP** (6th Plan, 1980), **RLEGP** (1983), **JRY** (7th Plan, 1989).
**IRDP** gave **subsidy + bank credit** so poor rural families could cross the poverty line.
**Antyodaya** (Rajasthan, **1977**) is another target-group programme.

37.s: The six programmes—IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA, SITRA, Ganga Kalyan Yojana and Million Wells Scheme—were merged to form which programme on 1 April 1999?
37.x: The six earlier programmes were merged into Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY), launched on 1 April 1999.
37.tq: Identify the programme formed by a merger of several predecessor schemes.
xs: The six programmes were merged into **Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)** on **1 April 1999**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**NRLM** came from restructuring SGSY (2010, launched **2011**) and became **DAY-NRLM** in 2016; **RLEGP** (1983) was a separate direct-attack programme.
xa: SGSY shifted from IRDP's **individual family** approach to the **SHG/group** approach.
SGSY aimed to bring assisted poor families **above the poverty line** through SHG **group financing** (APPSC 2023, 2019).
⚠ **SGSY → NRLM** is the rural chain; **SJSRY → NULM** is the urban chain.

37.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the restructuring and renaming sequence of SGSY?
37.x: SGSY was restructured as NRLM, branded as Aajeevika, in 2010 and launched in 2011; it was subsequently renamed DAY-NRLM in 2016.
37.tq: Follow the scheme-renaming chain from the original programme to its current form.
xs: **SGSY → NRLM "Aajeevika" → DAY-NRLM** is the correct chain, option **(1)**.
SGSY was restructured in **2010**, NRLM launched in **2011**, renamed **DAY-NRLM** in **2016**.
**SJSRY → NULM** is the separate **urban** chain; **IRDP** and **NREP** came before SGSY, not after it.
xa: SGSY itself (**1 April 1999**) merged IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA, SITRA, Ganga Kalyan Yojana and the Million Wells Scheme.
DAY-NRLM is run by the **Ministry of Rural Development**.
APPSC 2019 asked that SGSY is "now known as **NRLM**".

37.s: The scheme launched on 1 April 1999 with the objective of bringing assisted poor families above the poverty line was
37.x: SGSY was launched on 1 April 1999 to bring assisted poor families above the poverty line through SHG-based group financing.
37.tq: Match the distinctive objective and launch date with the correct scheme.
xs: **SGSY** was launched on **1 April 1999** to bring assisted poor families above the poverty line by organising them into **SHGs**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**NREP** (1980), **JRY** (**1989**) and **IRDP** (1978-79) are older direct-attack programmes; IRDP was merged into SGSY.
xa: SGSY used **group financing**, replacing IRDP's **individual beneficiary** approach.
SGSY was restructured into **NRLM "Aajeevika"** (launched **2011**), later **DAY-NRLM**.
Asked in **APPSC 2023** and **2019**.

37.s: The National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM), launched in 2013 and later renamed DAY-NULM, replaced which earlier programme?
37.x: NULM (2013) replaced the urban SJSRY of 1997 and was later renamed DAY-NULM. SGSY was the rural programme restructured into NRLM. IRDP was merged into SGSY in 1999, and PMRY was merged into PMEGP in 2008.
37.tq: Rural: SGSY -> NRLM; urban: SJSRY -> NULM.
xs: **NULM** (2013) replaced the urban **Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY)** of **1997**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**SGSY** was the **rural** programme restructured into **NRLM**; **IRDP** was merged into SGSY in **1999**.
xa: ⚠ **SJSRY → NULM** = urban chain; **SGSY → NRLM** = rural chain.
NULM was renamed **DAY-NULM** under **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana**; ministry: **Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation** (now Housing & Urban Affairs).
In AP, DAY-NULM is implemented by **MEPMA** (**1 Sep 2007**).

37.s: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh, established in 1993, primarily aims at providing which of the following?
o: Micro-credit to poor women in the unorganised sector
37.x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh was established in 1993 to provide micro-credit to poor women working in the unorganised sector.
37.tq: Identify the precise objective associated with the named institution.
xs: **Rashtriya Mahila Kosh** (**1993**) gives **micro-credit to poor women in the unorganised sector**, so option **(1)** is correct.
Training rural youth for self-employment is **TRYSEM**/**RUDSETI**, not RMK.
xa: **Swayamsiddha** (**2001**): SHG-based integrated empowerment of women.
**Swalamban**: training and employment of poor women (former **NORAD** scheme).
**STEP**: Support to Training and Employment Programme for Women — skills and employment.

37.s: Swayamsiddha, launched in 2001, was principally associated with:
o: Integrated empowerment of women through self-help groups
Training of rural youth through RSETIs
37.x: Swayamsiddha was an SHG-based programme for the integrated empowerment of women and was launched in 2001.
37.tq: Use the year-objective association to distinguish similar women-focused schemes.
xs: **Swayamsiddha** (**2001**) was an **SHG-based integrated empowerment of women** programme, so option **(1)** is correct.
Training rural youth is the role of **RSETIs** (modelled on **RUDSETI**), not Swayamsiddha.
xa: **Rashtriya Mahila Kosh** (**1993**): micro-credit to poor women in the unorganised sector.
**Swalamban**: training and employment of poor women (former **NORAD** scheme).
**STEP**: skills and employment for women.

37.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Swalamban — Training and employment of poor women
Rashtriya Mahila Kosh — Training rural youth for self-employment
Swayamsiddha — Micro-credit to women in the unorganised sector
STEP — Restructuring of the Twenty Point Programme
37.x: Swalamban concerned training and employment of poor women and was the former NORAD scheme. The other pairings assign objectives of different programmes.
37.tq: Use objective-based matching and eliminate swapped programme functions.
xs: **Swalamban — training and employment of poor women** is correctly matched (former **NORAD** scheme), option **(1)**.
**Rashtriya Mahila Kosh** gives **micro-credit to poor women** in the unorganised sector, not youth training.
**Swayamsiddha** is **SHG-based integrated empowerment of women**; **STEP** is skills and employment for women — unrelated to the Twenty Point Programme.
xa: RMK dates to **1993**; Swayamsiddha to **2001**.
The **Twenty Point Programme** (**1975**) was restructured in **1982**, **1986**, **2006**.

37.s: The Support to Training and Employment Programme for Women (STEP) is intended to provide:
o: Skills and employment opportunities to women
Only pension support to elderly women
37.x: STEP stands for Support to Training and Employment Programme for Women and focuses on skills and employment.
37.tq: Expand the official acronym and connect it with its stated function.
xs: **STEP** = **Support to Training and Employment Programme for Women**: it gives women **skills and employment**, so option **(1)** is correct.
Micro-credit to poor women is **Rashtriya Mahila Kosh**, not STEP.
xa: **Swalamban**: training and employment of poor women (former **NORAD** scheme).
**Swayamsiddha** (**2001**): SHG-based integrated empowerment of women.
**DWCRA** (**1982**) was the forerunner of women's SHGs.

37.s:
Consider the following statements about the origin and spread of self-help groups:
1. The Grameen Bank model of collateral-free loans to poor women, associated with Prof. Muhammad Yunus, originated in Bangladesh.
2. SHGs became a formal poverty-alleviation tool in India during the Eighth Five-Year Plan.
3. Bank linkage of SHGs in India was pioneered by MYRADA in the mid-1980s.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
37.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh, associated with Muhammad Yunus, gave collateral-free loans to poor women. Statement 2 is wrong: SHGs became a formal poverty tool in the Seventh Plan (1985-90). Statement 3 is correct: MYRADA pioneered SHG bank linkage in the mid-1980s (NABARD's pilot came in 1992). So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
37.tq: SHG in India: 7th Plan; MYRADA mid-1980s; NABARD pilot 1992.

Statement 3 is wrong: the **Grameen Bank** is in **Bangladesh** (**Prof. Muhammad Yunus**) — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: AP: **36%** of national SHG-Bank Linkage share, **99.66%** recovery.
**Velugu** (**2000**) was World Bank-aided and run by **SERP**.
Grameen project began in **1976**; some notes date the SHG concept to **1975**.

37.s:
Assertion (A): TRYSEM was associated with self-employment.
Reason (R): TRYSEM was associated with rural youth.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
37.x: Both are true: TRYSEM trained rural youth for self-employment. Its target group does not explain its aim, so R does not explain A.
37.tq: Ask whether a target group explains an aim.
n: TRYSEM is associated with rural youth and self-employment. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 51-52]

37.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. NREP was associated with rural employment.
II. RLEGP was associated with rural landless employment.
III. JRY resulted from the merger of NREP and RLEGP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
37.x: All three are correct: NREP gave rural work, RLEGP gave work to the rural landless, and the two were merged into JRY in 1989.
37.tq: Recall the schemes merged into JRY.
n: NREP is associated with rural employment. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 51-52]
RLEGP is associated with rural landless employment. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 51-52]
JRY was formed through the merger of NREP and RLEGP. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 51-52]

37.s: IRDP was associated with which of the following?
37.x: IRDP was aimed at rural BPL households. TRYSEM was for rural youth, NREP for rural jobs, and RLEGP for the landless.
37.tq: Match each scheme to its target group.
n: IRDP is associated with rural BPL households. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 51-52]

37.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) First Community Development Programme
(b) First National Extension Service
(c) First National Rural Employment Programme
(d) First National Social Assistance Programme

List-II
(i) 1995
(ii) 1953
(iii) 1952
(iv) 1980
37.x: The Community Development Programme began in 1952, the National Extension Service in 1953, the NREP in 1980 and the NSAP in 1995. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
37.tq: Arrange the welfare programmes in time order.
n: The Community Development Programme was first launched in 1952. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The National Extension Service was first launched in 1953. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The National Rural Employment Programme was first launched in 1980. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The National Social Assistance Programme was first launched in 1995. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]

37.s:
Assertion (A): The First Five-Year Plan was welfare-oriented development.
Reason (R): The First Five-Year Plan covered the period 1951–56.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
37.x: Both are true: the First Plan focused on welfare, and it ran from 1951 to 1956. A date range does not explain a plan's focus, so R does not explain A.
37.tq: Ask whether a date explains a character.
n: The First Five-Year Plan was the first welfare-oriented development plan. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The First Five-Year Plan covered 1951–56. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]

37.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) First poverty alleviation programme
(b) First Integrated Rural Development Programme pilot
(c) First Food Security Programme
(d) First rights-based welfare legislation

List-II
(i) Public Distribution System
(ii) Rural Works Programme of the 1970s
(iii) Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005
(iv) 1976
37.x: The Rural Works Programme (1970s) was the first anti-poverty programme, the IRDP pilot began in 1976, the PDS was the first food-security programme, and MGNREGA (2005) the first rights-based welfare law. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
37.tq: Match each first to its holder.
n: The Rural Works Programme was the first poverty alleviation programme in the 1970s. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Integrated Rural Development Programme was first launched as a pilot programme in 1976. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Public Distribution System was the first Food Security Programme. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was the first rights-based welfare legislation in 2005. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]

37.s:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The first National Health Policy was formulated in 1983.
II. The first National Population Policy was formulated in 1976.
III. The first National Nutrition Policy was formulated in 1993.
37.x: All three are correct: the first National Health Policy came in 1983, the Population Policy in 1976, and the Nutrition Policy in 1993.
37.tq: Recall the first policy years.
n: The National Health Policy was first adopted in 1983. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The National Population Policy was first adopted in 1976. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The National Nutrition Policy was first adopted in 1993. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]

38.s:
With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. The RuPay debit card carries accident insurance cover of ₹2 lakh.
2. The overdraft facility has been raised to ₹10,000.
3. The accident insurance cover was originally ₹5 lakh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: The RuPay card accident cover was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh, and the overdraft limit was raised from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000. Statement 3 is false because the original cover was ₹1 lakh.
38.tq: Split the statements by checking the revised figures against the original figures.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **RuPay** card carries accident cover of **₹2 lakh**.
Statement 2 is correct: overdraft is now **₹10,000** (from **₹5,000**).
