Statement 3 is wrong: the original cover was **₹1 lakh**, not ₹5 lakh — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: After **14 Aug 2018** the focus moved from "every household" to "**every unbanked adult**".
PMJDY accounts: **59.09 crore** (19 Aug 2026); scheme completed **12 years** (Aug 2026).
Women hold **32.92 crore** accounts.

38.s: After 14 August 2018, the focus of the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana shifted from:
o: Rural households to urban households only
Every unbanked adult to every household
Every household to every unbanked adult
38.x: The focus changed from covering every household to covering every unbanked adult.
38.tq: Test the direction of change in a policy target rather than merely recalling both terms.
xs: After **14 Aug 2018**, PMJDY moved from "**every household**" to "**every unbanked adult**", option **(3)**.
Option **(2)** reverses the direction of the shift.
xa: PMJDY was launched on **28 Aug 2014**.
The same 2018 revision raised accident cover to **₹2 lakh** and overdraft to **₹10,000**.
Rural/semi-urban accounts: **45.95 crore** of **59.09 crore**.

38.s:
Which of the following was included in Phase II of the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana during 2015–2018?
1. Overdraft facility
2. Credit Guarantee Fund for overdraft defaults
3. Unorganised-sector pensions under Swavalamban
4. Replacement of RuPay cards by credit cards
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
38.x: Phase II included the overdraft facility, a Credit Guarantee Fund for overdraft defaults and unorganised-sector pensions under Swavalamban. Replacement of RuPay cards by credit cards was not a stated feature.
38.tq: Find the one unrelated policy measure among closely connected programme features.
xs: **Phase II (2015-18)** brought the **overdraft facility**, a **Credit Guarantee Fund for OD defaults** and unorganised-sector pensions (**Swavalamban**) — **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
Replacing **RuPay** cards with credit cards was never part of PMJDY; RuPay remains its debit card.
xa: Overdraft limit: **₹10,000** (from **₹5,000**).
Implementing body: **Department of Financial Services**.

38.s: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched on 28 August 2014 and is implemented by the
38.x: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014 and is implemented by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance. The Department of Economic Affairs, the RBI and NABARD are not its implementing agency.
38.tq: Jan Dhan = DFS, 28 Aug 2014.
xs: PMJDY (launched **28 Aug 2014**) is implemented by the **Department of Financial Services**, option **(2)**.
DFS also administers **PMJJBY** and **PMSBY** (Ministry of Finance).
xa: PMJDY accounts are the "**J**" of the **JAM** trinity — destination for funds.
**PMJJBY**/**PMSBY** premiums are **auto-debited** from PMJDY accounts.
⚠ **NABARD** is linked to SHG-bank linkage, not PMJDY.

38.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the JAM trinity.
List-I (Component)
a. Jan Dhan
b. Aadhaar
c. Mobile
List-II (Role)
i. Communication and intimation channel
ii. Biometric identity for beneficiary verification
iii. Bank account serving as destination for funds
Choose the correct answer:
38.x: Jan Dhan provides the bank account, Aadhaar verifies identity biometrically, and Mobile serves as the communication or intimation channel.
38.tq: Start from the sure pair: Jan Dhan is the bank-account component.
xs: **Jan Dhan – bank account (iii)**, **Aadhaar – biometric identity (ii)**, **Mobile – communication channel (i)**: option **(1)**.
Jan Dhan is the destination for funds; Aadhaar verifies the beneficiary; Mobile intimates.
xa: JAM was first proposed in **Economic Survey 2014-15**.
**PAHAL** (DBT for LPG) was the **first application of JAM**.
DBT was **scaled up in 2015** using the JAM trinity.

38.s: The JAM trinity was first proposed in—
38.x: The JAM trinity was first proposed in the Economic Survey 2014–15.
38.tq: Distinguish the proposal year from the later DBT scale-up year.
xs: The **JAM trinity** was first proposed in **Economic Survey 2014-15**, option **(1)**.
JAM = **Jan Dhan** (account), **Aadhaar** (identity), **Mobile** (communication).
xa: First application: **PAHAL** (DBT for LPG), national launch **1 Jan 2015**.
DBT was piloted on **1 January 2013** and scaled up with JAM in **2015**.
PMJDY itself started on **28 Aug 2014**.

38.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Consent — physical cash withdrawal through ATMs
38.x: The consent layer concerns consent-based data sharing through Account Aggregators, not physical cash withdrawal through ATMs.
38.tq: Find the option that reverses a layer-function relationship.
xs: **Consent — physical cash withdrawal** is wrong: the consent layer is **DEPA / Account Aggregator** data sharing, so option **(1)** is the mismatch.
**Cashless** = **UPI, AePS**; **Paperless** = **DigiLocker/e-Sign**; **Presence-less** = **Aadhaar** authentication — correctly matched.
xa: **AePS** = cash withdrawal at **micro-ATMs**.
**APBS** (Aadhaar Payment Bridge System) routes DBT.
**e-KYC** also sits in the paperless layer.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT):
1. It was piloted on 1 January 2013.
2. The pilot covered 20 schemes in 7 districts.
3. It was scaled up in 2015 using the JAM trinity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: DBT was piloted on 1 January 2013 (UPA-II). Statement 2 is wrong: the pilot covered 7 schemes in 20 districts, not 20 schemes in 7 districts. Statement 3 is correct: DBT was scaled up in 2015 using JAM. Hence '1 and 3 only'; the other options include the wrong statement 2 or leave out a correct one.
38.tq: Watch for swapped numbers: 7 schemes, 20 districts.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: DBT was piloted on **1 January 2013** (UPA-II).
Statement 2 is wrong: the pilot had **7 schemes in 20 districts**, not the reverse.
Statement 3 is correct: DBT was **scaled up in 2015** using **JAM** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: **FY 2024-25**: **₹6.9 lakh crore** across **327 schemes**.
Estimated savings **₹2-3 lakh crore** from removing ghost/duplicate beneficiaries.
Routing via **APBS** + **AePS**.

38.s: PAHAL, the DBT scheme for LPG, was launched nationally on—
38.x: PAHAL was launched nationally on 1 January 2015 and became the first application of JAM for LPG subsidy transfer.
38.tq: Discriminate between the DBT pilot date, PAHAL date and Ujjwala date.
xs: **PAHAL** (DBT for LPG) was launched nationally on **1 January 2015**, option **(2)**.
**1 May 2016** is **Ujjwala**; **1 January 2013** is the **DBT pilot**.
xa: PAHAL was the **first application of JAM**: LPG subsidy paid into accounts.
⚠ **PAHAL** = subsidy DBT (**2015**); **Ujjwala** = free LPG connections (**2016**, **Ballia**).
JAM was proposed in **Economic Survey 2014-15**.

38.s: The principal objective of Ujjwala is to provide—
o: Free LPG connections to women from BPL households and reduce indoor air pollution
LPG cylinders exclusively to Government employees
Free mobile phones to all rural women
Subsidised electricity connections to all urban households
38.x: Ujjwala provides free LPG connections to women belonging to BPL households, with the objective of reducing indoor air pollution.
38.tq: Connect the beneficiary group with the stated environmental and health objective.
xs: **Ujjwala (PMUY)** gives **free LPG connections** to **BPL women** to **cut indoor air pollution**, option **(1)**.
It is not for Government employees, phones or electricity.
xa: Launched **1 May 2016** at **Ballia**.
⚠ **PAHAL** (**2015**) = DBT of LPG **subsidy**; Ujjwala (**2016**) = LPG **connections**.
PAHAL was the first application of **JAM**.

38.s: Which statement about Jeevan Pramaan is correct?
o: It enables pensioners to create a digital life certificate using Aadhaar biometrics and was launched in 2014.
It is an LPG subsidy platform launched in 2015 without Aadhaar authentication.
It is a pension contribution platform available only to minors.
It is an accident insurance scheme launched in 2014 for workers aged 18–70 years.
38.x: Jeevan Pramaan was launched in 2014 and enables pensioners to create a digital life certificate using Aadhaar biometrics.
38.tq: Identify the service from its distinctive function rather than its general pension association.
xs: **Jeevan Pramaan** lets pensioners create a **digital life certificate** using **Aadhaar biometrics**; launched **2014** — option **(1)**.
The LPG subsidy platform is **PAHAL** (2015); minors' pension is **NPS Vatsalya**; the **18-70** accident scheme is **PMSBY**.
xa: Asked in **APPSC 2024**.
NSAP also uses a **Digital Life Certificate** app and the **SAMBAL** app.
Aadhaar risk: **biometric failure** for elderly with worn fingerprints.

38.s: Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 permits Aadhaar to be made a condition for receiving—
o: Subsidies from the Consolidated Fund of India
38.x: Section 7 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 permits Aadhaar to be required for subsidies charged to the Consolidated Fund.
38.tq: Use the exact statutory section and its limited welfare-related scope.
xs: **Sec 7** of the **Aadhaar Act, 2016** makes Aadhaar a condition for subsidies from the **Consolidated Fund**, option **(3)**.
Private use was under **Sec 57**, which **Puttaswamy II** (2018) struck down.
xa: Full name: Aadhaar (**Targeted Delivery** of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act.
**Puttaswamy II** (**2018**, **5 judges**, **4:1**) upheld Sec 7.
**Puttaswamy I** (**2017**, **9 judges**): privacy a fundamental right under **Art. 21**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Puttaswamy judgements:
1. In 2017, a nine-judge Bench held privacy to be a fundamental right under Article 21.
2. In 2018, a five-judge Bench upheld Aadhaar for welfare and subsidies under Section 7.
3. The 2018 judgement struck down private use of Aadhaar under Section 57.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: All three statements are correct. The 2017 nine-judge Bench recognised privacy under Article 21; the 2018 five-judge Bench upheld Aadhaar for welfare under Section 7 and struck down private use under Section 57.
38.tq: Track the two judgements separately by year, Bench strength and outcome.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **2017**, **9 judges**, privacy a fundamental right under **Art. 21**.
Statement 2 is correct: **2018**, **5 judges** upheld Aadhaar for welfare under **Sec 7**.
Statement 3 is correct: the 2018 verdict struck down private use under **Sec 57** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: The 2018 verdict was **4:1**.
⚠ Trap: **9** judges = privacy (2017); **5** judges = Aadhaar (2018).
Aadhaar Act: **2016**.

38.s:
Which of the following is a recognised challenge associated with Aadhaar-enabled service delivery?
1. Exclusion caused by biometric authentication failure, especially for elderly persons and labourers with worn fingerprints.
2. Privacy concerns arising from centralised data.
3. Complete elimination of all identity-verification risks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Biometric failure can exclude elderly persons and labourers with worn fingerprints, while centralised data raises privacy concerns. Aadhaar does not eliminate all identity-verification risks, so statement 3 is false.
38.tq: Reject the extreme claim in statement 3 and retain the two stated challenges.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **exclusion from biometric failure** (worn fingerprints of elderly/labourers) and **privacy of centralised data** are the Aadhaar challenges.
Statement 3 is wrong: Aadhaar does not eliminate all risks — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **Puttaswamy I** (**2017**) made privacy a fundamental right under **Art. 21**.
**Puttaswamy II** (**2018**) struck down private use (**Sec 57**).
Kerala's DBT-over-doorstep pension move raised elderly-delivery concerns (Aug 2026).

38.s: The eShram portal creates a national database of unorganised workers and provides each worker with a:
38.x: The eShram portal is the National Database of Unorganised Workers and provides a Universal Account Number (UAN).
38.tq: Match the portal with its distinctive identification number.
xs: The **eShram** portal gives each unorganised worker a **Universal Account Number (UAN)**, option **(3)**.
eShram (**26 Aug 2021**) is the **National Database of Unorganised Workers**.
xa: **Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act** (**2008**) is now in the **Code on Social Security, 2020**.
The **4** labour codes replaced **29** laws.
Social protection coverage: **64.3%** in **2025** (from **22%** in **2016**).

38.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act was enacted in 2008.
2. It has been subsumed in the Code on Social Security, 2020.
3. The four labour codes together replaced 44 labour laws.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Act dates to 2008. Statement 2 is correct: it is now subsumed in the Code on Social Security, 2020. Statement 3 is wrong: the four labour codes replaced 29 laws. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
38.tq: Remember the pair 4 codes / 29 laws.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act** is of **2008**.
Statement 2 is correct: it is subsumed in the **Code on Social Security, 2020**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **4** codes replaced **29** laws, not 44 — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **eShram** (**26 Aug 2021**) issues a **UAN** to unorganised workers.
**EPF & MP Act** (**1952**) covers establishments with **20 or more** employees.

38.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes PMJJBY from PMSBY?
o: PMJJBY provides accident cover, whereas PMSBY provides old-age pension.
PMJJBY provides life insurance, whereas PMSBY provides accident death and disability cover.
Both schemes provide only disability cover.
Both schemes provide life cover for rural landless households.
38.x: PMJJBY is a one-year renewable term life insurance scheme. PMSBY covers accidental death and disability.
38.tq: Separate the similar-looking schemes by the nature of their cover.
xs: **PMJJBY** is **life insurance**; **PMSBY** gives **accident death and disability** cover — option **(2)**.
Old-age pension is **APY**; rural landless cover is **Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana**.
xa: PMSBY: **18-70**, **₹20**/yr, ₹2 lakh death/full disability, ₹1 lakh partial.
Asked in **G2-GS 2024**: PMJJBY "life", PMSBY "accidental".

38.s: Which one of the following statements regarding PMSBY is correct?
o: It is a pension scheme for unorganised workers.
It covers suicide as an accidental death.
It provides ₹2 lakh for accidental death or total disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability.
38.x: PMSBY provides ₹2 lakh for accidental death or total disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability. It does not cover suicide.
38.tq: Use the benefit amounts and the exclusion to reject neighbouring schemes.
xs: **PMSBY** pays **₹2 lakh** for accidental death/full disability and **₹1 lakh** for **partial disability**, option **(3)**.
It is not a pension; it **does not cover suicide**; **₹30,000 natural death** is **Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana**.
xa: Enrolments: **58.09 crore+** (to Apr 2026).
Both PMSBY and PMJJBY launched on **9 May 2015**.

38.s: Which of the following correctly represents the age band, annual premium and life cover under PMJJBY?
38.x: PMJJBY is a life insurance scheme for persons aged 18–50 years, with an annual premium of ₹436 and cover of ₹2 lakh.
38.tq: Separate PMJJBY from PMSBY by comparing type, age, premium and cover.
xs: **PMJJBY**: age **18-50**, premium **₹436**/yr, cover **₹2 lakh** — option **(2)**.
**₹20** and **18-70** belong to **PMSBY**; **18-59** is Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana.
xa: PMJJBY is a **1-year renewable** life cover; claim settlement **99.95%**.
Enrolments: **27.43 crore+** (to Apr 2026).

38.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Health Insurance Scheme for weavers is correct?
1. It covers a weaver's family of four consisting of the self, spouse and two children.
2. At least 50% of the weaver's income must come from handloom work.
3. Both male and female weavers are eligible.
4. A prescribed age cap is a criterion for eligibility.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: The scheme covers a family of four, requires at least 50% income from handloom work, and admits both male and female weavers. An age cap is not an eligibility criterion, so statement 4 is false.
38.tq: Locate the exception: the apparently plausible age condition is not required.
xs: Statements 1-3 are correct: family of **four** (self, spouse, two children); at least **50%** income from **handloom**; **male and female** weavers eligible.
Statement 4 is wrong: an **age cap was not a criterion** (APPSC 2022) — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: The **Health Insurance Scheme** for handloom weavers dates to **2005-06**.
Life cover: **Mahatma Gandhi Bunkar Bima Yojana** (converged).
⚠ Trap set in **APPSC 2022**: the age-cap criterion.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY):
1. It is administered by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance.
2. Enrolments under it had crossed 34 crore by April 2023.
3. It provides life insurance cover for death due to any cause.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: DFS administers PMSBY, and enrolments reached 34.18 crore by 26 April 2023 (APPSC 2022). Statement 3 is wrong: PMSBY covers only accidental death and disability (and not suicide); death from any cause is covered by PMJJBY.
38.tq: PMSBY = accident only; PMJJBY = life.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: PMSBY is administered by **DFS**, Ministry of Finance.
Statement 2 is correct: enrolments were **34.18 crore** by **26 Apr 2023**.
Statement 3 is wrong: PMSBY covers only **accidental** death/disability (not suicide); life cover is **PMJJBY** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Enrolments reached **58.09 crore+** by Apr 2026.
Premium **₹20**/yr since **1 June 2022**.

38.s: Atal Pension Yojana, launched on 9 May 2015, primarily targets which category of persons?
o: Small and marginal farmers between 40 and 60 years
Unorganised-sector workers in the age group of 18–40 years
38.x: Atal Pension Yojana targets workers in the unorganised sector who enter the scheme between 18 and 40 years of age.
38.tq: Directly identify the target group and entry age of the scheme.
xs: **Atal Pension Yojana** (**9 May 2015**) targets **unorganised-sector workers** aged **18-40**, option **(4)**.
Small and marginal farmers are **PM-KMY**; Central Govt employees are under **NPS/UPS**.
xa: Income-tax payers are excluded.
Administered by **PFRDA**; **8.96 crore** subscribers.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM):
1. It covers unorganised workers aged 18–40 years.
2. The monthly income limit is ₹15,000.
3. The subscriber must already be covered under NPS, ESIC or EPFO.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: PM-SYM covers unorganised workers aged 18–40 years with monthly income up to ₹15,000. It excludes persons covered under NPS, ESIC or EPFO, making statement 3 false.
38.tq: Find the exclusion hidden in statement 3 by reversing the eligibility condition.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **PM-SYM** covers unorganised workers aged **18-40** with income **≤ ₹15,000/month**.
Statement 3 is wrong: those **in NPS/ESIC/EPFO are excluded** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Income-tax payers are also excluded.
Worker + **equal matching** Central share.
Pension **₹3,000**/month at **60**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about PM Kisan Maan-dhan (PM-KMY):
1. It is meant for small and marginal farmers who join between 18 and 40 years of age.
2. The farmer's contribution depends on entry age, ranges from ₹55 to ₹200 per month, and is matched by the Centre.
3. It provides a pension of ₹5,000 per month at the age of 60.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: PM-KMY targets small and marginal farmers aged 18-40. Statement 2 is correct: contribution is age-linked, ₹55-200/month, with matching Central share. Statement 3 is wrong: the pension is ₹3,000 per month at 60 (₹1,000-5,000 is the APY range). So '1 only', '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' are wrong; '1 and 2 only' is right.
38.tq: Maan-dhan schemes (PM-SYM, PM-KMY) pay a flat ₹3,000; only APY has the ₹1,000-5,000 range.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **PM-KMY** is for **small and marginal farmers** joining at **18-40**.
Statement 2 is correct: contribution by entry age, **₹55-200/month**, **matched by the Centre**.
Statement 3 is wrong: pension is **₹3,000**/month at 60 (₹1,000-5,000 is APY) — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Contribution range asked in **APPSC 2019**.
**PM-SYM** gives the same **₹3,000** pension to unorganised workers.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS):
1. It is an option for Central Government employees covered under NPS.
2. It assures a pension of 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months for 25 years of service.
3. Like NPS, it is a purely market-linked defined-contribution scheme without any Government backing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: UPS is an option for Central Government employees under NPS. Statement 2 is correct: assured pension is 50% of average basic pay of the last 12 months for 25 years' service. Statement 3 is wrong: UPS is Government-backed with an assured pension; it is NPS that is defined-contribution and market-linked. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
38.tq: UPS = assured (50%), NPS = market-linked; don't mix the two.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **UPS** is an **option** for **Central Govt employees under NPS**.
Statement 2 is correct: assured pension of **50%** of average basic pay of the **last 12 months** for **25 years'** service.
Statement 3 is wrong: UPS is **Govt-backed**; it is **NPS** that is defined-contribution — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: UPS was launched in **2025**.
NPS is compulsory for Central Govt civilian employees joining on or after **1 Jan 2004**.

38.s: The regulator of the National Pension System and the authority administering Atal Pension Yojana under the NPS architecture is—
38.x: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) regulates NPS and administers APY under the NPS architecture.
38.tq: Apply the ‘who regulates this financial product?’ method.
xs: **PFRDA** regulates **NPS** and administers **APY** under the NPS architecture, option **(3)**.
NPS is compulsory for Central Govt civilian employees joining on or after **1 Jan 2004**.
xa: NPS subscribers grew at **9.5% CAGR**; AUM at **37.3% CAGR** (**FY15-FY25**).
NPS also covers **OCIs**; minors via **NPS Vatsalya**.
APY: **8.96 crore** subscribers; a **Central Sector Scheme**.

38.s: The National Pension System became compulsory for Central Government civilian employees joining on or after—
38.x: NPS is compulsory for Central Government civilian employees who joined service on or after 1 January 2004.
38.tq: Distinguish the exact commencement date from nearby policy dates.
xs: NPS is compulsory for **Central Govt civilian employees joining on or after 1 January 2004**, option **(4)**.
Regulator: **PFRDA**.
xa: NPS is **defined contribution**, market-linked: corpus + annuity.
**UPS** (**2025**) is an assured-pension option for NPS employees.
⚠ Trap: an NPS account **cannot be opened for a third person** (APPSC 2024).

38.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of an NPS account?
o: An account can be opened by one person for any third person.
It is based on defined contribution and market-linked returns.
Minors may participate through NPS Vatsalya.
It may cover Government, private and unorganised-sector participants.
38.x: An NPS account cannot be opened for a third person. The other statements describe features of NPS.
38.tq: Find the statement that reverses the specific account-opening restriction.
xs: An NPS account **cannot be opened for a third person**, so option **(1)** is NOT a feature (APPSC 2024).
NPS is **defined contribution, market-linked**, admits minors via **NPS Vatsalya**, and covers govt, private, unorganised workers and **OCIs**.
xa: Regulator: **PFRDA**.
AUM grew at **37.3% CAGR** (**FY15-FY25**).
Compulsory for Central Govt civilian employees joining on/after **1 Jan 2004**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) under NSAP:
1. It covers severely disabled BPL persons aged 18-79 years with 80% or more disability.
2. It provides ₹200 per month to each beneficiary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: IGNDPS covers BPL persons aged 18-79 with 80%+ disability. Statement 2 is wrong: IGNDPS gives ₹300 per month; ₹200 is the IGNOAPS amount for ages 60-79. So '1 only' is right; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
38.tq: NSAP amounts: old age ₹200 (60-79)/₹500 (80+), disability ₹300.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **IGNDPS** covers severely disabled **BPL** persons aged **18-79** with **80%+** disability.
Statement 2 is wrong: IGNDPS pays **₹300**/month; **₹200** is **IGNOAPS** (60-79) — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: IGNOAPS pays **₹500** at **80+**.
**Annapurna**: free foodgrains (**10 kg/month**) to needy elderly not getting IGNOAPS.
**NSAP**: **15 Aug 1995**, **MoRD**, fulfils **Article 41**; **Core of Core** since **2016**.

38.s: The National Social Assistance Programme was launched in 1995 under the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
38.x: NSAP was launched in 1995 under the Ministry of Rural Development.
38.tq: Use the implementing ministry as the identifying feature of the programme.
xs: **NSAP** was launched on **15 Aug 1995** under the **Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD)**, option **(4)**.
It is a **Centrally Sponsored** scheme for **BPL** households.
xa: Aim: **old age pension to the very poor** (UPPSC 2008).
Fulfils **Article 41**; **Core of Core** scheme since **2016**.
⚠ The **National Maternity Benefit Scheme** left NSAP for **MoHFW** in **2001**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Social Assistance Programme:
1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
2. It fulfils the directive contained in Article 41 of the Constitution.
3. It is intended for Below Poverty Line households.
4. It became a Core of Core scheme from 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: NSAP is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for BPL households, fulfils Article 41 and has been a Core of Core scheme since 2016.
38.tq: When all statements describe separate institutional features, test whether the complete combination is valid.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: NSAP is **Centrally Sponsored**.
Statements 2 and 3 are correct: it fulfils **Article 41** and serves **BPL** households.
Statement 4 is correct: it is a **Core of Core** scheme since **2016** — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
xa: Launched **15 Aug 1995** under **MoRD**.
Scale: about **3.09 crore** beneficiaries; **₹9,652 crore** for **FY 2025-26**.
States add a top-up of **₹50-3,200/month**.

38.s: Under the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme, the monthly central assistance is:
o: ₹200 for 60–79 years and ₹300 for 80 years and above
₹500 for 60–79 years and ₹1,000 for 80 years and above
₹200 for 60–79 years and ₹500 for 80 years and above
₹300 for 60–79 years and ₹500 for 80 years and above
38.x: IGNOAPS provides ₹200 per month to persons aged 60–79 years and ₹500 per month to those aged 80 years and above.
38.tq: Compare the age bands before selecting the corresponding benefit.
xs: **IGNOAPS** pays **₹200**/month at **60-79** years and **₹500** at **80 and above**, option **(3)**.
**₹300** is the **IGNDPS** (disability) amount, not old age.
xa: IGNDPS: BPL persons **18-79** with **80%+** disability.
The pension has lost **nearly half** its real value to inflation (May 2026).
States add a top-up of **₹50-3,200/month**.

38.s: Which of the following is a major criticism concerning the old-age pension under NSAP?
o: Its real value has remained unchanged despite inflation.
Its real value has nearly doubled because of inflation.
Its real value has been reduced by nearly half because of inflation.
It has been converted entirely into a foodgrain benefit.
38.x: Inflation has eroded nearly half of the real value of the NSAP old-age pension.
38.tq: Distinguish nominal assistance from its inflation-adjusted real value.
xs: The NSAP old-age pension has **lost nearly half its real value** to **inflation** (May 2026), option **(3)**.
Its central amount is still **₹200**/month (60-79) and **₹500** (80+).
xa: States top up by **₹50-3,200/month**.
Old-age share is to rise **10.1% to 14.9%** (**2021-2036**) — more pension demand.
**Kerala**'s DBT move for pensions drew protests (Aug 2026).

38.s: The controversy in Kerala regarding pension delivery primarily concerned the choice between:
o: Bank accounts and postal savings certificates
DBT and doorstep delivery for elderly beneficiaries
38.x: Kerala’s decision to end doorstep pension delivery for DBT led to protests, highlighting the tension between digital transfers and doorstep delivery for the elderly.
38.tq: Identify the two alternative delivery mechanisms at the centre of the policy debate.
xs: **Kerala**'s move to end **doorstep pension delivery** in favour of **DBT** drew protests (8 and 11 Aug 2026): the debate is **DBT vs doorstep delivery for elderly**, option **(4)**.
It is not about private insurance, foodgrains or postal certificates — only the **delivery channel** for pensions.
xa: DBT in **FY 2024-25**: **₹6.9 lakh crore** across **327 schemes**.
Aadhaar risk: **biometric failure** for elderly with worn fingerprints.
**Jeevan Pramaan** (**2014**) lets pensioners give a **digital life certificate**.

39.s: According to the World Food Summit, 1996, food security exists when all people, at all times, have physical and economic access to which of the following?
o: Food of their choice irrespective of dietary needs
Adequate food supplied exclusively by the government
Sufficient, safe and nutritious food for an active and healthy life
Food grains available only during periods of shortage
39.x: The World Food Summit definition emphasizes physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food for an active and healthy life.
39.tq: Use the precise official definition and reject the look-alike phrase ‘food of their choice’.
xs: Per the **World Food Summit 1996** (FAO), food security means access to **sufficient, safe and nutritious food** for an **active and healthy life**, option **(3)**.
⚠ It does **not** mean food "**of their choice**" — a trap set in **APPSC G2 2017**; nor does it require supply only by government.
xa: The definition says **all people, at all times**, with **physical and economic access**.
Four dimensions: **availability, access (affordability), utilisation/absorption, stability**.
India achieved **national** food security (buffer stocks) without fully assuring **household** food security — hence **PDS** and **NFSA**.

39.s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognized dimension of food security?
39.x: Availability, accessibility, affordability or access, utilisation/absorption and stability are associated with food security. Accountability is not a dimension.
39.tq: Find the odd term among the established dimensions.
xs: **Accountability** is **not** a dimension of food security, option **(2)** (UPPSC 2025 trap).
**Stability**, **accessibility** and **availability** are recognised dimensions, along with **affordability** and **absorption/utilisation**.
xa: **Availability** = production + imports + previous stocks.
**Absorption/utilisation** = the body's ability to use the food.
Price and quantity of exports are also **not** dimensions.

39.s:
Assertion (A): Food security remains necessary even in years of food surplus.
Reason (R): Starvation may result from unequal distribution even when aggregate food availability is adequate.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
39.x: Both statements are true, and unequal distribution explains why aggregate surplus does not automatically ensure household food security.
39.tq: Test whether the reason explains the distinction between national and household security.
xs: **Both A and R are true** and R is the **correct explanation** of A, option **(1)** (UPPSC 2025).
Starvation can come from **unequal distribution**, so food security is needed **even in surplus years**.
xa: This is **Amartya Sen**'s **entitlement** idea (**Poverty and Famines, 1981**).
Famines arise from collapse of **entitlements** (income, exchange, transfers), not merely a fall in supply.
Households unable to afford the **ICMR-NIN** diet fell from about **52% (2011-12)** to **25% (2023-24)**.

39.s: According to Amartya Sen's entitlement approach, famines primarily arise from:
o: A fall in aggregate food production in every case
An increase in the nutritional content of food
Excessive buffer stocks maintained by the government
A collapse of people's command over food through income, exchange and transfers
39.x: Sen argued that famine results from a collapse of people's entitlements or command over food, not merely from a decline in overall food availability.
39.tq: Reject the supply-only explanation and apply the income-and-entitlement concept.
xs: For **Sen**, famines arise from a **collapse of people's command over food through income, exchange and transfers** (entitlements), option **(4)**.
He rejected the view that a **fall in food availability/supply** alone causes famine.
xa: Book: **Poverty and Famines**, **1981**.
⚠ Sen = **entitlement**, not availability.
The **Bengal Famine of 1943** (about **30 lakh** deaths) is the classic backdrop.

39.s: Which of the following best distinguishes national food security from household food security?
o: National food security concerns only imports, whereas household food security concerns only domestic production.
National food security concerns aggregate availability, whereas household food security concerns actual access and affordability for each household.
National food security applies to urban areas, whereas household food security applies only to rural areas.
National food security is based on nutrition, whereas household food security is based only on buffer stocks.
39.x: National food security refers to adequate aggregate production and stocks. Household food security requires that each household can actually obtain and afford food.
39.tq: Split the comparison into aggregate availability versus household-level access.
xs: **National** food security = **aggregate production/availability + buffer stock**; **household** = each household can **access and afford** food — option **(2)**.
Neither is defined by urban/rural or by imports alone.
xa: India achieved national food security without fully assuring household — hence **PDS** and **NFSA**.
**Affordability** = money enough for sufficient, safe, nutritious food.
**Accessibility** = food within reach of every person.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about buffer stocks in India:
1. FCI procures wheat and rice from surplus states at the pre-announced MSP fixed on CACP advice.
2. The strategic reserve is about 10 million tonnes above operational stocks.
3. OMSS (Domestic) sales are used to cool market prices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: FCI procures at MSP announced on CACP advice. Statement 2 is wrong: the strategic reserve is 5 million tonnes above operational stocks. Statement 3 is correct: OMSS (Domestic) sales cool prices. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
39.tq: Strategic reserve = 5 MT; procurement chain = CACP advises, Govt announces MSP, FCI buys.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **FCI** procures wheat and rice at **MSP** set on **CACP** advice.
Statement 2 is wrong: the strategic reserve is **5 million tonnes** above operational stocks, not 10.
Statement 3 is correct: **OMSS (Domestic)** sales cool prices — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Grain is sold at the lower **issue price** in deficit areas and calamities.
⚠ Norms fixed by **CCEA**; MSP by **CACP**; procurement by **FCI**.

39.s: Buffer stocks in India were formally introduced during the:
39.x: Buffer stocks were formally introduced during the Fourth Five-Year Plan, covering 1969–74.
39.tq: Link the policy innovation with its Five-Year Plan period.
xs: Buffer stocks were formally introduced in the **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74)**, option **(3)**.
The earlier and later Plans are not linked to buffer stocks in the notes.
xa: Minimum buffer norms are fixed by the **CCEA** for each quarter.
**Strategic reserve**: **5 million tonnes** above operational stocks.
**PDS** is older — a **World War II rationing** measure of the 1940s.

39.s: Which body fixes the minimum buffer stock levels for each quarter?
o: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
39.x: The minimum buffer stock levels are fixed by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs and specified for each quarter.
39.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the authority.
xs: Minimum buffer levels are fixed by the **Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)**, option **(2)**.
They are set for each quarter: **1 April, 1 July, 1 October, 1 January**.
xa: ⚠ **CACP** advises MSP; **FCI** procures; **CCEA** sets norms.
Stocks: about **602 LMT**, around **3 times** the norms.
**OMSS** lets FCI sell surplus grain in the open market.

39.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective or effect of the Open Market Sale Scheme?
o: Replacing the Food Corporation of India’s procurement function with private procurement
Offloading excess central-pool stocks and reducing carrying costs
Raising grain supply during lean seasons and in deficit regions
39.x: OMSS involves FCI selling surplus central-pool grain at predetermined prices. It raises supply, moderates prices, offloads excess stocks and reduces carrying costs, but it does not replace FCI procurement with private procurement.
39.tq: Find the option that introduces a function not belonging to the scheme.
xs: **OMSS** does **not replace FCI procurement** with private procurement, so option **(1)** is the odd one.
Under OMSS, **FCI** sells surplus central-pool grain at **predetermined prices**.
Its purposes: **raise supply** in lean seasons/deficit regions, **moderate prices**, **offload excess stock**, **cut carrying cost**.
xa: **OMSS (Domestic)** sales are used to cool prices.
FCI was created by the **Food Corporations Act 1964**.
Stocks about **602 LMT** (around **3 times** norms) make OMSS sales possible.

39.s:
Arrange the following developments in the Public Distribution System in chronological order:
A. Targeted Public Distribution System
B. Revamped Public Distribution System
C. National Food Security Act
D. Initial Public Distribution System
Select the correct sequence.
39.x: The sequence is initial PDS in the 1940s, RPDS in June 1992, TPDS in June 1997 and NFSA in 2013.
39.tq: Fix the earliest PDS stage first and then place the dated reforms.
xs: Order **D, B, A, C**: initial **PDS** (1940s) → **RPDS** (**June 1992**) → **TPDS** (**June 1997**) → **NFSA 2013**, option **(1)**.
RPDS covered **1,775 blocks**; TPDS split **BPL/APL**.
xa: Next: **PMGKAY 2020** → free NFSA grain from **2023**.
PDS began as a **World War II rationing** measure.
NFSA commenced in **July 2013**.

39.s: The Public Distribution System in India originated primarily as:
o: A World War II rationing measure
A replacement for the Integrated Child Development Services
39.x: The PDS began as a rationing measure during the Second World War, against the background of the Bengal famine.
39.tq: Use the historical origin rather than the later institutional form of the programme.
xs: PDS began as a **World War II rationing** measure in the 1940s, option **(1)**.
The **Bengal famine** (**1943**) was its backdrop.
xa: The **Essential Commodities Act 1955** is the base for PDS control orders.
**ICDS** (**1975**) is a separate nutrition scheme, not a PDS replacement.

39.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
a. PDS
b. ICDS
c. Mid-Day Meal/PM POSHAN
d. Food-for-Work

List-II (Food support)
i. Grain as wages
ii. Supplementary nutrition at anganwadis
iii. Subsidised or free grain through Fair Price Shops
iv. Hot cooked meal to eligible school-age children

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: PDS provides grain through Fair Price Shops; ICDS gives supplementary nutrition at anganwadis; PM POSHAN gives hot cooked meals; Food-for-Work gives grain as wages.
39.tq: Start with the sure pair ‘Food-for-Work—grain as wages’ and eliminate the codes.
xs: **PDS – grain via Fair Price Shops (iii)**, **ICDS – nutrition at anganwadis (ii)**, **PM POSHAN – hot cooked meal (iv)**, **Food-for-Work – grain as wages (i)**: option **(1)**.
A PYQ answer: all of these give food-based support — "**all of the above**".
xa: **ICDS** began in **1975** (experimental).
**Food-for-Work** was introduced in **1977-78**.
**PM POSHAN** is under the **Ministry of Education**.

39.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
39.x: TPDS was introduced in June 1997, not 1985. ICDS began in 1975, Mid-Day Meal in 1995, and Food-for-Work in 1977–78.
39.tq: Check each programme against its launch year and identify the swapped date.
xs: **Targeted Public Distribution System** (TPDS) began in **June 1997**, not 1985, so option **(4)** is the wrong pair.
**Food-for-Work 1977-78**, **ICDS 1975** and **Mid-Day Meal 1995** are correct.
xa: **RPDS** came earlier, in **June 1992** (**1,775** blocks).
TPDS introduced the **BPL/APL** split.
Mid-Day Meal is now **PM POSHAN** (Ministry of Education).

39.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013:
1. It gives a legal, justiciable right to subsidised foodgrains.
2. It commenced in July 2014.
3. It is administered by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution (DFPD).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: NFSA confers a legal, justiciable right to subsidised grain. Statement 2 is wrong: the Act commenced in July 2013 ('NFSA 2014' is a known distractor). Statement 3 is correct: DFPD under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and PD administers it. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
39.tq: The year is in the name: NFSA 2013, commenced July 2013.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **NFSA** gives a **legal, justiciable right** to subsidised foodgrains.
Statement 2 is wrong: it commenced in **July 2013** ("**NFSA 2014**" is a known distractor).
Statement 3 is correct: it is run by **DFPD**, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and PD — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Coverage: up to **75% rural** + **50% urban** ≈ **two-thirds**.
~**80-81 crore** beneficiaries.

39.s: The combined NFSA coverage of up to 75 per cent of the rural population and 50 per cent of the urban population is approximately equal to:
39.x: The prescribed rural and urban coverage together amount to approximately two-thirds, or about 67 per cent, of India’s population.
39.tq: Translate separate coverage percentages into the broad national proportion.
xs: **75% rural + 50% urban** comes to about **two-thirds (≈67%)** of India's population, option **(3)**.
It is neither the whole population nor one-half.
xa: ~**80-81 crore** beneficiaries.
⚠ Exam angle: rural answer **75%**, urban **50%**.
NFSA is administered by **DFPD**.

39.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the entitlement of an Antyodaya Anna Yojana household under the NFSA?
o: 7 kg per person without any household ceiling
39.x: An AAY household is entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains per household per month under the NFSA framework.
39.tq: Watch the distinction between person-based and household-based quantities.
xs: An **AAY** household gets **35 kg per household per month**, option **(4)**.
**5 kg per person** is the **PHH** entitlement; **7 kg per person** is the 2026 draft proposal — and that keeps a **35 kg** cap.
xa: ⚠ PHH = **per person**; AAY = **per household**.
AAY grain is now **free** under **PMGKAY**.
AP: AAY **35 kg/card**, free.

39.s: For the purpose of issuing a ration card under the NFSA, the head of the household should ordinarily be:
o: The eldest male member irrespective of age
The person holding the Aadhaar card with the highest income
The eldest woman who is at least 18 years old
39.x: The eldest woman of the household, provided she is 18 years or older, is treated as the head for issuing the ration card.
39.tq: Apply the women-empowerment provision precisely, including the minimum age condition.
xs: The **eldest woman (18+)** is head of household for ration cards under NFSA, option **(4)**.
This is NFSA's **women empowerment** provision.
xa: Maternity benefit (**Sec 4**): free meal + at least **₹6,000**.
PHH: **5 kg per person per month**; AAY: **35 kg per household**.
Ration card and FPS operations follow the **TPDS (Control) Order 2015**.

39.s: The draft National Food Security (Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposes to replace the AAY household entitlement with:
o: 7 kg per person, subject to an overall ceiling of 35 kg per household
35 kg per person, subject to an overall ceiling of 70 kg per household
10 kg per household, subject to a ceiling of 50 kg
5 kg per person, without a household ceiling
39.x: The draft Bill proposes 7 kg per person for AAY households, while retaining an overall cap of 35 kg per household.
39.tq: Read both parts of the proposed formula: the per-person figure and the household cap.
xs: The **draft NFS (Amendment) Bill, 2026** proposes **7 kg per person**, capped at **35 kg per household**, for AAY — option **(1)**.
It amends the first proviso to **Section 3(1)**.
xa: Released by **DFPD**, published **24 June 2026**; comments till **13 July**.
Aim: end the inequity where **small households get more per head**.
Opposed by **Tamil Nadu**, **Kerala** and **CPI(M)**.

39.s: The proposed amendment to the AAY entitlement is intended principally to address which issue?
o: The inequity whereby smaller households receive more foodgrains per head
The shortage of Aadhaar-seeded ration cards
The lack of portability between States
The rising economic cost of foodgrain procurement
39.x: The stated aim is to remove the inequity under which smaller AAY households receive a greater quantity per person when the entitlement is fixed per household.
39.tq: Identify the policy rationale rather than confusing it with digitisation, portability or procurement issues.
xs: The amendment aims to remove the inequity whereby **smaller households get more per head**, option **(1)**.
A fixed **35 kg per household** gives a small family more grain per person.
xa: New rule: **7 kg per person**, capped at **35 kg**.
Opposed by **Tamil Nadu**, **Kerala** and **CPI(M)** (10 Jul 2026).
Draft published **24 June 2026** by **DFPD**.

39.s: Under the NFSA, pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to:
o: Only subsidised wheat through Fair Price Shops
A monthly cash transfer of exactly ₹10,000 without food support
A take-home ration only after the child reaches six years
A free meal and a maternity benefit of at least ₹6,000
39.x: NFSA provides pregnant women and lactating mothers a free meal along with a maternity benefit of at least ₹6,000.
39.tq: Test the entitlement package as a combination of food support and maternity benefit.
xs: Pregnant women and lactating mothers get a **free meal** and a **maternity benefit of at least ₹6,000**, option **(4)**.
This is NFSA **Sec 4**.
xa: ⚠ **Sec 4** = maternity; **Sec 15** = DGRO; **Sec 16** = State Food Commission.
Children **6 months - 6 years**: take-home ration or hot meal through **ICDS/Anganwadi**.
Children **6-14**: mid-day meal in school.

39.s: Children in the age group of 6 months to 6 years are entitled under the NFSA to:
o: A take-home ration or hot meal through ICDS/anganwadi services
Only a school meal under PM POSHAN
39.x: Children aged 6 months to 6 years receive a take-home ration or hot meal through ICDS and anganwadi services.
39.tq: Separate the NFSA entitlement by age group and delivery channel.
xs: Children **6 months - 6 years** get a **take-home ration or hot meal** through **ICDS/Anganwadi**, option **(1)**.
School meals (**PM POSHAN**) are for ages **6-14**; grain as wages is **Food-for-Work**.
xa: ICDS began in **1975**.
Mothers get a free meal + at least **₹6,000** maternity benefit.
AP is exploring **convergence with Anganwadi and MDM**.

39.s: Under NFSA, a Priority Household is entitled to:
o: 35 kg per household per month free of cost in all cases
7 kg per household per month at the market price
10 kg per person per month at a uniform price of ₹5
5 kg per person per month at ₹3/₹2/₹1 for rice, wheat and coarse grain respectively
39.x: PHH entitlement is 5 kg per person per month. The issue prices are ₹3 for rice, ₹2 for wheat and ₹1 for coarse grain.
39.tq: Keep the unit, quantity and commodity-wise prices together to avoid mixing NFSA and AAY provisions.
xs: A **PHH** gets **5 kg per person per month** at **Rs 3 rice / Rs 2 wheat / Rs 1 coarse grains**, option **(4)**.
**35 kg per household** is **AAY**; **7 kg** is the 2026 draft AAY proposal.
xa: Issue prices **3/2/1** have **not been revised since July 2013**.
Now all NFSA grain is **free** (PMGKAY merger, **1 January 2023**).
AP: PHH **5 kg/unit** rice, free; wheat **1 kg/card** at **Rs 16/kg**.

39.s: The stated objective of the National Food Security Act, 2013 is to provide:
o: Food and nutritional security by ensuring access to adequate quality food at affordable prices so that people can live a life with dignity
A guaranteed 100 days of wage employment to every rural household
Procurement of all foodgrains produced in India at the Minimum Support Price
A Public Distribution System Act replacing the Food Corporations Act, 1964
39.x: The NFSA, 2013 aims at food and nutritional security at affordable prices so people live with dignity (APPSC 2025). Wage employment is MGNREGA's aim; the Act does not guarantee MSP procurement of all grain; 'PDS Act' and 'FCI Act' were the distractors in the exam.
39.tq: NFSA = food + nutrition + affordable prices + dignity.
xs: NFSA 2013 aims at **food and nutritional security** at **affordable prices** so people **live with dignity**, option **(1)** (APPSC 2025).
It does not promise wage employment or MSP procurement of all grain; "**PDS Act**" and "**FCI Act**" were exam distractors.
xa: FCI was created by the **Food Corporations Act 1964**.
NFSA gives a **legal, justiciable right**; commenced **July 2013**.
**Article 47** (DPSP): duty to raise nutrition and the standard of living.

39.s: Under the National Food Security Act, 2013, up to what percentage of the rural population is covered for subsidised foodgrains?
39.x: NFSA covers up to 75% of the rural population (asked in APPSC G2 2017). 50% is the urban ceiling, about 67% (two-thirds) is the combined national coverage, and 90% is not a ceiling under the Act.
39.tq: Rural 75, urban 50, together about two-thirds.
xs: NFSA covers up to **75 per cent** of the **rural** population, option **(3)** (APPSC G2 2017).
**50%** is the urban ceiling; **67%** (two-thirds) is the combined coverage.
xa: ~**80-81 crore** beneficiaries.
Ministry: Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution (**DFPD**).
Legal right commenced **July 2013**.

39.s:
With reference to grievance redress under the NFSA, consider the following statements:
1. An internal grievance-redress mechanism is provided.
2. A District Grievance Redressal Officer is provided under Section 15.
3. A State Food Commission is constituted in every State to monitor implementation and hear appeals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All three statements are correct. The NFSA provides an internal mechanism and District Grievance Redressal Officers, while State Food Commissions monitor implementation and hear appeals.
39.tq: Check the institutional chain from the internal mechanism to district and State-level bodies.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: NFSA has an **internal grievance mechanism**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Sec 15** provides a **District Grievance Redressal Officer**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Sec 16** sets up a **State Food Commission** in every State to monitor and hear appeals — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: One DGRO in each district.
Transparency: **Vigilance Committees**, **social audits**, disclosure of PDS records.

39.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NFSA grievance machinery:
1. A State Food Commission is provided in each State.
2. An existing commission may be designated as the State Food Commission.
3. Public servants failing to comply with relief recommended by the DGRO may be penalised.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All three statements are correct. Each State has a State Food Commission, an existing body may be designated to avoid new costs, and non-compliance with DGRO recommendations can attract penalties.
39.tq: Test the composition, cost-saving provision and enforcement consequence together.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: a **State Food Commission** in **every State** (**Sec 16**).
Statement 2 is correct: an **existing commission may be designated** to avoid new set-up costs.
Statement 3 is correct: public servants ignoring **DGRO**-recommended relief can be **penalised** — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: DGRO is under **Sec 15**; one in each district.
⚠ **Sec 4** = maternity benefit.

39.s:
Which of the following measures strengthens transparency and social accountability in the Public Distribution System under the NFSA framework?
1. Social audits
2. Mandatory disclosure of PDS records
3. Vigilance committees
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: Social audits, mandatory disclosure of PDS records and vigilance committees are all accountability mechanisms under the NFSA framework.
39.tq: Recognise the combination of transparency and community-monitoring mechanisms.
xs: **Social audits**, **mandatory disclosure of PDS records** and **Vigilance Committees** are all NFSA transparency tools — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
All three strengthen accountability of the Fair Price Shop system.
xa: Vigilance Committees: **state, district, block and FPS** levels.
**DGRO** (Sec 15) and **State Food Commission** (Sec 16) handle grievances.
AP: **98%** Aadhaar-linked ration cards.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY):
1. It was launched in 2020 as part of the COVID-19/Atmanirbhar package.
2. At launch it gave 5 kg of free grain per household in place of the NFSA entitlement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: PMGKAY began in 2020 under the COVID/Atmanirbhar package. Statement 2 is wrong: it gave 5 kg free grain per person, on top of (not in place of) the NFSA entitlement. Hence '1 only'.
39.tq: PMGKAY at launch: per person, over and above NFSA.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **PMGKAY** began in **2020** under the **Atmanirbhar/COVID** package.
Statement 2 is wrong: it gave **5 kg free grain per person**, **on top of** the NFSA entitlement — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: From **1 January 2023** PMGKAY **subsumed** NFSA: whole allocation **free**.
Extended **5 years**: **1 Jan 2024 – 31 Dec 2028**.
Cost about **Rs 11.80 lakh crore**, borne by the Centre.

39.s: From 1 January 2023, PMGKAY was subsumed with the NFSA entitlement. What was the principal effect of this decision?
o: The entitlement was converted into a cash transfer
NFSA allocations were discontinued for all beneficiaries
The entire NFSA allocation became free of cost
Only the APL category received free grain
39.x: From 1 January 2023, the entire NFSA allocation became free under the merged arrangement described as ‘One Nation–One Price–One Ration’.
39.tq: Test the policy change after merger rather than the original launch feature.
xs: From **1 January 2023** the **entire NFSA allocation became free**, option **(3)** ("One Nation-One Price-One Ration").
It was not converted to cash and allocations continued.
xa: Extension: **1 Jan 2024 – 31 Dec 2028**, about **Rs 11.80 lakh crore**.
Issue prices **Rs 3/2/1** were never revised since **July 2013**.
Food subsidy (Budget **2026-27**): **Rs 2,27,629 crore**.

39.s: For which period was the free food-grain arrangement under the extended PMGKAY continued?
39.x: The arrangement was extended for five years from 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2028.
39.tq: Use both boundary dates to distinguish the five-year extension.
xs: Extended PMGKAY runs **5 years**, **1 January 2024 to 31 December 2028**, option **(1)**.
Cost about **Rs 11.80 lakh crore**, borne by the **Centre**.
xa: PMGKAY began in **2020** (5 kg free per person).
Merged with NFSA from **1 January 2023**.
Food subsidy (Budget **2026-27**): **Rs 2,27,629 crore**.

39.s: Bharat-brand atta, rice and dal are sold through which combination of channels as a consumer price intervention?
o: Only State Food Commissions and Fair Price Shops
Only private supermarkets licensed by NITI Aayog
NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets and mobile vans
FCI warehouses and commercial banks only
39.x: Bharat-brand atta, rice and dal are sold at subsidised retail prices through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets, as well as mobile vans.
39.tq: Match the intervention with its complete distribution-channel combination.
xs: **Bharat brand** atta, rice and dal are sold through **NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar** outlets and **mobile vans**, option **(3)**.
It is a **consumer price intervention**, outside Fair Price Shops.
xa: **NCCF**: set up in **1965**, under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & PD.
**OMSS** is FCI's open-market route to cool grain prices.
AP's **Mee Mart** (with **NCCF**) sells items **Rs 3-5** below market.

39.s: The National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India (NCCF) was set up in ____ and functions under the ____.
o: 1965; Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
1965; Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
1955; Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
39.x: NCCF was set up in 1965 under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and PD, so A is right. B has the wrong ministry; C has the wrong year (1955 is the Essential Commodities Act); D has both wrong.
39.tq: Don't confuse NCCF (1965) with the Essential Commodities Act (1955) or the Food Corporations Act (1964).
xs: **NCCF** was set up in **1965** under the **Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution**, option **(1)**.
⚠ **1955** is the **Essential Commodities Act**, not NCCF.
xa: NCCF **procures essential goods** and runs **price-stabilisation** operations.
It is a Bharat-brand channel with **NAFED** and **Kendriya Bhandar**.
AP **Mee Mart** is a Civil Supplies + **NCCF** partnership; first outlet **Lalupuram near Guntur**.

39.s:
Consider the following statements regarding objections raised against the Global Hunger Index:
1. Three of its four indicators concern children only.
2. The undernourishment estimate is based on a small opinion-poll-type sample.
3. The index uses only income-based indicators.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: The objections relate to the child focus of three indicators and the small opinion-poll-type sample used for the undernourishment figure. The index does not use only income-based indicators.
39.tq: Reject the absolute and unrelated description in statement 3.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **three of the four** GHI indicators concern **children only**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **undernourishment** figure comes from a **small opinion-poll-type sample**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the index is not income-based — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: These are India's objections to both **GHI** and **FAO SOFI** indicators.
Households unable to afford the ICMR-NIN diet: about **52%** (2011-12) → **25%** (2023-24).
⚠ Food-security dimensions: **availability, access, utilisation/absorption, stability** — "accountability" is not one.

39.s:
Consider the following statements regarding food entitlements under the Andhra Pradesh PDS:
1. A Priority Household receives 5 kg of rice per unit free of cost.
2. An Antyodaya Anna Yojana household receives 35 kg of rice per card free of cost.
3. Wheat is supplied at 1 kg per card at Rs 16 per kg.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All three statements are correct. PHH entitlement is 5 kg per unit, AAY entitlement is 35 kg per card, and wheat is supplied at 1 kg per card at Rs 16 per kg.
39.tq: Check each entitlement separately before selecting the combined code.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: AP **PHH** gets **5 kg/unit rice, free**.
Statement 2 is correct: **AAY** gets **35 kg/card, free**.
Statement 3 is correct: **wheat 1 kg/card at Rs 16/kg** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: **Ragi** (all) / **Jowar** (Rayalaseema): up to **3 kg/card**, free, in lieu of rice.
Under NFSA the Act price was **Rs 3/2/1**, unrevised since **July 2013**; all NFSA grain is free since **1 January 2023**.

39.s: Which of the following correctly describes the millet entitlement under the Andhra Pradesh PDS?
o: 35 kg of ragi per card for AAY households only
Up to 3 kg per card of ragi for all areas and jowar in Rayalaseema, free of cost, in lieu of rice
5 kg of jowar per unit for PHH households at the market price
3 kg per unit of wheat throughout Andhra Pradesh at Rs 16 per kg
39.x: Ragi for all areas and jowar in Rayalaseema may be supplied up to 3 kg per card free of cost in lieu of rice.
39.tq: Discriminate between commodity, region, quantity and mode of substitution.
xs: AP gives **ragi** (all areas) and **jowar** (**Rayalaseema**) up to **3 kg per card**, **free**, **in lieu of rice**, option **(2)**.
**35 kg** is the **AAY** rice entitlement; wheat is **1 kg/card** at **Rs 16/kg**.
xa: PHH: **5 kg/unit** rice, free.
AP is exploring a wider basket: **pulses, oil, fortified foods**.
Doorstep delivery via **Mobile Dispensing Units** (launched **2021**).

39.s: Mee Mart in Andhra Pradesh is proposed to be linked with which of the following for subsidy delivery?
o: Digital Rupee or Central Bank Digital Currency
39.x: Mee Mart is proposed to be linked with the Digital Rupee, or CBDC, for a digital food-subsidy model.
39.tq: Identify the exact digital-payment instrument rather than a related digital platform.
xs: Mee Mart is to be linked with the **Digital Rupee (CBDC)** subsidy, option **(1)**.
A **Digital Rupee food-subsidy model** is also being piloted nationally.
xa: Partners: AP Civil Supplies Dept + **NCCF**.
First outlet: **Lalupuram near Guntur**.
AP is also exploring **DBT** and a wider PDS basket.

39.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Law or body)
 a. National Food Security Act, 2013
 b. Essential Commodities Act, 1955
 c. Food Corporations Act, 1964
 d. Article 47

List-II (Purpose)
 i. Duty to raise nutrition and the standard of living
 ii. Creation of the Food Corporation of India
 iii. Legal right to subsidised grain and food security with dignity
 iv. Control of production, supply, price and stocks of essential goods

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: NFSA provides the legal right to subsidised grain; the Essential Commodities Act regulates essential goods; the Food Corporations Act created FCI; and Article 47 concerns nutrition and living standards.
39.tq: Start from the sure institutional pair and eliminate codes containing mismatches.
xs: **NFSA 2013 – legal right to grain (iii)**, **Essential Commodities Act 1955 – control of essential goods (iv)**, **Food Corporations Act 1964 – creates FCI (ii)**, **Article 47 – nutrition (i)**: option **(1)**.
FCI does procurement, storage and distribution.
xa: The Essential Commodities Act is the base for **PDS control orders**.
**TPDS (Control) Order 2015**: rules for ration cards and FPS.
Article 47 is a **DPSP**.

39.s: Which of the following is a stated criticism of the present food subsidy framework?
o: Issue prices have remained frozen since 2013 while subsidy costs have risen.
The NFSA excludes all rural households from food support.
The PDS supplies only imported foodgrains and no domestic cereals.
Issue prices have increased every year while subsidies have been abolished.
39.x: A criticism is that issue prices have been frozen since 2013 even as the subsidy burden has increased.
39.tq: Identify the precise trend and avoid reversed or extreme statements.
xs: A key criticism: **issue prices frozen since 2013** while **subsidy** keeps rising, option **(1)**.
NFSA issue prices **Rs 3/2/1** were **not revised since July 2013** though MSP and economic cost rise.
xa: Food subsidy (Budget **2026-27**): **Rs 2,27,629 crore**.
PMGKAY extension costs about **Rs 11.80 lakh crore** (**2024-2028**).
NFSA covers **75% rural** and **50% urban** — not excluding rural households.

39.s: Which combination reflects the suggested expansion of the food-security basket and related convergence in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Imported wheat alone, with convergence with commercial banks
Sugar and petroleum, with convergence with the GST Council
Pulses, oil and fortified foods, with convergence with Anganwadi and MDM
Only cereals, with convergence limited to stock exchanges
39.x: Andhra Pradesh is exploring a wider PDS basket including pulses, oil and fortified foods, along with convergence with Anganwadi and the Mid-Day Meal programme.
39.tq: Apply the policy proposal to the correct commodities and linked programmes.
xs: AP is exploring a wider PDS basket — **pulses, oil, fortified foods** — with **convergence with Anganwadi and MDM**, option **(3)**.
AP is also exploring **DBT**.
xa: **Mee Mart** links PDS to the **Digital Rupee**.
AP already gives **ragi/jowar** up to **3 kg/card** in lieu of rice.
**ICDS/Anganwadi** serves children **0-6**; **MDM/PM POSHAN** serves school children.

39.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes poverty, hunger and unaffordability of a healthy diet?
o: They are unrelated and cannot occur together.
Only hunger has any connection with food affordability.
They are identical concepts and always affect exactly the same households.
They overlap but are not identical concepts.
39.x: Poverty, hunger and unaffordability of a healthy diet overlap in many cases, but they are not identical concepts.
39.tq: Discriminate between related concepts without treating them as synonyms.
xs: **Poverty, hunger and unaffordability of a healthy diet** **overlap but are not identical**, option **(4)**.
So the same household need not show all three.
xa: Unaffordability of the **ICMR-NIN** diet: about **25%** (**2023-24**).
**Sen**: starvation can arise from **unequal distribution** even in surplus years.
Multiple measures (GHI, SOFI) are disputed by India.

40.s: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee, which reviewed the Community Development Programme and National Extension Service, submitted its report in:
40.x: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee reviewed the Community Development Programme and National Extension Service and submitted its report in November 1957.
40.tq: Pair the committee with both its subject of review and its exact reporting year.
xs: The **Balwantrai Mehta Committee** reviewed **CDP and NES** and reported in **November 1957**, option **(3)**.
**1952** is the year of CDP itself, and **1974** is the **Minimum Needs Programme**.
xa: CDP began in **1952**, NES in **1953**.
CDP is the **first** rural development programme.
The topic's basis is **Unit 10 Decentralisation**.

40.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. SGSY
B. Community Development Programme
C. Bharat Nirman
D. Food for Work
40.x: The correct sequence is Community Development Programme (1952), Food for Work (1977–78), SGSY (1999), and Bharat Nirman (2005).
40.tq: Place the earliest and latest programmes first, then resolve the middle sequence by year.
xs: Order **B, D, A, C**: **CDP (1952)** → **Food for Work (1977-78)** → **SGSY** → **Bharat Nirman (2005)**, option **(1)**.
SGSY falls between Food for Work and Bharat Nirman, so it must be third.
xa: **Bharat Nirman** was a **rural infrastructure package** of **2005**, the same year as the **MGNREGA Act**.
**NES** (**1953**) and the **Minimum Needs Programme** (**1974**) also fall between CDP and Bharat Nirman.
CDP was reviewed by the **Balwantrai Mehta** Committee in **1957**.

40.s: Which institution conducts an annual Gram Panchayat-level ranking survey as part of its rural development framework?
40.x: Mission Antyodaya includes an annual Gram Panchayat-level ranking survey and functions as a convergence framework for rural development.
40.tq: Match the distinctive administrative activity with the institution performing it.
xs: **Mission Antyodaya** runs an **annual GP-level ranking survey**, option **(2)**.
It is a **convergence framework** to make **Gram Panchayats poverty-free**, from **Union Budget 2017-18**.
**CAPART** funds voluntary organisations; **DRDA** implemented district anti-poverty programmes; **ITDA** serves tribal areas.
xa: **CAPART** dates to **1986** (MoRD).
**DRDA** grew out of **IRDP** implementation.

40.s: CAPART is primarily associated with:
o: Funding voluntary organisations and promoting rural technology
Providing modern inputs only to desert farmers
40.x: CAPART, or the Council for Advancement of People's Action and Rural Technology, funds voluntary organisations and supports rural technology.
40.tq: Expand the acronym and connect it with its core institutional function.
xs: **CAPART** (Council for Advancement of People's Action and Rural Technology) **funds voluntary organisations and rural technology**, option **(3)**.
District anti-poverty implementation was the role of **DRDA**; all-weather roads are **PMGSY**.
xa: CAPART was set up in **1986** under **MoRD**.
**Mission Antyodaya** (**2017-18**) aims at poverty-free Gram Panchayats.
**ITDA/TADP** support tribal agriculture and livelihoods.

40.s: The principal objective of ITDA/TADP is to:
o: Raise agricultural output through modern inputs, horticulture and fruit plantations, while supporting tribal livelihoods
Provide only urban amenities to selected villages
Construct national highways in tribal districts
Promote industrial exports from metropolitan regions
40.x: ITDA and TADP seek to improve agricultural output through modern inputs, horticulture and fruit plantations and to strengthen tribal livelihoods.
40.tq: Select the option containing the complete objective rather than a narrow fragment.
xs: **ITDA/TADP** aim to **raise agricultural output with modern inputs**, **horticulture/fruit plantations** and **tribal livelihoods**, option **(1)**.
A PYQ held **all listed objectives** of TADP and ITDA to be correct.
xa: ITDA = **Integrated Tribal Development Agency**; TADP = **Tribal Area Development Programme**.
Both are tied to the **Tribal Sub-Plan** of the **5th Plan**.
**PURA** (urban amenities in rural areas) is a different, **Abdul Kalam** idea.

40.s: Which department became a separate Ministry in 2011 and, since June 2019, has been a Department under the Ministry of Jal Shakti?
40.x: Drinking Water and Sanitation became a separate Ministry in 2011 and has been a Department under the Ministry of Jal Shakti since June 2019.
40.tq: Track an institutional change through its two successive administrative stages.
xs: **Drinking Water & Sanitation** became a separate Ministry in **2011** and since **June 2019** is a Department under **Jal Shakti**, option **(2)**.
Land Resources handles DPAP and DDP, not drinking water.
xa: **Jal Jeevan Mission** (**15 Aug 2019**) and **SBM-G** sit under **Jal Shakti**.
⚠ JJM and SBM-G = **Jal Shakti**; PMGSY and PMAY-G = **Rural Development**.
SBM-G Phase II (**2020**) is run by **DDWS**.

40.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
o: PMGSY — 25 December 2000 — Ministry of Rural Development
Jal Jeevan Mission — 15 August 2019 — Ministry of Rural Development
Vibrant Villages Programme — 2022–23 — Ministry of Rural Development
40.x: PMGSY was launched on 25 December 2000 under the Ministry of Rural Development. PMAY-G is under Rural Development, Jal Jeevan Mission under Jal Shakti, and the Vibrant Villages Programme under Home Affairs.
40.tq: Start with the sure launch-date and ministry pair, then eliminate ministry swaps.
xs: **PMGSY — 25 Dec 2000 — Rural Development** is correct, option **(1)**.
**PMAY-G** is under **Rural Development**, **JJM** under **Jal Shakti**, and the **Vibrant Villages Programme** under **Home Affairs**.
xa: PMAY-G began in **2016**; JJM on **15 Aug 2019**.
VVP covers **villages on the northern border** (Budget **2022-23**).
PMGSY now connects **99.6%** of targeted eligible areas (Aug 2026).

40.s: The objective of ODF Plus under SBM-Gramin Phase II is to:
o: Provide only individual household toilets in urban areas
Provide pucca houses in difficult terrain
Sustain open-defecation-free status and undertake solid and liquid waste management
40.x: SBM-Gramin Phase II focuses on sustaining ODF status and managing solid and liquid waste, together described as ODF Plus.
40.tq: Distinguish the second-phase qualitative objective from the original sanitation drive.
xs: **ODF Plus** under **SBM-G Phase II** means **sustaining ODF** plus **solid and liquid waste management**, option **(3)**.
It is a rural sanitation goal, not urban toilets, housing or roads.
xa: SBM-G Phase II was approved in **2020**, up to **2024-25**, under **Jal Shakti (DDWS)**.
Achievements: **12.19 crore** toilets, **1,288 GOBARdhan** plants, **5.68 lakh** ODF Plus villages.
AP Budget **2026-27**: SBM **Rs 1,037 crore**.

40.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Drought-Prone Area Programme (DPAP) was launched in 1973-74 for drought-prone areas.
2. The Desert Development Programme (DDP) was launched in 1977-78 for hot desert areas only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
40.x: Statement 1 is correct: DPAP dates to 1973-74 and targets drought-prone areas. Statement 2 is wrong: DDP (1977-78) covers both hot and cold desert areas, not hot deserts only. Hence '1 only'.
40.tq: DPAP 1973-74 comes before DDP 1977-78; DDP = hot AND cold deserts.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **DPAP** (**1973-74**) is for **drought-prone areas**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **DDP** (**1977-78**) covers **hot and cold desert** areas, not hot deserts only — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Both are under **Rural Development / Land Resources**.
**Food for Work** also dates to **1977-78**.
The **Madanapalle Water Grid** serves drought-prone **Rayalaseema** in AP.

40.s: The Vibrant Villages Programme, announced in the Budget 2022–23, is administered by the:
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
40.x: The Vibrant Villages Programme was announced in Budget 2022–23 under the Ministry of Home Affairs and targets villages on the northern border.
40.tq: Apply the ministry-swap trap to a border-area development programme.
xs: The **Vibrant Villages Programme** (Budget **2022-23**) is under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, option **(1)**.
It covers **villages on the northern border**.
xa: ⚠ VVP = **Home Affairs**; JJM/SBM-G = **Jal Shakti**; PMGSY/PMAY-G = **Rural Development**.
**Mission Antyodaya** came in Union Budget **2017-18**.
**SPMRM** develops **300+** Rurban clusters.

40.s:
Consider the following statements about the population norms for eligible unconnected habitations under PMGSY:
1. In plain areas, habitations with 500 or more population are eligible.
2. In hill States, the North-East, deserts and Schedule V areas, habitations with 250 or more population are eligible.
3. In LWE-affected blocks, habitations with 250 or more population are eligible.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
40.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the norm is 500+ in plains and 250+ in hill/NE/desert/Schedule V areas. Statement 3 is wrong: in LWE-affected blocks the norm is 100+. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
40.tq: PMGSY ladder: 500 plains, 250 special areas, 100 LWE blocks.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **plains 500+**.
Statement 2 is correct: **hill States, NE, deserts, Schedule V/tribal areas 250+**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **LWE-affected blocks** need only **100+** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: ⚠ **500 – 250 – 100** = plains – hill/NE/tribal – LWE.
**RCPLWEA** (**2016**) builds LWE roads.

40.s: Which of the following correctly matches the phases of PMGSY?
o: PMGSY-I—2000—new connectivity; PMGSY-II—2013—upgradation; PMGSY-III—2019—through routes and major rural links
40.x: PMGSY-I began in 2000, PMGSY-II in 2013 focused on upgradation, and PMGSY-III began in 2019 for through routes and major rural links.
40.tq: Start from the phase years and verify each phase's distinctive function.
xs: **PMGSY-I 2000** (new connectivity), **PMGSY-II 2013** (**upgradation**), **PMGSY-III 2019** (**through routes and major rural links**) — option **(1)**.
**RCPLWEA** (**2016**) is the separate **LWE roads** component.
xa: PMGSY launched on **25 Dec 2000**.
It connects **99.6%** of targeted eligible areas.
LWE blocks need only **100+** population.

40.s: Under PMAY-G, the unit assistance for a house is correctly stated as:
o: Rs 1.00 lakh in plains and Rs 1.20 lakh in hilly areas
Rs 1.30 lakh in plains and Rs 1.50 lakh in hilly areas
Rs 1.50 lakh in plains and Rs 1.80 lakh in difficult terrain
Rs 1.20 lakh in plains and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly or difficult terrain
40.x: PMAY-G provides assistance of Rs 1.20 lakh per house in plain areas and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly or difficult terrain.
40.tq: Compare the standard unit assistance with the higher difficult-terrain amount.
xs: PMAY-G gives **Rs 1.20 lakh** in **plains** and **Rs 1.30 lakh** in **hilly/difficult terrain**, option **(4)**.
The other pairs misstate one or both amounts.
xa: Beneficiaries from **SECC 2011** housing-deprivation data, verified by the **Gram Sabha**.
**3.13 crore** rural homes completed by mid-2026.
AP Budget **2026-27**: urban + rural housing **Rs 5,451 crore**.

40.s: Beneficiaries under PMAY-G are identified primarily on the basis of:
o: Annual income-tax returns verified by the District Collector
Voter-list data approved by the State Cabinet
SECC 2011 housing-deprivation data, verified by the Gram Sabha
Census 2001 occupational data, without local verification
40.x: PMAY-G beneficiaries are identified using housing-deprivation data from SECC 2011, followed by verification by the Gram Sabha.
40.tq: Identify both the data source and the required local verification authority.
xs: PMAY-G beneficiaries come from **SECC 2011** housing-deprivation data, **verified by the Gram Sabha**, option **(3)**.
Income-tax returns, voter lists and Census 2001 are not the basis.
xa: Unit assistance: **Rs 1.20 lakh** / **Rs 1.30 lakh**.
Scheme launched in **2016**, under **Rural Development**.
Har Ghar Jal certification also uses a **Gram Sabha** resolution.

40.s: The Functional Household Tap Connection target under the Jal Jeevan Mission covers which of the following?
o: Rural households and specified public institutions
Only urban households and panchayat offices
40.x: The target covers every rural household as well as schools, anganwadis, Gram Panchayat buildings, health centres and ashramshalas.
