40.tq: Distinguish the complete beneficiary coverage from a limited institutional target.
xs: **FHTC** goes to **every rural household + public institutions** (schools, anganwadis, GP buildings, health centres, ashramshalas), option **(2)**.
It is not limited to households only or institutions only.
xa: FHTC = **Functional Household Tap Connection**.
Service level: **55 LPCD**.
**Har Ghar Jal** village: every household and institution has a tap, certified by **Gram Sabha**.

40.s: The prescribed service level under the Jal Jeevan Mission is:
40.x: The prescribed JJM service level is 55 litres per capita per day of water of the required quality.
40.tq: Recall the exact quantitative service norm.
xs: JJM's service level is **55 litres per capita per day (LPCD)** of prescribed quality, option **(3)**.
70, 45 and 40 LPCD are not the JJM norm.
xa: Delivered through **FHTCs** to households and institutions.
Target **19.36 crore**; connected **15.86 crore (81.94%)**.
**2.89 lakh** fully covered villages (Aug 2026).

40.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0:
1. The original deadline of the mission was 2024.
2. The Union Cabinet extended the mission up to December 2028.
3. The emphasis is shifting from infrastructure creation to service delivery.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: All three statements are correct. JJM originally targeted 2024, was extended to December 2028, and JJM 2.0 focuses more strongly on service delivery.
40.tq: Use the coded option containing all three linked policy facts.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the original deadline was **2024**.
Statement 2 is correct: Cabinet extended it to **December 2028** (Mar 2026) as **JJM 2.0**.
Statement 3 is correct: the shift is "**from infrastructure creation to service delivery**" — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: JJM 2.0 outlay: **Rs 8.69 lakh crore**.
Union Budget **2026-27**: **Rs 67,600 crore**.

40.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the funding pattern under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0:
List-I
A. Himalayan and North-Eastern States
B. Union Territories with legislature
C. Union Territories without legislature
D. Other States

List-II
1. 100% Union funding
2. 90:10 Centre-State sharing
3. 50:50 Centre-State sharing

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
40.x: Himalayan and North-Eastern States and UTs with legislature follow 90:10 sharing; UTs without legislature receive 100% Union funding; other States follow 50:50 sharing.
40.tq: Start from the sure funding pair and eliminate codes with reversed ratios.
xs: **Himalayan/NE States** and **UTs with legislature** = **90:10**; **UTs without legislature** = **100%** Centre; **others** = **50:50** — option **(1)**.
So A and B share code 2, C is 1, D is 3.
xa: JJM 2.0 outlay: **Rs 8.69 lakh crore**.
⚠ SPMRM uses **60:40** generally and **90:10** for NE and Himalayan States.
JJM 2.0 runs to **December 2028**.

40.s: A village may be certified as a Har Ghar Jal village when:
o: A water scheme receives administrative sanction from the Union Government
At least 81.94 per cent of households receive tanker water
Every household and institution has a tap connection and the Gram Sabha passes a resolution
Every rural household has an electricity connection certified by the Gram Panchayat
40.x: Har Ghar Jal certification requires tap connections for every household and institution, certified through a Gram Sabha resolution.
40.tq: Apply the certification conditions to a practical village situation.
xs: A **Har Ghar Jal** village has a tap for **every household and institution**, certified by a **Gram Sabha resolution**, option **(3)**.
**81.94%** is the national connection share, not a certification test.
xa: **2.12 lakh+** villages certified (Mar 2025).
**Jal Arpan**: handover to GPs and **Paani Samitis/VWSCs**.
**Sujal Gaon ID**: digital ID for every rural piped scheme.

40.s: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission is best described as:
o: A successor and expansion of the PURA approach
A special programme for urban slum redevelopment
A scheme exclusively for tribal hostels
A replacement for the National Extension Service
40.x: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission, launched in 2016, is the successor and expansion of the PURA approach.
40.tq: Use the successor–predecessor relationship to distinguish closely related rural development initiatives.
xs: **SPMRM** is the **successor/expansion of PURA**, option **(1)**.
Launched **21 Feb 2016** at **Kurubhat, Rajnandgaon** (Chhattisgarh).
xa: PURA = **Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas**, by **Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**.
SPMRM aims at **300+ Rurban clusters**.
**NES** (**1953**) was an early rural extension programme, unrelated.

40.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission?
o: Replacing all Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies
40.x: The mission aims to stimulate local economic development, enhance basic services and create well-planned clusters. It does not replace Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies.
40.tq: Find the option that exceeds the institutional scope of the mission.
xs: SPMRM does **not replace Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies**, so option **(4)** is NOT an objective.
Its PYQ objectives: **stimulate local economic development**, **enhance basic services**, **create well-planned clusters**.
xa: It keeps the "**rural soul**" while adding urban amenities.
Convergence of **MGNREGA, PMGSY, SBM, PMAY**.
⚠ The **16th FC** proposed an "**Urbanisation Premium**" for merging peri-urban villages.

40.s: A Rurban cluster in a plain or coastal area normally comprises contiguous villages having a population of:
40.x: For plain and coastal areas, a Rurban cluster comprises contiguous villages with a population of 25,000 to 50,000.
40.tq: Separate population norms by geographical category before selecting the range.
xs: A plain/coastal Rurban cluster has **25,000-50,000** population, option **(4)**.
**5,000-25,000** is one version of the **desert/hilly/tribal** range.
xa: Desert/hilly/tribal: **5,000-15,000** (some notes **5,000-25,000**).
Clusters are **contiguous villages**.
SPMRM aims at **300+** clusters.

40.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the funding pattern of the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission?
o: It is funded mainly through convergence of existing schemes, with Critical Gap Funding up to 30% of project cost.
It is funded only by the concerned State Government through a 90:10 formula.
It is financed through foreign assistance without any scheme convergence.
It is financed entirely through a dedicated Central grant.
40.x: The mission mainly uses convergence of existing schemes and provides Critical Gap Funding of up to 30% of project cost.
40.tq: Distinguish convergence-based financing from a wholly dedicated grant mechanism.
xs: SPMRM is funded mainly by **convergence** of existing schemes plus **Critical Gap Funding** up to **30%** of project cost, option **(1)**.
Converged schemes: **MGNREGA, PMGSY, SBM, PMAY**.
xa: Centre:State **60:40**; **90:10** for NE and Himalayan States.
Launched **2016**; aims at **300+** clusters.
AP: **359** panchayats classified under Rurban clusters.

40.s: Rurbanisation through SPMRM or PURA primarily seeks to:
o: Address the rural-urban divide and distress migration
Widen the rural-urban divide through separate infrastructure systems
Replace all rural occupations with urban occupations
40.x: Rurbanisation is intended to bridge the rural-urban divide and reduce distress migration by bringing urban amenities and opportunities to rural areas.
40.tq: Identify the development objective from the policy consequence described.
xs: Rurbanisation (**SPMRM/PURA**) addresses the **rural-urban divide and distress migration**, option **(2)**.
PYQ: the model aimed at **bridging the rural-urban divide**.
xa: PURA = **Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas** (**Abdul Kalam**).
Rurban clusters show **rising density, non-farm jobs, growing economic activity**.
**16th FC**: a **Rural-to-Urban Transition Policy**.

40.s: The PURA (Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas) model, later elaborated in the book Target 3 Billion, was originally propounded by:
40.x: PURA was the idea of Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, elaborated in Target 3 Billion (co-authored with Srijan Pal Singh) to bridge the rural-urban divide. Balwantrai Mehta headed the 1957 committee on CDP/NES; Swaminathan is linked to the Green Revolution; Sen to the entitlement approach to famine.
40.tq: PURA = Kalam; SPMRM 2016 is its successor.
xs: **PURA** was propounded by **Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**, option **(1)**.
It was elaborated in **Target 3 Billion** with **Srijan Pal Singh**.
**Balwantrai Mehta** reviewed CDP and NES in **1957**.
xa: PURA = Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas.
Successor: **SPMRM** (**21 Feb 2016**).
FIRST/LAST: **PURA idea = Abdul Kalam**; **CDP 1952** = first rural development programme.

40.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a remaining rural infrastructure gap?
o: Operation and maintenance of water schemes
Universal availability of high-speed rail connectivity
40.x: The identified gaps include piped water, operation and maintenance, housing and last-mile roads. High-speed rail connectivity is not listed as a rural infrastructure gap in this context.
40.tq: Find the option outside the stated group of infrastructure deficiencies.
xs: **High-speed rail** is not listed as a rural infrastructure gap, so option **(3)** is the answer.
Listed gaps: piped water (~**18%** unconnected), **O&M of water schemes**, **housing**, **last-mile roads**.
xa: Achievements: **Saubhagya** — **100%** willing-household electrification.
SBM-G: **12.19 crore** toilets; **5.68 lakh** ODF Plus villages.
Poor quality and irregularities in **JJM works** is another gap.

40.s: Which of the following correctly describes the employment and livelihood base mentioned for rural development?
o: MGNREGA provides 100 days of employment per household, while NRLM promotes SHG-based self-employment
MGNREGA is limited to women, while NRLM is limited to public institutions
MGNREGA provides permanent government jobs, while NRLM provides only urban wage employment
MGNREGA provides 55 litres of water per capita, while NRLM constructs roads
40.x: MGNREGA provides up to 100 days of wage employment per household, with one-third participation intended for women, while NRLM promotes SHG-based self-employment and livelihoods.
40.tq: Keep the distinct functions of a wage-employment programme and a livelihood mission separate.
xs: **MGNREGA** gives **100 days** of employment per household, and **NRLM (Aajeevika)** promotes **SHG-based self-employment**, option **(1)**.
MGNREGA is not women-only — it reserves **one-third** for women; **55 LPCD** is the **JJM** water norm.
xa: AP Budget **2026-27**: **NRLM Rs 955 crore**; **VB-G RAM G** (rural employment guarantee) **Rs 8,365 crore**.
The **MGNREGA Act** dates to **2005**, the year of **Bharat Nirman**.
**Food for Work** (**1977-78**) was an earlier wage-employment programme.

40.s: As on 31 March 2024, the share of Andhra Pradesh rural households having Functional Household Tap Connections was approximately:
40.x: In Andhra Pradesh, 70.04 lakh households, representing 73 per cent, had FHTCs as on 31 March 2024.
40.tq: Distinguish the State-level coverage percentage from the national figure.
xs: On **31 Mar 2024**, **70.04 lakh** AP households — **73 per cent** — had FHTCs, option **(2)**.
**81.94%** is the **national** connection share, not AP's.
xa: AP sanctioned **77,917** works worth **Rs 27,248.86 crore** in saturation mode.
AP has **112** water testing labs and **2,00,101** hand pumps.
Action plan: **+5.40 lakh** FHTCs (2024-25); **+10 lakh** each in 2025-26 and 2026-27.

40.s: The Madanapalle Water Grid is intended primarily to provide drinking water to:
o: The coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh
40.x: The Madanapalle Water Grid is intended to provide drinking water in drought-prone Rayalaseema.
40.tq: Apply the location-purpose association of a regional infrastructure project.
xs: The **Madanapalle Water Grid** gives drinking water to **drought-prone Rayalaseema**, option **(4)**.
It is not a coastal, Himalayan or Visakhapatnam-only project.
xa: AP aims at safe water to **every household by 2028**.
AP had **70.04 lakh** households (**73%**) with FHTCs on 31 Mar 2024.
**DPAP** (**1973-74**) was the national programme for drought-prone areas.

40.s:
Consider the following statements regarding rural development coverage:
1. Andhra Pradesh JJM coverage was reported as 73 per cent in March 2024.
2. National JJM coverage was approximately 82 per cent.
3. Andhra Pradesh’s target under JJM 2.0 is to provide safe water to every household by 2028.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh’s reported coverage was below the national level, while its State target is universal safe-water provision by 2028.
40.tq: Compare State and national coverage before applying the State deadline.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: AP JJM coverage was **73%** (Mar 2024).
Statement 2 is correct: national coverage is ~**82%** (**81.94%**).
Statement 3 is correct: AP targets **every household by 2028** — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(2)**.
xa: National: **15.86 crore** of **19.36 crore** households connected.
**2.89 lakh** fully covered villages (Aug 2026).

40.s: Which one of the following best describes the principal policy shift associated with JJM 2.0?
o: From service delivery to only asset construction
From rural water supply to urban transport
From Gram Panchayat participation to exclusive private ownership
From infrastructure creation to service delivery, including operation and maintenance
40.x: JJM 2.0 shifts emphasis from merely creating infrastructure to ensuring service delivery, including sustainable operation and maintenance.
40.tq: Identify the policy shift by contrasting assets with continuing service delivery.
xs: **JJM 2.0** shifts "**from infrastructure creation to service delivery**", including **O&M**, option **(4)**.
Option **(1)** reverses the shift.
xa: Cabinet extended JJM to **December 2028** (Mar 2026); original deadline **2024**.
Criticism: **cost overruns** and **poor-quality works**.
AP gave O&M to **panchayats** (Sept **2025**).

40.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Community Development Programme — first rural development programme, 1952
Rurban clusters — exclusively urban migration centres
Har Ghar Jal — only a road-connectivity programme
40.x: The Community Development Programme of 1952 is identified as the first rural development programme. The PURA idea is associated with Abdul Kalam, while Har Ghar Jal concerns tap-water access.
40.tq: Use the first-programme clue and reject options with swapped programme purposes.
xs: **CDP — first rural development programme, 1952** is correctly matched, option **(1)**.
The **PURA** idea is **Abdul Kalam**'s; **Saubhagya** is electrification; **Har Ghar Jal** is about **tap water**; Rurban clusters are rural areas with urban signs.
xa: CDP → **NES 1953** → **Balwantrai Mehta** review **1957**.
Saubhagya: **100%** willing-household electrification.
**2.12 lakh+** Har Ghar Jal villages certified (Mar 2025).

40.s: Who originated the Etawah Pilot Project, the first rural-development pilot project, in September 1948?
40.x: Lt. Col. Albert Mayer, an American town planner, started the Etawah Pilot Project in September 1948, India's first rural-development pilot.
40.tq: Recall who began the Etawah project.
n: Lieutenant Colonel Albert Mayer originated the Etawah Pilot Project. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]

40.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) National Extension Service
(b) Food for Work
(c) IRDP experimentally
(d) IRDP nationwide

List-II
(i) 2 October 1980
(ii) 1977–78
(iii) 1953
(iv) 1978–79
