40.tq: Arrange the programmes in time order.
n: The National Extension Service began in 1953. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
The Food for Work programme first started in 1977–78. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
The Integrated Rural Development Programme first started experimentally in 1978–79. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
The Integrated Rural Development Programme became nationwide on 2 October 1980. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]

40.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Etawah Pilot Project
(b) National Extension Service
(c) Employment Guarantee Scheme
(d) Antyodaya

List-II
(i) First programme of community development
(ii) First started in Rajasthan in 1977–78
(iii) First rural-development pilot project
(iv) First started in Maharashtra in 1972
40.x: Etawah was the first rural-development pilot, the NES the first community-development extension programme, the Employment Guarantee Scheme began in Maharashtra (1972), and Antyodaya in Rajasthan (1977–78). The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
40.tq: Match each first to its place or role.
n: The Etawah Pilot Project was the first rural-development pilot project. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
The National Extension Service was the first programme of community development. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
The Employment Guarantee Scheme first started in Maharashtra in 1972. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
Antyodaya first started in Rajasthan in 1977–78. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]

40.s:
Consider the following statements:

Statement A: Garibi Hatao was first introduced in the Fifth Five-Year Plan.
Statement B: The Employment Guarantee Scheme first started in Maharashtra in 1972.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
40.x: Both are true: Garibi Hatao entered planning with the Fifth Plan, and Maharashtra started the first Employment Guarantee Scheme in 1972.
40.tq: Recall the 1970s anti-poverty firsts.
n: Garibi Hatao was first introduced in the Fifth Five-Year Plan. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
The Employment Guarantee Scheme first started in Maharashtra in 1972. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]

41.s: In 1951, moneylenders supplied approximately what share of rural credit?
41.x: Moneylenders supplied approximately 70% of rural credit in 1951.
41.tq: Recall the historical baseline and distinguish it from the later institutional-credit structure.
xs: In **1951**, **moneylenders** supplied the bulk — about **70%** — of rural credit, so option **(3)** is correct.
This dominance of moneylenders is the historical backdrop to the **AIRCS Committee** set up by the **RBI** in **1951**.
xa: AIRCS, chaired by **A.D. Gorwala**, reported in **1954**; its verdict: "**rural credit has failed, but cooperation must succeed**".
Its outcome was the **SBI** (**1955**), formed from the **Imperial Bank**.
⚠ Sequence trap: AIRCS **1951** → report **1954** → **SBI 1955**.
Non-institutional lenders today: **moneylenders, traders, landlords, relatives**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about the All India Rural Credit Survey Committee:
1. It was constituted by the RBI in 1951.
2. It submitted its report in 1956.
3. Its recommendations led to the formation of the State Bank of India in 1955 from the Imperial Bank.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statement 1 is correct: the RBI set it up in 1951 under A.D. Gorwala. Statement 2 is wrong: the report came in 1954, not 1956. Statement 3 is correct: SBI was formed in 1955 from the Imperial Bank. Hence '1 only' omits 3, '2 and 3 only' wrongly includes 2, and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly includes 2.
41.tq: AIRCS: 1951 set up, 1954 report, 1955 SBI.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: the **RBI** constituted the AIRCS Committee in **1951** under **A.D. Gorwala** — correct.
Statement 2: the report came in **1954**, not 1956 — wrong.
Statement 3: its outcome was the **SBI** in **1955**, formed from the **Imperial Bank** — correct.
xa: Verdict of the Committee: "**rural credit has failed, but cooperation must succeed**".
In **1951** moneylenders supplied about **70%** of rural credit.
⚠ Order to remember: AIRCS **1951** → report **1954** → **SBI 1955**.

41.s: The statement associated with the findings of the All India Rural Credit Survey Committee was:
o: Agriculture must be replaced by industry
Banking must be confined to urban areas
Rural credit has failed, but cooperation must succeed
Rural credit has succeeded, but cooperation must be limited
41.x: The Committee famously concluded that rural credit had failed, but cooperation must succeed. This conclusion emphasised the role of cooperative institutions in rural credit.
41.tq: Recall the exact contrast in the committee’s well-known formulation.
xs: The AIRCS Committee's verdict was "**rural credit has failed, but cooperation must succeed**" — option **(3)**.
It stressed **cooperative institutions** as the way to replace moneylender dominance (about **70%** of rural credit in **1951**).
xa: Committee: **RBI**, chair **A.D. Gorwala**, **1951**, report **1954**.
Outcome: **State Bank of India (1955)** from the **Imperial Bank**.
Today **cooperatives/PACS** remain institutional sources giving credit, **marketing and storage** to small and marginal farmers.

41.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Commercial banks — Institutional credit
2. PACS — Institutional credit
3. Relatives — Non-institutional credit
4. Traders — Institutional credit
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
41.x: Commercial banks and PACS are institutional sources, while relatives are non-institutional. Traders are non-institutional, so pair 4 is incorrect.
41.tq: Spot the swapped category in the institutional–non-institutional classification.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Commercial banks** and **PACS/cooperatives** are **institutional** sources; **relatives** are **non-institutional**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **traders** are a **non-institutional** source, like moneylenders and landlords.
xa: Other institutional sources: **RRBs**, **SFBs**, **SHG-bank linkage**.
Non-institutional list: **moneylenders, traders, landlords, relatives**.
About **50%** of AP farmers depend on **non-institutional credit** (NABARD study).

41.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Kisan Credit Card scheme as described?
o: It has a validity period of five years.
It is restricted exclusively to landowning farmers and excludes tenants and sharecroppers.
It may be issued by public sector banks, private scheduled commercial banks, SFBs, RRBs and cooperative banks.
It covers crop, post-harvest, consumption and allied needs.
41.x: Tenants, sharecroppers, SHGs and JLGs are eligible under the described Kisan Credit Card framework. The other three statements are correct features.
41.tq: Use the eligibility exception to defeat the word ‘exclusively’.
xs: The false feature is that KCC is **restricted to landowning farmers** — option **(2)**; **tenants, sharecroppers, SHGs/JLGs** are eligible.
KCC is valid **5 years** — true.
It is issued by **PSBs, private SCBs, SFBs, RRBs and cooperative banks** — true.
It covers **crop, post-harvest, consumption and allied** needs — true.
xa: The KCC **limit** is fixed by the **cropping pattern**.
**MISS-KCC** benefits about **5.9 crore** farmers (Feb **2025**); applications via the **Kisan Rin Portal**.
AP has **CCRC** for tenant farmers, who carry more debt than owners (Guntur sample).

41.s: Which of the following correctly states the types of informal loans based on their repayment pattern or consequences?
41.x: Informal loans are described as temporary, chronic or debt-trap loans. A temporary loan may be repaid after harvest, whereas a debt trap involves taking a new loan to repay an old one.
41.tq: Use the exact classification and distinguish repayment pattern from lender type.
xs: Debt types are **temporary, chronic and debt-trap** — option **(3)**.
**Temporary** debt is seasonal, **repaid after harvest**; a **debt trap** means taking a **new loan to repay an old one**.
xa: **Usurious interest** leads to **distress sale**, sale of **land/gold** and **bonded-labour-like** arrangements.
Informal debt is often the **immediate trigger in farmer suicides**.
The **microfinance route** runs through **SHGs, JLGs, BC Sakhis** under **DAY-NRLM**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about farm indebtedness in Andhra Pradesh:
1. As per the NSSO 77th Round, 93.2% of agricultural households in AP are indebted, the highest among major States.
2. A NABARD study found that only about 25% of AP farmers depend on non-institutional credit.
3. A Guntur sample found that tenant farmers carry more debt than owner-cultivators.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statement 1 is correct: NSSO 77th Round puts AP at 93.2%, highest among major States. Statement 2 is wrong: the NABARD study puts dependence on non-institutional credit at about 50%, not 25%. Statement 3 is correct: the Guntur sample showed tenants more indebted than owners (hence CCRC for tenants). So '1 only' misses 3, '2 and 3 only' wrongly includes 2 and drops 1, and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly includes 2.
41.tq: AP indebtedness: 93.2% (highest), ~50% on informal credit, tenants worse off.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **93.2%** of AP agricultural households are indebted, **highest among major States** (NSSO **77th Round**) — correct.
Statement 2: NABARD puts dependence on **non-institutional credit** at about **50%**, not 25% — wrong.
Statement 3: in the **Guntur sample**, **tenant farmers** carry more debt than owners — correct; hence **CCRC** for tenants.
xa: AP **distress-migration belts**: **Rayalaseema** (drought-prone) and north Andhra (**Srikakulam**).
**Gulf migration** sources: **YSR Kadapa** and **Godavari/Konaseema** districts.
AP angle: highest indebted farm households plus **high tenancy**.

41.s: The microfinance route mentioned for rural borrowers operates through which combination?
o: SHGs, JLGs and BC Sakhis under DAY-NRLM
Only commercial exporters under the WTO
41.x: The described microfinance route uses self-help groups, joint liability groups and BC Sakhis under DAY-NRLM.
41.tq: Match the microfinance channels with the programme framework.
xs: The microfinance route works through **SHGs, JLGs and BC Sakhis under DAY-NRLM** — option **(1)**.
DAY-NRLM also has **9 lakh+ Community Resource Persons**.
xa: **SVEP** (Start-Up Village Entrepreneurship Programme), also under **DAY-NRLM**, funds rural **non-farm enterprises**.
**SHG-bank linkage** is counted among **institutional** credit sources.
**SHGs/JLGs** are also eligible for the **Kisan Credit Card**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC):
1. It is a statutory body under the Khadi and Village Industries Act, 1956.
2. The Act was amended in 1987 and 2006.
3. KVIC functions under the Ministry of MSME.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
41.x: All three statements are correct. KVIC is a statutory body under the 1956 Act, which was amended in 1987 and 2006, and it functions under the Ministry of MSME.
41.tq: Test a statutory body through its Act, amendments and administrative ministry.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **KVIC** is a **statutory body** under the **KVI Act 1956** — correct.
Statement 2: the Act was amended in **1987** and **2006** — correct.
Statement 3: it works under the **Ministry of MSME** — correct.
xa: KVIC is the implementing agency of **PMEGP**.
**KVI sales** reached **Rs 1.27 lakh crore** in **2025-26**.
**SVEP** (under **DAY-NRLM**) also funds rural non-farm enterprises.

41.s: The Start-Up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP) is intended primarily to:
o: Conduct the National Sample Survey on migration
Replace the Khadi and Village Industries Act
41.x: SVEP, under DAY-NRLM, funds rural non-farm enterprises. Its purpose is not urban infrastructure, legislative replacement or survey administration.
41.tq: Match the programme with its stated operational objective.
xs: **SVEP** funds **rural non-farm enterprises** — option **(1)**.
It runs under **DAY-NRLM**; it has nothing to do with surveys, urban infrastructure or the KVI Act.
xa: **KVIC** (KVI Act **1956**) implements **PMEGP**.
**DDU-GKY**: placement-linked skilling — **18.38 lakh** trained, **11.94 lakh** placed (Mar **2026**).
**MSMEs** give **38.9 crore** jobs, **2nd after agriculture**, and reduce distress migration.

41.s: Which of the following concerns was flagged by a parliamentary panel regarding DDU-GKY?
41.x: The parliamentary panel flagged low wages and drop-outs in relation to DDU-GKY. These concerns relate to the quality and retention of placement-linked skilling outcomes.
41.tq: Distinguish the reported criticism from the programme’s formal objective.
xs: A **Parliamentary panel** flagged **low wages and drop-outs** in **DDU-GKY** — option **(4)**.
DDU-GKY is **placement-linked skilling**: **18.38 lakh** trained, **11.94 lakh** placed (Mar **2026**).
xa: **SVEP** under **DAY-NRLM** funds rural non-farm enterprises.
**MSMEs**: **38.9 crore** jobs, second after agriculture.
**KVIC** implements **PMEGP**.

41.s: Which body is the implementing agency of the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)?
o: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
41.x: KVIC, a statutory body under the KVI Act 1956 working under the Ministry of MSME, implements PMEGP. NABARD is the apex rural development bank, SIDBI finances MSMEs, and DAY-NRLM runs SHG-based livelihoods (including SVEP), not PMEGP.
41.tq: PMEGP is run by KVIC (Ministry of MSME).
xs: **KVIC** is the implementing agency of **PMEGP** — option **(2)**.
KVIC is a **statutory body** under the **KVI Act 1956** (amended **1987**, **2006**) under the **Ministry of MSME**.
**DAY-NRLM** runs the **SHG** route and **SVEP**, not PMEGP.
xa: **KVI sales**: **Rs 1.27 lakh crore** in **2025-26**.
**MSMEs**: **8.7 crore** enterprises, about **31.1%** of GDP.
**DDU-GKY**: **18.38 lakh** trained, **11.94 lakh** placed (Mar **2026**).

41.s: Which one of the following is an indicator of rural distress rather than an indicator of improved rural fundamentals?
o: A fall in rural unemployment from 3.3% to 2.5%
Rising real farm and non-farm wages
A demand for MGNREGA work that is artificially suppressed
41.x: Claims of artificially suppressed MGNREGA demand indicate continuing rural distress. The other options are presented as signs of strengthening rural fundamentals.
41.tq: Separate an underlying distress signal from favourable aggregate indicators.
xs: **Unions** say MGNREGA demand was "**artificially suppressed**" — a distress signal, option **(3)**.
Options (1), (2), (4) are the **ES 2025-26** "strengthening fundamentals": rural unemployment **3.3% → 2.5%**, rising **real wages**, consumption at a **17-quarter high**.
xa: MGNREGA person-days fell from **389.09 crore (2020-21)** to **183.77 crore (2025-26, to Dec 2025)**.
Debate: falling MGNREGA demand **real or budget-suppressed**?
Urban wages are **1.7-2 times** rural (ES **2025-26**).

41.s: Which of the following statements regarding MGNREGA is correct?
o: It was introduced as NREGA in 2006 and renamed MGNREGA in 2009.
It was introduced in 2009 and renamed NREGA in 2006.
It guarantees 125 days to every household throughout India.
It excludes social audits from its implementation framework.
41.x: The Act (passed 2005) came into force as NREGA in 2006 and was renamed MGNREGA in 2009, so A is right. B reverses the dates, the guarantee is 100 days (not 125) per household, and social audit is part of the scheme.
41.tq: Check the direction of the name change against the years.
xs: MGNREGA began as **NREGA** in **2006** and was **renamed MGNREGA in 2009** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) reverses the years; the guarantee is **100 days**, not 125 (option 3); **social audit** is part of it (option 4).
xa: Wages are due within **15 days**; **one-third** women (actual **>50%** of person-days).
MGNREGA is replaced by **VB-G RAM G**.
⚠ **125 days** is AP's raised guarantee in distressed pockets under VB-G RAM G (Jun **2026**).

41.s: Which one of the following correctly states the principal provisions associated with MGNREGA as described?
o: 125 days per household, wages within 30 days and no women’s participation target
100 days per household, wages within 15 days and one-third women’s participation target
50 days per household, wages within 7 days and half the work reserved for women
100 days per individual, wages within 60 days and compulsory male participation
41.x: MGNREGA provides for 100 days per household, payment of wages within 15 days and one-third participation for women. Actual women’s participation has exceeded 50% of person-days.
41.tq: Combine the entitlement, payment period and gender provision without substituting figures.
xs: MGNREGA gives **100 days per household**, **wages within 15 days** and a **one-third women** target — option **(2)**.
Actual women's share exceeds **50%** of person-days; the scheme also has **social audit**.
xa: Began as **NREGA 2006**, renamed **2009**.
Replaced by **VB-G RAM G**; AP raised days to **125** in distressed pockets.

41.s:
Which of the following combinations correctly represents rural push factors and urban pull factors of migration?
1. Crop failure — push factor
2. Better wages — pull factor
3. Poor access to rural healthcare — push factor
4. Growth of urban industry and services — pull factor
41.x: Crop failure, poor rural healthcare and similar rural disadvantages are push factors, while better wages and urban industry and services are pull factors.
41.tq: Classify each item by asking whether it drives people out or attracts them in.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Push** (rural): few jobs, low wages, landlessness, **crop failure**, debt, **poor health** and school access.
**Pull** (urban): high labour demand, **better wages**, amenities, **industry and services growth**.
xa: **Unbalanced rural-urban development** is a push factor.
**BPSC 2024** PYQ: high urban labour demand, unbalanced development, few rural jobs — **all** are causes.
**26.8%** of rural Indians were migrants in **2020-21** (ES **2025-26**).

41.s: Distress migration is best distinguished from seasonal migration on the ground that distress migration is generally:
o: Migration caused exclusively by urban amenities
Forced by debt, landlessness or crop loss
A voluntary movement for education followed by permanent settlement
Movement only during the harvest season with assured return
41.x: Distress migration is forced by economic hardship such as debt, landlessness or crop loss. Seasonal migration involves moving for a particular season, such as harvest, and then returning.
41.tq: Separate the cause of migration from its duration.
xs: **Distress migration** is **forced by debt, landlessness or crop loss** — option **(2)**.
**Seasonal migration** is moving for a season (e.g. **harvest**) and **returning** — that is option (4).
xa: **Return migration** is also a type.
AP distress-migration belts: **Rayalaseema** and north Andhra (**Srikakulam**).
**MSMEs** help **reduce distress migration**.

41.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26 figures cited, what proportion of rural Indians were migrants in 2020-21?
41.x: The cited estimate places the proportion of rural Indians who were migrants in 2020-21 at 26.8%.
41.tq: Identify the exact percentage from closely spaced demographic figures.
xs: **26.8%** of rural Indians were migrants in **2020-21** (ES **2025-26**) — option **(2)**.
**45.9%** is the rural FLFPR for **2025**, and **35%** the share of rural households lacking healthcare within **5 km**.
xa: About **65%** of people are still **rural**; about **26%** aged **10-24**.
Rural secondary dropout is **>17%**.
Cities are near capacity; rural exodus leaves an **ageing population** behind.

41.s: Which of the following consequences of rural exodus was specifically highlighted?
o: Cities possess unlimited spare capacity and rural areas become younger
Cities approach capacity while an ageing population is left behind in rural areas
All rural households obtain quality healthcare within 5 km
41.x: The cited assessment describes cities as nearing capacity and rural exodus as leaving an ageing population behind in rural areas.
41.tq: Select the option that preserves the rural-urban contrast.
xs: Rural exodus means **cities near capacity** and an **ageing population left behind** in villages — option **(2)**.
Options (3) and (4) are false: about **35%** lack healthcare within **5 km**, and dropout is **>17%**.
xa: **26.8%** of rural Indians were migrants (**2020-21**).
About **65%** of people are still rural.
Pull factors: **better wages**, **education, healthcare, amenities**.

41.s: Feminisation of agriculture refers to which of the following phenomena?
o: The replacement of women agricultural workers by machines
The exclusive ownership of agricultural land by women
A rising share of women in the agricultural workforce as men move to non-farm and urban employment
The migration of women from urban areas to industrial centres
41.x: Feminisation of agriculture means an increasing proportion of women among cultivators, agricultural labourers and unpaid family workers, particularly as men shift to non-farm and urban work.
41.tq: Use the precise definition and distinguish workforce participation from ownership of land.
xs: **Feminisation of agriculture** is a **rising share of women** in the farm workforce as **men move to non-farm and urban work** — option **(3)**.
It covers women as **cultivators, labourers and unpaid family workers** — not land ownership (option 2).
xa: Main cause: **male out-migration**; also distress and **COVID-era return migration**.
**U-shaped curve** (Claudia Goldin): high in the **1980s**, fell **2004-05 to 2012**, rising after **2020**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about the feminisation of agriculture:
1. COVID-era return migration caused women to intensify farm work in some areas.
2. Distress and low household income may push rural women into low-productivity agricultural work.
3. Feminisation necessarily indicates that women have obtained ownership of agricultural land.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
41.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Feminisation concerns women’s increasing participation in agricultural work and does not necessarily imply ownership of land.
41.tq: Reject the statement that changes participation into ownership.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **COVID-era return migration** made women intensify farm work — correct.
Statement 2: **low household income** pushes rural women into **low-productivity farm work** — correct.
Statement 3: feminisation is about women's **share in the workforce**, not **land ownership** — wrong.
xa: Other causes: **male out-migration**; women's concentration in **subsistence farming and unpaid family work**.
Rural women were **80%** of the rise in female workers (**2017-18 to 2023-24**).
Debate: rising rural female work — **empowerment or distress**?

41.s:
Consider the following statements regarding female labour force participation:
1. Urban FLFPR for persons aged 15 years and above rose from 23.3% to 27.7%.
2. Rural women accounted for 80% of the rise in female workers between 2017-18 and 2023-24.
3. Rural FLFPR declined between 2019-20 and 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
41.x: Urban FLFPR rose from 23.3% to 27.7%, and rural women constituted 80% of the increase in female workers. Rural FLFPR rose, rather than declined, from 33.0% to 45.9%.
41.tq: Use the direction of change to eliminate the reversed trend.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: urban FLFPR rose **23.3% → 27.7%** — correct.
Statement 2: **rural women** were **80%** of the rise in female workers, **2017-18 to 2023-24** — correct.
Statement 3: rural FLFPR **rose**, **33.0% → 45.9%** — wrong.
xa: Overall FLFPR: **30% → 40%**.
Result: a **widening rural-urban FLFPR gap** (PLFS July **2026**).
**U-shaped curve** (Claudia Goldin) explains the fall and rise.

41.s: The U-shaped curve in women’s work participation, associated with Claudia Goldin, indicates which of the following sequences?
o: Low participation in agriculture in the 1980s, followed by a continuous rise until 2012
High participation in agriculture in the 1980s, a fall during 2004-05 to 2012, and a subsequent rise after 2020
A continuous decline from the 1980s because of mechanisation
High urban participation followed by a complete withdrawal from work after 2020
41.x: Women’s work participation was high in agriculture in the 1980s, fell with mechanisation between 2004-05 and 2012, and rose again after 2020, partly due to distress.
41.tq: Track the turning points in the sequence instead of treating the curve as a continuous trend.
xs: Goldin's **U-shaped curve**: **high** in agriculture in the **1980s**, **fell** with **mechanisation** **2004-05 to 2012**, **rising after 2020** — option **(2)**.
The renewed rise is **partly out of distress**, not only empowerment.
xa: **Feminisation of agriculture**: rising women's share as men move to non-farm and urban work.
**COVID-era return migration** intensified women's farm work.

41.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the principal distress-migration belts in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Only the urban districts around Visakhapatnam
Rayalaseema and north Andhra, including Srikakulam
41.x: Rayalaseema, which is drought-prone, and north Andhra, particularly Srikakulam, are identified as the main distress-migration belts. The other options omit or misidentify these belts.
41.tq: Use the location comparison to distinguish distress belts from other regions.
xs: AP's **distress-migration belts** are **Rayalaseema** (drought-prone) and **north Andhra (Srikakulam)** — option **(4)**.
The **Godavari/Konaseema** districts are **Gulf migration** sources, not distress belts.
xa: Gulf migration sources: **YSR Kadapa** and **Godavari/Konaseema**.
AP response: **125 days** under VB-G RAM G; **359 panchayats** in Rurban clusters.
About **50%** of AP farmers depend on non-institutional credit (NABARD).

41.s: Gulf migration from Andhra Pradesh comes mainly from which of the following areas?
o: All districts of Andhra Pradesh in equal proportions
Rayalaseema as a whole and Visakhapatnam city only
YSR Kadapa and the Godavari/Konaseema districts
Srikakulam alone and the Krishna delta
41.x: Gulf migration comes mainly from YSR Kadapa and the Godavari/Konaseema districts. The source districts are not described as being uniform across all of Andhra Pradesh.
41.tq: Separate Gulf-source districts from the broader distress-migration belts.
xs: **Gulf migration** comes mainly from **YSR Kadapa** and the **Godavari/Konaseema** districts — option **(3)**.
**Srikakulam** and **Rayalaseema** are **distress-migration belts**, a different category.
xa: AP raised guaranteed days to **125 per year** in distressed pockets (Jun **2026**).
**359 panchayats** in **Rurban clusters** to curb migration (Mar **2026**).
Tenant farmers carry more debt than owners (**Guntur** sample).

41.s: Which of the following represents a continuing debate concerning rural female work and MGNREGA demand?
o: Whether rising rural female work reflects empowerment or distress, and whether falling MGNREGA demand is genuine or budget-suppressed
Whether all rural female work is exclusively caused by industrialisation
Whether MGNREGA should be treated as a financial inclusion survey
Whether migration has no relationship with rural employment
41.x: The stated debates concern whether rising rural female work indicates empowerment or distress, and whether falling MGNREGA demand is real or suppressed by budget constraints. The other options do not capture these issues.
41.tq: Recognise the two-sided policy interpretation instead of accepting an absolute explanation.
xs: The debates: rising rural female work — **empowerment or distress**; falling MGNREGA demand — **real or budget-suppressed** — option **(1)**.
**Unions** say MGNREGA demand was "**artificially suppressed**", while the **ES 2025-26** sees strengthening fundamentals.
xa: MGNREGA person-days fell **389.09 crore** → **183.77 crore** (to Dec **2025**).
Goldin's **U-curve**: the post-**2020** rise is **partly out of distress**.
AP angle: highest indebted farm households (**93.2%**) and **high tenancy**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about the credit provided by Small Financing Banks:
I. Small business units are beneficiaries.
II. Small and marginal farmers are beneficiaries.
III. Entrepreneurs, particularly in rural areas, are beneficiaries.
IV. Financial-sector regulators are identified as beneficiaries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: I, II and III are correct: small finance banks lend to small businesses, small and marginal farmers, and rural entrepreneurs. Regulators are FSDC members, not borrowers.
41.tq: Find the group that is not a borrower.
n: Small Financing Banks provide credit to small business units. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 86-88]
Small Financing Banks provide credit to small and marginal farmers. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 86-88]
Small Financing Banks provide credit to entrepreneurs, particularly in rural areas. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 86-88]

42.s: How many population-size classes are used in the Census classification of Indian towns?
42.x: Indian towns are classified into six population-size classes, from Class I to Class VI.
42.tq: Recall the number of categories rather than the thresholds of one category.
xs: Census towns are grouped into **six** size classes, **Class I to VI** — option **(2) Six**.
This was the **CGPSC** answer "**06**".
xa: **Class I**: **1 lakh+**; **Class VI**: **below 5,000**.
**Class I cities hold 70%** of urban population (ES **2025-26**).
India has **53 million-plus** cities/UAs.

42.s: India ranks third in the world in terms of absolute urban population, after
42.x: India has the world’s third-largest absolute urban population, after China and the United States.
42.tq: Use the ranking order rather than the level of urbanisation.
xs: India is **3rd** in absolute urban population, after **China and the USA** — option **(2)**.
India's urban population in **2011**: **37.71 crore** (**31.16%**).
xa: Urban population projected at about **60 crore by 2031**.
Cities to host nearly **a billion people by 2050**.
⚠ Satellite (**DEGURBA**) estimate puts India about **63%** urban.

42.s: Which one of the following is a statutory town?
o: Any settlement with more than 50% of workers in non-agricultural activities
Any settlement with a density of 400 persons per square kilometre
A village with a population of 5,000 and 75% male non-agricultural workers
A place notified as a municipality or governed by a municipal corporation
42.x: A statutory town is a place with a municipal corporation, municipality, cantonment board or notified town area, notified by the State and administered by an urban local body.
42.tq: Separate the legal or administrative definition of a statutory town from the demographic criteria of a census town.
xs: A **statutory town** is any place with a **municipal corporation, municipality**, nagar panchayat, **cantonment board** or **notified town area** — option **(4)**.
It is **notified by the State** under State law and run by a **ULB**.
Option (3) describes a **census town** — administratively a village meeting **5,000 / 75% / 400**.
xa: ⚠ The **60%** male non-farm criterion is wrong; correct figure **75%** (**UPPSC 2010**).
**2011**: about **4,041** statutory and **3,892** census towns.
**Census 2027** keeps the **1981** census-town criteria.

42.s: How many million-plus cities were recorded in India in 2011?
42.x: India had 53 million-plus cities in 2011.
42.tq: Recall the census count while distinguishing it from the total number of towns.
xs: India had **53 million-plus** cities/UAs in **2011** — option **(3)**.
Largest UAs: **Greater Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata**.
xa: Highest slum share among million-plus: **Greater Visakhapatnam (~44%)**.
**Class I** = **1 lakh+**; Class I cities hold **70%** of urban population.
India is **3rd** in urban population after **China and USA**.

42.s: Which combination correctly states the criteria for a census town?
o: Population above 5,000; at least 50% of male workers in non-agricultural activities; density at least 1,000 persons per sq km
Population above 10,000; at least 50% of workers in non-agricultural activities; density at least 200 persons per sq km
Population above 20,000; at least 75% of total workers in non-agricultural activities; density at least 400 persons per sq km
Population above 5,000; at least 75% of male workers in non-agricultural activities; density at least 400 persons per sq km
42.x: A census town has a population exceeding 5,000, at least 75% of male workers engaged in non-agricultural work and a density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre.
42.tq: Check all three numerical thresholds before selecting the combination.
xs: A census town needs population **≥5,000**, **≥75%** of **male workers** in non-agricultural work and density **≥400/sq km** — option **(4)**.
It is **administratively a village** that meets **all 3** criteria.
xa: ⚠ **Trap**: "**60%** of males" is wrong — correct is **75%** (**UPPSC 2010**).
**RGI** retains census towns for **Census 2027** despite **MoHUA's** objection.
**2011**: about **3,892** census towns vs **4,041** statutory towns.

42.s: India’s level of urbanisation increased from 27.81% in 2001 to approximately what level in 2011?
42.x: The urbanisation rate rose from 27.81% in 2001 to 31.16% in 2011.
42.tq: Compare the two census percentages and identify the later figure.
xs: Urbanisation rose from **27.81% (2001)** to **31.16% (2011)** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **31.80%** printed in some notes is wrong (**UPPSC 2023**).
xa: Urban population **37.71 crore** in **2011**; rural **68.84%**.
Phases: **slow 1901-31**, **medium 1931-61**, **rapid 1961 onward**.

42.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the spatial importance of Indian cities:
1. Cities occupy about 3% of India’s land area.
2. Cities account for about 60% of India’s GDP.
3. Urban population is projected to reach approximately 60 crore by 2031.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
42.x: All three statements are correct: cities occupy about 3% of land, generate around 60% of GDP, and the urban population is projected to reach about 60 crore by 2031.
42.tq: Test a compact group of related quantitative statements.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Cities hold about **3% of land** but about **60% of GDP** — statements 1 and 2.
Urban population is projected at about **60 crore by 2031** — statement 3.
xa: Cities to host nearly **a billion people by 2050**; **>50%** of India urban by **2050**.
Doubling city size lifts productivity about **12%** (ES **2025-26**).
**Class I** cities hold **70%** of urban population.

42.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the least urbanised southern State referred to in the comparative data?
42.x: Andhra Pradesh, in the undivided-State comparison, had the lowest urbanisation level at about 33%, compared with Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
42.tq: Use the comparison figures to separate the similar southern-State options.
xs: The least urbanised southern State (**2011**) was **Andhra Pradesh** (undivided, about **33%**) — option **(4)**.
Comparison: **TN ~48%**, **Kerala ~48%**, **Karnataka ~39%**.
xa: Yet **Greater Visakhapatnam** had the **highest slum share (~44%)** among million-plus cities.
Most urbanised State: **Goa (~62%)**; least: **Himachal Pradesh (~10%)**.
Highest decadal urban growth 2001-11: **Sikkim**.

42.s: Which State recorded the highest decadal growth of urban population during 2001–2011?
42.x: Sikkim recorded the highest decadal growth of urban population during 2001–2011.
42.tq: Discriminate between a growth-rate fact and an urbanisation-level fact.
xs: **Sikkim** had the highest decadal urban growth in **2001-11** — option **(2)** (**UPPSC 2023**).
**Goa** was the **most urbanised** State (about **62%**), not the fastest-growing.
xa: Least urbanised: **Himachal Pradesh (~10%)**.
Least urbanised southern State: **Andhra Pradesh (~33%)**.
National level rose **27.81% → 31.16%**.

42.s:
Arrange the following phases of urbanisation in India in chronological order:
A. Rapid phase
B. Medium phase
C. Slow phase

Select the correct answer.
42.x: The slow phase occurred during 1901–1931, the medium phase during 1931–1961, and the rapid phase from 1961 onwards.
42.tq: Identify the time ranges and arrange the phases from earliest to latest.
xs: Order: **Slow → Medium → Rapid** — option **(2) C, B, A**.
xa: Urban population about **60 crore by 2031**.
About **68%** of the world urban by **2050** (UN).

42.s: The term ‘hidden urbanisation’ in the Indian context is associated with the estimate that India is approximately what percentage urban according to DEGURBA-based estimates?
42.x: DEGURBA-based estimates cited by the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister put India at about 63% urban, much higher than the Census figure.
42.tq: Distinguish an alternative spatial estimate from the official Census percentage.
xs: Satellite **DEGURBA** estimates put India about **63%** urban (**EAC-PM**, **2015** data) — option **(4)**.
Officially (**Census 2011**) India is only **31.16%** urban — the gap is "hidden urbanisation".
xa: Debate: India **under-counts** urbanisation, starving **peri-urban** areas of municipal funds.
**16th FC** gives an **Urbanisation Premium** for merging peri-urban villages.

42.s: According to the UN World Urbanization Prospects, approximately what share of the world's population is projected to live in urban areas by 2050?
42.x: The UN projects about 68% of the world to be urban by 2050 (a PYQ, linked to SDG 11). More than half (over 50%) of the world is already urban today, so 50% describes the present, not 2050; 58% and 80% are not the UN figures.
42.tq: World 2050 urban = 68%; already >50% now.
xs: The UN projects about **68 per cent** of the world urban by **2050** — option **(3)**.
**More than half** is already urban today (UNFPA SWOP), so **50%** is the present, not **2050**.
xa: It is a **PYQ** linked to **SDG 11**.
India's cities: nearly **a billion people by 2050**.

42.s:
Which of the following correctly distinguishes push and pull factors of urbanisation?
1. Rural unemployment is a push factor.
2. Urban employment opportunities are a pull factor.
3. Better urban amenities may act as a pull factor.
4. Monsoon failure can push rural workers towards cities.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
42.x: Rural unemployment and monsoon failure push people out of rural areas, while urban employment and amenities attract them to cities.
42.tq: Classify each factor as either an outward push or an urban pull.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Push**: **rural unemployment**; **monsoon failure** pushes the rural jobless to cities.
**Pull**: **urban jobs** and **amenities**.
xa: Exam angle: statement sets mixing push and pull are **usually all correct**.
**Migration** is the **major component** of urbanisation.
Other causes: **industrialisation**, commercialisation, transport, **reclassification**.

42.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the major component of urbanisation in India when natural increase in rural and urban areas is broadly similar?
42.x: Migration is the major component of urbanisation when natural increase in rural and urban areas is broadly similar.
42.tq: Identify the principal demographic component from the stated comparison.
xs: **Migration** is the major component, as **natural increase** is similar in rural and urban areas — option **(3)**.
**Monsoon failure** pushes the rural jobless to cities.
xa: Other causes: **industrialisation**, **commercialisation**, transport/communication, social change.
Also **natural growth** and **reclassification** (new towns).
**Population explosion + poverty-induced migration**.

42.s: The World Bank estimate cited for the number of slum dwellers in India is approximately
42.x: The cited World Bank estimate places India’s slum-dwelling population at approximately 177 million, the largest such population in the world.
42.tq: Separate the exact estimate from nearby rounded alternatives.
xs: The **World Bank** estimates **177 million** slum dwellers in India — the **largest in the world** — option **(3)**.
Highest slum share among million-plus (**2011**): **Greater Visakhapatnam ~44%**.
xa: **Greater Mumbai ~41%** and **Vijayawada ~41%**.
Urban **housing shortage**: about **18.78 million** units (**2012** Technical Group).
**Slum improvement** is a **Twelfth Schedule** function.

42.s: According to Census 2011 data cited for million-plus cities, which city had the highest proportion of its population living in slums?
42.x: Greater Visakhapatnam had the highest cited slum share among million-plus cities, at approximately 44%, compared with about 41% in Greater Mumbai and Vijayawada.
42.tq: Compare close percentages instead of selecting the more famous city.
xs: **Greater Visakhapatnam** (about **44%**) had the highest slum share among million-plus cities — option **(3)**.
**Greater Mumbai** and **Vijayawada** were about **41%** each.
xa: ⚠ Trap: highest is **Visakhapatnam**, **not Mumbai**.
**177 million** slum dwellers in India (**World Bank**).
AP paradox: least urbanised southern State, yet highest slum share city.

42.s: Which one of the following is a governance-related urban challenge identified in India?
o: Complete fiscal autonomy of all cities
Absence of any panchayats in rapidly urbanising areas
Uniform administrative control over all urban local bodies
Fragmented authority and limited fiscal autonomy of cities
42.x: Fragmented authority and inadequate fiscal autonomy constrain city governance. Rapidly urbanising areas may also remain under panchayat administration.
42.tq: Use the governance lens to identify the institutional constraint.
xs: **Fragmented authority** and cities' **lack of fiscal autonomy** (ES **2025-26**) — option **(4)**.
Rapidly urbanising areas are often **left under panchayats** — so option (2) is wrong.
xa: **Property tax** is the most important own revenue of ULBs.
**Twelfth Schedule** lists **18 functions** for municipalities.
Official **31%** vs satellite **63%** — under-counting starves peri-urban areas of funds.

42.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the most important source of own revenue of urban local bodies?
42.x: Property tax is the most important source of own revenue for urban local bodies. Other sources include advertisement tax, professional tax, fees, fines and municipal enterprises.
42.tq: Identify the principal item in a list of municipal revenue sources.
xs: **Property tax** is the most important own revenue of ULBs — option **(2)**.
Others: **advertisement tax**, **professional tax**, **octroi**, fees, fines, municipal enterprises.
xa: **State grants** come on top of own revenue.
**16th FC (2026-31)**: **Rs 3.6 lakh crore** for ULBs (**45%**).
First **municipal bond**: **Bangalore Mahanagara Palike (1997)**.

42.s: The Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution contains how many functions assigned to municipalities?
42.x: The Twelfth Schedule contains 18 functions relating to urban local governance.
42.tq: Test the constitutional schedule number through a direct numerical recall question.
xs: The **Twelfth Schedule** has **18 functions** for municipalities — option **(2)**.
They include **urban planning**, **land-use regulation**, **water supply**, **public health and sanitation**, **slum improvement**.
xa: Also **urban poverty alleviation**, **fire services**, **urban forestry**, **vital statistics**.
**Property tax** is the main own revenue source.
**MoHUA** formed in **2017** by merging **MoUD and MoHUPA**.

42.s: Which urban local body issued the first municipal bond in India?
42.x: The first municipal bond in India was issued by Bangalore Mahanagara Palike in 1997.
42.tq: Match the pioneering institution with the year-specific financial innovation.
xs: India's first municipal bond: **Bangalore Mahanagara Palike** in **1997** — option **(3)**.
**Ahmedabad (1998)** was the first **without a State guarantee**.
xa: **Budget 2026-27**: **Rs 100 crore** incentive for a single issue above **Rs 1,000 crore**.
**City Economic Regions**: **Rs 5,000 crore per CER** over **5 years**.
**MoHUA** formed **2017**.

42.s: Which municipal corporation was the first in India to issue a municipal bond without a State Government guarantee?
42.x: Ahmedabad was the first municipal corporation to issue a municipal bond without a State Government guarantee, in 1998.
42.tq: Discriminate between the first municipal bond and the first bond issued without a State guarantee.
xs: **Ahmedabad** (**1998**) issued the first municipal bond **without a State guarantee** — option **(1)**.
⚠ The very first municipal bond was **Bangalore Mahanagara Palike (1997)**.
xa: **Budget 2026-27**: **Rs 100 crore** incentive for an issue above **Rs 1,000 crore**.
**Property tax** is the most important own revenue.
**CERs** get **Rs 5,000 crore** each over **5 years**.

42.s:
With reference to Finance Commission grants to urban local bodies, consider the following statements:
1. Under the 15th Finance Commission, urban local bodies received 36% of local body grants.
2. The 16th Finance Commission raises the urban share to 45%.
3. Under the 16th Finance Commission, 80% is basic grant and 20% is performance grant.
4. Half of the basic grants are tied to sanitation, waste and water.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
42.x: The 15th Finance Commission allocated 36% of local body grants to urban local bodies. The 16th Finance Commission provides a 45% urban share, with 80% basic and 20% performance grants, and half of the basic grants tied to sanitation, waste and water.
42.tq: Combine percentage, grant composition and tied-purpose details in one coded statement question.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Statement 1: **15th FC (2021-26)** gave ULBs **36%** of local body grants — correct.
Statements 2-3: **16th FC (2026-31)** gives ULBs **45%**, split **80% basic / 20% performance** — correct.
Statement 4: **half of basic grants** are tied to **sanitation, waste, water** — correct.
xa: 16th FC: **Rs 3.6 lakh crore** ULBs vs **Rs 4.4 lakh crore** RLBs.
**Urbanisation Premium** for merging **peri-urban villages**.
**Local Finance Enquiry (1963)**: **K. Santhanam**.

42.s: The Local Finance Enquiry Committee of 1963, which examined the finances of local bodies, was chaired by:
42.x: K. Santhanam chaired the Local Finance Enquiry Committee (1963). Balwantrai Mehta (1957) and Ashok Mehta (1977-78) headed committees on panchayati raj; A. D. Gorwala chaired the All India Rural Credit Survey Committee (1951).
42.tq: Local finance 1963 = Santhanam.
xs: The **Local Finance Enquiry Committee (1963)** was chaired by **K. Santhanam** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **A.D. Gorwala** chaired the **All India Rural Credit Survey Committee** (RBI, **1951**), not this one.
xa: **Property tax** is the most important own revenue of ULBs.
**15th FC**: ULBs got **36%** of local body grants.
**16th FC**: **45%**, with an **Urbanisation Premium**.

42.s: Which Sustainable Development Goal is most directly associated with UN-Habitat’s urban-settlement mandate?
42.x: SDG 11 seeks to make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable, directly corresponding to the UN-Habitat mandate.
42.tq: Match the specialised agency’s mandate with the relevant SDG.
xs: **SDG 11** — **Sustainable Cities and Communities** — matches UN-Habitat's mandate — option **(2)**.
**UN-Habitat** (UN Human Settlements Programme) was set up in **1978** after **Habitat I (Vancouver, 1976)**.
xa: UN-Habitat HQ: **Nairobi**; publishes the **World Cities Report**.
About **68%** of the world urban by **2050** (PYQ linked to SDG 11).
A **UN-Habitat CoE** is to be set up in **Amaravati**.

42.s: The concept of ‘Right to the City’ is associated with which thinker?
42.x: The concept of the Right to the City was articulated by Henri Lefebvre in 1968.
42.tq: Match the concept with its originator and associated year.
xs: **Right to the City** is **Henri Lefebvre's** idea (**1968**) — option **(3)**.
It means residents, **including migrant workers**, can **shape and live in the city**.
xa: Adopted in the **New Urban Agenda** at **Habitat III (Quito, 2016)**.
**Habitat I**: **Vancouver 1976**; **UN-Habitat HQ**: **Nairobi**.
**APMCHUD**: first meet **New Delhi, 2006**.

42.s: The Right to the City was adopted in the New Urban Agenda at
42.x: The Right to the City was adopted in the New Urban Agenda at Habitat III, held in Quito in 2016.
42.tq: Match the forum, location and year without confusing the Habitat conferences.
xs: Right to the City entered the **New Urban Agenda** at **Habitat III, Quito, 2016** — option **(2)**.
**Habitat I** was at **Vancouver** in **1976** (option 3) — it led to UN-Habitat in **1978**.
xa: Concept by **Henri Lefebvre** (**1968**).
⚠ Habitat I = **Vancouver 1976**; Habitat III = **Quito 2016**; HQ = **Nairobi**.
**SDG 11**: Sustainable Cities and Communities.

42.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
42.x: Habitat I was held in Vancouver in 1976. Nairobi is the headquarters of UN-Habitat, which was set up in 1978 after Habitat I.
42.tq: Use the event-place-year association to identify the deliberately swapped location and date.
xs: **Habitat I — Nairobi, 1978** is wrong — option **(4)**; Habitat I was at **Vancouver** in **1976**.
**Nairobi** is **UN-Habitat's HQ**, and **1978** is when UN-Habitat was set up.
Pairs (1), (2), (3) are correct; **Habitat III** was **Quito 2016**.
xa: UN-Habitat publishes the **World Cities Report**.
**Right to the City** (**Lefebvre**, **1968**) adopted at Habitat III.
A **UN-Habitat CoE** is to be set up in **Amaravati**.

42.s: The World Cities Report is published by:
o: Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister
42.x: UN-Habitat publishes the World Cities Report.
42.tq: Identify the responsible international institution rather than an Indian urban-data agency.
xs: The **World Cities Report** is published by **UN-Habitat** — option **(2)**.
UN-Habitat (**UN Human Settlements Programme**) was set up in **1978** after **Habitat I (Vancouver, 1976)**; HQ **Nairobi**.
**APMCHUD** is a ministerial conference; the **RGI** runs the Census; **EAC-PM** gave the DEGURBA estimate.
xa: **Habitat III** (**Quito, 2016**) adopted the **New Urban Agenda**, including the **Right to the City**.
A **UN-Habitat CoE** is to be set up in **Amaravati**.
Linked goal: **SDG 11** — Sustainable Cities and Communities.

42.s: In the context of Satavahana administration, the term 'Nigama Sabha' referred to
o: A military council of the Satavahana kings
42.x: Nigama Sabha denoted city administration under the Satavahanas and is mentioned in the Nanaghat inscription.
42.tq: Discriminate between an urban administrative institution and other possible historical bodies.
xs: **Nigama Sabha** was the **city administration** under the **Satavahanas** — option **(1)**.
It is known from the **Nanaghat inscription**.
xa: Modern AP capital: **Amaravati** (AP Capital Region).
Today's urban functions are listed in the **Twelfth Schedule** (**18 functions**).
**Right to the City** (**Henri Lefebvre**, **1968**) is the modern idea of citizen participation.

42.s: The evidence for the Satavahana institution known as Nigama Sabha is associated with the
42.x: The Nanaghat inscription is associated with the reference to Nigama Sabha as a city-administration institution under the Satavahanas.
42.tq: Pair the historical institution with its specific epigraphic source.
xs: The **Nigama Sabha** is attested in the **Nanaghat inscription** — option **(2)**.
It denoted **city administration** under the **Satavahanas**.
xa: AP capital today: **Amaravati**, where a **UN-Habitat CoE** is planned.
AP's urban water vision: "**One Water, One City, One Future**".
**Visakhapatnam** has the highest slum share (about **44%**) among million-plus cities.

42.s: The Andhra Pradesh Government signed an MoU with UN-Habitat for establishing a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs at:
42.x: The MoU with UN-Habitat concerns a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs in Amaravati.
42.tq: Use the location-specific state current-affairs clue and avoid substituting a national headquarters.
xs: The **UN-Habitat** Centre of Excellence is to be set up at **Amaravati** — option **(4)**.
Amaravati is the **AP Capital Region**.
xa: **UN-Habitat**: set up **1978**, HQ **Nairobi**, publishes the **World Cities Report**.
**APMCHUD** first met in **New Delhi** (**2006**).
⚠ Habitat I = **Vancouver 1976**; Habitat III = **Quito 2016**.

42.s: Which of the following best expresses the criticism concerning India's measurement of urbanisation?
o: Official estimates show 31%, while satellite estimates show 63%.
Official estimates show 63%, while satellite estimates show 31%.
Both official and satellite estimates show 31%.
Both official and satellite estimates show 63%.
42.x: The criticism is that official data place urbanisation at about 31%, whereas satellite-based assessment places it at about 63%, resulting in under-counting of urbanisation.
42.tq: Read the reversed comparison carefully and preserve the correct source-percentage pairing.
xs: **Official** urbanisation is about **31%**, but **satellite** estimates show about **63%** — option **(1)**.
Options (2)-(4) reverse or merge the two figures.
xa: Criticism: India **under-counts** urbanisation, **starving peri-urban areas** of municipal funds.
**Census 2027** keeps the **1981** census-town criteria.

42.s: The alleged under-counting of urbanisation is criticised primarily because it may
o: Eliminate all rural settlements from the census
Starve peri-urban areas of municipal funds
Reduce the number of municipal bonds issued by Ahmedabad
Increase the constitutional powers of municipalities
42.x: Under-counting urbanisation can leave peri-urban areas outside adequate municipal planning and finance, thereby starving them of municipal funds.
42.tq: Move from the measurement problem to its stated governance and finance consequence.
xs: Under-counting **starves peri-urban areas of municipal funds** — option **(2)**.
Official **31%** vs satellite **63%** means many urban-like areas stay **under panchayats**.
xa: **16th FC** offers an **Urbanisation Premium** for merging **peri-urban villages**.
**RGI** retains census towns for **Census 2027** despite MoHUA's objection.

42.s: Which Ministry was formed in 2017 by merging the Ministry of Urban Development and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
42.x: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs was formed in 2017 by merging the Ministry of Urban Development and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation.
42.tq: Use the institutional-merger trap by matching the new ministry with its predecessor ministries.
xs: **MoHUA** — **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs** — formed in **2017** by merging **MoUD and MoHUPA** — option **(1)**.
MoHUA objected to census towns before the **Parliamentary Standing Committee** on Housing and Urban Affairs.
xa: That committee's chair: **Magunta Sreenivasulu Reddy**.
**RGI** still retains census towns for **Census 2027**.
First municipal bond: **Bangalore 1997**.

43.s:
Arrange the following urban schemes in chronological order of their launch:
A. Smart Cities Mission
B. JNNURM
C. Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban
D. AMRUT
43.x: JNNURM was launched in December 2005, SBM-Urban on 2 October 2014, and AMRUT and the Smart Cities Mission were launched in June 2015.
43.tq: Fix the earliest and latest schemes first, then place the 2014 and 2015 launches.
xs: Order: **JNNURM → SBM-Urban → AMRUT/Smart Cities** — option **(1) B, C, D, A**.
**JNNURM**: **Dec 2005**; **SBM-Urban**: **2 Oct 2014**; **AMRUT** and **Smart Cities**: **June 2015** (same day).
xa: **PMAY-U** was launched the same day in **June 2015**.
**JNNURM** was the **first mega urban mission**.
**Rurban Mission (SPMRM)** came in **2016** — rural focus.

43.s:
Which of the following were components of JNNURM concerned with urban poor housing and slum development?
1. Basic Services to the Urban Poor
2. Integrated Housing and Slum Development Programme
3. Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme
4. In-situ Slum Redevelopment
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
43.x: BSUP and IHSDP were JNNURM components. CLSS and ISSR are associated with PMAY-U, not JNNURM.
43.tq: Separate JNNURM components from similarly themed PMAY-U verticals.
xs: JNNURM's components were **BSUP** (Basic Services for Urban Poor) and **IHSDP** (Integrated Housing and Slum Development) — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**CLSS** and **ISSR** are **PMAY-U** verticals, not JNNURM.
xa: JNNURM reform: **25% of municipal budget** for the urban poor.
**25% of developed land** reserved for **EWS/LIG**.
**7-point charter**: tenure, housing, water, sanitation, education, health, social security.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about JNNURM reforms:
1. 25% of the municipal budget was to be earmarked for the urban poor.
2. 25% of developed land was to be reserved for EWS/LIG.
3. Its seven-point charter included export promotion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x: Statement 1 is correct: 25% of the municipal budget for the urban poor. Statement 2 is correct: 25% of developed land for EWS/LIG. Statement 3 is wrong: the seven-point charter covered tenure, housing, water, sanitation, education, health and social security, not export promotion. So '1 only' misses 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include 3.
43.tq: JNNURM: two 25% rules and a 7-point charter of basic services.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **25% of municipal budget** for the urban poor — correct.
Statement 2: **25% of developed land** for **EWS/LIG** — correct.
Statement 3: the **7-point charter** covered **tenure, housing, water, sanitation, education, health, social security** — no export promotion — wrong.
xa: JNNURM components: **BSUP** and **IHSDP**.
JNNURM (**Dec 2005**) = **first mega urban mission**.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about AMRUT:
1. It initially covered 500 cities, which became 485 after 15 were merged.
2. It covers about 65% of India's urban population.
3. Its total outlay was Rs 1 lakh crore, of which the central share was Rs 75,000 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x: Statement 1 is correct: 500 cities, 15 merged, leaving 485. Statement 2 is correct: coverage is about 65% of the urban population (some sources say ~60%). Statement 3 is wrong: the outlay of Rs 1 lakh crore included a central share of Rs 50,000 crore, not Rs 75,000 crore. So '1 only' misses 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include 3.
43.tq: AMRUT: 500 to 485 cities, ~65% urban population, Rs 1 lakh crore with Rs 50,000 crore central.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **500 cities** at start, **15 merged** → **485** — correct.
Statement 2: covers about **65%** of urban population (some notes say about **60%**) — correct.
Statement 3: outlay **Rs 1 lakh crore** with **Rs 50,000 crore** central, not Rs 75,000 crore — wrong.
xa: Period **2015-16 to 2019-20**, extended to **Sept 2025**.
States submit **State Annual Action Plans**.

43.s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for inclusion as an AMRUT mission city?
o: Urban Local Bodies with population of one lakh or more
Every village with a population below one lakh
43.x: AMRUT includes ULBs with population of one lakh or more, capitals, HRIDAY cities, river-stem cities, hill-state, island and tourist cities. Every village below one lakh is not a criterion.
43.tq: Identify the option that changes an urban selection criterion into a universal rural rule.
xs: **Every village below one lakh** is not a criterion — option **(4)**; AMRUT is for **ULBs**.
Mission cities: ULBs with **1 lakh+**, **State/UT capitals**, all **HRIDAY** cities — options (1)-(3).
xa: Also cities on **stems of main rivers**, **hill-State, island and tourist** cities.
PYQ: **Dausa** was **not** a Rajasthan mission city.
About **65%** of urban population covered.

43.s: Which of the following is NOT a thrust area of AMRUT?
43.x: AMRUT’s thrust areas include water supply, sewerage and septage, storm-water drains, green spaces and parks, non-motorised transport and capacity building. Crop procurement is unrelated.
43.tq: Separate urban-service components from an agricultural-sector activity.
xs: **Crop procurement** is not an AMRUT thrust area — option **(2)**.
Thrust areas: **water supply; sewerage and septage; storm-water drains; green spaces and parks; non-motorised urban transport; capacity building**.
xa: **AMRUT 2.0**: **100% sewerage/septage** in the **500** AMRUT cities.
Urban **tap connectivity** up **64% since 2011**.
Projects worth **Rs 2.79 lakh crore** sanctioned under AMRUT + 2.0.

43.s: AMRUT 2.0, launched in 2021 and continuing up to 2025-26, seeks universal water supply in:
43.x: AMRUT 2.0 aims at universal water supply in all statutory towns.
43.tq: Distinguish universal statutory-town coverage from the separate 500-city sewerage target.
xs: **AMRUT 2.0** aims at universal water supply in **all statutory towns** — option **(4)**.
**100% sewerage/septage** is targeted in the **500** AMRUT cities, not all towns.
xa: Also **water-body rejuvenation**, **outcome-based funding**, support to **JJM-Urban**.
AMRUT + 2.0: **Rs 2.79 lakh crore** of projects sanctioned.
AP mobilised about **Rs 19,561 crore** under AMRUT 2.0 and other sources (Jul **2026**).

43.s: Which one of the following cities of Rajasthan was NOT an AMRUT mission city?
43.x: AMRUT mission cities include State capitals (Jaipur), all HRIDAY cities (Ajmer) and ULBs with 1 lakh+ population (Jodhpur). Dausa did not meet any criterion and was the PYQ answer.
43.tq: Capital, HRIDAY or 1 lakh+ = AMRUT city; Dausa = none.
xs: **Dausa** was **not** an AMRUT mission city — option **(3)** (PYQ).
Mission cities include **State capitals**, all **HRIDAY** cities (Ajmer is one) and ULBs with **1 lakh+** population.
xa: Also cities on **stems of main rivers** and **hill-State, island, tourist** cities.
**500** cities initially, **485** after mergers.
About **65%** of urban population covered.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about the Smart Cities Mission:
1. It was launched in June 2015 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
2. Its 100 cities were selected through a competitive challenge.
3. Smart Cities were shared among States giving equal weight to urban population and the number of districts of each State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x: Statement 1 is correct: MoHUA launched it in June 2015. Statement 2 is correct: 100 cities were chosen by a two-stage competitive challenge. Statement 3 is wrong: equal weight was given to urban population and the number of statutory towns, not districts. So '1 only' misses 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include 3.
43.tq: State share = urban population + statutory towns (not districts).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **MoHUA** launched it in **June 2015** — correct.
Statement 2: **100 cities** chosen by a competitive **challenge** — correct.
Statement 3: equal weight was to **urban population** and **number of statutory towns**, not districts — wrong.
xa: Selection: **two-stage**, **four rounds** from **Jan 2016**; last city **June 2018**.
Central support: **Rs 48,000 crore**.

43.s: Which of the following combinations correctly describes the two components of the Smart Cities Mission approach?
o: Rural cluster development and river-basin planning
Area-Based Development and Pan-City technology solutions
Universal rural housing and crop insurance
43.x: The approach combines Area-Based Development with Pan-City technology solutions. Area-Based Development includes retrofitting or redevelopment of a minimum 50 acres.
43.tq: Match the mission’s paired design components with their exact terminology.
xs: The two components are **Area-Based Development** and **Pan-City** tech solutions — option **(2)**.
**ABD** = retrofitting/redevelopment of min. **50 acres**; **Pan-City** = tech, **Integrated Command and Control Centres**.
xa: Each city has an **SPV** under the **Companies Act 2013**.
Criticism: **elite bias** of ABD.
Vizag: **integrated command centre** + **intelligent traffic system**.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about the Special Purpose Vehicle under the Smart Cities Mission:
1. One SPV is created for each city.
2. It is a company under the Companies Act, 2013.
3. Its equity is shared equally by the State or Union Territory and the Urban Local Body.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: Each Smart City has an SPV registered as a company under the Companies Act, 2013, with 50:50 equity participation by the State/UT and the ULB.
43.tq: Verify institutional structure, legal status and ownership separately.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**One SPV per city**, a company under the **Companies Act 2013**.
Equity is **50:50** between the **State/UT** and the **ULB**.
xa: Centre: **Rs 48,000 crore**, matched by State/ULB.
Other sources: **FC grants, municipal bonds, PPP, loans, convergence**.
Progress (**11 Jul 2025**): **7,636 (95%)** of **8,063** projects done.

43.s: CITIIS 2.0, launched in 2023, is associated with how many Smart Cities and with which broad area?
43.x: CITIIS 2.0 covers 18 Smart Cities and focuses on integrated waste management, with AFD, KfW, the EU and NIUA as associated partners.
43.tq: Combine the programme’s coverage number with its distinctive thematic focus.
xs: **CITIIS 2.0 (2023)** covers **18 smart cities** for **integrated waste management** — option **(2)**.
Partners: **AFD, KfW, EU** and **NIUA**.
xa: Smart Cities Mission has **100** cities.
**SBM-Urban** aims at **ODF** and scientific **solid waste management**.
AP: waste segregation **96.07%**; **6,890 TPD** processed (**2024-25**).

43.s: Which criticism of the Smart Cities Mission relates specifically to the Area-Based Development approach?
o: It is financed only through agricultural taxes
43.x: Area-Based Development has been criticised for elite bias, while weak revenue generation has raised concerns about sustaining created assets.
43.tq: Link the criticism to the component it directly concerns.
xs: **Area-Based Development** is criticised for **elite bias** — option **(1)**.
The other criticism is **weak revenue** to sustain assets.
xa: ABD = min. **50 acres** retrofitting/redevelopment.
**Pan-City** uses tech solutions and command centres.
Wider debate: schemes **sector-specific, under-utilised**; ULBs lack capacity to borrow.

43.s: HRIDAY stands for:
o: National Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana
Heritage Rejuvenation and Integrated Development of All Yards
Housing and Renewal Initiative for Developed Urban Areas
Heritage Roads and Infrastructure Development Yojana
43.x: HRIDAY is the National Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana, launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
43.tq: Test the exact expansion of the acronym against plausible look-alike expansions.
xs: HRIDAY = **National Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana** — option **(1)**.
Launched in **2015** by **MoHUA**.
xa: Aim: **heritage-sensitive planning** of **cultural, natural, living and built** heritage.
**12 cities**, including **Amaravati (AP)** and **Warangal**.
All HRIDAY cities are also **AMRUT** mission cities.

43.s: Which one of the following is the Andhra Pradesh city included in HRIDAY?
43.x: Amaravati is the Andhra Pradesh city included among the 12 HRIDAY cities.
43.tq: Use the state-specific membership fact rather than the broader list of urban schemes.
xs: **Amaravati** is AP's HRIDAY city — option **(2)**.
**Visakhapatnam, Tirupati, Kakinada** are AP **smart cities**, not HRIDAY cities.
xa: ⚠ HRIDAY cities from the Telugu states = **Amaravati** and **Warangal**.
HRIDAY has **12 cities**.
AP angle: **four smart cities**; Amaravati an HRIDAY city; **UN-Habitat MoU** (Jul **2026**).

43.s: Which of the following correctly lists only HRIDAY cities?
o: Indore, Surat, Ahmedabad and Navi Mumbai
43.x: Ajmer, Amritsar, Badami and Dwarka are all included in the HRIDAY list. The other options contain cities from other programmes or cities not in the HRIDAY list.
43.tq: Start with membership certainty and eliminate lists containing non-HRIDAY cities.
xs: **Ajmer, Amritsar, Badami and Dwarka** are all HRIDAY cities — option **(1)**.
Kakinada, Tirupati, Visakhapatnam, Indore, Surat, Dausa are **not** in the HRIDAY list.
xa: Full list (**12**): Ajmer, **Amaravati**, Amritsar, Badami, Dwarka, Gaya, Kanchipuram, Mathura, Puri, Varanasi, Velankanni, **Warangal**.
HRIDAY: **2015**, MoHUA.
All HRIDAY cities qualify as **AMRUT** mission cities.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about PMAY-Urban:
1. It was launched in 2015 under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
2. It aims to provide pucca all-weather houses only in million-plus cities.
3. PMAY-U 2.0 (2024) aims at 1 crore more urban houses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x: Statement 1 is correct: PMAY-U began in 2015 under MoHUA. Statement 2 is wrong: it covers all statutory towns, not only million-plus cities. Statement 3 is correct: PMAY-U 2.0 (2024) targets 1 crore more urban houses. So '1 only' misses 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include 2.
43.tq: PMAY-U covers all statutory towns.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **PMAY-U** since **2015** under **MoHUA** — correct.
Statement 2: houses are for **all statutory towns**, not only million-plus cities — wrong.
Statement 3: **PMAY-U 2.0 (2024)** targets **1 crore** more urban houses — correct.
xa: Sanctions: **1.25 crore+** houses under PMAY-U and 2.0.
Budget **2026-27** **trimmed PMAY-U**.

43.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the verticals of PMAY-U:
List-I (Vertical)
 a. ISSR
 b. CLSS
 c. AHP
 d. BLC
List-II (Type)
 i. Central Sector
 ii. Centrally Sponsored Scheme

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
43.x: ISSR, AHP and BLC are Centrally Sponsored Schemes, whereas CLSS is a Central Sector scheme.
43.tq: Start with the sure CLSS pair and then complete the remaining classification.
xs: **CLSS** is **Central Sector**; **ISSR, AHP, BLC** are **CSS** — option **(1) a–ii, b–i, c–ii, d–ii**.
**ISSR** uses **land as resource**; **AHP** = Affordable Housing in Partnership; **BLC** = Beneficiary-led Construction.
xa: ⚠ **CLSS** = the **only Central Sector** vertical.
**PMAY-U 2.0** verticals: **BLC, AHP, Affordable Rental Housing, Interest Subsidy Scheme**.
**1.25 crore+** houses sanctioned.

43.s: Which of the following is NOT a vertical under PMAY-U 2.0?
43.x: PMAY-U 2.0 includes BLC, AHP, Affordable Rental Housing and the Interest Subsidy Scheme. ISSR belongs to the earlier PMAY-U vertical structure.
43.tq: Distinguish the revised verticals from the earlier scheme’s verticals.
xs: **In-situ Slum Redevelopment (ISSR)** is not a PMAY-U 2.0 vertical — option **(3)**.
PMAY-U 2.0 verticals: **BLC**, **AHP**, **Affordable Rental Housing**, **Interest Subsidy Scheme**.
xa: ISSR was a vertical of the original **PMAY-U (2015)**, a **CSS**.
PMAY-U 2.0 (**2024**): **1 crore** more urban houses.
**CLSS** was the only **Central Sector** vertical.

43.s: The Global Housing Technology Challenge-India is associated with which objective?
o: Replacing municipal bodies with private corporations
Mainstreaming innovative and disaster-resilient construction technologies
Providing crop insurance to urban farmers
43.x: GHTC-India, under MoHUA, seeks to mainstream innovative and disaster-resilient construction technologies.
43.tq: Match the named challenge with its distinctive technological objective.
xs: **GHTC-India** mainstreams **innovative, disaster-resilient construction technologies** — option **(2)** (PYQ).
It is run by **MoHUA**.
xa: **Light House Projects**: **Indore, Rajkot, Chennai, Ranchi, Agartala, Lucknow**.
Foundation laid **Jan 2021**.
**PMAY-U** gives **pucca all-weather houses**.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about the Urban Infrastructure Development Fund (UIDF):
1. It was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24.
2. It is managed by NABARD.
3. It is meant for Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x: Statement 1 is correct: UIDF was announced in Budget 2023-24. Statement 2 is wrong: it is managed by the National Housing Bank (NHB), not NABARD. Statement 3 is correct: it targets Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities. So '1 only' misses 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include 2.
43.tq: UIDF: Budget 2023-24, NHB, Tier-2/3 cities, funded by PSL shortfall.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **UIDF** announced in **Union Budget 2023-24** — correct.
Statement 2: managed by the **National Housing Bank (NHB)**, not NABARD — wrong.
Statement 3: for **Tier-2 and Tier-3** cities — correct.
xa: Funded from **priority sector lending shortfall**, about **Rs 10,000 crore a year**.
**APPSC G1 2024** PYQ: only statement III valid.

43.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Urban Infrastructure Development Fund:
1. It is funded from the priority sector lending shortfall of banks.
2. It is funded through Government securities issued by the Union Government.
3. Its annual size is approximately Rs. 10,000 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x: UIDF is funded from banks’ priority sector lending shortfall and is approximately Rs. 10,000 crore annually. It is not funded from G-Sec bonds.
43.tq: Split the funding source from the approximate fund size; the G-Sec statement is the trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
UIDF is funded from banks' **priority sector lending shortfall**, about **Rs 10,000 crore a year** — statements 1 and 3.
Statement 2 is wrong: it is **not** funded by **G-Sec** bonds.
xa: ⚠ UIDF money = **PSL shortfall**, managed by **NHB**.
Announced in **Union Budget 2023-24**; for **Tier-2 and Tier-3** cities.

43.s: Under the Urban Challenge Fund, the Centre will fund what proportion of a project’s cost when a city raises at least 50 per cent through bonds, loans or public-private partnerships?
43.x: The Urban Challenge Fund provides central funding equal to 25 per cent of the project cost, subject to the city raising at least 50 per cent through specified sources.
43.tq: Link the qualifying condition with the precise central funding share.
xs: The Centre funds **25%** of project cost — option **(3) 25 per cent**.
The condition: the city raises **50%+** through **bonds, loans or PPP**.
xa: **UIDF** (**2023-24**) is a separate fund from **PSL shortfall**, managed by **NHB**.
AP mobilised about **Rs 19,561 crore** via AMRUT 2.0, AIIB, **Urban Challenge Fund**, UIDF, SBM 2.0.
Critique: ULBs **lack fiscal capacity to borrow**.

43.s: Which of the following is NOT an Andhra Pradesh city listed under the Smart Cities Mission?
43.x: The listed Andhra Pradesh Smart Cities are Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Tirupati and Amaravati. Warangal is not an Andhra Pradesh city in this list.
43.tq: Use state identity and the listed mission-city set to eliminate the outsider.
xs: **Warangal** is not an AP smart city — option **(2)**; it is a **HRIDAY** city.
**Vizag, Kakinada and Tirupati** reported progress on smart-city works (Apr **2026**).
xa: AP has **four smart cities**.
⚠ HRIDAY cities from the Telugu states: **Amaravati** and **Warangal**.
Vizag projects: **integrated command centre** + **intelligent traffic system**.

43.s: Anna Canteens in Andhra Pradesh provide meals to the urban poor at a price of:
43.x: Anna Canteens provide meals for Rs. 5 to the urban poor.
