APCNF covers **10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha** (2025-26).
⚠ Swaminathan = "Evergreen Revolution"; Palekar = ZBNF.

48.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh Community Managed Natural Farming (APCNF)?
o: It is run by RySS and uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham.
It is run by APEDA and uses only imported chemical fertilisers.
It is run by GEAC and regulates commercial GM crops.
It is run by NARS and releases climate-resilient seed varieties.
48.x: APCNF is run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS) and uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham.
48.tq: Identify the implementing body and the characteristic inputs together.
xs: **APCNF** is run by **Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS)** and uses **jeevamrutham** and **ghanajeevamrutham** — option **(1)** is correct.
**APEDA** runs NPOP; **GEAC** approves GM crops; **NARS** released climate-resilient varieties.
xa: Coverage: **10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha** (2025-26); some notes say **7 lakh+** farmers.
Won the **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024**.
APCNF is called a **global natural-farming model**.

48.s: APCNF received which award for the year 2024?
o: Sardar Patel Outstanding ICAR Institute Award
World Food Prize for Seed Innovation
48.x: APCNF won the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity in 2024.
48.tq: Match the programme with its specific award and year.
xs: **APCNF** won the **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024** — option **(2)** is correct.
APCNF is run by **Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS)**.
xa: It covers **10.20 lakh farmers** on **4.89 lakh ha** (2025-26).
It uses **jeevamrutham** and **ghanajeevamrutham**.
⚠ ZBNF itself was developed by **Subhash Palekar**.

48.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NMSA:
1. It is one of the eight missions under NAPCC.
2. It was merged into PM-RKVY from 2022–23.
3. Its components include Soil Health Management and the agroforestry sub-mission ‘Har Medh Par Ped’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: All three statements are correct. NMSA is one of the eight NAPCC missions, was merged into PM-RKVY from 2022–23, and includes the listed components.
48.tq: Combine institutional status, transition year and component details in a coded statement question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1 correct: **NMSA** is one of **8 NAPCC missions**.
Statement 2 correct: merged into **PM-RKVY since 2022-23**.
Statement 3 correct: components include **Soil Health Management** and the agroforestry sub-mission "**Har Medh Par Ped**".
xa: Another component: **Rainfed Area Development** (Integrated Farming Systems).
**Soil Health Cards** are issued **free every two years** under NMSA.

48.s: Glyricidia is used in agriculture mainly as a:
48.x: Glyricidia is a green leaf manure (PYQ key). Neem-based products are the bio-pesticides, Kamala is a genome-edited rice, and Nano Urea or Nano DAP are the nano fertilisers.
48.tq: Glyricidia = green leaf manure.
xs: **Glyricidia** is a **green leaf manure** — option **(1)** is correct (PYQ key).
**Neem-based pesticides** are the bio-pesticides; **Kamala** is a genome-edited rice; **Nano Urea/DAP** are nano fertilisers.
xa: **Vermicompost**: earthworms turn organic waste into rich manure (PYQ key).
AP green manure seeds: **sunn hemp (Jilledu)**, **dhaincha (Janumu)**, green gram.

48.s: Under the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY, 2015), each organic farming cluster consists of:
48.x: PKVY promotes cluster-based organic farming with 50 farmers and 50 acres per cluster, certified through PGS-India or NPOP. The other combinations are not the PKVY norm.
48.tq: PKVY cluster = 50 farmers / 50 acres.
xs: **PKVY (2015)** clusters have **50 farmers covering 50 acres** — option **(1)** is correct.
Certification is through **PGS-India** or **NPOP**.
xa: **NPOP** (**2001**) runs under the Commerce Ministry/**APEDA**.
AP added **200 new clusters** in Visakhapatnam's tribal areas.

48.s:
The Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971 provide for the establishment of which of the following bodies?
1. Central Insecticides Board
2. Registration Committee
3. National Pesticides Tribunal
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: The Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules, 1971 set up the Central Insecticides Board and the Registration Committee. A National Pesticides Tribunal is not mentioned as a body created by these provisions.
48.tq: Identify the correctly stated statutory bodies and reject the invented institutional name.
xs: Items 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
The **Insecticides Act, 1968** + **Rules, 1971** set up the **Central Insecticides Board** and the **Registration Committee**.
No "National Pesticides Tribunal" is set up by them.
xa: The **Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025** would replace them (comments due **4 Feb 2026**).
It proposes **higher penalties** and promotes **biological pesticides**.

48.s:
Consider the following statements about the Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025:
1. It would replace the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971.
2. It proposes higher penalties.
3. It seeks to curb the use of biological pesticides.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
48.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the draft Bill promotes biological pesticides. Hence 1 and 2 only (D).
48.tq: New Bill = replaces 1968 Act + 1971 Rules, tougher penalties, pro-biopesticide.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(4) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025** would replace the **1968** Act and **1971** Rules.
Statement 2 correct: it proposes **higher penalties**.
Statement 3 wrong: it **promotes biological pesticides**.
xa: Comments were due by **4 Feb 2026**.
India still uses at least **66 pesticides banned elsewhere**.

48.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India continues to use at least 66 pesticides that are banned elsewhere.
2. Aldrin was associated with the killing of mugger crocodiles in Kota.
3. Endosulfan was banned by the Supreme Court in 2011.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: All three statements are correct: at least 66 pesticides used in India are banned elsewhere, Aldrin killed mugger crocodiles in Kota, and the Supreme Court banned Endosulfan in 2011.
48.tq: Combine three related pesticide facts and select the complete set of correct statements.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1 correct: India uses at least **66 pesticides banned elsewhere**.
Statement 2 correct: **Aldrin** (banned) killed **mugger crocodiles** in **Kota**.
Statement 3 correct: the **Supreme Court** banned **Endosulfan** in **2011**.
xa: AP pesticide use fell from **2,650 MT (2014-15)** to **1,716 MT (2024-25)**.
**IPM** cuts pesticide use by combining biological, cultural and need-based chemical control.

48.s: Integrated Pest Management primarily combines:
o: Biological, cultural and need-based chemical control
48.x: IPM combines biological control, cultural control and need-based chemical control in order to reduce pesticide use.
48.tq: Identify the management approach from the combination of control methods rather than from one component alone.
xs: **IPM** combines **biological, cultural and need-based chemical control** — option **(4)** is correct.
Its aim is to **cut pesticide use**.
xa: **Neem-based pesticides** are bio-pesticides.
Second Green Revolution stresses **integrated nutrient and pest management**.
AP pesticide use fell from **2,650 MT** to **1,716 MT** of active ingredient.

48.s: PMKSY is best described as a/an:
o: Umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2015–16
48.x: The Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana is an umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2015–16.
48.tq: Check both the scheme structure and the launch period.
xs: **PMKSY** is an **umbrella Centrally Sponsored scheme**, launched **2015-16** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is neither State-funded nor a Central Sector scheme.
xa: Components: **AIBP**, **Har Khet Ko Pani**, **Watershed (WDC-PMKSY 2.0)**, **Per Drop More Crop**.
Over **10 years**: **27 million** farmers benefited; **24.61 Mha** covered.
**M-CADWM** sub-scheme: **2025-26**, **₹1,600 crore**.

48.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its PMKSY role?
o: HKKP — minor irrigation, CAD&WM, RRR of water bodies and groundwater
AIBP — major and medium projects, including National Projects
Watershed Development — Department of Land Resources
PDMC — presently a component of PMKSY under Agriculture
48.x: PDMC was part of PMKSY during 2015–2021 but is now under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY), not presently under PMKSY.
48.tq: Look for the time-sensitive exception in the present status of PDMC.
xs: **PDMC** is **not** presently a PMKSY component — option **(4)** is the mismatch.
PDMC was under PMKSY from **2015** to **Dec 2021**; it is **now under RKVY**.
HKKP, AIBP and Watershed (Dept of **Land Resources**, MoRD) are correctly matched.
xa: AIBP is under **Jal Shakti**; watershed works target rainfed/degraded areas.
PDMC has brought **109 lakh ha** under micro-irrigation.

48.s: Per Drop More Crop under PMKSY is primarily associated with:
48.x: Per Drop More Crop focuses on micro-irrigation. It was under PMKSY from 2015 to December 2021 and is now under RKVY.
48.tq: Distinguish the component’s functional focus from its administrative placement.
xs: **Per Drop More Crop** is about **micro-irrigation** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was under **PMKSY** from **2015** to **Dec 2021**; now under **RKVY**.
xa: PDMC brought **109 lakh ha** under micro-irrigation.
Micro-irrigation subsidy up to **55%** (cap **5 ha**).
**AIBP** handles major/medium projects, not PDMC.

48.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-KUSUM:
1. It was launched in 2019.
2. It supports solar pumps and the solarisation of grid-connected farm pumps.
3. Solar irrigation over-draws groundwater everywhere, irrespective of hydrogeology and cropping.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
48.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: solar irrigation over-draws groundwater only where hydrogeology and cropping allow it. Hence 1 and 2 only (D).
48.tq: Absolute words like 'everywhere' or 'irrespective' usually mark the false statement.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(4) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **PM-KUSUM** began in **2019**.
Statement 2 correct: it gives **solar pumps** and **solarises grid-connected farm pumps**.
Statement 3 wrong: solar irrigation over-draws groundwater **only where hydrogeology and cropping allow**.
xa: **Micro-irrigation** subsidy: up to **55%** (cap **5 ha**).
**PDMC** has covered **109 lakh ha** under micro-irrigation.

48.s: The Standard Operating Procedure for drone spraying was issued on:
48.x: The SOP for drone spraying, including crop-specific SOPs, was issued on 20 April 2023.
48.tq: Distinguish the operational guideline date from scheme-launch and current-report dates.
xs: Crop-specific **SOPs for drone spraying** came on **20 April 2023** — option **(3)** is correct.
The SOPs are issued **crop-specific**, under the mechanisation drive (**SMAM**).
xa: **Rs 141.41 crore** for **Kisan drones** under SMAM.
Drones: **500** distributed nationally; AP **529** (2025-26).
Second Green Revolution: **precision farming** with drones and AI.

48.s: India’s farm mechanisation level is estimated at approximately:
48.x: India’s farm mechanisation level is reported as 40-45 percent.
48.tq: Select the precise range rather than a rounded but unsupported estimate.
xs: India's farm mechanisation level is **40-45 percent** — option **(4)** is correct.
**SMAM** has subsidised **20.93 lakh** machines to raise it.
xa: **27,563** custom hiring centres under SMAM.
AP seeks Central help for **drones and mechanisation**.

48.s:
With reference to agricultural technology projects, consider the following statements:
1. NATP was launched in 1998.
2. NATP was World Bank-aided.
3. NAIP was implemented during 2006-2014.
4. NAIP was World Bank-funded.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: NATP began in 1998 with World Bank aid, while NAIP ran from 2006 to 2014 and was also World Bank-funded.
48.tq: Check each project against its year, duration and funding source before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**NATP** began in **1998**, **World Bank-aided**.
**NAIP** ran **2006-2014**, also **World Bank-funded**.
xa: NAIP components: **ICAR as a catalyst for change**, **production-to-consumption research**, **sustainable rural livelihood security**, **basic and strategic research**.
**ATMA** (**2005**) is a district extension society.

48.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding agricultural research institutes and their locations:

List-I (Institute)

a. Central Rice Research Institute (CRRI)
b. Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI)
c. Central Tobacco Research Institute (CTRI)
d. International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT)

List-II (Location)

i. Patancheru, Hyderabad
ii. New Delhi (Pusa)
iii. Cuttack
iv. Rajahmundry

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
48.x: CRRI is located at Cuttack, IARI at New Delhi (Pusa), CTRI at Rajahmundry and ICRISAT at Patancheru, Hyderabad.
48.tq: Start from the sure institute–location pairs and eliminate codes containing a mismatched pair.
xs: **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — option **(1)** is correct.
**CRRI** (now National Rice Research Institute) — **Cuttack**; **IARI** — **New Delhi (Pusa)**.
**CTRI** (tobacco) — **Rajahmundry (AP)**; **ICRISAT** — **Patancheru, Hyderabad**.
xa: **IIRR**, **IIOR** and **IIMR (Millets)** are all in **Hyderabad**.
⚠ Indian Institute of **Maize** Research = **Ludhiana**.
AP: **RARS Maruteru** (rice).

48.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Indian Institute of Rice Research — Hyderabad
2. Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research — Hyderabad
3. Indian Institute of Millets Research — Hyderabad

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
48.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. IIRR, IIOR and IIMR are located at Hyderabad.
48.tq: Check whether the common location is correctly applied to all the listed specialised institutes.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**IIRR (rice)**, **IIOR (oilseeds)** and **IIMR (Millets Research)** are all in **Hyderabad**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** Indian Institute of **Maize** Research (also **IIMR**) is at **Ludhiana**.
**ICRISAT** is at **Patancheru**, Hyderabad.
**CTRI** is at **Rajahmundry**.

48.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Indian Institute of Maize Research — Ludhiana
Indian Institute of Millets Research — Ludhiana
Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research — New Delhi
48.x: The Indian Institute of Maize Research is located at Ludhiana. It should not be confused with the Indian Institute of Millets Research, which is located at Hyderabad; both use the acronym IIMR.
48.tq: Distinguish similar acronyms by expanding the institute names before matching the location.
xs: The **Indian Institute of Maize Research** is at **Ludhiana** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **Millets** Research (same acronym **IIMR**) is at **Hyderabad**, not Ludhiana.
**Rajahmundry** has **CTRI** (tobacco); **IIOR** (oilseeds) is in **Hyderabad**, not New Delhi.
xa: **IARI** is at **New Delhi (Pusa)**; **CRRI** at **Cuttack**.
**IIRR** (rice) is in **Hyderabad**.

48.s:
Consider the following statements about Kisan Call Centres:
1. They were launched on 21 January 2004 by the Department of Agriculture.
2. They use the toll-free number 1800-180-1551.
3. They answer queries in 17 languages from 22 locations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
48.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the figures: KCCs work in 22 languages from 17 locations. Hence 1 and 2 only (D).
48.tq: 22 languages, 17 locations - watch for swapped numbers.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(4) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Kisan Call Centres** were launched on **21 Jan 2004** by the **Department of Agriculture**.
Statement 2 correct: toll-free **1800-180-1551**.
Statement 3 wrong: it is **22 languages** from **17 locations** — reversed.
xa: **Meghdoot** app (IMD-ICAR, **2019**) gives agromet advisories.
**ANGRAU** runs weather-linked SMS alerts.

48.s:
Consider the following statements about Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs):
1. The first KVK was set up in 1974 at Puducherry on the recommendation of the Mohan Singh Mehta Committee.
2. KVKs are 50% centrally funded under ICAR.
3. KVKs are coordinated by 11 ATARIs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
48.x: Statement 1 is correct (1974, Puducherry, Mohan Singh Mehta Committee). Statement 2 is wrong: KVKs are 100% centrally funded under ICAR. Statement 3 is correct: 11 ATARIs coordinate them. Hence 1 and 3 only (C).
48.tq: KVK = 1974 Puducherry, 100% ICAR, 11 ATARIs.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: first **KVK** in **1974** at **Puducherry**, per the **Mohan Singh Mehta Committee**.
Statement 2 wrong: KVKs are **100% centrally funded** under ICAR.
Statement 3 correct: coordinated by **11 ATARIs**.
xa: Upgrade plan: **300 KVKs by March 2027**.
Entrepreneurship centres in all KVKs by **Dec 2028**.

48.s:
Consider the following statements about the Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA):
1. It is a demand-driven district-level extension society dating from 2005.
2. It plans its activities through Soil Health Cards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
48.x: Statement 1 is correct: ATMA is a demand-driven district extension society (2005). Statement 2 is wrong: ATMA plans through Strategic Research and Extension Plans (SREP), not Soil Health Cards. Hence 1 only (A); B, C and D wrongly accept statement 2 or reject statement 1.
48.tq: ATMA = district, demand-driven, 2005, SREP.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **ATMA** is a **demand-driven district extension society** (**2005**).
Statement 2 wrong: ATMA plans through **SREP (Strategic Research and Extension Plans)**, not Soil Health Cards.
xa: AP released **₹1,803 lakh** for ATMA in **2025-26**.
Extension principle: "**Seeing is believing**" through demonstrations.

48.s: The Agriculture Integrated Command and Control Centre was inaugurated in March 2024 at
48.x: The Agriculture Integrated Command and Control Centre was inaugurated in March 2024 at Krishi Bhawan in Delhi.
48.tq: Use the location trap to distinguish the national command centre from agricultural extension institutions.
xs: The **Agriculture Integrated Command and Control Centre** was inaugurated in **March 2024** at **Krishi Bhawan, Delhi** — option **(4)** is correct (APPSC 2024).
It is in Delhi, not at **ANGRAU** or Puducherry.
xa: **Meghdoot** app: IMD-ICAR, **2019**.
**Kisan Call Centres**: launched **21 Jan 2004**.
First **KVK**: **1974, Puducherry**.

48.s: Rythu Seva Kendras, formerly known as Rythu Bharosa Kendras, function primarily as:
o: Village-level one-stop centres for agricultural services
48.x: Rythu Seva Kendras are village one-stop centres providing a range of agricultural inputs and services.
48.tq: Infer the institutional role from the range of services delivered at the centre.
xs: **Rythu Seva Kendras** (formerly **Rythu Bharosa Kendras**) are **village one-stop centres** for agricultural services — option **(1)** is correct.
Services: **inputs**, **soil testing**, **e-Panta**, **CCRCs**, **insurance**, **procurement**.
xa: Soil sampling through **10,778 RSKs**, rationalised to **8,489** functional centres.
Permanent buildings coming up under **MGNREGS**.
AP Seeds supplies **7.46 lakh quintals** of subsidised seed through RSKs.

48.s: Permanent buildings for the rationalised Rythu Seva Kendras are being taken up under:
48.x: Permanent buildings for RSKs are coming up under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS).
48.tq: Match the infrastructure activity with the implementing programme.
xs: Permanent buildings for the rationalised **Rythu Seva Kendras** are coming up under **MGNREGS** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **PPV&FR Act** protects breeders and farmers' seed rights; **NPOP** is organic certification — neither builds RSKs.
xa: Soil sampling ran through **10,778 RSKs**, rationalised to **8,489 functional centres**.
RSKs were formerly **Rythu Bharosa Kendras** — village one-stop centres.
Services: inputs, soil testing, **e-Panta**, **CCRCs**, insurance, procurement.
AP Seeds supplies **7.46 lakh quintals** of subsidised seed (**₹294 crore**) through RSKs (2026-27).

48.s: Which of the following is classified as an input subsidy rather than public investment in agriculture?
o: Construction of a major irrigation project
Establishment of an agricultural research institute
48.x: Fertiliser subsidy is an input subsidy and represents a current transfer. Irrigation projects, agricultural research and rural infrastructure are forms of public investment and capital formation.
48.tq: Classify the item by asking whether it is a current transfer to inputs or capital formation.
xs: **Subsidised fertiliser supplied to farmers** is an **input subsidy** (a current transfer) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Irrigation projects**, **research** and **rural infrastructure** are **public investment** (capital formation).
xa: Input subsidies: **fertiliser, power, irrigation water, seed, credit (interest subvention)**.
⚠ **MSP** = price support, **not** an input subsidy.
Fertiliser subsidy is the **second-largest subsidy after food**.

48.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Minimum Support Price from an input subsidy?
o: MSP is a price support measure, whereas fertiliser subsidy is an input subsidy.
MSP is an input subsidy, whereas seed subsidy is a price support measure.
Both MSP and fertiliser subsidy are forms of public investment.
Both MSP and fertiliser subsidy are capital-formation measures.
48.x: MSP is a price support measure. Fertiliser, power, irrigation water, seed and credit support are input subsidies.
48.tq: Separate price support for output from subsidised inputs used in production.
xs: **MSP** is a **price support** measure, while **fertiliser subsidy** is an **input subsidy** — option **(1)** is correct.
Neither is public investment or capital formation; those are **irrigation projects, research, rural infrastructure**.
xa: Input subsidies: **fertiliser, power, irrigation water, seed, credit**.
Budget **2026-27** fertiliser subsidy: **₹1.71 lakh crore**.
The **ES** suggests **acre-based support** instead of urea-centred subsidy.

48.s: Which of the following is a criticism of agricultural subsidies mentioned in the context of their distributional effects?
o: They are directed exclusively towards agricultural research.
They mainly benefit prosperous regions and the fertiliser industry.
They have completely eliminated regional disparities.
They benefit only farmers in rain-fed regions.
48.x: Although subsidies helped small farmers adopt high-yielding varieties, they are criticised for disproportionately benefiting prosperous regions and the fertiliser industry.
48.tq: Identify the balanced criticism rather than an absolute claim about subsidy outcomes.
xs: Subsidies **mainly benefit prosperous regions and the fertiliser industry** — option **(2)** is correct.
They did help **small farmers adopt HYV** seeds.
xa: Urea-centred subsidy distorts the **NPK ratio** — **10.9:4.1:1** vs ideal **4:2:1**.
The **ES** suggests **acre-based support** instead.
Fertiliser subsidy is the **second-largest subsidy after food**.

48.s: The urea-centred subsidy regime is criticised primarily because it
o: converts MSP into a capital investment
prevents the use of all chemical fertilisers
48.x: A urea-centred subsidy regime is criticised for distorting the balance among nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, expressed as the NPK ratio.
48.tq: Link the policy focus on one fertiliser to its stated effect on nutrient balance.
xs: A urea-centred subsidy **distorts the NPK ratio** — option **(2)** is correct.
Cheap **urea** (statutory price control) → **nitrogen overuse**.
xa: The **ES** suggests **acre-based support** instead.
**PM-PRANAM**: states keep **50%** of the subsidy saved by cutting chemical fertiliser use.

48.s: An acre-based support system has been suggested as an alternative to the existing
48.x: An acre-based support system has been suggested as an alternative to the urea-centred subsidy approach.
48.tq: Match the proposed policy alternative with the regime it is intended to address.
xs: **Acre-based support** is suggested by the **ES** in place of the **urea-centred subsidy approach** — option **(1)** is correct.
The reason: urea-centred subsidy **distorts the NPK ratio**.
xa: **West Asia crisis** doubled urea prices between **Dec 2025** and **Apr 2026**.
The subsidy bill may reach **₹2.41 lakh crore**.
**NBS** (**2010**) already gives a fixed per-kg subsidy on **N, P, K and S** for P&K fertilisers.

49.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Green Revolution package approach?
o: Assured irrigation through canals and tubewells
Withdrawal of price support and formal credit
49.x: The package included HYV seeds, assured irrigation, fertilisers, pesticides, mechanisation, institutional credit and MSP or assured procurement. Withdrawal of price support and formal credit was not a component.
49.tq: Find the option that reverses a core element of the package approach.
xs: **Withdrawal of price support and formal credit** was not part of the GR package — option **(4)** is the answer.
The package in fact included **institutional credit** and **MSP / assured procurement** (UPSC Economy p.186).
Its other parts: **HYV seeds**, **assured irrigation** (canals, tubewells), **chemical fertilisers + pesticides**, **mechanisation**.
xa: HYV traits: **short-statured** (do not lodge), respond to fertiliser and water, mature quicker → **double cropping**.
First crop transformed: **wheat**; pioneer state: **Punjab**.
First semi-dwarf rice in India: **Taichung Native-1 (TN-1)**, **1965**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the Intensive Agricultural District Programme (IADP):
1. It began as a pilot programme in 1960.
2. It covered seven districts in seven states.
3. West Godavari was the IADP district in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: IADP began in 1960 as a pilot in seven districts of seven states, and West Godavari was Andhra Pradesh's IADP district.
49.tq: Combine the programme's year, scale and Andhra Pradesh location before selecting the coded option.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statements 1 and 2 correct: **IADP** began in **1960** as a pilot in **7 districts** of **7 states**.
Statement 3 correct: AP's IADP district was **West Godavari**.
xa: **IAAP** (**1964-65**) extended the approach to **114 districts**; **117** blocks in AP, starting in West Godavari.
⚠ **IADP** = **1960**, 7 districts; **IAAP** = **1964-65**, 114 districts.
**MTU** rice varieties come from **RARS Maruteru**, West Godavari.

49.s: Which of the following correctly describes the coverage of the Intensive Agricultural Area Programme (IAAP)?
o: It covered 117 districts and 114 blocks in Andhra Pradesh, beginning in Krishna district
It covered 7 districts and 7 states, with West Godavari as the only Andhra Pradesh unit
It was confined to the Punjab-Haryana region and excluded Andhra Pradesh
It extended to 114 districts and 117 blocks in Andhra Pradesh, beginning in West Godavari
49.x: IAAP extended to 114 districts and 117 blocks in Andhra Pradesh, beginning in West Godavari.
49.tq: Separate the programme's district and block figures and watch for their reversal.
xs: IAAP extended to **114 districts** and **117 blocks in AP**, beginning in **West Godavari** — option **(4)** is correct.
Option (1) swaps the numbers and names Krishna; **7 districts / 7 states** describes **IADP**.
xa: IAAP began in **1964-65**; IADP in **1960**.
Coastal AP became a **rice-surplus belt** thanks to the **delta canals**.

49.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a high-yielding variety or wheat selection?
o: Taichung Native-1 — First semi-dwarf rice introduced in India
Kalyan Sona — Mexican dwarf wheat developed by Borlaug
Lerma Rojo 64-A — Dwarf rice from the Philippines
49.x: Taichung Native-1, or TN-1, was the first semi-dwarf rice introduced in India in 1965. IR-8 was dwarf rice from IRRI, while Kalyan Sona was an Indian dwarf wheat selection and Lerma Rojo 64-A was Mexican dwarf wheat.
49.tq: Separate rice varieties from Mexican wheat and Indian wheat selections.
xs: **Taichung Native-1 (TN-1)** was the **first semi-dwarf rice introduced in India** (**1965**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**IR-8** is dwarf **rice** from **IRRI, Philippines**, not an Indian wheat.
**Kalyan Sona** is an **Indian** dwarf wheat selection, not Mexican.
**Lerma Rojo 64-A** is a **Mexican (Borlaug) dwarf wheat**, not Philippine rice.
xa: IR-8 = "**miracle rice**", **1966**.
**Sonora 64** is the other Mexican dwarf wheat.

49.s:
Which of the following statements regarding HYV crops is correct?
1. Their short stature helps them resist lodging.
2. They respond to fertiliser and water.
3. Their quicker maturity can permit double cropping.
49.x: All three statements are correct. HYVs are short-statured, respond to fertiliser and water, mature faster and can therefore support double cropping.
49.tq: Recognise a complete set of linked agronomic characteristics rather than isolating one feature.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
HYVs are **short-statured** → **do not lodge**.
They **respond to fertiliser and water**.
They **mature quicker** → allow **double cropping**.
xa: **Kalyan Sona** and **Sonalika** are Indian dwarf wheat selections that **resist lodging**.
The GR package also included **assured irrigation**, **chemical fertilisers** and **MSP**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the gains of the Green Revolution:
1. India became self-sufficient in foodgrains and stopped relying on PL-480 imports.
2. Foodgrain output rose from about 70-75 MT in the mid-1960s to a record 357.73 MT in 2024-25.
3. Rice gained the most in the initial phase of the Green Revolution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
49.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: wheat gained the most; rice gained in a wider, later phase. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
49.tq: Green Revolution = wheat first; rice later.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: India became **self-sufficient**, ending reliance on **PL-480** imports.
Statement 2 correct: foodgrains rose from about **70-75 MT** (mid-1960s) to a record **357.73 MT in 2024-25**.
Statement 3 wrong: **wheat gained the most**; rice gained in a **wider, later phase**.
xa: Gains were in **Punjab, Haryana and western UP**; rice gains in the **AP** and **TN** deltas.
Costs: farmers with more than **10 ha** benefited most.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the costs of the Green Revolution:
1. Farmers with more than 10 hectares benefited the most.
2. Pulses, oilseeds and millets were neglected.
3. The disparities it created were only regional, not interpersonal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
49.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the disparities were both regional and interpersonal. Hence 1 and 2 only (D).
49.tq: Disparity was regional + interpersonal; big farmers (>10 ha) gained most.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(4) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: farmers with more than **10 ha** benefited most.
Statement 2 correct: **pulses, oilseeds and millets** were neglected.
Statement 3 wrong: disparity was **regional + interpersonal**.
xa: **Punjab** and **Haryana** extract **35-57%** more groundwater than recharge.
Soil costs: **salinity**, biodiversity loss, skewed **N:P:K of 10.9:4.1:1**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the ecological consequences of the Green Revolution:
1. Groundwater extraction in Punjab and Haryana is estimated to be 35–57 per cent more than recharge.
2. Salinity and loss of biodiversity are among its environmental costs.
3. The predominant fertiliser nutrient ratio was balanced at 1:1:1 for nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Groundwater extraction in Punjab and Haryana is 35–57 per cent above recharge, and salinity and biodiversity loss are recognised costs. The reported N:P:K ratio was skewed at 10.9:4.1:1, not 1:1:1.
49.tq: Split the options by checking the ecological figures and the reversed fertiliser-ratio trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Punjab** and **Haryana** extract **35-57%** more than recharge.
Statement 2 correct: **salinity** and **loss of biodiversity** are GR costs.
Statement 3 wrong: the N:P:K ratio is skewed at **10.9:4.1:1**, not balanced.
xa: The **Johl Committee** proposed shifting **20%** of paddy area.
Rice-wheat monoculture is **water-intensive** → need for **crop diversification**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI):
1. It is a sub-scheme of RKVY.
2. It has been implemented since 2014-15.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
49.x: Statement 1 is correct: BGREI is a sub-scheme of RKVY. Statement 2 is wrong: it has been implemented since 2010-11. Hence 1 only (B).
49.tq: BGREI = RKVY sub-scheme since 2010-11.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(2) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **BGREI** is a **sub-scheme of RKVY**.
Statement 2 wrong: BGREI has run since **2010-11** (PYQ key), not 2014-15.
xa: Aim: raise **rice-based productivity in the eastern region**.
Tools: **HYVs**, irrigation, balanced nutrients, **IPM**.
UPSC notes list six BGREI states and omit **Chhattisgarh**.

49.s: Which of the following correctly states the aim of BGREI?
o: To shift all cotton production from western India to eastern India
To promote petroleum production through eastern industrial corridors
To establish dairy cooperatives in every eastern district
To raise rice-based productivity in eastern India through HYVs, irrigation, balanced nutrients and IPM
49.x: BGREI aims to raise rice-based productivity in eastern India through high-yielding varieties, irrigation, balanced nutrient use and integrated pest management.
49.tq: Match the scheme with its crop, region and intervention package.
xs: **BGREI** aims to **raise rice-based productivity in eastern India** via **HYVs, irrigation, balanced nutrients and IPM** — option **(4)** is correct (UPSC Env p.256).
It is not about cotton, petroleum or dairy.
xa: BGREI: **sub-scheme of RKVY**, since **2010-11**.
"**Purvodaya**" later took the same logic — shifting the rice bowl eastward.

49.s: MTU rice varieties are associated with which research station?
o: Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi
Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru, West Godavari
49.x: MTU varieties come from the Regional Agricultural Research Station at Maruteru in West Godavari. BPT varieties are associated with Bapatla.
49.tq: Origin-place discrimination between the MTU and BPT varietal groups.
xs: **MTU** varieties come from **Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru (West Godavari)** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **BPT** varieties come from **Bapatla**.
xa: **MTU 1010**: rabi rice of southern states; parent of **Pusa DST Rice 1**.
**MTU 7029 (Swarna)**: popular mega-variety.
**BPT 5204 (Samba Mahsuri)**: parent of **DRR Dhan 100 Kamala**.

49.s: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by which organisation?
o: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
49.x: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB).
49.tq: Apply the ‘who launched the programme?’ institutional trap.
xs: **Operation Flood** was launched by the **National Dairy Development Board (NDDB)** in **1970** — option **(2)** is correct.
It built a **national milk grid**.
xa: Model: **Amul (Anand, Gujarat)** three-tier cooperative.
Phase I (**1970-80**) was financed by the **World Food Programme**.
**Dr. Verghese Kurien** = Father of the **White Revolution**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the phases of Operation Flood:
1. Phase I (1970-80) was financed by the World Food Programme.
2. Phase II (1981-85) raised the number of milk sheds from 18 to 36.
3. Phase III (1985-96) added 30,000 new dairy cooperatives.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
49.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Phase II raised milk sheds from 18 to 136, not 36. Hence 1 and 3 only (B); A misses statement 3, C and D include the wrong statement 2.
49.tq: Phase I WFP-funded; Phase II 18 -> 136 milk sheds; Phase III 30,000 cooperatives.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: Phase I (**1970-80**) was financed by the **World Food Programme**.
Statement 2 wrong: Phase II (**1981-85**) raised milk sheds from **18 to 136**, not 36.
Statement 3 correct: Phase III (**1985-96**) added **30,000** dairy cooperatives.
xa: Phase I linked milk sheds in **18 states** to **Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai**.
Phase II raised urban markets **up to 200**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about White Revolution 2.0:
1. It was launched by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare in September 2024.
2. It plans 75,000 new dairy cooperative societies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
49.x: Statement 1 is wrong: White Revolution 2.0 was launched by the Ministry of Cooperation (Sept 2024). Statement 2 is correct: it plans 75,000 new dairy cooperative societies. Hence 2 only (D).
49.tq: White Revolution 2.0 = Ministry of Cooperation, 75,000 societies.
xs: Only statement 2 is correct — option **(4) 2 only**.
Statement 1 wrong: **White Revolution 2.0** was launched by the **Ministry of Cooperation** in **Sept 2024**.
Statement 2 correct: it plans **75,000** new dairy cooperative societies.
xa: Procurement target: **1,007 lakh kg/day** by **2028-29**.
Milk output: **239.3 MMT** in **2023-24**, now about **248 MT**.

49.s: Operation Flood was implemented by the National Dairy Development Board from 1970 mainly to:
o: Build a national milk grid based on the Anand cooperative model
Promote cotton exports through a technology mission
Expand marine fishing along the eastern coast
Increase oil-palm cultivation in rainfed areas
49.x: Operation Flood was run by the NDDB from 1970 and built a national milk grid on the Anand or Amul cooperative model.
49.tq: Identify the institution, time period and principal objective of a major programme together.
xs: Operation Flood (**NDDB**, **1970**) built a **national milk grid** on the **Anand** cooperative model — option **(1)** is correct.
Cotton = **Silver Fibre** Revolution; fisheries = **Blue**; oil palm = **Yellow** (NMEO-Oil Palm).
xa: Three tiers: **village society → district union → state federation**.
Phase II: milk sheds **18 → 136**.

49.s:
With reference to agricultural revolutions in India, consider the following pairs:

a. Blue Revolution — Hiralal Chaudhuri and Arun Krishnan
b. Pink Revolution — Durgesh Patel
c. Red Revolution — Vishal Tewari
d. Golden Revolution — Nirpakh Tutej

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
49.x: All four pairs are correct: the Blue Revolution (fisheries) is linked with Hiralal Chaudhuri and Arun Krishnan, Pink (meat processing, prawn, onion) with Durgesh Patel, Red (meat and tomato) with Vishal Tewari, and Golden (horticulture and honey) with Nirpakh Tutej. Hence a, b, c and d (D).
49.tq: Use the person-product association in each pair rather than relying on the colour alone.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) a, b, c and d**.
**Blue** — **Hiralal Chaudhuri, Arun Krishnan**; **Pink** — **Durgesh Patel**.
**Red** — **Vishal Tewari**; **Golden** — **Nirpakh Tutej**.
xa: Blue = fisheries (current vehicle **PMMSY**); Pink = meat processing, prawn, onion, pharmaceuticals.
Red = meat and tomato; Golden = horticulture and honey (**1991-2003**).

49.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Golden Fibre Revolution - Jute
2. Silver Fibre Revolution - Cotton (Technology Mission on Cotton)
3. Golden Revolution - Eggs and poultry
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
49.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Pair 3 is wrong: the Golden Revolution is horticulture and honey; eggs and poultry belong to the Silver Revolution. Hence 1 and 2 only (C).
49.tq: Golden Fibre = jute, Silver Fibre = cotton, Silver = eggs, Golden = horticulture/honey.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 2 only**.
Pair 1 correct: **Golden Fibre** = **jute**.
Pair 2 correct: **Silver Fibre** = **cotton** (Technology Mission on Cotton).
Pair 3 wrong: **Golden** = **horticulture and honey**; eggs and poultry = **Silver**.
xa: Egg maximisation = **Silver Revolution** (APPSC 2018 key).
**Sweet** Revolution = honey / beekeeping.

49.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
49.x: The Round Revolution is associated with potato, not oilseeds. Oilseeds are associated with the Yellow Revolution.
49.tq: Find the single commodity that belongs to another colour revolution.
xs: **Round Revolution** is **potato**, not oilseeds — option **(3)** is the mismatch.
Oilseeds = **Yellow** Revolution.
**Brown** = leather / cocoa, **Black** = petroleum, **Grey** = fertilisers — all correct.
xa: Some notes also list **fertilisers** under Brown.
⚠ **Golden** = horticulture/honey; **Golden Fibre** = jute.

49.s: The expression ‘Rainbow Revolution’ refers to:
o: A programme limited to horticulture and honey production
Only the simultaneous growth of foodgrain and dairy production
The sequence of phases of the Green Revolution
The umbrella of colour revolutions covering crops, livestock and fisheries
49.x: Rainbow Revolution is the umbrella term for the different colour revolutions and represents holistic agricultural growth across crops, livestock and fisheries.
49.tq: Distinguish an umbrella concept from one of its component revolutions.
xs: **Rainbow Revolution** is the **umbrella of all colour revolutions**, covering **crops, livestock and fisheries** — option **(4)** is correct.
It means **holistic agricultural growth**, not just horticulture or dairy.
xa: **Golden** Revolution alone covers horticulture and honey.
**Evergreen Revolution**: sustainable, climate-smart farming.

49.s: The current effort associated with the Yellow Revolution is the:
49.x: The current Yellow Revolution effort is represented by the National Mission on Edible Oils.
49.tq: Identify the current mission linked to a traditional revolution label.
xs: The current Yellow Revolution effort is the **National Mission on Edible Oils** → **NMEO-Oil Palm** — option **(3)** is correct.
Yellow Revolution = **oilseeds / edible oils** (**1986-87**).
xa: Linked with **Sam Pitroda**.
Blue Revolution's current vehicle is **PMMSY**.

49.s: Who among the following is associated with the Green Revolution in India and who with the Green Revolution at the global level, respectively?
49.x: M.S. Swaminathan is associated with the Green Revolution in India, while Norman Borlaug is associated with it at the global level.
49.tq: Discriminate between two persons associated with the same revolution at different levels.
xs: **M.S. Swaminathan** (India) and **Norman Borlaug** (world) — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses them; **Pitroda**, **Kurien** and **Durgesh Patel** belong to other revolutions.
xa: Borlaug: **Mexican dwarf wheat** (**Lerma Rojo 64-A**, **Sonora 64**).
Green Revolution dated **1968**: foodgrains (HYV wheat, rice).

49.s: The Yellow Revolution, initiated during 1986–87, was associated with which of the following persons?
49.x: The Yellow Revolution of 1986–87, related to oilseeds and edible oils, is associated with Sam Pitroda.
49.tq: Match the named person with the correct revolution and period.
xs: The **Yellow Revolution** (**1986-87**) is linked with **Sam Pitroda** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kurien** = White; **Swaminathan** = Green (India); **Durgesh Patel** = Pink.
xa: Yellow = **oilseeds / edible oils**; current effort **NMEO-Oil Palm**.
⚠ **Kurien** = White; **Pitroda** = Yellow.

49.s: In the APPSC 2018 key, 'egg maximisation' and 'fisheries development' were linked respectively to which revolutions?
49.x: Egg maximisation is the Silver Revolution (eggs and poultry) and fisheries development is the Blue Revolution (APPSC 2018 keys). Golden is horticulture and honey, Pink is meat processing, prawn and onion, Yellow is oilseeds and Grey is fertilisers.
49.tq: Silver = eggs (white shell), Blue = water/fish.
xs: Egg maximisation = **Silver Revolution**; fisheries development = **Blue Revolution** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2018).
**Golden** = horticulture and honey; **Pink** = meat processing, prawn, onion; **Yellow** = oilseeds; **Grey** = fertilisers.
xa: ⚠ **Silver** = eggs; **Silver Fibre** = cotton.
Blue Revolution's current vehicle: **PMMSY**.

49.s: The Johl Committee proposed shifting what proportion of paddy area as part of crop-diversification efforts?
49.x: The Johl Committee proposed shifting 20 per cent of the paddy area to address the problems associated with water-intensive rice-wheat monoculture.
49.tq: Direct percentage recall linked to the policy response to monoculture.
xs: The **Johl Committee** proposed shifting **20 per cent** of paddy area — option **(3)** is correct.
The aim is **crop diversification** away from water-intensive rice-wheat.
xa: **Punjab** and **Haryana** extract **35-57%** more groundwater than recharge.
GR neglected **pulses, oilseeds and millets**.

49.s: Which one of the following best captures the principal criticism of the rice-wheat pattern associated with the Green Revolution?
o: It eliminated regional and interpersonal disparities
It is water-intensive and creates a need for crop diversification
It uses no irrigation and therefore lowers groundwater extraction
It placed pulses, oilseeds and millets at the centre of production
49.x: The rice-wheat monoculture is criticised for being water-intensive and for limiting crop diversification. It is also associated with disparities and neglect of several nutritious crops.
49.tq: Identify the accurate cause-effect comparison between monoculture and diversification.
xs: The rice-wheat pattern is **water-intensive**, creating a **need for crop diversification** — option **(2)** is correct.
It widened disparities, deepened groundwater extraction and neglected **pulses, oilseeds and millets** — the reverse of the other options.
xa: **Johl Committee**: shift **20%** of paddy area.
Farmers with more than **10 ha** benefited most.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the first crop transformed by the Green Revolution and its pioneer state?
49.x: Wheat was the first crop transformed by the Green Revolution and Punjab was the pioneer state. Rice gained in a wider, later phase, including in the AP and TN deltas; Haryana gained but was not the pioneer.
49.tq: First = wheat, Punjab; rice and the deltas came later.
xs: **Wheat** was the first crop transformed and **Punjab** the pioneer state — option **(3)** is correct.
Rice gained in a **wider, later phase** (AP and TN deltas); **Haryana** gained but was not the pioneer.
xa: Wheat **gained the most** of all crops.
Main GR region: **Punjab, Haryana and western UP**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Pantnagar had the first Agricultural University in 1960.
II. The first Krishi Vigyan Kendra was established at Puducherry in 1974.
III. The first implementation of WBCIS took place in Karnataka during Kharif 2007.
IV. The first introduction of HYVs during the Green Revolution took place in 1966–67.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All four are correct: the first farm university at Pantnagar (1960), the first KVK at Puducherry (1974), the first WBCIS in Karnataka (Kharif 2007), and HYVs in 1966–67.
49.tq: Recall the farm firsts.
n: Pantnagar was the first Agricultural University. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
The first Agricultural University was established in 1960. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
The first Krishi Vigyan Kendra was established in Puducherry. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
The first Krishi Vigyan Kendra was established in 1974. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
The first implementation of WBCIS took place in Karnataka during Kharif 2007. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
The first introduction of HYV under the Green Revolution took place in 1966–67. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]

50.s: Agricultural growth at 2011-12 prices in 2015-16 was approximately:
50.x: Agricultural growth in 2015-16 was about 0.7% at 2011-12 prices.
50.tq: Preserve the decimal place in a low-growth numerical fact.
xs: Agricultural growth in **2015-16** was about **0.7%** at **2011-12** prices — option **(2)** is correct (PYQ key).
It came right after **2014-15**, a **negative-growth** year.
xa: The other negative year: **2002-03** (drought).
FY16-FY25 average: **4.4%** a year — the highest decadal growth ever.
Agriculture's share in national income: **56.5%** in **1950-51** vs ~**18%** now.

50.s:
With reference to the agricultural growth performance of Plans, consider the following statements:
1. The Third Plan recorded the lowest growth among the listed Plans.
2. The Eighth Plan recorded 4.68% growth, exceeding its 4.1% target.
3. The Eighth Plan was the best-performing Plan for agriculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: All three statements are correct. The Third Plan recorded 0.73%, while the Eighth Plan achieved 4.68% against a 4.1% target and was the best-performing Plan.
50.tq: Combine the lowest value, target comparison and overall ranking.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1 correct: the **3rd Plan** had the lowest growth, **0.73%**.
Statements 2 and 3 correct: the **8th Plan** achieved **4.68%** (above the **4.1%** target) — the **best-performing** Plan for agriculture.
xa: ⚠ Lowest = **3rd Plan (0.73%)**; highest = **8th Plan (4.68%)**.

50.s: The collapse of agricultural performance during the Third Plan, largely due to droughts, contributed to the beginning of the:
50.x: The drought-related collapse during the Third Plan helped set off the Green Revolution.
50.tq: Identify the policy or technological response linked to the stated crisis.
xs: The **3rd Plan** collapse (droughts) set off the **Green Revolution** — option **(1)** is correct.
Agricultural growth in the 3rd Plan (**1961-66**) was just **0.73%**, the lowest.
xa: The **Annual Plans 1966-69** that followed grew **4.16%**.
⚠ Lowest = **3rd Plan**; best = **8th Plan (4.68%)**.

50.s: The National Agricultural Policy, 2000, targeted agricultural growth of:
50.x: The National Agricultural Policy, 2000, set a target of more than 4% annual agricultural growth.
50.tq: Recall the policy target rather than the later realised growth rate.
xs: The **National Agricultural Policy 2000** targeted **over 4% per annum** growth — option **(1)** is correct.
The 5%, 3% and 2% figures are not the policy's target.
xa: The **8th Plan** had a **4.1%** target and achieved **4.68%**.
FY16-FY25 averaged **4.4%** a year.
**National Commission on Agriculture**: set up **1970**, final report **1976**.
**Ashok Dalwai Committee** (Doubling Farmers' Income): set up **2016**, report **2018**.

50.s: The share of agriculture in national income declined from 56.5% in 1950-51 to approximately:
50.x: Agriculture's share in national income declined from 56.5% in 1950-51 to about 18% in the current reference period.
50.tq: Compare the historical and present shares without confusing share with growth rate.
xs: Agriculture's share in national income fell from **56.5% (1950-51)** to about **18% at present** — option **(1)** is correct.
The share shrank as the rest of the economy grew faster.
xa: Growth is now led by **livestock** (**7.1%**) and **fishing** (**8.8%**), while crops grew only **3.5%** (FY16-FY25).
Agricultural exports = **$54.70 billion**.
Holdings: **86%** small or marginal; average **1.08 ha**.

50.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Agriculture and allied sector growth in Q1 FY27 was 3.6%.
2. Agriculture and allied sector growth in FY26 provisional estimates was 3.0%.
3. Agriculture and allied sector growth in FY24 was 4.6%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. FY24 growth was 2.7%, not 4.6%; 4.6% was the initial FY25 estimate.
50.tq: Find the incorrect year-rate association among closely spaced fiscal years.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Q1 FY27** growth was **3.6%**.
Statement 2 correct: **FY26** provisional estimate is **3.0%** (advance estimate **3.1%**).
Statement 3 wrong: **FY24** was **2.7%**; **4.6%** was the first **FY25** estimate.
xa: FY25 was later revised to **4.2%**.
FY16-FY25 average: **4.4%**, above the world's **2.9%**.

50.s:
Consider the following statements about agricultural growth during FY16-FY25:
1. Agriculture and allied growth averaged 4.4% a year, above the world average of 2.9%.
2. Fishing and aquaculture grew at 8.8% and livestock at 7.1%.
3. Crops were the fastest-growing component.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
50.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: crops grew only 3.5%; fishing (8.8%) and livestock (7.1%) led growth. Hence 1 and 2 only (C).
50.tq: Allied sectors (fish 8.8, livestock 7.1) drive growth; crops only 3.5%.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **4.4%** a year (constant prices) — highest decadal growth ever, above the world's **2.9%**.
Statement 2 correct: **fishing and aquaculture 8.8%**, **livestock 7.1%**.
Statement 3 wrong: **crops** grew only **3.5%** — the slowest.
xa: Criticism: growth now led by livestock/fisheries while crop yields lag world averages.
Growth comes more from **area** than yield.

50.s: The total foodgrain production of India reached which figure in 2025-26 according to the cited estimate?
50.x: Total foodgrain production reached 376.56 million tonnes in 2025-26.
50.tq: Distinguish the total annual figure from kharif and rabi component estimates.
xs: **2025-26** foodgrains (2nd Advance Estimates) reached **376.56 million tonnes** — option **(4)** is correct.
**357.73 MT** is the **2024-25** final record.
xa: Kharif **1,741.44 LMT** and rabi **1,745.13 LMT** — both records.
Horticulture in **2025-26**: **377.78 MT**.

50.s: Which of the following correctly describes the trend in India's foodgrain production from 2019-20 to 2024-25?
o: It fluctuated without any definite direction.
50.x: Foodgrain production recorded a steady increase over the period from 2019-20 to 2024-25.
50.tq: Test the direction of a reported time-series trend.
xs: From **2019-20 to 2024-25**, production showed a **steady increase** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC 2024; PYQ keys).
The run ended in a record **357.73 MT** in **2024-25**.
xa: **Oilseeds**: area, production and productivity all rose.
**NMEO** targets nearly **70 million t** of oilseeds by **2030-31**.
Paddy and pulses **recovered** in **2024-25**.

50.s: Which one of the following comparisons between foodgrain and horticulture production in 2024–25 is correct?
o: Horticulture exceeded foodgrains, with production of 367.72 million tonnes.
Horticulture production was below the 2018–19 foodgrain figure.
Foodgrains exceeded horticulture by about 10 million tonnes.
Both were recorded at approximately 357.73 million tonnes.
50.x: Horticulture production was 367.72 million tonnes, exceeding foodgrain production of 357.73 million tonnes in 2024–25.
50.tq: Comparison-table based identification of the larger value.
xs: **Horticulture exceeded foodgrains**, at **367.72 million tonnes** — option **(1)** is correct.
Foodgrains were **357.73 MT** in **2024-25** — about **10** MT less, not more.
xa: Horticulture range cited: **362-368 MT**.
In **2025-26**: foodgrains **376.56 MT** vs horticulture **377.78 MT**.

50.s: Which one of the following sets contains only commodities in which India ranks first globally?
50.x: India ranks first globally in milk, pulses and spices. Wheat, fruits, vegetables, eggs, cotton and silk are listed among commodities in which India ranks second.
50.tq: Group identification by separating first-rank commodities from second-rank commodities.
xs: India ranks **1st** in **milk, pulses and spices** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Wheat, sugarcane, fruits, vegetables, eggs, cotton, silk** are **2nd**-rank items.
**Rice** is 1st per the newer figure, but wheat and sugarcane in option (2) are 2nd.
xa: Also 1st: **millets**, **jute**, dry onions.
**Fish**: **2nd** (official version), **1st in shrimp**.

50.s: India's pulse production and consumption position is correctly described as
50.x: India is both the largest producer and the largest consumer of pulses, with production of 25.68 million metric tonnes as the cited latest figure.
50.tq: Direct recall of a paired production-consumption position.
xs: India is the **largest producer and largest consumer** of pulses — option **(4)** is correct (APPCA 2026).
Pulse output: **25.68 MMT**.
xa: **Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses** (**2025-31**): tur, urad, masur — to end pulse imports.
Leading pulse state: **Madhya Pradesh**, then Rajasthan, Maharashtra.
El Niño years cut pulse output by **6-30%**.

50.s: Which one of the following statements regarding India's position in fish production is correct?
o: India ranks first in total fish production and second in shrimp output.
India ranks second in fish production and aquaculture, and first in shrimp output and exports.
India ranks third in fish production and first in all forms of aquaculture.
India ranks second in fish production but has no stated position in shrimp exports.
50.x: The official figure places India second in fish production and aquaculture, while it ranks first in shrimp output and exports. Fish accounts for 8% of world output.
50.tq: Separate overall fish ranking from the specialised shrimp ranking.
xs: India is **2nd** in fish and aquaculture and **1st in shrimp output and exports** — option **(2)** is correct (IYB 2026).
Fish is **8%** of world output.
xa: ⚠ Another list puts fish at **3rd**; the **official version (2nd)** is the one to use.
Fishing and aquaculture grew **8.8%** in FY16-FY25 — the fastest driver.

50.s: Which one of the following crop–leading state pairs is NOT correctly matched?
50.x: Gujarat is the leading state for cotton, followed by Telangana and Maharashtra. Rajasthan leads rapeseed-mustard, Gujarat leads groundnut, and Madhya Pradesh leads soybean.
50.tq: Use the crop-wise leader table and identify the swapped state.
xs: **Cotton — Punjab** is wrong: **Gujarat** leads cotton, then **Telangana** and **Maharashtra** — option **(1)** is the mismatch.
**Soybean — MP**, **Rapeseed-mustard — Rajasthan**, **Groundnut — Gujarat** are correct.
xa: **Punjab's cotton area fell 37.5%** to **80,000 ha** in **2026**.
⚠ Soybean leader is **MP** (not Maharashtra) in one list.

50.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the description 'Rice Bowl of central India'?
50.x: Chhattisgarh is described as the 'Rice Bowl of central India'.
50.tq: Match the descriptive agricultural title with the state.
xs: **Chhattisgarh** is the "**Rice Bowl of central India**" — option **(4)** is correct.
**West Bengal, UP and Punjab** are the traditional rice leaders, but not this title.
xa: **Punjab** has the **highest rice yield**.
Chhattisgarh is in the **BGREI** list of eastern rice states.

50.s: Which one of the following crop–leading state pairs is correctly matched?
50.x: Madhya Pradesh leads in pulses, followed by Rajasthan and Maharashtra. Uttar Pradesh, not Maharashtra or Gujarat, leads in sugarcane; Punjab is not a leading pulse state.
50.tq: Pulses = MP; sugarcane = UP.
xs: **Pulses — Madhya Pradesh** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Sugarcane** is led by **Uttar Pradesh**, not Maharashtra or Gujarat.
Pulses are led by **MP**, then **Rajasthan, Maharashtra** — not Punjab.
xa: Highest **pulse yields**: **MP and Gujarat**.
**Soybean** also led by **MP**.

50.s: Which of the following crops experienced a fall in area of 18 lakh hectares, with output declining to 290.91 lakh bales in 2025–26 from about 350 lakh bales?
50.x: Cotton area fell by 18 lakh hectares, and its output declined to 290.91 lakh bales in 2025–26 from approximately 350 lakh bales.
50.tq: Linking a crop with its distinctive area and output figures.
xs: **Cotton** area fell **18 lakh ha** and output dropped to **290.91 lakh bales** (**2025-26**) from about **350** — option **(4)** is correct.
Paddy and pulses, by contrast, **recovered** in **2024-25**; soybean's fall was in **MP** area (**10%**).
xa: **India became a net importer of raw cotton**.
Cotton yield: about **440 kg/ha** vs global ~**770**.
**Kapas Kanti** mission targets **755 kg/ha**.

50.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a recent change in India's cotton trade position?
o: India became a net importer of silk owing to cotton-area expansion.
India became a net importer of raw cotton following declining output and area.
India discontinued raw-cotton imports because of higher cotton yields.
India became a net exporter of raw cotton after a rise in domestic output.
50.x: India became a net importer of raw cotton after declines in cotton area and output.
50.tq: Cause-effect recall with reversed trade-position distractors.
xs: **India became a net importer of raw cotton** as area and output fell — option **(2)** is correct.
Area fell **18 lakh ha**; output fell to **290.91 lakh bales** in **2025-26**.
xa: **Punjab's cotton area** fell **37.5%** to **80,000 ha** (2026).
**Bt cotton** had raised yields from **190 (2002)** to **480 kg/ha (2023)**.

50.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses:

1. It targets production of 350 lakh tonnes from 310 lakh hectares.
2. It provides for 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor.
3. It covers the period 2025–26 to 2030–31.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: All three statements are correct. The mission targets 350 lakh tonnes from 310 lakh hectares, provides 100% MSP procurement for tur, urad and masoor, and runs from 2025–26 to 2030–31.
50.tq: Statement combination covering targets, procurement and time period.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1 correct: target **350 lakh t** from **310 lakh ha**.
Statement 2 correct: **100%** MSP procurement of **tur, urad and masoor**.
Statement 3 correct: runs **2025-26 to 2030-31**, outlay **₹11,440 crore**.
xa: Aim: **end pulse imports** (APPCA 2026).
India pulse output: **25.68 MMT**.

50.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the kharif and rabi paddy yields of Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
50.x: The kharif paddy yield was 5,612 kg/ha, while the rabi yield was higher at 6,979 kg/ha.
50.tq: Check the seasonal labels before comparing the two yields.
xs: AP's **2024-25** paddy yield: **kharif 5,612 kg/ha**, **rabi 6,979 kg/ha** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) swaps them; **6,063** is the overall paddy yield and **6,453** is **maize**.
xa: AP paddy (about **6 t/ha**) is among the best.
AP paddy output **2024-25**: **127.15 lakh t**.

50.s:
Consider the following statements regarding rice yields:
1. West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh were identified as below the national average in the cited estimate.
2. Heat, dry spells and unseasonal rain were cited among the reasons for lower yields in major rice states.
3. Punjab's high rice yield is associated with canal and tubewell irrigation despite low rainfall.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: All three statements are correct. The cited explanation links lower yields in major rice states with climatic stresses, while Punjab benefits from canal and tubewell irrigation despite low rainfall.
50.tq: Combine the distributional fact with its environmental and irrigation explanations.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1 correct: **WB, UP, Telangana, Odisha, AP, TN** are **below the national average**.
Statement 2 correct: reasons cited — **heat, dry spells, unseasonal rain**.
Statement 3 correct: **Punjab**'s top yield comes from **canal + tubewell irrigation** despite low rainfall.
xa: Rice is ~**67%** irrigated vs pulses ~**26%**.
Yields fall about **8%** per **1°C** rise.

50.s: India's rice yield of about 2,929 kg per hectare is best compared with China's rice yield of approximately:
50.x: India's rice yield was about 2,929 kg/ha, compared with approximately 7,100 kg/ha in China.
50.tq: Distinguish the China comparison from the separate global foodgrain average.
xs: China's rice yield is about **7,100 kg per hectare** vs India's **2,929 kg/ha** — option **(3)** is correct.
India's yield is **less than half** of China's.
**4,000 kg/ha** is the global average some notes give; **5,612** and **6,063** are AP paddy yields.
xa: ⚠ Some notes (**8** Jun 2026) call **2,929 kg/ha** the foodgrain yield.
**Punjab** has India's highest rice yield.

50.s: The Kapas Kanti mission has a target of raising cotton yield to:
50.x: The Kapas Kanti mission targets a cotton yield of 755 kg per hectare.
50.tq: Separate a future mission target from the present Indian and global averages.
xs: The **Kapas Kanti** mission targets **755 kg per hectare** — option **(2)** is correct.
**770** is the global average; **480** is the **2023** Bt cotton level.
xa: Present cotton yield: about **440 kg/ha**.
India became a **net importer of raw cotton**.

50.s: Which states are specifically associated with the highest pulse yields in the cited comparison?
50.x: Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat have the highest pulse yields, helped by black or semi-arid soils and high seed replacement rates.
50.tq: Link the yield ranking with the stated soil and seed-replacement factors.
xs: Highest pulse yields are in **Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat** — option **(4)** is correct.
Reasons: **black/semi-arid soils** and high seed replacement (**SRR**).
xa: **MP** is also the leading pulse producer.
Pulses are only ~**26%** irrigated.
El Niño years cut pulse yields **5-25%**.

50.s: Cereal yield is defined as the quantity of cereals produced per hectare of
50.x: Cereal yield is measured in kilograms per hectare of harvested land under cereals.
50.tq: Precise-definition discrimination among similar agricultural-area terms.
xs: **Cereal yield** = kg per hectare of **harvested land under cereals** (World Bank usage) — option **(4)** is correct.
It is not measured on irrigated, total cultivated or net sown area.
xa: India's yields of **cereals, maize, soybean and pulses** trail global averages.
Exception: **groundnut**.

50.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a major cause of India's cereal-yield gap?
o: Rainfed farming covering about 50–51% of net sown area
Universal access to efficient cold-chain infrastructure
Small and marginal holdings forming about 86% of holdings
A skewed NPK ratio and low seed replacement rate
50.x: Universal access to efficient cold-chain infrastructure is not a stated cause; rather, cold-chain losses account for about 30%. The other three factors contribute to the yield gap.
50.tq: Find the exception by reversing a stated constraint into an advantage.
xs: **Universal access to efficient cold-chain infrastructure** is not a cause — there are **30%** cold-chain losses — option **(2)** is the answer.
Real causes: **rainfed** farming (**50-51%** of net sown area), **86%** small/marginal holdings, skewed **NPK ratio** and low **SRR**.
xa: Average holding: **1.08 ha**.
Soybean below **2 t/ha** in many rainfed districts.

50.s:
Consider the following statements regarding climate-related yield effects:

1. Yields fall by about 8% for every 1°C rise in temperature.
2. Wheat yields may fall by 6–10% under heat stress.
3. A 1°C rise can wipe out about four years of rice and wheat productivity gains.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: All three statements reflect the reported effects of heat on agricultural productivity: around 8% yield loss per 1°C, wheat losses of 6–10%, and the loss of about four years of rice and wheat productivity gains.
50.tq: Statement verification using related climate-impact figures.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1 correct: yields fall about **8%** per **1°C**.
Statement 2 correct: **wheat** falls **6-10%**.
Statement 3 correct: **1 deg C** wipes ~**4 years** of rice/wheat productivity gains.
xa: A **20%** rainfall deficit also cuts yields ~**8%**.
El Niño years: pulse yield falls **5-25%**.

50.s:
Consider the following pairs (pathway for raising productivity - means):
1. Better seed - SRR/VRR and genome editing
2. Mechanisation - Custom Hiring Centres
3. Balanced nutrition - Direct Seeded Rice (DSR)
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
50.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Pair 3 is wrong: balanced nutrition comes through the Soil Health Card; DSR is a water-saving pathway. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A misses pair 2, C and D include the wrong pair 3.
50.tq: Seed - SRR/VRR; water - DSR/SRI/micro-irrigation; nutrition - Soil Health Card; machines - CHCs.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Pair 1 correct: **better seed** via **SRR/VRR** and **genome editing**.
Pair 2 correct: **mechanisation** via **CHCs**.
Pair 3 wrong: **balanced nutrition** is via the **Soil Health Card**; **DSR** is a **water** pathway.
xa: Water pathways: **micro-irrigation**, **DSR**, **SRI**.
Causes they target: low **SRR** / HYV seed replacement and a skewed **NPK ratio**.

50.s: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana is intended to cover how many low-productivity districts during 2025–26 to 2030–31?
50.x: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana covers 100 low-productivity districts during 2025–26 to 2030–31.
50.tq: Direct numerical recall of scheme coverage and period.
xs: **PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana** covers **100 low-productivity districts** (**2025-26 to 2030-31**) — option **(3)** is correct.
It targets the yield gap where productivity is lowest.
xa: **Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses** runs the same period, **₹11,440 crore**.
**NFSM** was renamed **NFSNM** in **FY25**.
**BGREI** (**2010-11**) targets rice systems of eastern states.

50.s: Which one of the following crops is identified as an exception to India's generally lower yields compared with global averages?
50.x: India's yields of cereals, maize, soybean and pulses trail global averages, whereas groundnut is identified as an exception because of semi-arid concentration and improved varieties.
50.tq: Exception-based recall from a comparative yield statement.
xs: **Groundnut** is the exception to India's lower-than-global yields — option **(3)** is correct.
Reasons: **semi-arid concentration** and **improved varieties**.
**Soybean**, **maize** and **pulses** trail global averages.
xa: **Gujarat** leads groundnut.

50.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of El Niño on pulses?
o: Acreage rises by 2–9% and output rises by 6–30%.
Acreage falls by 2–9% and output falls by 6–30%.
Acreage falls by 6–30% and output falls by 2–9%.
Acreage remains unchanged while output rises by 5–25%.
50.x: In El Niño years, pulse acreage declines by about 2–9%, while output declines by about 6–30%.
50.tq: Separating two similar percentage ranges by the variable they describe.
xs: In El Niño years, pulse **acreage falls 2-9%** and **output falls 6-30%** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (3) swaps the ranges; nothing rises.
xa: Pulse **yield** falls **5-25%** in El Niño years.
Kharif 2026 sowing was only ~**61%** of normal by **19 Aug** (El Nino).

50.s: Total factor productivity in agriculture refers to
o: output growth not explained by growth in inputs such as land, labour, capital and fertiliser
the total value of agricultural exports divided by farm employment
output growth explained only by expansion of cultivated land
the ratio of fertiliser use to cropped area
50.x: Total factor productivity is the part of output growth that cannot be explained by increased use of inputs such as land, labour, capital and fertiliser.
50.tq: Definition-based discrimination against single-input productivity measures.
xs: **TFP** = **output growth not explained by growth in inputs** (land, labour, capital, fertiliser) — option **(1)** is correct.
It is not an export ratio, land expansion or fertiliser intensity.
xa: TFP drivers: **research and new varieties**, **irrigation**, **rural roads and markets**, **extension**, **education**.
The **ES 2025-26** discusses TFP only for the whole economy.

50.s: The Technology Mission on Oilseeds, launched in 1986, was associated with which of the following developments?
o: Promotion of oilseeds, with pulses and maize added later, under the Yellow Revolution
Promotion of rice-based systems in eastern India under the White Revolution
Promotion of millets exclusively for industrial use
Promotion of sugarcane and cotton under the Blue Revolution
50.x: The Technology Mission on Oilseeds was launched in 1986. It focused on oilseeds, with pulses and maize added later, and was associated with the Yellow Revolution led by Sam Pitroda.
50.tq: Match the mission with its launch year, target crops and associated revolution.
xs: The **Technology Mission on Oilseeds** (**1986**) promoted **oilseeds**, with **pulses and maize added later**, under the **Yellow Revolution** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is linked with **Sam Pitroda**.
Rice-based systems in eastern India are **BGREI**, not the White Revolution.
xa: Later oilseed missions: **NMOOP (2014)**, **NMEO-Oil Palm (2021)**, **NMEO-Oilseeds (2024)**.
NMEO targets nearly **70 million t** of oilseeds by **2030-31**.
"**Tilhan Mission**" (Feb **2020**, PYQ) also relates to **oilseed production**.

50.s:
Consider the following pairs (mission - target crops):
1. BGREI - rice-based systems of eastern States, including Chhattisgarh
2. INSIMP - millets for nutritional security
3. NMOOP - pulses and maize only
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
50.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Pair 3 is wrong: NMOOP (2014) covers oilseeds and oil palm. Hence 1 and 2 only (D).
50.tq: NMOOP = oilseeds + oil palm; INSIMP = millets; BGREI = eastern rice.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct — option **(4) 1 and 2 only**.
Pair 1 correct: **BGREI** = rice-based systems of eastern states, incl. **Chhattisgarh**.
Pair 2 correct: **INSIMP** (under RKVY) = **millets** for nutritional security.
Pair 3 wrong: **NMOOP (2014)** covers **oilseeds + oil palm**, not pulses and maize.
xa: BGREI (**2010-11**) is a sub-scheme of **RKVY**.
Pulses and maize were added to the **Technology Mission on Oilseeds** (**1986**).

50.s: The ‘Tilhan Mission’, referred to in February 2020, relates primarily to which of the following?
50.x: 'Tilhan' means oilseeds, so the Tilhan Mission (Feb 2020, PYQ) relates to oilseed production, in the line of the Technology Mission on Oilseeds and NMEO. Pulses have a separate mission (Aatmanirbharta in Pulses) and millets come under INSIMP.
50.tq: Discriminate between similarly named crop initiatives by identifying the target crop.
xs: The **Tilhan Mission** (Feb **2020**, PYQ) relates to **oilseed production** — option **(4)** is correct.
Pulses have their own **Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses**; millets fall under **INSIMP**.
xa: The **Technology Mission on Oilseeds** dates from **1986**.
**NMEO** targets nearly **70 million t** by **2030-31**.

50.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Food Security Mission (NFSM):
1. It was launched in 2007-08.
2. It initially covered rice, wheat and pulses.
3. It was renamed the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) in FY25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: All three are correct. NFSM began in 2007-08 with rice, wheat and pulses, later added coarse cereals, commercial crops and nutri-cereals, and was renamed NFSNM in FY25 (Economic Survey 2025-26). So A, B and C each leave out a correct statement.
50.tq: NFSM 2007-08 → NFSNM FY25 (nutrition added).
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1 correct: **NFSM** began in **2007-08**.
Statement 2 correct: it first covered **rice, wheat, pulses**; later coarse cereals, commercial crops, nutri-cereals.
Statement 3 correct: renamed **NFSNM** in **FY25** (ES **2025-26**).
xa: **PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana**: **100 low-productivity districts** (**2025-26 to 2030-31**).
**INSIMP** (**2011-12**) covers millets.

50.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Commission on Agriculture was set up in 1970 and submitted its final report in 1976.
2. The Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income was chaired by M.S. Swaminathan.
3. The Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income was set up in 2016 and submitted its report in 2018.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
50.x: Statement 1 is correct: the NCA was set up in 1970 and gave its final report in 1976. Statement 2 is wrong: the Doubling Farmers' Income Committee was chaired by Ashok Dalwai, not M.S. Swaminathan. Statement 3 is correct: it was set up in 2016 and reported in 2018. Hence 1 and 3 only.
50.tq: Dalwai = Doubling (2016-18); Swaminathan = National Commission on Farmers.

50.s: The foodgrain production of Andhra Pradesh was 157.59 lakh tonnes in which year?
50.x: Andhra Pradesh produced 157.59 lakh tonnes of foodgrains in 2017-18.
50.tq: Match the exact state production figure with its agricultural year.
xs: AP produced **157.59 lakh tonnes** of foodgrains in **2017-18** — option **(4)** is correct (PYQ key; APPSC 2019).
xa: AP output: **143 → 162 → 190 lakh t** across **2023-26**.

50.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the agricultural performance of Andhra Pradesh in 2023–24 in the Survey series?
o: It was the only year of contraction, with agriculture and allied growth of −9.82%.
It was the only year of contraction, with agriculture and allied growth of −1.58%.
It recorded positive growth because the crops sub-sector rose by 9.82%.
It recorded the highest growth, with agriculture and allied growth of 13.5%.
50.x: 2023–24 was the only year of contraction in the Survey series, with agriculture and allied growth of −1.58%. The crops sub-sector fell by 9.82% at AE, which is a separate figure.
50.tq: Separate the overall agriculture figure from the crops sub-sector figure.
xs: **2023-24** was the **only year of contraction**, with agriculture & allied at **-1.58%** (FRE) — option **(2)** is correct.
**9.82%** is the fall in the **crops sub-sector** (at AE), not the agriculture & allied figure.
xa: AP foodgrains fell to **143.31 lakh t** in 2023-24.

50.s: Which one of the following best describes the agricultural situation in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Its paddy yield is about 10 tonnes per hectare and output remains constant each year.
