58.s: The proposal made in September 2025 concerning the Public Distribution System involved which of the following?
o: Limiting the PDS exclusively to wheat procurement
Replacing all Fair Price Shops with direct cash transfers
Trimming cereal entitlements and adding pulses to the PDS
Increasing cereal entitlements and removing pulses from the PDS
58.x: The proposal was to trim cereal entitlements and add pulses to the PDS. It was presented in the context of reviewing the composition of PDS entitlements.
58.tq: Distinguish the proposed change in the commodity mix from extreme replacement or exclusion claims.
xs: The **Sep 2025** proposal was to **trim cereal entitlements** and **add pulses** to the PDS — option **(3)** is correct.
It figures in the PDS criticism and debates, alongside leakage and DBT vs in-kind grain.
xa: The **Shanta Kumar Committee** had earlier recommended adding **pulses and millets** to PDS.
Stocks far above norms raise **carrying costs** and the rising **economic cost**.

58.s: If food-grain stocks remain far above the prescribed norms, which consequence is most directly associated with such a situation?
o: Automatic reduction in food subsidy expenditure
58.x: Stocks substantially above norms increase carrying costs because larger quantities have to be stored and maintained.
58.tq: Apply the direct cause-and-effect relationship rather than choosing an absolute consequence.
xs: Stocks far above norms push up **carrying costs** — option **(1) Increase in carrying costs** is correct.
Subsidy does not fall automatically: food subsidy = **economic cost minus CIP**, and the economic cost keeps rising.
xa: **Economic cost** = **MSP + bonus** + **procurement incidentals** + **distribution cost**; pooled grain cost is about **two-thirds** of it.
A **hidden subsidy** example: FCI's carrying cost financed by borrowing instead of budget releases.
FCI challenges: rising operating costs, **excess stocks + wastage**, falling issue-price earnings.

59.s: Which one of the following correctly describes stunting, wasting and underweight, respectively?
o: Low weight-for-age, low height-for-age and low weight-for-height
Low height-for-age, low weight-for-height and low weight-for-age
Low weight-for-height, low weight-for-age and low height-for-age
Low height-for-age, low weight-for-age and low weight-for-height
59.x: Stunting denotes low height-for-age, wasting denotes low weight-for-height, and underweight denotes low weight-for-age.
59.tq: Match each indicator with its precise measurement before examining the options.
xs: **Stunting** = low **height-for-age**, **wasting** = low **weight-for-height**, **underweight** = low **weight-for-age** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) swaps all three; options (3) and (4) mix up wasting and underweight.
xa: Stunting shows **chronic** undernutrition; wasting shows **acute** undernutrition.
NFHS-6: stunting **29.3%**, severe wasting **5.2%**, underweight **31.8%**.
**Double burden of malnutrition** = undernutrition + overnutrition in the same population.

59.s:
Consider the following statements regarding forms of malnutrition:
1. Undernutrition includes protein-energy malnutrition and micronutrient deficiency.
2. Stunting and wasting are included within undernutrition.
3. Overnutrition includes overweight and obesity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: All three statements are correct. Undernutrition encompasses protein-energy malnutrition, micronutrient deficiency, stunting, wasting and underweight, whereas overnutrition includes overweight and obesity.
59.tq: Separate the two broad categories and verify each component individually.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statements 1 and 2: **undernutrition** = **protein-energy malnutrition** + **micronutrient deficiency** + **stunting** + **wasting** (+ underweight) (APPSC-GS 2019; WHO).
Statement 3: **overnutrition** = **overweight and obesity**.
xa: Both together in one population = **double burden of malnutrition**; **NFHS-6** confirms India faces it.
**Underweight** = low weight-for-age.

59.s: The occurrence of undernutrition and overnutrition in the same population is known as:
59.x: The coexistence of undernutrition and overnutrition in the same population is called the double burden of malnutrition.
59.tq: Test the exact official term for a paired concept.
xs: Undernutrition and overnutrition together in the same population is the **double burden of malnutrition** — option **(4)** is correct.
**NFHS-6** confirms India faces this double burden (**5 Jun 2026**).
xa: Undernutrition covers protein-energy malnutrition, micronutrient deficiency, stunting and wasting.
Overnutrition = **overweight and obesity**.
NFHS-6: stunting down to **29.3%**, yet the double burden persists.

**Early (adolescent) pregnancy** and **poverty and gender gaps** are also listed causes.

59.x: The National Goitre Control Programme was launched in 1962 and renamed NIDDCP in 1992.
59.tq: Distinguish the original launch year from the renaming year.
xs: The Goitre programme became **NIDDCP** in **1992** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1962** is when the **National Goitre Control Programme** began; **1970** is the Vitamin A and anaemia prophylaxis programmes.
**1999** is a trap: "NIDDCP - 1999" was a **wrong** pair in APPSC-GS 2024.
xa: NIDDCP is under **Health & FW**; AP runs it under **NP-NCD**.
**Double-fortified salt** carries **iodine + iron**.

59.s: MAA, or Mothers’ Absolute Affection, is a programme related to:
59.x: MAA is a breastfeeding promotion programme launched in 2016.
59.tq: Decode the programme title and connect it with its health objective.
xs: **MAA (Mothers' Absolute Affection)** promotes **breastfeeding** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was launched in **2016** under **Health & FW** (correctly dated in APPSC-GS 2024).
xa: NFHS-6: breastfeeding within 1 hour of birth rose from **41.8%** to **50.1%**.
Complementary feeding (6-8 months): **45.9% to 59.5%**.

59.s: PM POSHAN, which renamed the Mid-Day Meal scheme in 2021, is administered by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
59.x: PM POSHAN (renamed from MDM in 2021) is under the Ministry of Education. ICDS is under Women and Child Development; NIDDCP, MAA and Anaemia Mukt Bharat are under Health and Family Welfare; the PDS is under Food and Public Distribution.
59.tq: School meals = Education; ICDS = WCD; NIDDCP/MAA/AMB = Health.
xs: **PM POSHAN** (renamed from Mid-Day Meal in **2021**) is under the **Ministry of Education** — option **(3)** is correct.
**ICDS** is under **Women & Child Development**; **NIDDCP**, **MAA** and **Anaemia Mukt Bharat** are under **Health & FW**.
xa: The Mid-Day Meal (NP-NSPE) began on **15 Aug 1995**; the idea came from **Tamil Nadu**.
Fortified rice Phase I (**2021-22**) covered ICDS and PM POSHAN.

59.s: The principal goal associated with POSHAN Abhiyaan is expressed as:
59.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan aims to achieve a Suposhit Bharat through convergence, technology and a Jan Andolan.
59.tq: Distinguish the programme’s stated goal from other national slogans.
xs: POSHAN Abhiyaan's goal is **Suposhit Bharat** — option **(1)** is correct.
It works through **convergence**, **technology** and **Jan Andolan**.
xa: It targets **stunting**, **undernutrition/underweight**, **anaemia** and **low birth weight**.
**Mission Poshan 2.0** runs over the **15th FC period 2021-22 to 2025-26**.
The **POSHAN Tracker** app monitors Anganwadi services in real time.

59.s: Which of the following is NOT among the major outcomes targeted by POSHAN Abhiyaan?
o: Reduction in anaemia among children, women and adolescent girls
59.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan targets reductions in stunting, undernutrition or underweight, anaemia and low birth weight. Universal increase in adult obesity is not an objective.
59.tq: Find the option outside the programme’s stated target set.
xs: **Universal increase in adult obesity** is not a POSHAN Abhiyaan target — option **(1)** is the answer.
It targets reduction of **stunting**, **undernutrition/underweight**, **anaemia** and **low birth weight**.
xa: Anaemia targets cover children **6-59 months** and women and adolescent girls **15-49**.
Obesity is **overnutrition**, the other half of the double burden.
Goal: **Suposhit Bharat**.

59.s: What is the function of the POSHAN Tracker application?
o: It provides real-time monitoring of Anganwadi services.
It fixes the procurement price of cereals.
59.x: The POSHAN Tracker enables real-time monitoring of Anganwadi services.
59.tq: Match the digital tool with the administrative function it performs.
xs: The **POSHAN Tracker** gives **real-time monitoring of Anganwadi services** — option **(2)** is correct.
POSHAN Abhiyaan leans on **technology** with convergence and Jan Andolan.
xa: Poshan Tracker data (**July 2025**) show **UP** worst for stunting (**48.8%**).
**Bihar** is worst for wasting (**9.3%**); **MP** for underweight (**24.8%**).

59.s: Adolescents aged 10–19 years receive weekly iron and folic acid supplementation under which intervention?
59.x: Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation, abbreviated WIFS, covers adolescents aged 10–19 years under Anaemia Mukt Bharat interventions.
59.tq: Separate the similarly placed nutrition acronyms by their specific intervention.
xs: **WIFS** gives weekly IFA to adolescents aged **10-19** — option **(2)** is correct.
**NIDDCP** is the iodine programme and **MAA** promotes breastfeeding.
xa: WIFS falls under **Anaemia Mukt Bharat**: **IFA** tablets, deworming, outreach for **6 target groups**.
Anaemia Mukt Bharat dates to **2018**, under Health & FW.

59.s: Which of the following is a component of the Anaemia Mukt Bharat strategy?
o: Replacement of all supplementary nutrition with cereals
IFA tablets, deworming and outreach for six target groups
59.x: Anaemia Mukt Bharat uses IFA tablets, deworming and outreach directed at six target groups. It is not limited to calcium supplementation.
59.tq: Identify the intervention bundle rather than a single nutrient measure.
xs: Anaemia Mukt Bharat uses **IFA tablets, deworming and outreach for six target groups** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is about iron and folic acid, not calcium-only or cereal-only measures.
xa: **WIFS**: weekly IFA for adolescents aged **10-19**.
It began in **2018** under **Health & FW**.
POSHAN Abhiyaan also targets **anaemia** among children **6-59 months** and women/girls **15-49**.

59.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the phases of fortified rice distribution:
1. Phase I covered ICDS and PM POSHAN.
2. Phase II extended coverage to 291 Aspirational and High-Burden districts under TPDS.
3. Phase III covered all districts under TPDS.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: Phase I in 2021-22 covered ICDS and PM POSHAN, Phase II in 2022-23 added 291 districts under TPDS, and Phase III in 2023-24 covered all districts under TPDS.
59.tq: Check each statement against the successive expansion of coverage.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: Phase I (**2021-22**) covered **ICDS** and **PM POSHAN**.
Statement 2: Phase II (**2022-23**) added **291 Aspirational and High-Burden districts** under TPDS.
Statement 3: Phase III (**2023-24**) covered **all districts** under TPDS.
xa: The pilot came in **2019**; rollout was complete by **March 2024** with **100%** lifting.
FSSAI fortification logo: **"+F"**.

59.s: Which symbol represents the FSSAI fortification logo?
59.x: The FSSAI fortification logo is represented by the symbol '+F'.
59.tq: Test the exact official label rather than a descriptive expansion of the logo.
xs: The FSSAI fortification logo is **"+F"** — option **(2)** is correct.
It marks fortified foods such as the **fortified rice** supplied through **ICDS**, **PM POSHAN** and **TPDS**.
xa: **Double-fortified salt** carries **iodine + iron**.
Fortified rice reached **all TPDS districts** in Phase III (**2023-24**).

59.s: Double-fortified salt contains which combination of nutrients?
59.x: Double-fortified salt is fortified with iodine and iron.
59.tq: Separate the nutrient pair in double-fortified salt from other fortification combinations.
xs: **Double-fortified salt** carries **iodine and iron** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Iron and folic acid** is the **IFA** tablet combination of Anaemia Mukt Bharat, not the salt.
xa: The FSSAI fortification logo is **"+F"**.
**NIDDCP** (**1992**), formerly the Goitre programme (**1962**), tackles iodine deficiency.
Anaemia Mukt Bharat tackles iron deficiency with **IFA** tablets and deworming.

59.s: Anna Amrutha Hastham provides which benefit?
o: A corpus payable to orphaned children at age 23
Free antenatal check-up on the ninth day of every month
One full meal a day at the Anganwadi Centre for pregnant and lactating women
A monthly supply of 30 eggs to children aged 6–36 months
59.x: Anna Amrutha Hastham provides one full meal a day at the Anganwadi Centre to pregnant and lactating women.
59.tq: Match the scheme name with its direct service benefit.
xs: **Anna Amrutha Hastham** gives **one full meal a day** at Anganwadi centres to **pregnant and lactating women** — option **(3)** is correct.
**30 eggs** a month for children 6-36 months is the **tribal-area package**, not this scheme.
xa: **Bala Sanjeevani** gives these women Take Home Ration plus a **₹250** monthly nutrition kit.
Bala Sanjeevani runs through **47,296 AWCs** in plain areas.

59.s: Children aged 36–72 months under the plain-area package receive:
o: A meal, one egg and 200 ml milk
A hot cooked meal, one egg and 100 ml milk
A hot cooked meal, two eggs and 200 ml milk
59.x: Children aged 36–72 months receive a hot cooked meal, one egg and 100 ml milk under the plain-area package.
59.tq: Match the age group with its specific meal and milk entitlement.
xs: Plain-area children **36-72 months** get a **hot cooked meal**, **egg** and **100 ml milk** — option **(2)** is correct.
**200 ml** milk is the **tribal-area** provision.
xa: ⚠ The tribal package doubles milk for 36-72 months (**100 ml → 200 ml**).
Children **6-36 months** (plain) get **Balamrutham 2.5 kg + 25 eggs + 2.5 l milk** a month.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about the tribal-area nutrition package:
1. Children aged 36–72 months receive a meal, one egg and 200 ml milk.
2. Children aged 6–36 months receive 2.5 kg Balamrutham, 30 eggs and 6 litres milk per month.
3. Children aged 6–36 months receive fewer eggs than children in the plain-area package.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The tribal-area package provides 30 eggs, which is more than the 25 eggs provided in the plain-area package, so statement 3 is false.
59.tq: Use comparison of quantities to detect the reversed claim in statement 3.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: tribal children **36-72 months** get a meal, egg and **200 ml** milk.
Statement 2: tribal children **6-36 months** get **2.5 kg Balamrutham**, **30 eggs** and **6 l milk**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **30 eggs** is more than the plain-area **25 eggs**.
xa: Plain-area 6-36 months milk is only **2.5 l**.
Older notes call the tribal package **YSR Sampoorna Poshana Plus**.

59.s: The adolescent-girl programme in Andhra Pradesh is implemented in which of the following districts or areas?
o: All districts uniformly through urban Anganwadi Centres
ASR, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa
59.x: The adolescent-girl programme is implemented in ASR, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa, covering 14,942 girls.
59.tq: Test the exact geographical coverage instead of assuming statewide uniformity.
xs: AP's adolescent-girl coverage is in **ASR, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa** — option **(2)** is correct.
It covers **14,942** adolescent girls.
xa: Poshan 2.0 in AP covers **19.13 lakh** children below 6.
**₹99.58 crore** was released for **9,958 AWCs**; **192** new AWCs under **PM JANMAN**.

59.s: As per 2024-25 data, the ICDS network in Andhra Pradesh comprises about:
59.x: AP ICDS (2024-25) has 55,607 AWCs and 257 projects (200 rural, 33 urban, 24 tribal) in 26 districts. 47,296 is the number of AWCs delivering Bala Sanjeevani in plain areas; 9,958 AWCs received ₹99.58 crore; 192 are new AWCs under PM JANMAN.
59.tq: AP ICDS: 55,607 AWCs, 257 projects (200 rural, 33 urban, 24 tribal).
xs: AP ICDS (2024-25) has **55,607 AWCs** and **257 projects** — option **(2)** is correct.
**47,296** is Bala Sanjeevani's plain-area AWCs; **9,958** AWCs got funds; **192** are new PM JANMAN AWCs.
xa: The 257 projects split into **200 rural**, **33 urban**, **24 tribal**, across **26** districts.
ICDS was launched on **2 Oct 1975**.

59.s: Which of the following is identified as a criticism in the debate on food security and nutrition policy?
o: GHI uses only agricultural production data
HFSS foods are permitted without restriction near schools
Cereal-centric PDS may limit dietary diversity
Fortification eliminates the need for all dietary diversity
59.x: The cereal-centric nature of the PDS is criticised for not adequately ensuring dietary diversity. Methodology of the GHI and food labelling are also subjects of debate.
59.tq: Select the policy criticism that follows directly from the stated nutrition debate.
xs: **Cereal-centric PDS vs dietary diversity** is a named criticism — option **(3)** is correct.
HFSS foods are not unrestricted: there is a **ban** within **50 m** of schools.
xa: Other debates: **methodology of the GHI**, **FSSAI labelling**.
**Cereal-heavy diets** short on protein, iron and micronutrients cause malnutrition.

59.s: The restriction concerning HFSS foods mentioned in the context of school nutrition relates to their sale within what distance of schools?
59.x: The cited policy debate concerns the ban on HFSS foods within 50 metres of schools.
59.tq: Identify the precise distance attached to the regulatory restriction.
xs: The ban covers **HFSS foods** within **50 metres** of schools — option **(2)** is correct.
It appears with **FSSAI labelling** in the debates (**29 Jun 2026**).
xa: Other debates: **cereal-centric PDS** vs dietary diversity and the **GHI** methodology.
AP angle: last-mile gaps in **tribal hamlets** and **Rayalaseema**.

60.s: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) has been implemented since:
60.x: MIDH is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme running since 2014-15. 2005-06 is the launch year of the National Horticulture Mission, which MIDH later subsumed.
60.tq: Distinguish the implementation year of MIDH from the launch year of NHM.
xs: **MIDH** has been a Centrally Sponsored Scheme since **2014-15** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2023).
**2005-06** is the year of the **NHM**, which MIDH later subsumed.
xa: MIDH also subsumed the **NE/Himalayan horticulture mission**.
The horticulture boom of **1991-2003** is called the **Golden Revolution**.
Horticulture output (**367.72 MT**, 2024-25) now exceeds foodgrains (**357.73 MT**).

60.s: The Golden Revolution in India is associated with the period:
60.x: The horticulture boom during 1991–2003 is known as the Golden Revolution.
60.tq: Associate the named revolution with its stated time span.
xs: The **Golden Revolution** (horticulture boom) covers **1991-2003** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **Golden Revolution** = horticulture, but **Golden Fibre** = **jute**.
xa: **Silver Fibre** = cotton; **Sweet Revolution** = honey; **Blue** = fisheries; **White** = milk.
**MIDH** (since **2014-15**) is today's horticulture scheme.

60.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s horticulture sector:
1. Horticulture output in 2024-25 was 367.72 million tonnes.
2. It exceeded foodgrain output of 357.73 million tonnes.
3. Horticulture contributes approximately 33% of agricultural GVA.
4. It uses less than 14% of the cropped area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
60.x: All four statements are correct. Horticulture output was 367.72 million tonnes, above foodgrain output of 357.73 million tonnes, contributed about 33% of agricultural GVA and used under 14% of cropped area.
60.tq: Check the output, comparison, GVA share and land-use figures as a single data cluster.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Statements 1 and 2: horticulture output was **367.72 MT** (2024-25), above foodgrains at **357.73 MT**.
Statements 3 and 4: about **33% of agricultural GVA** on under **14%** of cropped area.
xa: Older 2026 notes put the GVA share at **30.4%**.
Top fruit by production: **banana**.
AP horticulture: **46.43 lakh acres**, **406.38 lakh MT** (AP Survey 2025-26).

60.s: Which one of the following is the leading fruit in India by production?
60.x: Banana is India's top fruit by production, ahead of mango, apple and grapes.
60.tq: Distinguish production ranking from export prominence.
xs: India's top fruit by production is **banana** — option **(3)** is correct.
Mango, apple and grapes rank below it.
xa: AP sent **32,000 MT** of bananas to the Gulf on **8** refrigerated trains from **Tadipatri**.
Banana is part of the **Rayalaseema** horticulture hub.
Export mango varieties: **Alphonso**, **Kesar**, **Banganapalli** and **Totapuri**.

60.s: Which of the following pairs of mango varieties is associated with Andhra Pradesh’s exports?
60.x: Banganapalli and Totapuri are the mango varieties identified with Andhra Pradesh’s exports.
60.tq: Separate Andhra Pradesh export varieties from mango varieties associated with other regions.
xs: **Banganapalli** and **Totapuri** are the AP export mangoes — option **(1)** is correct.
**Alphonso** and **Kesar** are export varieties too, but not AP's.
xa: AP horticulture covers **46.43 lakh acres**, producing **406.38 lakh MT**.
**Rayalaseema** hub crops: banana, oil palm, cashew, coconut, **Araku coffee**.

60.s: Which of the following crops or products is NOT included among the horticultural activities identified for the development of Rayalaseema as a horticulture hub?
60.x: The identified activities include banana, oil palm, cashew, coconut and Araku coffee. Tea is not included in that list.
60.tq: Find the crop outside the stated regional horticulture cluster.
xs: **Tea** is not in the Rayalaseema hub list — option **(3)** is the answer.
The hub covers **banana**, **oil palm**, **cashew**, **coconut** and **Araku coffee**.
xa: **NABARD 2026-27** AP plan: **₹5,313 crore** for horticulture in Rayalaseema and Prakasam.
AP is **No. 1** in oil palm (**2.27 lakh ha**) and **4th** in coconut.

60.s: Andhra Pradesh holds which position in coconut production among the rankings cited?
60.x: Andhra Pradesh is 4th in coconut production. It is 1st in oil palm (2.27 lakh ha), so do not confuse the two rankings.
60.tq: Distinguish the coconut rank from the State’s first rank in oil palm and fruit production.
xs: AP is **4th in coconut** — option **(4) Fourth** is correct.
⚠ Do not confuse it with **oil palm**, where AP is **No. 1** (**2.27 lakh ha**).
xa: AP is **1st in eggs** but only **7th in milk**.
AP is **5th in meat** and **2nd** largest raw silk producer.

60.s: India is the largest producer of turmeric, and the National Turmeric Board is headquartered at:
60.x: India is the largest producer of turmeric, and the National Turmeric Board is located at Nizamabad.
60.tq: Match the commodity leadership fact with the Board’s location.
xs: The **National Turmeric Board** is at **Nizamabad** — option **(2)** is correct.
India is the **largest producer** of turmeric.
xa: **NDDB** is at **Anand, Gujarat** (set up **1965**).
**MPEDA** is at **Kochi**, under the Ministry of **Commerce**.

60.s: Which statement about horticulture in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Rayalaseema is being developed as an aquaculture hub rather than a Horticulture Hub.
Horticulture covered 45.59 lakh acres and produced 406.38 lakh tonnes exclusively in coastal districts.
Horticulture covered 46.43 lakh hectares and produced 45.59 lakh MT.
Horticulture covered 46.43 lakh acres and produced 406.38 lakh MT; Rayalaseema is being developed as a Horticulture Hub.
60.x: The Survey reported 46.43 lakh acres and 406.38 lakh MT, and identified Rayalaseema for development as a Horticulture Hub.
60.tq: Avoid unit and sector substitution in a multi-part fact.
xs: AP horticulture covered **46.43 lakh acres**, producing **406.38 lakh MT**, with **Rayalaseema** as the Horticulture Hub — option **(4)** is correct.
Options (1)-(3) twist the region, the area unit (acres, not hectares) or the output.
xa: Rayalaseema hub crops: banana, oil palm, cashew, coconut, **Araku coffee**.
**NABARD 2026-27**: **₹5,313 crore** for horticulture in Rayalaseema and Prakasam.
Digital horticulture programme: **"Emircha"** with Digital Green.

60.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the three sub-schemes of the National Livestock Mission?
1. Breed development covering poultry, sheep, goat and piggery
2. Feed and fodder
3. Innovation and extension, including livestock insurance
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
60.x: All three listed components form the sub-schemes of the National Livestock Mission.
60.tq: Test whether all components of a named scheme have been retained.
xs: All three are NLM sub-schemes — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**Breed development** (poultry, sheep, goat, piggery), **Feed and fodder**, and **Innovation and extension** (includes livestock insurance).
xa: NLM has run since **2014-15** and was **revised 2021-22**.
**LHDCP** controls disease through **prophylactic vaccination**.

60.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
(a) Rashtriya Gokul Mission
(b) National Livestock Mission
(c) AHIDF
(d) LHDCP

List-II (Association)
(i) Disease control through prophylactic vaccination
(ii) Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund
(iii) Indigenous bovine breeds
(iv) Livestock productivity, feed and fodder, health and entrepreneurship

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
60.x: Rashtriya Gokul Mission concerns indigenous bovine breeds; NLM covers productivity and related areas; AHIDF is the infrastructure fund; LHDCP uses prophylactic vaccination.
60.tq: Start from the unambiguous acronym pair and complete the matching code.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Rashtriya Gokul Mission** = indigenous bovine breeds; **NLM** = productivity, feed and fodder, health, entrepreneurship.
**AHIDF** = Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund; **LHDCP** = **prophylactic vaccination**.
xa: RGM and NLM date to **2014**; AHIDF to **2020**.
NLM sub-schemes: **Breed development**, **Feed and fodder**, **Innovation and extension**.

60.s:
Consider the following statements about egg production:
1. India ranks second in the world in egg production.
2. Per capita availability of eggs in India is about 106 eggs per year.
3. Tamil Nadu is the leading egg-producing State, followed by Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
60.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: India is 2nd in the world (149.11 billion eggs) with about 106 eggs per head per year. Statement 3 is wrong: Andhra Pradesh leads (18.37%), followed by Tamil Nadu. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 reverse the AP-TN order.
60.tq: AP is 1st in eggs - any statement putting another State ahead of AP is false.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: India is **2nd** in eggs (**149.11 billion**), about **106 per head per year**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Andhra Pradesh (18.37%)** leads, followed by **Tamil Nadu**.
xa: Other top egg States: **Telangana**, **West Bengal**, **Karnataka**.
AP produced **2,548.74 crore eggs** (2023-24) — **1st in eggs**.
⚠ AP = **1st** in eggs but only **7th** in milk.

60.s: The Credit Guarantee Scheme for the Livestock Sector was launched by:
o: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying
60.x: The Credit Guarantee Scheme for the Livestock Sector was launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (APPSC-G2 2025). NABARD, RBI and the Ministry of Finance are the usual distractors and are wrong.
60.tq: Livestock credit guarantee = DAHD, not NABARD/RBI/MoF.
xs: The **Credit Guarantee Scheme for the Livestock Sector** was launched by the **Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-G2 2025).
⚠ Distractors **NABARD**, **RBI** and **MoF** are wrong.
xa: The same department runs **AHIDF** (**2020**) and the **National Livestock Mission**.
**LHDCP** controls disease through **prophylactic vaccination**.

60.s:
Consider the following statements about Operation Flood:
1. It was launched by the National Dairy Development Board, set up in 1965 at Anand, Gujarat.
2. It was based on the Amul cooperative model.
3. It was implemented in four phases between 1970 and 1996.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
60.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NDDB (1965, Anand) launched Operation Flood on the Amul cooperative model. Statement 3 is wrong: it ran in three phases, not four, during 1970-1996. Hence 1 and 2 only; every other option includes statement 3.
60.tq: Operation Flood: NDDB, Amul model, THREE phases, 1970-96.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: **NDDB** (set up **1965** at **Anand, Gujarat**) launched Operation Flood on the **Amul cooperative model**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it ran in **three** phases, not four, during **1970-1996**.
xa: It built a **national milk grid** and made India the world's **largest milk producer**.
**White** Revolution = milk.

60.s: India's present position in global milk production and its approximate share of world output are:
60.x: India is the world's number-one milk producer and accounts for approximately 25 per cent of global milk output.
60.tq: Link the rank with the corresponding global share.
xs: India is **No. 1** in milk with about **25 per cent** of world output — option **(3) First** is correct.
Some notes give the share as **24.76%**.
xa: Per capita availability: **471 g/day**.
Top States: **Uttar Pradesh (15.66%)**, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra.
⚠ Older notes give **190 MT** and **394 g** — stale.

60.s:
Consider the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY):
1. It was launched in 2020 with an outlay of about ₹20,050 crore.
2. It initially ran from FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25 and was extended to FY 2025-26.
3. Training and capacity building under it are handled by MPEDA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
60.x: Statement 1 is correct: PMMSY, the flagship Blue Revolution scheme, began in 2020 with ₹20,050 crore. Statement 2 is correct: it ran 2020-21 to 2024-25 and was extended to 2025-26. Statement 3 is wrong: training and capacity building are handled by the National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB); MPEDA, under the Commerce Ministry, promotes marine exports. Hence 1 and 2 only.
60.tq: PMMSY: 2020, ₹20,050 crore, NFDB trains; MPEDA = exports (Commerce).

60.s: With reference to PMMSY funding, which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Centrally Sponsored component in North-Eastern and Himalayan States — 90:10 Centre-State funding
Centrally Sponsored component in general States — 90:10 Centre-State funding
Central Sector component — 60:40 Centre-State funding for all States
Centrally Sponsored component in Union Territories — 60:40 Centre-State funding
60.x: The Centrally Sponsored component follows a 90:10 Centre-State ratio in North-Eastern and Himalayan States. The general ratio is 60:40, while Union Territories receive 100% central funding.
60.tq: Split the options by funding category and beneficiary region.
xs: The CSS component in **NE/Himalayan** States is funded **90:10** — option **(1)** is correct.
General States are **60:40**, not 90:10; UTs get **100%** central funding, not 60:40.
The **Central Sector** component is **100%** Centre, not 60:40.
xa: CSS covers production, post-harvest infrastructure and regulation.
⚠ **PM-MKSSY** = **Central Sector** sub-scheme.

60.s: Which of the following is covered under the Central Sector component of PMMSY?
o: Production subsidy exclusively for general States
60.x: The Central Sector component includes training, quarantine, harbour modernisation and data systems.
60.tq: Match the activity with the correct scheme component.
xs: PMMSY's **Central Sector** component covers **training and capacity building** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is **100%** Centre-funded: training, quarantine, harbour modernisation, data systems.
Production and regulation fall under the **Centrally Sponsored** component instead.
xa: CSS funding: **60:40** general, **90:10** NE/Himalayan, **100%** UTs.
**NFDB** handles training under PMMSY.

60.s: PM-MKSSY is best described as:
o: A Central Sector sub-scheme under PMMSY for formalising fisheries and supporting fisheries micro-enterprises
A fund exclusively for constructing fishing harbours
A Centrally Sponsored scheme for horticultural exports
A programme for inland river ranching under Namami Gange
60.x: PM-MKSSY, or Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana, is a Central Sector sub-scheme under PMMSY aimed at formalising the fisheries sector and supporting fisheries micro-enterprises.
60.tq: Distinguish a sub-scheme’s purpose from related fisheries programmes.
xs: **PM-MKSSY** is a **Central Sector sub-scheme under PMMSY** for **formalising** fisheries and supporting **micro-enterprises** — option **(1)** is correct.
Fishing harbours fall under **FIDF**; river ranching under **Namami Gange**.
xa: Full name: **Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana**.
All three PYQ statements on it were correct (APPSC-G1 2024).

60.s:
Consider the following statements about the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA):
1. Its headquarters is at Kochi (Cochin).
2. It functions under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
3. It is the apex body for the export of marine products.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
60.x: Statement 1 is correct: MPEDA is headquartered at Kochi. Statement 2 is wrong: MPEDA is under the Ministry of Commerce, not Agriculture. Statement 3 is correct: it is the apex body for marine-product exports. Hence 1 and 3 only; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with 2 include the wrong ministry.
60.tq: MPEDA = exports, so think Commerce ministry; HQ Kochi.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: MPEDA is at **Kochi (Cochin)**.
Statement 2 is wrong: MPEDA is under the **Ministry of Commerce**, not Agriculture.
Statement 3: it is the **apex body** for marine-product exports.
xa: ⚠ **MPEDA** is under **Commerce**, not the Department of Fisheries (APPSC-GS 2019).
Agri exports (2024-25) hit a record **$51.9 billion** = **11.86%** of merchandise exports.

60.s: The Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) is primarily associated with the development of:
60.x: FIDF supports fisheries and aquaculture infrastructure, particularly fishing harbours and landing centres.
60.tq: Identify the infrastructure-specific fund from its functional area.
xs: **FIDF** funds **fishing harbours and landing centres** — option **(4)** is correct.
Its full name is the **Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund**.
xa: **AHIDF** (**2020**) is the animal husbandry equivalent.
PMMSY's Central Sector part includes **harbour modernisation**.

60.s: Which allied agricultural sub-sector has recorded an annual growth rate of about 9.08% since 2014-15?
60.x: Fisheries has been the fastest-growing allied sub-sector, recording growth of about 9.08% annually since 2014-15.
60.tq: Associate the distinctive growth rate with the correct allied sector.
xs: **Fisheries** is the fastest-growing allied sub-sector at **9.08%** a year since **2014-15** — option **(2)** is correct.
ES 2025-26 puts the decadal rate (FY16-FY25) at **8.8%**.
xa: Output rose **103%**: **95.79 lakh t** (2013-14) → about **195 lakh t**.
**Inland fisheries** give over **75%** of output.
In AP, fishing & aquaculture is the largest allied sub-sector, growing **17.69%**.

60.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh’s position in aquaculture and farmed-shrimp production?
o: It is the second-largest producer, with only tiger shrimp being produced.
It is the largest producer of marine fish but not farmed shrimp.
It is the fourth-largest producer, with trout as the main variety.
It is the largest producer, with Vannamei as the predominant farmed shrimp variety.
60.x: Andhra Pradesh is the largest aquaculture and farmed-shrimp producer, with Vannamei being the predominant variety.
60.tq: Separate aquaculture ranking from marine-fish and cold-water categories.
xs: AP is the **largest** aquaculture and farmed-shrimp producer, mostly **Vannamei** — option **(4)** is correct.
It gives about **29-30%** of India's fish output.
xa: AP fish output: **47.28 lakh t** up to Dec 2025 = **72%** of target.
NABARD 2026-27: **₹21,098 crore** to fisheries in AP.
⚠ India is **1st** in milk, but AP's lead is in **aquaculture**.

60.s: What proportion of India’s total fish output is contributed by inland fisheries?
60.x: Inland fisheries contribute more than 75% of India’s total fish output.
60.tq: Use the broad percentage category rather than an artificially precise figure.
xs: **Inland fisheries** give **more than 75%** of total fish output — option **(2)** is correct.
Some notes rank inland differently, but the over-**75%** share is the stated figure.
xa: Fish output rose **103%** to about **195 lakh t**.
River ranching in the **Ganga** by **ICAR-CIFRI** under **Namami Gange**.

60.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
60.x: Karnataka is the leading state in mulberry silk. Jharkhand leads in tasar, while Assam leads in muga and eri silk.
60.tq: Discriminate among closely related state–product pairs.
xs: **Mulberry silk — Karnataka** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Tasar** = **Jharkhand**; **Muga** and **eri** = **Assam**.
xa: India is the **2nd largest silk producer** and the **only country** producing **all five silks**.
AP is the **2nd largest raw silk producer** (**61,394 MT** cocoons, 2024-25).

60.s: The main sericulture belt of Andhra Pradesh is associated primarily with:
o: Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur around Hindupur and Chittoor
60.x: The principal sericulture belt lies in Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur, particularly around Hindupur, and in Chittoor.
60.tq: Identify the precise geographical concentration from a set of nearby districts.
xs: AP's sericulture belt is **Sri Sathya Sai / Anantapur** around **Hindupur**, and **Chittoor** — option **(2)** is correct.
These Rayalaseema districts are named as AP's sericulture belt.
xa: AP is the **2nd largest raw silk producer** (**61,394 MT** cocoons, 2024-25).
**Chittoor** is also AP's top dairy district.
⚠ Mulberry = **Karnataka**; tasar = **Jharkhand**; muga & eri = **Assam**.

60.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its revolution or fibre designation?
60.x: The Sweet Revolution is associated with honey and apiculture. Golden Fibre denotes jute, Silver Fibre denotes cotton, and Blue Revolution denotes fisheries.
60.tq: Separate similar revolution names from fibre designations.
xs: **Sweet Revolution — honey** (apiculture) is correctly matched — option **(2)**.
**Golden Fibre** = **jute**; **Silver Fibre** = **cotton**; **Blue** = **fisheries** (milk is **White**).
xa: The **National Beekeeping and Honey Mission (2020)** runs the Sweet Revolution via the **National Bee Board**.
**Golden Revolution (1991-2003)** = horticulture.

60.s: The National Beekeeping and Honey Mission, launched in 2020 under Atmanirbhar Bharat, implements the Sweet Revolution through the:
60.x: The National Beekeeping and Honey Mission implements the Sweet Revolution through the National Bee Board.
60.tq: Apply the ‘scheme–implementing body’ association test.
xs: The **National Beekeeping and Honey Mission** runs the Sweet Revolution through the **National Bee Board** — option **(4)** is correct.
**NFDB** trains under PMMSY and **NDDB** launched Operation Flood — neither runs the honey mission.
xa: The mission was launched in **2020** under **Atmanirbhar Bharat**.
**Sweet Revolution** = honey (apiculture); **Golden Revolution (1991-2003)** = horticulture.
**NDDB** was set up in **1965** at **Anand, Gujarat**.

60.s: India occupies which position in the production of silk, and what distinction is associated with its silk production?
o: First; it produces only one variety of silk
Second; it is the only country producing all five varieties of silk
Second; it produces only the mulberry variety
Third; it is the only country producing three varieties of silk
60.x: India is the second-largest silk producer and is identified as the only country producing all five varieties of silk.
60.tq: Combine the rank and the associated distinction instead of treating them as separate clues.
xs: India is the **second** largest silk producer and the **only country** producing **all five varieties of silk** — option **(2)** is correct.
The five: **mulberry**, **tropical tasar**, **oak tasar**, **eri**, **muga**.
xa: Mulberry = **Karnataka**; tasar = **Jharkhand**; muga & eri = **Assam**.
AP is the **2nd largest raw silk producer** (**61,394 MT** cocoons, 2024-25).

60.s: Andhra Pradesh's rank among Indian States in raw silk production (2024-25) is:
60.x: AP is the 2nd largest raw silk producer (61,394 MT of cocoons in 2024-25), with its belt around Hindupur (Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur) and Chittoor. India as a whole is also 2nd in the world. First, third and fifth are wrong.
60.tq: AP = 2nd in raw silk; India = 2nd in world silk.
xs: AP is the **2nd largest raw silk producer** — option **(2) Second** is correct.
It produced **61,394 MT** of cocoons in **2024-25**.
xa: AP's sericulture belt: **Sri Sathya Sai / Anantapur** around **Hindupur**, and **Chittoor**.
India too is the **2nd largest silk producer** in the world.
India is the only country producing **all five silks**.

60.s: PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana is an umbrella scheme of which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
60.x: PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana is the umbrella scheme of the Ministry of Food Processing Industries.
60.tq: Apply the ‘which Ministry’ trap by distinguishing neighbouring ministries.
xs: **PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana** is the umbrella scheme of the **Ministry of Food Processing Industries** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is a food-processing scheme, not one of Commerce, Rural Development or Agriculture.
xa: **Mega Food Parks** follow a **cluster approach** linking farms → processing → markets.
**PMFME** works under **One District One Product (ODOP)**.
Processed food export share (2024-25): "around **23%**" (APPSC-GS 2025 key).

60.s: The cluster approach adopted under Mega Food Parks primarily seeks to establish a link between:
60.x: Mega Food Parks use a cluster approach that links farms to processing facilities and then to markets.
60.tq: Identify the complete value-chain sequence in the scheme.
xs: **Mega Food Parks** use a **cluster approach** linking **farms**, **processing** and **markets** — option **(1)** is correct.
The cluster runs from **farms → processing → markets**, not across banks, schools or transport hubs.
xa: **PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana** is the umbrella scheme of the **Ministry of Food Processing Industries**.
**Operation Greens (TOP)**, **2018**, now covers all fruits and vegetables.
**PMFME** formalises **micro** food-processing units under **ODOP**.

60.s: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) is associated with which approach?
60.x: PMFME formalises micro food-processing units under the One District One Product (ODOP) approach.
60.tq: Discriminate between similar one-unit policy slogans.
xs: **PMFME** formalises **micro food-processing units** under **One District One Product (ODOP)** — option **(1)** is correct.
The other "One ..." labels are not linked to PMFME.
xa: **Mega Food Parks** use a **cluster approach**.
**PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana** is the **MoFPI** umbrella scheme.

60.s: For 2024–25, the approximate share of processed food exports used in the relevant General Studies answer key was:
60.x: The APPSC-GS 2025 key used 'around 23%' as the share of processed food exports for 2024-25, so pick the option offered. 11.86% is a different figure: agri exports' share of merchandise exports.
60.tq: Separate two close percentage figures instead of treating them as interchangeable.
xs: The APPSC-GS 2025 key put processed food exports at "around **23%**" for 2024-25 — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: answer with the option offered; **11.86%** is a different figure — agri exports' share of merchandise exports.
xa: Agri exports (2024-25) hit a record **$51.9 billion**.
**MPEDA** (Kochi, under **Commerce**) is the apex body for marine-product exports.

60.s: Which State is the largest producer of fruits in India according to the cited agricultural data?
60.x: Andhra Pradesh leads India in fruit production; it also leads in shrimp, oil palm and eggs. Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka are not first in fruit.
60.tq: Identify the State rank and retain the associated national share.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** leads in fruit — option **(1)** is correct.
AP leads in **shrimp**, **fruit**, **oil palm** and **eggs**.
xa: AP is **1st** in eggs and oil palm, **2nd** in sheep and poultry numbers.
AP horticulture: **46.43 lakh acres**, **406.38 lakh MT**.
**Banana** is India's top fruit by production.

60.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the growth of allied agricultural sectors in India:
1. Livestock recorded growth of 7.1%.
2. Fisheries recorded growth of 8.8%.
3. Fisheries grew at a lower rate than livestock.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
60.x: Livestock growth was 7.1% and fisheries growth was 8.8%. Therefore, fisheries grew faster than livestock, making statement 3 false.
60.tq: Compare the numerical values before accepting the statement on relative growth.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: ES 2025-26 gives **livestock 7.1%** and **fisheries 8.8%**.
Statement 3 is wrong: at **8.8%**, fisheries grew **faster** than livestock.
xa: Fisheries grew **9.08%** a year since **2014-15** — the fastest allied sub-sector.
Livestock grew **12.77% CAGR** in nominal terms (FY15-FY24).

60.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh:
1. Fisheries is the largest and fastest-growing allied sub-sector.
2. Fisheries recorded a growth rate of 17.69%.
3. Fishing and aquaculture is not a major contributor to agricultural GVA in the State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
60.x: Fisheries is the largest and fastest-growing allied sub-sector in Andhra Pradesh and recorded 17.69% growth. Statement 3 is false because fishing and aquaculture is the State’s largest agricultural GVA sub-sector.
60.tq: Find the false reversal in the third statement and verify the precise growth figure.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: fisheries is AP's **largest and fastest-growing** allied sub-sector, at **17.69%**.
Statement 3 is wrong: fishing & aquaculture is AP's **largest agri GVA sub-sector**.
xa: AP gives about **29-30%** of India's fish output, mostly **Vannamei** shrimp.
NABARD 2026-27: **₹21,098 crore** to fisheries in AP.

60.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India and Andhra Pradesh:
1. India ranks first in milk production.
2. Andhra Pradesh ranks seventh among States in milk production.
3. Andhra Pradesh’s principal national lead among the sectors mentioned is in aquaculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
60.x: India ranks first in milk production, while Andhra Pradesh ranks seventh among the States. Andhra Pradesh’s notable lead is in aquaculture; hence all three statements are correct.
60.tq: Combine national and State rankings without reversing the comparison.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statements 1 and 2: India is **1st in milk**, while AP is only **7th** among States.
Statement 3: AP's lead is in **aquaculture**.
xa: AP's milk fell **9.41%**; it was **5th** on 2022-23 figures.
India's milk share is about **25%** of world output; top State **UP (15.66%)**.

61.s:
Arrange the following industrial developments in chronological order:
A. Incorporation of TISCO
B. Establishment of the first successful cotton textile mill in Bombay
C. Establishment of the first jute mill at Rishra
D. Introduction of tariff protection that stimulated the sugar industry
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
61.x: The correct sequence is the cotton mill in 1854, the jute mill in 1855, TISCO in 1907, and tariff protection for sugar in 1932.
61.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then order the intervening milestones.
xs: Correct order: **B, C, A, D** — option **(1)**.
**Cotton mill, Bombay** (**1854**) → **jute mill, Rishra** (**1855**) → **TISCO** (**1907**) → **tariff protection** for **sugar** (**1932**).
xa: Some notes date the Bombay cotton mill to **1853**; it was set up by **Cowasjee Nanabhoy**.
**Indian Cement** came in **1914**.
**1900-1947** saw steel, cement, sugar and paper come up.

61.s: Which of the following correctly describes the early ownership pattern of the Indian jute and cotton mill industries?
o: Cotton mills were foreign-dominated, whereas jute mills were Indian-dominated.
Jute mills were foreign-dominated, whereas cotton mills were Indian-dominated.
61.x: The jute mills were foreign-dominated, while the cotton mills were predominantly Indian-dominated.
61.tq: Test the direction of a comparison rather than recalling the industries separately.
xs: **Jute mills** were **foreign-dominated**; **cotton mills** were **Indian-dominated** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the pattern; options (3) and (4) ignore the contrast.
xa: ⚠ First cotton mill = **Bombay** (**1854**); first jute mill = **Rishra** (**1855**).
**TISCO** was incorporated at **Jamshedpur** in **1907**.

61.s:
The textile companies are arranged below according to their years of establishment. Which sequence is correct from earliest to latest?
A. Raymond
B. Bombay Dyeing
C. Grasim (Gwalior Rayon)
D. Lakshmi Mills
61.x: The correct order is Bombay Dyeing (1879), Lakshmi Mills (1910), Raymond (1925), and Grasim (1947).
61.tq: Arrange named companies by their establishment years.
xs: Correct order: **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)**.
**Bombay Dyeing (1879)** → **Lakshmi Mills (1910)** → **Raymond (1925)** → **Grasim (1947)**.
xa: **Lakshmi Mills** = **Coimbatore**; **Grasim** = **Gwalior Rayon**.
This founding-year sequence was asked in **APPSC-GS 2024**.

61.s: Which of the following was the first textile unit of its kind in the Madras Presidency?
o: Munagala Raja's textile unit at Vijayawada
61.x: Munagala Raja's textile unit at Vijayawada, established in June 1906, was the first of its kind in the Madras Presidency.
61.tq: Link the regional industrial milestone with its founder and location.
xs: **Munagala Raja's textile unit** at **Vijayawada** (**June 1906**) was the first of its kind in **Madras Presidency** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Bombay Dyeing** and **Raymond** were not in Madras Presidency; **Lakshmi Mills** came later, in **1910**.
xa: The first successful cotton mill was in **Bombay** (**1854**).
**Bombay Dyeing** dates to **1879**, **Raymond** to **1925**.

61.s:
Consider the following pairs (phase of industrial growth - approximate growth rate):
1. 1951-65, rapid public-sector-led heavy industrialisation - about 7-8%
2. 1965-80, deceleration and licence-raj stagnation - about 7-8%
3. 1980s, recovery with partial liberalisation - about 7-8%
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
61.x: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct: both 1951-65 and the 1980s recovery saw about 7-8% growth. Pair 2 is wrong: the 1965-80 deceleration saw only about 4%. So '1 only' misses the 1980s recovery, and options with 2 ignore the slowdown.
61.tq: Growth curve: high (1951-65), dip to ~4% (1965-80), back up (1980s).
xs: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Pair 1: **1951-65** public-sector-led growth was about **7-8%**.
Pair 2 is wrong: the **1965-80** deceleration saw only about **4%**.
Pair 3: the **1980s** recovery was also about **7-8%**.
xa: The 1965-80 slowdown came from **wars**, **droughts**, **infrastructure bottlenecks** and **licensing**.
**Dani Rodrik**'s **premature deindustrialisation**: manufacturing peaks at lower income than in early industrialisers.

61.s: The number of industries reserved for the public sector under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, and the number retained under the 1991 policy were, respectively
61.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 reserved 17 industries for the public sector, while the 1991 policy reduced the number to 8.
61.tq: Compare the two policy benchmarks and watch for reversal of the figures.
xs: **IPR 1956** reserved **17** industries for the public sector; the **1991 policy** cut this to **8** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses the two numbers.
xa: The **Second Plan (1956-61)** pushed heavy and basic industries on the **Nehru-Mahalanobis model**.
After 1991, cheap imports shut many **small units**.

61.s: Which of the following was NOT among the principal factors associated with industrial deceleration during 1965–80?
61.x: Wars, droughts, infrastructure bottlenecks and licensing were associated with the 1965–80 deceleration. Complete liberalisation of imports was not a feature of that period.
61.tq: Find the policy condition that conflicts with the licence-raj phase.
xs: **Complete liberalisation of imports** was not a cause of the **1965-80** slowdown — option **(1)** is the answer.
The real causes: **wars**, **droughts**, **infrastructure bottlenecks** and **licensing** (licence-raj stagnation, about **4%**).
xa: Partial liberalisation came only in the **1980s**, with a recovery of about **7-8%**.
Full liberalisation came from **1991**.

61.s: The concept of premature deindustrialisation, associated with Dani Rodrik, means that
o: manufacturing's share peaks at a lower income level than in early industrialising countries
industrial employment rises continuously after reaching high income
services remain smaller than agriculture at every income level
61.x: Premature deindustrialisation occurs when manufacturing's share of output or employment peaks at a lower income level than it did in early industrialisers.
61.tq: Distinguish a lower-income peak from the complete disappearance of manufacturing.
xs: **Premature deindustrialisation** (**Dani Rodrik**): **manufacturing**'s share **peaks** at a **lower income** than in early industrialisers — option **(1)** is correct.
It does not mean manufacturing vanishes or that employment keeps rising.
xa: After 1991, **cheap imports** shut many small units.
**Services**, not industry, gained most GDP share after 1991.

61.s: The Second Five Year Plan, associated with the Mahalanobis model, gave particular emphasis to:
61.x: The Second Plan and the Mahalanobis model stressed the development of basic and heavy industries.
61.tq: Link the planning model with its characteristic industrial emphasis.
xs: The **Second Plan (1956-61)** stressed **heavy and basic industries** on the **Nehru-Mahalanobis model** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **First Plan** had focused on **agriculture**.
xa: **Bhilai**, **Rourkela** and **Durgapur** were set up in the Second Plan.
**IPR 1956** reserved **17** industries for the public sector.

61.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the change in India's sectoral GDP structure after 1991?
o: All three major sectors gained equal shares.
Industry gained the most share relative to services.
Agriculture gained the most share relative to services.
Services gained the most share, while industry's share did not rise significantly relative to services.
61.x: After 1991, the services sector gained the most share in GDP. Industry did not rise significantly in share relative to services.
61.tq: Avoid the reversal trap between industry and services in structural-change questions.
xs: After 1991 **services gained the most** GDP share; industry's share did not rise much relative to services — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ "Industry's share rose significantly compared to services" is **false** (APPSC-GS 2023 key: only II and III correct).
xa: Industry is about **25.3%** of GVA.
Manufacturing's **real** share stays at **17-18%**.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about India's industrial structure since 1991:
1. Post-LPG growth favoured capital- and skill-intensive sectors.
2. Automobiles, specialty chemicals, pharmaceuticals and IT hardware benefited from this pattern.
3. Auto components and pharmaceuticals became part of global value chains.
4. Services lost the greatest share of GDP after 1991.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because services gained the most GDP share after 1991.
61.tq: Use the sectoral-trend statement to eliminate the otherwise correct-looking combination containing a reversed trend.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: post-LPG growth favoured **capital- and skill-intensive** sectors — **automobiles, specialty chemicals, pharma, IT hardware**.
Statement 3: **auto components** and **pharma** joined **Global Value Chains**.
Statement 4 is wrong: **services gained** the most GDP share after 1991.
xa: ES 2025-26: medium- and high-tech manufacturing share is **46.3%**.
About **57 lakh** jobs were added in organised manufacturing (2015-16 to 2024-25).

61.s: Industry accounts for approximately what share of Gross Value Added in India?
61.x: Industry accounts for approximately 25.3 per cent of GVA. The 13–14 per cent figure relates to the public sector's contribution to GDP, while 17–18 per cent refers to manufacturing's real-term share.
61.tq: Separate similar percentages by linking each figure to its correct economic aggregate.
xs: Industry is about **25.3 per cent** of GVA — option **(4)** is correct.
**13-14%** is the public sector's share of GDP; **17-18%** is manufacturing's real share.
xa: Real industry GVA grows at about **7%**.
Industry GVA grew **7.0%** in H1 FY26.

61.s: Why did manufacturing's share of nominal GVA decline despite its real-term share remaining broadly stable?
o: Because the private sector withdrew from manufacturing
Because construction was excluded from GVA
Because manufacturing output ceased to grow after 1991
61.x: The decline in manufacturing's nominal GVA share was attributed to relative price changes. In real terms, manufacturing's share remained broadly steady at 17–18 per cent.
61.tq: Distinguish nominal changes caused by prices from real changes in output.
xs: Manufacturing's **nominal** GVA share fell only because of **relative price** changes — option **(1)** is correct.
Its **real** share stayed steady at **17-18%**, so output did not stop growing.
xa: Manufacturing GVA grew **9.13%** in Q2 FY26.
Industry as a whole is about **25.3%** of GVA.

61.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
61.x: Bhilai Steel Plant was established with Soviet collaboration. Rourkela had West German collaboration, Durgapur had UK collaboration and Bokaro had USSR collaboration.
61.tq: Start from the sure collaboration and identify the swapped foreign partners.
xs: **Bhilai — USSR** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Rourkela** = **West Germany**; **Durgapur** = **UK**; **Bokaro** = USSR.
xa: Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur were set up in the **Second Plan (1956-61)**.
Bhilai is in **Chhattisgarh** (then MP); Bokaro in **Jharkhand**.
**RINL (Vizag Steel)** was also a **USSR** collaboration.

61.s:
Consider the following statements regarding major public-sector steel plants:
1. Rourkela was the first integrated public-sector steel plant.
2. Rourkela had a capacity of one million tonnes.
3. Rourkela is located in Odisha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Rourkela in Odisha was the first integrated public-sector steel plant and had a capacity of one million tonnes.
61.tq: Test all components of a multi-detail industrial description rather than relying on location alone.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Rourkela** (**Odisha**) was the **first integrated PSU steel plant**, with **1 MT** capacity, built with **West Germany**.
xa: ⚠ First PSU steel unit = **Bhadravati**; first integrated PSU steel plant = **Rourkela**.
**Durgapur** (West Bengal) = **UK**; **Bhilai** = **USSR**.

61.s: The first public-sector steel unit in India was
61.x: Visvesvaraya Iron & Steel Works at Bhadravati was the first public-sector steel unit in India.
61.tq: Use the historical-priority clue and distinguish the early unit from the Second Plan plants.
xs: The first public-sector steel unit was **Visvesvaraya Iron & Steel Works, Bhadravati** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Rourkela** was the first **integrated** PSU steel plant; **Bhilai** and **Bokaro** came with the USSR.
xa: Rourkela had **1 MT** capacity, with **West Germany**.
**TISCO** (private) was incorporated in **1907** at Jamshedpur.

61.s: BHEL's first plant at Bhopal was established with the collaboration of
61.x: BHEL's first plant at Bhopal was built with British collaboration, specifically involving AEI.
61.tq: Apply the foreign-collaboration trap by separating BHEL units from steel plants.
xs: BHEL **Bhopal** was built with **Britain** through **AEI** — option **(3)** is correct (MPPSC 2024).
**Haridwar** = USSR; **Tiruchirappalli** and **Hyderabad** = Czechoslovakia.
xa: BHEL makes **boilers, turbines, transformers**.
BHEL is a **Maharatna** CPSE.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about the textile industry:
1. It provides direct employment to about 4.5 crore persons.
2. Its indirect employment exceeds 10 crore persons.
3. It is the largest employer after agriculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: The textile industry directly employs about 4.5 crore persons, indirectly employs over 10 crore persons and is the largest employer after agriculture.
61.tq: Verify each employment figure and the comparative employment claim separately.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Textiles employ **4.5 crore** directly and over **10 crore** indirectly — the **largest employer after agriculture**.
xa: Cotton textiles have three segments: **mill**, **powerloom**, **handloom**.
**Powerlooms** make the bulk of cloth.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about the cotton textile industry:
1. Its three segments are mill, powerloom and handloom.
2. The handloom segment produces the bulk of cloth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: Statement 1 is correct: cotton textiles have mill, powerloom and handloom segments. Statement 2 is wrong: powerlooms, not handlooms, make the bulk of cloth. Hence 1 only; '2 only' and 'Both' accept the wrong segment, and 'Neither' rejects a true statement.
61.tq: Bulk of cloth = POWERloom.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: the segments are **mill**, **powerloom** and **handloom**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **powerlooms**, not handlooms, make the bulk of cloth.
xa: Textiles employ **4.5 crore** directly.
The first successful cotton mill was in **Bombay** (**1854**).

61.s: India was the world's second-largest crude steel producer in 2024, with production of
61.x: India produced 149.4 million tonnes of crude steel in 2024 and ranked second after China, which produced 1,005.1 million tonnes.
61.tq: Distinguish production from capacity and from the leading country's output.
xs: India produced **149.4 million tonnes** of crude steel in **2024**, 2nd largest — option **(4)** is correct.
**1,005.1 MT** is China's output; **200.33 MT** is India's capacity; **93** is the % of coal-based ironmaking.
xa: India depends on **imported coking coal**, its main imported input.
SAIL plants **Bhilai**, **Rourkela**, **Durgapur** date to the **Second Plan**.

61.s: The three public-sector steel plants established during the Second Plan were
61.x: The Second Plan period, 1956–61, saw the establishment of Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur with foreign assistance.
61.tq: Recall the standard three-plant Second Plan group.
xs: The Second Plan (**1956-61**) plants were **Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Bhadravati** was the first PSU steel unit; **Bokaro** and **Visakhapatnam** came later.
xa: Bhilai = **USSR**; Rourkela = **West Germany**; Durgapur = **UK**.
**Bhilai, Rourkela, Bokaro** grew as public-sector townships.

61.s: With reference to Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (Vizag Steel), which one of the following is correct?
o: It was set up with West German collaboration and its foundation stone was laid in 1959
It was set up with Soviet (USSR) collaboration and its foundation stone was laid on 20 January 1971
It was set up with British collaboration and its foundation stone was laid on 12 June 1979
It was the first public-sector steel unit of India
61.x: RINL (Vizag Steel) was set up with USSR collaboration; its foundation stone was laid on 20 January 1971 and the agreement signed on 12 June 1979 (so 12 June 1979 is the agreement date, not the foundation stone). West German collaboration fits Rourkela, and the first public-sector steel unit was Visvesvaraya Iron & Steel Works, Bhadravati.
61.tq: Vizag Steel: USSR; foundation 20 Jan 1971; agreement 12 Jun 1979.
xs: **RINL (Vizag Steel)** was a **Soviet (USSR)** collaboration; foundation stone laid on **20 January 1971** — option **(2)** is correct.
**12 Jun 1979** is the **agreement** date, not the foundation stone.
**West Germany** fits **Rourkela**; the first PSU steel unit was **Bhadravati**.
xa: RINL turned **Vizag** into a heavy-industry + port hub.
**Neyveli** is the regional-balance example for **NLC**.

61.s: The principal cause of capacity under-utilisation in Indian industry identified in the material is
61.x: Deficient basic infrastructure is identified as the main cause of capacity under-utilisation, although weak demand also contributes.
61.tq: Select the primary cause while distinguishing it from a secondary contributing factor.
xs: The main cause of capacity under-utilisation is **deficient basic infrastructure** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2007).
**Weak demand** also adds: the Manufacturing PMI in **Jul 2026** was the lowest since **Aug 2021**.
xa: Other problems: **regional concentration**, **jobless growth**, **import dependence**, **low R&D**.
Infrastructure bottlenecks also drove the **1965-80** slowdown.

61.s: Industrial concentration in India is particularly pronounced in which group of States?
o: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh
61.x: Industrial activity is regionally concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, while eastern and central States lag behind.
61.tq: Identify the established industrial cluster and contrast it with lagging regions.
xs: Industry is concentrated in **Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Eastern and central** States lag.
xa: Highest capital intensity in manufacturing (2017-18): **Madhya Pradesh** (MPPSC 2025).
PSU townships such as **Bhilai, Rourkela, Bokaro** were meant for regional balance.

61.s: As per 2017-18 data, which State had the highest capital intensity in manufacturing?
61.x: Madhya Pradesh had the highest capital intensity in manufacturing in 2017-18 (MPPSC 2025). Maharashtra, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu are where industry is concentrated, which is a different point from capital intensity.
61.tq: Capital intensity top (2017-18) = MP; concentration = Maha, Guj, TN, Kar.
xs: **Madhya Pradesh** had the highest capital intensity in manufacturing (**2017-18**) — option **(3)** is correct (MPPSC 2025).
**Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu** are where industry is **concentrated** — a different point.
xa: Eastern and central States lag in industry.
Contract workers are now **42%** of the factory workforce.

61.s: Which of the following best shows 'jobless growth' in Indian factories during 2011-2023?
o: Direct factory employment rose from 47% to 61% of the workforce
The share of directly employed workers fell from 61% to 47%, and contract workers now make up about 42%
Contract workers fell to about 4% of the factory workforce
Factory employment grew faster than factory output
61.x: Directly employed workers fell from 61% to 47% of the factory workforce (2011-2023), and contract workers now make up about 42%. Option A reverses the trend, C understates contract labour, and D is the opposite of jobless growth.
61.tq: Jobless growth: direct 61% -> 47%; contract 42%.
xs: **Jobless growth**: direct factory employment fell from **61%** to **47%** (**2011-2023**); contract workers are now about **42%** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the trend; (3) understates contract labour.
xa: Regular CPSE employment fell by **30,000** in **2024**, replaced by contract workers.
About **57 lakh** jobs were added in organised manufacturing (2015-16 to 2024-25).

61.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Index of Industrial Production (IIP):
1. It is a composite indicator of short-term changes in the volume of industrial production.
2. It measures changes against a specified base period.
3. It covers mining, manufacturing and electricity.
4. It includes agriculture, services and construction activity as its broad sectors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: The IIP measures short-term changes in industrial production relative to a base period and covers mining, manufacturing and electricity. Agriculture, services and construction activity are outside its coverage.
61.tq: Find the false inclusion statement by distinguishing industrial sectors from excluded activities.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: the IIP tracks short-term changes in the **volume of industrial production** against a **base period**.
Statement 3: it covers **mining, manufacturing, electricity**.
Statement 4 is wrong: **services, agriculture, construction** are **outside** the IIP.
xa: It is compiled monthly by the **NSO (MoSPI)**.
The base moved from **2011-12** to **2022-23** from **1 June 2026**.

61.s: In the 2011-12 series of the IIP, which use-based category had the highest and which had the lowest weight respectively?
61.x: Primary goods had the highest weight at about 34 per cent, while capital goods had the lowest weight at 8.22 per cent in the 2011-12 series.
61.tq: Pair the maximum and minimum values instead of considering either value in isolation.
xs: In the 2011-12 series, **primary goods** weighed most (**34%**) and **capital goods** least (**8.22%**) — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses them.
xa: In **FY 2023**, **capital goods** and **infrastructure/construction goods** indices grew most (BPSC 2024).
New-series weights: **manufacturing 76.1%**, mining **11.1%**, electricity and gas **10.9%**.

61.s: The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is compiled monthly by the:
o: National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
61.x: The IIP is compiled monthly by the National Statistical Office under MoSPI. The NSO replaced the earlier Central Statistical Office in this role.
61.tq: Identify the present compiling agency while distinguishing it from the former agency.
xs: The IIP is compiled monthly by the **National Statistical Office** under **MoSPI** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was formerly done by the **CSO**.
⚠ The **Index of Eight Core Industries** is compiled by **DPIIT** (Office of the Economic Adviser), not the IIP.
xa: The new **Index of Services Production** (base **2024-25**) was first released on **14 July 2026**.

61.s: With effect from 1 June 2026, the base year of the IIP was shifted from:
61.x: The new IIP series shifted the base year from 2011-12 to 2022-23, effective 1 June 2026. Readings before June 2026 use the old base.
61.tq: Test the direction and effective date of a base-year revision.
xs: The IIP base moved from **2011-12 to 2022-23**, effective **1 June 2026** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Any IIP reading from before June 2026 is on the old base.
xa: The new basket has **1,042 products** in **463** item groups (old: **407** items).
The **WPI** base was revised to **2022-23** at the same time.
This was the **10th** revision.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about the new IIP series:
1. Mining, manufacturing and electricity are included.
2. Gas supply, water supply, sewerage and waste management have been added.
3. Minor and rare-earth minerals are included.
4. Renewable electricity is shown separately.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: All four statements are correct features of the new IIP series. It retains the principal industrial sectors and expands coverage to additional utilities, minerals and renewable electricity.
61.tq: Use an all-inclusive option when every listed feature belongs to the same revised series.
xs: All four are features of the new IIP series — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
It keeps **mining, manufacturing, electricity** and adds **gas supply** and **water supply, sewerage and waste management**.
It adds **minor and rare-earth minerals** and shows **renewable electricity** separately.
xa: New weights: manufacturing **76.1%**, mining **11.1%**, electricity and gas **10.9%**, water supply **2.02%**.
Weights rest on each sector's share of **GVA in 2022-23**.

61.s: In the new IIP series, sectoral weights are based on each sector's share of:
o: Gross Domestic Product at current prices in 2022-23
61.x: The weights in the new IIP series are derived from the sectoral shares of Gross Value Added in 2022-23.
61.tq: Distinguish the statistical basis of weights from other macroeconomic aggregates.
xs: New IIP weights are based on each sector's share of **Gross Value Added in 2022-23** — option **(3)** is correct.
GDP, employment and exports are not the weighting basis.
xa: Manufacturing **76.1%**, mining **11.1%**, electricity and gas **10.9%**, water supply **2.02%**.
The base year itself is **2022-23**, effective **1 June 2026**.

61.s: The Index of Services Production, with base year 2024-25, is best described as:
o: A supplementary index of agricultural production
A measure of wholesale price inflation in services
A replacement for the IIP covering only manufacturing
The services counterpart of the IIP
61.x: The Index of Services Production is the services counterpart of the IIP. Its first release was scheduled for 14 July 2026 with a 60-day lag.
61.tq: Discriminate between two similarly named production indices by their sectoral coverage.
xs: The **Index of Services Production** (base **2024-25**) is the **services counterpart of the IIP** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is not about agriculture, prices or manufacturing; services lie **outside** the IIP.
xa: Its first release came on **14 July 2026**, with a **60-day** lag.
The IIP itself was rebased to **2022-23** from **1 June 2026**.
IIP is compiled by the **NSO (MoSPI)**.

61.s: In FY 2023, which use-based groups of the IIP recorded the highest growth?
61.x: In FY 2023, the capital goods and infrastructure/construction goods indices grew the most (BPSC 2024). Primary goods had the highest weight in the 2011-12 series, but they were not the fastest-growing group. The other pairs did not lead.
61.tq: FY23 IIP leaders: capital goods + infra/construction goods.
xs: In **FY 2023**, the **capital goods** and **infrastructure/construction goods** indices grew most — option **(2)** is correct (BPSC 2024).
**Primary goods** had the highest **weight** (**34%**) in the 2011-12 series, but did not grow fastest.
xa: **Capital goods** had the lowest weight (**8.22%**) in that series.
In **Feb 2026**, non-core manufacturing and capital goods outpaced core sectors.

61.s:
With reference to the Index of Core Industries (ICI), consider the following statements:
1. It is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser under the DPIIT.
2. The revised series of the ICI has 2022-23 as its base year.
3. Iron ore was added to the revised series with a weight of 4.905 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: The ICI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT. The revised series uses 2022-23 as the base year and includes iron ore with a weight of 4.905 per cent.
61.tq: Use the institutional-identity and numerical clues together before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the ICI is compiled by the **Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT** (Ministry of Commerce & Industry).
Statements 2 and 3: the revised series has base **2022-23** and adds **iron ore** at **4.905%**.
xa: The revision came in **July 2026**, with effect from **April 2023**.
⚠ IIP = **NSO (MoSPI)**; ICI = **DPIIT**.

61.s: Under the revised 2022-23 series of the Index of Core Industries, which one of the following has the highest weight?
61.x: Electricity carries the highest weight in the revised series, at 30.93 per cent. Refinery products have the second-highest weight at 22.57 per cent.
61.tq: Compare the revised weights rather than relying on the older series.
xs: In the 2022-23 series **electricity** weighs most (**30.93%**) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Refinery products** come second (**22.57**), then **steel** (**17.58**) and **crude oil** (**7.43**).
xa: In the old series, **refinery products** led (**28.04%**), electricity was second (**19.85%**).
**Fertilisers** remain the lowest (**2.73** new; **2.63** old).

61.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the number of industries and the combined IIP weight under the revised 2022-23 series of the Index of Core Industries?
61.x: The revised series contains nine core industries and their combined weight in the IIP is 32.88 per cent. Iron ore was added to the earlier list of eight industries.
61.tq: Split the option into two parts and verify both the count and the percentage.
xs: The revised ICI has **9 industries** with a combined IIP weight of **32.88 per cent** — option **(4)** is correct.
The old series had **8** industries weighing **40.27%**.
xa: **Iron ore** is the ninth, newest core industry (weight **4.905%**).
In **Jun 2026**, the new-series ICI grew **5%**, driven by iron ore (+**43.9%**).

61.s: With reference to the revised methodology of the Index of Core Industries, which of the following statements is correct?
o: It counts coking coal alone and uses net steel output.
It counts raw coal only and uses gross steel output.
It counts imported coal and uses net steel output.
It excludes coal and uses finished steel output only.
61.x: The revised methodology counts only raw coal and uses gross steel output. These methodological changes apply to the revised core industries series.
61.tq: Discriminate between paired technical terms such as raw/gross and coking/net.
xs: The revised method counts **raw coal** only and uses **gross steel** output — option **(2)** is correct.
The other options mix up coking or imported coal with net or finished steel.
