xa: The **joint sector** concept is also sometimes credited to **1973** (notes follow **1970**).
**MRTP Act** was passed in **1969** (in force **1970**).
**FERA** dates from **1973**.

63.s: The R. K. Hazari report of 1967 primarily examined which subject?
63.x: The R. K. Hazari report examined industrial licensing and reported that big business houses had cornered licences.
63.tq: Match the committee or report with its precise policy subject.
xs: The **R.K. Hazari report (1967)** examined **industrial licensing** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It showed that **big houses cornered licences**.
xa: The **Subimal Dutt** Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee (**1967**, report **1969**) led to the **MRTP Act**.
⚠ **Hazari** = report (1967); **Dutt** = Inquiry Committee → MRTP.
Item reservation for SSI also began in **1967**.

63.s: Who chaired the Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee which submitted its report in 1969?
63.x: The Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee was chaired by Subimal Dutt. Its report was submitted in 1969 and contributed to the enactment of the MRTP Act.
63.tq: Separate the report author from the later legislation and its commonly used committee name.
xs: The Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee was chaired by **Subimal Dutt** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) names the committee, not its chairman; **R.K. Hazari** wrote the **1967** report on licensing.
xa: The committee was set up in **1967** and reported in **1969**.
Its report led to the **MRTP Act** (**1969**, in force **1970**).
The **joint sector** came with the **1970** licensing policy after the Dutt Committee.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Industrial Policy Statement of 1977:
1. It was introduced by the Janata Government.
2. It was largely drafted by Morarji Desai.
3. It shifted emphasis from heavy industry towards decentralisation and rural industrialisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 1977 Statement came from the Janata Government. Statement 2 is wrong: it was largely drafted by George Fernandes. Statement 3 is correct: it shifted focus from heavy industry to decentralisation and rural industrialisation. So A misses statement 3, C and D include the wrong statement 2; B is right.
63.tq: 1977 = Janata + George Fernandes + DICs + tiny units.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **1977** Statement came from the **Janata Government**.
Statement 2 wrong: it was largely drafted by **George Fernandes**, not Morarji Desai.
Statement 3 correct: it shifted from heavy industry to **decentralisation** and **rural industrialisation**.
xa: It created **District Industries Centres (DICs)**.
It curbed large houses through **MRTP** and **FERA** → **IBM** and **Coca-Cola** exited India.
It identified **'tiny' units** in the small-scale sector.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Industrial Policy Statement of 1977:
1. It gave emphasis to small-scale industries, including identified ‘tiny’ units.
2. It accorded importance to khadi and handlooms.
3. It treated employment generation as an important objective.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: The 1977 policy emphasised small-scale and tiny units, khadi and handlooms, and employment generation.
63.tq: Use the all-inclusive option after checking each policy emphasis separately.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **1977** Statement emphasised the **small-scale** sector, identifying **'tiny' units**.
It gave importance to **khadi and handlooms** and to **employment**.
xa: **DICs** gave one-roof support in every district.
Drafted largely by **George Fernandes** (Janata Government).
⚠ **1977** = tiny units, DICs, IBM/Coca-Cola exit; **1980** = export orientation, economic federalism.

63.s: District Industries Centres (DICs), created under the Industrial Policy Statement of 1977, were intended primarily to:
o: Provide one-roof support to small and cottage industries in every district
Issue licences exclusively to public-sector undertakings
Regulate the expansion of large industrial houses
63.x: DICs were established in every district to provide integrated support to small and cottage industries under one roof.
63.tq: Ask which institution would perform the described decentralised support function.
xs: **DICs** gave **one-roof support to small and cottage industries in every district** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Support covered **credit**, **raw material**, **machinery** and **marketing**.
Curbing large houses was done via **MRTP** and **FERA**, not DICs.
xa: DICs were created by the **Industrial Policy Statement 1977** (Janata Government).
The 1977 Statement was drafted largely by **George Fernandes**.
The 1977 policy also identified **'tiny' units**.

63.s: The Industrial Policy Statement of 1977 sought to curb large industrial houses mainly through:
63.x: The policy used the MRTP and FERA frameworks to curb the influence of large industrial houses.
63.tq: Match the policy objective with the two relevant regulatory instruments.
xs: The **1977** Statement curbed large houses through **MRTP and FERA** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**DICs** supported small units; **SIPB** is an AP approval board; **DPIIT** dates from **2019**.
xa: As a result, **IBM** and **Coca-Cola** exited India.
The **1980** Statement later relaxed MRTP, letting firms expand up to **25%** without fresh approval.

63.s: Which one of the following statements regarding small-scale industries is correct?
o: The last SSI items were dereserved in 1980.
The 1977 policy defined tiny units and the 1980 policy raised SSI investment limits.
SSI item reservation began only after the New Industrial Policy, 1991.
The 1977 policy abolished tiny units and the 1980 policy ended SSI reservation.
63.x: The 1977 policy introduced the definition of tiny units, while the 1980 policy raised investment limits for small-scale industries. SSI item reservation began in 1967 and the last items were dereserved in 2015.
63.tq: Keep the two closely related policy changes in their correct year-policy combination.
xs: **The 1977 policy defined tiny units and the 1980 policy raised SSI investment limits** — option **(2)** is correct.
SSI item reservation began in **1967** (not after 1991), and the last items were dereserved in **2015** (not 1980).
The 1977 policy promoted tiny units; it did not abolish them.
xa: The **1980** Statement also **regularised excess capacity** and stressed **export orientation**.
It allowed MRTP firms to expand up to **25%** without fresh approval.
SSI reservation **continued after 1991**.

63.s: Which of the following was a major focus of the Industrial Policy Statement of 1980?
o: Reintroduction of import and export restrictions
Exclusive promotion of cottage industries without modernisation
Complete withdrawal of the state from industry
63.x: The 1980 policy emphasised technological upgradation, modernisation and export orientation, with export orientation receiving strong emphasis for the first time.
63.tq: Identify the positive policy objectives while rejecting reversals of the reform direction.
xs: The **1980** Statement focused on **technological upgradation and export orientation** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It gave **export orientation** its **first strong emphasis**.
Removal of import-export restrictions came only with **1991**; the state did not withdraw from industry.
xa: "**Economic federalism**": tax holidays and cheap credit for **backward districts**.
It **regularised excess capacity** and raised SSI investment limits.
It was based on **IPR 1956** with modifications.

63.s: The concept of ‘economic federalism’ in the Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 involved:
o: Centralisation of all industrial approvals in metropolitan cities
Incentives for backward districts, including tax holidays and cheap credit
Uniform industrial incentives for every district
Withdrawal of credit support from backward regions
63.x: Economic federalism meant providing incentives to backward districts, including tax holidays and cheap credit.
63.tq: Translate a policy phrase into its practical regional incentive measures.
xs: **Economic federalism** meant **incentives for backward districts**, including **tax holidays and cheap credit** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It targeted backward districts, not uniform or metro-centred incentives.
xa: Economic federalism is the hallmark of the **Industrial Policy 1980**.
The 1980 policy also stressed **technological upgradation** and **export orientation**.
⚠ **1977** = DICs; **1980** = economic federalism.

63.s: The New Industrial Policy, 1991 was announced during the Prime Ministership of P. V. Narasimha Rao, with Manmohan Singh serving as:
63.x: The 1991 policy was announced by Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao, with Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister.
63.tq: Match the reform policy with the correct political and ministerial combination.
xs: **Manmohan Singh** was **Finance Minister** when the NIP was announced — so option **(3)** is correct.
The PM was **P.V. Narasimha Rao**; the policy came on **24 July 1991**.
xa: It followed the **balance-of-payments crisis**.
It had two parts: large/medium industry + **SSI**.
⚠ IPR 1948 was announced by Industry Minister **Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee**.

63.s: The New Industrial Policy, 1991 was introduced in the context of which major economic difficulty?
63.x: The 1991 policy was introduced after India faced a severe balance-of-payments crisis.
63.tq: Link a major policy response with the economic crisis that triggered it.
xs: **NIP 1991** followed a **balance-of-payments crisis** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Forex reserves were not in excess then; today they are at an all-time high of **USD 702.28 bn** (Nov 2025).
xa: Announced on **24 July 1991** by PM **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and FM **Manmohan Singh**.
GDP growth moved from the "**Hindu rate**" (~**3.5%**) to **7-8%**.
The **National Renewal Fund (1992)** cushioned workers hit by restructuring.

63.s: After the later reduction in the list, industrial licensing under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 continued for how many industries?
63.x: Licensing was initially abolished except for 18 industries and was later reduced to five industries: alcohol, cigarettes and tobacco, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, industrial explosives, and hazardous chemicals.
63.tq: Read the question carefully for the later figure rather than the initial figure.
xs: Compulsory licensing now covers **5** industries — so option **(1)** is correct.
It started at **18** in July 1991; **8** is the 1991 public-sector reservation count.
xa: The 5: **alcohol**, **cigarettes/tobacco**, **electronic aerospace & defence equipment**, **industrial explosives**, **hazardous chemicals**.
⚠ Older notes say **6** — the post-1998-99 list included **drugs & pharmaceuticals**, since delicensed.

63.s: Which of the following was NOT among the five industries retained under compulsory industrial licensing after the later reduction of the list?
63.x: The five retained industries were alcohol, cigarettes/tobacco, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, industrial explosives and hazardous chemicals. Drugs and pharmaceuticals appeared in the older six-item list but were later delicensed.
63.tq: Use the later-versus-older licensing list to detect the excluded item.
xs: **Drugs and pharmaceuticals** are not in today's list of five — so option **(3)** is the answer.
They were in the older **6**-item list but were later delicensed.
**Alcohol**, **hazardous chemicals** and **industrial explosives** are still licensed.
xa: The other two of the five: **cigarettes/tobacco** and **electronic aerospace & defence equipment**.
**Coal** and **petroleum** were delicensed in the **Budget 1998-99**, leaving **6**.
Delicensed units file only an **Industrial Entrepreneur Memorandum (IEM)**.

63.s: An industrial unit delicensed under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 was required to file:
o: A Foreign Investment Promotion Board application
63.x: Delicensed units were required to file only an Industrial Entrepreneur Memorandum (IEM).
63.tq: Match the simplified compliance requirement with delicensing.
xs: Delicensed units had to file only an **Industrial Entrepreneur Memorandum (IEM)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**FIPB** handled foreign-investment approvals; **BIFR** handled sick companies; MRTP asset thresholds were scrapped.
xa: Licensing was abolished except **18 industries**, later reduced to **5**.
**1993**: **automobiles**, **white goods**, **leather** delicensed.
**FIPB** was abolished in **June 2017**.

63.s: Which of the following was a major effect of the 1991 industrial reforms?
o: Replacement of private industry by exclusive state ownership
Continuation of all expansion limits and price controls
Removal of licensing, expansion limits, price controls and import-export restrictions
63.x: The 1991 reforms ended the licence-permit-quota raj by removing industrial licensing, expansion limits, price controls and import-export restrictions.
63.tq: Identify the option that correctly combines the reform measures without reversing their direction.
xs: The 1991 reforms brought **removal of licensing, expansion limits, price controls and import-export restrictions** — option **(4)** is correct.
They **ended** the **licence-permit-quota raj**, which **IPR 1956** had begun.
xa: Public-sector reservation was cut from **17** to **8**.
Automatic approval for up to **51%** foreign equity in **high-priority** industries.
**MRTP** asset threshold scrapped; Act later replaced by the **Competition Act 2002**.

63.s:
Which of the following measures was associated with public-sector reform under the New Industrial Policy, 1991?
1. Grant of autonomy to public-sector undertakings through Memoranda of Understanding.
2. Reference of sick public-sector undertakings to BIFR.
3. Beginning of disinvestment in 1991–92.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: The 1991 policy provided autonomy through MoUs, referred sick PSUs to BIFR and initiated disinvestment in 1991–92.
63.tq: Combine related public-sector reform measures and identify the complete set.
xs: All three are 1991 PSU measures — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Greater **autonomy through MoUs**; chronically sick PSUs referred to **BIFR**.
**Disinvestment** began in **1991-92**, with **20%** stake sales in selected PSUs.
xa: **BIFR** was set up under **SICA 1985**; in **2016** SICA was repealed and BIFR dissolved, cases going to the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code**.
Public-sector reservation was cut from **17** to **8**.
Today only **atomic energy** and **railway operations** remain reserved.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the industries reserved for the public sector:
1. Eight industries were reserved under the New Industrial Policy, 1991.
2. The number was subsequently reduced to three.
3. After May 2001, only atomic energy and railway operations remained reserved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: All three statements are correct. The number declined from eight in 1991 to three and ultimately to two after defence was opened to private participation in May 2001.
63.tq: Track the policy sequence from the initial number to the present position.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **NIP 1991** reserved **8** industries (cut from **17**).
Statement 2: the list was later reduced to **3** (arms & ammunition, atomic energy, rail transport).
Statement 3: after **May 2001** (defence opened), only **atomic energy** and **railway operations** remain.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "**atomic energy and defence**" as today's two is WRONG.
IPR 1956 Schedule A had **17** industries reserved for the State.

63.s: Which one of the following was opened to the private sector in May 2001, thereby reducing the industries reserved for the public sector?
63.x: Defence production, including arms and ammunition, was opened to the private sector in May 2001. Atomic energy and railway operations continued in the reserved category.
63.tq: Distinguish the industry removed from the reserved list from those retained.
xs: **Defence production** (arms & ammunition) was opened to the private sector in **May 2001** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Atomic energy** and **railway operations** are the two still reserved.
**Atomic minerals** were in the **8** of 1991 and dropped from the later list of three in some notes.
xa: Reservation fell **17 → 8 → 3 → 2**.
⚠ Trap: "atomic energy, atomic minerals and rail transport de-reserved in **1993**" is WRONG — those were the ones kept.
Under **IPR 1948**, arms & ammunition, atomic energy and railways were an exclusive Central monopoly.

63.s: With reference to the institutional changes concerning BIFR, which of the following is correct?
o: BIFR was converted into a department of the WTO in 2016
SICA was repealed and BIFR was dissolved in 2016, with cases moving under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code
SICA and BIFR were strengthened and retained without change after 2016
BIFR was dissolved in 1991 and replaced by SICA in 2016
63.x: SICA was repealed and BIFR was dissolved in 2016; pending cases moved under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
63.tq: Use the chronology and distinguish repeal and dissolution from continuation.
xs: In **2016**, **SICA was repealed and BIFR dissolved**, with cases moving to the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code** — so option **(2)** is correct.
BIFR was set up under **SICA 1985**, so it could not be "replaced by SICA in 2016".
xa: BIFR handled chronically sick PSUs referred for **revival or closure** after **1991**.
Enactment timeline: **IDR Act 1951**, **MRTP 1969**, **FERA 1973**, **SICA 1985**.
The **MRTP Act** was replaced by the **Competition Act 2002**.

63.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correctly matched?
63.x: Defence equipment, atomic energy and railway transport formed the public-sector-only list, so B is the wrong pair. Drugs and pharmaceuticals were never reserved for the public sector; they appeared only in the older six-industry compulsory-licensing list and were later delicensed.
63.tq: Separate two nearby lists by identifying the item belonging to licensing rather than public-sector reservation.
xs: **Pharmaceuticals — public-sector-only list** is wrongly matched — so option **(2)** is the answer.
The NCERT public-sector-only list: **defence equipment**, **atomic energy**, **railway transport**.
**Drugs & pharmaceuticals** were only in the older **6**-industry compulsory-licensing list, since delicensed.
xa: Today only **atomic energy** and **railway operations** are reserved.
Licensed industries now (**5**): alcohol, cigarettes/tobacco, electronic aerospace & defence equipment, industrial explosives, hazardous chemicals.
**Arms & ammunition** were opened to private players in **May 2001**.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the MRTP framework under the New Industrial Policy, 1991:
1. The asset threshold for MRTP firms was scrapped.
2. MRTP firms continued to need prior approval for expansion and mergers.
3. The MRTP Act was later replaced by the Competition Act, 2002.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x: Statement 1 is correct: the asset threshold for MRTP firms was scrapped. Statement 2 is wrong: scrapping it removed the need for prior approval for expansion and mergers. Statement 3 is correct: the MRTP Act was replaced by the Competition Act, 2002. So A misses statement 3, C and D include the false statement 2; B is right.
63.tq: 1991 = MRTP threshold gone, no pre-approval; MRTP -> Competition Act 2002.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **asset threshold** for MRTP firms was **scrapped**.
Statement 2 wrong: there was **no prior approval** needed for expansion/mergers after that.
Statement 3 correct: MRTP was replaced by the **Competition Act 2002**.
xa: **MRTP Act**: **1969** (in force **1970**), after the **Subimal Dutt** committee.
The **1980** Statement had let MRTP firms expand up to **25%** without fresh approval.
M&A was freed from MRTP pre-approval after 1991.

63.s: Under the New Industrial Policy, 1991, equity participation in small-scale industry units by other industrial undertakings (foreign or domestic) was permitted up to:
63.x: Equity participation in small-scale industry units by other industrial undertakings, foreign or domestic, was permitted up to 24%.
63.tq: Separate the small-scale industry ceiling from the 51% high-priority-industry ceiling.
xs: Other undertakings could hold up to **24%** equity in SSI units — so option **(2)** is correct.
**51%** was the automatic foreign-equity limit for **high-priority** industries.
xa: ⚠ 1991 = **51%** automatic foreign equity (priority list); SSI = **24%**; now **100%** automatic in most sectors.
SSI reservation continued after **1991**; last items dereserved in **2015**.
The 1991 policy had two parts: large/medium industry + **SSI**.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the mandatory convertibility clause under the 1991 industrial policy framework:
1. It related to financial institutions converting term loans into equity.
2. According to the stated provision, it applied only to term loans of less than 10 years.
3. It applied exclusively to foreign equity investments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: The mandatory convertibility clause concerned financial institutions converting term loans into equity and, as specified, applied only to term loans of less than 10 years. It was not exclusively a foreign-equity provision.
63.tq: Separate the nature and duration of a financial clause from an unrelated FDI provision.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the clause concerned **FIs/lenders converting term loans to equity**; it was relaxed.
Statement 2: per the key, it applies only to term loans of **less than 10 years** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
Statement 3 wrong: it was a lending clause, not a foreign-equity provision.
xa: **FIPB** was created to speed foreign-investment approvals.
**National Renewal Fund (1992)** was the workers' safety net.
⚠ Learn the key's wording: "term loans of **less than 10 years**".

63.s: Automatic approval up to 51 per cent foreign equity under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 initially applied to which category?
o: High-priority, high-investment and high-technology industries on the specified list
63.x: Automatic approval up to 51 per cent foreign equity applied to a specified list of high-priority, high-investment and high-technology industries. It was not available to all industries without restriction.
63.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘all’ and identify the specified sectoral category.
xs: Automatic approval up to **51%** foreign equity applied to **high-priority, high-investment and high-technology industries** on a list — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: it did **not** apply to all industries (APPSC-G1 **2012**).
Examples: **capital goods**, **entertainment electronics**, **food processing**.
xa: It also applied to **export trading companies**.
**Foreign technology agreements** also got automatic approval in high-priority industries.
Now: up to **100%** automatic-route FDI in most sectors, **negative-list** approach.

63.s:
Which of the following was permitted under the foreign investment and technology provisions of the New Industrial Policy, 1991?
1. Automatic approval for foreign technology agreements in high-priority industries
2. Use of foreign brand names and trademarks
3. Establishment of the Foreign Investment Promotion Board to speed approvals
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: All three measures formed part of the liberalised foreign investment and technology framework associated with the 1991 policy.
63.tq: Test several related liberalisation measures together and use the complete combination only when all are supported.
xs: All three were permitted — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Automatic approval for **foreign technology agreements** in high-priority industries.
**Foreign brand names/trademarks** were permitted, and **FIPB** was set up to speed approvals.
xa: Automatic approval for up to **51%** foreign equity in high-priority industries.
FIPB was abolished in **June 2017**.
Gross inward equity FDI (2022-23 to 2025-26) = **$317.80 bn**; repatriation **$178.9 bn** → net FDI falling.

63.s: Which one of the following statements about the later foreign investment approval framework is correct?
o: FIPB was abolished in June 2017 and approvals are processed through the FIF portal.
FIPB continues to be the sole approval authority for all foreign investment.
The negative-list approach was replaced by a complete prohibition on foreign equity.
63.x: The Foreign Investment Promotion Board was abolished in June 2017, and approvals were shifted to the FIF portal. FDI up to 100 per cent under the automatic route is permitted in most sectors subject to the applicable negative list.
63.tq: Identify the institutional change while rejecting absolute statements about FDI.
xs: **FIPB was abolished in June 2017**, with approvals through the **FIF portal** — option **(1)** is correct.
Automatic-route FDI was not abolished: up to **100%** is allowed in most sectors under a **negative-list** approach.
xa: FIF portal integrated with the **National Single Window System** since **Aug 2022**.
FIPB was created under **NIP 1991**.
**DPIIT** handles **FDI policy**.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the regional impact of the post-1991 industrial policy:
1. Investment became concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
2. The policy eliminated regional disparities in industrial investment.
3. Regional imbalance was identified as a criticism of the policy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: Investment became concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, making regional imbalance a criticism. The policy did not eliminate regional disparities.
63.tq: Find the reversed claim in the statement that says the policy eliminated disparities.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: investment stuck in **Maharashtra**, **Gujarat**, **TN** and **Karnataka**.
Statement 3: **regional imbalance** is a listed criticism.
Statement 2 wrong: the policy did not eliminate regional disparities.
xa: Other criticisms: **jobless growth**, **premature deindustrialisation** of small units, **import dependence**, **environmental** damage.
Correctives now: **PLI** and the **National Manufacturing Mission**.
The **1980** policy had used "**economic federalism**" for backward districts.

63.s: Which one of the following was NOT a criticism of the 1991 industrial policy?
63.x: Increase in consumer choice was an achievement associated with the post-1991 reforms, not a criticism. The other three were criticisms.
63.tq: Separate achievements from criticisms by locating the positive outcome.
xs: **Increase in consumer choice** was an achievement, not a criticism — so option **(3)** is the answer.
Criticisms: **regional concentration**, capital-intensive **jobless growth**, **premature deindustrialisation**.
xa: ⚠ Achievements (not criticisms): **higher growth**, **FDI + forex surge**, **consumer choice**, **global Indian MNCs**.
Growth rose from the "**Hindu rate**" (~**3.5%**) to **7-8%**.
Other criticism: **environmental degradation**.

63.s:
Assertion (A): Mergers and acquisitions became easier after the 1991 reforms.
Reason (R): Prior approval under the MRTP framework for mergers and acquisitions was removed.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
63.x: Both statements are true, and removal of MRTP pre-approval directly made mergers and acquisitions easier.
63.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the liberalisation of mergers and acquisitions.
xs: **Both A and R are true** and R is the **correct explanation** of A — option **(1)** is correct.
After 1991, the **MRTP asset threshold** was scrapped, so **no prior approval** was needed for expansion/mergers.
That is why **M&A** became easier.
xa: The **MRTP Act** was replaced by the **Competition Act 2002**.
The MRTP Act dates from **1969** (in force **1970**).
The **1977** Statement had used MRTP and FERA to curb large houses.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding MSMEs after 1991:
1. Removal of protection exposed small units to import competition.
2. Import competition adversely affected many small units.
3. SSI reservation continued after 1991.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: Removal of protection and import competition hurt small units, while reservation for SSI continued after 1991. All three statements are correct.
63.tq: Combine the adverse impact with the institutional continuity that remained after reform.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Removal of protection** exposed small units to **import competition**, which hurt many.
**SSI reservation continued after 1991**; last items dereserved in **2015**.
xa: Premature deindustrialisation: cheap imports from **China** closed many units.
Under 1991, others could hold up to **24%** equity in SSI units.
SSI item reservation began in **1967**.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding DPIIT:
1. DIPP was renamed DPIIT in 2019.
2. Internal trade and traders' welfare were added to its responsibilities on renaming.
3. Integrated development of logistics was allotted to it in 2019 along with the renaming.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x: Statement 1 is correct: DIPP became DPIIT in 2019. Statement 2 is correct: internal trade, traders' welfare and Startups were added. Statement 3 is wrong: logistics was allotted in November 2021, not 2019. So A misses statement 2, C and D include the wrong statement 3; B is right.
63.tq: DPIIT 2019; logistics mandate Nov 2021 - two different dates.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: DIPP was renamed **DPIIT** in **2019**.
Statement 2: **internal trade**, **traders' welfare** and **Startups** were added.
Statement 3 wrong: **logistics** was allotted in **Nov 2021**, not 2019.
xa: DPIIT mandate: **Make in India**, **PLI**, **PM GatiShakti NMP**, industrial corridors, **FDI policy**, EoDB.
It also handles **IPR** — patents, trademarks, designs, GIs.
**DIPP** itself was created in **1995**.

63.s:
Which of the following is included in the mandate of DPIIT?
1. Promotion of Startups
2. Formulation of FDI policy
3. Intellectual property rights relating to patents, trademarks, designs and geographical indications
4. Promotion of industrial corridors
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: DPIIT’s mandate includes Startups, FDI policy, industrial corridors and IPR matters relating to patents, trademarks, designs and geographical indications, along with Make in India, PLI, PM GatiShakti NMP and ease of doing business.
63.tq: Check whether each listed function belongs to the broad industrial-promotion mandate.
xs: All four are in DPIIT's mandate — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Mandate: **Startups**, **FDI policy**, **IPR** (patents, trademarks, designs, GIs) and **industrial corridors**.
xa: It also covers **Make in India**, **PLI**, **PM GatiShakti NMP** and **EoDB**.
Logistics was added in **Nov 2021**.
DIPP became **DPIIT** in **2019**.

63.s: The Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (DIPP) was created as a separate department in:
63.x: DIPP was created as a separate department in 1995. 1961 is when the Department of Industry was set up, 1967 is when it was renamed the Department of Industrial Development, and 2019 is when DIPP was renamed DPIIT.
63.tq: 1961 Dept of Industry -> 1995 DIPP -> 2019 DPIIT.
xs: **DIPP** was created as a separate department in **1995** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2019**).
**1961**: Department of Industry; **1967**: renamed Department of Industrial Development; **2019**: DIPP renamed **DPIIT**.
xa: **2000**: Department of Industrial Development merged with DIPP.
**Nov 2021**: logistics mandate given to DPIIT.
DPIIT stands for **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade**.

63.s: Which of the following is NOT a target of Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0?
63.x: The targets include ₹30 lakh crore investment, USD 10 billion FDI and five lakh manufacturing jobs; USD 100 billion FDI is not specified.
63.tq: Spot the altered magnitude in a set of policy targets.
xs: **USD 100 billion FDI** is not a target — so option **(3)** is the answer; the FDI target is **USD 10 bn**.
Targets: **₹30 lakh crore** investment, **USD 10 bn FDI**, **5 lakh** manufacturing jobs.
xa: Exports to rise from **USD 20 → 40 bn**.
**175+ industrial parks**.
CII Partnership Summit, Visakhapatnam (**14-15 Nov 2025**): **₹2,80,384 crore** committed.

63.s: Which authority chairs the State Investment Promotion Board (SIPB) in Andhra Pradesh?
63.x: The SIPB is chaired by the Chief Minister, while the SIPC is associated with the Chief Secretary.
63.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish the two approval bodies.
xs: The **SIPB** is chaired by the **Chief Minister** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **SIPC** is chaired by the **Chief Secretary**.
xa: ⚠ **SIPB** = CM; **SIPC** = Chief Secretary.
Investment bands: **Large** ₹500-1,000 cr, **Mega** ₹1,000-5,000 cr, **Ultra Mega** >₹5,000 cr.
AP Industrial Development Policy 4.0: **G.O. Ms. No. 68**, **26 Oct 2024**.

63.s:
The MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 includes which of the following provisions?
1. ‘One Family One Entrepreneur’ by 2030
2. 175 MSME parks
3. Capital subsidy of 25%, rising to 45% for special categories
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: All three provisions form part of the MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 for 2024-29.
63.tq: Verify the policy slogan, numerical target and differentiated subsidy before choosing the combined code.
xs: All three are provisions of the **MSME & Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0** — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
"**One Family One Entrepreneur**" by **2030**; **175 MSME parks**.
**Capital subsidy 25%**, rising to **45%** for special categories.
xa: The policy covers **2024-29**.
The rest of the 4.0 suite: **Food Processing**, **Private Parks**, **EV 4.0**; **Aerospace & Defence**, **Space 4.0** (**2025-30**).
AP Industrial Policy 4.0 targets **175+ industrial parks**.

63.s: The target for industrial parks and exports under Industrial Development Policy (4.0) 2024-29 is:
o: 200 industrial parks and increase exports from US$10 billion to US$30 billion
40+ industrial parks and increase exports from US$20 billion to US$175 billion
175+ industrial parks and increase exports from US$20 billion to US$40 billion
175+ industrial parks and increase exports from US$40 billion to US$20 billion
63.x: The policy targets more than 175 industrial parks and an increase in exports from US$20 billion to US$40 billion.
63.tq: Pair the infrastructure target with the correct export base and destination figures.
xs: Targets: **175+ industrial parks** and exports from **USD 20 bn to USD 40 bn** — option **(3)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses the export figures.
xa: Other targets: **₹30 lakh crore** investment, **USD 10 bn FDI**, **5 lakh** manufacturing jobs.
Policy issued as **G.O. Ms. No. 68**, **26 Oct 2024**.
⚠ The MSME Policy 4.0 separately plans **175 MSME parks**.

63.s: Under Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29), which of the following is classified as a 'propelling' sector rather than a 'sustenance' sector?
63.x: Propelling sectors are semiconductors and electronics, EVs, aerospace-defence, blue economy and green energy. Automobiles, pharmaceuticals and textiles (with chemicals) are sustenance sectors.
63.tq: Sustenance = old base (auto, pharma, chemicals, textiles); propelling = new tech.
xs: **Semiconductors and electronics** is a **propelling** sector — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Auto**, **pharma**, **chemicals** and **textiles** are **sustenance** sectors.
xa: Other propelling sectors: **EVs**, **aerospace-defence**, **blue economy**, **green energy**.
Policy period **2024-29**; valid **5 years**.
Approvals: **SIPB** (CM), **SIPC** (Chief Secretary).

63.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Industrial Policy Resolution, 1980 — District Industries Centres
Industrial Policy Statement, 1973 — Joint sector concept
Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 — District Industries Centres
63.x: The Industrial Policy Statement, 1973 is associated with the joint sector concept and the core sector list. District Industries Centres were associated with the 1977 policy, while economic federalism was linked with the 1980 policy.
63.tq: Use policy-label association and reject swapped years.
xs: **Industrial Policy Statement, 1973 — Joint sector concept** is the keyed match — option **(3)**; the table credits 1973 with the joint sector and the **core sector** list.
**Economic federalism** belongs to **1980**, not 1977; **DICs** belong to **1977**, not 1980 or 1956.
xa: ⚠ The notes elsewhere follow the **Industrial Policy of 1970** for the joint sector; both **1970** and **1973** are cited.
⚠ **1948** = mixed economy; **1956** = Licence Raj; **1977** = DICs; **1980** = economic federalism.
The **1973** Statement also tightened **MRTP**.

63.s: The beginning of the ‘licence-permit-quota raj’ in India is generally associated with which policy resolution?
63.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 is associated with the beginning of the licence-permit-quota raj.
63.tq: Identify the policy linked with the historical label rather than the later reform policy.
xs: The **licence-permit-quota raj** began with the **Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2019**).
**NIP 1991** ended it; **IPR 1948** laid the mixed economy.
xa: Licensing rested on the **IDR Act, 1951**.
IPR 1956 is also the "**Economic Constitution of India**" and "**Bible of State Capitalism**".
**R.K. Hazari (1967)** showed big houses cornered licences.

63.s:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order:
A. Sick Industrial Companies Act
B. MRTP Act
C. Industries (Development and Regulation) Act
D. FERA
63.x: The correct order is Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951; MRTP Act, 1969; FERA, 1973; and Sick Industrial Companies Act, 1985.
63.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest enactments, then place the middle years.
xs: The order is **C, B, D, A** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: MRTP came into force in **1970**; replaced by the **Competition Act 2002**.
**FERA** was replaced by **FEMA 1999**.
SICA was repealed in **2016** and BIFR dissolved.

63.s: Which industrial policy formed the basis of the Second Five-Year Plan?
63.x: The IPR 1956, built on the Mahalanobis model of heavy and basic industries, formed the basis of the Second Plan. IPR 1948 came before the First Plan; the 1977 Statement stressed small and cottage industries and DICs; the 1980 Statement stressed economic federalism and exports.
63.tq: Second Plan = IPR 1956 = Mahalanobis.
xs: The **Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956** formed the basis of the **Second Five-Year Plan** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2024**).
It followed the **Mahalanobis model** of heavy and basic industries.
**1977** stressed DICs and small units; **1980** stressed economic federalism and exports.
xa: IPR 1956 was announced on **30 April 1956**.
Goal: "**Socialist pattern of society**" (Avadi, **1955**).
IPR 1948 was the **first** industrial policy (**6 April 1948**).

63.s: The post-1991 concern that growth was capital-intensive and regionally concentrated is sought to be addressed in the current policy context through:
o: PLI and the National Manufacturing Mission
A return to universal industrial licensing
A ban on foreign direct investment
63.x: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes and the National Manufacturing Mission are identified as corrective measures for these concerns.
63.tq: Apply the stated policy response to the identified structural criticism.
xs: Capital-intensive, regionally concentrated growth is being corrected through **PLI and the National Manufacturing Mission** — option **(1)** is correct.
A return to licensing or an FDI ban would reverse the 1991 reforms.
xa: Post-1991 criticisms: **jobless growth**, **regional imbalance**, **import dependence**.
Licence raj bred **rent-seeking**, **entry barriers**, **lack of scale**.
**PLI** is part of the **DPIIT** mandate.

63.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 is significant because it:
o: Established the public-sector-led, licence-based industrial model that continued until 1991
Introduced complete deregulation of all industries
Ended the role of the public sector in basic industries
Restricted industrial development entirely to foreign companies
63.x: The 1956 Resolution shaped a public-sector-led and licence-based industrial model that continued until the 1991 reforms.
63.tq: Identify the defining institutional feature associated with the 1956 Resolution.
xs: **IPR 1956** set up the **public-sector-led, licence-based** model that lasted **until 1991** — option **(1)** is correct.
It expanded, not ended, the public sector; it did not deregulate industry.
xa: Schedule A reserved **17** industries for the State; Schedule B (**12**) progressively State-owned.
It began the **Licence-Permit Raj**.
It was the basis of the **Second Five Year Plan**.

63.s: Which of the following combinations correctly describes the criticism of the licence raj?
o: Removal of all regulatory barriers and complete competition
Automatic entry, low compliance costs and excess scale
Rent-seeking, entry barriers and lack of scale
63.x: The licence raj was criticised for encouraging rent-seeking, creating entry barriers and preventing firms from achieving adequate scale.
63.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of linked criticisms.
xs: The licence raj bred **rent-seeking, entry barriers and lack of scale** — option **(4)** is correct.
It did the opposite of free entry and low compliance.
xa: It began with **IPR 1956** and ended with **NIP 1991**.
**R.K. Hazari report (1967)**: big houses cornered licences.
After 1991, the government's role shifted from **regulator → facilitator**.

63.s: A major significance of the post-1991 reforms was the shift in the role of government from:
63.x: The reforms shifted the government’s role from direct regulation towards facilitation, forming the basis for today’s FDI framework and competition law.
63.tq: Watch for the reversed comparison in the two roles of government.
xs: Post-1991, the government's role shifted from **regulator to facilitator** — option **(1)** is correct.
This shift is the base of today's **FDI** and **competition law**.
xa: **IPR 1956** had shaped the public-sector-led, licence-based model until **1991**.
The **Competition Act 2002** replaced the MRTP Act.
Now up to **100%** automatic-route FDI in most sectors.

63.s: Which Industrial Policy Resolution introduced the Joint Sector concept?
o: First Industrial Policy of independent India, 1948
63.x: The 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution brought in the idea of a joint sector, with public and private ownership together. The 1948 policy set up the mixed economy.
63.tq: Discriminate the 1948 and 1956 policies.
n: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 introduced the Joint Sector concept. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]

63.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. The LPG model consists of Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation.
II. Globalisation involves the reduction of import duties on capital goods.
III. Liberalisation reduces restrictions.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: All three are correct: LPG means liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation. Globalisation included cutting import duty on capital goods, and liberalisation reduces restrictions.
63.tq: Recall the LPG model.
n: Liberalisation reduces restrictions. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
The LPG model consists of Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Globalisation involves the reduction of import duties on capital goods. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]

63.s: The New Industrial Policy announced in 1991 served as the primary starting anchor of:
63.x: The New Industrial Policy of 24 July 1991 was the starting point of liberalisation. It ended licensing for most industries.
63.tq: Recall the 1991 starting point.
n: The New Industrial Policy was the primary starting anchor of Liberalisation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]

63.s:
Assertion (A): Liberalisation instruments boost domestic manufacturing competitiveness.
Reason (R): They lower the cost of technology and capital equipment.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
63.x: Both are true: liberalisation tools such as lower import duties make domestic manufacturing more competitive because they cut the cost of technology and capital equipment. R explains A.
63.tq: Ask whether lower costs explain competitiveness.
n: Liberalisation instruments lower the cost of technology. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Liberalisation instruments lower the cost of capital equipment. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Lower technology and capital-equipment costs boost domestic manufacturing competitiveness. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]

63.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) 1951
(b) 1956
(c) 1991
(d) 2000

List-II
(i) New Industrial Policy with massive de-licensing and deregulation
(ii) SEZ Policy announced under the Globalisation framework
(iii) Industrial Policy Resolution with public and joint sector dominance
(iv) IDR Act establishing the licensing framework
63.x: 1951 is the IDR Act (licensing), 1956 the Industrial Policy Resolution (public sector lead), 1991 the New Industrial Policy (de-licensing), and 2000 the SEZ Policy. The answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
63.tq: Arrange the policies in time order.
n: The Industrial Development and Regulation Act was enacted in 1951. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
The Industrial Development and Regulation Act established the licensing framework. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
The Industrial Policy Resolution was adopted in 1956. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
The 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution established public-sector dominance. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
The 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution established joint-sector dominance. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
The New Industrial Policy was introduced in 1991. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
The 1991 New Industrial Policy brought massive de-licensing. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
The 1991 New Industrial Policy brought deregulation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
The Special Economic Zone Policy was announced on 1 April 2000. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
The Special Economic Zone Policy was announced under the Globalisation framework. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Industrial de-licensing is an instrument of Liberalisation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]

63.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Special Economic Zone Policy was announced on April 1st, 2000.
The SEZ Policy aimed to attract foreign investment.
The SEZ Policy was announced on July 24th, 1991.
One objective of the SEZ Policy was to promote exports.
63.x: Option C is incorrect: the SEZ Policy was announced on 1 April 2000. 24 July 1991 is the New Industrial Policy.
63.tq: Match each policy to its date.
n: The Special Economic Zone Policy was announced on April 1, 2000. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
The objective of the Special Economic Zone Policy was to promote exports. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
The objective of the Special Economic Zone Policy was to attract foreign investment. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
The New Industrial Policy was introduced on July 24, 1991. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
The objective of the Special Economic Zone Policy includes export promotion. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
The objective of the Special Economic Zone Policy includes foreign direct investment. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]

63.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution was introduced in which year?
63.x: The first Industrial Policy Resolution came in 1948. 1956 is the second, and 1991 the New Industrial Policy.
63.tq: Arrange the policies in time order.
n: The Industrial Policy Resolution was introduced in 1948. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the original SICA, 1985 definition of a sick industrial company:
1. Accumulated losses had to equal or exceed net worth at the end of a financial year.
2. Cash losses in that financial year and the preceding financial year were relevant.
3. The company had to have been registered for at least seven years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: The original definition included all three conditions: at least seven years of registration, accumulated losses equal to or exceeding net worth, and cash losses in the relevant and preceding years.
64.tq: Combine the threshold, loss and cash-loss conditions before selecting the coded option.
xs: All three conditions were in the original SICA test — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **accumulated losses equal or exceed net worth** at the end of a financial year.
Statement 2: **cash losses** in that year and the **preceding year**.
Statement 3: registered for **at least 7 years**.
xa: The **1993 amendment** cut the age to **5 years** and dropped the cash-loss test.
⚠ SICA: **7 years** (original) → **5 years** (1993).
**RBI** test for micro/small units: NPA **> 3 months** or net worth eroded **50%**.

64.s: Which change was introduced by the 1993 amendment to the SICA definition of a sick company?
o: The registration requirement was increased to ten years and cash losses were retained.
The registration requirement was reduced to three years and net worth was excluded.
The registration requirement was abolished and accumulated losses were ignored.
The registration requirement was reduced to five years and the cash-loss test was dropped.
64.x: The 1993 amendment reduced the minimum registration period from seven to five years and dropped the cash-loss test.
64.tq: Compare the original and amended definitions by isolating both changed elements.
xs: The **1993 amendment** cut the registration requirement to **five years** and **dropped the cash-loss test** — option **(4)** is correct.
The original **SICA 1985** test needed **7 years** of registration.
xa: The net-worth test (accumulated losses ≥ net worth) stayed.
Older notes give only the **7-year** version.
**BIFR** under SICA was set up in **January 1987**.

64.s:
With reference to the RBI approach to sickness in micro and small units, consider the following statements:
1. A unit is sick if any borrowal account stays NPA for more than 3 months.
2. A unit is sick if its net worth is eroded by 25 per cent through accumulated losses in the previous year.
3. The 2016 Framework for Revival and Rehabilitation of MSMEs stresses early identification of incipient stress through SMA-0/1/2 categories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x: Statement 1 is correct: an NPA for more than 3 months marks sickness. Statement 2 is wrong: the erosion threshold is 50 per cent, not 25. Statement 3 is correct: the 2016 framework uses SMA-0/1/2 for early identification and Committees for Stressed MSMEs. So A misses statement 3, C and D include the wrong statement 2; B is right.
64.tq: RBI sick MSE: NPA > 3 months or 50% net-worth erosion.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: a borrowal account **NPA for more than 3 months** marks sickness.
Statement 2 wrong: the erosion threshold is **50%**, not 25%.
Statement 3 correct: the **2016 Framework** uses **SMA-0/1/2** for early stress identification.
xa: The 2016 Framework also set up **Committees for Stressed MSMEs**.
**One-time restructuring** of stressed MSME loans without downgrade: **2019**, extended **2020-21**.
⚠ RBI: NPA **> 3 months** or net worth eroded **50%**.

64.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I: Causes of industrial sickness
 a. Poor working-capital management
 b. Aggressive competition
 c. Obsolete technology
 d. Sudden changes in export-import policy

List-II: Classification
 i. Internal production cause
 ii. External demand cause
 iii. Internal finance cause
 iv. External policy cause

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
64.x: Poor working-capital management is an internal finance cause; aggressive competition is an external demand cause; obsolete technology is an internal production cause; and export-import policy changes are external policy causes.
64.tq: Start by pairing the clear internal finance and external policy examples, then complete the classification.
xs: Correct match: **a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**Poor working-capital management** = internal **finance**; **aggressive competition** = external **demand**.
**Obsolete technology** = internal **production**; **export-import policy** changes = external **policy**.
xa: Internal management causes: poor planning, **diversion of funds**, faulty project appraisal.
External infrastructure causes: chronic **power shortages**, transport bottlenecks.
External credit cause: **delayed and costly credit**.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about the consequences of industrial sickness:
1. Bank loans may turn into non-performing assets.
2. Plant, land and funds may remain idle in unviable units.
3. Industrial sickness can cause unemployment.
4. It necessarily increases revenue receipts of the exchequer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: Sickness can create NPAs, unemployment and locked capital. Idle assets also result in revenue loss to the exchequer, so statement 4 is false.
64.tq: Reject the reversed fiscal consequence and retain the three direct consequences.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Sickness turns bank loans into **NPAs**, locks **plant, land and funds** in unviable units, and causes **unemployment**.
Statement 4 wrong: locked capital means **revenue lost to the exchequer**, not a gain.
xa: To protect jobs, the State took over sick private units, esp. **textiles and engineering**.
This **lowered PSU returns**.
NPAs **weaken lenders**.

64.s: The State takeover of certain sick private units, particularly in textiles and engineering, was primarily intended to:
o: Transfer all industrial land to banks
64.x: The State took over certain sick private units, especially textile and engineering units, mainly to protect jobs and employment.
64.tq: Link the policy intervention to its stated employment objective rather than ownership alone.
xs: The State took over sick private units, especially in **textiles and engineering**, to **protect employment** — option **(2)** is correct.
Unemployment is a key consequence of sickness.
xa: The public sector absorbing these units **lowered PSU returns**.
Sickness is concentrated in **textiles (cotton mills)**, **jute**, **sugar** and **engineering**.
**IRBI** (**1971**) was set up to rehabilitate sick units.

64.s: Industrial sickness has been particularly concentrated in which group of sectors?
64.x: The sectors especially associated with industrial sickness are textiles, including cotton mills, jute, sugar and engineering.
64.tq: Recall the sectoral cluster rather than selecting a group of generally important industries.
xs: Industrial sickness is concentrated in **textiles, jute, sugar and engineering** — option **(2)** is correct.
Within textiles, **cotton mills** stand out.
xa: Sick private textile and engineering units were taken over by the State to protect jobs.
Internal causes include **obsolete technology** and poor quality control.
The **Kohli Working Group (1999-2000)** looked at rehabilitation of sick **SSI** units.

64.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Tiwari Committee (1984-85) recommended special legislation on industrial sickness.
2. The Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act was enacted in 1987.
3. The BIFR was set up in January 1987.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Tiwari Committee (1984-85) probed sickness and recommended special legislation. Statement 2 is wrong: SICA was enacted in 1985. Statement 3 is correct: BIFR was set up in January 1987. So A misses statement 3, C and D include the wrong statement 2; B is right.
64.tq: Tiwari 1984-85 -> SICA 1985 -> BIFR 1987: Act and Board years differ.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Tiwari Committee (1984-85)** recommended special legislation.
Statement 2 wrong: **SICA** was enacted in **1985**, not 1987.
Statement 3 correct: **BIFR** was set up in **January 1987**.
xa: ⚠ **SICA** = 1985 Act; **BIFR** under it set up **January 1987**.
⚠ **Tiwari** → SICA; **Eradi** → NCLT; **Viswanathan** → IBC.
Appeals from BIFR went to the **AAIFR**.

64.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the functions associated with BIFR?
o: Early detection of sickness, revival of viable units and closure of unviable units
Regulation of stock exchanges, revival of banks and promotion of exports
Recovery of all agricultural loans and supervision of public-sector recruitment
Promotion of small-scale industries, control of inflation and management of foreign exchange
64.x: BIFR was concerned with early detection of industrial sickness, revival of viable units and closure or winding-up of unviable units.
64.tq: Identify the option that combines the three functions rather than a neighbouring economic responsibility.
xs: BIFR's functions: **early detection of sickness**, **revival of viable units** and **closure of unviable units** — option **(1)** is correct.
Its core job was **revival of sick industries** — not stock markets, loan recovery or SSI promotion.
xa: BIFR covered both **public and private** companies with industrial undertakings.
Appeals: **AAIFR**.
BIFR ceased on **30 November 2016**; cases went to **NCLT/NCLAT** under **IBC 2016**.

64.s: Which institution, set up in 1971, was associated with the rehabilitation of sick industrial units?
o: Appellate Authority for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
64.x: The Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India, established in 1971, was set up to rehabilitate sick industrial units.
64.tq: Match the institution with its rehabilitation role and distinguish it from later forums.
xs: The **Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India (IRBI)**, set up in **1971**, rehabilitated sick units — option **(3)** is correct.
**NCLT** and **NCLAT** date from the **IBC 2016** era; **AAIFR** heard BIFR appeals; the **National Renewal Fund** began in **1992**.
xa: IRBI was the **first dedicated rehabilitation bank**.
BIFR was the **last SICA-era forum** (dissolved **1 Dec 2016**).
**Liberalized Margin Money Scheme** (**June 1987**) reduced sickness in the small-scale sector.

64.s: The principal purpose of the National Renewal Fund was to:
o: Finance voluntary retirement, retraining and redeployment of displaced workers
Provide foreign exchange to importing firms
64.x: The Fund financed voluntary retirement schemes, retraining and redeployment for workers displaced by restructuring or closure of industrial units.
64.tq: Recognise the social-safety-net function from the worker-displacement scenario.
xs: The **National Renewal Fund** financed **VRS compensation, retraining and redeployment** of displaced workers — option **(1)** is correct.
It was not an export, forex or irrigation fund.
xa: Set up in **1992** as a **social safety net for industrial restructuring**.
It also supported restructuring and **modernisation** of industries.
It was **wound up in 2000**.

64.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a reason for the failure of the BIFR-based regime?
o: Legal loopholes enabling promoters to stall debt recovery
Excessively rapid resolution of all sick units
64.x: The regime was criticised for procedural delays, legal loopholes and an ineffective revival mechanism; rapid resolution was not a reason for its failure.
64.tq: Find the option that reverses the documented criticism of the institution.
xs: **Excessively rapid resolution** was not a reason for BIFR's failure — option **(4)** is the answer.
BIFR failed due to **procedural delays**, **legal loopholes** that let promoters stall recovery, and an **ineffective revival mechanism**.
xa: A **SICA reference froze debt recovery**.
BIFR references **took years**; SICA **protected defaulting promoters**.
The successor **IBC 2016** promises **time-bound resolution**.

64.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. SICA, 1985
 b. BIFR
 c. AAIFR
 d. Debtor-in-possession

List-II
 i. Creditor-in-control under the new regime
 ii. National Company Law Appellate Tribunal
 iii. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
 iv. National Company Law Tribunal

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
64.x: SICA corresponds to the earlier regime replaced by IBC, BIFR was succeeded by NCLT, AAIFR by NCLAT, and debtor-in-possession was replaced by creditor-in-control.
64.tq: Start with the sure institutional successor pairs and eliminate codes with a repeated mismatch.
xs: Correct match: **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**Debtor-in-possession** → **creditor-in-control**.
xa: The IBC regulator is **IBBI**, with licensed **Insolvency Professionals**.
IBC aims at **time-bound resolution** and "**maximisation of asset value**".
IBC came from the **T.K. Viswanathan (BLRC, 2015)** committee.

64.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the present insolvency framework?
o: IBBI — appellate tribunal for BIFR cases
64.x: Under the IBC framework the NCLT is the adjudicating authority, so B is correct. NCLAT is the appellate tribunal (insolvency professionals are licensed, with IBBI as regulator), IBBI is the regulator rather than an appellate body, and SICA was the old regime replaced by the IBC.
64.tq: Identify the correct authority-function pair while rejecting swapped institutional roles.
xs: **NCLT — adjudicating authority** is correctly matched — option **(2)**.
**NCLAT** is the appellate tribunal; **IBBI** is the **regulator**; **SICA** was the old regime replaced by IBC.
xa: Insolvency Professionals are **licensed** under IBBI.
NCLT replaced **BIFR**; NCLAT replaced **AAIFR**.
The **Eradi Committee (1999)** recommended NCLT/NCLAT.

64.s: Which statement correctly describes the one-time restructuring measure for stressed MSME loans?
o: It was introduced in 2016 and prohibited all forms of restructuring.
It was introduced in 2019 without downgrade and extended during 2020-21.
It was introduced in 1987 and applied only to large public-sector companies.
It was introduced in 1992 and permanently cancelled all MSME loans.
64.x: A one-time restructuring of stressed MSME loans without downgrade was permitted in 2019 and extended during 2020-21.
64.tq: Track the measure through both its introduction year and extension period.
xs: The **one-time restructuring** of stressed MSME loans **without downgrade** came in **2019** and was **extended in 2020-21** — option **(2)** is correct.
**2016** brought the RBI MSME revival framework; **1987** the Liberalized Margin Money Scheme; **1992** the NRF.
xa: The **2016 framework** stresses early identification via **SMA-0/1/2**.
The 2016 framework also set up **Committees for Stressed MSMEs**.
Delayed payments now go to **MSME Samadhaan**.

64.s: Which of the following correctly represents the present institutional arrangement for dealing with industrial distress and delayed MSME payments?
o: National Renewal Fund for companies, and IRBI for delayed payments
SICA through BIFR for companies, and AAIFR for delayed payments
NCLAT for all delayed payments, and RBI for winding-up companies
IBC 2016 through NCLT for companies, and MSME Samadhaan for delayed payments
64.x: The present framework uses IBC, 2016 and NCLT for company insolvency matters, while MSME Samadhaan addresses delayed payments to MSMEs.
64.tq: Separate the insolvency forum from the mechanism dealing specifically with delayed MSME payments.
xs: Today: **IBC 2016 through NCLT** for companies and **MSME Samadhaan** for delayed payments — option **(4)** is correct.
**SICA**, **BIFR**, **AAIFR**, **IRBI** and the **National Renewal Fund** are past institutions.
xa: BIFR was dissolved on **1 Dec 2016**.
The NRF was wound up in **2000**.
IBC is **creditor-in-control**, with regulator **IBBI**.

64.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
A. Tiwari Committee
B. Omkar Goswami Committee
C. Kohli Working Group
D. Eradi Committee

List-II (Subject or outcome)
1. Insolvency and winding-up leading to NCLT/NCLAT
2. Industrial sickness leading to SICA, 1985 and BIFR
3. Rehabilitation of sick SSI units
4. Industrial sickness and corporate restructuring

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
64.x: The Tiwari Committee was associated with SICA, 1985 and BIFR; the Omkar Goswami Committee examined industrial sickness and corporate restructuring; the Kohli Working Group dealt with rehabilitation of sick SSI units; and the Eradi Committee examined insolvency and winding-up, leading to NCLT/NCLAT.
64.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with swapped committee outcomes.
xs: Correct match: **A-2, B-4, C-3, D-1** — option **(1)**.
**Tiwari** → sickness, **SICA 1985** and BIFR; **Omkar Goswami** → sickness and corporate restructuring.
**Kohli** → rehabilitation of sick **SSI** units; **Eradi** → insolvency and winding-up → **NCLT/NCLAT**.
xa: **T.K. Viswanathan (BLRC, 2015)** → bankruptcy law → **IBC 2016**.
⚠ **Tiwari** → SICA; **Eradi** → NCLT; **Viswanathan** → IBC.

64.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 was based on the recommendations of the:
64.x: The IBC was based on the T.K. Viswanathan Committee, also known as the Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee, 2015.
64.tq: Identify the committee associated with a reform.
xs: **IBC 2016** came from the **T.K. Viswanathan Committee** (**BLRC, 2015**) — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Eradi Committee (1999)** led to NCLT/NCLAT; **Tiwari** to SICA.
xa: IBC is administered through **NCLT** (adjudicating) and **NCLAT** (appellate), with regulator **IBBI**.
IBC shifted from **debtor-in-possession** to **creditor-in-control**.
SICA → IBC shifted power to creditors and improved **ease of doing business**.

64.s: The delayed settlement of invoices is a major cause of sickness among MSMEs. Which of the following was required by the MSME Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha in August 2026 to address this problem?
o: State governments were required to route all industrial loans through BIFR.
MSMEs were required to submit insolvency cases directly to NCLAT.
Banks were required to waive all overdue payments owed by MSMEs.
Central Public Sector Enterprises were required to settle MSME invoices through TReDS.
64.x: The measure required Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) to settle MSME invoices through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS), addressing delayed payments, a major cause of MSME sickness.
64.tq: Identify the institution required to act and the specific payment platform involved.
xs: The MSME Bill passed by the **Rajya Sabha** (**4 Aug 2026**) requires **CPSEs to settle MSME invoices through TReDS** — option **(4)** is correct.
BIFR no longer exists (dissolved **1 Dec 2016**), and there is no blanket waiver of MSME dues.
xa: **Delayed payments** by large buyers and government are a **major trigger** of MSME sickness.
Delayed-payment cases go to **MSME Samadhaan**.
Company insolvency now goes to **NCLT** under **IBC 2016**.

64.s:
Assertion (A): The shift from SICA to the IBC strengthened the position of creditors in insolvency resolution.

Reason (R): The earlier SICA framework was criticised for protecting defaulting promoters and allowing BIFR proceedings to remain pending for years.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
64.x: Both the Assertion and the Reason are true. The weaknesses associated with SICA and prolonged BIFR proceedings explain the movement towards an IBC framework that gave creditors a stronger role.
64.tq: Check whether the criticism of the old framework explains the institutional shift towards creditor control.
xs: **Both A and R are true** and R is the **correct explanation** of A — option **(1)**.
SICA → IBC **shifted power from debtor to creditor** and improved credit recovery.
The shift was a response to SICA protecting **defaulting promoters** and BIFR references taking **years**.
xa: IBC is **creditor-in-control**, with **time-bound resolution**.
Regulator **IBBI**; licensed **Insolvency Professionals**.
IBC came from the **BLRC (2015)** under **T.K. Viswanathan**.

65.s: The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 primarily provided for
o: Transfer of management of all industries to foreign investors
Regulation of agricultural land ceilings alone
Licensing for starting or expanding industrial units and the creation of Development Councils
Abolition of all industrial licences and quotas
65.x: The IDRA, 1951 provided for licensing of industrial units when they were started or expanded and also provided for Development Councils. It was amended in 1953.
65.tq: Identify the Act from its two core functions instead of confusing it with later liberalisation measures.
xs: The **IDRA, 1951** provided **licensing for starting or expanding industrial units** and created **Development Councils** — option **(3)** is correct.
It set up licensing rather than abolishing it; licences were largely abolished only by **NIP 1991**.
xa: The Act was **amended in 1953**.
It is the base of the licensing regime: **IDRA 1951** → **MRTP 1969** → **FERA 1973** → **SICA 1985**.
Today only **5** industries need a compulsory licence.

65.s: The Hazari Report of 1967 and the Dutt Committee of 1969 exposed the fact that industrial licensing
o: Was confined exclusively to public sector enterprises
Had eliminated concentration of economic power
65.x: The Hazari Report and Dutt Committee found that the licensing system tended to favour large business houses, contributing to the subsequent MRTP framework.
65.tq: Link the reports to their common finding rather than confusing their dates with the MRTP enactment year.
xs: The **Hazari Report (1967)** and **Dutt Committee (1969)** showed that licensing **favoured big business houses** — option **(3)** is correct.
Their findings led to the **MRTP Act**.
xa: Some notes date the Dutt Committee to **1964**.
The Dutt Committee is the **Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee**.
The MRTP Act was enacted in **1969** and came into force in **1970**.

65.s: The negative list announced in 1988 contained how many industries?
65.x: The negative list of 1988 contained 26 industries.
65.tq: Use the year-number association and avoid swapping it with the 32 groups delicensed in the 1980s.
xs: The **1988** negative list had **26** industries — option **(2)** is correct.
**32** groups were delicensed in the **1980s**; **18** is the NIP 1991 licensing list.
xa: Under **NIP 1991**, **18** industries needed compulsory licences.
Now only **5**: alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, electronic aerospace & defence equipment, industrial explosives.
Licensing originated in the **IDRA, 1951**.

65.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the five industries that continued under compulsory licensing?
65.x: The five remaining categories were alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, and industrial explosives. Leather had been delicensed in 1993.
65.tq: Find the sector removed from the final compulsory-licensing list by recalling the earlier delicensing step.
xs: **Leather** is not among the five licensed industries — option **(4)** is the answer.
The five: **alcohol**, **cigarettes**, **hazardous chemicals**, **electronic aerospace & defence equipment**, **industrial explosives**.
xa: NIP **1991** started with **18** licensed industries.
The **1988** negative list had **26** industries.
In the **1980s**, **32** groups were delicensed.

65.s: Which one of the following was the principal purpose of the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969?
o: To control private monopolies and concentration of economic power
To promote foreign direct investment in high-priority industries
To provide automatic approval for technology agreements
65.x: The MRTP Act, 1969 aimed to control private monopolies and prevent concentration of economic power. Its enactment followed the recommendations associated with the Dutt Committee.
65.tq: Distinguish the objective of the MRTP Act from objectives of later liberalisation measures.
xs: The **MRTP Act, 1969** aimed to **control private monopolies and concentration of economic power** — option **(1)** is correct.
It also curbed **monopolistic, restrictive and unfair trade practices** (APPSC-GS **2019**).
Foreign exchange control was **FERA**'s job (**1973**), later replaced by **FEMA 1999**.
xa: It was recommended by the **Dutt Committee**.
Original MRTP threshold: assets **₹20 crore+** or **33%** market share.
Replaced by the **Competition Act, 2002**; MRTP Commission → **CCI**.

65.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the MRTP framework:
1. The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969 and came into force in 1970.
2. The asset threshold for MRTP firms was raised to Rs. 100 crore in 1985.
3. The market-share criterion was reduced from 33 per cent to 25 per cent in 1984.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
65.x: All three statements are correct. The Act was enacted in 1969 and brought into force in 1970; the market-share limit was reduced in 1984 and the asset limit was raised in 1985.
65.tq: Check each date and numerical change independently before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: MRTP enacted **1969**, in force **1970**.
Statement 2: asset limit raised to **₹100 crore** in **1985**.
Statement 3: market share cut from **33%** to **25%** in **1984**.
xa: The original asset threshold was **₹20 crore+**.
**NIP 1991** scrapped the asset threshold.
⚠ Market share **33% → 25%** (1984); assets **₹20 crore → ₹100 crore** (1985).

65.s: The MRTP Act, 1969 was replaced by which legislation?
65.x: The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the MRTP Act. The MRTP Commission was replaced by the Competition Commission of India.
65.tq: Use the enactment-year trap to distinguish the Competition Act from FEMA.
xs: The MRTP Act was replaced by the **Competition Act, 2002** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2018** key).
**FEMA 1999** replaced **FERA**, not MRTP.
xa: Some notes say "**Competition Act, 2001**" — the key is **2002**.
The Act commenced on **31 Mar 2003**; **CCI** was established on **14 Oct 2003**.
⚠ Replacements: **FERA → FEMA**; **MRTP → Competition Act**; **SICA → IBC**.

65.s: What was the effect of the New Industrial Policy, 1991 on the MRTP asset threshold of Rs. 100 crore?
o: It made the threshold applicable only to public sector firms
It reduced the threshold to Rs. 50 crore
It doubled the threshold to Rs. 200 crore
It scrapped the threshold for large firms
65.x: The New Industrial Policy, 1991 scrapped the MRTP asset threshold. Large firms no longer required prior approval for expansion, mergers or takeovers merely because of their asset size.
65.tq: Apply the reform measure to the specific regulatory restriction being removed.
xs: **NIP 1991** **scrapped the MRTP asset threshold** (₹100 crore since **1985**) — option **(4)** is correct.
Large firms no longer needed **prior approval** to expand, merge or take over.
xa: Original threshold: assets **₹20 crore+** or **33%** market share.
In **1984**, the share criterion was cut to **25%**.
MRTP was later replaced by the **Competition Act, 2002**.

65.s: The MRTP Act, 1969 was recommended by the
65.x: The Dutt Committee, formally the Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee, recommended the MRTP legislation.
65.tq: Trap the closely associated Hazari and Dutt committees by asking which one made the recommendation.
xs: The **MRTP Act, 1969** was recommended by the **Dutt Committee** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Hazari Report (1967)** exposed licensing bias but was a report, not the recommending committee; **Rangarajan** (**1993**) was on disinvestment.
xa: Dutt Committee = **Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee** (**1969**).
MRTP came into force in **1970**.
Purpose: **control private monopoly** and concentration of economic power.

65.s: The MRTP Commission was replaced by the
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
65.x: The MRTP Commission was replaced by the Competition Commission of India (CCI) under the competition-law framework.
65.tq: Match the abolished statutory body with its institutional successor.
xs: The **MRTP Commission** was replaced by the **Competition Commission of India (CCI)** — option **(2)** is correct.
This came with the **Competition Act, 2002**.
xa: **CCI** was established on **14 Oct 2003**, under the **Ministry of Corporate Affairs**.
CCI has a **Chairperson + 2-6 members**.
**NCLAT** hears CCI appeals from **26 May 2017**.

65.s: The Competition Act, 2002 was recommended by which committee?
65.x: The Competition Act, 2002 was recommended by the S.V.S. Raghavan Committee in 2000.
65.tq: Distinguish the committee associated with competition law from committees on insolvency and company law.
xs: The **Competition Act, 2002** was recommended by the **S.V.S. Raghavan Committee** (**2000**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**T.K. Viswanathan** (BLRC **2015**) led to the IBC; **Eradi** to NCLT; the **Disinvestment Commission** (**1996**) advised on PSU sales.
xa: The Act was introduced by **Arun Jaitley**.
It replaced the **MRTP Act**.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about the Competition Commission of India:
1. It was established on 14 October 2003.
2. It consists of a Chairperson and two to six members.
3. It functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
4. The Competition Act has been amended in 2007, 2009 and 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
65.x: All four statements are correct. The CCI was established on 14 October 2003, has a Chairperson and two to six members, functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, and the Act was amended in 2007, 2009 and 2023.
65.tq: Combine composition, administrative control and amendment dates in one institutional question.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
