66.tq: DB rankings → foreign investors.
xs: Doing Business rankings mainly guided **foreign investors** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2019**).
They were not tools for consumers, election bodies or central banks.
xa: The report was conceptualised by the **IFC**, the World Bank Group's private-sector arm.
It had **10** parameters, from **starting a business** to **resolving insolvency**.
India's rank improved from **142** to **63**.

66.s:
Which of the following reforms is correctly associated with the area of improvement it was intended to support?
1. GST — paying taxes and a unified market
2. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 — resolving insolvency
3. SPICe+ — starting a business
4. Online building-plan approvals — construction permits

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
66.x: GST, IBC 2016, SPICe+ and online building-plan approvals are correctly matched with the respective areas of improvement.
66.tq: Match each reform with its functional outcome before selecting the complete code.
xs: All four are correctly matched — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**GST** — paying taxes, unified market; **IBC 2016** — resolving insolvency.
**SPICe+** — starting a business; **online building-plan approvals** — construction permits.
xa: **SPICe+** (**2020**) bundles **11 services** of **3 ministries**; also **MCA21 V3**.
**DILRMP**, **ULPIN**, **NGDRS** improved **registering property**.
**GST** as an EoDB reform was the APPSC-G2 **2025** key.

66.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a reform credited with improving India’s Ease of Doing Business performance?
o: Removal of all foreign ownership restrictions
Land records reforms through DILRMP and ULPIN
66.x: Faceless assessment, faster electricity connections and land-record reforms were credited reforms. Removal of all foreign ownership restrictions was specifically not identified as such a reform.
66.tq: Watch for the extreme word ‘all’ in a policy claim and eliminate the unsupported reform.
xs: **Removal of all foreign ownership restrictions** was not a credited EoDB reform — option **(2)** is the answer.
Credited reforms include **faster electricity connections**, **faceless tax assessment** and land records (**DILRMP**, **ULPIN**).
xa: ⚠ Trap — not reforms: removal of all foreign ownership restrictions, **nationalisation**, **PSU expansion**.
Other credited reforms: **GST**, **IBC 2016**, **SPICe+**, **e-Sanchit**, **commercial courts**.
The new EoDB wave stresses **digital governance** and **trust-based regulation** (**9 Jun 2026**).

66.s: The e-Biz platform was introduced as which of the following?
o: A State-level portal exclusively for environmental clearances
A Mission Mode Project under the National e-Governance Plan for online registration, filing and payments
A World Bank index for measuring business regulations
An investment promotion joint venture between FICCI and CII
66.x: e-Biz is a Mission Mode Project under NeGP that enables online registration, filing and payment for businesses.
66.tq: Distinguish the function of a digital business service from an investment agency or ranking index.
xs: **e-Biz** is a **Mission Mode Project under the National e-Governance Plan (NeGP)** for **online registration, filing and payments** — option **(2)** is correct.
The FICCI-CII joint venture describes **Invest India**, not e-Biz.
xa: e-Biz is part of the **New Processes** pillar of Make in India.
**NSWS** gives access to **686** central and **7,498** state approvals.
**DPIIT Single Window Systems Guidebook (2025)**: **80** services = **44** essential + **36** desirable.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Single Window System:
1. The Foreign Investment Facilitation portal was merged with it in August 2022.
2. Udyam Registration for MSMEs was introduced in 2020.
3. It provides access only to central government approvals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the system provides access to both central and State approvals.
66.tq: Reject the absolute ‘only’ statement after checking the two-level approval coverage.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the **FIF portal** merged with NSWS in **Aug 2022**.
Statement 2: **Udyam Registration** for MSMEs began in **2020**.
Statement 3 wrong: NSWS covers **686 central** and **7,498 state** approvals.
xa: **e-Biz** is a Mission Mode Project under **NeGP**.
DPIIT's guidebook lists **80** single-window services.
**Invest India** was set up in **2009**.

66.s: Invest India, established in 2009, is best described as:
o: A statutory regulator under the Reserve Bank of India for foreign exchange transactions
A World Bank Group index for ranking investment destinations
A not-for-profit joint venture involving DIPP, FICCI, CII, NASSCOM and the States, serving as the national investment promotion agency
A private company established exclusively by NASSCOM for software exports
66.x: Invest India was established in 2009 as a not-for-profit joint venture involving DIPP, FICCI, CII, NASSCOM and the States, and serves as the national investment promotion agency.
66.tq: Separate the investment-promotion agency from a regulator, index or private industry body.
xs: **Invest India** (**2009**) is a **not-for-profit JV of DIPP, FICCI, CII, NASSCOM and the States**, the **national investment promotion agency** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is not a regulator, an index or a NASSCOM-only company.
xa: It also acts as an **investment-facilitation SPV**.
**NSWS**: **686** central + **7,498** state approvals.
The **FIF** portal joined NSWS in **Aug 2022**.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about the Jan Vishwas 2.0 Bill:
1. It was introduced on 18 August 2025.
2. It amended 355 provisions but decriminalised none of them.
3. It was passed by Parliament in 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Bill was introduced on 18 August 2025 and passed by Parliament in 2026. Statement 2 is wrong: of the 355 provisions across 16 Acts and 10 ministries, 288 were decriminalised. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
66.tq: Jan Vishwas 2.0: 16 Acts, 355 provisions, 288 decriminalised.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: introduced on **18 Aug 2025**.
Statement 2 wrong: of **355** provisions, **288** were **decriminalised**.
Statement 3: **passed by Parliament in 2026**.
xa: It covers **16** Acts across **10** ministries.
**Jan Vishwas Act 2026**: an **Improvement Notice** for first-time Legal Metrology lapses.
DPIIT runs a **Reducing Compliance Burden** exercise.

66.s: Business Reform Action Plan, commonly abbreviated as BRAP, was first released in 2015 by:
o: DIPP, now DPIIT, in association with the World Bank Group
The Ministry of Finance and the IMF
66.x: BRAP was first released in 2015 by DIPP, now DPIIT, with the World Bank Group.
66.tq: Who-launched-what trap using neighbouring institutions as distractors.
xs: **BRAP** was first released in **2015** by **DIPP (now DPIIT)** with the **World Bank Group** — option **(1)** is correct.
NITI Aayog runs a separate **Investment Friendliness Index**.
xa: BRAP = **Business Reform Action Plan** (APPSC-GS **2019**).
AP was **2nd** in BRAP **2015** (Gujarat **1st**).
DPIIT is preparing **BRAP 2026**.

66.s: Which statement correctly describes Andhra Pradesh's BRAP position from 2016 onwards?
o: It had no BRAP position after 2016.
It ranked No. 1 only in the 2024 edition.
It ranked second consistently after Gujarat.
It remained No. 1 consistently, with the 2016 position jointly shared with Telangana.
66.x: Andhra Pradesh was jointly first with Telangana in BRAP 2016 and is described as No. 1 consistently from 2016 onwards.
66.tq: Distinguish a specific jointly held rank from the subsequent continuing position.
xs: From **2016** onwards AP stayed **No. 1 consistently**, sharing **2016** jointly with **Telangana** — option **(4)** is correct.
In **2015** AP was **2nd** (Gujarat **1st**), so it did not rank second "consistently".
xa: APPSC-GS **2023** key: AP **1st**.
BRAP **2024** was the **7th edition** with **435** reform points.
NITI Aayog's index (**Jul 2026**) put AP among **"Frontrunners"**.

66.s: The four principles associated with the 435 reform points in BRAP 2024 were:
66.x: The BRAP 2024 reform points were organised around Simplification, Elimination, Digitisation and Decriminalisation.
66.tq: Direct recall of a four-part policy framework.
xs: BRAP **2024**'s **435** points follow **Simplification, Elimination, Digitisation and Decriminalisation** — option **(4)** is correct.
These are **state-specific** reform points, aimed at cutting and digitising procedures, not adding inspections or penalties.
xa: BRAP **2024** was the **7th edition**.
**DBRAP** extends reforms to **Tier-II** and **Tier-III** cities.
**Jan Vishwas** laws also pursue **decriminalisation**.

66.s: District BRAP, or DBRAP, is intended primarily to:
o: Extend business reforms to district-level administration and Tier-II and Tier-III cities
Measure the competitiveness of Indian states against foreign countries
Rank only metropolitan cities on exports
66.x: DBRAP extends the reform process to districts and Tier-II and Tier-III cities.
66.tq: Apply the meaning of the district-level extension to the appropriate administrative scope.
xs: **DBRAP** takes business reforms to **district level** and **Tier-II and Tier-III cities** — option **(1)** is correct.
It does not replace state-level BRAP or compare states with foreign countries.
xa: State-level **BRAP** began in **2015** under **DIPP** with the **World Bank Group**.
DPIIT is preparing **BRAP 2026**.
AP has been **No. 1** consistently from **2016**.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about the NITI Aayog Investment Friendliness Index announced in July 2026:
1. It uses 953 indicators.
2. It is organised around 8 pillars.
3. Andhra Pradesh was placed among the Frontrunners with a score of 45–50.
4. Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Goa and Odisha were identified as Top Performers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: All four are correct: the NITI Aayog Investment Friendliness Index (July 2026) uses 953 indicators across 8 pillars, places Andhra Pradesh among the Frontrunners (score 45-50), and names Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Goa and Odisha as Top Performers.
66.tq: Use the all-inclusive option after checking the indicators, pillars, AP category and top-performer list.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
NITI Aayog's **Investment Friendliness Index** (**Jul 2026**) uses **953 indicators** and **8 pillars**.
AP is among **"Frontrunners"** (score **45-50**); **Top Performers** = **Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Goa, Odisha**.
xa: ⚠ Doing Business = **10** parameters; B-READY = **3** pillars; this index = **8** pillars.
AP's **Single Desk Portal** cleared **99.20%** approvals within SLA.
IMD Competitiveness rank: **43** (2021) → **41** (2025).

66.s:
Which of the following areas is identified as a weak indicator affecting the ease of doing business in India?
1. Contract enforcement
2. Property registration
3. Digital literacy
4. Export promotion
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
66.x: Contract enforcement and property registration are identified as significant remaining bottlenecks. Digital literacy and export promotion are not cited as the weakest indicators in this context.
66.tq: Identify the specific weak indicators instead of selecting broader development objectives.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Contract enforcement** and **property registration** are the **weakest indicators** (legal bottlenecks).
Digital literacy and export promotion are not named as EoDB bottlenecks.
xa: Other bottlenecks: **labour** (four **labour codes**) and **compliance** burden.
**DILRMP**, **ULPIN** and **NGDRS** target registering property.
**Commercial courts** and **e-Sanchit** customs filing are among the credited EoDB reforms.

66.s: The four labour codes and the proposed central rules primarily seek to promote which broad outcome?
o: Replacement of all state labour laws by municipal laws
Formalisation of labour and consolidation of labour regulations
Restriction of employment to the public sector
66.x: The four labour codes and the draft central rules are associated with labour-law consolidation and increasing formalisation. They do not eliminate informal employment completely.
66.tq: Link the reform instrument with its stated broad policy objective.
xs: The four **labour codes** aim at **formalisation of labour** and consolidation of labour regulations — option **(3)** is correct.
Formalisation is projected to rise from **60.4% to 75.5%**, with **77 lakh** jobs — but **over 80%** of workers remain informal, so informality is not eliminated.
xa: Draft central rules were issued in **Dec 2025**.
The debate: EoDB must be matched by "**ease of living**" and **workers' rights**.
DPIIT's **Reducing Compliance Burden** exercise tackles regulatory cost.

66.s: Which one of the following chronological sequences is correct?
o: National Manufacturing Policy — Make in India — PLI schemes — India Semiconductor Mission — National Logistics Policy
Make in India — National Manufacturing Policy — PLI schemes — National Logistics Policy — India Semiconductor Mission
National Manufacturing Policy — PLI schemes — Make in India — India Semiconductor Mission — National Logistics Policy
PLI schemes — National Manufacturing Policy — Make in India — India Semiconductor Mission — National Logistics Policy
66.x: The sequence is 2011 National Manufacturing Policy, September 2014 Make in India, 2020 PLI, December 2021 India Semiconductor Mission, and September 2022 National Logistics Policy.
66.tq: Use the dated milestones to establish the full sequence rather than relying on programme familiarity.
xs: The order is **NMP → Make in India → PLI → ISM → National Logistics Policy** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: **National Policy on Electronics**: **20 Feb 2019**.
**PM GatiShakti**: **October 2021**.
**National Manufacturing Mission**: Budget **2025-26**.

66.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Make in India — Manufacturing and investment hub
Digital India — Digital infrastructure, services and empowerment
66.x: Skill India aims at skilling youth for jobs, not real-time digital payments. Digital India, Make in India and Startup India are correctly matched with their respective objectives.
66.tq: Find the one objective wrongly transferred from a different digital initiative.
xs: **Skill India — Real-time digital payments** is wrongly matched — option **(1)** is the answer.
**Skill India** (**15 July 2015**) is about **skilling the workforce**.
**Digital India** = digital infrastructure, services, literacy; **Startup India** = start-up ecosystem; **Make in India** = manufacturing hub.
xa: ⚠ **Digital India** **1 July 2015** vs **Skill India** **15 July 2015**.
**Startup India**: **16 Jan 2016** (National Startup Day).
**Make in India**: **25 Sept 2014**.

66.s:
Arrange the following missions in chronological order of their launch:
A. Startup India
B. Make in India
C. Digital India
D. Skill India
66.x: Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014, Digital India on 1 July 2015, Skill India on 15 July 2015 and Startup India on 16 January 2016, so the order is B, C, D, A. Digital India precedes Skill India by two weeks, which rules out option B.
66.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two July 2015 missions.
xs: The order is **B, C, D, A** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Make in India** (**25 Sept 2014**) → **Digital India** (**1 July 2015**) → **Skill India** (**15 July 2015**) → **Startup India** (**16 Jan 2016**).
xa: ⚠ Digital India precedes Skill India by two weeks — the classic trap.
**16 Jan** = **National Startup Day**.
DPIIT-recognised startups: **502** (2016) → **2.47 lakh** (**12 Aug 2026**).

66.s: The expression “China+1” in the context of Make in India and PLI refers most closely to:
o: A bilateral tax treaty between India and China
Diversifying global supply chains by adding India as an alternative manufacturing location
Adding one percentage point to India's GDP growth
Replacing China with one Indian state in all trade
66.x: “China+1” refers to diversification of global value chains by creating an additional manufacturing base, such as India, alongside China.
66.tq: Interpret the policy phrase in its global value-chain context rather than literally.
xs: **"China+1"** means **diversifying global supply chains by adding India as an alternative manufacturing location** — option **(2)** is correct.
EoDB and PLI aim to lift manufacturing's share and help India **join global value chains**.
xa: Make in India's strategy shifted to **integration with global value chains** (**Jun 2026**).
Smartphones became India's **largest export category in 2025**.
Medium- and high-tech manufacturing = **46.3%** of total (ES **2025-26**).

66.s:
Which of the following is identified as a criticism of the manufacturing strategy?
1. Gains may reflect assembly without sufficient domestic value addition.
2. PLI gains are concentrated in electronics and semiconductors.
3. The 25 per cent of GDP manufacturing target has been missed.
4. Manufacturing has already exceeded the 25 per cent target in all sectors.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
66.x: The stated criticisms include assembly without adequate value addition, concentration of PLI gains in electronics and semiconductors, and failure to meet the 25 per cent of GDP target. Statement 4 reverses this criticism.
66.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the stated performance assessment.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are criticisms — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
"**Assemble in India**" vs **value addition**; **PLI gains concentrated in electronics and semiconductors**.
The **25%-of-GDP target was missed**; statement 4 is the reverse of the truth.
xa: Manufacturing is still **~16.3-17.5%** of GVA/GDP.
EoDB must be balanced with "**ease of living**" and **workers' rights**.
ES **2025-26** still credits **PLI** and the **National Manufacturing Mission** with driving investment.

66.s: Ease of doing business reforms are expected to be balanced with which of the following considerations?
o: Restriction of employment rights to formal workers
Only the interests of foreign investors
Ease of living and workers' rights
66.x: The debate emphasises that ease of doing business should be accompanied by ease of living and protection of workers' rights.
66.tq: Identify the balancing principle in a policy debate rather than choosing an absolute position.
xs: EoDB must be balanced with **ease of living and workers' rights** — option **(4)** is correct (**28 Jul 2026**).
Complete deregulation without labour protection is the concern the debate warns against.
xa: **Labour codes** aim to raise formalisation from **60.4%** to **75.5%**.
Yet **over 80%** of workers remain informal.
The new EoDB wave stresses **trust-based regulation**.

67.s: Which institution is the nodal agency for recognition of start-ups under the Startup India framework?
67.x: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) is the nodal agency for Startup India recognition.
67.tq: Identify the correct institutional authority rather than a financing agency.
xs: The nodal agency for Startup India recognition is **DPIIT** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Startup India was launched on **16 January 2016** with DPIIT as nodal body and a **19-point** Action Plan.
**NCGTC** gives the guarantee under **CGSS**; **SIDBI** manages the **Fund of Funds** — neither recognises start-ups.
xa: **16 January** is now observed as **National Startup Day**.
DPIIT also runs the **States' Startup Ranking Framework**, which assesses state start-up policies.
⚠ **DPIIT** = Startup India; **Ministry of Finance** = Stand-Up India.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about the Startup India framework:
1. Its Action Plan contains 19 points.
2. An entity formed by splitting or reconstructing an existing business is not treated as a start-up.
3. A start-up may be constituted only as a private limited company.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: The Action Plan has 19 points, and an entity formed by splitting or reconstructing an existing business is excluded. Eligible legal forms also include partnerships, LLPs and cooperatives, so statement 3 is false.
67.tq: Reject the word ‘only’ when the legal-form coverage is broader.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: the Startup India **Action Plan** has **19 points**.
Statement 2 correct: an entity formed by **splitting or reconstructing** an existing business is **not a start-up**.
Statement 3 wrong: a start-up may be a **Pvt Ltd company, partnership, LLP or co-operative**.
xa: Age limit: up to **10 years** (start-up) and up to **20 years** (deep-tech start-up).
Turnover limit: not above **₹200 crore** (start-up); **₹300 crore** (deep-tech). Older notes give **₹100 crore**.
Startup India was launched on **16 January 2016**; nodal body **DPIIT**.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly compares an ordinary start-up with a deep-tech start-up?
o: Ordinary start-up: up to 20 years and ₹300 crore turnover; deep-tech start-up: up to 10 years and ₹200 crore turnover
Ordinary start-up: up to 10 years and ₹200 crore turnover; deep-tech start-up: up to 20 years and ₹300 crore turnover
Both: up to 10 years and ₹300 crore turnover
Both: up to 20 years and ₹200 crore turnover
67.x: The stated criteria are up to 10 years and turnover not above ₹200 crore for a start-up, and up to 20 years and ₹300 crore for a deep-tech start-up. Both may have the listed legal forms.
67.tq: Read both age and turnover columns before selecting the comparison.
xs: Ordinary start-up: up to **10 years** and **₹200 crore** turnover; deep-tech: up to **20 years** and **₹300 crore** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses the two sets of limits; options (3) and (4) wrongly give both the **same** limits.
Both categories share the same legal forms: **Pvt Ltd, partnership, LLP, co-operative**.
xa: The **₹200 crore** turnover cap is a revision; older notes give **₹100 crore**.
⚠ Trap: an entity formed by **splitting or reconstructing** a business is not a start-up.
Benefit: income-tax deduction for **3 consecutive years out of 10** under **s.80-IAC**.

67.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated benefit available under the Startup India framework?
o: Self-certification under specified labour and environmental laws
Permanent exemption from all taxes for the entire life of the enterprise
Income-tax deduction for three consecutive years out of ten under Section 80-IAC
67.x: The framework provides a tax deduction for three consecutive years out of ten, self-certification and fast-track patent facilities. It does not provide a permanent exemption from all taxes.
67.tq: Find the exaggerated benefit using the extreme-word trap.
xs: **Permanent exemption from all taxes** is NOT a Startup India benefit — option **(3)**.
The tax benefit is limited: a deduction for **3 consecutive years out of 10** under **Section 80-IAC**.
**Fast-track patents** and **self-certification** under labour and environment laws are genuine benefits.
xa: The s.80-IAC deduction applies to start-ups incorporated before **1 Apr 2030**.
Start-ups can also be **wound up under IBC** (a faster exit).
**Angel tax** was abolished for all investors in **Budget 2024-25**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Startup Advisory Council was notified in January 2020.
2. Startup India Yatra searches for entrepreneurial talent mainly in Tier-1 metro cities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
67.x: Statement 1 is correct (22 Jan 2020). Statement 2 is wrong: the Yatra searches talent in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities. Hence '1 only'.
67.tq: Yatra = Tier-2/3 cities.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **National Startup Advisory Council** was notified in **January 2020** (**22 Jan 2020**).
Statement 2 wrong: **Startup India Yatra** searches for talent in **Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities**, not Tier-1 metros.
xa: About **53%** of start-ups come from **Tier-2/3** cities.
**Udyam Abhilasha** was a national-level entrepreneurship awareness campaign (**APPSC-GS 2018**), linked to **SIDBI**.
**NIDHI** (**DST**) is the umbrella programme turning knowledge-based innovations into start-ups.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS):
1. Start-ups receive the support directly from commercial banks, not through incubators.
2. It has an outlay of Rs 945 crore and was launched on 19 April 2021.
3. It gives up to Rs 20 lakh grant for proof of concept and up to Rs 50 lakh investment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
67.x: Statement 1 is wrong: SISFS is routed through incubators (up to Rs 5 crore each). Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
67.tq: SISFS flows via incubators.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 wrong: SISFS support is routed **via incubators** (up to **₹5 crore** each), not commercial banks.
Statement 2 correct: outlay **₹945 crore**; launched **19 April 2021**.
Statement 3 correct: up to **₹20 lakh grant** for proof of concept + up to **₹50 lakh investment**.
xa: **Fund of Funds (FFS)**: **₹10,000 crore**, managed by **SIDBI**, invests through SEBI-registered AIFs.
**FFS 2.0** adds another ₹10,000 crore for **deep tech, space, AI**.
**CGSS** (Oct 2022) supports collateral-free loans through **NCGTC** guarantees.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about the Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS):
1. It has a corpus of Rs 10,000 crore managed by SIDBI.
2. It invests directly in recognised start-ups.
3. FFS 2.0 adds another Rs 10,000 crore for deep tech, space and AI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
67.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: FFS invests through SEBI-registered AIFs, not directly in start-ups. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
67.tq: FFS = fund of funds: invests via AIFs.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: corpus **₹10,000 crore**, managed by **SIDBI**.
Statement 2 wrong: FFS invests **through SEBI-registered AIFs**, not directly in start-ups.
Statement 3 correct: **FFS 2.0** adds another ₹10,000 crore for **deep tech, space and AI**.
xa: ⚠ **SIDBI** both manages the Fund of Funds and gives **Stand-Up India refinance** — each **₹10,000 crore**.
**Seed Fund (SISFS)**: **₹945 crore**, launched **19 April 2021**, routed via incubators.
**Angel tax** was abolished for all investors in **Budget 2024-25**.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly describes venture capital?
o: Early-stage equity investment accompanied by active guidance for high-growth firms
Collateral-free bank lending guaranteed through NCGTC
Individuals investing their own money at the idea or seed stage
Small sums collected from many people through online platforms
67.x: Venture capital consists of early-stage equity investment with active guidance for high-growth firms. The other descriptions refer to crowdfunding, angel investment and CGSS respectively.
67.tq: Discriminate among similar start-up financing sources by their defining features.
xs: **Venture capital** = **early-stage equity** with **active guidance** for high-growth firms — option **(1)**.
Option (2) describes **CGSS** (collateral-free loans guaranteed through **NCGTC**).
Option (3) describes **angel investors**; option (4) describes **crowdfunding**.
xa: **CGSS** was introduced in **Oct 2022**; maximum **₹20 crore** per borrower; fee **1%** for champion sectors.
CGSS replaced the earlier **Credit Guarantee Fund for Startups**.
**Fund of Funds** (₹10,000 crore, **SIDBI**) invests via SEBI-registered **AIFs**.

67.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding start-up taxation and financing?
o: The Fund of Funds invests directly in every recognised start-up.
Angel tax was abolished only for government investors.
CGSS provides only grants and not guaranteed loans.
Angel tax was abolished for all investors in Budget 2024–25.
67.x: Angel tax was abolished for all investors in Budget 2024–25. The Fund of Funds invests through SEBI-registered AIFs, while CGSS supports collateral-free loans through guarantees.
67.tq: Separate a broad tax-policy change from the mechanisms of funding schemes.
xs: **Angel tax was abolished for all investors in Budget 2024-25** — option **(4)**.
Option (1) wrong: the **Fund of Funds** invests through **SEBI-registered AIFs**, not directly.
Option (2) wrong: the abolition covered **all investors**, not just government ones.
Option (3) wrong: **CGSS** provides **guaranteed, collateral-free loans** through **NCGTC**.
xa: **FFS** corpus **₹10,000 crore** (SIDBI); **FFS 2.0** adds another ₹10,000 crore for deep tech, space, AI.
**SISFS**: up to ₹20 lakh grant + ₹50 lakh investment, via incubators.
Startup tax benefit: deduction for **3 consecutive years out of 10** under **s.80-IAC**.

67.s: A privately held start-up valued at US$1 billion or more before listing is commonly called a:
67.x: A unicorn is a privately held start-up valued at US$1 billion or more before it is listed.
67.tq: Recall the precise valuation and ownership definition of a unicorn.
xs: A privately held start-up valued **US$1 billion+** before listing is a **unicorn** — option **(1)**.
Government count: **~125** active unicorns with combined value **$389 bn** (Jan 2026).
Only **4** unicorns existed in **2014**.
xa: **Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2026**: India **4th with 61** (down from 64), overtaken by the **UK (70)**.
Leaders: **USA 806**, **China 381**; Indian cities: **Bengaluru 25**, **Mumbai 13**.
⚠ Counts differ by methodology: **~125** (government) vs **61** (Hurun).

67.s:
Consider the following statements about India's start-up ecosystem:
1. India is the third-largest start-up ecosystem in the world.
2. DPIIT-recognised start-ups exceeded 2.47 lakh by August 2026.
3. Fewer than 10,000 start-ups were recognised in 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: India is the 3rd-largest ecosystem and recognised start-ups crossed 2.47 lakh (12 Aug 2026). Statement 3 is wrong: about 44,000 were added in 2025, the highest ever. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
67.tq: 3rd-largest; 2.47 lakh; ~44,000 added in 2025.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: India is the **3rd-largest** start-up ecosystem (**17 Jan 2026**).
Statement 2 correct: recognised start-ups crossed **2.47 lakh** (**12 Aug 2026**).
Statement 3 wrong: about **44,000** were added in **2025** — the **highest ever**.
xa: Government count of unicorns: **~125**, combined value **$389 bn** (Jan 2026).
Start-ups have created **20 lakh+** jobs since **2016**.
**~48%** have a woman director; **53%** are from **Tier-2/3** cities.

67.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
67.x: Udyam Abhilasha is a national entrepreneurship-awareness campaign associated with SIDBI. Swavalambini is associated with MSDE and NITI Aayog, while ASPIRE and PM Vishwakarma are Ministry of MSME programmes.
67.tq: Start from the sure programme-agency pair and eliminate swapped ministries.
xs: **Udyam Abhilasha — SIDBI** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
Udyam Abhilasha was a **national-level entrepreneurship awareness campaign** (**APPSC-GS 2018**).
**ASPIRE** (2015) belongs to the **Ministry of MSME**, not Commerce and Industry.
xa: ASPIRE sets up **Livelihood Business Incubators** in the agro-rural sector.
⚠ **NIDHI** = **DST**; **ASPIRE** = Ministry of MSME; **Udyam Abhilasha** = SIDBI.
SIDBI also manages the **Fund of Funds** (**₹10,000 crore**).

67.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with NIDHI?
o: PRAYAS—prototype development; EIR—fellowship up to ₹30,000 per month
67.x: NIDHI is a DST umbrella programme for converting knowledge-based innovations into start-ups. PRAYAS supports prototypes, while the EIR programme offers a fellowship of up to ₹30,000 per month.
67.tq: Match each named NIDHI component with its specific function.
xs: NIDHI: **PRAYAS — prototypes**; **EIR — fellowship up to ₹30,000/month** — option **(1)**.
**NIDHI** is a **DST** umbrella programme turning knowledge-based innovations into start-ups.
Collateral-free loans belong to **CGSS**; Atal Tinkering Labs belong to **AIM** — not NIDHI.
xa: NIDHI also supports **TBIs** (technology business incubators).
⚠ **NIDHI** = DST; **ASPIRE** = Ministry of MSME; **Udyam Abhilasha** = SIDBI.
**AIM 2.0**: till March 2028, **₹2,750 crore**, **2,500** new ATLs.

67.s: The Stand-Up India Scheme was launched on:
67.x: Stand-Up India was launched on 5 April 2016.
67.tq: Use the direct date-recall approach for a flagship scheme.
xs: Stand-Up India was launched on **5 April 2016** — option **(1)**.
**19 April 2021** = **Seed Fund (SISFS)** launch; **16 January 2016** = **Startup India** launch.
**22 January 2020** = notification of the **National Startup Advisory Council**.
xa: Stand-Up India is run by the **Ministry of Finance** through scheduled commercial bank branches.
Loans of **₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore** to **SC/ST and women** entrepreneurs (18+).
Operational till **31 March 2025**: **2.75 lakh** loans, **₹62,790 crore**.

67.s: Under the Stand-Up India Scheme, the loan amount generally ranges between:
67.x: Stand-Up India loans range from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore.
67.tq: Identify the correct range among closely spaced monetary figures.
xs: Stand-Up India loans range from **₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore** — option **(1)**.
They go to **SC/ST and women** entrepreneurs for **greenfield** enterprises.
xa: Loan covers up to **85%** of project cost; borrower contribution min **10%**.
Repayment up to **7 years** with an **18-month moratorium**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Stand-Up India Scheme:
1. It is implemented through scheduled commercial bank branches.
2. It covers greenfield enterprises rather than brownfield enterprises.
3. It is confined to manufacturing enterprises.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: The scheme operates through scheduled commercial bank branches and supports greenfield enterprises. It covers manufacturing, services, trading and agri-allied activities, so statement 3 is false.
67.tq: Find the restrictive sector statement that conflicts with the wider coverage.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: implemented via **scheduled commercial bank branches**.
Statement 2 correct: only **greenfield** (first-time) enterprises; **not brownfield**.
Statement 3 wrong: it covers **manufacturing, services, trading and agri-allied** activities.
xa: Launched **5 April 2016** by the **Ministry of Finance**.
**SIDBI** gives **₹10,000 crore** refinance; portal **Standupmitra**.
Extended for the **15th FC** period; operational till **31 March 2025**.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the nodal ministry and the online portal of the Stand-Up India Scheme?
67.x: Stand-Up India (5 April 2016) is run by the Ministry of Finance through scheduled commercial bank branches, and its portal is Standupmitra. DPIIT is nodal for Startup India, the Udyam portal is for MSME registration, and NITI Aayog is not the nodal body.
67.tq: Stand-Up = Finance Ministry + Standupmitra; Startup = DPIIT.
xs: Stand-Up India: **Ministry of Finance**, portal **Standupmitra** — option **(1)**.
**DPIIT** is the nodal body for **Startup India**, not Stand-Up India.
Stand-Up India works through **scheduled commercial bank branches**.
xa: Launched **5 April 2016**.
**SIDBI** provides **₹10,000 crore** refinance.
Status: extended for the **15th FC** period; operational till **31 March 2025** (IYB 2026).

67.s: Which institution functions as the State nodal agency for start-ups and innovation in Andhra Pradesh?
67.x: The AP Innovation Society (APIS) is the State nodal agency for start-ups and innovation in Andhra Pradesh.
67.tq: Identify the institution associated with the exact administrative role.
xs: The State nodal agency for start-ups and innovation is the **AP Innovation Society (APIS)** — option **(4)**.
**DPIIT** is the national nodal body; **RTIH** is a hub-and-spoke innovation hub, not the nodal agency.
xa: FY 2024-25: **6,935** start-ups; **2,493 (36%)** DPIIT-recognised; **1,203** women-led.
**50** incubators (**7th largest** start-up infrastructure); **175** mentors on APIS portal.
**564** EISCs and **590 ATLs**; **25,000** jobs; **₹480 crore** raised.

67.s: The hub of the hub-and-spoke model of Ratan Tata Innovation Hub is located at:
67.x: The central hub of Ratan Tata Innovation Hub is located at Amaravati in Mangalagiri. The other places are among its spoke locations.
67.tq: Separate the central hub from the spoke centres in a location-based question.
xs: The RTIH hub is at **Amaravati (Mangalagiri)** — option **(3)**.
**Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam and Tirupati** are **spokes**, not the hub.
xa: Other spokes: **Rajahmundry** and **Anantapuramu** (2025-26).
RTIH was established in **Aug 2025**.
Target: **20,000 start-ups and 1 lakh jobs** in 5 years ("One Family, One Entrepreneur").

67.s: The Ratan Tata Innovation Hub aims to create, over five years,
67.x: RTIH targets 20,000 start-ups and one lakh jobs over five years under the ‘One Family, One Entrepreneur’ vision.
67.tq: Match the target numbers and time period as a single policy objective.
xs: RTIH aims at **20,000 start-ups and one lakh jobs** in five years — option **(4)**.
The tagline is **"One Family, One Entrepreneur"**.
**1,203** is AP's count of **women-led** start-ups; **25,000** is jobs created per APIS data.
xa: RTIH was established in **Aug 2025** on a **hub-and-spoke** model.
Programmes: **Spark**, **Future Founders**, **Catalyst** (18-week incubation), **Velocity Labs**.
**Davos**: CM announced a **₹50 crore** entrepreneurship fund (20 Jan 2026).

67.s: The States’ Startup Ranking Framework of DPIIT primarily promotes:
o: Allocation of all start-up funds exclusively to one state
Direct ranking of individual start-up founders by personal income
Competitive federalism by assessing state start-up policies and their implementation
Assessment of only the number of unicorns in each district
67.x: The framework promotes competitive federalism by assessing the policies adopted by states and their implementation for start-up development.
67.tq: Identify the framework’s purpose rather than a narrow output indicator.
xs: The framework promotes **competitive federalism** by assessing **state start-up policies and implementation** — option **(3)**.
It is run by **DPIIT** and ranks states, not founders or districts.
xa: Categories: **Best Performers, Top Performers, Leaders, Aspiring Leaders, Emerging Start-up Ecosystems**.
AP was **No. 1 in the National States Startup Ranking 2022**.
AP was **9th in the India Innovation Index 2022**.

67.s: According to the stated States’ Startup Ranking 2022 and India Innovation Index 2022 positions, Andhra Pradesh was:
o: No. 1 in the States’ Startup Ranking and 9th in the India Innovation Index
9th in the States’ Startup Ranking and No. 1 in the India Innovation Index
67.x: Andhra Pradesh was ranked No. 1 in the States’ Startup Ranking 2022 and 9th in the India Innovation Index 2022.
67.tq: Keep the two rankings separate and avoid reversing their positions.
xs: AP was **No. 1 in the States' Startup Ranking 2022** and **9th in the India Innovation Index 2022** — option **(1)**.
The States' Startup Ranking is conducted by **DPIIT**.
xa: AP has **50** incubators — the **7th largest** start-up infrastructure.
**6,935** start-ups in AP (FY 2024-25), of which **2,493 (36%)** DPIIT-recognised.
AP's nodal agency: **AP Innovation Society (APIS)**.

67.s: Which one of the following is NOT mentioned as a criticism or debate concerning the start-up ecosystem?
o: Banks being risk-averse to first-generation borrowers
67.x: High start-up mortality, thin late-stage capital and bank risk aversion are identified concerns. Excessive availability of late-stage capital is not; the concern is its thinness.
67.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated trend or criticism.
xs: **Excessive availability of late-stage capital** is NOT a listed criticism — option **(3)**.
The actual concern is the opposite: **thin late-stage capital**.
Other listed criticisms: **banks risk-averse** to first-generation borrowers and **high start-up mortality**.
xa: Tech start-ups raised **$9.1 bn in 2025**, up **23%**.
**CGSS** offers collateral-free loans to ease credit access (max **₹20 crore**).
**Fund of Funds 2.0** adds ₹10,000 crore for **deep tech, space, AI**.

67.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Stand-Up India from MUDRA in terms of loan coverage?
o: Stand-Up India: up to ₹20 lakh; MUDRA: ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore
Stand-Up India: ₹20 lakh to ₹1 crore; MUDRA: up to ₹5 lakh
Stand-Up India: up to ₹10 lakh; MUDRA: above ₹1 crore
Stand-Up India: ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore; MUDRA: up to ₹20 lakh under Tarun Plus
67.x: Stand-Up India covers loans from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore, while MUDRA covers micro units up to ₹20 lakh under Tarun Plus.
67.tq: Split the options by scheme and verify both loan ranges together.
xs: **Stand-Up India: ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore; MUDRA: up to ₹20 lakh** under **Tarun Plus** — option **(4)**.
Stand-Up India targets **SC/ST and women** entrepreneurs.
**MUDRA** covers **micro units**.
xa: Stand-Up loans cover up to **85%** of project cost; repayment up to **7 years**.
Stand-Up India was launched on **5 April 2016** by the **Ministry of Finance**.
Norm: at least **one SC/ST and one woman borrower per bank branch**.

68.s: The Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Policy was announced in April 2000 through which policy framework?
68.x: The SEZ Policy was announced in April 2000 through the EXIM Policy 2000-01.
68.tq: Identify the policy framework associated with the announcement year.
xs: The SEZ Policy of **April 2000** was announced through the **EXIM Policy 2000-01** — option **(3)**.
This was the APPSC-GS **2025** key.
Sequence: Policy **2000** → **SEZ Act 2005** → Act and Rules in force **10 Feb 2006**.
xa: Before SEZs came **EPZs** from **1965**, Kandla being the first.
APPSC-G1 2018 treated the policy as "announced" in **both 2000 and 2006**.
**SEZ (Amendment) Rules 2025** cut minimum land for semiconductor SEZs from **50 ha to 10 ha**.

68.s: A principal institutional feature introduced under the SEZ framework is:
o: Mandatory clearance only through the Reserve Bank of India
Single-window clearance for Central and State matters
Separate customs clearance for every unit
68.x: The SEZ framework provides single-window clearance for matters involving both the Central and State Governments.
68.tq: Match the institutional mechanism with its practical administrative purpose.
xs: The SEZ framework gives **single-window clearance for Central and State matters** — option **(3)**.
This came with the SEZ Act and **SEZ Rules** in force from **10 Feb 2006**.
xa: SEZ proposals go via the **State** to the **Board of Approval**.
SEZs can be set up **jointly or severally** by the Centre, a State or **any person**.
**100% FDI** is allowed under the automatic route for most manufacturing in SEZs.

68.s: Which of the following is the correct description of a free trade zone?
o: An area reserved exclusively for agricultural exports
An area where goods may be landed, stored, processed and re-exported without customs duty
An area where imported goods must be consumed before re-export
An area where only domestically produced goods may be sold without State taxes
68.x: A free trade zone permits goods to be landed, stored, processed and re-exported without payment of customs duty.
68.tq: Apply the operational definition by checking all four permitted activities.
xs: A **free trade zone** is an area where goods may be **landed, stored, processed and re-exported without customs duty** — option **(2)**.
No restriction to agricultural exports or to domestic consumption is part of the definition.
xa: **Kandla (Gujarat)** was India's **first Free Trade Zone** and **Asia's first EPZ** (**1965**).
Existing **EPZs** and **EOUs** could convert into SEZs.
An SEZ may also serve as a **Free Trade Warehousing Zone**.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
68.x: Falta is an Export Processing Zone in West Bengal. SEEPZ is located in Santacruz, Mumbai, while MEPZ is associated with Chennai.
68.tq: Use location-based elimination among similar-sounding export-processing zones.
xs: **Falta — West Bengal** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**SEEPZ** (Santacruz Electronics EPZ) is in **Mumbai**, not Chennai.
**MEPZ** is in **Chennai**, not Cochin; **Noida** EPZ is not in Gujarat.
xa: ⚠ **Kandla** = first EPZ (Gujarat); **Falta** = West Bengal; **SEEPZ** = Mumbai.
Falta was the **UPPSC 2023** key.
Other EPZs: **Cochin** and **Visakhapatnam**.

68.s: With the SEZ framework in force from 2006, which existing units were allowed to convert into Special Economic Zones?
o: Export Processing Zones and Export Oriented Units
National Investment and Manufacturing Zones and Coastal Economic Zones
Industrial corridors and industrial smart cities
68.x: Existing EPZs and EOUs could convert into SEZs (Kandla, for example, became an SEZ). NIMZs and CEZs are later, separate concepts; corridors and smart cities are not SEZ conversions; FTWZs are a type of SEZ purpose, not a unit that converts.
68.tq: EPZ/EOU → SEZ.
xs: Existing **Export Processing Zones** and **Export Oriented Units** could convert into SEZs — option **(1)**.
**Kandla**, for instance, began as an EPZ and later became an SEZ.
**Coastal Economic Zones** are a separate **Sagarmala** concept, and industrial corridors are not SEZ conversions.
xa: A **Free Trade Warehousing Zone** is one of the purposes an SEZ may serve.
SEZ Act and Rules in force from **10 Feb 2006**.
EPZs had existed from **1965**.

68.s:
An SEZ may be set up by which of the following combinations?
1. Central Government
2. State Government
3. Private persons
4. Joint-sector entities
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
68.x: SEZs may be established jointly or severally by the Central Government, State Government or any person, including public, private and joint-sector entities.
68.tq: Use an inclusive list and test whether the extreme restriction that excludes private or joint-sector entities is justified.
xs: All four — **Centre, State, private persons, joint sector** — may set up an SEZ — option **(3)**.
SEZs may be set up **jointly or severally** by the Central Government, State Government or **any person** (public, private, joint sector).
xa: SEZs under the Act are **mainly private**.
Purpose: manufacturing, services, or a **Free Trade Warehousing Zone**.
Proposals go via the **State** to the **Board of Approval**.

68.s: Proposals for setting up SEZs are routed through the State Government to which body for approval?
68.x: Proposals for SEZs are routed through the State Government to the Board of Approval.
68.tq: Identify the specific approving body rather than a neighbouring economic institution.
xs: SEZ proposals go through the State to the **Board of Approval** — option **(2)**.
The SEZ framework provides **single-window clearance** for Central and State matters.
xa: Developers: Centre, State or **any person**, **jointly or severally**.
⚠ Trap: SEZs are set up primarily for **exports**, not employment (APPSC-G2 **2017** key).
**s.18** of the SEZ Act allows an **IFSC** in an SEZ.

68.s:
With reference to an International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) in an SEZ, consider the following statements:
1. Section 18 of the SEZ Act allows an IFSC in an SEZ.
2. More than one IFSC may be established in the same SEZ under the stated provision.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
68.x: Section 18 allows an IFSC in an SEZ, but only one IFSC is permitted per SEZ.
68.tq: Test the statutory permission together with its numerical limitation.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Section 18** allows an **IFSC** in an SEZ.
Statement 2 wrong: only **one IFSC per SEZ** is permitted.
xa: The **Baba Kalyani Committee** (2018) suggested a **unified IFSC regulator**.
**100% FDI** under the automatic route for most manufacturing in SEZs.

68.s:
Consider the following statements about tax benefits for SEZ units under Section 10AA of the SEZ Act:
1. Eligible units get 100% income-tax exemption for the first five years.
2. For the next five years, the exemption is 50%.
3. The SEZ tax holidays were phased out during 2010-2013 under a sunset clause.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
68.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: s.10AA gives 100% exemption for 5 years, then 50% for the next 5 (and 50% of reinvested profit for 5 more). Statement 3 is wrong: the tax holidays were phased out during 2017-2020, not 2010-2013. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, while the options with 3 are wrong.
68.tq: Remember the 5-5-5 ladder (100% / 50% / 50% of reinvested profit) and the 2017-2020 sunset.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **s.10AA** gives **100%** income-tax exemption for the first **5** years.
Statement 2 correct: **50%** for the next **5** years.
Statement 3 wrong: tax holidays were phased out during **2017-2020** (sunset clause), not 2010-2013.
xa: A further **50%** of **reinvested profit** is exempt for **5** more years.
⚠ **s.10AA** = tax holiday; **s.18** = IFSC.
The **Baba Kalyani Committee** recommended **extending the sunset clause**.

68.s: Special Economic Zones in India are set up primarily to:
o: Raise tax revenue for State Governments
68.x: An SEZ is an export-oriented enclave; its primary aim is exports. Employment is a benefit but 'primarily to generate employment' was the wrong option in the APPSC-G2 2017 key. Raising State revenue or giving land to farmers is not its purpose.
68.tq: SEZ primary aim = exports, not jobs.
xs: SEZs are set up primarily to **promote exports** — option **(2)**.
⚠ "Primarily to **generate employment**" is NOT true — the **APPSC-G2 2017** key.
Raising State revenue or giving land to landless farmers is not their purpose; land acquisition is in fact a criticism.
xa: SEZ exports FY 2024-25: **₹14,63,669 crore (~US$173 bn)**, **~21%** of India's exports.
SEZs employ **31,77,893** people in **6,695** units.
The **Baba Kalyani Committee** proposed renaming SEZs **"Employment and Economic Enclaves"**.

68.s: Which one of the following was identified as a criticism of the performance of SEZs?
o: SEZs received more than half of total foreign direct investment.
Domestic tariff area sales were completely unrestricted.
SEZs received less than 3% of foreign direct investment.
No SEZ units were shut during the five-year period.
68.x: SEZs received less than 3% of FDI. Other criticisms included capped DTA sales and the closure of many units.
68.tq: Select the qualified performance criticism and reject reversed or absolute statements.
xs: A criticism is that SEZs received **less than 3% of FDI** — option **(3)**.
**DTA sales** were **capped**, not unrestricted.
**466 units shut** in five years across seven SEZs (**100** in FY25), so option (4) is false.
xa: Export growth was **<4%** in FY25.
Other criticisms: land acquisition (**Nandigram**), revenue loss, under-used land, **WTO**-inconsistent subsidies.
Scale: **6,695** units, investment **₹7,82,192 crore**.

68.s: The Baba Kalyani Committee, constituted in 2018, recommended renaming SEZs as:
68.x: The committee recommended renaming SEZs as 3Es—Employment and Economic Enclaves.
68.tq: Discriminate among closely similar expansions of an official abbreviation.
xs: The **Baba Kalyani Committee** (2018) proposed renaming SEZs **"3Es" — Employment and Economic Enclaves** — option **(3)**.
It also called for separate rules for **manufacturing and services**.
xa: Other recommendations: **extend the sunset clause** and a **unified IFSC regulator**.
The **DESH Bill** (Budget 2022-23) proposes to replace the SEZ Act.
DESH = **Development of Enterprise and Services Hubs**.

68.s:
Which of the following changes is associated with the proposed DESH Bill?
1. Removal of the positive Net Foreign Exchange condition
2. Permission for Domestic Tariff Area sales
3. Immediate replacement of the SEZ Act through an enacted law
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
68.x: The DESH proposal removes the positive NFE condition and allows DTA sales. It remains pending and has not immediately replaced the SEZ Act.
68.tq: Separate proposed provisions from the legal status of a Bill that is still pending.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: DESH **removes the positive NFE** condition.
Statement 2 correct: it **allows DTA sales**.
Statement 3 wrong: the Bill is **still pending**, so it has not replaced the SEZ Act.
xa: DESH was announced in **Budget 2022-23**.
Current SEZ rule: DTA sales are **capped**; concessional SEZ-to-DTA sales allowed from **Apr 2026**.
**Baba Kalyani Committee** (2018) earlier proposed the **"3Es"** rename.

68.s: The Nandigram protests of 2007 were associated with opposition to land acquisition for a:
o: Free Trade Warehousing Zone at Kandla
68.x: Nandigram in West Bengal witnessed violent protests in 2007 against land acquisition for a chemical-hub SEZ.
68.tq: Link the place and year to the specific project that triggered the conflict.
xs: Nandigram (**West Bengal, 2007**) saw protests against land acquisition for a **chemical-hub SEZ** — option **(2)**.
The protests were **violent**, making Nandigram the symbol of SEZ land disputes.
xa: Other criticisms: **revenue loss**, **under-used land**, **WTO**-inconsistent export subsidies.
**466 units shut** in five years across seven SEZs.
⚠ **Falta** EPZ is also in **West Bengal**.

68.s: Which department and ministry are associated with NICDC?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Department of Heavy Industry, Ministry of Steel

68.tq: Identify the correct ministry and department rather than a neighbouring authority.
xs: Industrial corridors (NICDC) come under **DPIIT**, **Ministry of Commerce and Industry** — option **(1)**.
The apex trust funding the nodes is **NICDIT** (**₹3,000 crore** BE **2026-27**).
xa: **NICDC** implements **BHAVYA** (₹33,660 crore, FY27-FY32).
Operational smart cities: **Dholera** (Gujarat) and **Shendra-Bidkin** (Maharashtra).
AP nodes: **Orvakal** (HBIC) and **Kopparthy** (VCIC).

68.s: Which pair of operational greenfield industrial smart cities is correctly matched with its State?
68.x: The operational cities identified are Dholera in Gujarat and Shendra-Bidkin in Maharashtra.
68.tq: Start from the sure location pair in a location-based matching question.
xs: **Dholera — Gujarat** and **Shendra-Bidkin — Maharashtra** — option **(1)**.
Both are **operational** industrial smart cities with **₹2.02 lakh crore** investment.
xa: AP smart city nodes: **Orvakal** (Kurnool, HBIC) and **Kopparthy** (Kadapa, VCIC).

68.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Industrial city)
 a. Orvakal
 b. Kopparthy
 c. Krishnapatnam

List-II (Corridor)

xs: **Orvakal — HBIC**, **Kopparthy — VCIC**, Krishnapatnam — CBIC: **a-iii, b-i, c-ii** — option **(2)**.
**Orvakal** is in **Kurnool** on the **HBIC**; **Kopparthy** is in **Kadapa** on the **VCIC**.
xa: Orvakal: **2,621 acres**, **₹1,781 crore**.
Kopparthy: **2,596 acres**, **₹1,264 crore**.
⚠ **Orvakal** = HBIC (Kurnool); **Kopparthy** = VCIC (Kadapa).
**VCIC 2035** targets: manufacturing output **₹4.20 trillion**, **33%** women, **24x7** power.

68.s:
Consider the following statements about BHAVYA:
1. It has an allocation of ₹33,660 crore.
2. It covers FY27–FY32.
3. It aims to establish 100 plug-and-play industrial parks.
4. It is implemented by NICDC through an SPV of NICDIT and a State agency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: All four statements correctly describe BHAVYA: its ₹33,660 crore allocation, FY27–FY32 period, 100 parks and implementation structure.
68.tq: Test a complete scheme profile through an all-statements option.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**BHAVYA**: **₹33,660 crore**, covering **FY27-FY32**.
Aims at **100 plug-and-play industrial parks**.
Implemented by **NICDC**; SPV of **NICDIT** + State agency.
xa: BHAVYA parks portal was launched on **9 Jun 2026**.
NICDIT gets **₹3,000 crore** in BE **2026-27**.
Corridors come under **DPIIT**, Ministry of Commerce & Industry.

68.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Coastal Economic Zones:
1. They involve industrial clusters and SEZs near ports.
2. Fourteen Coastal Economic Zones were identified.
3. Their concept is linked with port-led industrialisation under Sagarmala.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: All three statements are correct: CEZs involve port-proximate industrial clusters and SEZs, 14 were identified, and they were proposed under Sagarmala's port-led industrialisation pillar.

xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
CEZs are **industrial clusters and SEZs near ports**.
**14 CEZs** were identified.
They come from **Sagarmala**'s National Perspective Plan (**2016**) under its **port-led industrialisation** pillar.

**BHAVYA** (2026) separately plans **100** plug-and-play industrial parks.

68.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or debate concerning SEZs and industrial policy?
o: Land acquisition, including the Nandigram controversy
Guaranteed expansion of employment in every notified SEZ
68.x: Land acquisition, revenue loss, under-used land and WTO-inconsistent export subsidies are identified criticisms. Guaranteed employment expansion in every SEZ is not listed as a criticism.
68.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated criticism set.
xs: **Guaranteed expansion of employment in every SEZ** is NOT a listed criticism — option **(4)**.
Listed criticisms: **land acquisition** (**Nandigram**), **revenue loss**, **under-used land**, **WTO**-inconsistent export subsidies.
xa: Slowdown: **466 units shut** in five years; export growth **<4%** in FY25.
SEZs get **<3%** of FDI.
⚠ SEZs are primarily for **exports**, not employment (APPSC-G2 2017 key).

68.s: The criticism that SEZ incentives may be WTO-inconsistent relates primarily to:
68.x: One criticism is that export subsidies associated with SEZs may be inconsistent with WTO obligations.
68.tq: Match the international trade concern with its precise subject.
xs: The WTO-inconsistency criticism concerns **export subsidies** — option **(3)**.
It is listed with **land acquisition**, **revenue loss** and **under-used land**.
xa: SEZ tax holidays (**s.10AA**) were phased out **2017-2020** under a sunset clause.
The **DESH Bill** removes the positive **NFE** condition.
**Nandigram** (2007) is the land-acquisition example.

68.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) India's first EPZ
(b) First private-sector EPZ
(c) Conversion of Surat EPZ into SEZ
(d) SEZ Act and Rules came into effect

List-II
(i) November 1st, 2000
(ii) February 10th, 2006
(iii) Kandla, Gujarat
(iv) Surat
68.x: Kandla (Gujarat) was India's first EPZ, Surat the first private-sector EPZ, Surat EPZ became an SEZ on 1 November 2000, and the SEZ Act and Rules took effect on 10 February 2006. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
68.tq: Match each first to its place or date.
n: The SEZ Act and Rules came into effect on February 10, 2006. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
Kandla, Gujarat, had India's first Export Processing Zone (EPZ). [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
Surat had India's first private-sector Export Processing Zone (EPZ). [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
The Surat EPZ was converted into an SEZ on November 1, 2000. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
Kandla, Gujarat, had Asia's first Export Processing Zone (EPZ). [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]

68.s:

68.x: The order is the SEZ policy (1 April 2000), the Act passed by Parliament (May 2005), Presidential assent (23 June 2005), and the Act in force (10 February 2006). The answer is B, D, C, A.
68.tq: Arrange the SEZ steps in time order.

The SEZ Act was passed by Parliament in 2005. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]

The SEZ Act and Rules came into effect on February 10, 2006. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
