78.x: Railway operations are prohibited except for permitted activities, but railway infrastructure is included among sectors permitting 100% automatic FDI. Lottery business, chit funds and atomic energy are prohibited sectors.
78.tq: Separate a prohibited activity from a permitted infrastructure activity.
xs: **Railway infrastructure** is a **100% automatic** sector, not prohibited — option **(4)**.
**Lottery**, **chit funds** and **atomic energy** are prohibited.
xa: ⚠ **Railway operations** (other than permitted activities) are prohibited — not railway infrastructure.
Other prohibited: **gambling and betting (incl. casinos)**, **Nidhi companies**, **trading in TDRs**.
Also prohibited: **real estate business and farmhouses**; **cigars/cigarettes of tobacco**.
Civil aviation **MRO** and **ports** are also **100% automatic**.

78.s:
Consider the following activities:
1. Trading in transferable development rights
2. Manufacture of cigars and cigarettes containing tobacco
3. Railway operations, except permitted activities
4. Real-estate business and construction of farmhouses
Which of the above are prohibited sectors for FDI?
78.x: Trading in TDRs, manufacture of tobacco cigars or cigarettes, prohibited railway operations, and real-estate business or farmhouses are all included in the prohibited list.
78.tq: Test the complete prohibited-sector list by grouping related activities.
xs: All four — **TDR trading**, **tobacco cigars/cigarettes**, **railway operations** (except permitted) and **real estate/farmhouses** — are prohibited: **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(3)**.
Railway **operations** are barred only "other than permitted activities" — still on the prohibited list.
xa: Other prohibited sectors: **lottery**, **gambling and betting (incl. casinos)**, **chit funds**, **Nidhi companies**, **atomic energy**.
⚠ **Construction and real-estate broking** is **100% automatic** — unlike the real estate business.
**Railway infrastructure** is **100% automatic**.

78.s: Which one of the following sectoral FDI combinations is correctly stated?
o: Defence — 100% automatic route without any government route
78.x: Telecom permits 100% FDI through the automatic route. Multi-brand retail is limited to 51% under the government route, single-brand retail allows 100% automatic FDI, and defence has 74% automatic FDI with government approval possible beyond that up to 100%.
78.tq: Compare the sectoral cap and route together, not the percentage alone.
xs: **Telecom** permits **100% FDI automatic** — option **(3)**.
**Single-brand retail** is **100% automatic** (not 51%); **multi-brand retail** is **51% Government route**.
**Defence** is **74%** automatic, up to **100%** Government route.
xa: **Insurance**: **100% automatic** (Budget **2025-26**).
Exam angle: "**multi-brand retail cap**" — **51%**.
Multi-brand retail is in practice treated as **barred** (**Jul 2026**).

78.s:
Which of the following sectors permits 100% automatic FDI according to the stated policy?
1. Medical devices
2. NBFCs
3. Construction and real-estate broking
4. Single-brand retail
Select the correct answer using the code below.
78.x: Medical devices, NBFCs, construction and real-estate broking, and single-brand retail are all listed as permitting 100% automatic FDI.
78.tq: Use the sector-list completeness test for 100% automatic categories.
xs: **Medical devices**, **NBFCs**, **construction and real-estate broking** and **single-brand retail** are all **100% automatic** — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
None of the four needs **Government route** approval.
xa: Other **100% automatic**: **telecom**, civil aviation **MRO**, **ports**, **railway infrastructure**.
⚠ **Multi-brand retail** is **51%**, Government route.
⚠ **Food products made in India** trading: **100%**, but **Government route**.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the evolution of the FDI limit in the insurance sector?
78.x: The insurance FDI limit progressed from 26% to 49% in 2015, 74% in 2021 and 100% in 2025. The 100% limit is subject to the stated regulatory condition.
78.tq: Arrange successive policy revisions by year and verify the increasing limits.
xs: Insurance FDI was **26% initially**, then **49% in 2015**, **74% in 2021** and **100% in 2025** — option **(2)**.
The other options misplace the years against the limits.
xa: **100%** is **automatic**, subject to **IRDAI**, on condition that the **entire premium** is invested in India.
It was announced in Union Budget **2025-26** and enabled via the **FEMA (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019**.
Insurance = **Entry 47, Union List**; IRDAI HQ **Hyderabad**.

78.s: The 100% FDI limit in insurance was enabled by amending the:
78.x: The 100% insurance FDI limit was enabled through an amendment to the FEMA (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019.
78.tq: Identify the correct legal instrument rather than the sector regulator.
xs: **100%** insurance FDI was enabled by amending the **FEMA (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019** — option **(1)**.
The **SEBI (FPI) Regulations 2019** govern **FPIs**, not insurance FDI.
xa: Announced in Union Budget **2025-26**; condition: **entire premium invested in India**.
Subject to **IRDAI** (HQ **Hyderabad**).

78.s: Insurance is listed as Entry 47 in the:
78.x: Insurance is Entry 47 of the Union List. The headquarters of IRDAI is located in Hyderabad.
78.tq: Use the constitutional-list classification to eliminate neighbouring lists.
xs: **Insurance** is **Entry 47** of the **Union List** — option **(2)**.
So it is not a **State**, **Concurrent** or residuary subject; the Centre legislates on it.
xa: **IRDAI** is headquartered in **Hyderabad**.
Insurance FDI: **100%, automatic** (Budget **2025-26**).
Condition: the **entire premium** must be invested in India.

78.s: With reference to foreign direct investment in the defence sector of India, which of the following is correct?
o: 100% is permitted under the automatic route without sectoral conditions
20% is permitted only through the Government route
49% is permitted under the automatic route and up to 74% through the Government route
74% is permitted under the automatic route and up to 100% through the Government route
78.x: FDI up to 74% in defence is permitted through the automatic route, while investment up to 100% may be allowed through the Government route.
78.tq: Check the sectoral cap and distinguish the automatic route from the Government route.
xs: **Defence**: **74%** **automatic**, up to **100%** via **Government route** — option **(4)**.
**100%** is not fully automatic; **20%** Government route is the **public sector bank** limit; **49%** is the automatic slab in **private banks**.
xa: Post-**2014** caps were raised in **defence**, **insurance**, **pension**.
Government route covers "defence **beyond 74%**".
**Space**: up to **100%** with sectoral conditions.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding FDI in the banking sector:
1. Foreign investment in private-sector banks is permitted up to 74%.
2. In private-sector banks, investment up to 49% is permitted through the automatic route.
3. Foreign investment in public-sector banks is permitted up to 20% through the Government route.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct. The private-bank cap is 74%, with 49% under the automatic route, whereas public-sector banks have a 20% Government-route limit.
78.tq: Split the options by identifying the separate caps and routes for private and public-sector banks.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **private-sector banks** — **74%**.
Statement 2 is correct: **49% automatic**, beyond via **Government route**.
Statement 3 is correct: **public sector banks** — **20%**, Government route — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: The private-bank cap was raised to **74%** in **2004**.
Private banks illustrate "**automatic up to a cap, approval beyond**".
**NBFCs** are **100% automatic**.

78.s:
With reference to FDI in civil aviation, consider the following statements:
1. Scheduled air transport services permit up to 100% foreign investment.
2. Investment up to 49% is permitted through the automatic route, with investment beyond that requiring the Government route.
3. For NRIs, 100% investment is permitted through the automatic route.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct for scheduled air transport services. The 100% automatic treatment applies specifically to NRIs, while investment beyond 49% for other investors requires the Government route.
78.tq: Separate the general route from the special treatment applicable to NRIs.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **scheduled air transport** allows up to **100%**.
Statement 2 is correct: **49% automatic**, beyond via **Government route**.
Statement 3 is correct: **NRIs** get **100% automatic** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: ⚠ Notes that say "**100% automatic**" for aviation are true **only for NRIs**.
Civil aviation **MRO** is a **100% automatic** sector.
**Telecom** is **100% automatic**.

78.s: FDI in trading, including e-commerce, of food products manufactured or produced in India is permitted up to:
78.x: Trading, including e-commerce, of food products made in India permits 100% FDI through the Government route.
78.tq: Test the difference between a 100% cap and the route through which it is permitted.
xs: Trading (incl. **e-commerce**) of **food products made in India** permits **100%** via the **Government route** — option **(1)**.
It is **100%** but not automatic — prior approval is needed.
xa: ⚠ E-commerce **marketplace** model is **100% automatic**; the **inventory** model is barred (except for **exports**, **Jul 2026**).
**Multi-brand retail**: **51%**, Government route.
**Single-brand retail**: **100% automatic**.

78.s: Which one of the following sectors permits up to 100% FDI subject to sectoral conditions rather than an unconditional automatic route?
78.x: The space sector permits up to 100% FDI subject to sectoral conditions. The other options have different specified caps or routes.
78.tq: Use the qualifying phrase ‘subject to sectoral conditions’ to identify the exact policy category.
xs: **Space** allows up to **100%** FDI **with sectoral conditions** — option **(3)**.
**Public sector banks** are **20%** Government route; **defence** is **74%** automatic; **multi-brand retail** is **51%** Government route.
xa: Government route sectors include **satellites**, **broadcasting**, **print media**.
**Atomic energy** is a **prohibited** sector.
Defence beyond **74%** up to **100%** needs Government approval.

78.s:
Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the broad FDI categories based on approval and sectoral limits?
1. 100% automatic sectors
2. Government route up to 100%
3. Automatic route up to a cap, with approval required beyond the cap
4. Fixed-cap sectors only
Select the correct answer.
78.x: All four categories are valid: (1) 100% automatic sectors such as civil aviation MRO, ports and railway infrastructure; (2) Government-route sectors with varying caps, such as multi-brand retail, satellites, broadcasting and print media; (3) automatic up to a cap with approval beyond, such as private banks; and (4) fixed-cap-only sectors.
78.tq: Check whether the option includes the complete classification rather than a partial list.
xs: All four categories exist — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
(1) **100% automatic**: civil aviation **MRO**, **ports**, **railway infrastructure**.
(2) **Government route** (caps vary): multi-brand retail up to **51%**, satellites, broadcasting, print media; (3) automatic up to a cap: **private banks**; (4) **fixed cap only**.
xa: More than **90% of sectors** are automatic (**negative list**).
Private banks: **49%** automatic, up to **74%** via Government route.
Prohibited sectors form a separate list — e.g. **lottery**, **atomic energy**.

78.s: The FDI limit and route for multi-brand retail trading in India is:
78.x: Multi-brand retail allows up to 51% FDI only through the Government route (in practice treated as barred). 100% automatic applies to single-brand retail, telecom and e-commerce marketplaces; 74% automatic is the defence limit; 49% automatic is the automatic slab within the private-bank and scheduled-airline caps.
78.tq: Multi-brand 51% (Govt); single-brand 100% (auto).
xs: **Multi-brand retail**: **51%**, **Government route** — option **(3)**.
**100% automatic** is single-brand retail/telecom; **74% automatic** is defence; **49% automatic** is the private-bank/airline automatic slab.
xa: In practice multi-brand retail is treated as **barred** (**TH, Jul 2026**).
Exam angle: "**multi-brand retail cap**" — **51%**.
The **inventory e-commerce** ban also keeps the multi-brand retail curbs.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about FDI in insurance:
1. 100% FDI in insurance was announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, on the condition that the entire premium is invested in India.
2. The headquarters of IRDAI is in Hyderabad.
3. Insurance is a subject in the Concurrent List.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Statement 1 is correct: Budget 2025-26 raised the insurance FDI limit to 100% (automatic, subject to IRDAI), on the condition that the entire premium is invested in India. Statement 2 is correct: IRDAI is headquartered in Hyderabad. Statement 3 is wrong: insurance is Entry 47 of the Union List. So '1 and 2 only'.
78.tq: Insurance: 100% (Budget 2025-26), Union List Entry 47, IRDAI Hyderabad.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Budget **2025-26** announced **100%** insurance FDI, on condition the **entire premium is invested in India**.
Statement 2 is correct: **IRDAI** HQ is **Hyderabad**.
Statement 3 is wrong: insurance is **Entry 47, Union List** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Enabled by amending the **FEMA (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019**.
⚠ CDI dates it to Budget **2026-27**, but the PYQ confirms **2025-26**.

78.s:
With reference to Press Note 3 of 2020, consider the following statements:
1. It required Government approval for FDI from countries sharing a land border with India.
2. It was issued in April 2020.
3. It was introduced partly to prevent opportunistic takeovers during the COVID-19 period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct. Press Note 3, issued in April 2020, required Government approval for FDI from land-border countries and sought to prevent opportunistic takeovers during the COVID-19 period.
78.tq: Check the policy requirement, issue date and stated purpose as separate components.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Press Note 3** required **government approval** for FDI from any **land-border** country.
Statement 2 is correct: it was issued in **April 2020**.
Statement 3 is correct: its purpose was to **stop opportunistic takeovers during Covid** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: It did not name **China** but covered it.
**Amended March 2026**, effective **1 May 2026**: up to **10%** Chinese/HK beneficial ownership may use the **automatic route**.
Response: **29 projects worth ₹4,895.65 crore** by **Aug 2026**.

78.s: Which of the following countries was included among the countries sharing a land border with India whose FDI was covered by Press Note 3 of 2020?
78.x: The countries listed were China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan and Afghanistan. Sri Lanka, Thailand and Maldives were not part of that stated land-border list.
78.tq: Test membership in the named list rather than relying on regional proximity.
xs: **Bhutan** is one of the **land-border** countries covered by **Press Note 3** — option **(2)**.
The list: **China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan, Afghanistan**.
xa: PN3 (**April 2020**) requires **government approval** for all FDI from these countries.
Purpose: stop **opportunistic takeovers** during **Covid**.
**Beneficial owner** is defined as per the **PML Rules, 2005**.

78.s: Under the March 2026 amendment to Press Note 3, which one of the following entities may invest through the automatic route from 1 May 2026, subject to the stated condition?
o: Any company registered in China with up to 10% Chinese ownership
A foreign firm with Chinese or Hong Kong beneficial ownership of up to 10%, provided it is not registered in China, Hong Kong or another land-border country
Any entity registered in a land-border country without Government approval
A company registered in Hong Kong with beneficial ownership exceeding 10%
78.x: From 1 May 2026, foreign firms with Chinese or Hong Kong beneficial ownership up to 10% may use the automatic route, but entities registered in China, Hong Kong or another land-border country remain excluded. Beneficial ownership is defined under the PML Rules, 2005.
78.tq: Separate beneficial ownership from place of registration and apply both conditions together.
xs: From **1 May 2026**, firms with up to **10%** **Chinese/Hong Kong beneficial ownership** may use the **automatic route**, if **not registered** in China, HK or another land-border country — option **(2)**.
Entities **registered in China, HK** or other land-border countries remain excluded.
xa: The amendment was approved by the **Cabinet** in **March 2026**.
**Beneficial owner** is defined as per the **PML Rules, 2005**.
Response: **29 projects worth ₹4,895.65 crore** by **Aug 2026**.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India's FY 2024-25 FDI position?
o: Gross FDI was $94.6 billion and net FDI was $44 billion.
Gross FDI was $81 billion and net FDI was only $353 million.
Gross FDI was $23.6 billion and net FDI was $7.6 billion.
Gross FDI was $353 million and net FDI was $81 billion.
78.x: India recorded gross FDI of $81 billion in FY 2024-25, while net FDI was only $353 million.
78.tq: Distinguish gross inflows from net inflows rather than treating them as interchangeable.
xs: **FY 2024-25**: gross FDI **$81 billion** (**+14%**), but net FDI only **$353 million** — option **(2)**.
**$94.6 bn** is the record gross for **FY26**; **$44.0 bn** the net peak of **2020-21**; **$23.6 bn** is **ODI** in FY25.
xa: Top sources FY 2024-25: **Singapore (30%)**, **Mauritius (17%)**, **US (11%)**.
Services sector was the top recipient.

78.s: The three leading sources of FDI in India during FY 2024-25, in descending order, were:
o: Singapore, Mauritius and the United States
The United States, Japan and the Netherlands
Singapore, Japan and the United Arab Emirates
78.x: Singapore contributed 30%, Mauritius 17% and the United States 11% of FDI in FY 2024-25.
78.tq: Arrange the source countries by their stated shares, not by general economic size.
xs: FY 2024-25 top sources: **Singapore (30%)**, **Mauritius (17%)**, **US (11%)** — option **(1)**.
**Japan**, **Netherlands** and the **UAE** were not in FY 2024-25's top three.
xa: **FY26** (RBI) order: **Singapore, US, Mauritius, Japan, Netherlands**.
⚠ Earlier **FY23**: **Mauritius 26%**, **Singapore 23%**.
**April 2026**: **>75%** of inflows came from **Japan, Singapore, Mauritius**.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about FDI during FY 2025-26:
1. Gross FDI during April-February was $88.3 billion.
2. Gross FDI during April-February increased by 18.1%.
3. Manufacturing, computer, financial, business and communication services together received over two-thirds of equity inflows.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three are correct. In April-February FY 2025-26 gross FDI was $88.3 billion, up 18.1%; and for FY26 manufacturing, computer, financial, business and communication services together took over two-thirds of equity inflows.
78.tq: Verify the amount, growth rate and sectoral composition separately before choosing the combined code.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: gross FDI was **$88.3 bn in Apr-Feb** FY 2025-26.
Statement 2 is correct: up **18.1%**.
Statement 3 is correct: **manufacturing, computer, financial, business, communication services** took over **two-thirds** of equity inflows — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Net FDI was **negative for five straight months** (**Sep 2025-Jan 2026**) due to repatriation + **ODI**.
Full-year gross FDI FY26: a record **$94.6 bn**; net only **$7.6 bn**.
**Feb 2026**: net FDI **+$4.6 bn**, first positive after **6 months**.

78.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, services accounted for what share of FDI during FY 2023-FY 2025?
78.x: Services accounted for 80.2% of FDI during FY 2023-FY 2025. Information and communication alone accounted for 25.8%.
78.tq: Distinguish the aggregate services share from the narrower information-and-communication share.
xs: Per **ES 2025-26**, **services** took **80.2%** of FDI in **FY23-FY25** — option **(4)**.
**25.8%** is the share of **information and communication** alone.
xa: Global FDI fell **11%** in **2024**; India stayed the largest FDI recipient in **South Asia**.
**WIR 2026**: global FDI rose **6%** to **$1.6 trillion** in **2025**; **US** the largest recipient and source.
⚠ Manufacturing's share of effective inflows fell to **10.6%** (**2026**).

78.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with India's outward FDI in FY 2025?
o: $23.6 billion — Singapore, the United States and the UAE among the leading destinations
$9.4 billion — Japan, Mauritius and the Netherlands among the leading destinations
$44 billion — China, Germany and France among the leading destinations
$81 billion — Singapore, Australia and Canada among the leading destinations
78.x: Outward FDI was $23.6 billion in FY 2025, with Singapore, the United States and the UAE among the leading destinations.
78.tq: Match the outward-flow amount with its leading destination countries.
xs: Outward FDI (**ODI**) was **$23.6 bn in FY25**, top destinations **Singapore**, **US**, **UAE** — option **(1)**.
**$9.4 bn** is **Karnataka**'s H1 FY26 FDI; **$44 bn** is the net FDI peak (**2020-21**); **$81 bn** is FY25 gross FDI.
xa: ODI is one reason **net FDI** is weak.
Others: **profit repatriation** and **PE/VC exits** via IPOs.
Net FDI was **$353 million** in FY 2024-25.

78.s: Which statement best explains why net FDI may remain weak even when gross FDI inflows are high?
o: Net FDI is always lower because services are excluded from it.
Profit repatriation, outward FDI by Indian firms and private-equity or venture-capital exits reduce the net figure.
Net FDI excludes all equity investment by foreign companies.
Gross FDI is calculated only after deducting imports.
78.x: Net FDI is reduced by profit repatriation, outward FDI by Indian firms and PE/VC exits through mechanisms such as IPOs.
78.tq: Apply the gross-versus-net distinction to the flow components that raise or reduce the net value.
xs: Net FDI is cut by **profit repatriation**, **outward FDI by Indian firms** and **PE/VC exits** via IPOs — option **(2)**.
These outflows are subtracted from gross inflows, so a big gross can coexist with a tiny net.
xa: **ODI** was **$23.6 bn in FY25** (top: **Singapore**, **US**, **UAE**).
About **$40 bn** of **2014-26** equity "inflows" were **accounting changes**, not fresh capital.
FY26: record gross **$94.6 bn** but net only **$7.6 bn**.
Gross vs net FDI is debated between the **CEA** and critics.

78.s: Which of the following correctly represents the FDI figures cited for FY 2025-26?
o: Gross FDI was $23.6 billion, while net FDI was $9.4 billion.
Gross FDI was $88.3 billion, while net FDI was $44 billion.
Gross FDI was $94.6 billion, while net FDI was $7.6 billion.
Gross FDI was $81 billion, while net FDI was $353 million.
78.x: The cited FY 2025-26 table gives record gross FDI of $94.6 billion and net FDI of $7.6 billion. Net FDI had fallen below $1 billion in FY 2024-25 after peaking at $44 billion in 2020-21.
78.tq: Separate the record gross figure from the distinct net-FDI series across financial years.
xs: **FY 2025-26**: record gross FDI **$94.6 billion**, but **net FDI** only **$7.6 billion** — option **(3)**.
**$81 bn / $353 million** are **FY 2024-25**; **$88.3 bn** is only the **Apr-Feb** gross; **$44 bn** was the **2020-21** net peak.
xa: **$23.6 bn** is **ODI in FY25**; **$9.4 bn** is **Karnataka**'s H1 FY26 FDI.
Net FDI was **negative for five straight months** (**Sep 2025-Jan 2026**) due to repatriation + **ODI**.
**Feb 2026**: net FDI **+$4.6 bn**, first positive after **6 months**.
**April 2026**: gross **$15.3 bn**, net **$6.6 bn** — highest in nearly **5 years**.

78.s: The peak net FDI recorded in the cited series was:
78.x: Net FDI peaked at $44.0 billion in 2020-21, before falling below $1 billion in 2024-25 and recovering to $7.6 billion in 2025-26.
78.tq: Distinguish the peak net-flow figure from gross-FDI records and later recovery values.
xs: Net FDI peaked at **$44.0 billion in 2020-21** — option **(1)**.
It then fell **under $1 bn** (**2024-25**) and recovered to **$7.6 bn** (**2025-26**); **$94.6 bn** is FY26 **gross**, not net.
xa: **$23.6 bn** is outward FDI (**ODI**) in **FY25**.
FY 2024-25 net FDI: only **$353 million** against gross **$81 billion**.
Weak net FDI: **profit repatriation**, **ODI**, **PE/VC exits** via IPOs.

78.s: The UNCTAD World Investment Report 2026 stated that global foreign direct investment in 2025:
o: rose by 6 per cent to $1.6 trillion
rose by 10.6 per cent to $560 billion
fell by 6 per cent to $1.6 trillion
78.x: According to the UNCTAD World Investment Report 2026, global FDI rose by 6 per cent to $1.6 trillion in 2025.
78.tq: Keep the direction of change, percentage and aggregate value together.
xs: **WIR 2026 (UNCTAD)**: global FDI **rose 6% to $1.6 trillion in 2025** — option **(1)**.
**10.6%** is manufacturing's share of effective inflows (**2026**); **$560 bn** is India's **2014-26** equity inflows; **$94.6 bn** is India's FY26 gross FDI.

78.s: With reference to limits applicable to Foreign Portfolio Investors in government securities, which one of the following is correct?
o: 2% of outstanding Central Government securities and 6% of outstanding State Government securities under the General Route
10% of outstanding Central Government securities and 5% of outstanding State Government securities under the General Route
6% of outstanding Central Government securities and 2% of outstanding State Government securities under the General Route
6% of outstanding Central Government securities and 6% of outstanding State Government securities under the General Route
78.x: Under the General Route, the overall FPI limit is 6% of outstanding Central Government securities and 2% of outstanding State Government securities. Security-wise and short-term limits have been removed.
78.tq: Use the paired percentages and avoid reversing the Central and State figures.
xs: **General Route** FPI limits: **6%** of outstanding **Central G-secs** and **2%** of **State securities** — option **(3)**.
Option (1) swaps the two figures.
xa: **Security-wise and short-term limits** have been removed.
**VRR** (Voluntary Retention Route) and **FAR** (Fully Accessible Route) steadied debt flows.
The **JP Morgan EM bond index** inclusion (**10%** target weight) draws passive bond inflows.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about recent FPI flows and their determinants:
1. FPI flows are influenced significantly by US Federal Reserve interest rates and global risk appetite.
2. A flight to safety may lead to FPI outflows from India.
3. Domestic fundamentals are identified as the sole determinant of FPI flows.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. FPI flows are strongly affected by US interest rates and global risk sentiment, and a flight to safety can cause outflows; domestic fundamentals are not the sole determinant.
78.tq: Reject the extreme word 'sole' when the material identifies multiple external drivers.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: FPI flows are driven by **US Fed/interest rates** and **global risk appetite**.
Statement 2 is correct: a "**flight to safety**" causes outflows.
Statement 3 is wrong: flows depend on global factors, **not domestic fundamentals** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: FY26 FPI outflows: about **Rs 2.2 lakh crore**.
Outflows were a key cause of **rupee weakness** — past **96/$** in **May 2026**.
FPI is "**hot money**" — short-term and liquid.

78.s:
With reference to FPI flows in FY 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The reported overall FPI outflow was about ₹2.2 lakh crore.
2. Net FPI outflow in March 2026 was reported at 13.6 billion US dollars.
3. FPI outflows pushed the rupee beyond ₹96 per US dollar in May 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct: the FY26 outflow was about ₹2.2 lakh crore, March 2026 recorded a net outflow of $13.6 billion, and the rupee crossed ₹96 per US dollar in May 2026 amid the outflows.
78.tq: Retain the different units—rupees, dollars and exchange rate—while checking each statement independently.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: FY26 FPI outflows were about **Rs 2.2 lakh crore**.
Statement 2 is correct: net FPI outflow of **$13.6 bn in March 2026**.
Statement 3 is correct: outflows pushed the **rupee past 96/$** in **May 2026** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Over **₹2 lakh crore** was withdrawn from **equities** by **May 2026** (**₹24,829 crore** in May alone).
Drivers: **US Fed** rates and global risk appetite.
Debt stabilisers: **VRR** and **FAR**.

78.s: India's inclusion in the JP Morgan Emerging Market bond index is expected to have which of the following effects?
o: It shifts all FPI investment from equities to State securities
It fixes the exchange rate of the rupee at a predetermined level
It attracts passive bond inflows through a target weight of 10%
It prohibits foreign investment in Indian government securities
78.x: India's inclusion in the JP Morgan Emerging Market bond index, with a target weight of 10%, is expected to draw passive bond inflows.
78.tq: Link index inclusion with the passive investment flows it mechanically generates.
xs: Inclusion in the **JP Morgan EM bond index** (**10% target weight**) **attracts passive bond inflows** — option **(3)**.
It does not fix the rupee, ban G-sec investment or shift equity money into State securities.
xa: FPI G-sec limits: **6%** Central, **2%** State (General Route).
**VRR** and **FAR** routes steadied debt flows.
Rupee weakness in **May 2026** (past **96/$**) came from FPI **equity** outflows.

78.s: Which of the following correctly gives the order of the top three states by FDI during the first half of FY 2025-26?

xs: **H1 FY26**: **Maharashtra** first, **Karnataka** (**$9.4 bn**) second, **Tamil Nadu** (**$3.6 bn**) third — option **(1)**.

xa: **FY23** (older): **Maharashtra 29%**, **Karnataka 24%**, **Gujarat 17%**, **Delhi 13%**, **Tamil Nadu 5%**.

78.s: Why did India opt out of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership in 2019?
o: A prohibition on all Indian exports to Australia and New Zealand
The requirement that India withdraw from the World Trade Organization
Concerns regarding China's market dominance, a widening trade deficit with China, and risks to farm, dairy and small industries
The absence of any ASEAN country from the proposed partnership
78.x: India withdrew over concerns about China's market dominance, the rise in its trade deficit with China, and possible adverse effects on agriculture, dairy and small industries. The deficit rose from $53.5 billion in 2018–19 to $99.2 billion in 2024–25.
78.tq: Identify the option that combines the stated market, trade-deficit and domestic-industry concerns.
xs: India **opted out of RCEP in 2019** over **China's market dominance**, a widening **deficit with China**, and protection for **farm/dairy and small industry** — option **(3)**.
The stated reasons are only these two — **China's dominance** and **protection concerns**; the other options are not among them.
xa: The deficit with China rose from **$53.5 bn** (**2018-19**) to **$99.2 bn** (**2024-25**).
**Press Note 3** (**April 2020**) later required approval for FDI from land-border countries incl. **China**.
The **UK CETA** came into force on **15 Jul 2026**.

78.s: The trade deficit between India and China mentioned in the context of India's RCEP withdrawal increased from approximately what amount in 2018–19 to what amount in 2024–25?
78.x: The India-China trade deficit increased from $53.5 billion in 2018–19 to $99.2 billion in 2024–25, strengthening concerns associated with joining RCEP.
78.tq: Read the two-year sequence carefully and avoid changing either the starting or ending figure.
xs: India's deficit with China rose from **$53.5 billion** (**2018-19**) to **$99.2 billion** (**2024-25**) — option **(3)**.
Option (4) has the right start but the wrong end figure.
xa: This **China dominance** fear was why India **opted out of RCEP in 2019**.
Other RCEP concern: protecting **farm/dairy** and **small industry**.
**PN3** (**2020**) put Chinese FDI on the **Government route**; the **March 2026** amendment allowed up to **10%** via the automatic route.

Statement 3 is correct: FDI **brings technology and jobs**.
Statement 4 is wrong: gross FDI mixes fresh capital with **accounting changes** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: About **$40 bn** of **$560 bn** equity inflows (**2014-15** to **2025-26**) were accounting changes.

78.s: The debate concerning gross and net FDI in India has involved the Chief Economic Adviser and critics primarily because:
o: net FDI excludes all foreign equity inflows
gross FDI may include accounting changes and therefore may not reflect fresh capital fully
manufacturing FDI is always higher than services FDI
gross FDI and net FDI always represent identical flows
78.x: The debate arises because gross FDI can include accounting changes, whereas the amount of fresh capital may be considerably lower, as reflected in the difference between gross and net figures.
78.tq: Apply the gross-versus-net distinction to the stated policy debate.
xs: **Gross FDI** may include **accounting changes**, so it does not fully reflect **fresh capital** — option **(2)**.
About **$40 bn** of **$560 bn** equity inflows (**2014-15** to **2025-26**) were accounting changes, fuelling the **CEA vs critics** debate.
xa: Net FDI also falls due to **profit repatriation**, **ODI** and **PE/VC exits**.
**Manufacturing**'s share of effective inflows fell to **10.6%** (**2026**).
⚠ **ES 2025-26**: **services** took **80.2%** of FDI in **FY23-FY25** — far above manufacturing.
