106.tq: Start from the distinctive content of the macroeconomic and expenditure statements, then eliminate the remaining codes.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Macro-Economic Framework Statement** → GDP growth, inflation, external balance, assumptions and risks (iii).
**Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement** → **3-year rolling targets** (iv); **Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement** → tax, expenditure, borrowing and debt strategy (ii).
**Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement** → 3-year expenditure projections/ceilings (i).
xa: All four are laid under **Section 3** of the Act in **Parliament**.
The **MTEFS** was added by the **2012** amendment and is laid **after the Budget**.
MTFPS indicators: **RD, FD, tax revenue** and **total outstanding liabilities**.

106.s:
The Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement contains three-year rolling targets for which of the following?
1. Revenue deficit
2. Fiscal deficit
3. Tax revenue or tax-GDP indicator
4. Total outstanding liabilities
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
106.x: The Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement covers four rolling indicators: revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, tax-related revenue or tax-GDP indicator, and total outstanding liabilities as percentages of GDP.
106.tq: Count the complete set of indicators rather than treating the tax-GDP indicator as a legal deficit target.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — option **(4)**.
The **Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement** gives **three-year rolling targets** for **RD, FD, tax revenue** (tax-GDP) and **total outstanding liabilities** as % of GDP.
Only these targets are rolling; the **tax-GDP ratio** is projected here but is not a legal target.
xa: MTFPS rolling targets have been **suspended since 2021-22** for post-pandemic flexibility.
**Budget 2026-27** laid a combined **MTFPS cum FPSS** with the **MEFS**.
The **Macro-Economic Framework Statement** covers growth, inflation, external balance and risks.

106.s: The three-year rolling fiscal targets under the FRBM framework were suspended from 2021-22 mainly to provide:
o: A constitutional basis for State borrowing
A permanent exemption from fiscal reporting
Automatic permission for unlimited off-budget borrowing
106.x: Three-year rolling targets were suspended from 2021-22 to provide flexibility in the post-pandemic period.
106.tq: Link the suspension year with its stated policy purpose.
xs: The rolling targets were suspended from **2021-22** for **post-pandemic flexibility** — option **(4)**.
MTFPS three-year rolling targets have **not been given since 2021-22**.
They are still suspended as of **Budget 2026-27**.
xa: COVID year **2020-21**: FD peaked at **9.2% of GDP**; the escape clause was used without a fresh amendment.
The **2025-26** FD target "below **4.5%**" (set in FY 2021-22) was met at **4.4%**.
Budget 2026-27 shifted to a **debt-GDP rule** (**50 ± 1% by 2031**).

106.s: The additional guarantees issued against the Consolidated Fund in a year are capped at:
106.x: Additional guarantees against the Consolidated Fund are capped at 0.5% of GDP in a year.
106.tq: Recall the annual ceiling and avoid confusing it with the fiscal-deficit target.
xs: Additional guarantees against the **Consolidated Fund** are capped at **0.50% of GDP** a year — option **(2)**.
This cap is part of what FRBM **prescribes**, along with deficit limits and transparency disclosures.
⚠ **3%** is the FD target; **0.25%** is the buoyancy-clause FD cut — not the guarantee cap.
xa: Escape-clause deviation is also capped at **0.5% of GDP** in a year.
The Act has **no penal provisions** for missing targets.
Buoyancy clause: FD must fall by **at least 0.25% of GDP** when growth rises sharply.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the Task Force on Implementation of the FRBM Act, 2004:
1. It was chaired by Vijay Kelkar.
2. It recommended meeting FRBM targets mainly through tax reform - widening the base and a comprehensive GST.
3. Its chairman later headed the Fourteenth Finance Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is correct: Vijay Kelkar chaired the 2004 Task Force. Statement 2 is correct: it recommended tax reform, a wider base and a comprehensive GST. Statement 3 is wrong: Kelkar chaired the Thirteenth Finance Commission (2010-15), not the Fourteenth. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
106.tq: Kelkar 2004 = implement FRBM via tax reform/GST; 13th FC. N.K. Singh 2016-17 = review, debt anchor.

106.s: The recommendations of the N.K. Singh FRBM Review Committee were reflected in which Union Budget?
106.x: The committee was announced in Budget 2016-17, and its recommendations were reflected in Budget 2017-18.
106.tq: Separate the announcement of a committee from the later Budget reflecting its recommendations.
xs: The N.K. Singh Committee's recommendations were reflected in **Budget 2017-18** — option **(3)**.
The committee was announced in **Budget 2016-17**, constituted in **2016**, and reported in **2017**.
The **2018 amendment** later wrote its **debt anchor** and **escape clause** into the Act.
xa: It recommended **FD 3% of GDP** for the next three years, then a lower glide path.
Escape clause: deviation up to **0.5% of GDP** on defined grounds.
APPSC-G2 2017 asked the head of the FRBM review panel = **N.K. Singh**.

106.s:
Consider the following recommendations of the N.K. Singh FRBM Review Committee:
1. Debt-to-GDP should be the principal fiscal anchor, with the fiscal deficit as the operational target.
2. General government debt should be brought to 60% of GDP by 2023.
3. The general government debt limit should be split as Centre 50% and States 10% of GDP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is correct: debt-to-GDP is the principal anchor and FD the operational target. Statement 2 is correct: general government debt 60% of GDP by 2023. Statement 3 is wrong: the split was Centre 40% + States 20%. So '1 only' misses 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' accept the wrong split; the answer is 1 and 2 only.
106.tq: 60 = 40 (Centre) + 20 (States); debt is the anchor, FD the operational target.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **debt-to-GDP** is the principal anchor; **FD** is the operational target.
Statement 2 is correct: general government debt **60% of GDP by 2023**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the split was **Centre 40% + States 20%**, not 50/10.
xa: Other recommendations: **FD 3% of GDP** for three years; **RD 0.8% of GDP by 2023**; an independent advisory **Fiscal Council**.
⚠ The new 2026-27 debt rule targets Central debt of **50 ± 1%** by **2031** — above FRBM's **40%**.
The **2018 amendment** set general govt **60%**, Centre **40%** by **31 March 2025**.

106.s: The Fiscal Council recommended by the N.K. Singh Committee was envisaged as:
o: A parliamentary committee with executive powers
A department of the Reserve Bank of India
A constitutional court with binding adjudicatory powers
106.x: The proposed Fiscal Council was an independent, advisory institution rather than a body with binding executive or judicial powers.
106.tq: Identify the body's character by checking both its independence and its advisory nature.
xs: The **Fiscal Council** was envisaged as an **independent, advisory** body — option **(3)**.
It was one of the **N.K. Singh Committee** (**2016-17**) recommendations.
Critics note FRBM still has **no independent fiscal council** yet.
xa: The committee made **debt** the principal anchor: general govt **60% of GDP by 2023** (Centre **40%** + States **20%**).
It also recommended an escape clause with deviation up to **0.5% of GDP**.
Another design gap critics cite: **no penalty clause**.

106.s: The debt anchor and escape-clause recommendations of the N.K. Singh Committee were incorporated into the FRBM Act through which amendment?
106.x: The committee's debt anchor and escape clause were written into the FRBM Act through the 2018 amendment.
106.tq: Match the substantive institutional change with the later amendment, not the amendment that added expenditure projections.
xs: The debt anchor and escape clause were written into the Act by the **2018 amendment** — option **(1)**.
2018 also set **FD 3% by 31 March 2021**, dropped RD/ERD targets and added a **buoyancy clause**.
**2012** added ERD and the MTEFS; **2015** deferred target dates — neither brought the debt anchor.
xa: 2018 debt anchor: general govt **60%**, Centre **40%** by **31 March 2025**.
The escape-clause deviation is capped at **0.5% of GDP**.
The Act is now cited as "**FRBM Act, 2003 (amended 2018)**".

106.s: The 2018 amendment to the FRBM framework envisaged which combination of targets?
o: Fiscal deficit of 3% by 31 March 2021, general government debt of 60% and Central debt of 40% by 31 March 2025
Fiscal deficit of 3% by 31 March 2018 and Central debt of 50% by 2025
Fiscal deficit of 4.5% by 31 March 2025, general government debt of 50% and Central debt of 30% by 2031
Revenue deficit of zero and Central debt of 60% by 31 March 2021
106.x: The 2018 amendment set a 3% fiscal-deficit target by 31 March 2021 and debt anchors of 60% for general government and 40% for the Centre by 31 March 2025.
106.tq: Combine the year, date and multiple numerical targets without swapping their deadlines.
xs: The 2018 amendment set **FD 3% by 31 March 2021**, general govt debt **60%** and Central debt **40% by 31 March 2025** — option **(1)**.
It also dropped RD/ERD targets and added an **escape clause** (**0.5%** cap) and a **buoyancy clause**.
The **50%** Central debt by **2031** figure belongs to the new **2026-27** debt rule, not the 2018 amendment.
xa: The Government has acknowledged **deviation** from the Act's **3% FD** and **40% Central debt** targets.
COVID **2020-21**: FD **9.2%**; escape clause used, no amendment.

106.s:
Arrange the following FRBM developments in chronological order:
A. Targets suspended after the global financial crisis
B. Effective revenue-deficit target and Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement added
C. FRBM Rules notified and annual reduction targets introduced
D. Debt anchor, escape clause and buoyancy clause introduced through amendment
106.x: The sequence is 2004 Rules, 2008-09 suspension, 2012 additions, and 2018 amendment introducing the debt anchor and clauses.
106.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the 2008-09 and 2012 developments.
xs: Order: **C, A, B, D** — option **(1)**.
C: **2004** — FRBM Rules notified with annual reduction targets.
A: **2008-09** — targets suspended after the **global financial crisis**; B: **2012** — **ERD** and **MTEFS** added.
D: **2018** — **debt anchor**, escape clause and buoyancy clause.
xa: **2015**: target dates deferred (FD 3% by 2017-18).
**2020-21**: escape clause used for COVID; no amendment, to keep flexibility.
Rules in force from **5 July 2004**; Act enacted **2003**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements regarding deviations from fiscal targets:
1. The targets were suspended during the 2008 global financial crisis to permit fiscal stimulus.
2. During COVID-19 in 2020–21, the fiscal deficit was recorded at 9.2 per cent of GDP.
3. After COVID-19, the targets were recalibrated with a gradual return path.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: All three statements are correct. Fiscal targets were suspended during the global financial crisis, the COVID-19 fiscal deficit reached 9.2 per cent of GDP in 2020–21, and a gradual return path was adopted thereafter.
106.tq: Check each episode separately before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: targets were suspended after the **2008 global financial crisis** for stimulus.
Statement 2: COVID **2020-21** FD was **9.2% of GDP** (BPSC 2023).
Statement 3: targets were **recalibrated with a gradual return path**.
xa: The commitment to halve the 2020-21 FD in five years was met: **4.4% in 2025-26**.
In **2020-21** the escape clause was used with no amendment, to keep flexibility.

106.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated ground for invoking the escape clause under the FRBM framework?
o: A routine shortfall in tax collection caused by administrative delay
A sharp fall in real output growth
106.x: The stated grounds include national security, war, national calamity, agricultural collapse, structural reforms with unforeseen fiscal effects and a sharp fall in real output growth. A routine administrative tax-collection delay is not listed.
106.tq: Find the exceptional, economy-wide grounds and reject an ordinary administrative shortfall.
xs: A **routine shortfall in tax collection caused by administrative delay** is NOT a ground — option **(2)**.
Grounds: **national security, war, national calamity**; **collapse of agriculture**; **structural reforms** with unanticipated fiscal effects.
Also a **sharp fall in real output growth** — **3 percentage points** below the previous four quarters' average.
xa: Deviation limit: **not more than 0.5% of GDP** in a year.
The government must justify the deviation and give a return path, placed before **Parliament**.
⚠ Escape clause = deviation up to **0.5%**; buoyancy clause = FD cut of at least **0.25%**.

106.s: A sharp fall in real output growth is treated as a trigger for the escape clause when real output growth falls by:
o: 1 percentage point below the average of the previous four quarters
3 percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters
5 percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters
2 percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters
106.x: One escape-clause trigger is a fall in real output growth by 3 percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters.
106.tq: Read the threshold together with its comparison base: the average of the previous four quarters.
xs: The trigger is a fall of **3 percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters** — option **(2)**.
This "severe slowdown" ground came with the **2018 amendment**.
Other grounds: **national security, war, national calamity**, collapse of agriculture, **structural reforms**.
xa: Deviation under the escape clause: **not more than 0.5% of GDP** in a year.
Buoyancy clause: if growth rises sharply, FD must fall by **at least 0.25% of GDP**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the FRBM escape clause:
1. The permitted deviation from the fiscal-deficit target must not exceed 1% of GDP in a year.
2. The Government must justify the deviation and place a path back to the target before Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the deviation is capped at not more than 0.5% of GDP in a year. Statement 2 is correct: the Government must justify the deviation and give a path back to the target, placed before Parliament. Hence '2 only'.
106.tq: Escape clause = up to 0.5%; buoyancy clause = cut of at least 0.25%.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the buoyancy clause:
1. It is associated with the 2018 FRBM amendment.
2. If real output growth rises sharply, the fiscal deficit must fall by at least 0.25% of GDP.
3. It permits the fiscal deficit to rise by 0.5% of GDP whenever growth accelerates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The buoyancy clause requires a reduction in the fiscal deficit when real output growth rises sharply; it does not permit an automatic increase.
106.tq: Separate the direction of fiscal adjustment from the escape-clause deviation limit.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **buoyancy clause** came with the **2018** amendment.
Statement 2 is correct: if real output growth rises sharply, **FD must fall by at least 0.25% of GDP**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the buoyancy clause forces a cut; the **0.5%** deviation belongs to the **escape clause**.
xa: ⚠ Escape clause = deviation up to **0.5%**; buoyancy clause = FD cut of at least **0.25%**.
2018 also set the **debt anchor**: general govt **60%**, Centre **40%** by **31 March 2025**.

106.s: Which of the following best describes the Government’s formal position regarding the FRBM targets?
o: It has replaced the 3% fiscal-deficit target with a zero revenue-deficit target by law.
It has achieved both targets and withdrawn the deviation statement.
It has formally acknowledged deviation from the 3% fiscal-deficit and 40% Central-debt targets.
It has repealed both the 3% fiscal-deficit and 40% Central-debt targets.
106.x: The Government has formally acknowledged deviation from the Act’s 3% fiscal-deficit and 40% Central-debt targets through the FRBM deviation statement.
106.tq: Distinguish acknowledgement of deviation from repeal or achievement of a target.
xs: The Government has **formally acknowledged deviation from the 3% FD and 40% Central-debt targets** — option **(3)**.
This is done through the **FRBM deviation statement**.
The targets came from the **2018 amendment**: **FD 3% by 31 March 2021**; Central debt **40% by 31 March 2025**.
xa: New rule from **2026-27**: Central debt **50 ± 1% of GDP by 31 March 2031** — above FRBM's **40%**.
The halving commitment was met: **9.2%** (2020-21) to **4.4%** (2025-26), not a legislative target.

106.s: Which one of the following correctly states the fiscal-deficit recommendations associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Centre 3.5% of GDP and States 3% of GSDP by 2030-31
Centre 4.3% of GDP and States 3% of GSDP by 2026-27
Centre 3.5% of GDP and States 4% of GSDP by 2030-31
Centre 3% of GDP and States 3.5% of GSDP by 2030-31
106.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended that the Centre reach a fiscal deficit of 3.5% of GDP and States reach 3% of GSDP by 2030-31.
106.tq: Keep the Centre and State limits separate before comparing the two figures.
xs: The **16th FC**: Centre FD **3.5% of GDP** and States **3% of GSDP** by **2030-31** — option **(1)**.
**4.3%** is the Centre's FD in **2026-27 BE**, not an FC recommendation.
**4%** of GSDP was the **15th FC** State borrowing limit for **2021-22**.
xa: The 16th FC also asked for State fiscal-rule reform and a wider deficit definition covering **off-budget borrowing**.
It found State fiscal rules "**effectively unenforced**".
⚠ FRBM 2018 target for the Centre was **3%**; the 16th FC path is **3.5%** by 2030-31.

106.s: The commitment to halve the 2020-21 fiscal deficit within five years was fulfilled when the fiscal deficit reached:
106.x: The 2020-21 fiscal deficit of 9.2% was more than halved to 4.4% in 2025-26. This was a commitment, not a legislative target.
106.tq: Calculate the direction of change while retaining the distinction between a commitment and a statutory target.
xs: The halving commitment was met when FD reached **4.4% of GDP in 2025-26** — option **(3)**.
**2020-21** FD was **9.2%**; halving it in five years was a commitment, **not a legislative target**.
xa: The **2025-26** target "below **4.5%**" (set in FY 2021-22) was met.
The **16th FC** path: Centre FD **3.5% of GDP by 2030-31**.

106.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act is correct?
o: It was enacted in 2004 and prohibits all open-market borrowing by the State.
It was enacted in 2009 and targets a revenue surplus of 3% of GSDP.
It was enacted in 2005 and targets elimination of revenue deficit and fiscal deficit of 3% of GSDP.
It was enacted in 2018 and fixes fiscal deficit at 5% of GSDP.
106.x: The Andhra Pradesh FRBM Act was enacted in 2005. Its objectives include eliminating the revenue deficit and limiting the fiscal deficit to 3% of GSDP.
106.tq: Pair the State law with its year and two principal fiscal objectives.
xs: The **AP FRBM Act, 2005** targets **elimination of the revenue deficit** and **FD of 3% of GSDP** — option **(3)**.
Its full name is the **Andhra Pradesh Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2005** (some notes say **2009**).
It restrains, but does not prohibit, AP's **open-market borrowing** — so option (1) is wrong.
xa: It has been amended from time to time to match **Finance Commission** borrowing limits.
**AP BE 2026-27**: FD **3.84%**, RD **1.11%** of GSDP — above the **3%** norm.
Slippage: FD **5.05%** vs mandated **4%** ceiling; borrowings **₹81,071 crore**.

106.s: State fiscal responsibility legislation was promoted after the Twelfth Finance Commission because debt relief was linked to:
o: The Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility
The Goods and Services Tax Compensation Fund
106.x: The Twelfth Finance Commission linked debt relief for States to the enactment of fiscal responsibility legislation through the Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility.
106.tq: Identify the specific facility associated with the debt-relief incentive.
xs: The **12th FC** tied debt relief to the **Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility** — option **(1)**.
States enacted Fiscal Responsibility Legislation mostly after this link.
Several States passed FRBM Acts on the **central model**; AP's came in **2005**.
xa: AP FRBM Act targets: eliminate RD, **FD 3% of GSDP**.
The central FRBM Act does **not apply to States**.
**16th FC** found State fiscal rules "**effectively unenforced**".

106.s: The fiscal responsibility limits under the Andhra Pradesh FRBM framework primarily constrain the State’s:
106.x: The FRBM limits restrain Andhra Pradesh’s open-market borrowing by imposing fiscal and borrowing discipline.
106.tq: Ask which financial activity is directly controlled by a State fiscal rule.
xs: AP FRBM limits restrain the State's **open-market borrowing** — option **(2)**.
The **AP FRBM Act, 2005** targets RD elimination and **FD at 3% of GSDP**.
It is amended from time to time to match **Finance Commission** borrowing limits.
xa: Slippage: borrowings **₹81,071 crore**; FD **5.05%** vs **4%** ceiling (7 Mar 2026).

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sixteenth Finance Commission and State fiscal rules:
1. It asked for State fiscal-rule reform with a wider deficit definition covering off-budget borrowing.
2. It found State fiscal rules to be 'effectively unenforced'.
3. The Union promptly amended the fiscal responsibility legislation to implement this.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the 16th FC asked for State fiscal-rule reform and a wider deficit definition covering off-budget borrowing, and called State fiscal rules 'effectively unenforced'. Statement 3 is wrong: the Union deferred amending the fiscal responsibility legislation. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
106.tq: 16th FC proposed; Union deferred.

106.s:
With reference to the Fifteenth Finance Commission's net borrowing limits for States, consider the following statements:
1. The limit was 4% of GSDP in 2021-22.
2. The limit was 3% of GSDP in 2022-23.
3. The limit was 3% of GSDP from 2023-24 to 2025-26, plus 0.5% linked to power-sector reforms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is correct: 4% of GSDP in 2021-22. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2022-23 limit was 3.5%, not 3%. Statement 3 is correct: 3% for 2023-24 to 2025-26, with an extra 0.5% linked to power-sector reforms. So '1 only' misses 3, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' accept the wrong 2022-23 figure; the answer is 1 and 3 only.
106.tq: Step down 4 -> 3.5 -> 3, plus 0.5 for power reforms.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **4%** of GSDP in **2021-22**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **2022-23** limit was **3.5%**, not 3%.
Statement 3 is correct: **3%** for **2023-24 to 2025-26**, plus **0.5%** linked to power-sector reforms.
xa: FRBM limits restrain AP's **open-market borrowing**.
AP slippage: FD **5.05%** vs mandated **4%** ceiling (7 Mar 2026).
**16th FC**: States **3% of GSDP** by **2030-31**.

106.s: Which one of the following best expresses the significance of the FRBM framework?
o: It abolished the requirement of presenting the Budget to Parliament.
It made monetary policy a function of the Finance Commission.
It transferred the power of taxation entirely to the States.
It made fiscal discipline a legal duty and created disclosure statements accompanying the Budget.
106.x: The FRBM framework gave fiscal discipline a legal basis and established disclosure statements as part of the Budget process.
106.tq: Select the option stating both linked institutional consequences.
xs: FRBM **made fiscal discipline a legal duty and created disclosure statements accompanying the Budget** — option **(4)**.
The statements: **MEFS**, **MTFPS**, **FPSS**, **MTEFS** — laid in **Parliament**.
It also requires transparency disclosures on **borrowings** and **contingent liabilities**.
xa: Criticism: frequent **escape-clause** use and repeated target deferrals.
Design gaps: **no penalty clause**; no independent **fiscal council** yet.
Current relevance: Budget 2026-27 switched to a debt-GDP rule (**50 ± 1% by 2031**).

106.s: Which one of the following is identified as a criticism of the operation of the FRBM framework?
o: The framework imposes automatic penalties for every deviation.
The framework prohibits any deviation during crises.
An independent fiscal council is already fully operational.
Frequent use of the escape clause and repeated deferral of targets weaken credibility.
106.x: Frequent use of the escape clause and repeated postponement of targets are criticised for weakening the credibility of the fiscal framework. There is also no independent fiscal council yet.
106.tq: Find the option that states the recognised criticism rather than an institutional opposite.
xs: **Frequent use of the escape clause and repeated deferral of targets** is the criticism — option **(4)**.
Critics say FRBM targets were **missed repeatedly**, weakening credibility.
Option (3) is wrong: there is **no independent fiscal council yet**; option (1) is wrong: there is **no penalty clause**.
xa: The new rule **tolerates higher debt** than FRBM's **40%** Central-debt target.
Budget 2026-27 (**1 Feb 2026**) switched to a debt-GDP rule (**50 ± 1% by 2031**); rolling FD targets still suspended.
**FY27 FD** reached **26.8%** of target by July (1 Sep 2026).

106.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the newer debt anchor and the earlier FRBM framework:
1. The newer rule targets debt of 50 ± 1 per cent of GDP by 2031.
2. The new rule is criticised for tolerating a higher debt level than the 40 per cent level associated with FRBM.
3. The FRBM framework has been criticised because its targets have been missed repeatedly and it contains no penalty clause.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: All three statements are correct. The new debt anchor is 50 ± 1 per cent by 2031, higher than the 40 per cent level associated with FRBM, while repeated misses and the absence of a penalty clause remain criticisms.
106.tq: Combine the new rule with two distinct criticisms of the earlier framework.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: the new rule targets Central debt of **50 ± 1% of GDP by 31 March 2031**.
Statement 2: it **tolerates higher debt** than FRBM's **40%** Central-debt target.
Statement 3: FRBM targets were **missed repeatedly** and the Act has **no penalty clause**.
xa: Central debt in **BE 2026-27**: **55.6%** of GDP; FD **4.3%**.
Under the new rule, **debt**, not FD, is the primary target.
Experts want a published debt and FD glide path with a **nominal GDP** assumption (5 Feb 2026).

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first Budget in India was presented in 1860 by James Wilson.
2. The first Budget of free India was presented in 1947 by Vijay Kelkar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is correct: James Wilson presented India's first Budget in 1860. Statement 2 is wrong: the first Budget of free India (1947) was presented by R.K. Shanmukham Chetty; Vijay Kelkar chaired the FRBM Task Force and the 13th Finance Commission. So only 1 is correct; 'Both' and '2 only' accept the wrong name and 'Neither' rejects the true statement.
106.tq: 1860 Wilson; 1947 Shanmukham Chetty; Kelkar is a distractor.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: India's first Budget was presented in **1860** by **James Wilson**.
Statement 2 is wrong: free India's first Budget (**1947**) was by **R.K. Shanmugham Chetty**, not Vijay Kelkar.
xa: **Vijay Kelkar** chaired the **Task Force on Implementation of the FRBM Act, 2004** and the **13th Finance Commission** (**2010-15**).
The FRBM Act was introduced by **Yashwant Sinha** and enacted in **2003**.
FRBM Rules came into force on **5 July 2004**.

106.s:
Assertion (A): The main aim of the FRBM Act is to promote fiscal discipline and fiscal prudence.
Reason (R): Its main focus includes reducing the fiscal deficit, revenue deficit and public debt.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
106.x: Both are true: the FRBM Act aims at fiscal discipline, and it does so by cutting the fiscal deficit, revenue deficit and public debt. R explains A.
106.tq: Ask whether the targets explain the aim.
n: The aim of the FRBM Act is fiscal discipline. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-32]
The aim of the FRBM Act is fiscal prudence. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-32]
The main focus of the FRBM Act is to reduce the fiscal deficit. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-32]
The main focus of the FRBM Act is to reduce the revenue deficit. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-32]
The main focus of the FRBM Act is to reduce public debt. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-32]
Discipline in public finances is an objective of the FRBM Act. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-32]
Strengthening fiscal prudence is an objective of the FRBM Act. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-32]

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the FRBM Review Committee:
I. It was formed in May 2016.
II. N.K. Singh was its Chairman.
III. It submitted its report in January 2017.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: All three are correct: the FRBM Review Committee was set up in May 2016 under N.K. Singh and reported in January 2017.
106.tq: Recall the N.K. Singh Committee.
n: The FRBM Review Committee was formed in May 2016. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-32]
N.K. Singh was the chairman of the FRBM Review Committee. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-32]
The FRBM Review Committee submitted its report in January 2017. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-32]
The N.K. Singh Committee is the FRBM Review Committee. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-32]

107.s: Which of the following statements about the Union Budget changes associated with the end of Plan and non-Plan classification is correct?
o: The Railway Budget was abolished and the Budget was presented on 15 August.
The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget and the Budget was presented on 31 March.
The Railway Budget was separated and the Budget was presented on 1 April.
The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget and the Budget was presented on 1 February.
107.x: The relevant Budget changes included the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget and presentation of the Union Budget on 1 February.
107.tq: Pair the two associated procedural changes instead of selecting only one of them.
xs: In **2017** the **Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget** and the Budget moved to **1 February** — option **(4)**.
The **plan/non-plan distinction** was removed in the same Budget, **2017-18**.
Before 2017 the Budget was presented on the **last working day of February**.
xa: ⚠ **2017** = three changes together: **Railway merger** + **1 February** date + **plan/non-plan** ended.
The separate Railway Budget had run from **1924** (**Acworth Committee**, 1921) — a **92-year** practice ended.
The plan/non-plan split was removed on the advice of the **Expenditure Management Commission**.

107.s:
Match List-I (Person) with List-II (Budget record):
List-I
a. James Wilson
b. Liaquat Ali Khan
c. R.K. Shanmukham Chetty
d. Morarji Desai
List-II
1. First budget of independent India, 26 November 1947
2. First budget of India, 7 April 1860
3. Presented the most budgets (10)
4. 1947-48 budget of the Interim Government
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
107.x: James Wilson presented India's first budget on 7 April 1860 (a-2). Liaquat Ali Khan presented the 1947-48 budget in the Interim Government (b-4). R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first budget of independent India on 26 November 1947 (c-1). Morarji Desai presented the most budgets, 10 (d-3). Option B swaps Liaquat Ali Khan and Chetty; option C swaps Wilson and Liaquat Ali Khan; option D swaps Chetty and Morarji Desai.
107.tq: 1860 Wilson; interim 1947-48 Liaquat; independent India Nov 1947 Chetty.

107.s: The separate Railway Budget was introduced in 1924 on the recommendation of the:
107.x: The separate Railway Budget began in 1924 following the recommendations of the Acworth Committee constituted in 1921.
107.tq: Match the reform with the committee that recommended it.
xs: The separate Railway Budget began in **1924** on the **Acworth Committee** (**1921**) recommendation — option **(2)**.
It was merged with the Union Budget in **2017** (Budget 2017-18), ending a **92-year** practice.
The **Expenditure Management Commission** is linked to ending the plan/non-plan split, not the Railway Budget.
xa: The Budget date also moved to **1 February** in **2017**.
**Outcome Budget / Gender Budget** came in **2005-06**; the Budget went **paperless** in **2021**.

107.s: The distinction between plan and non-plan expenditure was removed in 2017-18 on the recommendation of the:
107.x: The plan/non-plan distinction was removed in 2017-18 following the recommendation of the Expenditure Management Commission.
107.tq: Use the committee-function association and avoid swapping reform bodies.
xs: The plan/non-plan distinction was removed in **2017-18** on the **Expenditure Management Commission**'s recommendation — option **(4)**.
It was replaced by the **revenue/capital** classification.
The **Acworth Committee** (**1921**) is linked to the separate Railway Budget of **1924**.
xa: Non-plan expenditure was the larger part: **interest payments, defence, subsidies, salaries, pensions**.
APPSC-G2 2025: non-plan expenditure = **interest payments**.
⚠ **2017-18** also saw the **Railway merger** and the **1 February** date.

107.s: India's Budget has been presented in paperless or digital form since:
107.x: The Budget has been presented in paperless or digital form since 2021.
107.tq: Recall the starting year of the digital reform.
xs: The Budget has been **paperless (digital)** since **2021** — option **(4)**.
**2017** is the year the Budget moved to **1 February** and the Railway Budget merged.
**2019** is when **Nirmala Sitharaman** began presenting every Budget.
xa: Printing begins with the **Halwa ceremony** at **North Block**.
The word "Budget" comes from French **bougette** ("little bag") and is **not in the Constitution**.

107.s:
Which of the following statements is correct?
1. Morarji Desai presented the largest number of Union Budgets.
2. The 1973-74 Budget was known as the Black Budget.
3. The 1997-98 Budget was known as the Dream Budget.
4. Nirmala Sitharaman has presented every Budget since 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: All four statements are correct. Morarji Desai presented 10 budgets; 1973-74 was the Black Budget, 1997-98 was the Dream Budget, and Nirmala Sitharaman has presented every Budget since 2019.
107.tq: Verify each historical label and office-holder fact before selecting the inclusive option.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: **Morarji Desai** presented the **most budgets** (**10**).
Statements 2 and 3: **1973-74** was the "**Black Budget**"; **1997-98** the "**Dream Budget**".
Statement 4: **Nirmala Sitharaman** has presented every Budget since **2019**.
xa: Budget 2026-27 was presented on **1 February 2026**, a **Sunday**.
⚠ Older notes calling **Indira Gandhi** the "only woman" to present a budget are outdated.
**Peter Pyhrr** developed zero-based budgeting; **Jimmy Carter** first used it in government.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The word 'Budget' is derived from the French word 'bougette', meaning 'little bag'.
2. The word 'Budget' is expressly used in the Constitution of India.
3. Printing of the Budget begins with the Halwa ceremony at North Block.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: bougette means 'little bag'. Statement 2 is wrong: the word 'Budget' is not in the Constitution (it speaks of the Annual Financial Statement). Statement 3 is correct: printing begins with the Halwa ceremony at North Block. So 1 and 3 only; options A, C and D wrongly include statement 2.
107.tq: Constitution says 'Annual Financial Statement' (Art. 112), never 'Budget'.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: "Budget" comes from French **bougette** ("**little bag**").
Statement 2 is wrong: the word is **not in the Constitution**; Art. **112** speaks of the **Annual Financial Statement**.
Statement 3 is correct: printing begins with the **Halwa ceremony** at **North Block**.
xa: The **Budget circular** is issued in **September**.
The Budget is prepared by the **Budget Division, Department of Economic Affairs**, Ministry of Finance.

107.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Performance budgeting — First Hoover Commission and Administrative Reforms Commission
2. Zero-Based Budgeting — Peter Pyhrr
3. First use of Zero-Based Budgeting in government — Jimmy Carter
4. Outcome Budget — Acworth Committee
107.x: Performance budgeting is associated with the First Hoover Commission in the USA and the Administrative Reforms Commission in India. Zero-Based Budgeting is associated with Peter Pyhrr and was first used by Jimmy Carter; the Acworth Committee was related to the Railway Budget separation, not Outcome Budget.
107.tq: Use the person-committee-purpose trap by matching each reform with its proper association.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Pair 1: **Performance budgeting** came from the **First Hoover Commission** (USA); the **ARC** recommended it for India.
Pairs 2 and 3: **Peter Pyhrr** developed **zero-based budgeting**; **Jimmy Carter** first used it in government.
Pair 4 is wrong: the **Acworth Committee** led to the separate **Railway Budget** (**1924**), not the Outcome Budget.
xa: India adopted performance budgeting from the **late 1960s** on ARC advice.
**Outcome Budget** was introduced in **2005**, from **2005-06**.
APPSC-G2 2025: justifying the entire budget from the beginning = **zero-base budgeting**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about types of budget:
1. A balanced budget is one in which receipts equal expenditure.
2. A surplus budget curbs inflation but may slow growth.
3. A deficit budget, in which expenditure exceeds receipts, carries no risk of inflation or debt.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: balanced = receipts equal expenditure. Statement 2 is correct: a surplus budget curbs inflation but may slow growth. Statement 3 is wrong: a deficit budget (India's normal case) is a counter-cyclical tool but risks inflation and debt. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: Surplus = anti-inflation, may slow growth; deficit = counter-cyclical, risks inflation and debt.

107.s: A budget in which each item of expenditure is justified afresh from zero in every period is called:
107.x: Zero-based budgeting requires every expenditure item to be justified afresh from zero for each period.
107.tq: Identify the exact official term from its defining procedure.
xs: Justifying every activity afresh from zero each period is a **zero-based budget** — option **(1)**.
It was developed by **Peter Pyhrr** and first used in government by **Jimmy Carter**.
A **performance** budget links spending to activities and results; an **outcome** budget tracks outputs and outcomes.
xa: APPSC-G2 2025: justifying the entire budget from the beginning = **zero-base budgeting**.
The **line-item** budget is the traditional type — control over items of expenditure.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Performance budgeting links spending to activities or work done.
2. Outcome budgeting links outlays to measurable outcomes.
3. Gender budgeting views allocations by their gender impact.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: All three statements correctly describe performance, outcome and gender budgeting respectively.
107.tq: Test each budget type against its defining linkage before accepting the combined option.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Performance** budgeting links spending to programmes, **activities/work done** and results.
**Outcome** budgeting tracks outputs and outcomes, not outlays; **gender** budgeting allocates by gender where disparities are chronic.
xa: Performance budgeting: **First Hoover Commission** (USA); India from the **late 1960s** on **ARC** advice.
Outcome and Gender Budgets both date from **2005-06**; Gender Budget = **Statement 13**.
**Green** budgeting tracks environment-related spending.

107.s: Which one of the following statements regarding specialised budget practices in India is correct?
o: Zero-based budgeting links outlays only to gender impact.
Outcome budgeting was introduced in India only after 2020.
Performance budgeting began in India from 2005-06 on the advice of the Finance Commission.
Output-Outcome budgeting began from 2005-06, while the Gender Budget Statement has also been presented since 2005-06.
107.x: Output-Outcome budgeting and the Gender Budget Statement are associated with 2005-06. Performance budgeting in India dates from the late 1960s on ARC advice.
107.tq: Separate similar budget labels by their starting period and distinctive purpose.
xs: **Output-Outcome budgeting** and the **Gender Budget Statement** both date from **2005-06** — option **(4)**.
Option (3) is wrong: **performance budgeting** began in India in the **late 1960s** on **ARC** advice, not via the Finance Commission.
Option (2) is wrong: outcome budgeting dates from **2005**, not after 2020; option (1) confuses zero-based with gender budgeting.
xa: The Outcome Budget is now a **budget document** — output-outcome framework for schemes.
Gender Budget 2026-27: **₹5.01 lakh crore (9.37%)**, highest ever.
The **16th Finance Commission** ties Centrally Sponsored Schemes to measurable outcomes.

107.s: The Gender Budget Statement is associated with which of the following?
107.x: The Gender Budget is presented as Statement 13 and has been in place since 2005-06.
107.tq: Test a document number together with its commencement year.
xs: The Gender Budget is **Statement 13**, presented since **2005-06** — option **(1)**.
It tracks women-specific (**Part A, 100%**), **30-99%** (**Part B**) and **below 30%** (**Part C**) allocations.
The **Outcome Budget** was introduced in the same year, **2005-06**.
xa: Gender Budget 2026-27: **₹5.01 lakh crore (9.37%)** — highest ever.
Gender budgeting allocates by gender where **disparities are chronic**.

107.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Performance budget — expenditure without reference to results
Line-item budget — traditional control over items of expenditure
Green budget — tracking only defence expenditure
Gender budget — tracking only environmental spending
107.x: A line-item budget is traditional and focuses on control over individual items of expenditure.
107.tq: Find the correctly matched concept among reversed descriptions.
xs: **Line-item budget — traditional control over items of expenditure** is correct — option **(2)**.
A **performance** budget links spending to results, so option (1) is wrong.
A **green** budget tracks environment spending and a **gender** budget allocates by gender — options (3) and (4) swap them.
xa: **Zero-based** budgeting justifies every activity afresh from zero (**Peter Pyhrr**).
**Outcome** budgeting tracks outputs and outcomes, not outlays (from **2005-06**).

107.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
A. Article 112
B. Article 113
C. Article 114
D. Article 115

List-II (Provision)
1. Appropriation Bill
2. Supplementary, additional or excess grants
3. Annual Financial Statement
4. Procedure on estimates and demands for grants

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
107.x: Article 112 concerns the Annual Financial Statement, Article 113 the procedure on estimates, Article 114 the Appropriation Bill, and Article 115 supplementary, additional or excess grants.
107.tq: Start with the secure Article 112–Budget pair and complete the consecutive financial-Article sequence.
xs: Correct match: **A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 112** = **Annual Financial Statement**; **Art. 113** = procedure on estimates, **demands for grants**.
**Art. 114** = **Appropriation Bill**; **Art. 115** = supplementary, additional or excess grants.
xa: **Art. 116** = **vote on account**, vote of credit, exceptional grants; **Art. 117** = special provisions on financial bills.
**Art. 266** Consolidated Fund; **Art. 266(2)** Public Account; **Art. 267** Contingency Fund.
**Art. 110(1)(a)** — Finance Bill as a Money Bill.

107.s:
With reference to the Annual Financial Statement, consider the following statements:
1. It is mentioned in Article 112 of the Constitution.
2. It presents estimated receipts and expenditure under the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account.
3. The word ‘Budget’ is expressly used in the Constitution for this statement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: The Annual Financial Statement is provided under Article 112 and covers the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account. The Constitution does not use the word ‘Budget’ for it.
107.tq: Identify the constitutional provision and reject the look-alike constitutional terminology.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the AFS is under **Article 112**.
Statement 2 is correct: it estimates receipts and expenditure in the **Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account**.
Statement 3 is wrong: "**Budget**" is **not a word used in the Constitution**.
xa: The AFS is presented on the "**first working day of February**" — in practice **1 February**, even on a Sunday (**2026**).
The **Contingency Fund of India** (Art. 267) corpus was raised to **₹30,000 crore** from **2021-22**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Demands for Grants:
1. They are provided under Article 113.
2. There is usually one Demand for Grants for each ministry or department.
3. They include revenue expenditure, capital expenditure and loans.
4. Charged expenditure is not shown separately in them.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Demands for Grants are covered by Article 113, are generally ministry-wise, and include revenue, capital and loan components. Charged items are shown separately, making statement 4 false.
107.tq: Find the single reversed detail in a list of budget-document features.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Demands for Grants are under **Art. 113**, usually **one per ministry/department**, covering **revenue + capital + loans**.
Statement 4 is wrong: **charged items** (like interest) **are shown separately** and not voted.
xa: Demands are voted **only by Lok Sabha** and need the **President's recommendation**.
**Guillotine**: on the last allotted day, remaining demands are put to vote **without discussion**.
Cut motions: **policy cut ₹1**; **token cut ₹100**; economy cut by a stated amount.

107.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Receipt Budget — output-outcome framework for schemes
Expenditure Profile — detailed estimates of tax receipts
Outcome Budget — output-outcome framework for schemes
107.x: The Outcome Budget presents the output-outcome framework for schemes. The Receipt Budget deals with receipts, while the Expenditure Budget or Expenditure Profile deals with spending.
107.tq: Start from the sure document-function pair and eliminate swapped descriptions.
xs: **Outcome Budget — output-outcome framework for schemes** is correct — option **(3)**.
The **Receipt Budget** gives estimates and trends of tax, non-tax and capital receipts — so option (1) is wrong.
The **Expenditure Profile** is scheme- and ministry-wise **spending**; the **Finance Bill** carries **tax proposals**.
xa: **Appropriation Bill**: **Art. 114(3)** — authorises withdrawal from the CFI.
**Finance Bill** is under **Art. 110(1)(a)**, with an explanatory **Memorandum**.
Other documents: **Budget at a Glance**; FRBM statements (**MEFS**; **MTFPS cum FPSS**).

107.s: Who prepares the Union Budget through the Budget Division?
o: NITI Aayog independently of the Ministry of Finance
Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
107.x: The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of Finance prepares the Union Budget, in coordination with NITI Aayog and spending ministries.
107.tq: Apply the ‘who performs this job?’ test to distinguish adjoining financial institutions.
xs: The Budget is prepared by the **Budget Division, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance** — option **(2)**.
It works with **NITI Aayog** and the spending ministries — NITI does not prepare it independently.
The **Department of Revenue** (**CBDT/CBIC**) only furnishes revenue estimates.
xa: The DEA also prepares budgets of **States under President's Rule** and **UTs**.
The **Budget circular** is issued in **September**; printing begins with the **Halwa ceremony** at **North Block**.

107.s: Revenue estimates in the Union Budget are furnished by which of the following?
o: CBDT and CBIC under the Department of Revenue
Department of Expenditure and Comptroller and Auditor General
NITI Aayog and the Reserve Bank of India
107.x: Revenue estimates are furnished by the Department of Revenue through the CBDT and CBIC.
107.tq: Identify the responsible department rather than the department that compiles the Budget.
xs: Revenue estimates come from the **Department of Revenue** — **CBDT and CBIC** — option **(1)**.
The **Budget Division** of the **DEA** prepares the Budget itself.
The Budget Division works with **NITI Aayog** and spending ministries.
xa: The **Receipt Budget** gives detailed estimates and trends of **tax, non-tax and capital receipts**.
Net tax to the Centre 2026-27 BE: **₹28,72,135 crore** (**+7.2%**).

107.s: A Finance Bill is treated as a Money Bill under which constitutional provision?
107.x: A Finance Bill comes within the scope of a Money Bill under Article 110(1)(a), insofar as it contains provisions dealing with taxation.
107.tq: Distinguish the constitutional provision governing taxation-related Money Bills.
xs: The Finance Bill is a **Money Bill** under **Article 110(1)(a)** — option **(2)**.
It gives effect to the **tax proposals** and comes with an explanatory **Memorandum**.
**Art. 112** is the **Annual Financial Statement**, not the Finance Bill.
xa: The Finance Bill must be enacted within **75 days** (**Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931**).
It is the **sixth** and last stage of the budget process, after the **Appropriation Bill**.

107.s: Which sequence correctly represents the classification order of receipts in the budget?
o: Tax revenue → Revenue receipts → Capital receipts → Non-tax revenue
Revenue receipts → Tax revenue → Non-tax revenue → Capital receipts
Capital receipts → Revenue receipts → Tax revenue → Non-tax revenue
Non-tax revenue → Tax revenue → Revenue receipts → Capital receipts
107.x: The prescribed sequence is Revenue receipts, Tax revenue, Non-tax revenue and Capital receipts.
107.tq: Use the first-and-last elements to eliminate incorrect sequences.
xs: **Revenue receipts → Tax revenue → Non-tax revenue → Capital receipts** — option **(2)**.
This is the **APPSC-GS 2025** key sequence.
Revenue receipts (tax and non-tax) create no liability and reduce no assets; capital receipts do one or the other.
xa: **Debt** capital receipts create liabilities (market loans, T-Bills, external loans).
**Non-debt** capital receipts reduce assets (**recovery of loans**, **disinvestment**).

107.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Receipt)
 a. Market borrowings
 b. Recovery of loans
 c. GST
 d. Fees and fines

List-II (Classification)
 i. Tax revenue
 ii. Non-tax revenue
 iii. Debt capital receipt
 iv. Non-debt capital receipt

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
107.x: Market borrowings are debt capital receipts, recovery of loans is a non-debt capital receipt, GST is tax revenue and fees and fines are non-tax revenue.
107.tq: Start from the sure classification of GST and then complete the pairs.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Market borrowings** = **debt capital receipt**; **recovery of loans** = **non-debt capital receipt**.
**GST** = **tax revenue**; **fees and fines** = **non-tax revenue**.
xa: Other debt receipts: **T-Bills**, external loans, small savings/PF, borrowing from RBI.
Rupee comes from: **borrowings and other liabilities 24 paise** — the largest source in 2026-27.

107.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its budget-account characteristic?
o: Capital account — current-year routine transactions only
Capital account — no transactions involving liabilities
Revenue account — creation of long-term assets only
107.x: The revenue account records current-year transactions, while the capital account relates to assets and liabilities.
107.tq: Use the running-versus-asset-creation distinction to reject reversed descriptions.
xs: **Revenue account — current-year transactions** is correct — option **(3)**.
The **capital account** records **assets and liabilities**, so options (1) and (2) are wrong.
Revenue spending **creates no asset** — it maintains assets (salaries, pensions, interest, subsidies).
xa: Capital spending creates assets or reduces liabilities: capex, roads, **defence equipment**, loans given, debt repayment.
Mnemonic: "Revenue = Running the government; Capital = Creating assets".

107.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
107.x: Wealth tax, gift tax and estate duty were described as paper taxes because they never generated large revenue and are now abolished. GST is not a paper tax.
107.tq: Find the item outside the stated group rather than the abolished examples.
xs: **GST — paper tax** is wrongly matched — option **(3)**.
"**Paper taxes**" were **wealth tax, gift tax and estate duty** — they never raised large revenue and are now abolished.
**GST** is a major indirect **tax revenue** source.
xa: **GST and other taxes** bring **15** paise of every rupee in 2026-27.
**GST 2.0** came in **Sep 2025**.

107.s:
Under the erstwhile Plan and non-Plan classification of government expenditure, Plan expenditure comprised:
1. Expenditure on Central Plans
2. Central assistance for State and Union Territory Plans
3. Interest payments on public debt
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Plan expenditure covered Central Plans and central assistance for State and Union Territory Plans. Interest payments were classified as non-Plan expenditure.
107.tq: Separate the two components of the former Plan category from a familiar non-Plan item.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Plan expenditure** covered **Central Plans** (Five Year Plans) and **central assistance for State/UT Plans**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **interest payments** were the classic **non-plan** item.
xa: The distinction was removed in **2017-18** (**Expenditure Management Commission**).
APPSC-G2 2025: non-plan expenditure = **interest payments**.

107.s: Which one of the following was a non-Plan expenditure item under the former classification?
o: Expenditure on a new Central Plan
Central assistance for Union Territory Plans
107.x: Interest payments formed part of the larger non-Plan expenditure category. Central Plans and central assistance for State and Union Territory Plans were Plan expenditure.
107.tq: Use the direct association between interest payments and the former non-Plan category.
xs: **Interest payments** were **non-plan** expenditure — option **(2)**.
Non-plan was the **larger part**: interest, **defence, subsidies, salaries, pensions**, and maintenance of earlier Plan assets.
Central Plans and central assistance for **State/UT Plans** were **plan** expenditure — options (1), (3), (4).
xa: APPSC-G2 2025 key: non-plan expenditure = **interest payments**.
Rupee goes to: **interest payments** take **20** paise in 2026-27.
Interest takes **40%** of revenue receipts.

107.s: Capital expenditure is expenditure that generally:
o: Never includes loans given by the government
Is limited to payment of interest
107.x: Capital expenditure creates assets or reduces liabilities; examples include capital works, loans given and debt repayment.
107.tq: Apply the core classification rule rather than memorising isolated examples.
xs: Capital expenditure **creates assets or reduces liabilities** — option **(4)**.
Examples: **capex**, roads, **defence equipment**, **loans given** (incl. to States), **debt repayment** — so option (1) is wrong.
**Subsidies**, grants and **interest** are **revenue** expenditure — options (2) and (3) are wrong.
xa: Capex 2026-27 BE: **₹12.22 lakh crore**.
ES 2025-26: capex up **28%** (Apr-Nov 2025, ~**59%** of BE), revenue expenditure up only **1.8%**.

107.s: Developmental expenditure primarily relates to:
o: Debt charges and court decrees only
107.x: Developmental expenditure covers economic and social services, whereas interest, defence, administration and pensions are classified as non-developmental.
107.tq: Discriminate between the developmental service group and the non-developmental group.
xs: Developmental expenditure covers **economic and social services** — option **(2)**.
**Interest, defence, administration and pensions** are **non-developmental** — so options (3) and (4) are wrong.
**Debt charges** and **court decrees** are charged items, not the definition of developmental spending.
xa: Development expenditure examples: **education, health, employment, industry**.
**Defence** is "**committed**" spending, with little scope for cuts.
The old **plan/non-plan** split was replaced by **revenue/capital** from **2017-18**.

107.s: The guiding rule that borrowings should be used only to invest and not to fund current spending is most closely related to:
o: Using borrowed resources for productive capital formation
Using only tax revenue for infrastructure
Financing recurrent revenue expenditure through debt
Replacing all capital expenditure with subsidies
107.x: The guiding fiscal rule is to borrow for investment or productive capital formation rather than for current expenditure.
107.tq: Apply the fiscal principle to distinguish investment borrowing from borrowing for consumption.
xs: "Borrow only to invest" means **using borrowed resources for productive capital formation** — option **(1)**.
The guiding rule: **borrow only to invest, not to fund current spending** — option (3) is the opposite.
**Capital** spending creates assets or reduces liabilities; **revenue** spending creates no asset.
xa: Mnemonic: "**Revenue** = Running the government; **Capital** = Creating assets".
**Borrowings and other liabilities** are the largest source of the rupee in 2026-27 (**24** paise).
Capex 2026-27 BE: **₹12.22 lakh crore**.

107.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Type of expenditure)
A. Development expenditure
B. Non-development expenditure
C. Committed expenditure
D. Plan/non-plan distinction

List-II (Associated item or feature)
1. Replaced by revenue/capital classification from 2017-18
2. Defence spending with little scope for cuts
3. Education, health, employment and industry
4. Defence, police, interest and administration

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
107.x: Development expenditure includes education, health, employment and industry; non-development expenditure includes defence, police, interest and administration. Defence is committed expenditure, and plan/non-plan was replaced by revenue/capital classification.
107.tq: Start with the distinctive defence and reform pairs, then complete the classification.
xs: Correct match: **A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1** — option **(1)**.
**Development** expenditure → **education, health, employment, industry**; **non-development** → **defence, police, interest, administration**.
**Committed** expenditure → **defence**, little scope for cuts; **plan/non-plan** → replaced by **revenue/capital** from **2017-18**.
xa: The plan/non-plan split was removed on the **Expenditure Management Commission**'s advice.
APPSC-G2 2025: non-plan expenditure = **interest payments**.

107.s:
Which of the following correctly describes charged expenditure?
1. It is not submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha.
2. It may be discussed in Parliament.
3. Interest on public debt is an example of charged expenditure.
4. It is not shown separately in the Appropriation Act.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
107.x: Charged expenditure is non-votable but discussable, and interest on public debt is an example. It is shown separately as an appropriation, making statement 4 false.
107.tq: Use the key distinction ‘discussable but non-votable’ and reject the reversed statement.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Charged expenditure is **not voted** by Lok Sabha but can be **discussed** (**Art. 113(1)**).
**Debt charges** (interest, redemption) are charged items.
Statement 4 is wrong: charged items are **shown separately**; the Appropriation Bill may not vary them.
xa: The list of charged items is under **Art. 112(3)**.
Charged expenditure comes **straight from the Consolidated Fund**.

107.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: President’s emoluments; interest on public debt; salary and office expenses of the CAG
Salaries of all Members of Parliament; grants to States; election expenditure
All Demands for Grants; salaries of ministers; public debt receipts
Finance Commission grants; subsidies; salaries of all government employees
107.x: The President’s emoluments, interest on public debt, and the salary and administrative office expenses of the CAG are charged expenditure. The other sets contain items not identified as charged expenditure here.
107.tq: Use elimination by checking whether every item belongs to the charged category.
xs: **President's emoluments; interest on public debt; salary and office expenses of the CAG** — all charged — option **(1)**.
Charged items also include salaries of RS **Chairman/Deputy Chairman** and LS **Speaker/Deputy Speaker**, and **UPSC** chairman/members.
**Court decrees/awards** and anything **Parliament declares charged by law** are also charged.
xa: Basis: **Art. 112(3)**; charged items are **not voted**, only discussed.
⚠ **SC judges** = salaries + pensions charged; **HC judges** = only **pensions** charged.

107.s: Which one of the following is charged expenditure in relation to the higher judiciary?
o: Salaries and allowances of all advocates appearing before the Supreme Court
All grants made by High Courts to subordinate courts
Only the travel expenses of High Court advocates
Salaries, allowances and pensions of Supreme Court judges and pensions of High Court judges
107.x: Salaries, allowances and pensions of Supreme Court judges, and pensions of High Court judges, are charged expenditure.
107.tq: Discriminate between constitutional judicial expenditure and unrelated legal expenses.
xs: **Salaries, allowances and pensions of SC judges** and **pensions of HC judges** are charged — option **(4)**.
⚠ For **HC judges** only **pensions** are charged, not salaries.
Advocates' salaries or court grants are not on the charged list.
xa: Other charged items: **President**'s emoluments, **CAG**'s salary, **UPSC**, **debt charges**.
Charged expenditure is **non-votable** but **discussable** (**Art. 113(1)**).

107.s:
The salaries and office expenses of which of the following are charged expenditure?
1. Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
2. Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
3. Chairman and members of the Union Public Service Commission
4. Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
107.x: The specified salaries and office expenses of the presiding officers, UPSC, and CAG are charged expenditure. Such expenditure is discussable but not voted.
107.tq: Test a complete constitutional list while avoiding substitution of a neighbouring office.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — option **(4)**.
Salaries of **Chairman/Deputy Chairman (RS)** and **Speaker/Deputy Speaker (LS)** are charged.
**UPSC** chairman/members + office expenses and the **CAG**'s salary + office expenses are charged.
xa: Charged items are listed under **Art. 112(3)**.
Also charged: **President**'s emoluments, **debt charges**, **SC judges**' salaries and pensions.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the Public Account of India:
1. It is provided for in Article 266(2) of the Constitution.
2. Provident funds, small savings and deposits are credited to it.
3. Every withdrawal from it requires parliamentary appropriation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Public Account is under Art. 266(2). Statement 2 is correct: provident funds, small savings and deposits go into it, with the government acting as banker. Statement 3 is wrong: because the government only acts as banker, no parliamentary appropriation is needed for withdrawals. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: Public Account = government as banker, so no appropriation needed.

107.s: The list of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is laid down in:
107.x: Article 112(3) lists charged expenditure (President's emoluments, debt charges, judges' salaries, CAG etc.). Art 114(3) bars withdrawal from the CFI without an Appropriation Act, Art 266(2) is the Public Account, and Art 110(1)(a) brings tax provisions within a Money Bill.
107.tq: Charged list = 112(3); discussable but not votable = 113(1).
xs: Charged expenditure is listed in **Article 112(3)** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 114(3)** bars withdrawal from the CFI without an **Appropriation Act**.
**Art. 266(2)** is the **Public Account**; **Art. 110(1)(a)** is the **Finance Bill**.
xa: Charged items include the **President**'s emoluments, **debt charges**, **SC judges**' salaries, the **CAG**.
Charged expenditure is **not voted**, only **discussed** (**Art. 113(1)**).

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the presentation of the Union Budget:
1. There is no discussion on the Budget on the day it is presented.
2. The Economic Survey is presented a day or more before the Budget.
3. Cut motions are moved during the general discussion that follows the presentation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: there is no discussion on the day of presentation. Statement 2 is correct: the Economic Survey comes a day or more earlier. Statement 3 is wrong: the general discussion (3-4 days, both Houses) has no cut motions or voting; cut motions come at the voting on demands. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: General discussion = talk only; cut motions and votes come at the demands stage.

107.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the preparation of the Union Budget is correct?
o: The Budget circular is issued by the Rajya Sabha Secretariat in September.
The Budget circular is issued in September and the Halwa ceremony marks the beginning of printing.
The Halwa ceremony marks the voting of Demands for Grants.
The Budget circular is issued in February and printing begins after the Finance Bill.
107.x: The Budget circular is issued in September, and the Halwa ceremony marks the printing of the Budget documents.
107.tq: Combine two process markers and reject swapped institutions or stages.
xs: The **Budget circular** is issued in **September** and the **Halwa ceremony** marks printing — option **(2)**.
Printing begins at **North Block**.
The circular is not a **Rajya Sabha** matter; the Budget is prepared by the **Budget Division, DEA**.
xa: The DEA also prepares budgets of **States under President's Rule** and **UTs**.
Revenue estimates come from **CBDT/CBIC** (Department of Revenue).

107.s:
Arrange the following stages of the Union Budget process in the correct chronological order:
A. Voting on Demands for Grants
B. Presentation of the Budget
C. Finance Bill
D. General discussion
107.x: The sequence is presentation, general discussion, voting on Demands for Grants and then the Finance Bill, with the Appropriation Bill preceding the Finance Bill.
107.tq: Fix the first and last stages, then place discussion and voting between them.
xs: Order: **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)**.
**Presentation** → **general discussion** → **DRSC scrutiny** → **voting on demands** → **Appropriation Bill** → **Finance Bill**.
The **Finance Bill** is the **last** stage, after the Appropriation Bill.
xa: General discussion: both Houses, **3-4 days**; no cut motions.
Voting on demands (**Art. 113**): **only Lok Sabha**.
Finance Bill must be enacted within **75 days**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the stages of the Budget process:
1. General discussion ordinarily lasts three to four days and takes place in both Houses.
2. Department-related Standing Committees scrutinise the Demands for Grants.
3. Voting on Demands for Grants takes place in the Lok Sabha only.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: All three statements are correct: general discussion is held in both Houses, committees scrutinise the Demands, and voting occurs only in the Lok Sabha.
107.tq: Separate the roles of both Houses, committees and the Lok Sabha in the process.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: **General discussion** is in **both Houses**, **3-4 days**.
2: **Department-related Standing Committees** examine their ministries' demands during recess.
3: Voting on demands (**Art. 113**) is **only in Lok Sabha**.
xa: Demands need the **President's recommendation**.
**Guillotine**: remaining demands put to vote **without discussion** on the last allotted day.

107.s: In parliamentary financial procedure, the guillotine refers to
o: putting all outstanding demands to vote without discussion on the last day
the automatic rejection of all demands for grants
the President's power to withhold assent to a Money Bill
the referral of a financial Bill to a Joint Parliamentary Committee
107.x: On the last day fixed for the discussion of demands, all outstanding demands are put to vote without further discussion. This procedure is called the guillotine.
107.tq: Recognise the procedural meaning of a specialised parliamentary term.
xs: The **guillotine** puts **all outstanding demands to vote without discussion on the last day** — option **(1)**.
This was a **PYQ in APPSC-GS 2025**.
It applies to **voting on demands** in **Lok Sabha** (**Art. 113**).
xa: ⚠ **Policy cut** = reduce to **₹1**; **token cut** = by **₹100**; **economy cut** = by a stated amount.
General discussion runs **3-4 days** in both Houses.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about a Vote on Account:
1. It is provided under Article 116.
2. It is usually granted for two months.
3. It becomes unnecessary in election years because the Budget is presented on 1 February.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: A Vote on Account is covered by Article 116 and is usually granted for two months. It continues to be used in election years; the change to a 1 February Budget date has not made it ineffectual.
107.tq: Spot the false causal conclusion in statement 3 while retaining the article and duration facts.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1: **Vote on account** is under **Art. 116**.
2: It is an advance grant for about **two months** (**one-sixth**).
3 is wrong: ⚠ it is **still used in election years**, so it has **not** become ineffectual after the **1 February** move.
xa: In election years it covers **3-5 months**.
It covers **only expenditure**, until the budget is passed.

107.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Appropriation Bill from the Finance Bill?
o: The Appropriation Bill gives effect to tax proposals, whereas the Finance Bill authorises withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund.
The Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund, whereas the Finance Bill gives effect to tax proposals.
Both Bills exclusively authorise withdrawal from the Public Account.
Both Bills are merely estimates and have no legal effect.
107.x: The Appropriation Bill provides legal authority for withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund, while the Finance Bill gives effect to tax proposals.
107.tq: Use a direct function-versus-function comparison to avoid swapping two similar Bills.
xs: The **Appropriation Bill** authorises **withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund**; the **Finance Bill** gives effect to **tax proposals** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 114(3)**: no withdrawal without an **Appropriation Act**.
The Finance Bill is a **Money Bill** under **Art. 110(1)(a)**.
xa: The Finance Bill must be enacted within **75 days** (**Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931**).
The **Public Account** needs no appropriation — the government acts as banker.

107.s:
Consider the following statements regarding cut motions on Demands for Grants:
1. A policy cut motion seeks to reduce the demand to Re 1.
2. An economy cut motion seeks to reduce the demand by a specified amount.
3. A token cut motion seeks to reduce the demand by Rs 1,000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: a policy cut reduces the demand to Re 1 (disapproval of policy). Statement 2 is correct: an economy cut reduces it by a stated amount. Statement 3 is wrong: a token cut reduces it by Rs 100, not Rs 1,000. So 1 and 2 only; B, C and D include the false statement 3 or leave out a true one.
107.tq: Policy = to Re 1; Economy = by stated amount; Token = by Rs 100.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1: a **policy cut** reduces the demand to **₹1**.
2: an **economy cut** reduces it by a **stated amount**.
3 is wrong: a **token cut** reduces it by **₹100**, not Rs 1,000.
xa: Cut motions are moved during **voting on demands**, not in general discussion.
**Guillotine**: outstanding demands put to vote **without discussion**.

107.s: Which statement regarding the Appropriation Bill is correct?
o: No amendment may vary a voted grant, change its destination or vary charged expenditure.
It permits amendments that alter the destination of a voted grant.
It may vary charged expenditure without restriction.
It is introduced only in the Rajya Sabha.
107.x: Article 114 governs the Appropriation Bill, and amendments cannot vary a voted grant, change its destination or vary charged expenditure.
107.tq: Spot the option that correctly states the constitutional restrictions on amendment.
xs: **No amendment may vary a voted grant, change its destination or vary charged expenditure** — option **(1)**.
This is the rule for the **Appropriation Bill** under **Art. 114**.
**Art. 114(3)**: no withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund without an **Appropriation Act**.
xa: The Appropriation Bill is **stage 5**, after voting on demands in **Lok Sabha**.
Voting on demands is **only in Lok Sabha** — so option (4) is wrong.

107.s: Under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931, the Finance Bill must be enacted within:
107.x: The Finance Bill must be enacted within 75 days under the stated provision of the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931.
107.tq: Recall the statutory time limit using closely spaced numerical options.
xs: The Finance Bill must be enacted within **75 days** — option **(3)**.
This comes from the **Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931**.
The Finance Bill is a **Money Bill** under **Art. 110(1)(a)** and gives effect to tax proposals.
xa: Budget = estimate statement; **Finance Bill** = the legal instrument for taxes.
The Finance Bill comes with an explanatory **Memorandum**.

107.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a vote on account from an interim budget?
o: A vote on account is a full statement of accounts, whereas an interim budget only authorises expenditure.
An interim budget authorises expenditure without presenting receipts, whereas a vote on account presents full receipts and expenditure.
A vote on account authorises expenditure for part of the year, whereas an interim budget is a full statement of receipts and expenditure by an outgoing government in an election year.
Both are identical and are presented only by a newly elected government.
107.x: A vote on account is an advance grant for expenditure for part of the year. An interim budget is a full statement of receipts and expenditure presented by an outgoing government in an election year.
107.tq: Separate two similar terms by their scope and purpose.
xs: **Vote on account** = expenditure for **part of the year**; **interim budget** = full statement by an **outgoing government** in an **election year** — option **(3)**.
A vote on account (**Art. 116**) covers **only expenditure**, about **two months**.
An interim budget is a **full statement** of receipts and expenditure.
xa: In election years a vote on account covers **3-5 months**.
⚠ Vote on account is rarely needed since **1 February**, except in **interim budget** years.

107.s:
Which of the following statements about the Consolidated Fund is correct?
1. It is referred to in Article 266.
2. No money can be withdrawn from it without an Appropriation Act.
3. A vote on account provides a grant in advance for expenditure from it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Article 266 refers to the Consolidated Fund; withdrawal requires an Appropriation Act, while a vote on account authorises advance expenditure for part of the year.
107.tq: Combine the article, appropriation rule and advance-grant function.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: the **Consolidated Fund** is under **Art. 266**.
2: **Art. 114(3)** — no withdrawal without an **Appropriation Act**.
3: a **vote on account** (**Art. 116**) is an advance grant for part of the year.
xa: **Charged expenditure** comes straight from the Consolidated Fund (**Art. 112(3)**).
**Public Account** is **Art. 266(2)**; **Contingency Fund** is **Art. 267**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Union Budget 2026-27:
1. Total expenditure was estimated at ₹53,47,315 crore.
2. Receipts excluding borrowing were estimated at ₹36,51,547 crore.
3. The fiscal deficit was estimated at 4.3 per cent of GDP.
4. The debt was estimated at 45.6 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Expenditure was ₹53,47,315 crore, receipts excluding borrowing were ₹36,51,547 crore and fiscal deficit was 4.3 per cent of GDP. Debt was 55.6 per cent, not 45.6 per cent.
