xa: ⚠ 2025-26 FAE fastest sector = **services (10.67%)**; Q2 2025-26 review fastest = **agriculture (13.5%)**.
2025-26 industry growth: **9.15%**.
2023-24 FRE: agriculture **-1.58%**, industry **7.52%**, services **7.71%**.

109.s: Agriculture and allied sectors accounted for what share of Andhra Pradesh GSDP?
109.x: Agriculture and allied sectors accounted for 33.20% of Andhra Pradesh GSDP.
109.tq: Distinguish the state GSDP share from the livestock share of national GVA.
xs: Agriculture & allied = **33.20%** of AP GSDP — option **(3)** is correct.
It is **₹5,39,454 crore** of **₹17,62,357 crore** (2025-26 AE, current prices).
**30.87%** is livestock's share of agri & allied GVA (2023-24), not agriculture's share of GSDP.
xa: Agri-allied growth 2025-26 FAE: **10.14%**, led by **fisheries**.
NITI Aayog: agriculture contributes **more than one-third** of GSDP.
India's agriculture share ≈ **18%** of GVA.
AP supplies about **10%** of India's farm output.

109.s: Which sub-sector had the largest GVA at constant prices in the agriculture and allied sector in both the 2024-25 FAE and 2025-26 FAE series?
109.x: Fishing and aquaculture led the agriculture and allied constant-price series in 2024-25 at ₹77,085 crore and again in 2025-26 at ₹90,673 crore.
109.tq: Compare the leading item across two years instead of relying on the current-price ranking.
xs: **Fishing & Aquaculture** had the largest constant-price GVA in both years — option **(4)** is correct.
Next were **Livestock** (₹66,456 cr) and **Horticulture** (₹60,527 cr) in 2024-25; crops only ₹25,584 cr.
xa: ⚠ **Price basis trap:** **Livestock** leads at **current** prices; **fishing & aquaculture** at **constant** prices.
Fishing also grew fastest in 2025-26 (**17.69%**).
Lowest GVA: **Forestry & Logging** in both years.
Fishing's share of agri-allied GVA rose ~**33% to ~36%**.

109.s: At current prices in 2024-25, which sub-sector had the largest GVA among all sub-sectors of Andhra Pradesh?
109.x: Livestock had the largest GVA among all sub-sectors at current prices in 2024-25, with a share of about 12%.
109.tq: Apply the price-basis distinction: current-price leadership differs from constant-price leadership.
xs: At current prices in 2024-25 **Livestock** had the largest GVA of all sub-sectors (about **12%** of total GVA) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Horticulture** was about **10%**, crops **4%**, forestry **1%**.
xa: ⚠ At **constant** prices **Fishing & Aquaculture** leads the agri-allied group.
Livestock was also the largest sub-sector at current prices in the **2021-22** AE (PYQ).
In **2025-26** (current) **Manufacturing** and **Livestock** tie at **10.84%**.
Livestock's agri-allied share fell from ~**29%** to ~**26%** (2024-25 → 2025-26).

109.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the fastest-growing sub-sector in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26 FAE?
o: Agriculture and allied activities — Fishing and Aquaculture
Agriculture and allied activities — Forestry and Logging
109.x: Fishing and Aquaculture was the fastest-growing sub-sector within agriculture and allied activities, with growth of 17.69%.
109.tq: Separate the fastest sub-sector within each major sector from the overall sector ranking.
xs: **Agriculture and allied — Fishing and Aquaculture** (**17.69%**) is correctly matched — option **(1)** is correct.
Industry's fastest was **Construction (14.18%)**, not Mining (**7.88%**).
Services' fastest was **Communications (15.13%)**, not Banking (**13.59%**).
**Forestry** was the agri-allied **lowest** (**2.39%**).
xa: ⚠ In 2024-25 the agri-allied leader was **crops (14.99%)**.
Lowest services sub-sector 2025-26: **Public Administration 0.05%**.
Fishing & Aquaculture = **9.42%** of total GVA (current, 2025-26).

109.s: The average growth of agriculture and allied activities in Andhra Pradesh since bifurcation, as reported in 2018, was approximately:
109.x: The average growth of agriculture and allied activities since bifurcation was reported as 17% as of 2018.
109.tq: Distinguish the average growth rate from the later peak and the policy target.
xs: Average agri & allied growth since bifurcation (as of 2018) = **17%** — option **(2)** is correct.
**18.23%** was the **peak (2017-18)**; **30%** is the five-year target; **13.5%** is the Q2 2025-26 figure.
xa: Fertiliser use fell **80.78% (2015-16) → 38.1% (2016-17 AE)** of allotment.
India = **2nd-largest** fertiliser consumer.
AP supplies about **10%** of India's farm output.

109.s: Which of the following correctly matches the agricultural growth figures of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Peak growth in 2017–18 – 30%; five-year agriculture and allied target – 18.23%
Peak growth in 2017–18 – 18.23%; five-year agriculture and allied target – 30%
Average growth since bifurcation – 30%; Q2 2025–26 growth – 17%
109.x: The peak agriculture and allied growth was 18.23% in 2017–18, while the target was 30% growth over five years.
109.tq: Match each percentage with its time frame and status—peak versus target.
xs: **Peak 2017-18 – 18.23%**; **five-year target – 30%** — option **(3)** is correct.
The 30% target (2024-25 Survey) is to come via **17 growth engines**.
**17%** = average growth since bifurcation (as of 2018); **13.5%** = Q2 2025-26 agri growth.
xa: National agri-allied growth: **4.4%** a year over 5 years.
Agriculture contracted only in **2023-24** (**-1.58%** FRE).
AP agriculture share ≈ **twice** India's **~18%**.

109.s: The utilisation of fertiliser as a percentage of allotment in Andhra Pradesh changed from 2015–16 to 2016–17 AE in which manner?
109.x: Fertiliser utilisation as a percentage of allotment fell sharply from 80.78% in 2015–16 to 38.1% in 2016–17 AE.
109.tq: Read the direction of change carefully and attach each figure to its correct year.
xs: Fertiliser use **fell from 80.78% (2015-16) to 38.1% (2016-17 AE)** of allotment — option **(3)** is correct.
It did not rise or remain unchanged.
xa: India = **2nd-largest** fertiliser consumer.
Peak agri growth: **18.23% (2017-18)**; average since bifurcation **17%** (APPSC 2018).
NLM fodder (2023-24): **49,000 quintals** fodder seed, **₹2.72 crore**.

109.s: Which of the following was covered by the White Paper on agriculture-related sectors in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Horticulture, textiles, ports, railways, animal husbandry and marketing
Agriculture, horticulture, sericulture, animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries and marketing
Agriculture, mining, defence, banking, dairy, fisheries and tourism
Sericulture, information technology, defence, fisheries, tourism and banking
109.x: The White Paper covered agriculture, horticulture, sericulture, animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries and marketing.
109.tq: Recall the complete sectoral list and reject options containing unrelated administrative sectors.
xs: The White Paper covered **Agriculture, Horticulture, Sericulture, Animal Husbandry, Dairy, Fisheries and Marketing** — option **(2)** is correct.
Textiles, ports, railways, mining, defence, banking, IT and tourism were not in it.
xa: APPSC 2022 A-R question on it: **both true, R explains A**.
Swarnandhra horticulture KPIs: micro-irrigation, horticulture area, **oil palm** area, post-harvest infrastructure, productivity.
Target: **30% growth** in agri & allied over five years through **17 growth engines**.

109.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh supplies about 10 per cent of India's farm output.
2. The 2024-25 Survey targets 30 per cent growth in agriculture and allied sectors over five years through 17 growth engines.
3. India is the largest consumer of fertilisers in the world.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Statement 1 is correct: AP supplies about 10% of India's farm output. Statement 2 is correct: the 2024-25 Survey target is 30% growth over five years via 17 growth engines. Statement 3 is wrong: India is the 2nd-largest fertiliser consumer. So only '1 and 2 only' fits; every option with statement 3 is wrong.
109.tq: 30% in 5 years via 17 growth engines; India 2nd in fertiliser use.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
**1 — correct:** AP supplies about **10%** of India's farm output.
**2 — correct:** **30% growth** over five years via **17 growth engines** (2024-25 Survey).
**3 — wrong:** India is the **2nd-largest** fertiliser consumer, not the largest.
xa: National agri-allied growth: **4.4%** a year over 5 years.
AP fertiliser use fell **80.78% → 38.1%** of allotment (2015-16 → 2016-17 AE).
Peak AP agri growth: **18.23% (2017-18)**.

109.s: Which of the following is the correct order of Andhra Pradesh's ranks in 2025–26 for eggs, meat and milk production, respectively?
109.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked first in eggs, fourth in meat and seventh in milk production.
109.tq: Retain the sequence of three rankings without reversing the commodities.
xs: Eggs **1st**, meat **4th**, milk **7th** — option **(3)** is correct.
SES 2025-26: eggs **2,739 crore**; meat **11.37 lakh MT**; milk **139.46 lakh MT**.
xa: AP is **1st** in fruits (**15.6%**) and tobacco exports (**67%**).

109.s: The ICAR Breed Conservation award associated with Andhra Pradesh relates to:
109.x: The ICAR Breed Conservation award was conferred in relation to Punganur cattle.
109.tq: Test the award-recipient association using closely related livestock alternatives.
xs: The ICAR **Breed Conservation award** was for **Punganur cattle** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is one of AP's **ICAR** recognitions listed with its awards and FIRSTs; the notes name no award for Gir, Ongole or Kangayam.
xa: **ICAR-NRC Banana** recognised AP as the **largest banana exporter**.
Livestock Census 2019: AP **2nd** in sheep (**176.3 lakh**) and poultry (~**1,079 lakh**).
AP was the **3rd** State to reach 100% household electrification.

109.s: Which institution recognised Andhra Pradesh as the largest banana exporter?
o: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education
Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority
109.x: ICAR-NRC Banana recognised Andhra Pradesh as the largest banana exporter.
109.tq: Identify the correct institution associated with a sector-specific recognition.
xs: **ICAR-NRC Banana** recognised AP as the **largest banana exporter** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is the **ICAR** national research centre for banana; the notes credit no other body with this recognition.
xa: ICAR's **Breed Conservation award** went to AP for **Punganur cattle**.
AP = **1st** in fruits (**15.6%** of national output), **3rd** in horticulture GVA.
AP = **6th largest exporting state** — **824** commodities to **194** countries (FY 2024-25).

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding selected socio-economic achievements of Andhra Pradesh:
1. Andhra Pradesh was the third State to achieve 100 per cent household electrification.
2. Andhra Pradesh ranked third in MGNREGS employment in 2025-26.
3. Andhra Pradesh ranked first in SHG-bank linkage in 2025-26.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: All three statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh was third in household electrification, third in MGNREGS employment in 2025-26, and first in SHG-bank linkage in 2025-26.
109.tq: Test multiple rank-based achievements while retaining the relevant years.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
**1:** AP was the **3rd** State to reach **100%** household electrification.
**2:** **3rd** in **MGNREGS** employment 2025-26.
**3:** **1st** in **SHG-bank linkage** (SES 2025-26).
xa: ICAR **Breed Conservation award** for **Punganur cattle**.
AP = **1st** in eggs and fruits.
Bank density: AP **14.98** branches per lakh vs Goa **43.31**.

109.s: Which one of the following correctly states Andhra Pradesh’s position in the production of fruits and horticulture?
o: Second in fruits, with 10.6 per cent of national output, and first in horticulture GVA
Third in fruits, with 15.6 per cent of national output, and second in horticulture GVA
First in fruits, with 15.6 per cent of national output, and third in horticulture GVA
First in fruits, with 5.8 per cent of national output, and seventh in horticulture GVA
109.x: Andhra Pradesh ranks first in fruit production, contributes 15.6 per cent of national fruit output, and ranks third in horticulture GVA.
109.tq: Keep production rank, national share and GVA rank as separate clues.
xs: **First in fruits**, **15.6%** of national output, **third in horticulture GVA** — option **(3)** is correct.
**5.8%** was AP's share of India's exports (**2020-21**), not fruit output.
xa: Horticulture output 2023-24: **365.92 lakh MT** on **45.59 lakh acres**.
AP = **2nd** in raw silk (after **Karnataka**).
ICAR-NRC Banana: AP = **largest banana exporter**.

109.s: Andhra Pradesh contributes approximately what share of India's cultured shrimp exports?
109.x: Andhra Pradesh accounts for about 75% of India's cultured-shrimp exports (SES 2025-26); it is also 1st in marine exports with a 43% share. The other percentages are not the cultured-shrimp figure.
109.tq: Discriminate between shrimp exports and total seafood exports.
xs: AP accounts for about **75%** of India's **cultured shrimp exports** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is also **1st in marine exports** with a **43%** share.
xa: Fishing & Aquaculture: AP's largest constant-price agri GVA (**₹90,673 crore**, 2025-26).
Fishing grew fastest in 2025-26 FAE at **17.69%**.
AP is **1st** in tobacco exports (**67%**).

109.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's national position (SES 2025-26):
1. It ranks second in raw silk production, after Karnataka.
2. It ranks first in tobacco exports, with a 67 per cent share.
3. It ranks first in milk production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Statement 1 is correct: AP is 2nd in raw silk, after Karnataka. Statement 2 is correct: AP is 1st in tobacco exports (67%). Statement 3 is wrong: AP is 7th in milk (139.46 lakh MT); it is 1st in eggs and fruits. So '1 and 2 only'; options with statement 3 are wrong.
109.tq: 1st: eggs, fruits, tobacco exports; 2nd: raw silk; 4th: meat; 7th: milk.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
**1 — correct:** **2nd** in raw silk, after **Karnataka**.
**2 — correct:** **1st** in tobacco exports (**67%**).
**3 — wrong:** AP is only **7th** in milk (**139.46 lakh MT**).
xa: AP is **1st** in eggs and fruits.
AP: **75%** of India's cultured shrimp exports.

109.s: Which sub-sector had the highest growth in 2024-25 FAE among the following?
109.x: Construction recorded the highest growth among the listed industrial sub-sectors at 9.55%. Manufacturing grew by 5.32%, electricity by 5.87% and mining by 2.70%.
109.tq: Select the maximum after comparing all four sub-sector growth rates.
xs: **Construction** grew fastest in 2024-25 FAE at **9.55%** — option **(1)** is correct.
Others: **Electricity 5.87%**, **Manufacturing 5.32%**, **Mining 2.70%** (slowest).
xa: Construction stayed fastest in 2025-26 (**14.18%**).
Manufacturing = **1,06,281** cr, about half of industry.

109.s: Which one of the following statements regarding historical sub-sector records is correct?
o: Electricity recorded its highest growth of 37.27% in 2020-21.
Mining recorded its lowest growth of -26.5% in 2019-20.
Manufacturing recorded its highest growth of 37.27% in 2019-20.
Mining recorded its lowest growth of -26.5% in 2020-21.
109.x: Mining recorded its lowest growth, -26.5%, in 2020-21. Electricity recorded its highest growth of 37.27% in 2019-20.
109.tq: Match the record percentage with both the correct sub-sector and year.
xs: **Mining recorded its lowest growth of -26.5% in 2020-21** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Electricity**'s record **37.27%** came in **2019-20**, not 2020-21 — option (1) is wrong.
**Manufacturing**'s record was **37.72%** in **2020-21**, not 37.27% in 2019-20 — option (3) is wrong.
xa: ⚠ **37.72%** (manufacturing, 2020-21) vs **37.27%** (electricity, 2019-20) — near-identical digits.
2020-21 was the lowest year overall: **1.52%** (constant) and **5.70%** (current).
2024-25 FAE: mining slowest industrial sub-sector at **2.70%**; construction fastest **9.55%**.
Services' lowest growth was also in **2020-21** (**-9.21%**).

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding services sub-sector growth in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Banking and insurance grew by 14.25 per cent in 2024-25.
2. Public administration recorded the lowest growth in 2024-25 at 0.09 per cent.
3. Communications was the top-performing services sub-sector in 2025-26 at 15.13 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: All three statements are correct: banking and insurance grew 14.25%, public administration recorded 0.09% in 2024-25, and communications led in 2025-26 with 15.13%.
109.tq: Check each year separately because the leading and lowest sub-sectors change across years.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
**1:** **Banking & Insurance** grew **14.25%** in 2024-25 (top services sub-sector).
**2:** **Public Administration** lowest in 2024-25 at **0.09%**.
**3:** **Communications** topped 2025-26 FAE at **15.13%**.
xa: 2025-26 ranks: Banking **13.59%** (2nd), Trade-Hotels **12.41%** (3rd), Public Admn **0.05%** (lowest).
SES 2025-26 revised 2024-25: Communications **18.70%**, Banking **16.93%**.
⚠ **Communications** = smallest sub-sector but fastest-growing in 2025-26.

109.s: How many sub-sectors constitute the services sector classification used for Andhra Pradesh?
109.x: The classification contains eight sub-sectors, including trade, transport, communications, banking, real estate, public administration and other services.
109.tq: Direct recall of a classification count.
xs: AP's services sector has **Eight** sub-sectors — option **(2)** is correct.

They are: **Trade, Hotels & Restaurants**; **Railways**; **Transport by other means & Storage**; **Communications**; **Banking & Insurance**; **Real Estate & Dwellings**; **Public Administration**; **Other Services**.
xa: Industry has **4** sub-sectors and agriculture **5**; all sectors together have **17** sub-sectors.
Largest: **Trade, Hotels & Restaurants** and **Real Estate & Dwellings**; smallest: **Railways** and **Communications**.
⚠ India's new services index covers **19** sub-sectors — do not confuse it with AP's eight.

109.s:
Consider the following statements about the services sub-sectors of Andhra Pradesh:
1. By GVA in 2024-25, the two largest were Trade, Hotels & Restaurants and Real Estate & Ownership of Dwellings.
2. By GVA in 2024-25, the two smallest were Railways and Communications.
3. Communications was the slowest-growing services sub-sector in 2025-26 (FAE).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
109.x: Statement 1 is correct: Trade, Hotels & Restaurants and Real Estate & Dwellings were the largest in 2024-25. Statement 2 is correct: Railways and Communications were the smallest. Statement 3 is wrong: Communications, though small, was the FASTEST-growing services sub-sector in 2025-26 (15.13%); Public Administration was the slowest (0.05%). Hence '1 and 2 only'.
109.tq: Communications = smallest but fastest-growing.

109.s: India's new services index, described as the services counterpart of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), has which of the following features?
o: 19 sub-sectors covering about 60 per cent of services, with base year 2024-25
17 sub-sectors covering about 50 per cent of services, with base year 2022-23
8 sub-sectors covering all services, with base year 2011-12
19 sub-sectors covering about 60 per cent of services, with base year 2011-12
109.x: The services index covers 19 sub-sectors (about 60% of services) with base year 2024-25 and is the services counterpart of the IIP. 17 sub-sectors and 2022-23 confuse it with the GVA classification and the new GDP base. Eight is the number of services sub-sectors in AP's GVA. 2011-12 is the old base still used by AP.
109.tq: Services index: 19 sub-sectors, ~60%, base 2024-25.
xs: The services index has **19 sub-sectors**, covers **~60%** of services, base **2024-25** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is the **services counterpart of the IIP** (15 Jul 2026).
**2011-12** is AP's GSDP base; **2022-23** is the new GDP base; **8** is AP's services sub-sector count.
xa: India's first **ISP** was released in **July 2026**.
New GDP series: FY26 tertiary growth **8.9%**.
AP has **17** sub-sectors across the three broad sectors.

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding rural workers in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Regular wage or salaried workers constituted 13.7%.
2. Casual labour constituted 33.8%.
3. The share of casual labour was higher than the corresponding Indian share of 22.5%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: All three statements are correct: regular wage or salaried workers formed 13.7%, casual labour 33.8%, and the latter exceeded India's 22.5%.
109.tq: Use both the state figures and the national comparator.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
**1:** rural regular wage/salaried = **13.7%**.
**2:** casual labour = **33.8%**.
xa: Nationally, **70-75%** of service workers are informal (PLFS).
AP workforce: agriculture **45.6%**, manufacturing **22.8%**, services **31.6%**.

109.s: Nationally, approximately what share of service workers are informal according to the cited PLFS-based estimate?
109.x: The cited national estimate places the share of informal service workers at approximately 70-75%.
109.tq: Recall the range rather than a single-point estimate.
xs: Nationally, **70-75%** of service workers are **informal** (PLFS) — option **(4)** is correct.
The figure is a **national** estimate (Nov 2025); the notes give no PLFS share of AP workers in services.
xa: Rural AP casual labour **33.8%** vs India **22.5%**.
Rural AP regular wage/salary workers: **13.7%**.
AP services share in workforce (SES 2024-25): **31.6%**.

109.s: Which set of cities emerged as locations for new IT parks in Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation?
109.x: After bifurcation left Andhra Pradesh without Hyderabad's IT export base, new IT parks came up in Visakhapatnam, Tirupati and Vijayawada.
109.tq: Recall the three-city location cluster.
xs: New IT parks: **Visakhapatnam, Tirupati and Vijayawada** — option **(2)** is correct.
Bifurcation left AP **without Hyderabad's IT export base**.
xa: RMZ's **GCC Park at Kapuluppada** (Visakhapatnam): part of a **US$10 bn** partnership + **1 GW** data-centre cluster.
Visakhapatnam hosts **Google data centre**, **TCS**, **Cognizant**.
AP is also courting **Capgemini** (13 Mar 2026).

109.s: Which institutions constitute the education and health anchors identified for Andhra Pradesh's emerging services sector?
o: AIIMS Mangalagiri, IIM Visakhapatnam and IIT Tirupati
AIIMS Tirupati, IIM Mangalagiri and IIT Visakhapatnam
AIIMS Visakhapatnam, IIM Tirupati and IIT Mangalagiri
AIIMS Vijayawada, IIM Guntur and IIT Amaravati
109.x: The identified anchors are AIIMS Mangalagiri, IIM Visakhapatnam and IIT Tirupati.
109.tq: Match each institution with its correct Andhra Pradesh location.
xs: **AIIMS Mangalagiri, IIM Visakhapatnam and IIT Tirupati** — option **(1)** is correct.
They are the education and health anchors named in the **Industrial Policy 2024-29**; the other options swap the cities.
xa: IT parks: **Visakhapatnam, Tirupati, Vijayawada**.
**GCC Park at Kapuluppada** (Visakhapatnam) — **US$10 bn** partnership.
Industrial Development Policy **4.0 (2024-29)** puts manufacturing at the centre.

109.s: According to data as on March 2016, the districts having the maximum number of post offices, telephone connections and bank branches respectively were:
109.x: As per the March 2016 data, Chittoor had the most post offices, while Visakhapatnam led in both telephone connections and bank branches.
109.tq: Sequence-based recall of three linked district leaders.
xs: **Chittoor, Visakhapatnam and Visakhapatnam** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC G2 2017, data as on March 2016).
Chittoor led post offices; Visakhapatnam led both telephone connections and bank branches.
xa: ⚠ Latest (31 Dec 2024): post offices led by **Prakasam (668)**; bank branches still **Visakhapatnam (624)**.
Landlines (13 old districts): **Krishna (8,764)**; mobiles (2025): **Visakhapatnam (3.77 lakh)**.
Answers change with district reorganisation — note the **data year**.

109.s: Which district had the highest number of post offices as on 31 December 2024?
109.x: Prakasam had the highest number of post offices, with 668, followed by SPSR Nellore with 643 and YSR Kadapa with 580.
109.tq: Direct district-wise leader recall.
xs: **Prakasam** led with **668** post offices (31 Dec 2024) — option **(2)** is correct.
Then **SPSR Nellore (643)** and **YSR Kadapa (580)**; **Visakhapatnam** had the **fewest** (**156-158**).
xa: SES 2025-26 update: **10,660** post offices (31 Dec 2025).
Rural districts have more branch POs (universal service).

109.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
109.x: Visakhapatnam had the fewest post offices, whereas Prakasam had the highest number. Visakhapatnam led in mobile connections and bank branches, while Krishna led in landline connections.
109.tq: Find the one reversed district-leader relationship.
xs: **Post offices — Visakhapatnam** is NOT correct — option **(3)**: Visakhapatnam has the **fewest** post offices; **Prakasam (668)** leads.
Visakhapatnam leads **mobiles (3.77 lakh)** and **bank branches (624)**; **Krishna (8,764)** leads landlines.
xa: ⚠ **Visakhapatnam** = most bank branches but **fewest** post offices.
Mobile connections state total: **46.05 lakh**; then Guntur, Tirupati.
Telephone exchanges (SES 2025-26): highest **NTR**, East Godavari, Visakhapatnam.

109.s: Which district recorded the highest Credit-Deposit ratio in Andhra Pradesh according to APSES 2024-25?
109.x: Palnadu recorded the highest Credit-Deposit ratio at 264%.
109.tq: Direct recall of the extreme value in a comparison pair.
xs: **Palnadu** had the highest CD ratio — **264%** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Tirupati** had the **lowest** (**85%**).
xa: State CD ratio: **157.40%** (RBI norm **60%**).
Deposits **₹6,08,834 crore**; credit **₹9,58,277 crore**.
Several districts have CD ratios **>200%**.

109.s: Which one of the following statements about Visakhapatnam as an urban service hub is correct?
o: It has the highest number of bank branches and mobile connections, and hosts Google data centre, TCS and Cognizant facilities.
It is the location of IIT Tirupati and AIIMS Mangalagiri.
It has the highest post-office count and the lowest number of bank branches.
It has the lowest Credit-Deposit ratio and no major IT presence.
109.x: Visakhapatnam leads in bank branches and mobile connections and has the presence of Google data centre, TCS and Cognizant.
109.tq: Combine several identifying features to recognise the correct urban hub.
xs: Visakhapatnam has the **most bank branches and mobile connections** and hosts **Google data centre, TCS and Cognizant** — option **(1)** is correct.
**IIT** is at **Tirupati** and **AIIMS** at **Mangalagiri**; Visakhapatnam has the **fewest** post offices; the lowest CD ratio is **Tirupati (85%)**.
xa: Visakhapatnam: **624** bank branches, **3.77 lakh** mobile connections.
**GCC Park at Kapuluppada** — **US$10 bn** partnership.
**Visakhapatnam ER**: **10 districts**, target **$750-800 bn by 2047**.

109.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding banking infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The State had 14.98 bank branches per lakh population and 43.31% credit-deposit ratio.
The State had 10,660 bank branches and a credit-deposit ratio of 43.31%.
The State had 8,555 bank branches and a credit-deposit ratio below 100%.
The State had 8,555 bank branches and a credit-deposit ratio of 157.4%.
109.x: Andhra Pradesh had 8,555 bank branches and a credit-deposit ratio of 157.4%; several districts recorded ratios above 200%.
109.tq: Separate statewide totals and ratios from the per-lakh population comparison.
xs: AP had **8,555** bank branches and a CD ratio of **157.4%** — option **(4)** is correct.
**14.98** is branches per lakh population; **43.31** is Goa's density; **10,660** is the post-office count.
xa: RBI CD-ratio norm: **60%**; several districts **>200%**.
Highest district CD: **Palnadu 264%**; lowest **Tirupati 85%**.
Deposits **₹6,08,834 crore**; credit **₹9,58,277 crore**.

109.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the distribution of branch post offices and commercial bank branches in the comparison provided?
o: Urban districts generally have more branch post offices, while Andhra Pradesh has 43.31 commercial bank branches per lakh population.
Rural districts generally have more branch post offices, while Andhra Pradesh has 14.98 commercial bank branches per lakh population compared with Goa's 43.31.
Rural districts generally have fewer branch post offices, while Andhra Pradesh has 157.4 branches per lakh population.
Rural districts and urban districts have an equal number of branch post offices, while Goa has 14.98 branches per lakh population.
109.x: Universal-service requirements result in more branch post offices in rural districts. Andhra Pradesh has 14.98 commercial bank branches per lakh population, against Goa's 43.31.
109.tq: Combine the distributional explanation with the exact inter-State figure comparison.
xs: **Rural districts have more branch POs**; AP has **14.98** bank branches per lakh vs **Goa's 43.31** — option **(2)** is correct.
Rural branch POs reflect **universal service**; urban districts have fewer.
**157.4** is AP's CD ratio (%), not branch density.
xa: Density source: **SDG India Index 2023-24**.
Post offices: **9,101** of **10,672** are branch POs (BPO).
⚠ **Visakhapatnam** (urban) has the fewest post offices (**156-158**).

109.s:
Consider the following statements about backward areas of Andhra Pradesh:
1. North Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema are the recognised backward regions of the State.
2. The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provides a special development package for nine backward districts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
109.x: Statement 1 is correct: North Coastal Andhra (Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam) and Rayalaseema (Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur, Chittoor) are the recognised backward regions. Statement 2 is wrong: the package covers SEVEN backward districts (3 + 4). Hence '1 only'.
109.tq: 3 North Coastal + 4 Rayalaseema = 7 backward districts.

109.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the seven backward districts covered by the special development package under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
109.x: Nalgonda is not an Andhra Pradesh backward district; it is located in Telangana. The seven districts include Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor.
109.tq: NOT-correctly-matched question using a neighbouring State's district as the trap.
xs: **Nalgonda** is NOT among them — option **(3)** is correct; it is in **Telangana**.
**Srikakulam** (North Coastal) and **Kurnool**, **Chittoor** (Rayalaseema) are among the **7** districts.
xa: Others: **Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Kadapa, Anantapur**.
Coastal Andhra (**Krishna-Guntur**) is the more developed region.
**Vizianagaram** is also an **Aspirational District** (NITI Aayog).

109.s:
With reference to the Aspirational Districts Programme and backward-region assistance, consider the following statements:
1. The Aspirational Districts Programme covers 112 districts.
2. Vizianagaram is among the districts of Andhra Pradesh covered by the programme.
3. The Backward Regions Grant Fund is currently an active programme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Backward Regions Grant Fund is now defunct, so statement 3 is false.
109.tq: Statement question using the current-status trap in a welfare programme.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
**1 — correct:** the **Aspirational Districts Programme** (NITI Aayog) covers **112** districts.
**2 — correct:** AP's include **Vizianagaram**.
**3 — wrong:** the **BRGF** is now **defunct**.
xa: AP Reorganisation Act, 2014: package for **7 backward districts**.
MPI headcount: highest **Kurnool (12.84%)**.

109.s:
Consider the following statements about multidimensional poverty (MPI headcount) in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Kurnool has the highest headcount among AP's districts.
2. West Godavari has the highest headcount among AP's districts.
3. AP's headcount (6.06%) is below India's (14.96%).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
109.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kurnool has the highest MPI headcount (12.84%). Statement 2 is wrong: West Godavari has the LOWEST (2.42%). Statement 3 is correct: AP 6.06% vs India 14.96%. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
109.tq: Kurnool highest, West Godavari lowest.

109.s:
Consider the following statements about the number of districts in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Undivided AP had 20 districts on 1 November 1956.
2. Residual AP had 23 districts in 2014.
3. The reorganisation of 4 April 2022 raised the number to 26.
4. The latest number of districts is 28.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Statement 1 is correct: 20 districts in 1956. Statement 2 is wrong: residual AP had 13 districts in 2014. Statement 3 is correct: 26 districts after 4 April 2022. Statement 4 is correct: the latest count is 28 (Markapuram among the new districts). Hence '1, 3 and 4 only'.

109.s: Why are district-level GDDP and per capita income series before and after 2022 not directly comparable?
o: The district boundaries and composition changed after reorganisation.
Only urban districts were counted before 2022.
Per capita income was replaced by national income.
109.x: District reorganisation altered the boundaries and composition of districts, making pre-2022 and post-2022 district-level GDDP and PCI series not directly comparable.
109.tq: Application question linking administrative boundary changes with statistical comparability.
xs: **District boundaries and composition changed** — option **(1)** is correct.
Districts went **13 → 26** (4 April 2022) → **28**, so pre- and post-**2022** GDDP/PCI series do not match.
GDDP was not discontinued, nor was PCI replaced.
xa: PCI is computed on **NSDP**.
"Maximum district" answers also change with reorganisation — note the data year.

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's public finances:
1. The debt-GSDP ratio in 2024-25 RE was below 30 per cent.
2. Capital outlay more than doubled, from ₹16,141 crore in 2024-25 to ₹33,135 crore in 2025-26 RE.
3. Restructuring of 370 loans saved about ₹8,269 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Statement 1 is wrong: debt was 35.15% of GSDP in 2024-25 RE (about 35%), not below 30%. Statement 2 is correct: capital outlay rose from ₹16,141 crore to ₹33,135 crore. Statement 3 is correct: 370 loans were restructured, saving ₹8,269 crore. So '2 and 3 only'; every option with statement 1 is wrong.
109.tq: Debt ~35% of GSDP; capex doubled to ₹33,135 cr; 370 loans saved ₹8,269 cr.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
**1 — wrong:** debt/GSDP was **35.15%** in 2024-25 RE, not below 30%.
**2 — correct:** capital outlay **₹16,141 cr → ₹33,135 cr**.
**3 — correct:** **370** loans restructured, saving **₹8,269 cr**.
xa: Planning Dept priority: step up **capital expenditure**.

109.s: The Sunrise Andhra Pradesh Vision 2029 was launched in which year?
109.x: The Sunrise Andhra Pradesh Vision 2029 was launched in 2016 for the residual State after bifurcation.
109.tq: Directly recall the launch year of a State vision document.
xs: **Sunrise AP Vision 2029** was launched in **2016** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was for the **residual AP** after **2014**.
xa: Goals: **top three States by 2022**, **best State by 2029**, **most preferred investment destination by 2050**.
HDI target: **0.9 by 2029** via the **Saturation approach**.
**Vision 2020** (**1999**) was undivided AP's first long-term vision.

109.s: Vision 2020, described as the first long-term vision of undivided Andhra Pradesh, was released in 1999 by the government headed by:
109.x: Vision 2020 was released in 1999 by the Chandrababu Naidu government as the first long-term vision of undivided Andhra Pradesh.
109.tq: Use the person-document association rather than the target year alone.
xs: **Vision 2020** was released in **1999** by the **N. Chandrababu Naidu** government — option **(1)** is correct.
It was the **first long-term vision** of **undivided AP**, with Naidu's micro-plan.
xa: It set **first-rank targets** for several products; PYQ answer "**All the above**" (APPSC 2019).
Naidu also launched **Swarna Andhra @2047** on **13 Dec 2024**.
Successor: **Sunrise AP Vision 2029** (2016).

109.s: Under Vision 2020, the Andhra Pradesh Government identified first-rank targets for several products. Which of the following is the appropriate answer?
109.x: Vision 2020 (released 1999) set first-rank targets for several products across sectors, not for agriculture, horticulture or fisheries alone, so the APPSC 2019 key answer is 'All the above'.
109.tq: Recognise the inclusive “all the above” answer when the vision document covers several product areas.
xs: **All the above** — option **(4)** is correct (APPSC 2019 key).
**Vision 2020** (**1999**, Naidu government) set **first-rank targets for several products**, not one sector alone.
xa: Vision 2020 = first long-term vision of **undivided AP**; Naidu's micro-plan.
**Sunrise AP Vision 2029** followed for residual AP (**2016**).
**Swarna Andhra @2047** aligns with **Viksit Bharat 2047**.

109.s: What is the stated objective of Andhra Pradesh regarding the frequency with which its per capita income should double?
109.x: Andhra Pradesh aims to double its per capita income every five years.
109.tq: Test the time interval directly using numerical discrimination.
xs: AP aims to **double PCI every five years** — option **(3)** is correct.
This is the PCI target under **Vision 2029** and **Swarna Andhra @2047**.
xa: Vision 2030 (interim): PCI **₹5.15 lakh**.
2028-29: per capita GSDP **₹5.43 lakh**.

109.s:
Match the goals of Sunrise Andhra Pradesh Vision 2029 with their target years.
List-I (Goal)
a. Among the top three States
b. The best State in India
c. The most preferred global investment destination
List-II (Target year)
i. 2022
ii. 2029
iii. 2050
Select the correct code:
109.x: Sunrise AP Vision 2029 set three staged goals: among the top three States by 2022 (a-i), the best State in India by 2029 (b-ii), and the most preferred global investment destination by 2050 (c-iii). The other codes swap these years.
109.tq: 2022 top three, 2029 best State, 2050 global investment destination.
xs: **a-i, b-ii, c-iii** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Top three States by 2022**; **best State by 2029**; **most preferred global investment destination by 2050**.
xa: HDI target: **0.9 by 2029** via the **Saturation approach**.
Sunrise AP Vision 2029 launched **2016**.

109.s: Under Sunrise Andhra Pradesh Vision 2029, what Human Development Index (HDI) target was set for 2029, and through which approach?
o: 0.9, through the Saturation approach covering every eligible person
109.x: The vision targeted an HDI of 0.9 by 2029 through the Saturation approach, under which every eligible person is covered (APPSC-GS 2018 key). 0.7 and 0.8 are wrong values. Trickle-down is the opposite of saturation, which covers everyone directly.
109.tq: HDI 0.9 by 2029, Saturation approach.
xs: Sunrise AP Vision 2029 set **HDI 0.9 by 2029** through the **Saturation approach** — option **(1)** is correct.
Saturation means **every eligible person** is covered (APPSC-GS 2018 key).
**0.7** and **0.8** are wrong values; a trickle-down approach is not what the Vision names.
xa: Vision 2029 goals: **top three States by 2022**, **best State by 2029**, **most preferred investment destination by 2050**.
Launched in **2016** for residual AP.
Earlier vision: **Vision 2020**, released **1999** by the Naidu government.

109.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

b. Skilled workforce
c. Exports

List-II (Target by 2047)

Unemployment **<2%** (from **5.8%**); women's workforce participation **>80%** (from ~**45.8%**).

109.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the 10 Padi Sutralu of Swarna Andhra?
o: Deep Tech in all walks of life
109.x: Universal Basic Income is not listed among the 10 Padi Sutralu. The listed principles include Water Security, Global-Best Logistics and Deep Tech in all walks of life.
109.tq: Find the item that does not belong to a named list.
xs: **Universal Basic Income** is NOT a Padi Sutra — option **(3)** is correct.
The sutras include **Water Security** (4), **Global Best Logistics** (6) and **Deep Tech** (10).
xa: Full list: **Zero Poverty**, Population Management & HRD, Skilling & Employment, Water Security, Farmer-Agri Tech, Logistics, Energy cost optimisation, Product Perfection, **Swachh Andhra**, Deep Tech.

Plus **12 thematic sectors** and **651 KPIs**.

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Swarna Andhra Vision 2047:
1. It is aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047.
2. It seeks to develop a 'Wealthy, Healthy and Happy' Andhra Pradesh.
3. It is guided by Ten Sutras.

109.x: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 is aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047, adopts the goal of a Wealthy, Healthy and Happy State, and is guided by Ten Sutras.

xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** is correct.

**2:** its aim is a "**Wealthy, Healthy and Happy**" AP.

xa: Launched by CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu** on **13 Dec 2024**.

109.s: What annual growth rate is envisaged for Andhra Pradesh under the long-term Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 target?
109.x: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 envisages annual growth of 15 per cent for achieving its long-term targets.

xa: Vision 2030 (interim) also assumes **15%** growth (GSDP **₹31 lakh crore**).

Investment: **₹40.43 lakh cr** = **77%** private + **23%** public.

109.s: The ten guiding principles of Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 are known as:
109.x: The ten guiding principles are called Padi Sutralu.

xs: The ten guiding principles are the **Padi Sutralu** — option **(4)** is correct.

109.s:
Match the following milestones of Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 with their targets.

 a. 2024-25

 c. 2047-48

109.s: Who launched the ‘Swarna Andhra @2047’ vision on 13 December 2024?
109.x: Swarna Andhra @2047 was launched by Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on 13 December 2024.
109.tq: Direct recall of the person associated with a policy launch.
xs: **N. Chandrababu Naidu** launched Swarna Andhra @2047 on **13 Dec 2024** — option **(3)** is correct.

xa: Naidu's government also released **Vision 2020** in **1999**.

109.s: Which of the following correctly represents the target for GSDP under Swarna Andhra @2047?

109.s: Which target combination is correctly matched with Swarna Andhra @2047?
o: Unemployment — less than 2%; women’s workforce participation — more than 80%

109.s: Which of the following sets correctly represents the three economic regions identified by the Government of Andhra Pradesh?

Quarterly GSDP reviews and a manufacturing commission
Monthly GSDP reviews and an AI-based task force
109.x: Monthly GSDP reviews and an AI-based task force were ordered for monitoring the 2026–27 KPIs.
109.tq: Match the frequency of review with the specific monitoring institution instead of confusing it with a general planning body.
xs: **Monthly GSDP reviews** and an **AI-based task force** for 2026-27 KPIs — option **(4)** is correct.
The notes record no fiscal-review board, investment authority or manufacturing commission for this.
xa: Planning Dept priorities: **capital expenditure**, **manufacturing** revival, fast-tracking industrial projects.
Swarna Andhra monitoring: **651 KPIs**, **Monthly Economic Reports**.
Q2 2025-26: mega projects **₹2.88 lakh cr**.

109.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's Zero Poverty-P4 initiative:
1. P4 stands for Public-Private-People Partnership.
2. It was launched on Ugadi, 30 March 2025.
3. Its nodal body is the Swarna Andhra P4 Foundation under the Fisheries Department.
4. Well-off Margadarsis adopt poor Bangaru Kutumbam families.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: P4 = Public-Private-People Partnership, launched on Ugadi (30 March 2025), in which well-off Margadarsis adopt poor Bangaru Kutumbam families. Statement 3 is wrong: the Swarna Andhra P4 Foundation is under the Planning Department, not Fisheries. Hence '1, 2 and 4 only'.
109.tq: Margadarsi = mentor; Bangaru Kutumbam = family adopted; nodal = Planning Dept.

109.s: Which of the following is NOT a model listed under the P4 programme?
109.x: The listed P4 models are Adopt a Family, Adopt a Community and Fund a Need. Adopt a District is not listed.
109.tq: Find the extra item in a programme’s official model list.
xs: **Adopt a District** is NOT a P4 model — option **(1)** is correct.
The models are **Adopt a Family**, **Adopt a Community** and **Fund a Need**.
xa: ⚠ **Margadarsis** = well-off mentors; **Bangaru Kutumbam** = poor families adopted.
P4's aim = **poverty eradication** (asked in 2025).
Nodal body: **Swarna Andhra P4 Foundation** (Planning Dept.).

109.s: Which policy contains the goal ‘One Entrepreneur in One Family’?
109.x: The ‘One Entrepreneur in One Family’ goal is part of the MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy.
109.tq: Match a distinctive policy phrase with its policy document.
xs: "**One Entrepreneur in One Family**" is the goal of the **MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy** — option **(3)** is correct.
Its **2026** version gives incentives to **women-led units**.
xa: **Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29)**.
**Aviation Policy 2026-31 (APAP-2026)**.
Draft **Population Management Policy 2026**: **₹25,000** incentive for a second/third child.

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the draft Population Management Policy 2026:
1. It proposes an incentive of ₹25,000 for a second or third child.
2. It proposes removal of the two-child norm for local polls.
3. Andhra Pradesh’s total fertility rate is stated as 1.5.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: All three statements are correct: the draft policy proposes a ₹25,000 incentive, removal of the two-child norm for local polls and records AP’s TFR as 1.5.
109.tq: Test several provisions of a policy through coded statements.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
**1:** **₹25,000** incentive for a **second/third child**.
**2:** the **two-child norm** for local polls removed.
xa: Swarna Andhra Sutra 2 = **Population Management & HRD**.
**AP Wealth Fund** (Budget 2026-27): **₹100 crore** seed corpus.

109.s: Which one of the following statements about the Visakhapatnam Economic Region (VER) is correct?
o: It covers 10 districts, is a growth-hub pilot with NITI Aayog and targets an economy of $750-800 billion by 2047
It covers 9 districts and targets a GSDP of $2.4 trillion by 2047
It is the only economic region of the State and covers all 28 districts
It covers 10 districts and was set up under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014
109.x: VER covers 10 districts, is a growth-hub pilot with NITI Aayog, and targets $750-800 billion by 2047. Nine districts is the Amaravati ER, and $2.4 trillion is the State-wide Swarna Andhra GSDP target. The State has three economic regions (Visakhapatnam, Amaravati, Tirupati), not one. VER was launched on 13 Nov 2025, not under the 2014 Act.
109.tq: VER 10 districts + NITI pilot, $750-800 bn by 2047; Amaravati 9, Tirupati 10.
xs: VER covers **10 districts**, is a **NITI Aayog** growth-hub pilot and targets **$750-800 bn by 2047** — option **(1)** is correct.
**9 districts** is the **Amaravati ER**; **$2.4 trillion** is the State GSDP target.
AP has **three** regions (Visakhapatnam, Amaravati, Tirupati); VER was launched **13 Nov 2025**, not under the **2014** Act.
xa: VER investment potential: **₹9.5 lakh crore**.
**Tirupati ER**: **10** districts.

109.s:
With reference to the Socio-Economic Survey (SES) 2025–26 of Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. It was not tabled during the Budget Session.
2. It was released later on 12 April 2026.
3. Its First Advance Estimates placed Andhra Pradesh's growth below the national growth rate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: The SES 2025–26 was not tabled in the Budget Session and came out later on 12 April 2026. Its FAE placed Andhra Pradesh's growth at 9.88%, above India's 7.4%, making statement 3 false.
109.tq: Split the statements by checking the release detail and the direction of comparison.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
**1 — correct:** SES 2025-26 was **not tabled** in the Budget session.
**2 — correct:** it came out later (**12 Apr 2026**).
**3 — wrong:** FAE growth **9.88%** (constant) was **above** India's **7.4%**.
xa: Current prices 2025-26: AP **10.75%** vs India **8.0%**.
AP GSDP 2025-26 (FAE): **₹17.62 lakh cr**.
⚠ AP was slower than India in **2023-24** (**6.18%** vs **8.2%**).

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the sectoral composition of GVA:
1. Services account for about 52.9% of India's GVA under the new series for 2024–25.
2. Services account for about 43% of Andhra Pradesh's GVA.
3. Andhra Pradesh has a higher services share than the national average.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Services constitute 52.9% of India's GVA and 43% of Andhra Pradesh's GVA. Thus, Andhra Pradesh's services share is lower, making statement 3 false.
109.tq: Test the direction of the comparison after identifying both percentage values.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
**1 — correct:** India's services = **52.9%** of GVA (new series 2024-25).
**2 — correct:** AP's services ≈ **43%**.
**3 — wrong:** AP's share **trails** India's **50%+**.
xa: **Tamil Nadu** services share: **53.54%**.
AP services grew **10.67%** in 2025-26 FAE.
Public administration growth near zero (**0.05%**).

109.s: A reported growth rate of 11.43% for Andhra Pradesh in 2021–22 was subsequently revised to:
109.x: The initially reported record growth of 11.43% for 2021–22 was later revised to 7.14% because advance estimates are subject to revision.
109.tq: Test the revision from the initial estimate to the later figure.
xs: 2021-22's "record" **11.43%** was later revised to **7.14%** — option **(1)** is correct.
Advance estimates get revised — always quote the estimate stage.
xa: 2021-22 current-price series: **17.36%** (SRE), the highest current-price growth.
2024-25 real growth revised **9.24% → 8.27%** at FRE.

109.s:
Assertion (A): Andhra Pradesh's GSDP growth can fluctuate significantly with the monsoon.
Reason (R): Agriculture has a high share in Andhra Pradesh's economy.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
109.x: Both statements are true, and the high share of agriculture makes overall GSDP more sensitive to monsoon conditions.
109.tq: Check whether the structural fact directly explains the observed economic volatility.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)** is correct.
AP's high agriculture share makes GSDP swing with the monsoon: **-1.58%** (2023-24) → **+10.70%** (2024-25).
xa: Agriculture supports **60%** of AP's population.
AP's agriculture share ≈ **twice** India's **~18%**.
2023-24 was the only year of agri contraction.

109.s: In Q2 2025–26, which sector was reported to be the best-performing sector in Andhra Pradesh, with a growth rate of 13.5%?
109.x: Agriculture was the best-performing sector in Q2 2025–26, recording growth of 13.5%.
109.tq: Link the performance ranking with the stated sector-specific growth rate.
xs: **Agriculture** was the best-performing sector in Q2 2025-26 at **13.5%** — option **(1)** is correct.
Industry grew **10.6%** and services **9.9%**.
xa: Annual FAE 2025-26: agri-allied **10.14%**, led by **fisheries**.
Overall quarterly update (Aug 2026): **10.7%**.
⚠ FAE fastest sector = **services (10.67%)**.

110.s:
Consider the following statements about per capita income (PCI):
1. PCI rises only when national income grows faster than population.
2. Population growth, low productivity and a low-income, low-saving 'vicious circle' explain slow growth of PCI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
110.x: Statement 1 is correct: PCI = income / population, so it rises only if income grows faster than population. Statement 2 is correct: population growth, low productivity and the low-income, low-saving vicious circle are the causes of slow PCI growth. Hence 'Both 1 and 2'.
110.tq: PCI is a ratio - watch both numerator (income) and denominator (population).

110.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the distinction between per capita GSDP and per capita income?
o: PCI is based on NSDP divided by population.
Per capita GSDP is a gross measure.
Gross measures should be compared with gross measures and net measures with net measures.
Per capita GSDP and PCI are interchangeable terms.
110.x: Per capita GSDP and PCI are not interchangeable. Per capita GSDP is gross, whereas PCI is based on the net measure, NSDP.
110.tq: Find the statement that reverses the central net-versus-gross distinction.
xs: The NOT-correct statement is **(4)**: per capita GSDP and PCI are **not interchangeable**.
**PCI** = **NSDP ÷ population** (net); per capita **GSDP** is a **gross** measure.
Statements (1)–(3) are correct: match **gross with gross, net with net**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** "GSDP ÷ population" is loose; the Survey's PCI is **NSDP-based**.
⚠ Never compare AP's per capita GSDP with India's per capita income.
2023-24: AP per capita GSDP **₹2,70,295** vs India per capita GDP **₹2,15,935**.

110.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the measurement of per capita income:
1. The Survey-based measure uses Net State Domestic Product as the aggregate.
2. Net State Domestic Product is measured after accounting for depreciation.
3. Per capita income may be expressed at current prices or constant prices.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: All three statements are correct. The Survey's per capita income is based on NSDP, which is net of depreciation, and it may be measured at current or constant prices.
110.tq: Check each component of the definition separately before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
**1:** the Survey's PCI uses **NSDP**.
**2:** NSDP is **net** — after **depreciation**.
**3:** PCI can be at **current prices** (include inflation) or **constant (2011-12) prices** (real growth).
xa: **DDP** (district GDP) is compiled by the State **DES**, also nodal agency for GSDP.

110.s:
Assertion (A): Per capita income alone cannot provide a complete picture of economic well-being.
Reason (R): It is an average measure that can conceal inequality and does not account for differences in the cost of living.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
110.x: Both the assertion and reason are true. Since per capita income is an average and ignores inequality and cost-of-living variation, it cannot fully represent economic well-being.
110.tq: Test whether the reason directly explains the limitation stated in the assertion.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)** is correct.
PCI is an **average**: it **hides inequality** and **ignores cost-of-living differences** — so it cannot show full well-being.
xa: High PCI can coexist with **poverty + inequality**; the **P4** scheme targets that gap.
Karnataka: **Bengaluru Urban** PCI **₹8,55,960** vs State **₹3,86,156**.
Telangana: **Rangareddy ₹9.5 lakh** vs **Vikarabad ₹1.8 lakh** (2023-24).

110.s: In 2015-16, the per capita income figures cited for Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, respectively, were:
110.x: The cited 2015-16 figures were ₹15,454 for Telangana and ₹8,979 for Andhra Pradesh.
110.tq: Read the State order in the question carefully before comparing the values.
xs: 2015-16: Telangana **₹15,454** and AP **₹8,979** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2023 key, figures as keyed).
**₹93,903** is AP's PCI at bifurcation (**2014-15**).
xa: Pre-1956, Telangana already had **higher PCI and revenue** than Andhra State.
Telangana PCI 2022-23: **₹3.54 lakh** — richest major State.

110.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the relative per capita income of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh:
1. Telangana's per capita income was 6% above Andhra Pradesh's in 2004-05.
2. It was 1.3 times Andhra Pradesh's in 2013-14.
3. It was 1.35 times Andhra Pradesh's in 2024-25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: All three stated comparisons are correct: 6% higher in 2004-05, 1.3 times in 2013-14, and 1.35 times in 2024-25.
110.tq: Track the changing relative multiple across the three specified years.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Telangana's economy = **96.5%** of AP's size (2024-25).
Metro **Hyderabad** = **47.5%** of Telangana's output.
⚠ GDP share 2023-24: **Telangana 4.9%** > **AP 4.7%**.

110.s: Before the formation of Andhra Pradesh in 1956, the higher per capita income and revenue of Telangana were used by which body to argue that Telangana was viable on its own?
110.x: The Hyderabad PCC used Telangana's higher per capita income and revenue to argue for its independent viability in the context of the SRC discussions of 1955.
110.tq: Match the institutional actor with the argument it advanced.
xs: The **Hyderabad PCC** argued Telangana was viable alone — option **(2)** is correct (before the **SRC, 1955**).
It cited Telangana's **higher PCI and revenue** than Andhra State.
The **National Income Committee (1951)** made India's first PCI estimate — it argued nothing on Telangana.
xa: First national PCI estimate: **₹225** for **1948-49**.
Telangana vs AP gap later: **1.3x** (2013-14).

110.s:
Consider the following statements about the history of per capita income (PCI):
1. The National Income Committee (1951) estimated India's PCI for 1948-49 at ₹225.
2. Andhra Pradesh's PCI rose from ₹7,781 in 1960 to about ₹2.07 lakh in 2021-22.
3. Andhra Pradesh's PCI at bifurcation (2014-15) was ₹8,979.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: Statement 1 is correct: the National Income Committee put 1948-49 PCI at ₹225. Statement 2 is correct: ₹7,781 in 1960 against ₹2.07 lakh in 2021-22 (APPSC-GS 2023 key). Statement 3 is wrong: PCI at bifurcation was ₹93,903; ₹8,979 is AP's 2015-16 figure as keyed in a PYQ. So '1 and 2 only'; every option with statement 3 is wrong.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
**1 — correct:** **National Income Committee (1951)**: 1948-49 PCI **₹225**.
**3 — wrong:** PCI at bifurcation was **₹93,903**; **₹8,979** is a keyed **2015-16** figure.
xa: 2021-22 PCI later revised (older notes **₹1,97,214** SRE; latest **₹1,93,703**).
2020-21 PCI: about **₹1.70 lakh** (SES).

110.s: In which year did India's per capita income record its fastest growth among the years specified?
110.x: The fastest growth was recorded in 2021-22, at 18.6 percent, reflecting the post-COVID rebound.
110.tq: Link the peak growth rate with the post-COVID rebound.
xs: India's PCI grew fastest in **2021-22** (**+18.6%**) — option **(3)** is correct — a **post-COVID rebound**.
xa: ⚠ AP's PCI grew **15.26%** in 2021-22 — **below** India's that year.
AP's lowest PCI growth: **4.10% (2019-20)**.

110.s: Which of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's per capita income growth is correct?
o: The slowest growth occurred in 2021-22 at 4.10%.
The fastest growth occurred in 2019-20 at 15.26%.
The fastest growth occurred in 2025-26 at 17.35%, while the slowest occurred in 2014-15 at 4.10%.
The fastest growth occurred in 2021-22 at 15.26%, while the slowest occurred in 2019-20 at 4.10%.
110.x: In the latest AP series, PCI growth was fastest at 15.26% in 2021-22 and slowest at 4.10% in 2019-20 (the SES 2024-25 series put the 2021-22 peak at 17.35%). Options A, B and C attach these rates to the wrong years.
110.tq: Separate the maximum and minimum values before checking the year attached to each.
xs: Fastest PCI growth **15.26% in 2021-22**, slowest **4.10% in 2019-20** — option **(4)** is correct (latest series).
Options (1)–(3) attach these rates to the wrong years.
xa: ⚠ The **SES 2024-25** series put the 2021-22 peak at **17.35%**.
India's 2021-22 PCI growth: **18.6%**.

110.s:
With reference to Andhra Pradesh's per capita income, consider the following statements:
1. It remained above the national average in every year covered by the comparison.
2. In 2025-26, AP's PCI growth was 10.43%.
3. India's PCI growth in 2025-26 was 10.43%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false; India's PCI growth in 2025-26 was 6.9%.
110.tq: Identify the statement with the reversed state and national growth figures.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
**1 — correct:** AP's PCI was **above India's every year** since 2014-15.
**2 — correct:** AP's PCI grew **10.43%** in 2025-26.
**3 — wrong:** India's PCI grew only **6.9%**.
xa: AP ≈ **1.34 times** the national figure.

110.s: Under the Swarna Andhra objective, the target for per capita income by 2047 is approximately:
110.x: Swarna Andhra envisages per capita income exceeding $42,000 by 2047, approximately equivalent to ₹55 lakh.
110.tq: Convert the stated dollar target into its approximate rupee expression.
xs: Swarna Andhra PCI target: **>$42,000** by 2047, i.e. ~**₹55 lakh** — option **(3)** is correct.
**₹5.43 lakh** is per capita GSDP target for **2028-29**; **₹2.94 lakh** is the 2025-26 PCI; **$42,000** is in dollars, not rupees.
xa: ⚠ Dollar and rupee targets are separate statements.
Vision aim: **double PCI every five years**.

110.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: India — lower-middle-income economy; per capita income $2,760
India — upper-middle-income economy; per capita income $4,636
110.x: India is a lower-middle-income economy with per capita income of about $2,760. $2,760 is India's own per capita figure, not a World Bank threshold, India is not upper-middle-income, and $42,000 is AP's Swarna Andhra PCI target for 2047.
110.tq: Start from the sure income classification and verify the associated dollar figure.
xs: **India — lower-middle-income economy; $2,760** per capita — option **(1)** is correct.
**$2,760** is India's own figure, not a threshold; **$42,000** is AP's 2047 PCI target.
xa: India's new-series income per person: **₹2,43,180** (₹20,265 a month).
Swarna Andhra target: AP PCI **>$42,000** (~**₹55 lakh**) by 2047.

110.s:
Assertion (A): Andhra Pradesh's per capita income has remained above India's per capita income in every year since 2014-15.
Reason (R): In 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh's per capita income was approximately 1.34 times the national figure.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
110.x: Both statements are true. The 2025-26 ratio is a particular-year comparison and does not explain the entire historical trend since 2014-15.
110.tq: Separate a true general trend from a true but non-explanatory supporting fact.
xs: **Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)** is correct.
**A:** AP's PCI has been above India's **every year since 2014-15**.
**R:** in **2025-26** AP's PCI ≈ **1.34 times** India's — one year's ratio, which cannot explain the whole trend.

110.s: According to the EAC-PM report on Relative Economic Performance of Indian States, the respective shares of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in national GDP in 2023-24 were:
110.x: The EAC-PM report placed Andhra Pradesh's share at 4.7 per cent and Telangana's at 4.9 per cent in FY 2023-24 national GDP.
110.tq: Check the order of the two States before comparing their shares.
xs: EAC-PM: **AP 4.7 per cent** and **Telangana 4.9 per cent** of national GDP (FY 2023-24) — option **(2)** is correct.
Option **(4)** reverses the two shares (APPSC-G2 2023 key).
xa: Report: **Relative Economic Performance of Indian States (1960-61 to 2023-24)**.
⚠ Telangana's GDP share is larger though its economy = **96.5%** of AP's size (2024-25).
Telangana PCI = **1.35 times** AP's (2024-25).

110.s:
Arrange the following States in descending order of per capita income as stated for 2022-23:
A. Telangana
B. Karnataka
C. Haryana
D. Tamil Nadu
110.x: The order is Telangana, Karnataka, Haryana and Tamil Nadu. Their cited figures include ₹3.54 lakh for Telangana, ₹3.44 lakh for Karnataka and ₹3.09 lakh for Tamil Nadu.
110.tq: Arrange the States by descending numerical magnitude.
xs: Descending order: **Telangana, Karnataka, Haryana, Tamil Nadu** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Telangana ₹3.54 lakh** > **Karnataka ₹3.44 lakh** > Haryana (then Gujarat) > **Tamil Nadu ₹3.09 lakh** (2022-23).
xa: Telangana = **richest major State**.
⚠ In **2025-26** Tamil Nadu (**₹4.08 lakh**) is **2nd after Karnataka**.
Telangana PCI = **1.35 times** AP's.

110.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relative position of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
o: Telangana's PCI was 0.96 times Andhra Pradesh's, and its economy was 1.35 times Andhra Pradesh's size.
Telangana's PCI was 1.35 times Andhra Pradesh's, and its economy was 96.5 per cent of Andhra Pradesh's size.
Telangana's PCI was 96.5 times Andhra Pradesh's, and its economy was 1.35 per cent of Andhra Pradesh's size.
Telangana's PCI was 1.35 times Andhra Pradesh's, and its economy was 47.5 per cent of Andhra Pradesh's size.
110.x: Telangana's PCI was stated to be 1.35 times Andhra Pradesh's, while its economy was 96.5 per cent of Andhra Pradesh's size.
110.tq: Keep the multiplier and percentage comparison attached to the correct variable.
xs: Telangana's PCI = **1.35 times** AP's, and its economy = **96.5 per cent** of AP's size — option **(2)** is correct (2024-25).
**47.5%** is metro **Hyderabad**'s share of Telangana's output.
xa: GDP share 2023-24: Telangana **4.9%** vs AP **4.7%**.

110.s: The rise in the Gini coefficient of per capita income across Indian States from 0.230 in 1994-95 to 0.261 in 2025-26 indicates:
110.x: The increase in the Gini coefficient indicates greater divergence in per capita income among Indian States.
110.tq: Read the direction of change in the inequality measure before interpreting it.
xs: A rising Gini (**0.230** in **1994-95** → **0.261** in **2025-26**) shows **divergence among States** — option **(3)** is correct.
A higher Gini means **more** inter-State inequality, not convergence or uniformity.
xa: AP is **not in that list**.
District gaps exist in every southern State (e.g. Bengaluru Urban **₹8,55,960**).

110.s: Which of the following coastal regions of Andhra Pradesh has historically been more developed than North Andhra and Rayalaseema?
110.x: The Krishna-Guntur coastal belt has historically been more developed than North Andhra and Rayalaseema.
110.tq: Identify the precise regional comparison rather than selecting a neighbouring region.
xs: The **Krishna-Guntur coastal belt** has historically been more developed — option **(2)** is correct.
Kadapa-Chittoor and Kurnool-Anantapur are in **Rayalaseema**; Srikakulam-Vizianagaram is **North Andhra** — the lagging regions.
xa: North Andhra: **Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam**.
Rayalaseema: **Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur, Chittoor**.
Economic regions: **Visakhapatnam (10)**, **Amaravati (9)**, **Tirupati (10)**.

110.s: The seven backward districts identified under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 consisted of:
o: Four Rayalaseema districts and three North Coastal districts
Three Rayalaseema districts and four North Coastal districts
Two Rayalaseema districts and five North Coastal districts
Four Coastal Andhra districts and three Rayalaseema districts
110.x: The backward-area package covered seven districts—four in Rayalaseema and three in the North Coastal region.
110.tq: Split the total into its two component regional counts.
xs: The **7** backward districts = **4 Rayalaseema + 3 North Coastal** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (4) is wrong: Coastal Andhra (Krishna-Guntur) is the **developed** belt.
xa: Package: **₹50 cr per district a year**; releases stalled.
⚠ **Nalgonda** (Telangana) is NOT an AP backward area (APPSC-GS 2022 key).

110.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Rayalaseema:
1. It is characterised by a rain-shadow location and drought-prone conditions.
2. It accounts for 43% of Andhra Pradesh's horticulture area.
3. It accounts for 52% of the State's horticulture output.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: Rayalaseema is rain-shadow and drought-prone, but has emerged as a horticulture hub with 43% of the area and 52% of the output.
110.tq: Test a regional disadvantage together with its later sectoral strength.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
**1:** Rayalaseema is **rain-shadow** and **drought-prone**.
**2 & 3:** it is now a **horticulture hub** — **43%** of area and **52%** of output.
xa: Rayalaseema districts: **Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur, Chittoor**.
**4** of the **7** backward districts are in Rayalaseema.

110.s: Which district recorded the lowest multidimensional poverty percentage among the old 13 districts of Andhra Pradesh on the NFHS-5 basis?
110.x: West Godavari recorded the lowest multidimensional poverty percentage at 2.42%.
110.tq: Discriminate between the lowest and higher district-level poverty figures.
xs: **West Godavari** had the lowest MPI share — **2.42%** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Kurnool** was the highest (**12.84%**, MPI **0.054**); **Vizianagaram 8.66%**, **Visakhapatnam 7.60%**.
xa: Basis: **NFHS-5**, old **13** districts.
⚠ **Nalgonda** (Telangana) is NOT an AP backward area.

110.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a major driver of Visakhapatnam's leading district per capita income?
110.x: The identified drivers were Vizag Port; RINL, Hindustan Shipyard and HPCL refinery; Rushikonda IT Park; and the Eastern Naval Command. Amaravati Capital Region Secretariat was not included in that list.
110.tq: Find the option outside the stated set of sectoral and institutional drivers.
xs: **Amaravati Capital Region Secretariat** is NOT a driver — option **(3)** is correct.
Drivers: **Vizag Port**; **RINL**, **Hindustan Shipyard**, **HPCL refinery**; **Rushikonda IT Park**; IT; **Eastern Naval Command**.
xa: Visakhapatnam ranked **1st in PCI** for FY 2025-26 (DES, May 2026).
**NTR district**: PCI **₹3,21,651 (2023-24)**; top KPI score (**83** of **315** KPIs).

110.s:
Consider the following statements regarding district development monitoring in Andhra Pradesh:
1. District Vision Action Plans are tracked at district, constituency and mandal levels.
2. Collectors are to be rated on investment, jobs and the rise in district per capita income.
3. DDP is compiled by the State Directorate of Economics and Statistics.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: All three statements are correct. District development monitoring includes multi-level KPI tracking, Collector assessment on specified outcomes, and DES compilation of DDP.
110.tq: Combine institutional responsibility with the stated monitoring and evaluation mechanisms.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
**1:** **District Vision Action Plans** + KPI tracking at **district/constituency/mandal** level (SES 2025-26).
**2:** **Collectors** rated on **investment, jobs and rise in district PCI**.
**3:** **DDP** is compiled by the State **DES**.
xa: NTR district PCI target: **₹4,17,412**.
DES is also the nodal agency for **GSDP**.

110.s:
Consider the following statements about the 16th Finance Commission's income-distance criterion:
1. It gives a weight of 42.5% to income distance.
2. Andhra Pradesh's above-average per capita income raises its share in devolution under this criterion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
110.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 16th FC gives 42.5% weight to income distance. Statement 2 is wrong: a higher PCI means a smaller income distance from the richest States, so AP's above-average PCI LOWERS its devolution share. Hence '1 only'.
110.tq: Income distance rewards poorer States; a richer State gets less.

110.s: The P4 scheme is intended primarily to address which issue associated with a high per capita income?
o: The difference between central and state tax rates
The gap between NSDP and population estimates
The gap between average income and the persistence of poverty and inequality
The difference between current prices and constant prices
110.x: The P4 scheme targets the gap in which a high average per capita income coexists with poverty and inequality.
110.tq: Connect the policy intervention with the specific criticism of the average-income indicator.
xs: P4 targets **the gap between average income and the persistence of poverty and inequality** — option **(3)** is correct.
High PCI can coexist with **poverty + inequality** because PCI is an average.
xa: P4 = **Public-Private-People Partnership**.
PCI also ignores **cost-of-living** differences.

111.s: Which of the following correctly represents the area of residual Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation, as given in the relevant data?
o: 1,62,970 sq km from the date of bifurcation
1,60,205 sq km, later revised to 1,62,970 sq km
111.x: Residual Andhra Pradesh had an area of 1,60,205 sq km, subsequently shown as 1,62,970 sq km. Telangana covers 1,12,077 sq km.
111.tq: Use the exact area figures and distinguish the original and revised values.
xs: Residual AP had **1,60,205 sq km**, later revised to **1,62,970 sq km** — option **(4)** is correct.
The rise came from **7 Khammam mandals** moved to AP for **Polavaram**.
**1,12,077 sq km** is **Telangana**; **2,75,000 sq km** is undivided AP; 1,62,970 was not the figure from the date of bifurcation.
xa: Population (Census 2011): AP **4.96 crore**, Telangana **3.52 crore**.
APRA population ratio: **58.32 : 41.68**.
Telangana is **landlocked** — AP kept the **entire coastline**.

111.s:
With reference to the distribution of population between residual Andhra Pradesh and Telangana according to the 2011 Census, consider the following statements:
1. Residual Andhra Pradesh had a population of 4.96 crore.
2. Telangana had a population of 3.52 crore.
3. The population ratio under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act was 58.32:41.68.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: All three statements are correct. Residual Andhra Pradesh had 4.96 crore people, Telangana had 3.52 crore, and the APRA population ratio was 58.32:41.68.
111.tq: Check each population figure and the associated statutory ratio separately.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
**1:** residual AP **4.96 crore**; **2:** Telangana **3.52 crore** (Census 2011).
**3:** APRA population ratio **58.32 : 41.68**.
xa: Central Generating Station power: AP (**58%** population) got only ≈ **46%**.
Undivided AP ≈ **2,75,000 sq km**.

111.s: After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, which State retained the entire coastline and all the ports of the undivided State?
o: Both Andhra Pradesh and Telangana equally
111.x: Telangana is landlocked; therefore, residual Andhra Pradesh retained the entire coastline and all the ports of the undivided State.
111.tq: Use the geographical condition to identify the State retaining the coastal assets.
xs: **Residual Andhra Pradesh** kept the **entire coastline** and **all ports** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Telangana is landlocked**, so it got no coast.
xa: Ports: **Visakhapatnam, Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada, Machilipatnam**.
Coastline: **1,053.07 km**, **3rd longest** (after Gujarat, Tamil Nadu).
AP kept the coast, deltas and Krishna-Godavari tail-end; lost **coal** + Hyderabad industrial base.

111.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the coastline of Andhra Pradesh is NOT correct?
o: The 2023–24 remeasurement gives a figure of 1,053.07 km.
The 2023–24 remeasurement places Andhra Pradesh as the longest-coastline State in India.
The older commonly cited figure is 974 km.
The State has the third-longest coastline after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.
111.x: The 2023–24 remeasurement places Andhra Pradesh third, not first, after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu. The older figure of 974 km continues to appear in some publications.
111.tq: Find the reversed ranking hidden among otherwise correct coastline figures.
xs: Statement **(2)** is NOT correct: AP is **3rd longest**, not the longest.
**1,053.07 km** (2023-24 remeasurement; SES 2025-26) ranks **3rd** after **Gujarat** and **Tamil Nadu**.
The older **974 km** figure (2nd longest) still appears in some editions.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** some notes say "longest" — wrong.
Telangana is landlocked; AP kept the **entire coastline**.
Fisheries: AP ≈ **29%** of India's fish.

111.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding ports of Andhra Pradesh:
List-I (Port category)
a. Major port
b. Notified non-major ports
c. Greenfield ports under construction

List-II (Number or example)
i. Four
 ii. Visakhapatnam
 iii. Seventeen

Choose the correct answer:
111.x: Visakhapatnam is the one major port; there are 17 notified non-major ports and four greenfield ports under construction.
111.tq: Start from the sure port-category pair and eliminate codes.
xs: **a–ii, b–iii, c–i** — option **(1)** is correct.
Major port: **Visakhapatnam** (**1**, GoI); notified non-major: **17** (GoAP); greenfield under construction: **4**.
xa: Greenfield: **Ramayapatnam** (74% done), **Mulapeta**, **Machilipatnam** and one more.
Most cargo among non-major ports: **Krishnapatnam**.
**17** includes **3** captive ports.

111.s: Which one of the following statements about ports in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Machilipatnam handles the most cargo among the notified non-major ports.
Krishnapatnam handles the most cargo among the notified non-major ports.
There are four major ports under the Government of India.
Visakhapatnam is a greenfield port under construction.
111.x: Krishnapatnam handles the most cargo among the notified non-major ports. Visakhapatnam is the State's one major port.
111.tq: Apply the port-category distinction and identify the specific cargo-handling fact.
xs: **Krishnapatnam** handles the most cargo among non-major ports — option **(2)** is correct.
**Machilipatnam** is a **greenfield** port under construction; AP has only **1** major port (**Visakhapatnam**), which is not greenfield.
xa: **17** notified non-major ports under **GoAP**.
⚠ Only **1** major port (Visakhapatnam); most cargo among non-major = **Krishnapatnam**.

111.s:
With reference to the fisheries sector of Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh contributes approximately 29 per cent of India's fish production.
2. It accounts for approximately 75 per cent of India's cultured-shrimp exports.
