xs: Polavaram's hydel capacity is **960 MW through 12 units of 80 MW each** — option **(4)**.
Options (1), (2) and (3) jumble the same figures; **80 MW** is the size of each unit, not the total.
⚠ The **120 MW** figure comes from a wrong Jan 2026 CA note — the Economic Survey gives **960 MW**.
xa: Irrigation: **7.20 lakh acres** (= **2.91 lakh ha**).
Gross storage **194.6 TMC**; utilisation **322.73 TMC**.
**23.44 TMC** is earmarked for **Visakhapatnam** drinking water and industry.

114.s: Which of the following correctly states the Polavaram water-transfer and drinking-water provisions?
o: 23.44 TMC is transferred to the Krishna through the Right Main Canal and 80 TMC is earmarked for Visakhapatnam
28.5 TMC is transferred to the Krishna through the Right Main Canal and 23.44 TMC is earmarked for hydel generation
80 TMC is transferred to the Krishna through the Right Main Canal and 23.44 TMC is earmarked for Visakhapatnam
80 TMC is transferred to the Krishna through the Left Main Canal and 28.5 TMC is earmarked for Visakhapatnam
114.x: The project transfers 80 TMC of Godavari water to the Krishna through the Right Main Canal and provides 23.44 TMC for Visakhapatnam.
114.tq: Separate the transfer quantity, canal and destination from the drinking-water allocation.
xs: **80 TMC** goes to the **Krishna through the Right Main Canal**, and **23.44 TMC** is earmarked for **Visakhapatnam** — option **(3)**.
The **GWDT award (1980)** allowed **80 TMC** of Godavari water to be diverted into the Krishna **above Vijayawada**.
**28.5** is not a TMC figure: it is **28.5 lakh** people served in **540 villages**; the **Left Main Canal** goes to Visakhapatnam, not the Krishna.
xa: Split of the 80 TMC: **45 TMC** to AP + **35 TMC** to Karnataka (**21**) and Maharashtra (**14**).
**Pattiseema** is a temporary lift into the Polavaram **RMC**.
GWDT was set up in **1969**; award in **1980**.

114.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the two main canals is correct?
o: The Left Main Canal is used only for hydel generation and the Right Main Canal only for drinking water.
The Right Main Canal carries water to Visakhapatnam, whereas the Left Main Canal feeds the Krishna delta.
The Right Main Canal feeds the Krishna delta, whereas the Left Main Canal carries water to Visakhapatnam.
Both the Right and Left Main Canals feed only the Krishna delta.
114.x: The Right Main Canal feeds the Krishna delta, while the Left Main Canal carries water to Visakhapatnam.
114.tq: Use the reversed-destination trap to distinguish the two canals.
xs: The **Right Main Canal feeds the Krishna delta**, the **Left Main Canal carries water to Visakhapatnam** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) reverses the two canals; options (1) and (4) are wrong as both canals serve irrigation/water transfer to different regions.
xa: **Revised Administrative Sanction** for the LMC came in **Jun 2026**.
LMC up to **Visakhapatnam** is targeted for **Mar 2027** (as of **15 Aug 2026**).

114.s:
Consider the following statements about the history of the Polavaram Project:
1. It was first contemplated in 1941.
2. It was started in 2014 under Jalayagnam.
3. The proposal was named "Ramapada Sagaram" by Sir Sonti Venkataramamurthy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 1 is correct: the project was first contemplated in 1941. Statement 2 is wrong: it was started in 2005 under Jalayagnam, not 2014. Statement 3 is correct: Sir Sonti Venkataramamurthy named the proposal Ramapada Sagaram. Hence 1 and 3 only (C); A misses statement 3, B and D wrongly include statement 2.
114.tq: 1941 conceived, 2005 started (Jalayagnam); 2014 is the bifurcation year, a common trap.
xs: Only statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the project was **first contemplated in 1941**.
Statement 2 wrong: it was started under **Jalayagnam** in **2005**, not 2014.
Statement 3 correct: **Sir Sonti Venkataramamurthy** named the proposal **"Ramapada Sagaram"**.
xa: **2014** is the year of the **AP Reorganisation Act**, whose **Section 90** made Polavaram a national project.
The **Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal** (set up **1969**) gave its award in **1980**.
Site: on the **Godavari**, near Polavaram village, **Eluru district**.

114.s: Which of the following statements about the Polavaram Project is correct?
o: It is located in Krishna district and draws water from the Pennar River.
It is located in Visakhapatnam district and has no irrigation component.
It is located in Eluru district, which was earlier identified as part of West Godavari district.
It is located in Khammam district and transfers Krishna water to the Godavari.
114.x: The project is near Polavaram village in Eluru district; the site was earlier identified with West Godavari district. It is a Godavari project with substantial irrigation and water-transfer components.
114.tq: Use the present district name together with the earlier district identity to resolve the location change.
xs: Polavaram lies in **Eluru district**, earlier identified as **West Godavari** — option **(3)**.
It is on the **Godavari**, not the Pennar; it has a large **irrigation** component (**7.20 lakh acres**).
It transfers **Godavari** water to the **Krishna** (not the reverse), and Khammam is where the **submergence mandals** were moved from.
xa: ⚠ **West Godavari** is the old PYQ key for the district.
Dam: **2,467.50 m** earth-cum-rock fill; spillway **1,121.20 m**.
Started under **Jalayagnam** in **2005**; first contemplated in **1941**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal (GWDT):
1. It was set up in 1969 and gave its award in 1980.
2. The award cleared Polavaram with an FRL of +150 ft.
3. It allowed 80 TMC of Godavari water to be diverted into the Krishna above Vijayawada, of which Andhra Pradesh gets 45 TMC.
4. Of the remaining 35 TMC, Karnataka gets 14 TMC and Maharashtra 21 TMC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: GWDT was set up in 1969 with its award in 1980; it cleared Polavaram at FRL +150 ft; and of the 80 TMC diverted into the Krishna, AP gets 45 TMC. Statement 4 is wrong: the 35 TMC is split 21 TMC to Karnataka and 14 TMC to Maharashtra, not the reverse. Hence B; A omits statement 3, C and D wrongly include statement 4.
114.tq: 80 = 45 (AP) + 35 (Karnataka 21 + Maharashtra 14).
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **GWDT** was set up in **1969**; award in **1980**.
Statement 2 correct: the award cleared Polavaram with **FRL +150 ft**.
Statement 3 correct: **80 TMC** diverted into the Krishna **above Vijayawada**, **45 TMC** to AP.
Statement 4 wrong: the **35 TMC** goes **21 TMC to Karnataka** and **14 TMC to Maharashtra**, not the reverse.
xa: The transfer runs via the **Right Main Canal**.
Telangana says the proposed **Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar** link violates the **1980 GWDT award** and **APRA 2014**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pattiseema is a temporary lift into the Polavaram Right Main Canal.
2. The proposed Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link was earlier known as the Banakacherla link.
3. Telangana holds that the link is consistent with the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and the 1980 GWDT award.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 1 is correct: Pattiseema is a temporary lift into the Polavaram RMC. Statement 2 is correct: the link was earlier called the Banakacherla link. Statement 3 is wrong: Telangana contends the link VIOLATES both the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and the 1980 GWDT award. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
114.tq: Banakacherla = old name of Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link.

114.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Polavaram Project under Section 90 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. Under Section 90(3), the consent of the successor State of Telangana is deemed to have been given.
2. Under Section 90(4), the Government of Andhra Pradesh shall execute the project and obtain all environmental, forest and R&R clearances.
3. In practice, the Government of Andhra Pradesh executes the irrigation component on behalf of the Government of India and claims reimbursement or advances from the Centre.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 1 is correct: Section 90(3) deems Telangana's consent to have been given. Statement 2 is wrong: Section 90(4) says the Central Government shall execute the project and obtain the clearances. Statement 3 is correct: in practice AP executes the irrigation component on behalf of GoI and claims reimbursement/advance. Hence 1 and 3 only (C); A misses statement 3, B and D wrongly include statement 2.
114.tq: Law vs practice: in the Act the Centre executes (90(4)); in practice AP executes for the Centre.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Section 90(3)** — Telangana's consent is **deemed to have been given**.
Statement 2 wrong: under **90(4)** the **Central Government** shall execute the project and obtain environmental, forest and R&R clearances.
Statement 3 correct: **AP executes the irrigation component on behalf of GoI** and claims reimbursement/advance.
xa: **90(2)**: the **Union** takes control of regulation and development of the project for **irrigation**.
⚠ "Which section" — answer **90**; an old key says Section **30**, some CA notes say **89** — both wrong.
Centre funds **100%** of the remaining irrigation cost from **1 April 2014**.

114.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Polavaram Project Authority is correct?
1. The CEO's office is located in New Delhi.
2. The Authority was constituted by the Union after the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
3. The Authority has a role in inter-State coordination.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
114.x: All three statements are correct. The Authority was constituted after the Reorganisation Act, performs inter-State coordination functions, and the CEO sits in New Delhi.
114.tq: Use the institutional-location-function combination and test all three independent attributes.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the PPA **CEO sits in New Delhi**.
Statement 2: the PPA was constituted by the **Union** after the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014**.
Statement 3: it routes national-project funding and **mediates inter-State coordination**.
xa: **Shiv Nandan Kumar** was CEO as of **25 May 2024** (APPSC 2024 key).
**M. Raghuram** — Member-Secretary; **M. Ramesh Kumar** — Chief Engineer, **Rajamahendravaram**.
CAG (audit to **Mar 2023**) asked AP to settle submergence issues with neighbours **in consultation with PPA**.

114.s: As of 25 May 2024, who was the Chief Executive Officer of the Polavaram Project Authority?
114.x: Shiv Nandan Kumar was the PPA CEO as of 25 May 2024 (APPSC 2024 key); the CEO sits in New Delhi. M. Raghuram is Member-Secretary, M. Ramesh Kumar is Chief Engineer at Rajamahendravaram, and Sonti Venkataramamurthy named the original 'Ramapada Sagaram' proposal.
114.tq: PPA CEO (2024): Shiv Nandan Kumar.
xs: **Shiv Nandan Kumar** was CEO of the PPA as of **25 May 2024** — option **(2)** (APPSC 2024 key).
**M. Raghuram** is the PPA's **Member-Secretary**; **M. Ramesh Kumar** is Chief Engineer at **Rajamahendravaram**.
**Sir Sonti Venkataramamurthy** named the original **"Ramapada Sagaram"** proposal.
xa: The PPA CEO sits in **New Delhi**.
The PPA is a **central body** routing national-project funding and mediating inter-State coordination.

114.s: The Polavaram Irrigation Project was declared a national project under which section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
114.x: Section 90 declares Polavaram a national project, with the Union taking control of it, Telangana's consent deemed and the Centre executing it. Section 30 appears in an old wrong key, Section 89 concerns the KWDT reference, and Section 94 covers fiscal/industrial incentives and capital support.
114.tq: Polavaram = Sec 90.
xs: Polavaram was declared a national project under **Section 90** of the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** — option **(3)**.
⚠ An old key says **Section 30** and some CA notes say **Section 89** — both wrong.
xa: **90(2)**: Union takes control of the project for **irrigation**.
**90(3)**: Telangana's consent **deemed to have been given**.
**90(4)**: **Central Government shall execute** it and obtain environmental, forest and R&R clearances.

114.s:
With reference to Central funding of the Polavaram Project, consider the following statements:
1. The Centre funds 100 per cent of the remaining cost of the irrigation component from 1 April 2014.
2. The commitment covers the drinking-water component in the same manner as the irrigation component.
3. The hydel component is not covered by this commitment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: The Centre funds 100 per cent of the remaining irrigation-component cost from 1 April 2014. Drinking-water and hydel components are not covered by this commitment.
114.tq: Split the funding commitment by component and watch for the reversed coverage trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: Centre funds **100% of the remaining cost of the irrigation component** from **1 April 2014**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **drinking-water** component is **NOT covered**.
Statement 3 correct: the **hydel** component is also **not covered**.
xa: Older RCE: **₹55,548 crore**; release delayed.
Expenditure by Dec 2025: **₹25,700.47 crore**; GoI advance **₹5,052.71 crore**.
CM (26 Jan 2026): ~**₹12,000 crore** pending from the Centre.

114.s: In February 2026, Andhra Pradesh sought which of the following from the Centre for the Polavaram Project?
o: Rs 32,000 crore for Phase-II and permanent lifting of the MoEF stop-work order
Rs 12,000 crore for the hydel component and transfer of the PPA to Amaravati
Rs 55,548 crore as a one-time grant for drinking water
Rs 3,320 crore for the Left Main Canal only
114.x: AP sought Rs 32,000 crore for Polavaram Phase-II and permanent lifting of the MoEF stop-work order (11 Feb 2026). About Rs 12,000 crore is the amount the CM said was pending from the Centre, Rs 55,548 crore is the older RCE, and Rs 3,320 crore is the Union Budget 2026-27 allocation.
114.tq: Phase-II ask: Rs 32,000 crore.
xs: AP sought **₹32,000 crore for Phase-II** and **permanent lifting of the MoEF stop-work order** — option **(1)** (**11 Feb 2026**).
~**₹12,000 crore** is what the CM said was **pending** from the Centre (**26 Jan 2026**).
**₹55,548 crore** is the older RCE; **₹3,320 crore** is the Budget 2026-27 allocation.
xa: Centre covers **100%** of the remaining **irrigation** cost from **1 April 2014** — not drinking water or hydel.
Budget 2026-27 storage limit: **41.15 m**.
Dec 2025: expenditure **₹25,700.47 crore**; GoI advance **₹5,052.71 crore**.

114.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014, commonly referred to in this context as the Polavaram Ordinance Bill, primarily amended the territorial provision so as to:
o: Merge Odisha's submergence villages with Andhra Pradesh
Transfer the entire Khammam district to Andhra Pradesh
Transfer Bhadrachalam temple town to Andhra Pradesh
Keep the Khammam villages and mandals in the submergence area with Andhra Pradesh
114.x: The Ordinance amended the territorial provision so that Khammam villages and mandals in the Polavaram submergence area remained with Andhra Pradesh.
114.tq: Distinguish the limited territorial transfer from the incorrect claim of transferring an entire district.
xs: The **Polavaram Ordinance** kept the **Khammam villages and mandals in the submergence area with AP** — option **(4)**.
Not all of Khammam moved: **seven mandals** did, and **Bhadrachalam temple town** stayed out.
Odisha's villages were not merged — Odisha has a **submergence case** pending in the Supreme Court.
xa: Formal name: **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014**.
The Bill was passed by the **Lok Sabha on 11 July 2014**.
AP's area rose from **1,60,205** to **1,62,970 sq km**.

114.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the seven mandals moved from Khammam to Andhra Pradesh under the Polavaram-related territorial arrangement?
114.x: The seven mandals included Kukunoor, Velerupadu, VR Puram, Chintoor, Kunavaram, Bhadrachalam except the temple town, and Burgampadu. The Bhadrachalam temple town itself was excluded.
114.tq: Look for the stated exception within the otherwise transferred Bhadrachalam area.
xs: The **Bhadrachalam temple town** was **not** transferred — option **(2)**.
The seven mandals: **Kukunoor, Velerupadu, VR Puram, Chintoor, Kunavaram, Bhadrachalam (except the temple town), Burgampadu**.
So **Kukunoor**, **Velerupadu** and **Kunavaram** were all moved to AP.
xa: VR Puram = **Vararamachandrapuram**.
AP's area rose from **1,60,205** to **1,62,970 sq km**.
Done by the **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014** — the "**Polavaram Ordinance Bill**".

114.s:
Consider the following statements regarding objections to Polavaram submergence:
1. Odisha and Chhattisgarh objected in connection with protective embankments.
2. Telangana's concern relates to backwater at Bhadrachalam.
3. According to the CAG, the protective embankments for the neighbouring States were due by 2019-20.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Odisha and Chhattisgarh objected over protective embankments, and Telangana over backwater at Bhadrachalam. Statement 3 is wrong: the CAG noted the embankments were due by 2014-15, not 2019-20. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
114.tq: Pair the States with their grievance: Odisha/Chhattisgarh = embankments, Telangana = Bhadrachalam backwater.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Odisha and Chhattisgarh** object; protective embankments were due.
Statement 2 correct: **Telangana** fears **backwater at Bhadrachalam**.
Statement 3 wrong: the CAG says embankments were due by **2014-15**, not 2019-20.
xa: Odisha and Chhattisgarh submergence cases are pending in the **Supreme Court**.
CAG (audit to **Mar 2023**): settle submergence issues **in consultation with PPA** and build embankments.
Jul 2026: ~**189 villages** on alert in **Polavaram district** during **Godavari-Sabari** floods.

114.s: The tribal communities displaced by the Polavaram Project are reported to be predominantly which of the following?
114.x: The displaced population is predominantly composed of Koya and Kondh tribals.
114.tq: Identify the precise community names instead of relying on broad tribal associations.
xs: Those displaced are mostly **Koya and Kondh** tribals — option **(4)**.
Their complaints: **land-rights violation**, **low compensation**, **poor rehabilitation**.
xa: **Koya river traditions** face loss (Aug 2026).
R&R progress Aug 2026: **94% land acquisition**, **52% relocation**.
Compensation follows the **RFCTLARR Act, 2013**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements regarding land acquisition and R&R for the Polavaram Project:
1. In December 2025, land acquisition and R&R were only 27.40% complete and were the main bottleneck.
2. By August 2026, land acquisition had reached 94% and relocation of project-affected families 52%.
3. The R&R colonies were targeted for completion by March 2027.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 1 is correct: LA and R&R stood at only 27.40% in December 2025, the main bottleneck. Statement 2 is correct: August 2026 figures were 94% land acquisition and 52% relocation. Statement 3 is wrong: R&R colonies were targeted for December 2026 (March 2027 is the project completion target). Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
114.tq: Do not mix the R&R colony target (Dec 2026) with the project completion target (Mar 2027).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: in **Dec 2025** **LA and R&R** were only **27.40%** — the main bottleneck.
Statement 2 correct: **Aug 2026** — **94% land acquisition**, **52% relocation**.
Statement 3 wrong: R&R colonies were targeted for **Dec 2026**; **March 2027** is the project completion target.
xa: **₹1,943 crore** compensation paid in three phases (Mar 2026).
House-site value doubled from **₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh** (**1 May 2026**).
Displaced are mostly **Koya and Kondh** tribals.

114.s:
With reference to compensation for the Polavaram Project, consider the following statements:
1. ₹1,943 crore was paid in three phases.
2. The value of a house site in R&R colonies was increased from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh.
3. Compensation follows the RFCTLARR Act, 2013.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: All three statements are correct. Compensation of ₹1,943 crore was paid in three phases, house-site value was doubled to ₹2 lakh, and compensation follows the RFCTLARR Act, 2013.
114.tq: Combine a numerical fact, a revised entitlement and the governing legislation.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **₹1,943 crore** was paid in **three phases** (Mar 2026).
Statement 2: house-site value **doubled from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh** (Cabinet, **1 May 2026**).
Statement 3: compensation follows the **RFCTLARR Act, 2013**.
xa: Aug 2026: **94% land acquisition**, **52% relocation**; R&R colonies targeted **Dec 2026**.
Complaints of **Koya and Kondh** tribals: low compensation, poor rehabilitation, land-rights violation.

114.s:
Consider the following statements regarding expert reviews of the Polavaram Project:
1. A foreign expert panel, on its sixth visit with the CWC, reviewed Gap-1, Gap-2 and the diaphragm wall.
2. The safety of the spillway was cleared by the Polavaram Project Authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 1 is correct: the foreign expert panel (6th visit, with CWC) reviewed Gap-1, Gap-2 and the D-wall. Statement 2 is wrong: the Central Water Commission, not the PPA, cleared spillway safety (April 2026). Hence 1 only (A); B, C and D wrongly treat statement 2 as correct or reject statement 1.
114.tq: Technical safety clearances come from the CWC; the PPA routes funds and coordinates.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **foreign expert panel** (6th visit, with **CWC**) reviewed **Gap-1, Gap-2 and the D-wall** (Jan 2026).
Statement 2 wrong: the **CWC**, not the PPA, **cleared spillway safety** (Apr 2026).
xa: Diaphragm wall (**1,372 m**) rebuilt in **440 days**, ~**₹1,000 crore** extra.
The PPA's role is funding routing and **inter-State coordination**.

114.s: The target for completion of the Polavaram Project was shifted from December 2027 to:
114.x: The completion target was moved forward from December 2027 to March 2027, before the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu.
114.tq: Distinguish the revised target from the original target and the R&R deadline.
xs: The completion target moved from Dec 2027 to **March 2027** — option **(1)**.
The aim is to finish before the **2027 Godavari Pushkaralu**.
**December 2026** is the target for **R&R colonies**, not the whole project.
xa: Aug 2026: **90% civil works**, **77% overall**.
LMC up to **Visakhapatnam** also targeted for **Mar 2027**.

114.s: By August 2026, which of the following correctly represented the reported progress of the Polavaram Project?
114.x: By August 2026, civil works were reported at 90% and overall progress at 77%.
114.tq: Avoid reversing the component-progress figure and the overall-progress figure.
xs: By Aug 2026 the project showed **90% civil works and 77% overall** progress — option **(1)**.
**81.61%** (head works) and **92.79%** (RMC) are Dec 2025 component figures; **60.8%** was overall progress in Dec 2025 and **73.40%** the LMC.
Option (3) swaps the two figures.
xa: Dec 2024 overall progress: **53.47%**.
Completion target: **March 2027**.

114.s: Which of the following statements best expresses a major criticism concerning the storage level of the Polavaram Project?
o: The FRL was reduced from 41.15 metres to 35 metres.
Phase-I storage is planned at 45.72 metres instead of 41.15 metres.
The project has no provision for Phase-I storage.
Phase-I storage is planned at 41.15 metres instead of the 45.72-metre FRL.
114.x: A major criticism is that Phase-I storage is proposed at 41.15 metres, below the full reservoir level of 45.72 metres.
114.tq: Read the reversed comparison carefully: interim storage is lower than the full FRL.
xs: The criticism: **Phase-I storage at 41.15 m instead of the 45.72-m FRL** — option **(4)**.
Option (2) reverses the two levels; the approved FRL is **45.72 m** (TH, **13 May 2026**).
xa: Budget 2026-27: **₹3,320 crore** for revised cost, storage up to **41.15 m**.
Other criticisms: **tribal displacement**; **revised cost estimate** not yet cleared.
The GWDT award cleared Polavaram at **FRL +150 ft**.

114.s: Which of the following issues remains unresolved in relation to the Polavaram Project?
o: The revised cost estimate has not yet been cleared.
The Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal has not been constituted.
No rehabilitation policy exists for affected families.
The project has not been declared a national project.
114.x: The revised cost estimate had not yet been cleared. The other statements contradict the stated position or introduce facts not supported here.
114.tq: Identify the unresolved administrative issue without confusing it with settled project features.
xs: The **revised cost estimate has not yet been cleared** — option **(1)**.
The **GWDT** exists (set up **1969**, award **1980**), R&R follows the **RFCTLARR Act, 2013**, and Polavaram is a **national project** under **Section 90**.
xa: Other criticisms: **tribal displacement** and Phase-I storage at **41.15 m** instead of **45.72 m**.
Older RCE: **₹55,548 crore**; AP seeks **₹32,000 crore** for **Phase-II**.

115.s: Which district recorded the largest Gross Irrigated Area in Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24?
115.x: Eluru recorded the largest GIA at 2.39 lakh hectares, followed by Ananthapuramu at 2.04 lakh hectares and Nandyal at 1.98 lakh hectares.
115.tq: Use the district ranking and distinguish the highest value from the next two values.
xs: **Eluru** had the largest irrigated area in 2023-24 — option **(2)**, with **2.39 lakh ha**.
It is followed by **Ananthapuramu (2.04)** and **Nandyal (1.98)** (Annex 5.13).
xa: Largest source of irrigation in AP: **wells / tube wells** (~**48%** of GIA 2023-24).
AP ranked **1st nationally** in **micro-irrigation** 2024-25.

115.s: In Andhra Pradesh, minor irrigation covers schemes having an ayacut up to:
115.x: In Andhra Pradesh, minor irrigation covers schemes with an ayacut up to 5,000 acres.
115.tq: Distinguish the Andhra Pradesh threshold from the national classification.
xs: In AP, **minor irrigation** = **ayacut up to 5,000 acres** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **2,000** is the national figure, but in **hectares of CCA**, not acres.
xa: National CCA classes: minor up to **2,000 ha**; medium **2,000-10,000 ha**; major above **10,000 ha**.
Irrigation potential created (31 Dec 2025): minor **25.60 lakh acres**, medium **5.59**, major **67.23**.
By purpose: **lift irrigation** (HNSS, Pattiseema), **gravity diversion** (Veligonda), **barrage** (Prakasam).

115.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the national classification based on CCA?
o: Minor: up to 1,000 ha; Medium: 1,000–5,000 ha; Major: above 5,000 ha
Minor: up to 5,000 ha; Medium: 5,000–15,000 ha; Major: above 15,000 ha
Minor: up to 10,000 ha; Medium: 10,000–20,000 ha; Major: above 20,000 ha
Minor: up to 2,000 ha; Medium: 2,000–10,000 ha; Major: above 10,000 ha
115.x: Nationally, minor irrigation means CCA up to 2,000 ha, medium 2,000–10,000 ha and major above 10,000 ha.
115.tq: Compare classification thresholds carefully rather than applying the state-specific ayacut limit.
xs: National CCA classification: **minor up to 2,000 ha; medium 2,000-10,000 ha; major above 10,000 ha** — option **(4)**.
⚠ AP's own minor-irrigation limit is different: **ayacut up to 5,000 acres**.
xa: Multipurpose examples: **Nagarjuna Sagar**, **Polavaram**.
Lift irrigation examples: **HNSS**, **Pattiseema**; gravity diversion: **Veligonda**; barrage: **Prakasam**.
APSIDC lift irrigation potential: **8.32 lakh acres** (31 Dec 2025).

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding irrigation in Andhra Pradesh during 2023-24:
1. The gross irrigated area was 32.71 lakh hectares.
2. The net irrigated area was 26.03 lakh hectares.
3. The gross irrigated area was smaller than the net irrigated area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: The gross irrigated area was 32.71 lakh hectares and the net irrigated area was 26.03 lakh hectares. Gross irrigated area is not smaller than net irrigated area.
115.tq: Split the numerical statements and identify the reversed comparison.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **gross irrigated area** 2023-24 = **32.71 lakh ha** (**-10.53%**).
Statement 2 correct: **net irrigated area** = **26.03 lakh ha** (**-8.86%**).
Statement 3 wrong: gross (**32.71**) is larger than net (**26.03**), since gross counts land irrigated more than once.
xa: 2023-24 was a **drought year**; derived GIA/GCA **about 55%**.

115.s: As per 'AP Economy in Brief 2020', the ratio of Gross Irrigated Area to Gross Cropped Area (GIA/GCA) in Andhra Pradesh was about:
115.x: The PYQ (2021) figure for AP's GIA/GCA is 52%, per AP Economy in Brief 2020. A derived 2023-24 figure is about 55% and India's is 55.8%; 36% is close to AP's net-sown-area share of geographical area, and 64%/75% are not supported.
115.tq: AP GIA/GCA (PYQ) = 52%.
xs: AP's **GIA/GCA** was **52%** (AP Economy in Brief 2020) — option **(2)**, a **PYQ 2021** figure.
A derived 2023-24 figure is **about 55%** (cropping intensity **1.21** on **49.55 lakh ha** NSA).
xa: 2024-25 cropping intensity: **1.88**.

115.s: Which of the following statements regarding the source-wise distribution of Gross Irrigated Area in Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24 is NOT correct?
o: Wells and tube wells accounted for approximately 48%.
115.x: Other sources accounted for approximately 3%, not 12%. Wells and tube wells, canals and tanks accounted for approximately 48%, 40% and 8%, respectively.
115.tq: Find the single percentage that does not fit the source-wise distribution.
xs: The wrong statement is "others ~12%" — option **(2)**; **other sources** were only ~**3%** (**1.10 lakh ha**).
Correct shares (GIA 2023-24): **wells/tube wells ~48%** (**15.68**), **canals ~40%** (**13.24**), **tanks ~8%** (**2.69 lakh ha**).
xa: ⚠ **12%** is India's "others" share of net irrigated area in **2021-22**.
Groundwater = **41%** of GIA; ~**19 lakh** bore wells.
Tanks matter on the peninsular plateau; **canals dominate the Godavari-Krishna deltas**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Groundwater accounted for 41% of Gross Irrigated Area in Andhra Pradesh.
2. Andhra Pradesh had approximately 19 lakh bore wells.
3. Groundwater was the smallest source of irrigation in the State in 2023-24.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because groundwater, represented mainly by wells and tube wells, was the largest source of GIA.
115.tq: Reject the reversed ranking statement after verifying the quantitative statements.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **groundwater** = **41%** of GIA.
Statement 2 correct: AP has ~**19 lakh bore wells**.
Statement 3 wrong: **wells/tube wells** were the **largest** source (~**48%**), not the smallest.
xa: Groundwater irrigation: **29.12 lakh acres net**, **41.44 lakh acres gross** (2023-24).
Groundwater is **roughly 45%** of net irrigated area (derived).

115.s: India's source-wise distribution of net irrigated area in 2021-22 was headed by
115.x: Tube wells accounted for 47.3% of India's net irrigated area in 2021-22, followed by canals at 24.7%, other wells at 13.2% and other sources at 12%.
115.tq: Do not interchange the source category with the percentage belonging to it.
xs: India's net irrigated area in 2021-22 was led by **tube wells, with 47.3%** — option **(2)**.
**Canals** were **24.7%**, **other wells 13.2%**, others **12%** — options (1), (3), (4) mis-pair these.
xa: ⚠ India's largest = **tube wells 47.3%**; AP's GIA largest = **wells/tube wells ~48%**.
India's GIA/GCA: **55.8%**.
AP's canals: ~**40%** of GIA (2023-24).

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding sources of irrigation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Tank irrigation is important because of the undulating relief and impervious rocks of the peninsular plateau.
2. Canals dominate irrigation in the Godavari-Krishna deltas.
3. Tanks were the largest source of Gross Irrigated Area in the State in 2023-24.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 1 is correct: undulating plateau relief and impervious rocks favour tanks. Statement 2 is correct: canals dominate the Godavari-Krishna deltas. Statement 3 is wrong: wells/tube wells were the largest source (~48% of GIA) in 2023-24, with tanks only ~8%. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
115.tq: Tanks matter regionally (plateau), but wells/tube wells lead the State's GIA.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: tanks matter due to the plateau's **undulating relief** and **impervious rocks**.
Statement 2 correct: **canals dominate** the **Godavari-Krishna deltas**.
Statement 3 wrong: **wells/tube wells** (~**48%**) were largest; tanks only ~**8%**.
xa: Tanks: **2.69 lakh ha** of GIA 2023-24.
**Neeru-Chettu** works include **desilting tank beds** and developing **tank cascades**.

115.s: The foundation stone of Nagarjuna Sagar was laid by Jawaharlal Nehru on:
115.x: Jawaharlal Nehru laid the foundation stone of Nagarjuna Sagar on 10 December 1955.
115.tq: Test the exact date and associated national leader.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** laid Nagarjuna Sagar's foundation stone on **10 December 1955** — option **(4)** (PYQ 2018).
This fell in the last months of the **First Plan**.
xa: ⚠ Nagarjuna Sagar foundation = **Nehru 1955**; Veligonda foundation = **Naidu 1996**.
Nagarjuna Sagar is one of the **largest masonry dams in the world**, on the **Krishna**.
Its completion was prioritised in the **Fifth Plan (1974-79)**.

115.s: The Nagarjuna Sagar Project is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Godavari River and Tenth Five Year Plan
Krishna River and First Five Year Plan
Pennar River and Second Five Year Plan
Vamsadhara River and Fifth Five Year Plan
115.x: Nagarjuna Sagar is constructed on the Krishna River and was taken up during the First Five Year Plan. Its foundation stone was laid by Jawaharlal Nehru on 10 December 1955.
115.tq: Link the project with its river and plan period rather than relying on the project name alone.
xs: Nagarjuna Sagar = **Krishna River** + **First Five Year Plan** — option **(2)**.
Foundation laid by **Nehru** on **10 Dec 1955**, in the First Plan's last months.
**Tenth Plan** belongs to **Jalayagnam**; **Vamsadhara** and **Godavari** are other projects' rivers.
xa: Multipurpose project serving **AP and Telangana**.
Completion prioritised in the **Fifth Plan (1974-79)**.
One of the **largest masonry dams** in the world.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Prakasam Barrage:
1. It is situated on the Krishna River at Vijayawada.
2. Its construction began in February 1954 under the Prakasam ministry.
3. It replaced Cotton's Krishna anicut of the 1850s.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: All three statements are correct. The Prakasam Barrage is at Vijayawada on the Krishna, construction began in February 1954 under the Prakasam ministry, and it replaced Cotton's earlier Krishna anicut.
115.tq: Check each statement against the project’s location, construction period and predecessor.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Prakasam Barrage** is on the **Krishna at Vijayawada**.
Statement 2: construction from **Feb 1954** under the **Prakasam ministry**.
Statement 3: it replaced **Cotton's 1850s Krishna anicut**.
xa: Completed **1957**; a **First to Second Plan** project.
Pattiseema water reaches the **Krishna at Prakasam Barrage** via the Polavaram RMC.

115.s: Telugu Ganga primarily serves which of the following purposes?
o: Supplying drinking water to Vijayawada and irrigating the Krishna delta exclusively
Supplying drinking water to Hyderabad and irrigating Srikakulam
Supplying drinking water to Chennai and irrigating parts of Rayalaseema and Nellore
Supplying drinking water to Tirupati and irrigating only Kadapa
115.x: The Telugu Ganga project carries Krishna surplus through the Srisailam-Somasila-Kandaleru-Poondi system, supplying drinking water to Chennai and irrigation water to Rayalaseema and Nellore.
115.tq: Identify the project through its combined drinking-water and irrigation beneficiaries.
xs: **Telugu Ganga** supplies **drinking water to Chennai** and irrigates **Rayalaseema/Nellore** — option **(3)**.
It carries **Krishna surplus** via **Srisailam-Somasila-Kandaleru-Poondi**.
xa: An **NTR-era** project, begun **1983** (**Sixth Plan**).
Listed in the **Eleventh Schedule** of APRA **2014** for completion with existing water sharing.
Rayalaseema's Krishna-lift projects (HNSS, GNSS, Telugu Ganga) "often run dry".

115.s:
With reference to Handri-Neeva Sujala Sravanthi, consider the following statements:
1. It is a lift-irrigation project associated with the Krishna River system.
2. It is intended to carry water to drought-prone Rayalaseema.
3. Its target mentioned for completion is March 2027.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: Handri-Neeva is a Krishna-based lift-irrigation project for drought-prone Rayalaseema, and its stated target is March 2027. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
115.tq: Combine the project type, beneficiary region and completion target before selecting the code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **HNSS** is a **lift irrigation** project from the **Krishna (Srisailam)**.
Statement 2: it carries water to drought-prone **Rayalaseema**.
Statement 3: completion target **Mar 2027**; **Phase-I** is working.
xa: HNSS: **40 TMC**; **6.025 lakh acres**; **33 lakh** people.
⚠ **HNSS 40 TMC / 6.025** vs **GNSS 38 TMC / 2.60** vs **Veligonda 43.50 TMC / 4.47 lakh acres**.
HNSS was unfinished in **2025-26** under **Jalayagnam**.

115.s: The Galeru-Nagari Sujala Sravanthi project is associated with which of the following command-area figures and districts?
o: 4.47 lakh acres; Prakasam, Markapuram, Nellore and Kadapa
2.60 lakh acres; Kadapa, Annamayya, Tirupati, Chittoor and Nellore
115.x: Galeru-Nagari has a stated capacity of 38 TMC and an intended command area of 2.60 lakh acres covering Kadapa, Annamayya, Tirupati, Chittoor and Nellore.
115.tq: Use the command-area figure together with the district list to distinguish similar irrigation projects.
xs: **GNSS**: **2.60 lakh acres** in **Kadapa, Annamayya, Tirupati, Chittoor and Nellore** — option **(4)**.
**4.47 lakh acres** with Prakasam/Markapuram is **Veligonda**; **6.025 lakh acres** is **HNSS**; **20,000 acres** is **Vamsadhara**.
xa: GNSS uses **Krishna flood waters**; **38 TMC**.
Listed in APRA 2014's **Eleventh Schedule**.
Still unfinished under **Jalayagnam** in **2025-26**.

115.s: The foundation stone of the Veligonda project was laid on:
115.x: The foundation stone of the Veligonda project was laid on 5 March 1996 by N. Chandrababu Naidu.
115.tq: Separate the foundation date from the later inauguration date and other project dates.
xs: **Naidu** laid Veligonda's foundation on **5 March 1996** — option **(4)**.
**31 Aug 2026** is the **Phase-I inauguration**; **10 Dec 1955** is Nagarjuna Sagar's foundation; **Feb 1954** is Prakasam Barrage's start.
xa: Veligonda = **Poola Subbaiah** project, gravity from **Srisailam** via twin **Nallamala tunnels**.
Phase-I inaugurated at **Gantavanipalli** (Markapuram district), three decades after the foundation stone.
Naidu also launched **Neeru-Meeru** (**2000**).

115.s: Which of the following projects contributes to the potential created in the Pennar basin?
115.x: The Somasila project is on the Pennar and contributes to the irrigation potential created in the basin.
115.tq: Identify the project through the river basin with which it is specifically linked.
xs: **Somasila** is on the **Pennar** and contributes to potential created — option **(2)** (APSES).
**Veligonda** and **Handri-Neeva** draw on the **Krishna** (Srisailam); **Vamsadhara** is in **Srikakulam**.
xa: Somasila is part of the **Telugu Ganga** route (**Srisailam-Somasila-Kandaleru-Poondi**).
**Gandipalem** is a medium project on the **Pillaperu** in **SPSR Nellore**.

115.s: Under the Eleventh Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, which of the following projects were to be completed with the existing water sharing?
o: Nagarjuna Sagar, Prakasam Barrage, Somasila and Polavaram only
Handri-Neeva, Telugu Ganga, Galeru-Nagari, Veligonda, Kalwakurthy and Nettempadu
Vamsadhara, Somasila, Nagarjuna Sagar and Polavaram only
115.x: The Eleventh Schedule lists Handri-Neeva, Telugu Ganga, Galeru-Nagari, Veligonda, Kalwakurthy and Nettempadu for completion with the existing water-sharing arrangements.
115.tq: Recall the statutory project list as a complete group rather than selecting an isolated project.
xs: APRA 2014's **Eleventh Schedule** lists **Handri-Neeva, Telugu Ganga, Galeru-Nagari, Veligonda, Kalwakurthy, Nettempadu** — option **(3)**.
These were to be **completed with existing water sharing**.
**Hirakud** is on the **Mahanadi** in Odisha — not an AP project.
xa: **KRMB and GRMB** were set up under **Schedule 11** principles.
**KWDT** allocations are the basis of the **KRMB** operation protocol.

115.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Polavaram — National Project with irrigation, drinking water, hydropower and flood-control objectives
Prakasam Barrage — Multipurpose dam on the Godavari
Nagarjuna Sagar — Temporary lift scheme until Polavaram is completed
Galeru-Nagari — Project supplying Godavari water to the Krishna delta
115.x: Polavaram is a National Project with irrigation, drinking-water, hydropower and flood-control objectives. The other pairs confuse the functions or river systems of different projects.
115.tq: Use the project’s official status and multiple objectives to eliminate river and function swaps.
xs: **Polavaram** = **National Project** with irrigation, drinking water, hydropower and flood control — option **(1)**.
**Prakasam Barrage** is a barrage on the **Krishna**, not a Godavari dam.
The **temporary lift** is **Pattiseema**; **Galeru-Nagari** uses **Krishna flood waters**.
xa: The **GWDT award (1980)** permitted diversion of **80 tmc** Godavari water to the Krishna.
Polavaram status (May 2026): **88% civil works, 93% land acquisition, 45% R&R**.
Polavaram (started **2005**) is still a **Jalayagnam** project.

115.s: The dam now known as Polavaram was first proposed as:
115.x: The Polavaram dam was initially proposed as “Ramapada Sagaram”; the proposal is credited to Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy.
115.tq: Test the earlier name of a famous project, a common official-name trap.
xs: Polavaram was first proposed as **"Ramapada Sagaram"** — option **(1)**.
APHQ credits **Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy** with the proposal.
**Nallamala Sagar** is the reservoir fed by **Veligonda**.
xa: Polavaram is a **National Project** on the **Godavari**.
It was started in **2005** and remains a **Jalayagnam** project.

115.s: Vamsadhara Project is popularly known as the ‘Lifeline of North Coastal Andhra Pradesh’. It is associated with which district?
115.x: The Vamsadhara Project is associated with Srikakulam district and is described as the Lifeline of North Coastal Andhra Pradesh.
115.tq: Use the title–location association to distinguish nearby irrigation projects.
xs: **Vamsadhara** is in **Srikakulam** — option **(2)**; "**Lifeline of North Coastal AP**" (APPSC 2025).
**Phase-II Stage-II** is **93.5%** done, with **20,000 acres** new ayacut.
xa: **Vamsadhara-Nagavali link** due by December (Apr 2026).
**Gandipalem** (Pillaperu, **SPSR Nellore**) was also an APPSC 2025 question.

115.s: Veligonda Project receives water from the Srisailam reservoir through tunnels and serves which combination of districts?
115.x: The Veligonda Project draws from the Srisailam reservoir through tunnels and serves Prakasam, Nellore and YSR Kadapa districts.
115.tq: Match the source and served districts rather than relying on the project name alone.
xs: **Veligonda** serves **Prakasam, Nellore and YSR Kadapa** — option **(2)**.
Command: **4.47 lakh acres**, **30 mandals** in Prakasam, Markapuram, Nellore and Kadapa.
xa: Drinking water for about **23 lakh** people in **fluoride-hit** areas.
Capacity **43.50 TMC**; water via twin **Nallamala tunnels** into **Nallamala Sagar**.

115.s: Gandipalem Project is a medium irrigation project on which river and in which district?
115.x: Gandipalem is a medium project on the Pillaperu River in SPSR Nellore district.
115.tq: Directly test the river–district association of a less familiar project.
xs: **Gandipalem** is a medium project on the **Pillaperu River** in **SPSR Nellore** — option **(2)** (APPSC 2025).
**Pennar** hosts **Somasila**; **Vamsadhara** is in **Srikakulam**.
xa: Vamsadhara = "**Lifeline of North Coastal AP**" (APPSC 2025).
National medium class: CCA **2,000-10,000 ha**.

115.s: Veligonda project is correctly described as:
o: A multipurpose dam on the Godavari at Dowleswaram
A project transferring Penna water through canals into the Krishna basin
A barrage on the Vamsadhara River supplying the northern delta
A project taking Krishna water from Srisailam by gravity through Nallamala tunnels into Nallamala Sagar
115.x: Veligonda takes Krishna water from Srisailam by gravity through tunnels in the Nallamala range and conveys it into Nallamala Sagar.
115.tq: Identify the project from its source, mode of conveyance and destination.
xs: **Veligonda** takes **Krishna water from Srisailam by gravity through Nallamala tunnels into Nallamala Sagar** — option **(4)**.
It is a **gravity diversion** — not a Godavari dam nor a Vamsadhara barrage.
xa: Capacity **43.50 TMC**; **4.47 lakh acres**; **30 mandals**.
Also called **Poola Subbaiah** Veligonda; foundation **5 Mar 1996**.
Phase-I: **10.70 TMC** into Nallamala Sagar, **1.19 lakh acres**, drinking water to **4 lakh** people.

115.s: Which one of the following irrigation projects is correctly matched with its principal river and storage capacity?
115.x: Handri-Neeva draws from the Krishna system at Srisailam and has a capacity of 40 TMC. Polavaram is associated with the Godavari, while Galeru-Nagari and Veligonda are associated with the Krishna system.
115.tq: Use the river–project–capacity combination and reject swapped river identities.
xs: **Handri-Neeva — Krishna — 40 TMC** — option **(1)**.
**Galeru-Nagari** (**38 TMC**) and **Veligonda** (**43.50 TMC**) are **Krishna** projects, not Godavari.
**Polavaram** is on the **Godavari**, not the Krishna.
xa: ⚠ **HNSS 40 / GNSS 38 / Veligonda 43.50 TMC**.
HNSS irrigates **6.025 lakh acres** and serves **33 lakh** people.

115.s: Which of the following correctly matches the Andhra Pradesh project with its ayacut?
115.x: Handri-Neeva is intended to irrigate 6.025 lakh acres in Rayalaseema. Galeru-Nagari serves 2.60 lakh acres and Veligonda serves 4.47 lakh acres.
115.tq: Anchor the answer using the distinctive Handri-Neeva ayacut and eliminate swapped project figures.
xs: **Handri-Neeva — 6.025 lakh acres** — option **(1)**.
**Galeru-Nagari** = **2.60 lakh acres**; **Veligonda** = **4.47 lakh acres** — options (2) and (3) swap them.
xa: HNSS: **40 TMC**; target **Mar 2027**.
GNSS districts: **Kadapa, Annamayya, Tirupati, Chittoor, Nellore**.
Veligonda: **30 mandals**; drinking water for about **23 lakh** people.

115.s: Veligonda Phase-I, inaugurated on 31 August 2026, is associated with which of the following?
o: Release of 38 TMC into Srisailam and irrigation of 2.60 lakh acres
Release of 10.70 TMC into Nallamala Sagar, irrigation of about 1.19 lakh acres and supply of drinking water to 4 lakh people
Release of 43.50 TMC into the Krishna delta and irrigation of 4.47 lakh acres
Release of 20,000 TMC into Vamsadhara and irrigation of 6.025 lakh acres
115.x: Veligonda Phase-I releases 10.70 TMC into Nallamala Sagar, irrigates about 1.19 lakh acres and supplies drinking water to approximately 4 lakh people.
115.tq: Match the inauguration event with its specific release, irrigation and population figures.
xs: Veligonda Phase-I: **10.70 TMC** into **Nallamala Sagar**, **1.19 lakh acres**, drinking water to **4 lakh** people — option **(2)**.
**38 TMC / 2.60 lakh acres** is **GNSS**; **43.50 TMC / 4.47 lakh acres** is Veligonda's full design.
xa: Inaugurated **31 Aug 2026** at **Gantavanipalli** (Markapuram district).
Foundation laid by **Naidu** on **5 Mar 1996**.

115.s: Vamsadhara Phase-II Stage-II is correctly associated with which of the following?
o: Vamsadhara River, Srikakulam and 20,000 acres of new ayacut
Krishna River, Kadapa and 2.60 lakh acres
Pennar River, Nellore and 4.47 lakh acres
Godavari River, East Godavari and 6.025 lakh acres
115.x: Vamsadhara Phase-II Stage-II is a project on the Vamsadhara River in Srikakulam, with 93.5% completion and 20,000 acres of proposed new ayacut.
115.tq: Use the river, district and new-ayacut figure as a three-part identification test.
xs: Vamsadhara Phase-II Stage-II: **Vamsadhara River**, **Srikakulam**, **20,000 acres** new ayacut — option **(1)**.
It is **93.5%** done.
**2.60 lakh acres** is GNSS, **4.47** Veligonda, **6.025** HNSS.
xa: "**Lifeline of North Coastal AP**" (APPSC 2025).
**Vamsadhara-Nagavali link** due by December (Apr 2026).

115.s: Which of the following statements about the Pattiseema scheme is correct?
o: It lifts Krishna water into the Godavari Right Main Canal for delivery to the Godavari delta.
It lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram Right Main Canal, which carries it to the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage.
It transfers water from the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage to the Godavari through a gravity canal.
It diverts Pennar water into the Krishna through the Tungabhadra High Level Canal.
115.x: Pattiseema lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram Right Main Canal, which carries it to the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage. It is recognised as the first Godavari-Krishna link.
115.tq: Trace the direction of flow and identify both the source river and receiving river.
xs: Pattiseema **lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram Right Main Canal**, which carries it **to the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage** — option **(2)**.
It is the **first Godavari-Krishna link**; options (1) and (3) reverse the direction.
xa: **Lift irrigation scheme** (PYQ) with **24 pumps**; commissioned **2015**.
~**450 TMC** transferred so far.
Beneficiaries: **Krishna delta** farmers (PYQ 2018, 2017).

115.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the operational status intended for the Pattiseema scheme?
o: It was intended to operate only during years of normal monsoon rainfall.
It was intended as a temporary arrangement until gravity flow from Polavaram commenced.
It was designed exclusively for supplying drinking water to urban centres.
It was designed as a permanent replacement for Polavaram's gravity flow.
115.x: Pattiseema was a temporary scheme intended to function until gravity flow from the Polavaram project became available.
115.tq: Distinguish a temporary interim arrangement from a permanent project objective.
xs: Pattiseema is **temporary until Polavaram's gravity flow** starts — option **(2)**.
It is an **irrigation** lift for **Krishna delta** farmers, not a drinking-water or permanent scheme.
xa: Built **2014-19**; commissioned **2015**; **24 pumps**.
Kept the Krishna delta supplied during the **2026 El Nino** deficit.

115.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Pattiseema scheme is correct?
1. It had 24 pumps.
2. It was built during 2014-19.
3. It was commissioned in 2015.
4. It helped keep the Krishna delta supplied during the 2026 El Niño deficit.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: All four statements are correct. Pattiseema had 24 pumps, was built during 2014-19, commissioned in 2015 and helped supply the Krishna delta during the 2026 El Niño deficit.
115.tq: Combine structural, chronological and operational facts without confusing commissioning with completion.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Pattiseema has **24 pumps**, was built **2014-19**, commissioned **2015**.
It kept the **Krishna delta** supplied during the **2026 El Nino deficit**.
xa: ~**450 TMC** transferred.
⚠ PYQ false statement: "canal runs **100 km** through West Godavari".
Route: **Polavaram RMC** → **Krishna at Prakasam Barrage**.

115.s: Which one of the following statements about the Pattiseema scheme is NOT true, as per the PYQ?
o: It is a lift irrigation scheme on the Godavari
It mainly benefits farmers of the Krishna delta
It is a temporary arrangement until gravity flow from Polavaram begins
Its canal runs 100 km through West Godavari district
115.x: Pattiseema is a lift irrigation scheme on the Godavari, its water serves Krishna delta farmers, and it is temporary until Polavaram's gravity flow starts - all true. The claim that its canal runs 100 km through West Godavari was the false statement in the PYQ.
115.tq: Pattiseema: lift, Krishna delta, temporary.
xs: The false statement is "**canal runs 100 km through West Godavari**" — option **(4)**.
True: it is a **lift irrigation scheme on the Godavari**, benefits **Krishna delta** farmers, and is **temporary** until Polavaram gravity flow.
xa: Exam angle: "Pattiseema is a **lift irrigation project**" (PYQ 2018, 2017).
It is the **first Godavari-Krishna link**.

115.s:
Match List-I (Project/programme) with List-II (Plan period):
a. Prakasam Barrage (completed 1957)
b. Srisailam (sanctioned 1963)
c. Telugu Ganga (1983)
d. Jalayagnam (2004)

i. Third Plan
ii. First to Second Plan
iii. Tenth Plan
iv. Sixth Plan

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: Prakasam Barrage belongs to the First-to-Second Plan (a-ii); Srisailam was sanctioned in the Third Plan (b-i); Telugu Ganga (1983) is a Sixth Plan project (c-iv); Jalayagnam (2004) falls in the Tenth Plan (d-iii). Option A is correct; B swaps Prakasam and Srisailam, C swaps Telugu Ganga and Jalayagnam, D swaps Srisailam and Telugu Ganga.
115.tq: Convert years to Plans: 1963 = Third (1961-66), 1983 = Sixth (1980-85), 2004 = Tenth (2002-07).
xs: Correct match: a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii — option **(1)**.
**Prakasam Barrage** (completed **1957**) — **First to Second** Plan; **Srisailam** (sanctioned **1963**) — **Third**.
**Telugu Ganga** (**1983**) — **Sixth**; **Jalayagnam** (**2004**) — **Tenth Plan (2002-07)**.
xa: **Nagarjuna Sagar**: **First Plan** foundation; completion prioritised in **Fifth Plan (1974-79)**.
Jalayagnam was launched by the **YSR** government.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Jalayagnam:
1. It was launched during the Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07).
2. It was launched by the N. Chandrababu Naidu government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 1 is correct: Jalayagnam was launched during the Tenth Plan (2002-07). Statement 2 is wrong: it was launched by Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy, not N. Chandrababu Naidu (who is linked to Neeru-Meeru, 2000). Hence 1 only (A); B, C and D misjudge one of the statements.
115.tq: Jalayagnam = YSR (2004); Neeru-Meeru = Naidu (2000).
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Jalayagnam** belongs to the **Tenth Plan (2002-07)** (PYQ).
Statement 2 wrong: it was the **Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy** government (**2004**); Naidu is linked to **Neeru-Meeru (2000)**.
xa: Aim: irrigate **1 crore acres**, stabilise **21 lakh acres**.
**52 major and medium** projects; **41 major + 25 minor** proposed.

115.s: Which of the following correctly states the stated aims and proposed project composition of Jalayagnam?
o: Irrigate 40 TMC, stabilise 38 TMC, and take up 41 minor and 25 major projects
Irrigate 21 lakh acres, stabilise one crore acres, and take up 25 major and 41 minor projects
Irrigate 4.47 lakh acres, stabilise 2.60 lakh acres, and take up 52 minor projects only
Irrigate one crore acres, stabilise 21 lakh acres, and take up 41 major and 25 minor projects
115.x: Jalayagnam aimed to irrigate one crore acres and stabilise 21 lakh acres; 41 major and 25 minor projects were proposed.
115.tq: Keep the target figures and the major–minor project counts in their correct order.
xs: Jalayagnam: **irrigate 1 crore acres, stabilise 21 lakh acres**, **41 major + 25 minor** projects — option **(4)**.
Option (2) swaps the irrigate/stabilise figures; **40 TMC / 38 TMC** and **4.47 / 2.60 lakh acres** belong to HNSS, GNSS and Veligonda.
xa: It covers **52 major and medium** projects.
**Veligonda, HNSS, GNSS** were unfinished in **2025-26**.

115.s: Which of the following statements regarding Jalayagnam projects is correct?
o: Jalayagnam consisted exclusively of minor irrigation projects.
Polavaram, started in 2005, continues to be treated as a Jalayagnam project, while Veligonda, Handri-Neeva and Galeru-Nagari remained unfinished in 2025–26.
Only Vamsadhara Phase-II remained unfinished in 2025–26 among the listed projects.
Polavaram was completed before Jalayagnam was launched and was not included in it.
115.x: Polavaram, begun in 2005, is treated as a Jalayagnam project. Veligonda, Handri-Neeva and Galeru-Nagari were still unfinished in 2025–26.
115.tq: Watch for the false exclusion and completion claims in statements about programme projects.
xs: **Polavaram** (started **2005**) is still a Jalayagnam project; **Veligonda, HNSS, GNSS** were unfinished in **2025-26** — option **(2)**.
Jalayagnam had **41 major** + **25 minor** projects, so not "exclusively minor".
xa: Launched by **Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy** (**2004**), **Tenth Plan**.
Irrigation White Paper (**Jul 2026**): complete **36 projects by Dec 2028** at **Rs 35,555 crore**.

115.s: The Krishna River Management Board and Godavari River Management Board operate under the:
o: Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, with Schedule 11 principles
115.x: KRMB and GRMB operate under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, following the principles in Schedule 11.
115.tq: Apply the wrong-law trap to identify the governing statute.
xs: **KRMB and GRMB** are under the **AP Reorganisation Act 2014**, on **Schedule 11** principles — option **(2)**.
**KWDT** allocations form the basis of the KRMB operation protocol.
xa: Existing tribunal allocations unchanged; **future excess-flow allocations** bind both states.
Boards advise on **floods and droughts**, with **full authority to enforce orders**.
The **Tungabhadra Board** releases water to **HLC, LLC** and the **RDS**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards:
1. The operation protocol of the Ministry of Water Resources based on KWDT adjudication is binding on both States.
2. Existing tribunal allocations remain unchanged.
3. Future excess-flow allocations are binding on both States.
4. The Boards advise on floods and droughts and have authority to enforce their orders.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: All four statements correctly state the operating and enforcement principles applicable to the Boards.
115.tq: Treat each institutional power and allocation rule as an independent statement.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
The **MoWR protocol based on KWDT** adjudication binds both States; **existing tribunal allocations** stay unchanged.
**Future excess-flow allocations** bind both States; Boards advise on **floods + droughts** and **enforce orders**.
xa: KRMB/GRMB set up under **APRA 2014**, **Schedule 11**.
AP forum worry: Krishna settlement linked to consent to **Palamuru-Rangareddy** (May 2026).

115.s: The GWDT award of 1980 permitted diversion of how much Godavari water to the Krishna?
115.x: The 1980 GWDT award permitted the Polavaram diversion of 80 TMC of Godavari water to the Krishna.
115.tq: Recall the tribunal-specific diversion quantity and year.
xs: The **1980 GWDT award** permitted diversion of **80 TMC** Godavari water to the Krishna — option **(2)**.
**40 TMC** is HNSS's capacity — a distractor.
xa: **Pattiseema** was the first Godavari-Krishna link via the **Polavaram RMC**.
After Polavaram, ~**200 TMC** Godavari water is planned for **Nagarjunasagar** ayacut.

115.s: Which concern was raised by a forum of Andhra Pradesh intellectuals regarding the Krishna water settlement with Telangana?
o: That it would eliminate all drinking-water priorities
That it would transfer the Tungabhadra Board to Karnataka
That it was being linked to Andhra Pradesh’s consent to Palamuru–Rangareddy
That it would abolish the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal
115.x: The concern was that the Krishna water settlement with Telangana was being linked to Andhra Pradesh’s consent to the Palamuru–Rangareddy project.
115.tq: Identify the specific political linkage in an inter-State water controversy.
xs: The forum feared the Krishna settlement was **linked to AP's consent to Palamuru-Rangareddy** — option **(3)** (May 2026).
The **Tungabhadra Board** and **GWDT** are unaffected in the notes.
xa: **KWDT** allocations underpin the **KRMB** protocol.
Telangana objects to **Godavari links** — a standing debate.

115.s: Under APFAMGS, farmers primarily:
o: Construct only large dams and canals through compulsory land acquisition
Collect rainfall and well-level data, prepare crop-water budgets and voluntarily regulate pumping
Transfer all groundwater monitoring to the Union Government
Regulate irrigation exclusively according to urban water demand
115.x: APFAMGS promotes farmer-led collection of rainfall and well-level data, crop-water budgeting on a hydrological-unit basis and voluntary regulation of pumping.
115.tq: Apply the participatory-management principle to the functions actually performed by farmers.
xs: Under **APFAMGS**, farmers **collect rainfall and well-level data**, do **crop-water budgets** and **voluntarily regulate pumping** — option **(2)**.
Budgeting is on a **hydrological-unit** basis — no dams, compulsory acquisition or Union control.
xa: APFAMGS = **AP Farmer Managed Groundwater Systems**, an **FAO-supported NGO project** in drought-prone districts.
AP has ~**19 lakh** bore wells; **40,000-50,000** added yearly.

115.s:
Consider the following statements about APFAMGS:
1. It was an FAO-supported NGO project.
2. It operated in drought-prone districts.
3. Farmers prepared crop-water budgets on a hydrological-unit basis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: APFAMGS was an FAO-supported NGO initiative in drought-prone districts and used hydrological-unit-based crop-water budgeting by farmers. All three statements are correct.
115.tq: Check the institutional support, area of operation and operational method separately.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
APFAMGS: **FAO-supported NGO** project in **drought-prone districts**.
Farmers prepare **crop-water budgets** on a **hydrological-unit** basis.
xa: Farmers monitor their own **rainfall and well-level** data.
Pumping regulation is **voluntary**.

115.s: Which of the following is a provision associated with APWALTA, 2002?
o: The Act permits indiscriminate digging of borewells in all villages.
The Act applies only to hydropower projects and not to groundwater extraction.
Rainwater-harvesting structures are required on residential, commercial and other premises measuring 200 sq m or more.
Rainwater harvesting is required only on agricultural holdings above 200 hectares.
115.x: APWALTA, 2002 requires rainwater-harvesting structures on residential, commercial and other premises of 200 square metres or more and seeks to prevent indiscriminate borewell digging.
115.tq: Identify the statutory threshold and reject reversals of the law’s purpose.
xs: APWALTA, 2002 makes **rainwater-harvesting** structures mandatory on premises of **200 sq m** or more — option **(3)** (PYQ 2019).
It targets **indiscriminate borewell digging** (PYQ 2018) — the opposite of option (1).
xa: Bore-well siting follows **APWALTA-2002 norms**.
**258 over-exploited villages** proposed for notification (GEC 2024-25; SES 2025-26).
**Water Protection Board** set up in **2002**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding groundwater in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Groundwater investigations and bore-well siting follow APWALTA-2002 norms.
2. The stage of groundwater development is about 30%, in the safe category.
3. About 40,000-50,000 new bore wells are added every year, so the area irrigated per well is rising.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 1 is correct: investigations and siting follow APWALTA-2002 norms. Statement 2 is correct: development stage is ~30% (safe). Statement 3 is wrong: 40,000-50,000 new bore wells a year means the area irrigated per well is falling, not rising. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
115.tq: More wells drawing on the same aquifer means less area per well.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: investigations and siting follow **APWALTA-2002 norms**.
Statement 2 correct: development stage **~30% (safe)**.
Statement 3 wrong: **40,000-50,000** new bore wells yearly means area per well is **falling**.
xa: AP has **3,005 telemetry wells**; real-time monitoring set up by the **National Hydrology Project**.
**258 over-exploited villages** proposed under APWALTA.

115.s: Which Andhra Pradesh law seeks to check indiscriminate digging of borewells?
o: AP Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002
AP Farmer Managed Groundwater Systems Act, 2005
115.x: APWALTA - the AP Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002 - is AP's law against indiscriminate borewell digging (PYQ 2018) and also mandates rainwater harvesting on premises of 200 sq m or more. APFAMGS is a farmer-managed project, not an Act; the other two titles are distractors.
115.tq: Borewell law = APWALTA 2002.
xs: **APWALTA** — **AP Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002** — option **(2)** (PYQ 2018).
**APFAMGS** is an **FAO-supported NGO project**, not an Act.
xa: It mandates rainwater harvesting on premises of **200 sq m** or more.
**Neeru-Meeru** (**2000**): watershed + rainwater harvesting drive.
**Neeru-Chettu** (**2 Oct 2014**): **Water Resources Department** is nodal.

115.s: Which of the following best describes the primary focus of the Neeru-Meeru programme?
o: Urban solid-waste management and sewage treatment
Construction of only major irrigation dams
Rainwater harvesting and raising groundwater levels
Large-scale inter-basin transfer of river water
115.x: Neeru-Meeru was a watershed and rainwater-harvesting drive intended to raise groundwater levels.
115.tq: Identify the programme by matching its stated objective.
xs: **Neeru-Meeru** was a watershed drive for **rainwater harvesting and raising groundwater** — option **(3)**.
It was launched by **Naidu** in **2000** (APP).
xa: **Neeru-Chettu** followed on **2 Oct 2014**, with the **Water Resources Department** as nodal department.
**Water Protection Board** was set up in **2002**.
**APWALTA, 2002** mandates rainwater harvesting on premises of **200 sq m** or more.

115.s: Neeru-Chettu was launched in Andhra Pradesh on:
115.x: Neeru-Chettu was launched on 2 October 2014.
115.tq: Test the exact date attached to a government programme.
xs: **Neeru-Chettu** was launched on **2 October 2014** — option **(4)**.
It is a **water-conservation sub-mission** across line departments.
xa: Nodal department: **Water Resources Department**.
**1,00,171 works** at an estimated **Rs 6,790 crore** (2024-25, APSES).
2025-26: **₹445.89 crore** budgeted to clear pending bills.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Neeru-Chettu:
1. It is a water-conservation sub-mission implemented across line departments.
2. The Water Resources Department is its nodal department.
3. Its works include tank desilting, bund strengthening and check dams on minor streams.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: All three statements are correct. Neeru-Chettu operates across line departments under the Water Resources Department and includes the listed water-conservation works.
115.tq: Check whether the programme, nodal department and works are all correctly associated.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Neeru-Chettu** is a water-conservation **sub-mission across line departments**.
Statement 2: the **Water Resources Department** is the **nodal department**.
Statement 3: works include **desilting tank beds**, **strengthening tank bunds** and **check dams on minor streams**.
xa: Other works: repairs of **sluices, weirs and shutters**; desilting supply channels; **tank cascades**.

115.s: Jaladhara-Jalaharathi is associated with which of the following?
o: A 100-day water-conservation plan launched in April 2026
A five-year crop-insurance programme launched in 2024
115.x: Jaladhara-Jalaharathi is a 100-day water-conservation plan launched in April 2026.
115.tq: Separate similarly themed water programmes by their nature and launch period.
xs: **Jaladhara-Jalaharathi** is a **100-day water-conservation** action plan of **April 2026** — option **(1)**.
The **2003** micro-irrigation scheme is **APMIP**, not this.
xa: It is run with **Water Users Associations**.
It was launched at **Yadiki, Anantapur** (**7 Apr 2026**).

115.s: What is the approximate distribution of APMIP coverage between drip and sprinkler irrigation?
115.x: APMIP coverage consists of approximately 75% drip irrigation and 25% sprinkler irrigation.
115.tq: Test the direction of the percentage comparison.
xs: APMIP coverage is **75% drip and 25% sprinkler** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) reverses the shares.
xa: Since inception: **37.90 lakh acres** and **13.49 lakh farmers**.
APMIP was launched in **2003**; now run as **RKVY-PDMC**.
Subsidy **100% for SC/ST**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding micro-irrigation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. About 1.90 lakh hectares were covered between June 2024 and December 2025.
2. Andhra Pradesh ranked first nationally in micro-irrigation in 2024–25.
3. The subsidy is 100% for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: All three statements are correct: 1.90 lakh hectares were covered during the stated period, Andhra Pradesh ranked first nationally in 2024–25, and SC/ST beneficiaries receive 100% subsidy.
115.tq: Verify a cluster of current coverage, ranking and subsidy facts.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **1.90 lakh ha** covered **Jun 2024-Dec 2025**.
Statement 2: AP ranked **1st nationally** in micro-irrigation **2024-25**.
Statement 3: subsidy is **100% for SC/ST**.
xa: Targets: **35%** of gross sown area by **2030**; **50%** by **2047**.
Saturation could raise groundwater-based net irrigation to **40 lakh acres**.

115.s: The target for micro-irrigation as a share of gross sown area is:
115.x: The target is micro-irrigation over 35% of gross sown area by 2030 and 50% by 2047.
115.tq: Recall paired target years and percentages together.
xs: Target: micro-irrigation on **35% of gross sown area by 2030 and 50% by 2047** — option **(3)**.
The other pairs are not in the notes.
xa: AP ranked **1st** nationally in micro-irrigation **2024-25**.
APMIP: **75% drip, 25% sprinkler**.
Saturation could raise groundwater-based net irrigation to **40 lakh acres**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Per Drop More Crop (PDMC):
1. It began in 2015-16.
2. It gives 45% assistance to small and marginal farmers and 55% to others for drip and sprinkler systems.
3. It has been implemented under RKVY since 2022-23.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 1 is correct: PDMC began in 2015-16. Statement 2 is wrong: the pattern is 55% for small and marginal farmers and 45% for others (reversed here). Statement 3 is correct: it has been under RKVY since 2022-23. Hence 1 and 3 only (C); A misses statement 3, B and D wrongly include statement 2.
115.tq: Small and marginal farmers always get the higher share: 55%.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **PDMC** began in **2015-16**.
Statement 2 wrong: it gives **55%** to **small and marginal** farmers and **45%** to others — reversed here.
Statement 3 correct: PDMC is **under RKVY since 2022-23**.
xa: **102 lakh ha** covered nationally since **2015-16**.
⚠ PDMC **55%** small/marginal vs **45%** others; **APMIP 100%** for SC/ST.
PDMC is a component of **PMKSY**.

115.s: The Micro Irrigation Fund, having a corpus of ₹10,000 crore, is associated with:
o: NABARD, with Andhra Pradesh among the eight funded States
RBI, with Andhra Pradesh as the sole funded State
NWDA, with all States receiving equal funds
KRMB, with only the two Krishna-basin States receiving funds
115.x: The Micro Irrigation Fund is maintained through NABARD with a ₹10,000 crore corpus, and Andhra Pradesh is among the eight States funded.
115.tq: Use the ‘who administers the fund’ trap and verify the membership count.
xs: The **Micro Irrigation Fund** is with **NABARD**; **AP is among the eight states** funded — option **(1)**.
Its corpus is **Rs 10,000 crore**.
xa: **APMIP** (**2003**) now runs as **RKVY-PDMC**.
AP ranked **1st** nationally in micro-irrigation **2024-25**.

115.s: The Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project (APMIP) was launched in which year, and under which scheme is it now run?
115.x: APMIP began in 2003 and now runs as RKVY-PDMC. 2015 relates to PDMC's start nationally (and Har Khet Ko Pani is a different PMKSY component), Neeru-Meeru (2000) and Neeru-Chettu (2014) are water-conservation programmes, not micro-irrigation.
115.tq: APMIP 2003, now RKVY-PDMC.
xs: **APMIP** was launched in **2003** and now runs as **RKVY-PDMC** (**RKVY-Per Drop More Crop**) — option **(1)**.
**Neeru-Meeru** (**2000**) and **Neeru-Chettu** (**2014**) are water-conservation programmes; **Har Khet Ko Pani** is a separate **PMKSY** component.
xa: Coverage: **37.90 lakh acres**, **13.49 lakh farmers**; **75% drip, 25% sprinkler**.
**PDMC** began **2015-16**; under **RKVY since 2022-23**.

115.s: Which of the following projects is correctly matched with its river and State location?
o: Damodar Valley — Damodar — Jharkhand and West Bengal
Tungabhadra — Mahanadi — Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Nagarjuna Sagar — Damodar — Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
115.x: The Damodar Valley project is on the Damodar and is associated with Jharkhand and West Bengal. The other options reverse the river or project association.
115.tq: Start from the sure river-project pair and eliminate swapped locations.
xs: **Damodar Valley — Damodar — Jharkhand / West Bengal** — option **(1)**.
**Hirakud** is on the **Mahanadi** (Odisha), not the Krishna.
**Tungabhadra** is on the Tungabhadra; **Nagarjuna Sagar** is on the **Krishna**.
xa: Hirakud is **one of the longest earthen dams**.
Nagarjuna Sagar is **one of the largest masonry dams** in the world, serving **AP and Telangana**.

115.s: Hirakud is notable as:
o: A canal-only irrigation project without a dam
The largest concrete arch dam in Asia
A tidal barrage on the Krishna
One of the longest earthen dams
115.x: Hirakud in Odisha is noted as one of the longest earthen dams.
115.tq: Identify the distinctive descriptive feature of a named project.
xs: **Hirakud** is **one of the longest earthen dams** — option **(4)**.
It is on the **Mahanadi** in **Odisha** — not the Krishna.
xa: ⚠ **Nagarjuna Sagar** (Krishna) is one of the **largest masonry dams** in the world.
**Damodar Valley** spans **Jharkhand / West Bengal**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding irrigation debates in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Rayalaseema depends on Krishna-lift projects such as HNSS, GNSS and Telugu Ganga, which often run dry.
2. A key criticism is the gap between irrigation potential created and potential utilised.
3. Telangana supports Andhra Pradesh's proposed Godavari links.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 1 is correct: Rayalaseema relies on HNSS, GNSS and Telugu Ganga, which often run dry. Statement 2 is correct: potential created vs utilised is a standing criticism. Statement 3 is wrong: Telangana objects to the Godavari links (it says they violate APRA 2014 and the 1980 GWDT award). Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
115.tq: Inter-State angle: Telangana objects, it does not support.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Rayalaseema** relies on **HNSS, GNSS and Telugu Ganga**, which "**often run dry**".
Statement 2 correct: **potential created vs utilised** is a standing criticism.
Statement 3 wrong: **Telangana objects** to AP's **Godavari links**.
xa: Irrigation White Paper (**Jul 2026**): **36 projects by Dec 2028** at **Rs 35,555 crore**.
**Rs 24,611 crore** was spent in the previous two years.

115.s: Which of the following statements regarding recent proposals concerning the Polavaram project is correct?
o: Its completion was proposed before the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu, along with diversion of about 200 TMC of Godavari water to the Nagarjunasagar ayacut.
Its completion was proposed after the 2028 Irrigation White Paper deadline, without any proposed water diversion.
It was proposed to divert about 200 TMC of Krishna water to the Vamsadhara ayacut before the 2027 Pushkaralu.
It was proposed to be completed before the 2026 Pushkaralu by diverting 68 TMC of Godavari water.
115.x: The proposal was to complete Polavaram before the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu and to divert about 200 TMC of Godavari water to the Nagarjunasagar ayacut.
115.tq: Link the correct project, deadline, river, quantity and ayacut while rejecting swapped figures and locations.
xs: Polavaram completion **before the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu**, with ~**200 TMC** Godavari water to the **Nagarjunasagar ayacut** — option **(1)**.
The water is **Godavari**, not Krishna, and goes to Nagarjunasagar, not Vamsadhara.
xa: **Vamsadhara-Nagavali link** is due by December (Apr 2026).
White Paper: **36 projects by Dec 2028**.
Polavaram status (May 2026): **88% civil works**, **93% land acquisition**, **45% R&R**.

115.s:
Which of the following are components of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)?
1. Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme
2. Har Khet Ko Pani
3. Watershed
4. Per Drop More Crop
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: PMKSY includes AIBP, Har Khet Ko Pani, Watershed and Per Drop More Crop.
115.tq: Verify every item in a named-scheme list before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All four are **PMKSY** components — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
