PMKSY = **AIBP + Har Khet Ko Pani + Watershed + PDMC**.
xa: **M-CADWM** was approved in **2025-26** as a sub-scheme of **PMKSY-AIBP**.
**PDMC** gives **55%** to small/marginal farmers, **45%** to others.

115.s:
With reference to PMKSY, consider the following statements:
1. M-CADWM was approved in 2025–26.
2. M-CADWM is a sub-scheme of PMKSY-AIBP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Both statements are correct. M-CADWM was approved in 2025–26 as a sub-scheme of PMKSY-AIBP.
115.tq: Match the special sub-scheme with its approval year and parent programme.
xs: Both statements are correct — option **(3) Both 1 and 2**.
**M-CADWM** was approved in **2025-26** as a **sub-scheme of PMKSY-AIBP**.
xa: PMKSY components: **AIBP**, **Har Khet Ko Pani**, **Watershed**, **PDMC**.
PDMC has run **under RKVY since 2022-23**.

115.s: The National Hydrology Project helped Andhra Pradesh establish:
115.x: The National Hydrology Project set up Andhra Pradesh's real-time groundwater monitoring system.
115.tq: Identify the practical institutional outcome associated with the named national project.
xs: The **National Hydrology Project** set up AP's **real-time groundwater monitoring** — option **(4)**.
AP has **3,005 telemetry wells**.
xa: Groundwater development stage: **~30% (safe)**.
**40,000-50,000** new bore wells added yearly; area irrigated per well **falling**.

115.s: The Andhra Pradesh Irrigation White Paper of July 2026 set which target?
o: Complete 36 projects by December 2028 at Rs 35,555 crore
Complete 52 projects by March 2027 at Rs 24,611 crore
Complete 41 major projects by 2030 at Rs 55,548 crore
Complete 25 minor projects by December 2026 at Rs 6,790 crore
115.x: The White Paper aims to complete 36 projects by December 2028 at Rs 35,555 crore, backed by an Irrigation Action Calendar. Rs 24,611 crore was spent in the previous two years, Rs 55,548 crore is Polavaram's older RCE, and Rs 6,790 crore is the Neeru-Chettu works estimate.
115.tq: White Paper: 36 projects, Dec 2028.
xs: The **Irrigation White Paper (Jul 2026)**: **36 projects by December 2028** at **Rs 35,555 crore** — option **(1)**.
**Rs 24,611 crore** was spent in the previous two years; **Rs 6,790 crore** is the **Neeru-Chettu** works estimate.
xa: It is backed by an **Irrigation Action Calendar**.
**52** is Jalayagnam's count of major and medium projects; **41 major + 25 minor** were proposed.

115.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Coastal Andhra has the highest concentration of tanks, with more than 14,000 minor tanks.
Rayalaseema's tanks support irrigation and groundwater recharge.
Coastal Andhra has more than 6,800 active tanks mainly supporting groundwater recharge.
Rayalaseema has more than 6,800 active tanks.
115.x: Option C is incorrect: over 6,800 active tanks for irrigation and recharge belong to Rayalaseema. Coastal Andhra has over 14,000 minor tanks.
115.tq: Discriminate the tank figures of each region.
n: Coastal Andhra has more than 14,000 minor tanks. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 46-48]
Coastal Andhra has the highest concentration of tanks. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 46-48]
Rayalaseema has more than 6,800 active tanks. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 46-48]
Rayalaseema tanks support irrigation. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 46-48]
Rayalaseema tanks support groundwater recharge. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 46-48]

115.s:
Consider the following statements:

Statement A: Coastal Andhra includes Vizianagaram and Srikakulam in the regional tank distribution.
Statement B: Rayalaseema includes Annamayya and Chittoor in the regional tank distribution.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
115.x: Both are true: Vizianagaram and Srikakulam count under Coastal Andhra, and Annamayya and Chittoor under Rayalaseema.
115.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Coastal Andhra includes Vizianagaram and Srikakulam in the regional tank distribution. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 46-48]
Rayalaseema includes Annamayya and Chittoor in the regional tank distribution. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 46-48]

116.s: Which of the following correctly describes the industrial loss suffered by the residual State of Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation?
o: It lost the HITEC City and Financial District, which had been the engine of IT exports
It retained Hyderabad's IT clusters and lost only its agricultural-processing units
It retained HITEC City and the Financial District but lost its port-based industries
It lost all IT activity because no new IT park was established in the State
116.x: The residual State lost Hyderabad's HITEC City and Financial District, important centres of IT and IT-enabled services exports.
116.tq: Identify the precise sector-location combination rather than accepting an extreme statement.
xs: AP lost **HITEC City** and the **Financial District** — the **engine of IT exports** — option **(1)**.
AP did not lose all IT: it started new IT parks at **Visakhapatnam, Tirupati, Vijayawada**.
xa: Pharma: **Genome Valley** and the Hyderabad belt went; AP kept only a **bulk-drug base at Vizag**.
**MSMEs**: thousands of ancillary units ended up across the border, **breaking supply chains**.
Offsetting advantage: coastline and ports → **port-led, EXIM** strategy.

116.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the industrial base of residual Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation:
1. Genome Valley and the Hyderabad pharma belt with its R&D remained outside Andhra Pradesh.
2. Andhra Pradesh kept only a bulk-drug base at Visakhapatnam.
3. Hyderabad-linked ancillary MSMEs remained within Andhra Pradesh, keeping supply chains intact.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statement 1 is correct: Genome Valley and the Hyderabad pharma belt went with Telangana. Statement 2 is correct: AP kept only a bulk-drug base at Vizag. Statement 3 is wrong: thousands of ancillary MSMEs ended up across the border, breaking supply chains. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
116.tq: Everything clustered around Hyderabad (IT, pharma R&D, ancillaries) was lost to AP.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Genome Valley** and the Hyderabad **pharma belt** with R&D stayed outside AP.
Statement 2 correct: AP kept only a **bulk-drug base at Vizag**.
Statement 3 wrong: thousands of **ancillary MSMEs** went across the border, **breaking supply chains**.
xa: IT/ITeS: AP lost **HITEC City** and the **Financial District**.
Corporate and bank regional HQs stayed in Hyderabad — **no commercial nerve centre**.

116.s:
Just after bifurcation, the industrial structure of residual Andhra Pradesh was described as follows:
1. The State was approximately 60 percent agriculture-dependent.
2. Manufacturing accounted for around 10.5 percent of GSDP.
3. The figure of 10.5 percent represented the entire industry sector, including mining, construction and utilities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: Residual Andhra Pradesh was about 60 percent agriculture-dependent, and manufacturing was put at around 10.5 percent of GSDP. The 10.5 percent figure did not represent the whole industry sector.
116.tq: Separate a precise sectoral figure from the broader aggregate to catch a scope error.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: residual AP was ~**60% agriculture-dependent**.
Statement 2 correct: the "**10.5%** of GSDP" matches **manufacturing**.
Statement 3 wrong: it is not the whole **industry sector**, which includes **mining, construction, utilities**.
xa: 2025-26 GVA: services **43%**, agriculture **33%**, industry **24%**; manufacturing **10.84%**.
AP got **58%** of population but only **46%** of revenue.

116.s: Why did the retention of corporate and bank regional headquarters in Hyderabad create a difficulty for residual Andhra Pradesh?
o: It deprived the State of all banking services
It prevented the formation of any district administration
It left the State without a commercial nerve centre
It transferred all ports to Telangana
116.x: Corporate and bank regional headquarters stayed in Hyderabad, leaving residual Andhra Pradesh without a commercial nerve centre.
116.tq: Infer the institutional consequence from the location of headquarters.
xs: With corporate and bank regional HQs in Hyderabad, AP had **no commercial nerve centre** — option **(3)**.
AP kept its **ports** — its coastline drives a **port-led, EXIM** strategy.
xa: **Investment chill** after 2014: capital uncertainty, no ready administrative set-up, agitations.
Government moved from Hyderabad to **Velagapudi (Amaravati)**; APSWAN HQ moved in **2017**.

116.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding institutional division under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation framework.

List-I
 a. Schedule IX
 b. Schedule X
 c. Sheela Bhide Committee
 d. Section 53

List-II
 i. Division of 142 institutions, mostly in Hyderabad
 ii. Allocation of commercial undertakings by location and headquarters assets by population
 iii. Division of 91 companies and corporations
 iv. Committee associated with the division of institutions

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
116.x: Schedule IX covered 91 companies and corporations; Schedule X covered 142 institutions, mostly in Hyderabad; the Sheela Bhide Committee was associated with the division; and Section 53 provided the location and population basis.
116.tq: Start from the sure numerical pairs and then complete the institutional mapping.
xs: Correct match: a–iii, b–i, c–iv, d–ii — option **(1)**.
**Schedule IX** = **91** companies and corporations; **Schedule X** = **142** institutions, mostly in Hyderabad.
**Sheela Bhide Committee** handled the division; **Sec 53** splits commercial undertakings by **location**, HQ assets by **population**.
xa: ⚠ Schedule **IX = 91**; Schedule **X = 142**.
Result: **litigation**; **AP Bhavan** and **APPA, APFA** left out.
**Sec 5**: Hyderabad common capital up to **10 years (till 2024)**.

116.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the capital of Andhra Pradesh:
1. Under Section 5 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was the common capital for up to ten years, till 2024.
2. The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 made Amaravati the sole capital through a new Section 5(3).
3. The 2026 amendment began the three-capitals arrangement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statement 1 is correct: Section 5 made Hyderabad the common capital for up to 10 years (till 2024). Statement 2 is correct: the 2026 Amendment Act inserted Section 5(3) making Amaravati the sole capital. Statement 3 is wrong: the amendment ended the 2019-24 three-capitals uncertainty, it did not begin it. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
116.tq: 2014: Hyderabad common capital for 10 years; 2019-24: three-capitals uncertainty; 2026: Amaravati sole capital.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Sec 5** made **Hyderabad** the common capital up to **10 years (till 2024)**.
Statement 2 correct: the **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026** made **Amaravati the sole capital** (new **Sec 5(3)**).
Statement 3 wrong: it **ended** the **2019-24 three-capitals** uncertainty.
xa: State Cabinet resolution: **27 Mar 2026**.
Government moved to **Velagapudi (Amaravati)**.

116.s: Which one of the following best represents the broad outcome of the apportionment described for residual Andhra Pradesh?
o: It received 41.68 percent of the population and about 60 percent of the revenue.
It received equal shares of population, debt and revenue.
It received about 58 percent of the revenue and 46 percent of the population.
It received about 46 percent of the revenue, despite having about 58 percent of the population and debt.
116.x: Andhra Pradesh received about 58 percent of the population and debt but only around 46 percent of the revenue, reflecting the loss of Hyderabad's revenue base.
116.tq: Compare the three shares directly instead of treating them as identical bases.
xs: AP got ~**46% of revenue** despite **58% of population** and **58% of debt** — option **(4)**.
Debt was split on a **population basis**, so AP inherited the larger share.
Option (3) swaps the figures.
xa: Hyderabad's revenue base stayed with Telangana: **HITEC City**, **Genome Valley**.
SCS refused citing the **14th Finance Commission**; **Special Assistance Measure** of **₹24,350 crore** offered.

116.s:
Consider the following statements regarding commerce in Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation:
1. The high cost of doing business arose from the absence of mature power grids, logistics parks and ready factories.
2. Trade had to be re-routed away from Hyderabad-centred supply chains.
3. The investment chill after 2014 was caused mainly by the State's lack of a coastline.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statement 1 is correct: no mature power grids, logistics parks or ready factories raised costs. Statement 2 is correct: trade was re-routed away from Hyderabad-centred supply chains. Statement 3 is wrong: the investment chill came from capital uncertainty, no ready administrative set-up and agitations; AP has a long coastline (974 km old, 1,053 km remeasured) that is its offsetting advantage. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
116.tq: The coastline is AP's strength (port-led EXIM), never its handicap.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: no mature **power grids, logistics parks or ready factories** → **high cost of doing business**.
Statement 2 correct: trade was **re-routed away from Hyderabad-centred supply chains**.
Statement 3 wrong: the chill came from **capital uncertainty, no administrative set-up, agitations**; the coastline is an **advantage**.
xa: Coastline: **974 km** (old), **1,053 km** (remeasured) → **port-led, EXIM** strategy.
The **2026** Amendment Act (Amaravati sole capital) ends the **2019-24** three-capitals uncertainty.

116.s: Which statement regarding the coastline of Andhra Pradesh and its commercial strategy is correct?
o: The coastline was used only for tourism and not for export-import activity
The coastline was reported as 974 km in the older figure and 1,053 km after remeasurement, supporting a port-led EXIM strategy
The remeasured coastline was shorter than the old figure and ports were transferred to Telangana
The State had no significant coastline and therefore adopted an inland-only strategy
116.x: The older coastline figure was 974 km and the remeasured figure was 1,053 km. The coastline and the State's ports supported a port-led export-import strategy.
116.tq: Compare old and remeasured figures while linking them to the stated policy advantage.
xs: Coastline: **974 km** (old) and **1,053 km** (remeasured), supporting a **port-led EXIM strategy** — option **(2)**.
The coastline plus **all the State's ports** is AP's **offsetting advantage** after bifurcation.
Ports stayed with AP; the remeasured figure is longer, not shorter.
xa: AP lost **HITEC City** and **Genome Valley** to Telangana.
2025-26 GVA: industry **24%**, manufacturing **10.84%**.

116.s:
Consider the following statements about Section 94 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. Section 94(1) provides fiscal measures, including tax incentives, for industrialisation and growth.
2. The backward-area programmes under Section 94(2) cover nine districts of residual AP.
3. New units in the notified districts get additional depreciation and an investment allowance of 15% each.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sec 94(1) covers fiscal measures including tax incentives. Statement 2 is wrong: the backward-area programmes cover SEVEN districts (4 Rayalaseema + 3 North Coastal). Statement 3 is correct: new units there get additional depreciation and investment allowance of 15% each. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
116.tq: 94(1) tax incentives; 94(2) backward areas (7 districts); 94(3) capital.

116.s: Which form of assistance was offered by the Centre in place of Special Category Status to Andhra Pradesh?
o: A Special Assistance Measure of ₹2,500 crore
A separate Finance Commission grant of ₹15,000 crore
A Special Assistance Measure of ₹24,350 crore
A permanent exemption from all central taxes
116.x: Special Category Status was refused with reference to the 14th Finance Commission, and the Centre offered a Special Assistance Measure of ₹24,350 crore instead.
116.tq: Use the substitute-policy and amount together to distinguish the central response.
xs: The Centre offered a **Special Assistance Measure of ₹24,350 crore** — option **(3)**.
**Special Category Status** was refused citing the **14th Finance Commission**.
xa: Criticism: **Section 94** incentives and backward-area grants **fell short**, along with **SCS denial**.
Section 94 tax benefits: **15%** additional depreciation and investment allowance.

116.s: Which of the following places and industrial developments are associated with the rebuilding of Rayalaseema as an industrial hub?
o: JSW, Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, Royal Enfield near Tirupati and the Pharma City
Kia, JSW, Hindustan Aeronautics near Tirupati and the Space City
Kia, JSW, Royal Enfield near Tirupati and the Space City
Kia, Cochin Shipyard, Royal Enfield near Vijayawada and the Space City
116.x: The industrial-hub development in Rayalaseema is associated with Kia, JSW, Royal Enfield near Tirupati and the Space City.
116.tq: Match the regional-development claim with the complete set of projects and location details.
xs: Rayalaseema's industrial hub: **Kia, JSW, Royal Enfield near Tirupati and the Space City** — option **(3)**.
Royal Enfield is near **Tirupati**, not Vijayawada; the other names (Steel Plant, HAL, Cochin Shipyard) are not in this list.
xa: **Six BHAVYA parks** proposed (Aug 2026).
**SIPB** cleared **87 proposals** worth **₹34,000 crore** (Jun 2026).

116.s: Which of the following correctly describes the criticism concerning Andhra Pradesh's post-bifurcation economic support?
o: Only the backward-area grants were disputed; Section 94 incentives and SCS were accepted without controversy.
Section 94 incentives and backward-area grants exceeded the demands made by the State, while SCS was granted.
The criticism concerned BRAP rankings rather than incentives, grants or SCS.
Section 94 incentives and backward-area grants fell short of what was sought, along with the denial of SCS.
116.x: The criticism was that Section 94 incentives and backward-area grants fell short of what was asked, and that Special Category Status was denied.
116.tq: Find the option that preserves both elements of the controversy instead of reversing or omitting one.
xs: Criticism: **Section 94 incentives** and **backward-area grants fell short**, along with **SCS denial** — option **(4)**.
SCS was refused citing the **14th Finance Commission**; a **Special Assistance Measure** (**₹24,350 crore**) was offered.
xa: Tax benefits verdict: "some basic concessions ... **fell short**".
Backward-area funds for **7** districts: disbursement **stalled**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the December 2025 capacity figure of Andhra Pradesh:
1. It represents installed/contracted capacity.
2. Its value is 21,297.03 MW.
3. The figure is directly comparable on the same basis with the November 2024 total of 27,392 MW.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: The December 2025 figure is 21,297.03 MW and is based on installed/contracted capacity. It is not on the same basis as the November 2024 total, so statement 3 is false.
117.tq: Separate figures by both their date and measurement basis rather than comparing them mechanically.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: Dec 2025 **installed/contracted capacity** = **21,297.03 MW** (SES 2025-26).
Statement 3 wrong: it is on a **different basis** from the Nov 2024 total of **27,392 MW**.
xa: **267.37 MW** of expired contracts were deleted.
**APGENCO + APPDCL**: **8,789.03 MW** = **46.37%** of the AP grid.

117.s: Which one of the following sources does NOT form part of the installed power capacity mix of Andhra Pradesh?
117.x: Andhra Pradesh has no nuclear component in its installed capacity. Its capacity mix includes thermal, hydel, gas and renewable sources.
117.tq: Find the excluded source by identifying the one that does not belong to the stated mix.
xs: AP has **no nuclear power** in its installed capacity — option **(4)** (APPSC 2023).
Its mix is **thermal, hydel, gas and renewables**.
xa: **Kovvada, Srikakulam** is only **proposed**; no operating plant.
Dec 2025: APGENCO thermal **4,210 MW**, APPDCL thermal **2,400 MW**, APGENCO hydel **1,773.60 MW**.

117.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding agricultural and aqua power supply in Andhra Pradesh?
1. 22.36 lakh farm pump sets receive nine hours of free daytime power.
2. Aqua power is supplied at ₹1.50 per unit.
3. Free daytime power is limited to nuclear-powered pump sets.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
117.x: There are 22.36 lakh farm pump sets receiving nine hours of free daytime power, and aqua power is priced at ₹1.50 per unit. Statement 3 is false.
117.tq: Reject the extreme and unrelated qualification in the third statement while retaining the two stated policy facts.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **22.36 lakh** farm pump sets get **9 hours of free daytime power**.
Statement 2 correct: **aqua power** at **₹1.50/unit** (Aug 2026).
Statement 3 wrong: AP has **no nuclear** capacity at all.
xa: Peak demand: **15,016 MW** (**21 May 2026**); transmission losses **2.6%**.
State demand: **59,166.70 MU** (Apr-Dec 2025).

117.s: Which renewable-energy source has the largest installed capacity in Andhra Pradesh according to the APSES 2025–26 figures?
117.x: Solar is the largest renewable-energy source in Andhra Pradesh, with an installed capacity of 5,614.52 MW.
117.tq: Compare the source-wise table and identify the maximum value.
xs: **Solar** is AP's largest RE source — option **(3)**, with **5,614.52 MW** (Dec 2025).
**Wind** is next at **4,397.67 MW**; small hydro (**106.80**) and bagasse co-gen (**206.95 MW**) are far smaller.
xa: State RE total: **10,639.75 MW**.
Bagasse, biomass, small hydro and waste together: **627.56 MW**.
**Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park** is AP's solar landmark.

117.s: As per the PYQ answer key, the installed power capacity of Andhra Pradesh as of March 2022 was:
117.x: The PYQ key gives 25,726.89 MW (about 25.7 GW) as of March 2022. 27,392 MW is the 30 Nov 2024 figure, 21,297.03 MW is the Dec 2025 installed/contracted figure on a different basis, and 33,240 MW is AP's pumped-storage potential.
117.tq: Match figure to year: Mar 2022 = 25,726.89 MW.
xs: **27,392 MW** = **30 Nov 2024**; **21,297.03 MW** = Dec 2025 installed/contracted; **33,240 MW** = **PSP potential**.
xa: ⚠ Match the figure to the question's year and basis.
Peak demand **15,016 MW** (21 May 2026); **15,680 MW** expansion programme.

117.s: Which one of the following is associated with solar power generation in Andhra Pradesh?
117.x: The Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park is identified with solar power generation in Andhra Pradesh.
117.tq: Separate the solar project from the pumped-storage projects listed separately.
xs: **Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park** is AP's solar landmark — option **(3)**.
**Gadikota** (**1,200 MW**) and **Upper Sileru** (**1,350 MW**) are **pumped storage projects**; Kamalapadu is also a PSP (**950 MW**).
xa: **Tata Power hybrid**: **800 MW** — Pathikonda solar + Kanekallu wind.
Solar is AP's largest RE source: **5,614.52 MW**.

117.s: Andhra Pradesh's identified pumped storage potential is approximately:
117.x: AP's pumped-storage potential is 29 sites totalling 33,240 MW, of which APGENCO has six approved PSPs (1,320 + 1,200 + 1,000 + 950 + 800 + 750 = about 6,020 MW). 15,680 MW is the generation expansion programme and 160 GW is the clean-energy policy target.
117.tq: PSP potential: 29 sites, 33,240 MW.
xs: AP's PSP potential: **29 sites, 33,240 MW** — option **(3)**.
APGENCO has **six** approved PSPs; **15,680 MW** is the generation expansion programme; **160 GW** is the clean-energy target.
xa: Approved PSPs: **Aravetipalli 1,320**, **Gadikota 1,200**, **Yaganti 1,000**, **Kamalapadu 950**, **Rajupalem 800**, **Deenepalli 750**.
**APGENCO-NHPC JV** (Sep 2024): five PSPs incl. **Upper Sileru 1,350 MW**.

117.s: The Upper Sileru Pumped Storage Project of 1,350 MW is being taken up by:
117.x: The APGENCO-NHPC JV (Sep 2024) covers five PSPs including Upper Sileru PSP of 1,350 MW. Tata Power is behind the Pathikonda-Kanekallu hybrid project, APGIC is an oil and gas company, and NTPC Green is not mentioned.
117.tq: Upper Sileru PSP: APGENCO-NHPC.
xs: **Upper Sileru PSP (1,350 MW)** is under the **APGENCO-NHPC joint venture** — option **(2)** (Sep 2024).
The JV covers **five PSPs**.
**Tata Power** runs the Pathikonda-Kanekallu hybrid; **APGIC** (APIIC + APGENCO) is in **KG** exploration.
xa: ⚠ Upper Sileru **1,350** vs largest APGENCO approved PSP **Aravetipalli 1,320**.
PSP potential: **29** sites, **33,240 MW**.

117.s: What is the correct expansion of APEPDCL?
o: Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited
Andhra Pradesh Energy Power Development Company Limited
Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Corporation Limited
Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Development Corporation Limited
117.x: APEPDCL stands for Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited.
117.tq: Test the exact official expansion and distinguish Company from Corporation.
xs: APEPDCL = **AP Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited** — option **(1)**.
"**Corporation**" is used in the PYQ key for **APCPDCL**, not APEPDCL.
xa: APSPDCL = AP **Southern** Power Distribution **Company** Ltd (Tirupati).
⚠ PYQ key says "Corporation" for APCPDCL; some notes say "Company".

117.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its old-district jurisdiction?
o: APSPDCL — Nellore, Chittoor, Kadapa, Anantapur and Kurnool
117.x: Krishna, Guntur and Prakasam were associated with APCPDCL. APEPDCL covered Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and the two Godavari districts.
117.tq: Find the region wrongly transferred from one DISCOM to another.
xs: **APEPDCL — Krishna, Guntur and Prakasam** is wrong — option **(3)**; those are **APCPDCL**.
**APEPDCL** covers **Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, East and West Godavari**.
**APSPDCL** covers **Nellore, Chittoor, Kadapa, Anantapur, Kurnool**.
xa: **APRA 2014** moved **Anantapur and Kurnool** from APCPDCL to **APSPDCL**.
The new APCPDCL was carved out of APSPDCL in **2020**.

117.s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the four DISCOMs formed in the 2000 unbundling arrangement?
117.x: The 2000 arrangement consisted of EPDCL-Visakhapatnam, CPDCL-Hyderabad, NPDCL-Warangal and SPDCL-Tirupati. The Vijayawada-based APCPDCL was formed later.
117.tq: Identify the later entity among the original four DISCOM arrangements.
xs: **APCPDCL at Vijayawada** was not a 2000 DISCOM — option **(2)**; it was carved out of APSPDCL in **2020**.
The **2000** unbundling gave **EPDCL-Visakhapatnam, CPDCL-Hyderabad, NPDCL-Warangal, SPDCL-Tirupati**.
xa: Unbundling split **generation, transmission, distribution**.
**RDSS (2021)** replaced **UDAY (2015)**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh DISCOMs:
1. The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 moved Anantapur and Kurnool from APCPDCL to APSPDCL.
2. The present Vijayawada-based APCPDCL was carved out of APSPDCL in 2020.
3. Before 2014, APCPDCL was headquartered at Vijayawada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: APRA 2014 shifted Anantapur and Kurnool from APCPDCL to APSPDCL. Statement 2 is correct: the new Vijayawada-based APCPDCL was carved out of APSPDCL in 2020. Statement 3 is wrong: the pre-2014 APCPDCL was headquartered at Hyderabad. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
117.tq: Two APCPDCLs: old one at Hyderabad (2000 unbundling), new one at Vijayawada (2020).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **APRA 2014** moved **Anantapur and Kurnool** from APCPDCL to **APSPDCL**.
Statement 2 correct: **Vijayawada-based APCPDCL** was carved out of APSPDCL in **2020**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **pre-2014 APCPDCL HQ was Hyderabad**.
xa: APCPDCL now covers **Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam**.
The four DISCOMs date from the **2000** unbundling.

117.s: Which scheme replaced UDAY in the distribution-sector reform framework described for Andhra Pradesh?
117.x: The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), introduced in 2021, replaced UDAY, which was introduced in 2015.
117.tq: Discriminate between the two schemes by pairing each with its correct year and sequence.
xs: **RDSS (2021)** replaced **UDAY (2015)** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) gives the year of UDAY to RDSS.
xa: Loss reduction via **smart meters** and **feeder segregation** (**312 of 3,015** feeders done).
**APEPDCL + APSPDCL** among India's top performers on loss reduction (Jan 2026).

117.s: Which statement best reflects the nomenclature issue concerning APCPDCL?
o: APCPDCL stands for Andhra Pradesh Coastal Power Development Corporation Limited.
The abbreviation officially expands only as Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Company Limited in all references.
The abbreviation is given as Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation Limited, although some references use 'Company'.
APCPDCL is the abbreviation for Andhra Pradesh Central Power Generation Company Limited.
117.x: The expansion is given as Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation Limited, while some references use the word 'Company'.
117.tq: Watch for the exact Company–Corporation distinction in official-name questions.
xs: APCPDCL is given as **AP Central Power Distribution Corporation Ltd**, though some references say "**Company**" — option **(3)**.
⚠ The **PYQ key** says "Corporation"; some notes say "Company".
xa: APCPDCL is **Vijayawada-based**, carved out of APSPDCL in **2020**.
APEPDCL and APSPDCL use "**Company**".

117.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated feature of the Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024?
o: Target of more than 160 GW of clean energy
117.x: The policy targets Net Zero by 2047, not by 2030. Its other stated features include over 160 GW of clean energy, ₹10 lakh crore investment and 7.5 lakh jobs.
117.tq: Reject the altered year in a policy target.
xs: "**Net Zero by 2030**" is wrong — option **(1)**; the policy targets **Net Zero by 2047**.
Its targets: **160 GW+** clean energy, **₹10 lakh crore** investment, **7.5 lakh jobs**.
xa: Launched **June 2024**; it absorbed the **2023 Green Hydrogen & Ammonia Policy**.
Approvals worth **₹2.88 lakh crore** (**3.47 lakh** jobs).

117.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023 and the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024?
o: The 2023 policy was converted into a transport-only policy.
The 2024 policy replaced it with a coal-based energy framework.
The two policies operate as unrelated policies.
The 2023 policy was folded into the 2024 policy.
117.x: The AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023, was absorbed or folded into the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024.
117.tq: Test the relationship between two similarly named policies.
xs: The **2023 Green Hydrogen & Green Ammonia Policy** was **folded into the 2024 policy** — option **(4)**.
The **Integrated Clean Energy Policy** was launched in **June 2024**.
xa: Targets: **160 GW+**, **₹10 lakh crore**, **7.5 lakh jobs**, **Net Zero by 2047**.
The 2023 policy was asked in **2024** (no official key published).

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding green hydrogen:
1. Andhra Pradesh's Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration was made at Amaravati on 19 July 2025.
2. The Declaration aims to make Andhra Pradesh the "Green Hydrogen Capital".
3. Paradip, Kandla and Tuticorin, the National Green Hydrogen Mission hubs, are all in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Declaration was made at Amaravati on 19 July 2025. Statement 2 is correct: its aim is to make AP the Green Hydrogen Capital. Statement 3 is wrong: Paradip (Odisha), Kandla (Gujarat) and Tuticorin (Tamil Nadu) are NGHM hubs outside AP. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
117.tq: Know the national hubs are in other coastal States; AP's claim is via its own Declaration.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration** was made at **Amaravati** on **19 July 2025**.
Statement 2 correct: aim — make AP the "**Green Hydrogen Capital**".
Statement 3 wrong: **Paradip, Kandla, Tuticorin** are NGHM hubs, none in AP.
xa: Nodal agency: **SRM University**.

117.s: Which of the following best describes the Kakinada–Konaseema region in relation to Andhra Pradesh?
o: The principal cotton-textile cluster of Andhra Pradesh
The oil and gas hub of Andhra Pradesh
The state's major automobile manufacturing corridor
The principal iron-ore belt of Andhra Pradesh
117.x: The Kakinada–Konaseema region constitutes Andhra Pradesh's oil and gas hub and is associated with the KG basin.
117.tq: Use the direct location-to-sector association.
xs: **Kakinada-Konaseema** (KG basin) is the **oil and gas hub of Andhra Pradesh** — option **(2)**.
**APGIC** is a partner in a **KG exploration** consortium.
xa: APGIC (**2 Sep 2009**): **APIIC 51% + APGENCO 49%**.
The **Rayalaseema** industrial hub has **Kia, JSW, Royal Enfield**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about APGIC:
1. APIIC holds 51% and APGENCO 49% of its equity.
2. It was set up in 2019.
3. It is a partner in a KG basin exploration consortium.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: APGIC is APIIC 51% + APGENCO 49%. Statement 2 is wrong: APGIC was set up on 2 September 2009. Statement 3 is correct: it is a partner in a KG exploration consortium. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
117.tq: APGIC = APIIC 51 + APGENCO 49 (2009), KG basin.

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding South Coast Railway (SCoR):
1. It is India's 18th railway zone, headquartered at Visakhapatnam.
2. Its divisions are Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam.
3. It became operational on 1 August 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: SCoR is the 18th zone with HQ at Visakhapatnam. Statement 2 is correct: its divisions are Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam. Statement 3 is wrong: SCoR became operational on 1 June 2026; 1 August 2026 is when Bhogapuram airport opened. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
117.tq: 1 June 2026 = SCoR; 1 August 2026 = Bhogapuram airport.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **SCoR** is India's **18th zone**, HQ **Visakhapatnam**.
Statement 2 correct: divisions **Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam**.
Statement 3 wrong: SCoR began **1 June 2026**; **1 Aug 2026** is when **Bhogapuram airport** opened.
xa: Promised in APRA 2014's **13th Schedule**; carved from **SCR + ECoR**.
AP Industrial Policy 2024-29 prioritises **East Coast DFC** links; **Ballari-Guntakal** multi-tracking cleared (Jul 2026).

117.s:
Consider the following statements about South Coast Railway:
1. Its creation was promised in the A.P. Reorganisation Act, 2014.
2. The promise appears in the Thirteenth Schedule of the Act.
3. It was carved out of the South Central Railway and East Coast Railway.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: All three statements are correct. South Coast Railway was promised in the Thirteenth Schedule of the A.P. Reorganisation Act, 2014, and was carved from SCR and ECoR.
117.tq: Combine a legal provision with the organisational origin of a new body.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**SCoR** was promised in the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014**, in its **13th Schedule**.
It was carved from **SCR + ECoR**.
xa: India's **18th zone**; HQ **Visakhapatnam**; operational **1 June 2026**.
APRA 2014 also asked GoI to examine a **Duggirajupatnam major port** and airport upgrades.

117.s: The Andhra Pradesh Industrial Policy 2024–29 gives priority to industrial links with:
o: Western DFC and Eastern DFC only
East Coast DFC and North–South DFC
117.x: The policy gives priority to links with the East Coast Dedicated Freight Corridor and the North–South Dedicated Freight Corridor.
117.tq: Identify the exact pair of freight corridors named in the policy.
xs: AP Industrial Policy **2024-29** prioritises **East Coast DFC + North-South DFC** links — option **(2)**.
**Bharatmala** relates to the **Raipur-Visakhapatnam** expressway, not the DFC priority.
xa: **Ballari-Guntakal** multi-tracking cleared (Jul 2026).
**VCIC** is part of **ECEC**, ADB-funded.

117.s: The Raipur–Visakhapatnam greenfield expressway is associated with which programme?
117.x: The Raipur–Visakhapatnam greenfield expressway is described as a Bharatmala economic corridor.
117.tq: Identify the responsible national infrastructure programme.
xs: The **Raipur-Visakhapatnam greenfield expressway** is a **Bharatmala** economic corridor — option **(4)**.
**East Coast DFC** is a rail freight corridor, and the **Maritime Policy** concerns ports.
xa: AP's NH network: **8,744 km**; **93** projects (**2,065 km**, **₹45,633 crore**) under way.
⚠ Do not confuse: **Bharatmala** = expressway corridor; the Industrial Policy rail priority is **East Coast DFC** + **North-South DFC**.

117.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with an industrial-corridor node in Andhra Pradesh?
117.x: Krishnapatnam is a node on CBIC. Orvakal and Kopparthy are nodes on the Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.
117.tq: Start from the sure location–corridor pair and reject swapped corridor associations.
xs: **Krishnapatnam — CBIC** — option **(1)**.
**Orvakal** is a node of **HBIC** (Hyderabad-Bengaluru), not VCIC; Krishnapatnam is on CBIC, not HBIC.
xa: **VCIC** is part of **ECEC**, **ADB-funded**.
Industrial Policy 2024-29 prioritises **East Coast DFC** + **North-South DFC**.

117.s: The Andhra Pradesh Maritime Policy 2024–29 aims to make Andhra Pradesh:
117.x: The Andhra Pradesh Maritime Policy 2024–29 aims to make Andhra Pradesh India's leading maritime gateway.
117.tq: Identify the stated objective of a policy from its precise wording.
xs: The **AP Maritime Policy 2024-29** aims to make AP **India's leading maritime gateway** — option **(1)**.
Its SPV is **NSHIP-AP Ltd**, formed in **2026**.
xa: Phase-I: **+145 MTPA by 2030**; Phase-II: **300 MTPA by 2047**.
**APMB** is the nodal agency for **non-major ports**.

117.s:
Consider the following targets of the AP Maritime Policy 2024-29:
1. At least one port in the world's top 20.
2. A 20% share of all-India port cargo by 2047.
3. Training of 50,000 professionals by 2028.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the policy targets at least one port in the world's top 20 and 20% of all-India port cargo by 2047. Statement 3 is wrong: the skills target is 5,000 professionals by 2028, not 50,000. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
117.tq: Top 20 port; 20% cargo; 25% shipbuilding; 5,000 trained.

117.s: The nodal body for non-major ports in Andhra Pradesh is the:
117.x: The Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board is the nodal body for non-major ports in the State.
117.tq: Identify the authority responsible for the specific port category.
xs: The **AP Maritime Board (APMB)** is the nodal agency for **non-major ports** — option **(4)**.
**APIDC** (1960) is for industrial financing.
xa: APMB is the SLPE with the **highest net worth** (**₹12,600.65 crore**).
Maritime Policy aim: AP as **India's leading maritime gateway**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. APIDC was set up in 1960 for industrial financing and promotion.
2. APIIC was incorporated on 26 September 1973.
3. APIIC was set up as a joint venture of the State and Central Governments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: APIDC (1960) handles industrial financing and promotion. Statement 2 is correct: APIIC was incorporated on 26 September 1973. Statement 3 is wrong: APIIC is wholly State-owned. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
117.tq: APIDC 1960 = finance/promotion; APIIC 1973 = infrastructure, wholly State-owned.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **APIDC** (**1960**) — industrial **financing and promotion**.
Statement 2 correct: **APIIC** was set up on **26 September 1973**.
Statement 3 wrong: APIIC is **wholly state-owned**, not a State-Centre JV.
xa: ⚠ **APIDC 1960** (financing) vs **APIIC 1973** (infrastructure).
APIIC has **25 JVs** (SES 2025-26).

117.s:
Consider the following statements about APIIC:
1. It is wholly State-owned.
2. It is associated with industrial parks, estates, SEZs, EMCs and a land bank.
3. It performs industrial financing and promotion as its principal role instead of APIDC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Industrial financing and promotion are associated with APIDC, whereas APIIC focuses on industrial infrastructure and land development.
117.tq: Separate the roles of two similarly named industrial corporations.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **APIIC** is **wholly state-owned**.
Statement 2 correct: it handles **parks, estates, SEZs, EMCs, land bank**.
Statement 3 wrong: **financing and promotion** is **APIDC**'s role (1960).
xa: APIIC footprint: **331 parks + 304 estates + 331 UDLs = 635 clusters**.
Land bank: **41,998 acres**; ~**1.21 lakh acres** developed.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about APIIC:
1. After 1991, its role changed from manufacturer to facilitator.
2. It can allot up to 50 acres without Cabinet approval.
3. It is the nodal agency for the Centre's Sagarmala ports.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: after 1991 APIIC moved from manufacturer to facilitator. Statement 2 is correct: it can allot up to 50 acres without Cabinet approval. Statement 3 is wrong: APIIC is the nodal agency for the Centre's BHAVYA parks, not Sagarmala ports. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
117.tq: APIIC = facilitator, 50-acre power, BHAVYA nodal.

117.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bhogapuram airport — Became operational on 1 August 2026
SCoR zone — Became operational on 1 August 2026
Bhogapuram airport — Became operational on 1 June 2026
SCoR zone — Became operational on 1 September 2026
117.x: Bhogapuram airport became operational on 1 August 2026. The SCoR zone became operational on 1 June 2026.
117.tq: Start from the sure date and eliminate the swapped-date pairs.
xs: **Bhogapuram airport — operational 1 August 2026** — option **(1)**.
**SCoR** became operational on **1 June 2026** — options (2), (3), (4) mismatch the dates.
xa: APRA 2014 asked GoI to examine **Vizag/Vijayawada/Tirupati airport** upgrades.
Port limits cut under the **Indian Ports Act, 2025**.

117.s:
Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Government of India was to examine which of the following proposals?
1. Upgradation of the Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati airports
2. Creation of a new railway zone
3. Establishment of a major port at Duggirajupatnam
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: The Act provided for examination of upgrades to the Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati airports, a new railway zone and a major port at Duggirajupatnam.
117.tq: Treat the listed infrastructure commitments as a single statutory package.
xs: All three were to be examined by GoI under **APRA 2014** — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Vizag/Vijayawada/Tirupati airport upgrades**, a **new railway zone**, and a **Duggirajupatnam major port**.
xa: The railway zone became **SCoR** — India's **18th zone**, HQ **Visakhapatnam**, promised in the **13th Schedule**.
**Bhogapuram airport** became operational on **1 Aug 2026**.

117.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Industrial Corridor
(b) Economic Corridor
(c) Dedicated Freight Corridor
(d) NIMZ

List-II
(i) Large developed areas with an ecosystem for world-class manufacturing
(ii) Dedicated railway freight transportation infrastructure
(iii) Industrial development along with connectivity
(iv) Connectivity facilitating movement of goods, services and economic activity
117.x: An industrial corridor combines industry with connectivity, an economic corridor moves goods and services, a dedicated freight corridor is rail freight, and an NIMZ is a large manufacturing area. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
117.tq: Match each corridor to its meaning.
n: An industrial corridor combines industrial development with connectivity. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]
A National Investment and Manufacturing Zone (NIMZ) is a large developed area with an ecosystem for world-class manufacturing. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]
An economic corridor provides connectivity that facilitates the movement of goods, services, and economic activity. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]
A Dedicated Freight Corridor is dedicated railway freight transportation infrastructure. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]

National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs) are envisaged as large areas of developed land with the required ecosystem for world-class manufacturing. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]

118.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Tourism Policy:
1. The current policy covers the period 2024-29.
2. It is aligned with the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: the current policy is the AP Tourism Policy 2024-29. Statement 2 is wrong: the policy is aligned with Swarna Andhra @2047, not Viksit Bharat @2047. So the answer is 1 only (A); B and C wrongly accept statement 2, and D wrongly rejects statement 1.
118.tq: State policy = State vision: AP Tourism Policy 2024-29 goes with Swarna Andhra @2047.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the current policy is the **AP Tourism Policy 2024-29**.
Statement 2 wrong: it is aligned with **Swarna Andhra @2047**, not Viksit Bharat.
xa: Tourism + hospitality get **industry status across all segments**.
Targets: tourism > **20%** of state GVA and **20%** of the workforce.
**Swarna Andhra Tourism Vision 2047** was unveiled at the **FAITH** conclave.

118.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Tourism Policy 2024–29:
1. Tourism and hospitality have been accorded industry status across all segments.
2. Tailor-made packages are provided for Mega and Ultra Mega projects.
3. The policy provides only non-fiscal incentives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The policy provides fiscal, recurring and special incentives in addition to non-fiscal incentives, so statement 3 is false.
118.tq: Find the false exclusivity in statement 3 and retain the two supported policy features.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **industry status** for tourism + hospitality **across all segments**.
Statement 2 correct: **tailor-made packages** for **Mega/Ultra Mega** projects.
Statement 3 wrong: incentives are **fiscal, recurring and special**, besides non-fiscal support.
xa: Single desk: **13** pre-establishment + **11** pre-operation clearances.
**Investment Facilitation Cell at Vijayawada**.

118.s:
Consider the following targets of the Andhra Pradesh Tourism Policy 2024-29:
1. Tourism to contribute more than 20% of the State GVA.
2. Tourism to account for more than 20% of the workforce.
3. Andhra Pradesh to be among India's top five tourist destinations.
Which of the above are correct?
118.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the policy targets tourism above 20% of State GVA and 20% of the workforce. Statement 3 is wrong: the target is to place AP among India's top three destinations, not top five. So A is right; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
118.tq: Remember 20-20-3: 20% GVA, 20% workforce, top three.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: tourism > **20% of state GVA** and **20% of the workforce**.
Statement 3 wrong: target is AP among India's **top three** destinations, not top five.
xa: "**Best Tourism Promotion State**" at **GTM 2026**.

118.s: Budget hotels were promoted in Andhra Pradesh mainly with which objective?
o: To restrict private investment in tourism
To provide accommodation exclusively to government employees
118.x: Budget hotels were promoted mainly to attract tourists by expanding affordable accommodation facilities.
118.tq: Identify the practical tourism objective rather than an absolute or exclusionary claim.
xs: **Budget hotels** were promoted mainly **to attract tourists** — option **(1)** (APPSC G2 **2008** key).

The notes give no role to restricting private investment, replacing **luxury hotels** or reserving rooms for government staff; the policy instead courts private players with a **single desk** and an **Investment Facilitation Cell at Vijayawada**.
xa: **APTDC** runs **39 hotels** (**843** rooms).
Private hotels: **Oberoi** at Peruru (Tirupati), Gandikota, Annavaram; **Hyatt** at Tirupati.
**IITTM Nellore** trains hospitality staff.

118.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh won the ‘Best Tourism Promotion State’ award at GTM 2026.
2. A draft MICE policy was proposed for Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada.
3. Swarna Andhra Tourism Vision 2047 was unveiled at the FAITH conclave.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh received the GTM 2026 award, a draft MICE policy was proposed for Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada, and the tourism vision was unveiled at the FAITH conclave.
118.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when all three current tourism developments are supported.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: AP won "**Best Tourism Promotion State**" at **GTM 2026**.
Statement 2: a draft **MICE** policy for **Vizag and Vijayawada**.
Statement 3: **Swarna Andhra Tourism Vision 2047** unveiled at the **FAITH** conclave.
xa: Current policy: **AP Tourism Policy 2024-29**.
Tourism arrivals: **36.42 crore** (2025-26).

118.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: SASCI — Gandikota Fort and Gorge — ₹25.32 crore
118.x: The PRASHAD project at Annavaram temple has a cost of ₹25.32 crore. The other options incorrectly interchange schemes, projects or costs.
118.tq: Use the scheme-project-cost triple to detect swapped authorities and figures.
xs: **PRASHAD — Annavaram temple (Kakinada) — ₹25.32 crore** — option **(1)**.
**Gandikota** (SASCI) is **₹77.91 crore**; **Simhachalam** is under **PRASHAD**, not SD 2.0.
**Borra Caves** is under **Swadesh Darshan 2.0**, not CBDD.
xa: SASCI: **Havelock Bridge** + Pushkar ghat, Rajahmundry — **₹94.44 crore**.
CBDD: **Ahobilam** and **Nagarjunasagar** — **₹25 crore** each.

118.s: CBDD projects under Swadesh Darshan 2.0 in Andhra Pradesh include which of the following?
118.x: The CBDD projects are Ahobilam, described as spiritual, and Nagarjunasagar, described as heritage and adventure. Each has a cost of ₹25 crore.
118.tq: Identify the correct sub-scheme project pair rather than mixing projects across schemes.
xs: CBDD (sub-scheme of **SD 2.0**) projects are **Ahobilam and Nagarjunasagar** — option **(3)**.
Ahobilam is **spiritual**; Nagarjunasagar is **heritage and adventure**; **₹25 crore** each.
**Simhachalam, Annavaram** are PRASHAD; **Gandikota** is SASCI; **Borra Caves** is SD 2.0.
xa: CBDD = **Challenge Based Destination Development**.
**Salihundam** and **Ghantasala** are **Buddhist** sites.

118.s:
Consider the following expansions used in central tourism schemes:
1. SASCI - Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment
2. CBDD - Coastal Beach Development Division
Which of the above is/are correct?
118.x: 1 is correct: SASCI = Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment. 2 is wrong: CBDD = Challenge Based Destination Development, a sub-scheme of Swadesh Darshan 2.0. Hence '1 only'.
118.tq: CBDD = Challenge Based Destination Development (Ahobilam, Nagarjunasagar).

118.s:
Consider the following statements about the national tourism schemes:
1. Swadesh Darshan develops thematic circuits.
2. PRASHAD develops pilgrimage sites.
3. Swadesh Darshan 1.0 had 76 projects sanctioned in January 2015.
4. Of those 76 projects, 75 had been completed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All four statements are correct. Swadesh Darshan focuses on thematic circuits, PRASHAD on pilgrimage sites, and Swadesh Darshan 1.0 had 76 sanctioned projects, of which 75 were completed.
118.tq: Combine scheme functions with the numerical completion record before selecting the inclusive option.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Swadesh Darshan** = **thematic circuits**; **PRASHAD** = **pilgrimage** sites.
**SD 1.0** (Jan **2015**): **76** projects sanctioned, **75** completed (**₹5,290.33 crore**).
xa: **SD 2.0**: **52** projects; **PRASHAD**: **54** projects.
AP SD 2.0 project: **Borra Caves**, Araku (**₹29.87 crore**).

118.s: Which of the following correctly states the national project position under the tourism schemes?
118.x: Swadesh Darshan 2.0 had 52 projects, while PRASHAD had 54 projects sanctioned nationally.
118.tq: Compare the two scheme totals without reversing their order.
xs: **SD 2.0 — 52 projects; PRASHAD — 54 projects** — option **(3)**.
**76** and **75** are SD 1.0's sanctioned and completed projects; option (4) swaps 52 and 54.
xa: PRASHAD national outlay: **₹1,726.74 crore**.

118.s: Which pair of Andhra Pradesh tourism projects has been taken up under SASCI (Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment)?
o: Gandikota Fort and Gorge, and Havelock Bridge with Pushkar ghat at Rajahmundry
118.x: SASCI funds Gandikota Fort and Gorge (Rs 77.91 crore) and Havelock Bridge + Pushkar ghat, Rajahmundry (Rs 94.44 crore). Borra Caves is under Swadesh Darshan 2.0 and Simhachalam/Annavaram under PRASHAD; Ahobilam and Nagarjunasagar are CBDD projects.
118.tq: SASCI: Gandikota + Havelock Bridge.
xs: SASCI funds **Gandikota Fort and Gorge** and **Havelock Bridge + Pushkar ghat, Rajahmundry** — option **(2)**.
**Borra Caves** is SD 2.0; **Simhachalam/Annavaram** are PRASHAD; **Ahobilam/Nagarjunasagar** are CBDD.
xa: Costs: Gandikota **₹77.91 crore**; Havelock Bridge **₹94.44 crore**.
**Oberoi** plans a hotel at **Gandikota**.

118.s: Andhra Pradesh is described as the birthplace of which form of Buddhism and has approximately how many Buddhist monuments?
118.x: Andhra Pradesh is described as the birthplace of Mahayana Buddhism and has approximately 40 Buddhist monuments.
118.tq: Test the paired identity and approximate number together.
xs: AP is the birthplace of **Mahayana Buddhism**, with ~**40** monuments — option **(2)**.
AP has **2 Buddhist circuits**.
xa: Buddhist sites: **Amaravati**, Ghantasala, **Thotlakonda**, **Bavikonda**, **Bojjannakonda**, **Sankaram**.
**Salihundam** is called the "**Tibet of AP**".

118.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Buddhist circuit sites identified in Andhra Pradesh?
118.x: The listed Buddhist sites include Amaravati, Thotlakonda, Bavikonda, Bojjannakonda, Sankaram, Salihundam and Ghantasala. Srisailam is not included in this Buddhist-site list.
118.tq: Find the place outside the specified Buddhist circuit list.
xs: **Srisailam** is not a Buddhist circuit site — option **(1)**; it is in the **temple circuit**.
Buddhist sites: **Amaravati**, Ghantasala, Thotlakonda, Bavikonda, **Bojjannakonda, Sankaram** (Anakapalli), **Salihundam**.
xa: Salihundam = "**Tibet of AP**".
APTDC runs **ropeways at Srisailam**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about APTDC:
1. It is the fully state-owned operational arm of tourism in Andhra Pradesh.
2. It runs Haritha hotels, boating, sound-and-light shows and ropeways at Srisailam.
3. It is the national authority administering PRASHAD.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: APTDC is the fully state-owned operational arm and runs Haritha hotels, boating, sound-and-light shows and the Srisailam ropeway. Statement 3 is wrong: PRASHAD is a central scheme of the Union Ministry of Tourism, not run by APTDC. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
118.tq: APTDC = State operator; PRASHAD/Swadesh Darshan = central schemes.

118.s: Which beach in Andhra Pradesh has received Blue Flag recognition?
118.x: Rushikonda Beach has received Blue Flag recognition.
118.tq: Test the exact location associated with an environmental tourism certification.
xs: **Rushikonda Beach** has **Blue Flag** status — option **(4)**.
**21** more beaches are proposed, **9** shortlisted.
xa: **Visakhapatnam-Bhogapuram Coastal Corridor** of **55-60 km**.
Beach-shack policy modelled on **Goa's**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about beach tourism in Andhra Pradesh:
1. AP wants Vizag Beach Road moved from CRZ-3 to CRZ-2.
2. AP's proposed beach-shack policy is modelled on Kerala's.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: AP has sought the shift of Vizag Beach Road from CRZ-3 to CRZ-2. Statement 2 is wrong: the beach-shack policy is modelled on Goa's. Hence '1 only'.
118.tq: Beach shacks = Goa model.

118.s: Which of the following is NOT listed among the examples associated with Andhra Pradesh temple tourism circuits?
118.x: The listed examples are Tirupati, Srisailam, Simhachalam, Annavaram and Kanaka Durga. Lepakshi is not included in the stated list.
118.tq: Find the location outside the specified temple-tourism examples.
xs: **Lepakshi** is not listed — option **(1)**.
The **10 temple circuits** include **Tirupati, Srisailam, Simhachalam, Annavaram, Kanaka Durga**.
xa: PRASHAD projects: **Simhachalam** (**₹54.04 crore**) and **Annavaram** (**₹25.32 crore**).
CBDD: **Ahobilam** (spiritual).

118.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. AIIMS Mangalagiri is the anchor for national tele-medicine (eSanjeevani).
2. IITTM Nellore trains hospitality staff.
3. The Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone (AMTZ) is located at Amaravati.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: AIIMS Mangalagiri anchors eSanjeevani tele-medicine and IITTM Nellore trains hospitality staff. Statement 3 is wrong: AMTZ, the medical-device hub, is at Visakhapatnam; Amaravati has the 'Eye Tourism' zone. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
118.tq: AMTZ = Vizag; Eye Tourism = Amaravati.

118.s: The approved ‘Eye Tourism’ medical zone is associated with:
118.x: An Eye Tourism medical zone was approved in Amaravati.
118.tq: Test a distinctive project-location association through direct recall.
xs: The **"Eye Tourism" medical zone** is approved at **Amaravati** — option **(2)**.
**Mangalagiri** hosts AIIMS; **Visakhapatnam** hosts AMTZ; **Nellore** hosts IITTM.
xa: Amaravati also hosts **VIT, SRM, Amrita**.
Budget **2026-27**: **five regional medical hubs**.

118.s: According to the Union Budget 2026–27, which of the following pairs of proposals is correct?
o: Five university townships for medical tourism and five regional hospitals in coastal corridors
Five regional medical hubs for medical tourism and five university townships in industrial corridors
Five greenfield ports for medical tourism and five logistics parks in industrial corridors
Five medical-device zones and five port townships in tourism corridors
118.x: The Union Budget 2026–27 proposed five regional medical hubs for medical tourism and five university townships in industrial corridors.
118.tq: Match the number, purpose and location framework of two budget proposals.
xs: Budget **2026-27**: **five regional medical hubs** for medical tourism and **five university townships** in industrial corridors — option **(2)**.
Option (1) swaps the two proposals.
xa: **AMTZ** at **Visakhapatnam** is AP's medical-device hub.
**Amaravati** hosts **VIT, SRM, Amrita**; the CM wants top world universities.

118.s:
Which of the following institutions are located in or associated with the proposed education hub at Amaravati?
1. VIT
2. SRM
3. Amrita
4. IIT Tirupati
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
118.x: VIT, SRM and Amrita are associated with Amaravati. IIT Tirupati is an education institution in Andhra Pradesh but is not listed among the institutions hosted at Amaravati.
118.tq: Separate institutions in the State from those specifically associated with the named location.
xs: **VIT, SRM and Amrita** are at Amaravati — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**IIT Tirupati** is not in the Amaravati list.
xa: The CM wants **top world universities** in Amaravati.
Budget 2026-27: **five university townships** in industrial corridors.
**SRM University** is also nodal for the **Green Hydrogen Valley**.

118.s: Which of the following best captures the significance of tourism development in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Tourism development is confined to the capital region under a spoke-only model
Tourism has been given industry status and a hub-and-spoke model is intended to promote regional balance
Tourism has been merged with port administration and has no regional planning dimension
Tourism is treated exclusively as a cultural activity without industrial status
118.x: The significance identified is that tourism has industry status and that a hub-and-spoke model can support regional balance.
118.tq: Select the option that combines both stated dimensions instead of accepting a one-sided description.
xs: Tourism has **industry status**, and a **hub-and-spoke model** aims at **regional balance** — option **(2)**.
Industry status covers tourism + hospitality **across all segments**.
xa: Non-fiscal support: **Investment Facilitation Cell at Vijayawada**.
**Mega/Ultra Mega** projects get tailor-made packages.

118.s:
Which of the following is a criticism or implementation concern associated with tourism and related projects in Andhra Pradesh?
1. Coastal Regulation Zone limits affect Vizag beach projects.
2. Swadesh Darshan works have progressed slowly.
3. PRASAD works have also faced slow progress.
4. A Chief Minister's deadline was considered necessary to accelerate the works.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
118.x: All four statements reflect the stated criticism and implementation concerns: CRZ restrictions on Vizag beach projects, slow Swadesh Darshan and PRASAD works, and the need for a Chief Minister's deadline.
118.tq: Treat policy criticism as a cluster and verify each implementation-related statement.
xs: All four are listed concerns — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**CRZ limits** hit Vizag beach projects; **slow Swadesh Darshan and PRASAD** works needed a **CM deadline** (2026).
xa: CM deadline: all works by **May 2026**; **Havelock Bridge** open by **Dec 2026**.
AP wants Vizag Beach Road moved from **CRZ-3 to CRZ-2**.

119.s:
Which of the following was a consequence of the Andhra Pradesh IT Rules (Electronic Service Delivery), 2011?
1. Digitally signed certificates received legal sanctity.
2. Electronic delivery of services was made mandatory for departments.
3. The Information Technology Act, 2000 was repealed in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: The rules gave legal sanctity to digitally signed certificates and made electronic service delivery mandatory. They did not repeal the Information Technology Act, 2000.
119.tq: Reject the extreme legal-effect statement while retaining the two stated consequences.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **AP IT Rules (Electronic Service Delivery), 2011** gave **legal sanctity to digitally signed certificates**.
Statement 2 correct: the same rules made **electronic delivery of services mandatory** for departments.
Statement 3 wrong: the **IT Act, 2000** is the **national frame** and was not repealed; it was last amended in **2008**.
xa: The **2011** rules were an **APPSC 2022** key.
⚠ Trap: IT Act **2000** → amended **2008** → AP e-Service Rules **2011**.
The **AP Cyber Security Policy** came in **2017**; the **APCSOC** at Vijayawada followed on **23 April 2018**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The parent law of the AP IT (Electronic Service Delivery) Rules is the Information Technology Act, 2000.
2. The IT Act, 2000 was last amended in 2008.
3. The custodian ministry of the IT Act, 2000 is the Ministry of Communications.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: the AP e-Service Rules are made under the IT Act, 2000. Statement 2 is correct: the Act was last amended in 2008. Statement 3 is wrong: the custodian is the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). Hence '1 and 2 only'.
119.tq: IT Act 2000 (amended 2008, MeitY); AP e-Service Rules 2011.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about MeeSeva:
1. It was launched on 4 November 2011 in undivided Andhra Pradesh as a single-window citizen service delivery portal and centre network.
2. It served as the common service delivery front-end of the National e-Governance Plan.
3. It grew out of the APSWAN network offices of the 1990s.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: MeeSeva was launched on 4 November 2011 as a single-window citizen service portal and centres. Statement 2 is correct: it is the NeGP common service delivery front-end. Statement 3 is wrong: MeeSeva grew out of the Naidu-era eSeva centres (2001); APSWAN dates from November 2010. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
119.tq: CARD 1998 -> eSeva 2001 -> MeeSeva 2011.

119.s:
Arrange the following developments in Andhra Pradesh in chronological order:
A. APSWAN was established
B. MeeSeva was launched
C. AP State FiberNet Ltd. was incorporated
D. Village and Ward Secretariats were started
119.x: The correct sequence is APSWAN in November 2010, MeeSeva in November 2011, APSFL incorporation in October 2015, and Village and Ward Secretariats in October 2019.
119.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the intermediate milestones by year.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**APSWAN**: **November 2010**; **MeeSeva**: **4 Nov 2011**.
**APSFL** incorporated **October 2015**; **Village and Ward Secretariats** started **2 Oct 2019**.
xa: APSFL was **launched** on **27 Dec 2017** — two years after incorporation.
APSWAN was upgraded to **APSDWAN**, operational **1 May 2021**.
The network **SHQ** moved from Hyderabad to **Velagapudi** in **2017**.

119.s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the principal Andhra Pradesh e-governance platforms?
A. MeeSeva
B. CARD
C. eSeva
119.x: CARD was introduced in 1998, eSeva in 2001 and MeeSeva in 2011. Therefore, the order is B, C, A.
119.tq: Arrange the platforms by their introduction years from earliest to latest.
xs: The order is **B, C, A** — option **(2)**.
**CARD** came in **1998**, **eSeva** in **2001**, **MeeSeva** in **2011**.
xa: **e-Procurement** sits between them, from **2002**.
**Village and Ward Secretariats** followed on **2 Oct 2019**.
eSeva was **India's first integrated citizen service centres**, under **N. Chandrababu Naidu**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about eSeva in Andhra Pradesh:
1. It was launched in 2001.
2. It is described as India's first integrated citizen service centres.
3. It was launched under Chief Minister Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: eSeva (2001) was India's first integrated citizen service centre network. Statement 3 is wrong: it was launched under N. Chandrababu Naidu. So A is right; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
119.tq: Chronology CARD 1998, eSeva 2001 (Naidu), MeeSeva 2011.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **eSeva** was launched in **2001**.
Statement 2 correct: it was **India's first integrated citizen service centres**.
Statement 3 wrong: eSeva was launched under CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu**.
xa: eSeva later grew into **MeeSeva** (**4 Nov 2011**).
Naidu era (**1995-2004**): **HITEC City**, eSeva, **SMART governance** model.
Another AP first: **APSFL** — India's **first State-owned ISP**.

119.s: During its first year, MeeSeva training was delivered through television in partnership with:
119.x: MeeSeva training during its first year was delivered through television in partnership with MANA TV.
119.tq: Use the partner-organisation association and avoid confusing it with later technology institutions.
xs: MeeSeva's first-year training was delivered by television with **MANA TV** — option **(4)**.
This was an **APPSC 2022** key.
xa: MeeSeva was launched on **4 Nov 2011** as the **NeGP** service front-end.
It grew out of the Naidu-era **eSeva** centres (**2001**).
**NIELIT Tirupati** (at SV University) was formally inaugurated on **2 Oct 2025**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about electronic procurement in Andhra Pradesh:
1. e-Procurement has been operating since 2002.
2. The Konugolu e-auction portal came under G.O.Ms. No. 16 dated 27 September 2018.
3. The Konugolu portal was established under the AP IT Rules of 2011.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Konugolu portal came under G.O.Ms. No. 16 of 27 September 2018, not under the AP IT Rules of 2011.
119.tq: Use the date-and-authority distinction to reject the swapped legal basis.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **e-Procurement** has run since **2002**.
Statement 2 correct: **Konugolu** e-auction portal came under **G.O.Ms. No.16** of **27 Sep 2018**.
Statement 3 wrong: Konugolu rests on that **G.O.**, not the **AP IT Rules 2011** (which concern digitally signed certificates and e-delivery).
xa: ⚠ Chronology: **CARD 1998** → **eSeva 2001** → **e-Procurement 2002** → **MeeSeva 2011**.
The **2011** rules made electronic service delivery **mandatory** for departments.

119.s: Village and ward secretariats in Andhra Pradesh were launched on:
119.x: Village and ward secretariats were launched on 2 October 2019.
119.tq: Recall the exact launch date from closely spaced national-day options.
xs: **Village and Ward Secretariats** started on **2 October 2019** — option **(2)**.
They now offer **registration** at the **Gram Sachivalaya**.
xa: ⚠ Chronology: **CARD 1998** → **eSeva 2001** → **e-Procurement 2002** → **MeeSeva 2011** → **Secretariats 2019**.
**Mana Mitra** (WhatsApp Governance) came later, on **30 January 2025**.

119.s: AP State FiberNet Ltd. is notable for being:
o: A statutory authority limited to issuing digital signatures
India’s first private ISP and only a satellite television provider
The Union government’s exclusive broadband provider
India’s first State-owned ISP and a telecom and IPTV provider
119.x: APSFL is described as India’s first State-owned Internet Service Provider and also functions as a telecom and IPTV provider.
119.tq: Select the precise institutional description rather than an overbroad or restricted one.
xs: **APSFL** is **India's first State-owned ISP** and is licensed as **ISP + telecom + IPTV** provider — option **(4)**.
It is a state company, not private, not a Union provider, not a statutory signature authority.
It is also the **first telco in the state-government sector**.
xa: Incorporated **October 2015**; launched **27 Dec 2017**.
**AP Fiber Grid Phase-I**: **24,000 km** on an **IP-MPLS ring**; NOC at **Visakhapatnam**.
Last mile via **6,300+** local cable operators; **triple play** (internet, IPTV, voice).

119.s:
Consider the following statements about AP State FiberNet Ltd (APSFL):
1. It was incorporated in October 2015.
2. It was launched on 27 December 2017.
3. The Network Operations Centre of AP Fiber Grid Phase-I is at Velagapudi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: APSFL was incorporated in October 2015 and launched on 27 December 2017. Statement 3 is wrong: the Phase-I NOC is at Visakhapatnam; Velagapudi is where the network SHQ moved from Hyderabad in 2017. So A is right; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
119.tq: Incorporated 2015, launched 2017, NOC in Vizag.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: APSFL was **incorporated in October 2015**.
Statement 2 correct: it was **launched on 27 Dec 2017**.
Statement 3 wrong: the Phase-I **NOC** is at **Visakhapatnam**; **Velagapudi** is where the **SHQ** moved from Hyderabad in **2017**.
xa: Phase-I: **24,000 km** on an **IP-MPLS ring** (not GPON).
APSFL is the state agency for **BharatNet Phase-II**: **54,502 km**, **11,254 GPs**.

119.s: Which one of the following correctly describes AP Fiber Grid Phase-I?
o: 24,000 km of fibre on a GPON ring with the NOC at Hyderabad
78,502 km of fibre on an IP-MPLS ring with the NOC at Amaravati
54,502 km of fibre on a GPON ring with the NOC at Velagapudi
24,000 km of fibre on an IP-MPLS ring with the NOC at Visakhapatnam
119.x: Phase-I comprises 24,000 km of fibre on an IP-MPLS ring, and its Network Operations Centre is at Visakhapatnam.
119.tq: Check the technology, network length and NOC location together.
xs: Phase-I is **24,000 km** on an **IP-MPLS ring** with the **NOC at Visakhapatnam** — option **(4)**.
**GPON** is wrong — the notes stress IP-MPLS, **not GPON**.
**54,502 km** is BharatNet Phase-II; **78,502 km** is the total OFC.
xa: APSFL is India's **first State-owned ISP**, licensed as ISP + telecom + IPTV.
Extra state investment in BharatNet: **₹645.30 crore**.
**22,000+** government connections run on the network.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding APSFL and BharatNet Phase-II:
1. APSFL is the state implementing agency for BharatNet Phase-II.
2. BharatNet Phase-II in the state covers 54,502 km.
3. It covers 11,254 Gram Panchayats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: APSFL is the state implementing agency, and the Phase-II rollout covers 54,502 km and 11,254 Gram Panchayats.
119.tq: Combine agency, coverage length and administrative coverage in one coded question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **APSFL** is the **state agency** for BharatNet Phase-II.
Statements 2 and 3: Phase-II covers **54,502 km** and **11,254 GPs**.
xa: The state added **₹645.30 crore** of its own investment.
Cabinet cleared the **Amended BharatNet Programme** roadmap.
⚠ Phase-I **24,000 km** + BharatNet **54,502 km** = **78,502 km** OFC.

119.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
119.x: The APSDWAN upgrade became operational on 1 May 2021, not on 2 October 2019. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
119.tq: Find the one date that belongs to another Andhra Pradesh service initiative.
xs: The wrong pair is **APSDWAN upgrade — 2 October 2019**: APSDWAN became operational on **1 May 2021** — option **(3)**.
**2 Oct 2019** is the start of **Village and Ward Secretariats**.
Correct pairs: **MeeSeva 4 Nov 2011**, **APSFL launch 27 Dec 2017**, **APSWAN Nov 2010**.
xa: Some notes say APSDWAN was **introduced 2020**.
The network **SHQ** moved from Hyderabad to **Velagapudi** in **2017**.
APSFL was **incorporated** in **October 2015**.

119.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the core data hubs of e-Pragati?
119.x: The core e-Pragati data hubs are People Hub, Land Hub, Entity Hub, GIS Hub and IoT Hub. Finance Hub is not included in the listed core hubs.
119.tq: Find the extra item in a named institutional list.
xs: **Finance Hub** is not an e-Pragati core hub — option **(4)**.
The core hubs are **People Hub, Land Hub, Entity Hub, GIS Hub** and **IoT Hub**.
xa: e-Pragati = **State Enterprise Architecture**; **14 packages / 72 projects** in **33 departments**.
Goal: **faceless, paperless, cashless** governance.
It built **APOLIS** (police automation) and the **AP State Portal**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about e-Pragati:
1. It seeks to interconnect all e-governance systems through a whole-of-government approach.
2. It integrates departments such as Revenue, Registration, Transport and Municipal services through a single window.
3. It is built on the Seva model.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All three statements are correct. e-Pragati interconnects departmental systems, provides a single-window interface for several departments and follows the Seva model.
119.tq: Test the platform’s architecture, service integration and operating model together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: e-Pragati is a **whole-of-government** platform.
Statements 2 and 3: it integrates **Revenue, Registration, Transport, Municipal** etc. in a **single window**, on the **Seva model**.
xa: Goal: **faceless, paperless, cashless** governance.
**45 more services** added **Feb 2026**.
Moved **101 departmental servers** to the **State Data Centre**.

119.s: e-Pragati, the whole-of-government digital platform of Andhra Pradesh, was launched under which Chief Minister?
119.x: e-Pragati was launched under CM N. Chandrababu Naidu during 2014-19 (APPSC 2021 key, asked twice). YSR (2004-09) and Kiran Kumar Reddy (2010-14) led undivided AP before it; Jagan Mohan Reddy's term (2019-24) came after its launch.
119.tq: e-Pragati = Naidu, 2014-19 term.
xs: e-Pragati was launched under CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu** (**2014-19**) — option **(2)**.
This was an **APPSC 2021** key, asked twice.
xa: **eSeva** (**2001**) was also launched under Naidu.
**Mana Mitra** (WhatsApp Governance) came under minister **Nara Lokesh**, **30 January 2025**.
Naidu era (**1995-2004**): **HITEC City/Cyberabad**, **SMART governance** model.

119.s: The stated governance goal of e-Pragati in Andhra Pradesh is:
o: Fully privatised delivery of citizen services
119.x: e-Pragati aims at faceless, paperless, cashless governance by integrating departments on a single window. It is a state platform, not privatisation, and it is the opposite of offline district-wise records; decentralised/cooperative governance is not its stated goal.
119.tq: Three 'less' words: faceless, paperless, cashless.
xs: e-Pragati's goal is **faceless, paperless, cashless** governance — option **(1)**.
It integrates departments in a **single window** on the **Seva model** — a state platform, not privatisation or offline records.
xa: Core hubs: **People, Land, Entity, GIS, IoT**.
**45 more services** added **Feb 2026**.
It is the State's flagship digital governance platform (**e-Pragati Authority**).

119.s:
