Consider the following statements about the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) of Andhra Pradesh:
1. It has functioned since 2017.
2. It is the nodal agency for real-time monitoring, data analytics, AI and early warning.
3. Its work is confined to monitoring information-technology exports.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: RTGS dates from 2017. Statement 2 is correct: it is the nodal agency for real-time monitoring, data analytics, AI and early warning, running the Command & Control Centre and State Data Lake. Statement 3 is wrong: it is not confined to IT exports. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
119.tq: RTGS (2017) = command centre + data lake + Mana Mitra.

119.s: Which one of the following is the best description of the State Data Lake maintained at the Andhra Pradesh State Data Centre?
o: A satellite-based flood warning system restricted to Vijayawada
A blockchain platform used exclusively for property registration
A single source of truth for more than 40 departments and about 400 applications
A portal for conducting e-auctions of government contracts
119.x: The State Data Lake serves as a single source of truth for more than 40 departments and approximately 400 applications.
119.tq: Match the precise institutional function with the correct platform.
xs: The **State Data Lake** is the **"single source of truth"** for **40+ departments** and **~400 applications** — option **(3)**.
It also covers **335+ HoDs**; it sits at the **AP State Data Centre** with **Data Lens**.
Blockchain certificates are **AP DigiVerify**; e-auctions are **Konugolu**.
xa: Use case: found **2,51,868 children** (**2.51 lakh**) missing from rice cards.
Criticism: **privacy** and **algorithmic-bias** concerns about the Data Lake.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about Mana Mitra (WhatsApp Governance) of Andhra Pradesh:
1. It was launched on 30 January 2025.
2. It was launched under minister Nara Lokesh.
3. It is the e-auction portal notified under G.O.Ms. No.16 of 27 September 2018.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Mana Mitra was launched on 30 January 2025 under minister Nara Lokesh. Statement 3 is wrong: the e-auction portal under G.O.Ms. No.16 of 2018 is Konugolu, not Mana Mitra. So A is right; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
119.tq: Mana Mitra = WhatsApp services (2025, Lokesh); Konugolu = e-auction (2018).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statements 1 and 2: **Mana Mitra** was launched on **30 January 2025** under minister **Nara Lokesh**.
Statement 3 wrong: the e-auction portal under **G.O.Ms. No.16** (**2018**) is **Konugolu**.
xa: WhatsApp number: **9552300009**.
**865 services** per SES 2025-26; **921 services** shown to **Bill Gates**; target **1,000**.
Uptake: **₹22.26 crore** revenue for **21 temples**; **2.38 lakh** Class-10 hall tickets.

119.s:
Consider the following RTGS tools and their uses:
1. AWARE 2.0 - disaster early warning
2. AI4PGRS - AI-based grievance redressal
3. AP DigiVerify - flood forecasting
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
119.x: Pair 1 is correct: AWARE 2.0 gives disaster early warning (used in cyclones Montha and Ditwa). Pair 2 is correct: AI4PGRS is grievance AI. Pair 3 is wrong: AP DigiVerify issues blockchain certificates, not flood forecasts. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
119.tq: DigiVerify = blockchain certificates.

119.s: The AP Cyber Security Operations Centre (APCSOC) was set up at which place on 23 April 2018?
119.x: The AP Cyber Security Operations Centre was set up at Vijayawada on 23 April 2018 under the framework associated with the AP Cyber Security Policy 2017.
119.tq: Match the specific cyber-security institution with its location and date.
xs: **APCSOC** was set up at **Vijayawada** on **23 April 2018** — option **(2)**.
It is the **AP Cyber Security Operations Centre**.
xa: The **AP Cyber Security Policy** dates from **2017**.
**APTS** (**1986**) is nodal for cyber security, IT procurement, digital certificates.
**IIDT** (Tirupati) trains in **AI, VLSI, cyber** skills.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about AP Technology Services Ltd (APTS):
1. It was set up in 1986.
2. It is the nodal agency for IT procurement, cyber security, digital certificates and Aadhaar.
3. It depends on budget grants and is not self-financing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: APTS dates from 1986 and is the nodal body for IT procurement, cyber security, digital certificates and Aadhaar. Statement 3 is wrong: APTS is self-financing. So A is right; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
119.tq: APTS = 1986, procurement + certificates + Aadhaar, self-financing.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **APTS** (AP Technology Services Ltd) was set up in **1986**.
Statement 2: it is nodal for **IT procurement, cyber security, digital certificates, Aadhaar**.
Statement 3 wrong: APTS is **self-financing**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **APTS 1986** and **Dr NTR University of Health Sciences 1986**.
**APEITA** implements IT/Electronics policies; **APSAC** handles remote sensing and GIS.

119.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: APEITA — Implementation of IT and Electronics policies and investment promotion
APTS — Administration of remote sensing and GIS programmes
ITE&C Department — Parent department for IT, electronics and communications
119.x: APTS is responsible for IT procurement, cybersecurity, digital certificates and Aadhaar-related services. Remote sensing and GIS are associated with APSAC, not APTS.
119.tq: Find the institution whose assigned function has been swapped with that of a neighbouring body.
xs: **APTS — remote sensing and GIS** is wrongly matched — option **(3)**.
APTS (**1986**) handles **IT procurement, cyber security, digital certificates, Aadhaar**; remote sensing and **GIS** belong to **APSAC**.
The other pairs (**APEITA**, **APIS**, **ITE&C Department**) are correct.
xa: APTS is **self-financing**.
**IIDT** (Tirupati): AI, VLSI, cyber skills.
**RTIH** (**Aug 2025**): hub at **Amaravati**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about NIC-AP solutions:
1. MEDHAS stands for Medical Education & Health Administrative System.
2. MEDHAS was built for Dr NTR University of Health Sciences, Vijayawada.
3. D-Krishi is the computerised registration system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: MEDHAS (Medical Education & Health Administrative System) was built by NIC-APSC for Dr NTR University of Health Sciences, Vijayawada. Statement 3 is wrong: D-Krishi is the e-seed system; CARD handles registration. So A is right; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
119.tq: D-Krishi = seed, CARD = registration, e-PDS = rice cards.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**MEDHAS** = **Medical Education & Health Administrative System**, built by **NIC-APSC** for **Dr NTR University of Health Sciences**.
Statement 3 wrong: **D-Krishi** is **e-seed**; registration is **CARD**.
xa: Other NIC-AP solutions: **e-PDS** (**1.44 crore** rice cards), **WaterSoft**, **APMCORS**.
Dr NTR UHS (Vijayawada, **1986**) was India's **first health university**.

119.s: The Ratan Tata Innovation Hub (RTIH), set up in Andhra Pradesh in August 2025, follows a hub-and-spoke model. Where is its hub?
119.x: RTIH (Aug 2025) has its hub at Amaravati. Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati (with Rajahmundry and Anantapuramu) are spokes, not the hub.
119.tq: RTIH: hub Amaravati, five spokes.
xs: The **RTIH** hub is at **Amaravati** — option **(3)**.
**Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Tirupati**, Rajahmundry and Ananthapuramu are the **spokes**.
xa: RTIH was set up in **Aug 2025**.
₹**22-crore** **RTIH-SIDBI Seed Fund**; up to **₹20 crore** AIF seed equity.
**APIS** programmes: SPARK, Catalyst, Velocity Labs, Innotribe.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the IT & GCC Policy 4.0 of Andhra Pradesh:
1. It provides for capital subsidies.
2. It includes tax exemptions and employment-linked incentives.
3. It focuses on IT parks, co-working spaces and neighbourhood workspaces.
4. It covers emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing and cyber technology.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All four statements describe provisions or focus areas of the IT & GCC Policy 4.0 for 2024-29.
119.tq: Use the complete-policy option when all listed incentives, workspaces and technology areas belong together.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Statements 1 and 2: **capital subsidies**, **tax exemptions**, **employment-linked + rental incentives**.
Statements 3 and 4: **IT parks**, **co-working and neighbourhood workspaces**; **AI, cloud, cybersecurity**.
xa: Workspaces are in **Tirupati, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada**.
In force **12 December 2024**; aim: **global knowledge economy hub**.
A **GCC** is a multinational's own offshore unit, not a third-party vendor.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about the AP IT & GCC Policy 4.0 (2024-29):
1. It came into force on 12 December 2024.
2. Its aim is to make Andhra Pradesh a global knowledge economy hub.
3. Its co-working and neighbourhood workspaces are planned in Kurnool, Nellore and Kadapa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: the policy came into force on 12 December 2024. Statement 2 is correct: its aim is a global knowledge economy hub. Statement 3 is wrong: the co-working and neighbourhood workspaces are in Tirupati, Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
119.tq: IT parks/workspaces triad = Tirupati, Vizag, Vijayawada.

119.s: A Global Capability Centre (GCC), in the context of Andhra Pradesh's IT policy, is best understood as:
o: A multinational company's own offshore unit
A public sector semiconductor testing laboratory
A third-party vendor supplying temporary clerical staff
119.x: A GCC is an offshore unit owned and operated by a multinational company for its own capabilities and operations, rather than a third-party vendor.
119.tq: Discriminate between a multinational's captive unit and an outsourced third-party service provider.
xs: A **GCC** (**Global Capability Centre**) is a **multinational's own offshore unit** — option **(1)**.
It is **not a third-party vendor** — that is why the policy is named for it.
xa: **LIFT Policy 4.0** (**Land Incentive for Tech Hubs**) gives land for **GCCs** and IT infrastructure developers.
**RMZ** plans a **GCC Park** at **Kapuluppada**, Visakhapatnam.
⚠ **Karnataka** also runs GCC and data-centre policies.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0:
1. It covers the period 2024-29.
2. It targets electronics production of US$50 billion.
3. It targets investment of US$25 billion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the policy runs 2024-29 and targets production of US$50 bn (about Rs 4.2 lakh crore). Statement 3 is wrong: the investment target is US$10 bn (about Rs 84,000 crore). So A is right; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
119.tq: 50 for production, 10 for investment, 5 lakh first-time jobs.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: the **Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0** runs **2024-29**.
Statement 2: production target **US$50 bn** (**₹4.2 lakh crore**).
Statement 3 wrong: the investment target is **USD 10 bn** (**₹84,000 crore**).
xa: Jobs target: **5 lakh first-time jobs**.
Approaches: **50 Centres of Excellence**; **5 lakh** workers trained.
Instruments: **EMCs, SEZs, plug-and-play parks**, capital subsidies.

119.s: Which one of the following is the correct target of the Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0 of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Creation of 10 lakh permanent government jobs
119.x: The policy targets 5 lakh first-time employment opportunities. Creation of 2 lakh first-time entrepreneurs is not its target.
119.tq: Distinguish the precise employment target from the similar-sounding entrepreneurship figure.
xs: The target is **5 lakh first-time jobs** — option **(1)**.
⚠ "**2 lakh first-time entrepreneurs**" is **not** a target (PYQ; **APPSC G2 2025**).
Training is **5 lakh** workers, not 50 lakh.
xa: Production **US$50 bn**; investment **USD 10 bn**.
**50 Centres of Excellence**.
Related: **AP Semiconductor & Display Fab Policy 4.0**.

119.s:
Under the Zone A/B incentive of the Andhra Pradesh ESDM Policy, which of the following are reimbursed at 100 per cent?
1. Stamp duty
2. Transfer duty
3. Registration fee
4. Income tax
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: The ESDM Policy 2021-24 provides 100 per cent reimbursement of stamp duty, transfer duty and registration fee in the Zone A/B incentive. Income tax is not included in this stated incentive.
119.tq: Identify the three specified fiscal charges and reject the neighbouring tax term.
xs: **Stamp duty, transfer duty, registration fee** — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
The **ESDM Policy 2021-24** Zone A/B incentive gave **100% reimbursement** of these three; income tax is not part of it.
xa: Current analogue: **Amaravati Quantum Valley** — **100% stamp-duty and registration-fee exemption**.
ESDM was followed by **Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0** (**2024-29**).

119.s:
Consider the following statements about the AP Electronics Components Manufacturing Policy, 2025:
1. It aims to develop a component ecosystem in the State.
2. Component makers get advance and matching incentives, interim support and plug-and-play facilities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 2025 policy is for a component ecosystem. Statement 2 is correct: it offers advance and matching incentives, interim support and plug-and-play facilities to component makers. Hence 'Both 1 and 2'.
119.tq: Components Policy 2025 = component ecosystem.

119.s: The first unit cleared under the ISM framework in the context of Andhra Pradesh's semiconductor initiatives was an OSAT unit proposed by:
119.x: The first ISM-framework unit cleared was an OSAT project by Advanced System in Package Technologies, with an investment of ₹2,388 crore at Tarluvada, Visakhapatnam.
119.tq: Use the company-project association to distinguish the semiconductor unit from data-centre companies.
xs: The first **ISM-framework unit** was an **OSAT** by **Advanced System in Package Technologies** — option **(2)**.
It costs **₹2,388 crore**, at **Tarluvada**, Vizag.
**RMZ** runs a hyperscale cluster; **Adani Infra** an AI data-centre cluster; **Airtel Nxtra** partners Google's data centre.
xa: **OSAT** = **Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test**.
Google's AI data centre also has its foundation at **Tarluvada** (**28 Apr 2026**).

119.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
119.x: The IT Park at Madhurawada-Rushikonda is located in Visakhapatnam.
119.tq: Start from the sure location-facility pair and reject swapped locations.
xs: **Visakhapatnam — IT Park at Madhurawada-Rushikonda** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Drone City** is at **Orvakal** (Kurnool), not Tirupati; **Kopparthy** is an EMC in **YSR Kadapa**; **IIIT Sri City** is in **Tirupati district**.
xa: **TCS** and **Cognizant** started operations there in **2025**.
**4.45 acres** at Madhurawada (Rushikonda non-SEZ) went to **Phenom People** (**₹207.5 crore**).

119.s: Which of the following cities host the new IT parks built in Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation?
119.x: The new IT parks built after bifurcation are located in Tirupati, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam.
119.tq: Select the complete three-city group without substituting nearby AP cities.
xs: Post-bifurcation IT parks are in **Tirupati, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam** — option **(4)**.
The same three cities host the **co-working** spaces of the **IT & GCC Policy 4.0**.
xa: After 2014 the IT base was rebuilt around **Visakhapatnam**.
**APIIC**: **264 industrial parks** among **571** clusters.

119.s: Which of the following special economic zones in Andhra Pradesh is an IT/ITES SEZ?
o: Both Sri City and Kakinada SEZs
119.x: Visakhapatnam SEZ is the IT/ITES SEZ (PYQ 2022). Sri City and Kakinada are multi-product SEZs, so options A, B and D are wrong.
119.tq: Trap: Sri City and Kakinada are multi-product.
xs: **Visakhapatnam SEZ** is the **IT/ITES SEZ** — option **(3)** (**PYQ 2022**).
⚠ **Sri City** and **Kakinada** are **multi-product** SEZs.
xa: Vizag IT Park at **Madhurawada-Rushikonda** has SEZ and non-SEZ parts.
Visakhapatnam is the **Global AI hub city** (**APPSC 2025** key).

119.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Tirupati (Renigunta) — Tirupati district
2. Sri City — Tirupati district, formerly Chittoor
3. Kopparthy — YSR Kadapa district
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All three pairs are correct. Tirupati (Renigunta) and Sri City are associated with Tirupati district, while Kopparthy is in YSR Kadapa district.
119.tq: Verify every location pair before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Tirupati (Renigunta)** and **Sri City** are EMCs in **Tirupati district**; **Kopparthy** is in **YSR Kadapa**.
xa: Kopparthy: **VCIC** node, **2,596 acres**, smart industrial city.
**IIIT Sri City** is at Sri City; **IIDT** and a **NIELIT** centre are in Tirupati.

119.s: Which of the following institutions is located in Tirupati along with the Tirupati (Renigunta) Electronics Manufacturing Cluster?
119.x: IIDT and a NIELIT centre are also located in Tirupati in association with the Tirupati cluster area.
119.tq: Identify the institutions geographically associated with the cluster.
xs: **IIDT** and a **NIELIT** centre are in Tirupati — option **(2)**.
**RTGS** and **Data Lens** belong to the state's real-time governance set-up, not Tirupati's cluster.
xa: IIDT trains in **AI, VLSI, cyber** skills.
**NIELIT Tirupati** is at **SV University**, inaugurated **2 Oct 2025**.

119.s: Visakhapatnam is expected to become India's third international subsea cable landing station after:
119.x: Visakhapatnam is described as India's third international subsea cable landing station, after Mumbai and Chennai.
119.tq: Use the stated ordinal position and the two preceding locations to identify the answer.
xs: Vizag is India's **3rd international subsea cable landing station**, after **Mumbai** and **Chennai** — option **(1)**.
Only **Mumbai** and **Chennai** precede Vizag; option (4) wrongly lists **Visakhapatnam** itself.
xa: Vizag also hosts the **largest Google AI hub outside the US**.
Visakhapatnam = **Global AI hub city** (**PYQ 2025**).

119.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: AI data-centre cluster — Adani Infra — 1,000 MW and 601.4 acres
Hyperscale cluster and GCC Park — RMZ — up to 1 GW
Data-centre ecosystem — APCRDA — 1 GW in Amaravati
Google AI hub — 1 GW — Tarluvada, Adavivaram and Rambilli
119.x: The APCRDA data-centre ecosystem in Amaravati has a target of 9 GW, not 1 GW. The other three project-capacity-location associations are correctly matched.
119.tq: Find the altered capacity figure in a correctly structured project-location match.
xs: The wrong pair is **APCRDA — 1 GW in Amaravati**: APCRDA's data-centre ecosystem is **9 GW** — option **(3)**.
Correct: **Adani Infra** 1,000 MW, **601.4 acres**; **RMZ** up to **1 GW**; Google AI hub **1 GW** at **Tarluvada, Adavivaram, Rambilli**.
xa: APCRDA called **global tenders** for the **9 GW** ecosystem (**Aug 2026**).
AP **Data Center Policy 4.0** targets **up to 1 GW** extra capacity.

119.s:
With reference to Andhra Pradesh's data-centre policies, consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh Data Center Policy 4.0 targets up to 1 GW of additional capacity during 2024-29.
2. Gujarat Data Centre Policy 2026-29 targets 7.5 GW.
3. Andhra Pradesh's target is higher than Gujarat's target.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Andhra Pradesh targets up to 1 GW of additional data-centre capacity, while Gujarat targets 7.5 GW. Therefore, the Andhra Pradesh target is not higher than Gujarat's.
119.tq: Check both numerical targets before accepting the reversed comparison.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
AP **Data Center Policy 4.0** (**2024-29**): **up to 1 GW**; Gujarat **2026-29**: **7.5 GW**.
Statement 3 wrong: AP's **1 GW** is lower than Gujarat's **7.5 GW**.
xa: India has **no binding data-centre sustainability policy**.
APCRDA's Amaravati data-centre ecosystem call: **9 GW**.

119.s: Which city of Andhra Pradesh is being developed as a global AI hub, with Google's AI data centre?
119.x: Visakhapatnam is the global AI hub city (PYQ 2025; APPSC 2025 key), with Google's 1 GW AI data centre at Tarluvada. Amaravati is the Quantum Valley, Kakinada the green hydrogen cluster, and Tirupati an electronics cluster.
119.tq: AI hub = Vizag; Quantum = Amaravati.
xs: **Visakhapatnam** is the **Global AI hub city** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2025** key).
**Amaravati** = Quantum Valley; **Kakinada** = Green Hydrogen.
xa: Google's **1 GW** AI hub at **Tarluvada** is the **largest outside the US**.
The Finance Minister called it "A.P.'s mother of all deals".

119.s:
Consider the following statements about Google's AI data centre in Andhra Pradesh:
1. It is an investment of about US$15 billion over five years to 2030.
2. It is run by the Google subsidiary Raiden Infotech with AdaniConneX and Airtel Nxtra.
3. Its foundation stone was laid at Kopparthy in YSR Kadapa district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: about US$15 bn (₹1.35 lakh crore), run by Raiden Infotech with AdaniConneX and Airtel Nxtra. Statement 3 is wrong: the foundation stone was laid on 28 Apr 2026 at Tarluvada, Visakhapatnam; Kopparthy is an electronics cluster. So A is right; B, C and D include statement 3.
119.tq: Google = Raiden Infotech, Tarluvada, US$15 bn.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **~US$15 bn** over five years to **2030** (**₹1.35 lakh crore**).
Statement 2: run by **Raiden Infotech** with **AdaniConneX** + **Airtel Nxtra**.
Statement 3 wrong: foundation laid **28 Apr 2026** at **Tarluvada**, Visakhapatnam; **Kopparthy** is a Kadapa EMC.
xa: ⚠ Some notes give **₹87,520 crore** (SES 2025-26 earlier figure).
Inauguration set for **28 Sep 2028**.

119.s:
Arrange the following Andhra Pradesh technology clusters according to their stated locations:
A. Data & AI City
B. Quantum Valley
C. Green Hydrogen cluster
D. Drone City
Which of the following is the correct location sequence?
119.x: Data & AI City is at Visakhapatnam, Quantum Valley at Amaravati, the Green Hydrogen cluster at Kakinada and Drone City at Orvakal in Kurnool.
119.tq: Use the location sequence to eliminate options with swapped technology clusters.
xs: **Visakhapatnam, Amaravati, Kakinada, Orvakal** — option **(1)**.
**Data & AI City** → Vizag; **Quantum Valley** → Amaravati; **Green Hydrogen** → Kakinada; **Drone City** → Orvakal (Kurnool).
xa: Drone City is India's **first dedicated drone cluster** (**600 acres**).
Quantum Valley launch set for **January 2027**.

119.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Amaravati Quantum Valley is correct?
1. It is described as India's first Quantum Valley.
2. It functions under the National Quantum Mission.
3. Its areas of work include quantum computing, QKD and post-quantum cryptography.
4. Firms located there receive 100 per cent exemption from stamp duty and registration fee.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: All four statements are correct. Amaravati Quantum Valley is linked with the National Quantum Mission, works in the specified quantum fields and has been granted full exemption from stamp duty and registration fee for eligible firms.
119.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when the identity, institutional framework, activities and incentive are all correct.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Amaravati Quantum Valley** = India's first Quantum Valley, under the **National Quantum Mission**.
Work: **quantum computing, QKD, post-quantum cryptography**; **100% stamp-duty and registration-fee exemption**.
xa: **Quantum Computing Policy**: **7 projects** approved.
Launch set for **January 2027**; **AQRF** = Amaravati Quantum Reference Facilities.

119.s: The launch of Amaravati Quantum Valley has been scheduled for:
119.x: The launch of Amaravati Quantum Valley has been scheduled for January 2027.
119.tq: Distinguish the Quantum Valley launch date from the Google data-centre inauguration date.
xs: **Amaravati Quantum Valley** launch is set for **January 2027** — option **(2)**.
**September 2028** is Google's data-centre inauguration; **April 2026** its foundation stone.
xa: Under the **National Quantum Mission**; **7 projects** approved.
Work: **QKD** and **post-quantum cryptography**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about the Amaravati Drone Summit 2024:
1. The summit was held at Mangalagiri.
2. Its record drone show was held at Orvakal Drone City.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: the summit (22-23 October 2024) was at Mangalagiri. Statement 2 is wrong: the record drone show was held at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada. Hence '1 only'.
119.tq: Summit = Mangalagiri; show = Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada.

119.s:
Consider the following targets of AP Drone Policy 4.0 (2024-29):
1. 100 drone companies.
2. 50 skilling centres.
3. 25,000 drone pilots trained.
4. 25,000 direct jobs.
Which of the above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the policy targets 100 drone companies, 50 skilling centres and 25,000 trained pilots. Statement 4 is wrong: it targets 15,000 direct jobs (and 25,000 indirect jobs). So A is right; B, C and D include the wrong statement 4.
119.tq: Jobs trap: 15,000 direct + 25,000 indirect; the 25,000 figure also matches pilots trained.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
Targets: **100 drone companies**, **50 skilling centres**, **25,000 drone pilots** trained.
Statement 4 wrong: direct jobs = **15,000**; **25,000** is indirect jobs.
xa: Also **20+** remote pilot training organisations.
⚠ Trap: **25,000 pilots** and **25,000 indirect jobs**; direct **15,000**.

119.s:
With reference to Drone City in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. It is being established at Orvakal in Kurnool.
2. It is described as India’s first dedicated drone cluster.
3. Its total area is 600 acres, with 120 acres earmarked for Phase-I.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Drone City is at Orvakal in Kurnool, is described as India’s first dedicated drone cluster, and covers 600 acres, including 120 acres in Phase-I.
119.tq: Combine location, status and area figures in a multi-statement question.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Drone City** at **Orvakal** (Kurnool) is India's **first dedicated drone cluster**; **600 acres** (Phase-1 **120 acres**).
xa: Foundation stone **Nov 2025**.
Becoming a **national hub** (**Aug 2026**): **₹130 crore** secured, up to **₹5,000 crore** expected.

119.s: Which statement correctly describes the distribution of IT activity before the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014?
o: IT exports began only after the creation of RTGS.
Hyderabad's HITEC City and Cyberabad generated the state's IT exports.
Kopparthy was the principal source of the state's IT exports before 2014.
Residual Andhra Pradesh generated all the state's IT exports before bifurcation.
119.x: Before bifurcation, Hyderabad's HITEC City and Cyberabad, developed under N. Chandrababu Naidu, generated the state's IT exports.
119.tq: Separate the pre-bifurcation Hyderabad base from the post-bifurcation residual state.
xs: Before **2014**, Hyderabad's **HITEC City/Cyberabad** generated the state's IT exports — option **(2)**.
These were built under **N. Chandrababu Naidu**.
After bifurcation residual AP "**started from zero**", so option (4) is wrong.
xa: **RTGS** only came in **2017**.
After 2014 the IT base was rebuilt around **Visakhapatnam**.

119.s: The residual Andhra Pradesh IT sector was described as having started from zero after:
o: the bifurcation of the State in 2014
119.x: After bifurcation in 2014, residual Andhra Pradesh's IT sector was described as having started from zero.
119.tq: Link the sectoral trend to the relevant structural event.
xs: Residual AP's IT sector "**started from zero**" after **bifurcation in 2014** — option **(3)**.
Pre-2014 IT exports came from Hyderabad's **HITEC City/Cyberabad**.
xa: **CII Partnership Summit 2025**: **54 MoUs**, **₹1,95,294 crore**.

119.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Acronym)
A. LIFT Policy 4.0
B. GCC
C. RTIH
D. OSAT

List-II (Full form or description)
1. Global Capability Centre
2. Ratan Tata Innovation Hub
3. Land Incentive for Tech Hubs
4. Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
119.x: LIFT means Land Incentive for Tech Hubs; GCC means Global Capability Centre; RTIH means Ratan Tata Innovation Hub; OSAT means Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test.
119.tq: Start from the sure acronym pairs and eliminate codes with mismatched expansions.
xs: **LIFT** = **Land Incentive for Tech Hubs**; **GCC** = **Global Capability Centre**.
**RTIH** = **Ratan Tata Innovation Hub**; **OSAT** = **Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test**.
xa: **AQV / AQRF** = Amaravati Quantum Valley / Amaravati Quantum Reference Facilities.
RTIH (**Aug 2025**): hub at **Amaravati**.

119.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Policy)
 a. Data Center Policy 4.0
 b. LIFT Policy 4.0
 c. Electronics Components Manufacturing Policy
 d. ESDM Policy

List-II (Feature)
 i. Component ecosystem
 ii. Land incentives for GCCs and IT infrastructure developers
 iii. Zone A/B reimbursement incentives
 iv. Addition of up to 1 GW data-centre capacity

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
119.x: The Data Center Policy targets up to 1 GW additional capacity; LIFT offers land incentives; the Components Policy develops the component ecosystem; and the ESDM Policy provides Zone A/B reimbursement incentives.
119.tq: Start from the sure policy-feature pairs and eliminate codes with swapped incentives.
xs: **a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii** — option **(1)**.
**Data Center Policy 4.0** → up to **1 GW**; **LIFT** → land for **GCCs** and IT infra developers.
**Components Policy** → **component ecosystem**; **ESDM** → **Zone A/B** reimbursement.
xa: ESDM's Zone A/B gave **100%** reimbursement of stamp duty, transfer duty and registration fee.
Gujarat's data-centre target: **7.5 GW**.

119.s: Which of the following correctly describes the role of N. Chandrababu Naidu in Andhra Pradesh's technology development?
o: His 1990s IT push helped build HITEC City, while the post-2014 IT base was rebuilt around Visakhapatnam.
His IT push was confined to the establishment of APSFL after 2020.
He developed only the quantum test beds and had no role in earlier IT infrastructure.
His technology initiatives began only after 2014 and were centred exclusively on Tirupati.
119.x: Naidu's 1990s IT push contributed to HITEC City's development, and after 2014 Andhra Pradesh rebuilt its IT base around Visakhapatnam.
119.tq: Compare the pre- and post-2014 phases instead of treating them as one period.
xs: Naidu's **1990s IT push** built **HITEC City**; after **2014** the IT base was rebuilt around **Visakhapatnam** — option **(1)**.
His era (**1995-2004**) also gave **eSeva** and the **SMART governance** model.
xa: **e-Pragati** was launched under him (2014-19).
**APSFL** was incorporated in **October 2015**, not after 2020.

119.s: Which of the following concerns has been raised in relation to the Data Lake?
119.x: Privacy and algorithmic-bias concerns have been raised in relation to the Data Lake.
119.tq: Match the governance concern with the correct digital platform or data initiative.
xs: The **Data Lake** faces **privacy and algorithmic-bias concerns** — option **(4)**.
It is the "**single source of truth**" for **40+ departments** and **~400 applications**.
xa: It sits at the **AP State Data Centre** with **Data Lens**.
Found **2,51,868 children** missing from rice cards.

120.s: According to NITI Aayog, the cultivated area of Andhra Pradesh in 2020-21 was 10.1 million hectares, equivalent to approximately what share of its geographical area?
120.x: NITI Aayog reported 10.1 million hectares of cultivated area, equivalent to 37% of the geographical area.
120.tq: Connect the reported area with its stated percentage and year.
xs: **10.1 million ha** cultivated area = **37%** of the geographical area (NITI Aayog, **2020-21**) — option **(3)** (**PYQ 2023**).
xa: Cropping intensity **1.21** in **2023-24**.

120.s: The cropping intensity of Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24, calculated as gross cropped area divided by net sown area, was:
120.x: The APSES 2024-25 recorded cropping intensity of 1.21 for 2023-24.
120.tq: Apply the stated ratio concept to the reported year-specific value.
xs: Cropping intensity (**GCA / NSA**) was **1.21** in **2023-24** — option **(1)**.
⚠ **1.88** is a **2024-25** figure in some summaries; the notes flag it as implausibly large.
xa: Current fallows **14.90%**; other fallows **6.36%**; culturable waste **2.48%**.

120.s: According to the stated 2025-26 data, which of the following is correct regarding land use in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Net area sown is 59.14 per cent and forest area is 36.29 per cent of land use
Net area sown is 36.29 per cent and forest area is 59.14 per cent of land use
Net area sown is 22.63 per cent and forest area is 36.29 per cent of land use
Net area sown is 36.29 per cent and forest area is 22.63 per cent of land use
120.x: The net area sown was 59.14 lakh hectares, constituting 36.29 per cent, while forests constituted 22.63 per cent of land use.
120.tq: Separate the absolute figure from the percentage and match each with the correct land-use category.
xs: **59.14** is the NSA in **lakh ha**, not a percentage; **36.29%** of **162.97 lakh ha**.
xa: Net sown area is the **largest** land-use category.
⚠ NITI Aayog's **37%** is **cultivated area** (2020-21).

120.s: In 2024-25, paddy accounted for approximately what share of the food-grain area of Andhra Pradesh?
120.x: Paddy covered 20.97 lakh hectares out of the 37.51 lakh hectares under food grains, which is approximately 56%.
120.tq: Use the given area figures to identify the approximate proportion.
xs: Paddy covered **20.97 lakh ha** of **37.51 lakh ha** food-grain area = about **56%** — option **(3)**.
Source: **2nd Advance Estimates**, **2024-25**.
xa: Derived yield ≈ **6.1 t/ha**.
Paddy has the **largest area of any crop** in AP (**PYQ 2018**).

120.s: With reference to the Economic Survey 2025-26, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Yields of major crops remained unchanged nationally and globally.
Yields of major crops declined nationally but exceeded global averages.
Yields of major crops rose globally but declined nationally.
Yields of major crops rose nationally but remained below global averages.
120.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 reported that yields of major crops increased nationally, but they remained below global averages.
120.tq: Distinguish the direction of change from the comparison with the global average.
xs: Yields of major crops **rose nationally** but **remain below global averages** — option **(4)**.
This is the **Economic Survey 2025-26** finding.
xa: AP paddy yield ≈ **6.1 t/ha** (**127.15 lakh t** on **20.97 lakh ha**).
National horticulture productivity: **12.56 MT/ha** (**2024-25**).

120.s: The increase in food-grain area in Andhra Pradesh during 2024-25 was associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: 16.5% increase in area and 11.7% rainfall deficit
12.85% increase in area and 11.7% rainfall surplus
11.7% increase in area and 12.85% rainfall surplus
12.85% decrease in area and 16.5% rainfall surplus
120.x: The 2024-25 rise in food-grain area was 12.85%, following an 11.7% rainfall surplus. The preceding year had recorded a 16.5% rainfall deficit.
120.tq: Separate the area percentage from the rainfall percentage and avoid reversing the two figures.
xs: **+12.85%** area after an **11.7% rainfall surplus** — option **(2)**.
The year before (**2023-24**) had a **16.5% deficit**.
xa: Food-grain area went **33.24 → 37.51 lakh ha**.

120.s: Which crop occupies the largest area among all crops in Andhra Pradesh?
120.x: Paddy has the largest area of any crop in AP (PYQ 2018): 20.97 lakh ha in 2024-25, about 56% of the food-grain area. Groundnut, cotton and maize are important but cover far less.
120.tq: Paddy = largest area; cotton = fastest-expanding commercial crop.
xs: **Paddy** has the **largest area of any crop** in AP — option **(4)** (**PYQ 2018**).
In **2024-25** it covered **20.97 lakh ha**, about **56%** of the food-grain area.
xa: **Cotton** ("white gold") is the commercial crop that expanded most (**PYQ 2022**).
Criticism: paddy's dominance displaces indigenous crops and is a major **methane** source.

120.s: Which commercial crop, called 'white gold', has expanded most in area in Andhra Pradesh in recent years?
120.x: Cotton ('white gold') is the commercial crop whose area expanded most (PYQ 2022). Tobacco, sugarcane and chillies are commercial crops but are not identified as the fastest-expanding.
120.tq: White gold = cotton (Palasa cashew is also nicknamed so; don't mix).
xs: **Cotton** ("**white gold**") expanded most among commercial crops — option **(1)** (**PYQ 2022**).
**Tobacco** (FCV) is concentrated in **Prakasam** and **Nellore**; **chillies** in **Guntur**.
xa: Cotton is grown in the **Krishna zone** (Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam) with paddy and chillies.
⚠ **Palasa** is the cashew "**White Gold City**" — do not confuse with cotton.

120.s: Palasa in Srikakulam district is popularly associated with which horticultural product?
120.x: Palasa in Srikakulam is known as the “White Gold City” because of its association with cashew.
120.tq: Use the place-product association method.
xs: **Palasa** (Srikakulam) is the **cashew** "**White Gold City**" — option **(4)**.
**Oil palm** → East Godavari + Kakinada; **coffee** → **Araku Valley**; **banana** exports → **Tadipatri**.
xa: Cashew: **42,690 acres**; **402** processing units.
AP ranks **4th** in coffee, **100%** from Araku Valley.

120.s: Sulakshana, associated with ICAR-CTRI, is a high-yielding variety of:
120.x: Sulakshana is a high-yielding tobacco variety developed in association with the Central Tobacco Research Institute.
120.tq: Direct recall of a variety-crop association.
xs: **Sulakshana** is a high-yielding **tobacco** variety — option **(3)** (**PYQ 2024**).
It suits the **black soils and southern light soils of AP**; bred at **ICAR-CTRI**, Rajahmundry.
xa: FCV tobacco: **Prakasam** (main) + **Nellore**.
**Tobacco Board** is at **Guntur**.

120.s: The Central Tobacco Research Institute is located at:
120.x: The Central Tobacco Research Institute, an ICAR institute, is located at Rajahmundry.
120.tq: Recall the institute-location pair.
xs: **CTRI** (Central Tobacco Research Institute, ICAR) is at **Rajahmundry** — option **(2)**.
**Guntur** has the **Tobacco Board**; **Prakasam** is the main FCV tobacco district.
xa: CTRI's **Sulakshana** suits black and southern light soils.
⚠ Institute → place: **IIOPR Pedavegi**; **VBRI Vijayawada**.

120.s: Why were Kakinada farmers advised in December 2019 to stop growing Bondalu paddy?
o: The variety was prohibited under the Agriculture Census.
Kerala, which had purchased the rice from Andhra Pradesh, began growing it itself.
The variety was declared unsuitable for black soils.
The variety required more irrigation than other paddy varieties.
120.x: Officials advised stopping Bondalu paddy cultivation because Kerala, its earlier buyer, had started producing the rice itself.
120.tq: Identify the market-related cause behind an agricultural advisory.
xs: **Kerala**, the earlier buyer of **Bondalu** rice, now grows it itself — option **(2)**.
Officials advised **Kakinada** farmers in **December 2019** to stop growing it (**PYQ 2018**).
xa: The **Godavari delta** is AP's main rice area.
Paddy land in the delta is shifting to **aquaculture**.

120.s: Which region is identified as Andhra Pradesh's main rice-growing area and aquaculture hub?
o: Godavari delta comprising East and West Godavari
120.x: The Godavari delta, covering East and West Godavari, is the main rice-growing area and an aquaculture hub.
120.tq: Match a region with its distinctive crop and allied activity.
xs: The **Godavari delta** (East + West Godavari) is the main rice area and **aquaculture hub** — option **(3)**.
**Anantapuramu** = groundnut; **Prakasam** = FCV tobacco.
xa: Delta paddy land is being converted to aquaculture.
**India's first Mega Aqua Food Park**: **Godavari Mega Aqua Food Park, Tundurru** (West Godavari).

120.s: Which crop combination is particularly associated with the Krishna zone comprising Krishna, Guntur and Prakasam?
120.x: The Krishna zone grows paddy, chillies and cotton.
120.tq: Recall a multi-crop regional association.
xs: The **Krishna zone** (Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam) grows **paddy (rice), chillies and cotton** — option **(2)**.
Groundnut belongs to **Anantapuramu**; onion to **Kurnool and YSR Kadapa**.
xa: **Guntur** = chillies + **Tobacco Board**.
Prakasam is also the main **FCV tobacco** district.

120.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
120.x: Groundnut is the main crop of the scarce-rainfall district Anantapuramu. Guntur is associated with chillies, and Prakasam with FCV tobacco.
120.tq: Use the dominant crop-district pair and reject geographical swaps.
xs: **Groundnut — Anantapuramu** is correct — option **(1)**.
Chillies → **Guntur**, not Nellore; FCV tobacco → **Prakasam + Nellore**, not Kurnool; onion → **Kurnool and YSR Kadapa**.
xa: Anantapuramu is a **scarce-rainfall** district.
Kharif 2026: groundnut sown only **34%** of normal.

120.s: The main FCV tobacco districts of Andhra Pradesh are:
120.x: Prakasam and Nellore are the main FCV tobacco districts.
120.tq: Distinguish the broader tobacco districts from the location of the Tobacco Board.
xs: **Prakasam** (main) + **Nellore** are the **FCV tobacco** districts — option **(3)**.
Guntur holds the **Tobacco Board** and grows **chillies**.
xa: **CTRI** is at **Rajahmundry**; variety **Sulakshana**.
Top three crops (DES, Mar 2026): **chilli, oil palm, tobacco**.

120.s: The Tobacco Board of India is located at:
120.x: The Tobacco Board is located at Guntur, although Prakasam and Nellore are the main FCV tobacco districts.
120.tq: Separate the institution's location from the crop's dominant districts.
xs: The **Tobacco Board** is at **Guntur** — option **(3)**.
**Rajahmundry** has **CTRI**; **Prakasam** and **Nellore** are the growing districts.
xa: Guntur is also AP's **chillies** district.
⚠ Board (Guntur) vs research institute (Rajahmundry).

120.s: The current shift in the cropping pattern of Andhra Pradesh is primarily towards:
o: Only paddy and other food grains
120.x: The cropping pattern is shifting towards fruits, vegetables, flowers and spices because of their profitability and export potential.
120.tq: Distinguish the emerging diversification pattern from the traditional crop groups.
xs: The shift is towards **fruits, vegetables, flowers and spices** — option **(2)**.
Reasons: **profit + export**.
xa: Horticulture is the fastest-growing farm segment (about **10%** a year).
AP is **India's largest fruit producer** (**15.6%** of national fruit output).

120.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the 11 crops targeted for productivity improvement under the 17 growth engines of Swarna Andhra @2047?
120.x: The 11 crops include paddy, maize, jowar, bajra, ragi, redgram, blackgram, bengalgram, groundnut, sunflower and sesamum. Sugarcane is not included in this specified list.
120.tq: Find the option outside the explicitly enumerated crop list.
xs: **Sugarcane** is not among the **11 crops** — option **(4)**.
The 11: **paddy, maize, jowar, bajra, ragi, redgram, blackgram, bengalgram, groundnut, sunflower, sesamum**.
xa: Area expansion targeted for **sunflower, sesamum and millets**.
⚠ **17 growth engines**; **11 crops**; horticulture **22** crops; **11** crops in **24 clusters**.

120.s: The agricultural and allied-sector strategy under APSES 2024-25 targets what growth over five years?
120.x: The strategy targets 30% growth in agriculture and allied sectors over five years, delivered through 17 growth engines.
120.tq: Keep the target percentage and the number of delivery mechanisms together while rejecting swapped figures.
xs: **30% growth** over **five years** via **17 growth engines** — option **(2)**.
Strategy of the Agriculture Department (**2024-25**) under **Swarna Andhra @2047**.
xa: Raise productivity of **11 crops**; crop diversification + natural farming.
Horticulture: **22** growth-engine crops; target GVA **₹3 lakh crore** by **2029-30**.

120.s: The first separate agriculture budget in undivided Andhra Pradesh was presented in:
120.x: Undivided Andhra Pradesh first presented a separate agriculture budget in 2013.
120.tq: Test a state-level milestone using adjacent-year numerical distractors.
xs: The **first separate agri budget** was in undivided AP in **2013** — option **(3)**.
It came before bifurcation; the residual state has since kept a **Separate Agriculture & Allied Budget**.
xa: **2026-27** budget: **~₹53,753 crore**, by **K. Atchannaidu** (third time).
**₹500 crore** Price Stabilisation Fund in it.

120.s: The separate Agriculture and Allied Budget of Andhra Pradesh for 2026-27 (about ₹53,753 crore) was presented by:
o: Payyavula Keshav, for the first time
K. Atchannaidu, for the third time
Nara Lokesh, for the second time
K. Atchannaidu, for the first time
120.x: K. Atchannaidu presented the 2026-27 Agriculture & Allied Budget, for the third time. So A (Payyavula Keshav) and C (Nara Lokesh, the IT minister) name the wrong person, and D gets the count wrong: it was not his first.
120.tq: Agri budget 2026-27: Atchannaidu, 3rd time; first ever in 2013.
xs: **K. Atchannaidu**, for the **third time** — option **(2)**.
So options (1) and (3) name the wrong person, and (4) gets the count wrong.
xa: Size **~₹53,753 crore**; **₹13,722 crore** power subsidy.
First separate agri budget: undivided AP, **2013**.

120.s: Which one of the following correctly describes YSR Rythu Bharosa-PM Kisan during 2019–2024?
o: ₹12,000 per acre annually, restricted to landowners
₹6,000 per farmer family annually, covering only tenant farmers
₹13,500 per farmer family annually, covering owners, tenants and RoFR cultivators
₹20,000 per farmer family annually, restricted to CCRC holders
120.x: During 2019–2024, YSR Rythu Bharosa-PM Kisan provided ₹13,500 per family per year and covered owners, tenant farmers and RoFR cultivators.
120.tq: Separate the amount, period and beneficiary categories of two similarly named support schemes.
xs: **₹13,500** per family a year, covering **owners, tenants and RoFR** cultivators — option **(3)**.
It ran **2019-2024** and included the **₹6,000** central PM-KISAN part.
⚠ **₹12,000 per acre** is Telangana's; **₹20,000** is **Annadata Sukhibhava**.
xa: Its successor **Annadata Sukhibhava** (2024-25 onwards) gives **₹20,000**.
RoFR = **tribal** cultivators; tenants are covered through **CCRC** cards (**2019** Act).

120.s: The annual assistance under Annadata Sukhibhava-PM Kisan is:
o: ₹20,000 per farmer family, comprising ₹14,000 from the State and ₹6,000 from the Centre
₹12,000 per farmer family, comprising ₹6,000 from each government
₹13,500 per farmer family, entirely from the State Government
₹20,000 per acre, comprising ₹14,000 from the Centre and ₹6,000 from the State
120.x: Annadata Sukhibhava-PM Kisan provides ₹20,000 per farmer family annually, including ₹14,000 from the State and ₹6,000 under PM-KISAN from the Centre.
120.tq: Check both the unit of assistance and the State–Centre contribution split.
xs: **₹20,000** per farmer family = **₹14,000 State + ₹6,000 Centre** — option **(1)**.
It is per **family**, not per acre; ₹13,500 was **YSR Rythu Bharosa**.
xa: **3 instalments**: Kharif **₹7,000**, Rabi **₹7,000**, Summer **₹6,000**.
**2025-26**: **46.86 lakh** families; **₹6,309 crore** paid in **2** instalments.
**2026-27** proposal: **₹7,260 crore** for **51 lakh** families.

120.s:
With reference to Annadata Sukhibhava-PM Kisan, consider the following statements:
1. It commenced from 2024–25 onwards.
2. It includes tenant farmers holding CCRC.
3. The ₹6,000 PM-KISAN component is meant for landholders.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: Annadata Sukhibhava-PM Kisan operates from 2024–25 onwards, covers farmer families including CCRC-holding tenants, and includes the ₹6,000 PM-KISAN component for landholders.
120.tq: Test the scheme period and the distinction between tenant coverage and the landholder-linked central component.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
It runs **2024-25 onwards** (Super Six) and covers families **including tenant farmers** (CCRC holders).
The **₹6,000 PM-KISAN** part goes to **landholders**.
xa: **2025-26** beneficiaries include **1,16,021** RoFR cultivators.
Exam angle: "tenant farmers included" — **true**.

120.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Jala Yagnam — Interest subvention on crop loans
120.x: Panta Sanjeevani refers to the construction of farm ponds. GAP Polambadi concerns farmer field schools and Ind.GAP certification, while Jala Yagnam concerns irrigation projects.
120.tq: Separate similarly agriculture-related schemes by identifying their precise domain rather than their broad sector.
xs: **Panta Sanjeevani — farm ponds** is correct — option **(3)** (APPSC answer).
**GAP Polambadi** = Farmer Field Schools + **Ind.GAP**; **Vaddi Leni Runalu** = interest subvention; **Jala Yagnam** = irrigation (**52** projects).
xa: Farm ponds are dug under **MGNREGS** convergence for **protective irrigation**.
**Rythu Bazars** (**1999**) = farmer-to-consumer sales.

120.s: Under Vaddi Leni Runalu or Pavala Vaddi, interest subvention on crop loans is provided as follows:
o: 1% up to ₹1 lakh and 4% for ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lakh
1% on all crop loans up to ₹3 lakh
4% up to ₹3 lakh and 1% above ₹3 lakh
4% up to ₹1 lakh and 1% for ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lakh
120.x: The scheme provides 4% interest subvention up to ₹1 lakh and 1% for the loan amount from ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lakh.
120.tq: Keep the two loan slabs and their respective rates in the correct order.
xs: **Vaddi Leni Runalu / Pavala Vaddi** covers crop loans up to **₹3 lakh**.
xa: ⚠ Option (1) reverses the rates.
**PKCC** (livestock): repay within a year → effective **4%**.

120.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the administration of agricultural markets in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Rythu Bazars are run by Market Committees, whereas regulated yards are run by Estate Officers.
Rythu Bazars are run by Estate Officers, whereas regulated yards are run by Market Committees.
Both Rythu Bazars and regulated yards are run by District Collectors.
Both Rythu Bazars and regulated yards are run by Estate Officers.
120.x: A Rythu Bazar is run by an Estate Officer, while a regulated yard is run by a Market Committee.
120.tq: Split the options by comparing the authorities responsible for two similar institutions.
xs: **Rythu Bazar** → **Estate Officer**; **regulated yard** → **Market Committee** — option **(2)**.
⚠ PYQ false statement: "**District Collector** is the co-ordinating officer".
xa: Rythu Bazars (**1999**) sit under the **Revenue Department**.
**129** functioning, **10** under construction.

120.s: In Rythu Bazars, prices are generally fixed at which of the following levels?
o: About 25% below wholesale prices and above local retail prices
Equal to wholesale prices and above local retail prices
Equal to local retail prices and below wholesale prices
About 25% above wholesale prices and below local retail prices
120.x: Rythu Bazar prices are fixed at about 25% above wholesale prices but below local retail prices.
120.tq: Test the direction of a comparison by separating the wholesale and retail reference points.
xs: About **25% above wholesale**, **below local retail** — option **(4)**.
This lets farmers earn more while consumers pay less.
xa: Rythu Bazars run by an **Estate Officer** (Revenue Department).
**129** functioning.

120.s: Rythu Bharosa Kendras were established in Andhra Pradesh in 2020 with an initial network of:
120.x: Rythu Bharosa Kendras were established in 2020, and 10,778 centres were set up beside village secretariats.
120.tq: Match the institutional year with the original network count rather than the later functional count.
xs: **10,778** RBK centres were set up beside village secretariats — option **(2)**.
Figure per **Socio-Economic Survey 2023-24** (asked twice in G2).
**8,489** = rationalised functional RSKs; **10,606** = RSKs serving livestock farmers.
xa: Each is an **input shop + farmer knowledge centre**.
**Soil Health Cards** 2025-26: **5.52 lakh** samples tested across **10,778 RSKs**.

120.s: Rythu Bharosa Kendras are now known as Rythu Seva Kendras and have been rationalised to how many functional centres?
120.x: The centres are now called Rythu Seva Kendras, and the rationalised number of functional RSKs is 8,489.
120.tq: Use the confusable-pair method to distinguish the original establishment count from the current functional count.
xs: RBKs, now **Rythu Seva Kendras**, were rationalised to **8,489** functional RSKs — option **(1)**.
⚠ **10,778** set up → **8,489** functional.
xa: Also cited as "over **10,700**" / **10,606** RSKs.
Services include **e-Panta**, **CCRC issuance**, soil testing, crop insurance.

120.s: Which of the following services is NOT associated with Rythu Seva Kendras?
120.x: RSKs provide agricultural services such as soil testing, e-Panta, CCRC issuance, input subsidies, crop insurance, drone awareness and procurement. Issuing industrial licences is not among these services.
120.tq: Find the one option outside the closely related group of agricultural services.
xs: **Issuing industrial licences** is not an RSK service — option **(1)**.
RSKs do **soil testing**, **e-Panta**, CCRC issuance, input subsidies, **crop insurance**, drone awareness, procurement.
xa: Doorstep veterinary care via **Animal Husbandry Assistants**.
**e-Crop booking** is the basis for insurance, MSP procurement and loss assessment.

120.s: Rythu Bazars, where farmers sell their produce directly to consumers, were started in Andhra Pradesh in:
120.x: Rythu Bazars began in 1999. 1995 was when Naidu first became CM, 2004 the start of the YSR government and Jala Yagnam, and 2014 bifurcation.
120.tq: Rythu Bazar 1999; run by an Estate Officer.
xs: **Rythu Bazars** were started in AP in **1999** — so option **(2)** is correct.
In a Rythu Bazar farmers sell **directly to consumers**, at about **25%** above wholesale but below local retail prices.
Each Rythu Bazar is run by an **Estate Officer** of the **Revenue Department**; a regulated yard is run by a **Market Committee**.
xa: **129** Rythu Bazars are functioning and **10** are under construction (APSES 2024-25 said **124**).
⚠ PYQ trap: "**District Collector** is the co-ordinating officer" was the **false** statement.
El Nino plan (Jul 2026): **One Mobile Rythu Bazaar per district**.

120.s:
With reference to the Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA), consider the following statements:
1. It is a district-level demand-driven extension agency.
2. It prepares the Strategic Research and Extension Plan (SREP).
3. It is implemented as a centrally sponsored initiative with a 60:40 funding pattern.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: ATMA is district-level and demand-driven, prepares the SREP, and operates under a 60:40 centrally sponsored funding pattern.
120.tq: Combine institutional role, planning function and funding pattern in a coded statement question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1 is correct: ATMA is a **district-level, demand-driven** extension agency.
Statement 2 is correct: it prepares the district **SREP**.
Statement 3 is correct: it is **centrally sponsored** with a **60:40** funding pattern.
xa: ATMA = **Agricultural Technology Management Agency**, under the **Sub-Mission on Agricultural Extension**.
Coverage: all **26 districts**; **₹18.03 crore** released in 2025-26.
It is a district-level **autonomous body** with a Governing Board, Management Committee and Farmer Interest Groups.

120.s: CCRC holders can obtain all of the following without affecting the landowner's rights, EXCEPT:
o: Permanent ownership of the leased land
Access to MSP and government schemes
120.x: CCRCs facilitate loans, insurance, MSP and scheme access, but they do not confer permanent ownership on tenants.
120.tq: Find the option that reverses the distinction between entitlement and ownership.
xs: A CCRC does **not** give **permanent ownership of the leased land** — so option **(3)** is the exception.
CCRC holders get **loans**, **insurance**, **MSP** and **schemes** while the **landlord's title stays unaffected**.
xa: CCRC = **Crop Cultivator Rights Card**, under the **AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019**; valid **11 months**.
Issuance began on **2 Oct 2019**.
Criticism: a gap between **CCRCs** issued and holders actually financed.
A **new AP Tenancy Act, 2024** is only a **planned law**.

120.s: GAP Polambadi is associated with:
o: Farmer Field Schools, Good Agricultural Practices and Ind.GAP certification
Crop insurance enrolment and premium collection
Construction of major and medium irrigation projects
120.x: Polambadi means Farmer Field Schools. GAP Polambadi teaches Good Agricultural Practices, aims to reduce chemical pesticide use and is linked to Ind.GAP certification for better prices for FPOs.
120.tq: Match the extension activity with its training, certification and pesticide-reduction functions.
xs: **GAP Polambadi** = **Farmer Field Schools** teaching **Good Agricultural Practices**, linked to **Ind.GAP certification** — option **(2)**.
It aims to cut **chemical pesticide** use; Ind.GAP certification fetches **better prices for FPOs**.
Farm ponds are **Panta Sanjeevani**, and major/medium irrigation projects were **Jala Yagnam** — not Polambadi.
xa: **Polambadi** literally = **Farmer Field Schools**.
Other domain matches: **Vaddi Leni Runalu** = interest subvention on crop loans up to **₹3 lakh**; **Rythu Bazars** = farmer-to-consumer sales.
**Jala Yagnam** (YSR, 2004-09) covered **52** major/medium projects.

120.s: Crop Cultivator Rights Cards (CCRCs) for tenant farmers in Andhra Pradesh are issued under which law, and for what validity?
o: AP Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011; 5 years
AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019; 11 months
AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019; 3 years
120.x: CCRCs are issued under the AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019 and are valid for 11 months. The new AP Tenancy Act, 2024 is only planned; 5-year and 3-year validities are wrong.
120.tq: CCRC: Act 2019, 11 months, from 2 Oct 2019.
xs: CCRCs are issued under the **AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019**, with **11 months** validity — option **(2)**.
The **new AP Tenancy Act, 2024** is only a **planned law**, so option (3) is wrong.
xa: Issuance began on **2 Oct 2019**.
Tenants get loans, insurance, MSP and schemes **without affecting the landowner's rights**.
2025-26: **8,24,620** active CCRCs; **₹3,768.15 crore** tenant loans.
**Annadata Sukhibhava** covers **tenant farmers** holding CCRCs.

120.s: The primary objective of Soil Health Cards under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana is to promote:
120.x: Soil Health Cards promote judicious fertiliser use by providing information about soil conditions and nutrient requirements.
120.tq: Identify the practical objective of a programme from the action it promotes.
xs: **Soil Health Cards** under **RKVY** promote **judicious use of fertilisers** — option **(4)**.
They are based on soil samples tested for each farm.
xa: 2025-26: **6.0 lakh** samples collected; **5.52 lakh** tested across **10,778 RSKs**.
**Soil testing** is one of the services of the **Rythu Seva Kendras**.
RKVY also funds horticulture in **non-MIDH districts** (**₹24.07 cr**, 2024-25).

120.s: e-Crop booking at Rythu Seva Kendras is best understood as:
o: A digital land-sale register used only for property taxation
A veterinary database used for livestock vaccination
An online market-price bulletin used only by regulated yards
A digital crop record used for insurance, MSP procurement, input subsidy and loss assessment
120.x: e-Crop booking creates a digital crop record that serves as the basis for insurance, MSP procurement, input subsidy and loss assessment.
120.tq: Match a digital system with the full set of decisions and benefits it supports.
xs: **e-Crop booking** is a **digital crop record** at RSKs, the basis for **insurance, MSP procurement, input subsidy and loss assessment** — option **(4)**.
It is not a land-sale register or livestock database; it records crops grown each season.
xa: **e-Fish booking** does the same for **aqua farmers**.
**e-Panta** (e-crop) is listed among the RSK services, with soil testing and **CCRC issuance**.
**10,778** RBKs were set up; rationalised to **8,489** functional RSKs.

120.s: Farm ponds under Panta Sanjeevani were dug through convergence with:
120.x: Farm ponds under Panta Sanjeevani were dug through convergence with the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.
120.tq: Use the implementing-convergence relationship to distinguish the employment programme from insurance and certification schemes.
xs: Panta Sanjeevani farm ponds were dug through convergence with **MGNREGS** — option **(3)**.
The ponds harvest rain-water for **protective irrigation**.
xa: "Panta Sanjeevani" = **construction of farm ponds** (APPSC answer).
**Ind.GAP** is the certification linked to **GAP Polambadi**, not to farm ponds.
**Soil Health Cards** under **RKVY** promote judicious fertiliser use.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about the direct benefit transfer (DBT) of the free agricultural power subsidy in Andhra Pradesh:
1. It was piloted in Srikakulam district in 2020.
2. Under the pilot, smart meters were installed on domestic electricity connections.
3. The stated target is 100% renewable energy for agricultural pump-sets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is correct: the pilot was in Srikakulam district (2020). Statement 2 is wrong: the smart meters were fitted on farm pump-sets; the subsidy is credited to farmers, who then pay the discom. Statement 3 is correct: the target is 100% renewable energy for agricultural pump-sets. So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
120.tq: Smart meters go on farm pump-sets, not homes: Srikakulam 2020 pilot.

120.s: Which agency implements the Andhra Pradesh Community-Managed Natural Farming programme?
o: Andhra Pradesh State Seeds Development Corporation
Andhra Pradesh State Agro Industries Development Corporation
120.x: The Andhra Pradesh Community-Managed Natural Farming programme is implemented by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS).
120.tq: Use the implementing-agency identification method.
xs: **Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS)** implements **APCNF** — option **(2)**.
RySS is a not-for-profit company of the **Department of Agriculture, GoAP**, incorporated **October 2014**.
xa: APCNF began as **ZBNF** in **2016**.
APCNF is called the **world's largest agro-ecological transition**.
Coverage: **10.20 lakh** farmers on **4.89 lakh ha** in **4,116** Gram Panchayats.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS):
1. It is a not-for-profit company set up by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Andhra Pradesh.
2. It was incorporated in October 2016, the year ZBNF was launched in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is correct: RySS is a State not-for-profit company under the Department of Agriculture, GoAP. Statement 2 is wrong: RySS was incorporated in October 2014; 2016 is the year ZBNF was launched in AP. So '1 only'; 'Both' and '2 only' accept the wrong year, and 'Neither' rejects a true statement.
120.tq: RySS 2014, ZBNF in AP 2016, ZBNF devised mid-1990s.

120.s: In the context of Zero Budget Natural Farming, the expression “zero budget” primarily refers to
o: cultivation without purchased fertilisers or pesticides
120.x: “Zero budget” refers to avoiding purchased fertilisers and pesticides; it does not mean that every input or labour cost is absent.
120.tq: Interpret the exact meaning of a potentially misleading programme label.
xs: "Zero budget" means farming **without purchased fertilisers or pesticides** — option **(4)**.
It does not mean no labour, irrigation or seed cost.
xa: ZBNF was developed by **Subhash Palekar** (**Padma Shri**) in the **mid-1990s**.
AP launched it in **2016** and renamed it **APCNF**.
Its inputs are local: **Jeevamrutham** is a bio-fertiliser made from **cow dung, cow urine, jaggery, pulse flour, soil**.

120.s: Andhra Pradesh launched ZBNF in 2016 and subsequently renamed it as
120.x: The programme launched as ZBNF in 2016 was renamed APCNF, meaning Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming.
120.tq: Test the exact expansion of a renamed programme rather than a similar-sounding agricultural term.
xs: ZBNF (**2016**) was renamed **Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming (APCNF)** — option **(3)**.
Its implementing agency is **Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS)**.
xa: APCNF is the **world's largest agro-ecological transition**.
It won the **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024** (Lisbon).
It was the first Indian finalist of the **Food Planet Prize**.

120.s: Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF), which Andhra Pradesh adopted in 2016, was developed by:
120.x: ZBNF was developed in the mid-1990s by Maharashtrian agriculturist Subhash Palekar (Padma Shri). Swaminathan led the Green Revolution, Kurien Operation Flood, and Fukuoka is the Japanese natural-farming pioneer, not ZBNF's founder.
120.tq: ZBNF = Palekar; APCNF = RySS.
xs: ZBNF was developed by **Subhash Palekar** — option **(2)**.
Palekar, a **Padma Shri**, is a **Maharashtrian agriculturist** who developed ZBNF in the **mid-1990s**.
xa: AP adopted it in **2016**; it is now **APCNF**.
Its principles: no chemicals, **mulching**, microbial cultures, intercropping, **minimum tillage**, livestock integration.
⚠ The **M.S. Swaminathan Award** for Environment Protection went to **RySS** (2022-23); Swaminathan did not develop ZBNF.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about Zero Budget Natural Farming:
1. It emphasises minimum tillage.
2. It includes livestock integration.
3. It encourages crop diversity and intercropping.
4. It is based on exclusive use of chemical pesticides.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because ZBNF is based on avoiding chemicals, not their exclusive use.
120.tq: Identify the chemically opposite statement among otherwise correct principles.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct: ZBNF includes **minimum tillage** and **livestock integration**.
Statement 3 is correct: it encourages **crop diversity and intercropping**.
Statement 4 is wrong: ZBNF means **no chemicals**, not exclusive use of chemical pesticides.
xa: Other principles: seed treatment with local inputs, **mulching**, **microbial cultures**.
ZBNF was developed by **Subhash Palekar** in the **mid-1990s**.
Trap crops such as **marigold** and **castor** replace pesticides.

120.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Jeevamrutham — seed treatment with cow dung, cow urine and lime
Mulching — sowing before rains on residual moisture
120.x: Ghanajeevamrutham is the solid form of Jeevamrutham. Beejamrutham is the seed treatment, while mulching is the use of crop residue or straw cover.
120.tq: Start from the sure practice-definition pair and reject swapped meanings.
xs: **Ghanajeevamrutham** is the **solid form of Jeevamrutham** — option **(3)**.
**Beejamrutham** is seed treatment, not a solid form, so (1) is wrong.
**Jeevamrutham** is a bio-fertiliser, not a seed treatment, so (2) is wrong.
**Mulching** is crop-residue/straw cover; sowing before rains is **PMDS**, so (4) is wrong.
xa: ⚠ Trap: Beejamrutham = seed treatment; Jeevamrutham = bio-fertiliser; Ghanajeevamrutham = solid form.
Jeevamrutham uses **cow dung, cow urine, jaggery, pulse flour, soil**.
**365-day green cover** keeps soil covered all year by cover cropping and polyculture.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about APCNF practices:
1. Mulching uses crop-residue or straw cover to conserve moisture and suppress weeds.
2. Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing involves sowing before the rains on residual moisture.
3. PMDS is associated with millets, pulses and oilseeds.
4. A 365-day green cover is maintained through cover cropping and polyculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All four statements correctly describe mulching, PMDS and the 365-day green-cover approach.
120.tq: Combine closely related practice definitions while checking each statement independently.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Statement 1: **Mulching** = crop-residue/straw cover to keep moisture and suppress weeds.
Statements 2 and 3: **PMDS** = sowing before the rains on residual moisture, with **millets, pulses, oilseeds**.
Statement 4: **365-day green cover** comes from cover cropping and polyculture.
xa: PMDS in **Kurnool**: **92,000 acres**, due to the **El Nino** rain deficit (Jul 2026).
Mulching is also called **Acchadana**.
Other practices: **native seeds**, no/minimal tillage, livestock integration, **trap crops** (marigold, castor).

120.s: The natural farming programme works in clusters generally consisting of
120.x: The programme works in clusters of five villages covering approximately 1,500 to 2,500 acres.
120.tq: Recall a paired structural figure by linking the number of villages with the acreage range.
xs: A natural farming cluster is **5 villages** covering **1,500-2,500 acres** — option **(1)**.
This is the basic programme unit of APCNF.
xa: 2024-25 plan: **5-10 village clusters per Parliamentary Constituency**, **1,000 acres** each = **25,000 acres**.
Clusters cover technology, transition finance, post-harvest, marketing and women SHG enterprise.
⚠ PKVY organic clusters are **50 farmers / 50 acres**.

120.s: Which of the following correctly states the coverage and target of APCNF?
o: It covers 4.89 lakh farmers on 10.20 lakh hectares and targets 19 lakh farmers on 41 lakh hectares by 2028–29.
It covers 41 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh hectares and targets 10.20 lakh farmers on 19 lakh hectares.
It covers 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh hectares and targets 41 lakh farmers on 19 lakh hectares by 2028–29.
It covers 7 lakh farmers on 19 lakh hectares and targets 10.20 lakh farmers by 2028–29.
120.x: The stated APCNF coverage is 10.20 lakh farmers over 4.89 lakh hectares, with a target of 41 lakh farmers over 19 lakh hectares by 2028–29.
120.tq: Compare present coverage with future target while checking the farmer-area pairing.
xs: APCNF covers **10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha**, targeting **41 lakh farmers on 19 lakh ha by 2028-29** — option **(3)**.
Options (1) and (2) swap farmers and hectares.
"**7 lakh** farmers" is an older count, not the current figure.
xa: **4,116** Gram Panchayats covered; **3.68 lakh** NF kitchen gardens.
All Gram Panchayats targeted **by 2026-27**.
⚠ NMNF action plans: **7.78 lakh ha** + **19.75 lakh farmers** — do not mix with APCNF.

120.s: Which award was associated with APCNF for environmental protection in 2022-23?
o: M.S. Swaminathan Award for Environment Protection
120.x: The M.S. Swaminathan Award for Environment Protection (2022-23) went to RySS, the agency that implements APCNF. The other awards are not linked to APCNF.
120.tq: Distinguish the environmental award from other similarly themed awards.
xs: The **M.S. Swaminathan Award for Environment Protection** (2022-23) went to **RySS**, the APCNF agency — option **(3)**.
The notes link no other listed award to APCNF.
xa: **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024**: **11 July 2024**, Lisbon; shared with **2** others.
**Food Planet Prize 2026**: **$1.5 million**, Bastad (Sweden); APCNF was the first Indian finalist.
Replication: other states + **Zambia and Sri Lanka**.

120.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Food Planet Prize 2026:
1. APCNF was the first Indian finalist.
2. The prize amount was 1.5 million US dollars.
3. The award was associated with the Curt Bergfors Foundation.
4. It was held at Bastad in Sweden in June 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All four statements are correct: APCNF was the first Indian finalist, and the June 2026 prize at Bastad, Sweden, carried an award of 1.5 million US dollars from the Curt Bergfors Foundation.
120.tq: Verify a named international award through its amount, sponsor, place and finalist status.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
APCNF was the **first Indian finalist** of the **Food Planet Prize 2026**.
Prize: **$1.5 million**, from the **Curt Bergfors Foundation**, at **Bastad (Sweden)**, **June 2026**.
xa: **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024** — **11 July 2024**, Lisbon.
**M.S. Swaminathan Award for Environment Protection** to RySS (2022-23).
The Food Planet Prize win was on **4 Jun 2026**.

120.s: Which of the following correctly describes the international spread of the APCNF model?
o: It is being replicated only within Andhra Pradesh.
It has been replicated only in Kenya and Sweden.
It is restricted to the five-village clusters of Andhra Pradesh.
It is being replicated in other Indian States, Zambia and Sri Lanka.
120.x: The APCNF model is being replicated in other States of India as well as in Zambia and Sri Lanka.
120.tq: Test the geographical extent of replication against restrictive alternatives.
xs: APCNF is being replicated in **other Indian States, Zambia and Sri Lanka** — option **(4)**.
So it is not limited to AP or its clusters; **Kenya** only sent a study delegation, and **Sweden** hosted the Food Planet Prize.
xa: Kenyan delegation visited **Kollipara mandal** (Guntur) on **8 Jul 2026**.
A **Gujarat delegation** saw APCNF in **Guntur** (**10 Sep 2026**).
APCNF = **world's largest agro-ecological transition**.

120.s: The Andhra Pradesh Community-Managed Natural Farming programme received the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity in which year and at which place?
120.x: APCNF received the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity in 2024; the prize was shared and the recognition was associated with Lisbon on 11 July 2024.
120.tq: Combine the award, year and venue in a single recall unit.
xs: APCNF won the **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity** in **2024** at **Lisbon** — option **(3)**.
It was awarded on **11 July 2024** and shared with **2** others.
xa: **Food Planet Prize 2026**: **$1.5 million**, Bastad (Sweden); APCNF the first Indian finalist.
**M.S. Swaminathan Award for Environment Protection** went to RySS (2022-23).
**Kenya** sent a study delegation; it did not host an award.

120.s: Which one of the following correctly states the action-plan coverage under the National Mission on Natural Farming?
120.x: The NMNF action plans cover 7.78 lakh hectares and 19.75 lakh farmers.
120.tq: Avoid reversing the area and farmer figures in a paired quantitative comparison.
xs: NMNF action plans cover **7.78 lakh ha** and **19.75 lakh farmers** — option **(4)**.
Option (2) swaps the two numbers; option (1) is **APCNF's** coverage (**10.20 lakh** farmers, **4.89 lakh ha**).
xa: **70,021 Krishi Sakhis** trained under NMNF.
**14.43 lakh** farmers certified (Aug 2026).
⚠ NMNF = natural farming; **PKVY** = **organic** (PGS-India).

120.s: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) promotes:
o: Natural farming through Krishi Sakhis with no certification
Organic farming in clusters of 50 farmers / 50 acres with PGS-India certification
Oil palm expansion with a viability price paid by DBT
Micro-irrigation through drip and sprinkler subsidies
120.x: PKVY is the organic farming scheme: clusters of 50 farmers / 50 acres certified under PGS-India. Krishi Sakhis belong to the National Mission on Natural Farming, viability price to NMEO-OP, and drip subsidies to micro-irrigation (APMIP).
120.tq: PKVY = organic + PGS-India; NMNF = natural + Krishi Sakhis.
xs: **PKVY** promotes **organic** farming in clusters of **50 farmers / 50 acres** with **PGS-India** certification — option **(2)**.
**Krishi Sakhis** belong to **NMNF**, the **Viability Price** to **NMEO-OP**, and drip/sprinkler subsidy to **APMIP**.
xa: PKVY added **200** tribal clusters in **Visakhapatnam** (Feb 2026).
NMNF trained **70,021 Krishi Sakhis**.
APMIP covers **37.90 lakh acres** — **75% drip / 25% sprinkler**.

120.s:
Consider the following statements regarding horticulture in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Horticulture GVA of Andhra Pradesh was ₹1,52,950 crore.
2. Andhra Pradesh ranked third in India in horticulture GVA after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.
3. Horticulture GVA recorded 21% growth in 2024-25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh recorded horticulture GVA of ₹1,52,950 crore, ranked third after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra, and registered 21% growth in 2024-25.
120.tq: Check each numerical and ranking statement independently before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: horticulture GVA is **₹1,52,950 crore**.
Statement 2: AP is **3rd** in India after **UP** and **Maharashtra**.
Statement 3: growth was **+21%** in 2024-25.
xa: Earlier GVA: **₹1,23,533 cr** at current prices (2022-23).
Area & output (Survey 2025-26): **46.43 lakh acres**, **406.38 lakh MT**.
**Rayalaseema** = **52%** of output; target GVA **₹3 lakh crore** by **2029-30**.

120.s: What is the target horticulture GVA of Andhra Pradesh by 2029-30?
120.x: Andhra Pradesh has set a target of ₹3 lakh crore horticulture GVA by 2029-30, covering 22 growth-engine crops.
120.tq: Recall the target year together with its associated figure.
xs: AP targets **₹3 lakh crore** horticulture GVA by **2029-30** — option **(2)**.
The target covers **22** horticulture growth-engine crops.
xa: Current horticulture GVA: **₹1,52,950 crore** (3rd after UP, Maharashtra).
**11 growth-engine crops** in **24 clusters** (banana, mango, chilli, oil palm, cocoa, dragon fruit, coffee).
⚠ Trap: **17 growth engines**; **11 crops** for productivity; horticulture **22** crops.

120.s: Which region is known as the horticulture hub of Andhra Pradesh?
120.x: Rayalaseema is the horticulture hub of Andhra Pradesh, covering about 7.8 lakh hectares and contributing about half of horticulture GVA.
120.tq: Identify the region from its distinctive sectoral description.
xs: **Rayalaseema** is AP's **horticulture hub** — option **(3)**.
It holds **19.50 lakh acres** (43% of area) and **52%** of output.
It has about half of horticulture GVA (**₹76,458 cr**) and **71%** of micro-irrigation area.
