xa: The **Godavari delta** is the main rice area and the **aquaculture hub**, not the horticulture hub.
Rayalaseema's shift to horticulture depends on **drip irrigation**.
**Tadipatri** (Anantapur) sends **banana** exports by refrigerated trains.

120.s: Rayalaseema accounts for approximately what share of Andhra Pradesh's horticulture area and output, respectively?
120.x: Rayalaseema is the horticulture hub, with about 45% of the area (the figure the Survey prints; 19.50 lakh acres works out to about 43%) and 52% of output. Option A swaps the two shares.
120.tq: Do not reverse the area share and output share in a comparison question.
xs: **Rayalaseema** holds about **45% of area** and **52% of output** of AP horticulture — option **(2)**.
The Survey prints **45%**; Rayalaseema has **19.50 lakh acres** of horticulture.
Option (1) swaps the two shares; **21%** is horticulture's growth in 2024-25, not an area share.
xa: ⚠ The notes say **19.50 lakh acres** works out to **43%** of area — "the Survey prints 45%".
Rayalaseema also has about half of horticulture GVA (**₹76,458 cr**) and **71%** of micro-irrigation area.
AP horticulture: **46.43 lakh acres**, **406.38 lakh MT** (Survey 2025-26).

120.s: Which one of the following statements regarding coffee production in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh ranks third in India and all production comes from Araku Valley.
Andhra Pradesh ranks second in India and all production comes from Lambasingi.
Andhra Pradesh ranks fifth in India and coffee is mainly produced in Palasa.
Andhra Pradesh ranks fourth in India and 100% of its coffee comes from Araku Valley.
120.x: Andhra Pradesh ranks fourth in coffee production, and 100% of its coffee production comes from Araku Valley.
120.tq: Combine the rank with the specific production location.
xs: AP ranks **fourth** in coffee, and **100%** of it comes from **Araku Valley** — option **(4)**.
So "third", "second" and "fifth" are wrong; **Palasa** is the cashew "White Gold City", not a coffee area.
xa: **Coffee** is one of the **11 growth-engine crops** in **24 clusters**.
AP is **1st in productivity** of **oil palm, papaya, lime, cocoa, tomato, coconut** (2025-26).
AP is **India's largest fruit producer** (**15.6%** of national output).

120.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh ranks first in India in oil palm productivity.
2. Andhra Pradesh ranks second in India in mango production.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Both statements are correct, as keyed in APPSC Group 2 (2025): AP is 1st in oil palm productivity and 2nd in mango production. So 'only' options and 'neither' are wrong.
120.tq: Oil palm 1st; mango 2nd; coffee 4th.
xs: Both statements are correct — option **(3) Both 1 and 2**.
Statement 1: AP is **1st** in **oil palm productivity**.
Statement 2: AP is **2nd** in **mango** production — both keyed correct in **APPSC G2 2025**.
xa: AP leads India in oil palm **area, production and productivity**.
Other 2nd-rank crops: **sweet orange, turmeric** (APSES 2024-25).
Top three (DES, Mar 2026): **chilli, oil palm, tobacco**.

120.s:
With reference to oil palm production in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh ranks first in area, production and productivity of oil palm.
2. Oil palm occupies 2.49 lakh hectares in the 2025-26 analysis.
3. Andhra Pradesh accounts for 48% of India's oil-palm area.
4. Fresh fruit bunch production was 22.81 lakh metric tonnes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All four statements are correct for the 2025-26 analysis. Andhra Pradesh ranked first in all three oil-palm measures, with 2.49 lakh hectares, 48% of India's area and 22.81 lakh metric tonnes of fresh fruit bunches.
120.tq: Verify whether every item in a high-density numerical list is supported.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: AP is **1st in area, production, productivity** of oil palm.
Statements 2 and 3: **2.49 lakh ha**, i.e. **48%** of India's oil-palm area.
Statement 4: FFB output was **22.81 lakh MT** (with **CPO 4.07 lakh MT**).
xa: 2023-24 figures: **2.27 lakh ha**, **1.74 lakh farmers**, **17.63 lakh MT FFB**.
Main producers: **East Godavari** + **Kakinada**.
ICAR **IIOPR** is at **Pedavegi** (West Godavari region).

120.s:
Arrange the following initiatives in chronological order:
A. National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm
B. Oilseeds Technology Mission
C. National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm
Select the correct sequence.
120.x: The sequence is Oilseeds Technology Mission (1986), NMOOP (2014), and NMEO-OP (2021).
120.tq: Use the first-and-last years to establish the sequence.
xs: Order: **Oilseeds Technology Mission (1986)** → **NMOOP (2014)** → **NMEO-OP (2021)** — **B, C, A**, option **(2)**.
Oil palm was added to the oilseeds mission in **NMOOP 2014**.
xa: NMEO-OP aims to add **6.5 lakh ha** → **10 lakh ha by 2025-26**.
CPO targets: **11.20 lakh t by 2025-26**; **28 lakh t by 2029-30**.
A **Viability Price** is paid by DBT when prices crash.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm (NMEO-OP):
1. It is a centrally sponsored mission launched in 2021.
2. It aims to add 6.5 lakh ha to reach 10 lakh ha under oil palm by 2025-26.
3. Its crude palm oil target is 28 lakh tonnes by 2025-26.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NMEO-OP is centrally sponsored (2021) and targets adding 6.5 lakh ha to reach 10 lakh ha by 2025-26. Statement 3 is wrong: the CPO target is 11.20 lakh t by 2025-26; 28 lakh t is the target for 2029-30. So '1 and 2 only'; every other option includes statement 3.
120.tq: CPO: 11.20 lakh t by 2025-26, 28 lakh t by 2029-30.

120.s: India’s edible-oil import dependence declined from 63.2% in 2015–16 to what level in 2023–24?
120.x: Edible-oil import dependence fell to 56.25% in 2023–24 from 63.2% in 2015–16.
120.tq: Read the direction and exact endpoints of the trend.
xs: Edible-oil import dependence fell to **56.25%** in **2023-24** — option **(2)**.
It was **63.2%** in **2015-16** (Economic Survey 2025-26).
xa: NMEO-OP was launched in **2021** to raise domestic oil palm output.
CPO target: **28 lakh t by 2029-30**.
AP holds **48%** of India's oil palm area.

120.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the MIDH funding pattern?
o: 100% central funding for all States and institutions
60:40 for general States, 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States, and 100% central funding for NHB, CDB and CIH
50:50 for all States and 100% State funding for NHB, CDB and CIH
90:10 for general States, 60:40 for North-Eastern States, and 50% central funding for NHB
120.x: MIDH follows a 60:40 pattern in general States, 90:10 in North-Eastern and Himalayan States, and provides 100% central funding for NHB, CDB and CIH.
120.tq: Compare funding ratios by State category and institution.
xs: MIDH funding: **60:40** for general States, **90:10** for NE/Himalayan States, **100%** central for **NHB, CDB and CIH** — option **(2)**.
Options (1), (3) and (4) give wrong ratios.
xa: MIDH is centrally sponsored, launched **2014-15**.
Sub-schemes: **NHM**, **HMNEH**.
Non-MIDH districts get horticulture help under **RKVY** (**₹24.07 cr**, 2024-25).

120.s:
Which of the following are sub-schemes of MIDH?
1. National Horticulture Mission
2. Horticulture Mission for North East and Himalayan States
3. National Oilseeds Mission
4. National Food Security Mission
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: The National Horticulture Mission and the Horticulture Mission for North East and Himalayan States are sub-schemes of MIDH.
120.tq: Identify the schemes that belong to the same horticulture framework.
xs: **NHM** and **HMNEH** are MIDH sub-schemes — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct: MIDH's sub-schemes are the **National Horticulture Mission** and **Horticulture Mission for North East and Himalayan States**.
Statements 3 and 4 are wrong: oilseeds and food security fall outside MIDH's sub-schemes; oil palm has **NMEO-OP**.
xa: MIDH launched in **2014-15**; covers **fruits to bamboo**.
Funding: **60:40** general; **90:10** NE/Himalayan.

120.s: Andhra Pradesh has identified how many growth-engine crops in how many horticulture clusters?
120.x: Andhra Pradesh has identified 11 growth-engine crops across 24 clusters.
120.tq: Pair the count of crops with the count of clusters.
xs: AP has **11 growth-engine crops** in **24 clusters** — option **(1)**.
Crops include **banana, mango, chilli, oil palm, cocoa, dragon fruit, coffee**.
Option (2) swaps the numbers.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **17 growth engines**; **11 crops** for productivity; horticulture **22** growth-engine crops.
Horticulture GVA target: **₹3 lakh crore** by **2029-30**.
Strategy target: **30% growth** in agriculture + allied over **five years**.

120.s: The Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), with sub-schemes NHM and HMNEH, was launched in:
120.x: MIDH is a centrally sponsored scheme launched in 2014-15, subsuming NHM and HMNEH. 2005-06 was the launch of the earlier NHM, 2007-08 of RKVY, and 2021-22 of NMEO-OP's era, so those are wrong.
120.tq: MIDH 2014-15; 60:40 for general states.
xs: **MIDH** was launched in **2014-15** — option **(2)**.
It is centrally sponsored, with sub-schemes **NHM** and **HMNEH**.
**2021-22** is the year **NLM** was revised, not MIDH's launch.
xa: Funding: **60:40** general; **90:10** NE/Himalayan; **100%** central for NHB, CDB, CIH.
Coverage: **fruits to bamboo**.
⚠ **NLM** also began in **2014-15**.

120.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Kuppam — Indo-Israel Centre of Excellence for vegetables
2. Gundlapalli — Centre of Excellence for vegetables and spices
3. Nekarikallu mandal — Palnadu district
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
120.x: Kuppam is the Indo-Israel vegetable centre, while the new vegetable and spice centre is at Gundlapalli in Nekarikallu mandal of Palnadu district.
120.tq: Start with the sure location pair and verify the linked mandal and district.
xs: All three pairs are correctly matched — option **(4)**.
**Kuppam** (Chittoor) = Indo-Israel CoE for vegetables.
**Gundlapalli** = new CoE for **vegetables & spices**, in **Nekarikallu mandal**, **Palnadu district**.
xa: Gundlapalli CoE: **₹7.06 cr**; Israeli technology, disease-free planting material (PYQ 2025).
ICAR **IIOPR** = **Pedavegi**; **CTRI** = **Rajahmundry**.
**VBRI** = **Vijayawada**.

120.s: The ICAR Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research is located at
o: Pedavegi in the West Godavari region
120.x: The ICAR Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research is located at Pedavegi in the West Godavari region.
120.tq: Test institution-location recall with nearby horticultural locations as distractors.
xs: ICAR **IIOPR** is at **Pedavegi** (West Godavari region) — option **(1)**.
**Kuppam** has the vegetable CoE; **Venkataramannagudem** has the **Dr YSR Horticultural University**.
xa: ICAR **CTRI** = **Central Tobacco Research Institute, Rajahmundry**.
Exam angle: institute → place matching (**Pedavegi** vs Razole, Maruteru, Bapatla).
Oil palm main producers: **East Godavari** + **Kakinada**.

120.s: Which of the following correctly states the micro-irrigation targets for Andhra Pradesh?
o: 15% of GSA by 2030, 35% by 2047 and 50 lakh ha in five years
35% of GSA by 2030, 50% by 2047 and 15 lakh ha in five years
35% of GSA by 2025, 50% by 2030 and 15 lakh ha by 2047
50% of GSA by 2030, 35% by 2047 and 10 lakh ha in five years
120.x: The targets are 35% of GSA by 2030, 50% by 2047, and 15 lakh hectares within five years.
120.tq: Match each target with its correct time horizon.
xs: Targets: **35% of GSA by 2030**, **50% by 2047**, **15 lakh ha** in five years — option **(2)**.
The other options swap or misdate these numbers.
xa: APMIP covers **37.90 lakh acres** so far.
Rayalaseema's shift to horticulture depends on **drip irrigation**.

120.s:
With reference to the Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project (APMIP), consider the following statements:
1. It has been in operation since 2003-04.
2. It has covered 37.90 lakh acres.
3. It has benefited 13.49 lakh farmers.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
APMIP runs since **2003-04**, covers **37.90 lakh acres** and **13.49 lakh farmers**.
**Rayalaseema** = **71%** of coverage.

Now under **RKVY-PDMC**.

120.s: The target for post-harvest units in Andhra Pradesh during 2025–26 is:

Logistics plan: cost from **~14% to 8-9% of GSDP**.

120.s: The value-chain study referred to six crops. Which one of the following was NOT among them?
120.x: The six crops were mango, banana, tomato, pomegranate, sweet lime and papaya. Oil palm was not included in that study.

xs: **Oil palm** was not in the six-crop value-chain study — option **(3)**.
The six crops: **mango, banana, tomato, pomegranate, sweet lime, papaya** (**4 May 2026**).
xa: The logistics plan aims to cut cost from **~14% to 8-9% of GSDP**.
Target: **1,030** post-harvest units (2025-26).
Horticulture rebounded **21%** in 2024-25.

120.s: Operation Greens, modelled on Operation Flood, covers which crops?
120.x: Operation Greens is the TOP scheme: tomato, onion, potato, modelled on Operation Flood. Tea/coffee/rubber are plantation crops; turmeric/chilli/pepper are spices; mango/banana/papaya are among AP's value-chain study crops, not Operation Greens.
120.tq: TOP = Tomato, Onion, Potato.
xs: **Operation Greens** covers **Tomato, Onion, Potato (TOP)** — option **(2)**.

Mango, banana and papaya are AP's **value-chain study** crops, not Operation Greens.

AP is **1st in productivity** of **tomato** (2025-26).

120.s: Which allied-sector output of Andhra Pradesh retained the first national rank in each of the years 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25?
120.x: Eggs ranked first in all three years. The egg rank is noted as having never changed.

xs: Egg rank is the **only rank never moved**; AP was 1st in **2018-19** too.
**Meat** moved between **4th** and **5th**; **milk** between **5th** and **7th**.

Eggs are counted in **crore numbers**.

120.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the change in Andhra Pradesh's allied-sector outputs in 2023-24?
o: Milk production remained unchanged, while eggs and meat declined.
All three outputs increased, with meat showing the largest increase.
All three outputs fell, and milk recorded the largest decline of 9.41%.
Only egg production fell, while milk and meat increased.
120.x: Egg, meat and milk outputs all fell in 2023-24; milk recorded the largest decline, at 9.41%.
120.tq: Test the trend and the precise percentage together.
xs: In 2023-24 **all three outputs fell**, and **milk** fell most (**-9.41%**) — option **(3)**.
Milk held up through **crossbred cattle and graded Murrah buffaloes**.
xa: 2023-24 ranks: eggs **1st**, meat **5th**, milk **7th**.
2024-25: meat back to **4th** (**11.37 lakh MT**); milk **7th** (**139.46 lakh MT**).

120.s: Milk production in Andhra Pradesh was sustained comparatively because of:
o: crossbred cattle and graded Murrah buffaloes
120.x: Milk production was supported by crossbred cattle and graded Murrah buffaloes.
120.tq: Link the stated production outcome with its identified cause.
xs: Milk held up because of **crossbred cattle and graded Murrah buffaloes** — option **(2)**.
They offset the fall in headcount.
xa: AP's milk fell **9.41%** in 2023-24 — the largest fall of the three outputs.
Local breeds: **Ongole, Punganur** cattle; **Godavari** buffalo.

120.s: India produced 239.30 MT of milk in 2023-24, with per capita availability of:
120.x: India's per capita milk availability was 471 grams per day in 2023-24.
120.tq: Associate a national production figure with its per capita measure.
xs: India's per capita milk availability is **471 g/day** — option **(1)**.
National milk output was **239.30 MT** in 2023-24.
xa: Eggs: India **2nd** in the world, **142.77 billion** eggs; **103 eggs/year** per capita.
Meat: **10.25 MT**, **4th** in the world.
AP milk: **7th** with **139.46 lakh MT** (2024-25).

120.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's livestock-product position in 2023-24:
1. India ranks second in the world in egg production, with about 142.77 billion eggs.
2. Per capita egg availability in India is about 103 eggs per year.
3. India ranks first in the world in meat production.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is correct: India is 2nd in world egg production with 142.77 billion eggs. Statement 2 is correct: per capita availability is 103 eggs a year. Statement 3 is wrong: India's meat output (10.25 MT) is 4th in the world, not 1st. Hence '1 only' misses statement 2, and the options containing 3 are wrong.
120.tq: India: eggs 2nd, meat 4th in the world; 103 eggs per head per year.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: India is **2nd** in egg production with **142.77 billion** eggs.
Statement 2: per capita **103 eggs/year**.
Statement 3 is wrong: India's meat (**10.25 MT**) is **4th** in the world.
xa: Milk: **239.30 MT**; **471 g/day** per capita.
India has the **world's largest livestock population**.
AP is **1st** in eggs (**2,739 crore**, 2024-25).

120.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding Andhra Pradesh's livestock products?
120.x: The first option is incorrect because 2,739 crore eggs refers to egg production, not meat. Andhra Pradesh ranked fourth in meat production with 11.37 lakh tonnes.
120.tq: Find the swapped product-rank-output combination.
xs: "**Meat — First rank — 2,739 crore eggs**" is wrong — option **(1)**.
**2,739 crore** is the **egg** output, where AP is **1st**.
**Meat** is **4th** with **11.37 lakh MT**; **milk** is **7th** with **139.46 lakh MT** (2024-25).
xa: 2023-24: eggs **1st** (2,548.74 crore), meat **5th** (10.68 lakh MT), milk **7th**.
Egg rank never moved; AP **1st in 2018-19** too.

120.s: The correct unit for Andhra Pradesh's egg production figure of 2,548.74 in the 2023–24 assessment is:
120.x: The correct unit is crore eggs; the printing of lakh eggs is an erroneous unit representation.
120.tq: Resolve the unit trap by checking whether the number refers to eggs or tonnes.
xs: The correct unit for **2,548.74** is **crore eggs** — option **(3)**.
⚠ APSES 2024-25 printed "**2548.74 lakh eggs**" — a misprint; eggs are counted in **crore numbers**.
xa: India: **142.77 billion** eggs (2023-24), **2nd** in the world.

120.s: The 20th Livestock Census was conducted in:
120.x: The 20th Livestock Census was conducted in 2019.
120.tq: Recall the census year directly.
xs: The **20th Livestock Census** was held in **2019** — option **(3)**.
**2012** is the earlier census against which changes are measured.
xa: It counted **303.76 million** bovines, **74.26 million** sheep, **148.88 million** goats, **9.06 million** pigs.
**21st Livestock Census**: Nov **2024** to Feb **2025**; **1.35 crore** households in AP.
AP total livestock (2019): **340.60 lakh**.

120.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with Andhra Pradesh's 2019 Livestock Census State rank?
120.x: Cattle ranked fourteenth in Andhra Pradesh, not eleventh. Goat ranked eleventh; buffalo ranked sixth, while sheep and poultry ranked second.
120.tq: Detect the swapped rank between closely listed animal categories.
xs: "**Cattle — eleventh**" is wrong: cattle is **14th** — option **(3)**.
**Goat** is the one ranked **11th**.
**Sheep** and **poultry** are **2nd**; **buffalo** is **6th** — all correct.
xa: ⚠ Trap: AP **2nd** in sheep and poultry; cattle only **14th**.

120.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with a breed associated with Andhra Pradesh?
120.x: Aseel is a poultry breed, not a buffalo breed. Ongole is cattle, Godavari is buffalo and Nellore is sheep.
120.tq: Find the wrong species association in a breed list.
xs: "**Aseel — buffalo**" is wrong: **Aseel** is a **poultry** breed — option **(4)**.
**Ongole** = cattle, **Nellore** = sheep, **Godavari** = buffalo — all correctly matched.
xa: **Punganur** is another AP **cattle** breed.
AP is **2nd** in India in **sheep** and **poultry** (2019 Census).
**58** Local Breed Conservation Cow Farms in AP.

120.s:
Arrange the following Andhra Pradesh livestock species in descending order of their population according to the 2019 Census:
A. Cattle
B. Poultry
C. Sheep
D. Buffalo
120.x: The descending order is poultry (1,078.63 lakh), sheep (176.27 lakh), buffalo (62.19 lakh) and cattle (46.00 lakh).
120.tq: Arrange by magnitude, beginning with the clearly largest population.
xs: Descending order: **Poultry, Sheep, Buffalo, Cattle** — **B, C, D, A**, option **(1)**.
Poultry **1,078.63 lakh** > sheep **176.27 lakh** > buffalo **62.19 lakh** > cattle **46.00 lakh**.
xa: AP ranks: poultry and sheep **2nd**, buffalo **6th**, cattle **14th**.
National poultry: **851.81 million** (+16.81%).

120.s: Which institution is located at Vijayawada?
120.x: The Veterinary Biological Research Institute (VBRI) is located at Vijayawada.
120.tq: Use institution–location matching.
xs: The **Veterinary Biological Research Institute (VBRI)** is at **Vijayawada** — option **(1)**.
**Sri Venkateswara Veterinary University** is at **Tirupati**; NLM semen labs are at **Kurnool** and **Visakhapatnam**.
xa: VBRI also runs **AP Animal Feed Act** training jointly with **SMILE**.
ICAR-**CTRI** = **Rajahmundry**; ICAR-**IIOPR** = **Pedavegi**.

120.s: Under the relaunched Pashu Kisan Credit Card scheme, collateral-free credit is available up to:
120.x: The Pashu Kisan Credit Card provides up to ₹1.60 lakh without collateral at 7%. Credit up to ₹3 lakh may be available under bank norms.
120.tq: Distinguish the collateral-free ceiling from the broader bank-norm ceiling.
xs: PKCC gives up to **₹1.60 lakh without collateral at 7%** — option **(1)**.
Up to **₹3 lakh** is possible, but under **bank norms**, not collateral-free; **4%** is the effective rate after subvention.
xa: Relaunched in **Apr 2026** (21 Apr 2026).
Repay within a year → **3%** subvention → effective **4%**.
Earlier round: **2,02,052** cards sanctioned of **2,82,293** applications.

120.s: A livestock borrower under PKCC who repays within one year effectively pays what interest rate after subvention?
120.x: Timely repayment earns a 3% subvention on the 7% rate, resulting in an effective rate of 4%.
120.tq: Apply the interest-subvention calculation to the stated rates.
xs: Effective rate is **4%** — option **(2)**.
PKCC credit is at **7%**; repaying within a year earns **3%** subvention.
xa: Collateral-free limit: **₹1.60 lakh**; up to **₹3 lakh** under bank norms.
Eligible: **owners, lessees, SHG members**.
⚠ Crop loans: **Vaddi Leni Runalu** gives **4%** subvention up to ₹1 lakh.

120.s: Which of the following correctly represents the premium-sharing ratio under Pasu Bhima Padhakam for BPL, SC and ST beneficiaries?
120.x: For BPL, SC and ST beneficiaries, the Centre, State and beneficiary shares are 40:40:20.
120.tq: Separate the premium ratio for priority groups from the APL ratio.
xs: BPL/SC/ST premium share is **40:40:20** (Centre:State:beneficiary) — option **(3)**.
**25:25:50** is the **APL** share, so (2) is wrong.
xa: Claims are settled within **15 days**.
NLM livestock insurance release: **₹1,180.91 lakh** (2023-24).

120.s: The Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) is administered by:
120.x: AHIDF is run by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD).
120.tq: Use the ‘who runs the fund’ test to avoid institutional swaps.
xs: **AHIDF** is run by **DAHD** — option **(2)**.
Fund size: **₹29,110.25 crore**.
xa: It funds **dairy & meat processing**, **feed plants**, breed farms, **waste-to-wealth**, **vaccine plants**.
⚠ **NLM** is a separate scheme (**2014-15**, revised **2021-22**).

120.s: Which one of the following is NOT an activity funded by AHIDF?
120.x: AHIDF funds dairy and meat processing, feed plants, breed farms, waste-to-wealth projects and vaccine plants; irrigation canals are outside its stated scope.
120.tq: Find the activity outside the livestock infrastructure list.
xs: **Irrigation canals** are not funded by AHIDF — option **(4)**.
AHIDF funds **dairy & meat processing**, **feed plants**, breed farms, waste-to-wealth and **vaccine plants**.
xa: AHIDF: **₹29,110.25 crore**, run by **DAHD**.
Irrigation gets **₹14,277 crore** in AP's agri budget 2026-27.

120.s: The tie-up between the Andhra Pradesh Dairy Development Cooperative Federation and Amul was made in:
120.x: The AP Dairy Development Cooperative Federation entered into the Amul-AP tie-up in 2020.
120.tq: Direct recall of the year associated with an institutional arrangement.
xs: The **APDDCF–Amul** tie-up was made in **2020** — option **(3)**.
Under **Paala Velluva**, **Amul** procures milk from women's dairy units.
xa: **Chittoor** holds the top position in AP's dairy sector (**1 Aug 2026**).
Livestock units for women: **2,15,626** grounded.

120.s: Which district holds the top position in Andhra Pradesh’s dairy sector?
120.x: Chittoor holds the top position in Andhra Pradesh’s dairy sector.

**Kuppam** (Chittoor) has the vegetable CoE.
Amul-AP tie-up: **2020**.

120.s: Paala Velluva is associated with:
o: Sheep and goat units for women, with NLM procuring wool
Mobile veterinary clinics for dairy cooperatives
Dairy units for women, with Amul procuring milk
120.x: Paala Velluva provides dairy units for women, and Amul is associated with milk procurement under the initiative.

**Sheep and goat units** are **Jeeva Kranthi**; mobile vet clinics are **Sanchara Pasu Arogya Seva**.
xa: Amul-AP tie-up with **APDDCF**: **2020**.
**2,15,626** livestock units for women grounded.
Women do most of the livestock work.

120.s: Which scheme is associated with sheep and goat units?
120.x: Jeeva Kranthi is associated with sheep and goat units, whereas Paala Velluva concerns dairy units for women.
120.tq: Separate the two similar livelihood initiatives by the livestock involved.
xs: **Jeeva Kranthi** provides **sheep/goat units** — option **(1)**.
**Paala Velluva** = dairy units; **Pasu Bhima Padhakam** = livestock insurance.
xa: AP is **2nd** in sheep (**176.27 lakh**).
Goat population rose **22.82%** (AP **11th**).
**Nellore** sheep is an AP breed.

120.s: The National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP) is correctly described by which of the following?
o: It is a 100% centrally funded programme launched in September 2019 to eradicate FMD by 2030.
It is a 75% subsidised programme launched in 2014 to insure livestock.
It is a centrally sponsored programme launched in 2025 to promote feed plants.
It is a State-funded programme launched in 2021 for dairy procurement.
120.x: NADCP is 100% centrally funded, was launched in September 2019, and aims to eradicate foot-and-mouth disease by 2030.
120.tq: Match funding pattern, launch date and disease-control target.
xs: **NADCP** is **100% central**, launched **Sept 2019**, aiming at **FMD eradication by 2030** — option **(1)**.
It is not a State-funded or insurance scheme; insurance is under **Pasu Bhima Padhakam**.
xa: NADCP is now merged into **LHDCP**.
**Pashu Aadhaar** = **12-digit** ear-tag ID.
**1962 app** replaced **e-Gopala**.

120.s: NADCP has now been merged into:
120.x: NADCP has been merged into the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP).
120.tq: Distinguish the disease-control umbrella programme from financing missions.
xs: NADCP has been merged into **LHDCP** — option **(2)**.
**AHIDF** is an infrastructure fund; **NLM** a livestock mission; **APMIP** micro-irrigation.
xa: NADCP: **100% central**, **Sept 2019**, **FMD eradication by 2030**.
**Pashu Aadhaar**: **12-digit** ear-tag ID.

120.s: Pashu Aadhaar is:
o: A 12-digit insurance policy number for dairy farmers
A 12-digit ear-tag identification number for animals
A 10-digit bank account number for livestock credit
120.x: Pashu Aadhaar is a 12-digit identification number attached through an ear tag to livestock.
120.tq: Discriminate between an animal identifier and financial or insurance identifiers.
xs: **Pashu Aadhaar** is a **12-digit ear-tag** ID for animals — option **(2)**.
It identifies the animal, not a policy, bank account or hospital.
xa: The **1962 app** replaced **e-Gopala**.
NADCP aims at **FMD eradication by 2030**.

120.s: Which application replaced e-Gopala?
120.x: The 1962 app replaced e-Gopala for livestock-related services.
120.tq: Recall the replacement relationship between the two applications.
xs: The **1962 app** replaced **e-Gopala** — option **(1)**.
**Pashu Aadhaar** is the **12-digit** ear-tag ID, not an app replacing e-Gopala.
xa: NADCP: **100% central**, **Sept 2019**; merged into **LHDCP**.
Doorstep veterinary care comes via **Animal Husbandry Assistants** at RSKs.

120.s: Andhra Pradesh occupies which position in cultured-shrimp production?
o: A minor producer with no national significance
120.x: Andhra Pradesh is India's largest shrimp producer, accounting for about 75% of India's cultured-shrimp exports (2025-26). It is not second, third or a minor producer.
120.tq: Test the rank claim directly while distinguishing it from the export-share figure.
xs: AP is the **largest** shrimp producer — option **(1)**.
AP gives **~75% of India's cultured-shrimp exports** (2025-26).
xa: AP produces **~29-30% of India's fish**.
⚠ **31%** of India's **shrimp** exports (2024-25) vs **75%** of **cultured** shrimp exports.
**Visakhapatnam** RGCA centre for **black tiger shrimp** brood.

120.s: The coastline of Andhra Pradesh according to APSES 2025-26 is:
120.x: Andhra Pradesh has a coastline of 1,053 km according to APSES 2025-26. The older figure cited was 974 km.
120.tq: Distinguish the latest official figure from the older commonly cited figure.
xs: AP's coastline is **1,053 km** (APSES 2025-26) — option **(3)**.
**974 km** is the older figure.
xa: **Marine fishing ban**: **61 days**, **15 April-14 June**.
**10 fishing harbours** (₹3,699.09 cr) under **PMMSY**.

120.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Aquaculture Development Authority was established under the:
120.x: APSADA operates under the APSADA Act, 2020.
120.tq: Distinguish the state APSADA law from the separate coastal aquaculture law of 2005.
xs: APSADA works under the **APSADA Act, 2020** — option **(3)**.
The **CAA Act, 2005** is the central law for coastal farms.
xa: Related 2020 laws: **AP Feed (Quality Control) Act**; **Aquaculture Seed (QC) Amendment Act**.
APSADA licenses **freshwater** farms via **e-Matsyakar**.

120.s: Freshwater aquaculture in Andhra Pradesh is licensed through:
o: Rythu Seva Kendras under the Fisheries University Act
120.x: APSADA licenses freshwater aquaculture through the e-Matsyakar system.
120.tq: Identify the authority and digital mechanism appropriate to the activity described.
xs: Freshwater farms are licensed via **e-Matsyakar** under **APSADA** — option **(3)**.
**MPEDA** is the export body; coastal farms come under the **CAA Act** (**2005**).
xa: APSADA Act: **2020**.
⚠ Trap: freshwater → **APSADA (2020)**; within **2 km** of HTL → **CAA (2005)**.

120.s: Coastal aquaculture farms located within 2 km of the High Tide Line are regulated by the:
o: Fisheries University under the AP Fisheries University Act
Marine Products Export Development Authority under the MPEDA Act
Coastal Aquaculture Authority under the Coastal Aquaculture Authority Act, 2005
Andhra Pradesh State Aquaculture Development Authority under the APSADA Act, 2020
120.x: Coastal farms within 2 km of the High Tide Line are regulated by the Coastal Aquaculture Authority under the CAA Act, 2005.
120.tq: Use the location-based jurisdiction distinction between freshwater and coastal aquaculture.
xs: Coastal farms within **2 km** of the **High Tide Line** come under the **Coastal Aquaculture Authority** (CAA Act, **2005**) — option **(3)**.
**APSADA (2020)** licenses **freshwater** farms; **MPEDA** handles exports.
xa: CAA Act is a **GoI** law.
APSADA uses the **e-Matsyakar** portal.

120.s: Which of the following correctly states the aqua-power tariff arrangement in Andhra Pradesh?
o: ₹6.89 per unit for notified zones and ₹1.50 per unit outside them
₹1.50 per unit for all farms, irrespective of size and location
₹3.85 per unit for farms up to 10 acres and ₹6.89 per unit for all larger farms
₹1.50 per unit for farms up to 10 acres inside notified aqua zones and ₹3.85 per unit for bigger farms or farms outside such zones
120.x: The tariff is ₹1.50 per unit for farms up to 10 acres inside notified aqua zones and ₹3.85 per unit for bigger farms or farms outside those zones.
120.tq: Split the tariff by both farm size and location instead of treating it as a universal rate.
xs: **₹1.50/unit** for farms **up to 10 acres inside notified aqua zones**; **₹3.85/unit** for bigger farms or those outside — option **(4)**.
**₹6.89** was the earlier rate, not the current one.
xa: The **10-acre** cap was lifted (**G.O. 57**, Aug 2026).
Coverage: **54,033** connections; subsidy ~**₹942 cr** a year.

120.s: By the end of 2018-19, Andhra Pradesh’s share in India’s seafood export value was approximately:
120.x: Andhra Pradesh accounted for 36% of India’s seafood export value by the end of 2018-19. The later figures of 31% and 75% refer specifically to shrimp exports and cultured shrimp exports respectively.
120.tq: Distinguish the base of comparison—total seafood value versus shrimp-specific shares.
xs: AP had **36%** of India's seafood export **value** by **2018-19** — option **(3)**.
**31%** is AP's share of **shrimp** exports and **75%** of **cultured shrimp** exports — different bases.
xa: **~29-30%** is AP's share of India's **fish** output.
⚠ Trap: check the base — seafood, shrimp, or cultured shrimp.
India's seafood exports 2025-26: **₹73,890 crore**.

120.s: Which of the following correctly describes the later seafood-export shares associated with Andhra Pradesh?
o: 75% of India’s shrimp exports and 31% of cultured shrimp exports
31% of India’s total seafood exports and 75% of marine exports
31% of India’s shrimp exports and 75% of cultured shrimp exports
36% of shrimp exports and 60% of cultured shrimp exports
120.x: The later figures are 31% of India’s shrimp exports and 75% of India’s cultured shrimp exports. These percentages do not refer to all seafood exports.
120.tq: Discriminate between similar percentages by identifying the precise export base.
xs: Later shares: **31% of India's shrimp exports** (2024-25) and **75% of cultured shrimp exports** (2025-26) — option **(3)**.
Option (1) swaps them; **36%** is all-seafood export value (2018-19).
xa: ⚠ Trap: the base is shrimp or cultured shrimp, not all seafood.
AP is the **largest shrimp producer**.

120.s: The Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) functions as:
o: A regulatory body under the Ministry of Agriculture
The apex export body under the Ministry of Commerce
A financial institution under the Ministry of Finance
A research body under the Ministry of Environment
120.x: MPEDA is the apex export body under the Ministry of Commerce for marine products. Its arms include RGCA, NETFISH and NaCSA.
120.tq: Apply the ‘which ministry or authority?’ method to distinguish the institutional mandate.
xs: **MPEDA** is the **apex export body** under the **Ministry of Commerce** — option **(2)**.
Its arms: **RGCA**, **NETFISH**, **NaCSA**.
xa: MPEDA has proposed an **Aquatic Quarantine Facility** (Aug 2026).

120.s: Which country was the second-largest destination for India’s seafood exports in 2025-26?
120.x: China was the second-largest destination in 2025-26, with exports increasing by 20.1% by volume.
120.tq: Test the market ranking directly and avoid confusing it with the country on which exporters seek to reduce dependence.
xs: **China** was the **2nd largest** destination in 2025-26 — option **(3)**.
Exports to China rose **20.1%** by volume.
xa: EU up **35.2%**; South-East Asia up **28.2%**.
Farmers want more FTAs to **reduce dependence on the USA**.
Record export value: **₹73,890 crore** (2025-26).

120.s: India’s first Mega Aqua Food Park was operationalised at:
120.x: The Godavari Mega Aqua Food Park at Tundurru in West Godavari was India’s first operational Mega Aqua Food Park.
120.tq: Link the project title, location and district to avoid confusing it with other aqua infrastructure.
xs: India's first **Mega Aqua Food Park** is at **Tundurru** (**West Godavari**) — option **(1)**.
It is the **Godavari Mega Aqua Food Park**.
xa: The **Godavari delta** is AP's **aquaculture hub**.
PMMSY results include **12 Integrated Aquaparks**.

120.s: The 10 fishing harbours in Andhra Pradesh, involving an outlay of ₹3,699.09 crore, are being implemented under:
120.x: The 10 fishing harbours are under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme component of PMMSY, not Sagarmala. The outlay is ₹3,699.09 crore.
120.tq: Identify the correct programme and reject the nearby infrastructure-scheme trap.
xs: The **10 fishing harbours** (**₹3,699.09 cr**) are under **CSS-PMMSY** — option **(4)**.
⚠ They are **not under Sagarmala**.
xa: Modernisation of **Visakhapatnam** (**₹178.51 cr**); upgrade of **Kakinada** (**₹58.95 cr**).
**6 Fish Landing Centres** (**₹126.91 cr**) also under PMMSY.

120.s: Under PMMSY, the total subsidy is what for the general category and women/SC/ST beneficiaries respectively?
120.x: The subsidy is 40% for the general category and 60% for women, SC and ST beneficiaries. The GoI-GoAP shares are 24%-16% and 36%-24% respectively.
120.tq: Read the categories in the same order as the question and do not reverse the percentage comparison.
xs: PMMSY subsidy is **40%** general and **60%** for **women/SC/ST** — option **(4)**.
xa: PMMSY: **2020**, **₹20,050 crore** (Blue Revolution).
**100 Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages**.

120.s: The implementation period and outlay of PM-MKSSY are:
120.x: PM-MKSSY covers FY 2023-24 to 2026-27 and has an outlay of ₹6,000 crore.
120.tq: Pair the scheme period with its own outlay rather than the larger PMMSY investment.
xs: **PM-MKSSY** runs **FY 2023-24 to 2026-27** with **₹6,000 crore** — option **(2)**.
**₹20,050 crore** is PMMSY; **₹7,522 cr** is FIDF; **₹2,761.80 cr** is the 2026-27 budget.
xa: PM-MKSSY = **PM Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana**, a **central sector sub-scheme** of PMMSY.
**National Fisheries Digital Platform**: **30.60 lakh** stakeholders registered.

120.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated feature of PM-MKSSY?
o: Compulsory replacement of all fishing boats with trawlers
Institutional credit for the fisheries sector
120.x: PM-MKSSY supports institutional credit, aquaculture insurance and supply-chain traceability. Compulsory replacement of all boats with trawlers is not a stated feature.
120.tq: Find the extreme and unsupported programme feature among the genuine objectives.
xs: **Compulsory replacement of all fishing boats with trawlers** is not a PM-MKSSY feature — option **(1)**.
PM-MKSSY works through **institutional credit**, **aquaculture insurance** and **supply-chain traceability**.
xa: It is a **central sector sub-scheme** of PMMSY; outlay **₹6,000 crore**.
**National Fisheries Digital Platform**: **30.60 lakh** stakeholders.
GEF-FAO aquaculture project: **5 years** from **2025**.

120.s: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) was launched in:
120.x: PMMSY was launched in 2020 with ₹20,050 crore (Blue Revolution). ₹7,522 crore is the FIDF corpus and ₹6,000 crore the outlay of PM-MKSSY (2023-24 to 2026-27); option D is unrelated.
120.tq: PMMSY 2020 ₹20,050 cr; PM-MKSSY ₹6,000 cr.
xs: **PMMSY** was launched in **2020** with **₹20,050 crore** — option **(2)**.
**₹7,522 crore** is the **FIDF** corpus; **₹6,000 crore** is **PM-MKSSY** (2023-24 to 2026-27).
xa: PMMSY is the **Blue Revolution** scheme; centrally sponsored.
Subsidy: **40%** general, **60%** women/SC/ST.
PM-MKSSY is a **central sector sub-scheme** of PMMSY.

120.s: The marine fishing ban in Andhra Pradesh is imposed for how many days, generally from 15 April to 14 June?
120.x: The marine fishing ban lasts 61 days, covering the breeding season from 15 April to 14 June.
120.tq: Use the exact duration and dates as a linked numerical fact.
xs: The marine fishing ban lasts **61 days**, **15 April-14 June** — option **(2)**.
It covers the fish **breeding season**.
xa: **KCC** extended to fishers since **2018-19**.

120.s: The ban-period relief per fishing family from 2024-25 was:
120.x: The relief was ₹4,000 before 2019-20, ₹10,000 from 2019-20 and ₹20,000 from 2024-25.
120.tq: Arrange the changing benefit levels chronologically and identify the latest amount.
xs: Ban-period relief from **2024-25** is **₹20,000** per family — option **(4)**.
xa: 2019-20 APPSC key: **1,17,053** fishermen.
Ban: **61 days**, **15 April-14 June**.
⚠ Ex-gratia for deceased fishermen is **₹10 lakh** — do not confuse with ₹10,000 relief.

120.s: The ex-gratia assistance provided to the family of a deceased fisherman in Andhra Pradesh is:
120.x: Families of deceased fishermen receive ex-gratia assistance of ₹10 lakh. In 2024-25, ₹315 lakh was paid to 63 families.
120.tq: Distinguish individual family assistance from the aggregate amount paid to all beneficiaries.
xs: Ex-gratia for a deceased fisherman's family is **₹10 lakh** — option **(3)**.
In 2024-25, **₹315 lakh** went to **63** families.
xa: **Diesel subsidy** is given on fishing boats.
**KCC** for fishers since **2018-19**.

120.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the significance of agriculture in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Agriculture and allied activities contributed 33% of GVA in 2025–26.
2. Agriculture supports approximately 60% of the State's population.
3. Agriculture and allied activities contributed less than one-fifth of GVA in 2025–26.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because agriculture and allied activities contributed 33% of GVA, not less than one-fifth.
120.tq: Find the reversed share statement before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: agriculture + allied = **33%** of GVA (2025-26).
Statement 2: agriculture supports **60%** of AP's population.
Statement 3 is wrong: **33%** is about one-third, not less than one-fifth.
xa: Agriculture Budget **2026-27**: **₹53,753 crore**.
Credit plan 2025-26: **₹2,96,764 crore** = **97%** of target.
Horticulture is the fastest-growing farm segment (about **10%** a year).

120.s: Among the following Kharif crops, the highest MSP for 2026–27 was fixed for:
120.x: Sesamum had the highest MSP among the listed crops at ₹10,346 per quintal.
120.tq: Apply the comparison-table method by identifying the maximum value.
xs: **Sesamum** has the highest kharif MSP for 2026-27: **Rs 10,346/qtl** — option **(2)**.
Others: groundnut **Rs 7,517**, paddy **Rs 2,441**, maize **Rs 2,410**.
xa: Swarna Andhra strategy expands area under **sunflower, sesamum and millets**.
**Groundnut** is the main crop of **Anantapuramu**.

120.s: Which one of the following is a major criticism associated with the dominance of paddy cultivation in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It occupies the largest area, affects indigenous crops and is a major source of methane.
It is unsuitable for all irrigated regions of the State.
It completely eliminates the need for procurement support.
It occupies the smallest cultivated area and reduces methane emissions.
120.x: Paddy occupies the largest area, often at the cost of indigenous crops, and is a major source of methane. Crop diversification with procurement support has therefore been advocated.
120.tq: Select the option containing the complete cause-and-policy linkage rather than an absolute claim.
xs: Paddy occupies the **largest area**, at the cost of **indigenous crops**, and is a major **methane** source — option **(1)**.
Experts want **crop diversification** with **procurement support** (**26 Jul 2026**).
xa: Paddy: **20.97 lakh ha**, about **56%** of food-grain area (2024-25).
Paddy output 2024-25: **127.15 lakh t**.
El Nino plan: shift from paddy to **red gram, black gram, castor**.

120.s: Which of the following was NOT included in the El Nino action plan for Andhra Pradesh in July 2026?
o: A shift from paddy to red gram, black gram and castor
A compulsory shift from all crops to sugarcane
One Mobile Rythu Bazaar per district
A control room issuing advisories through Rythu Seva Kendras
120.x: The plan included a control room, advisories through Rythu Seva Kendras, crop shifts to red gram, black gram and castor, and one Mobile Rythu Bazaar per district. A compulsory shift to sugarcane was not part of the plan.
120.tq: Find the option that introduces an unrelated and absolute policy measure.
xs: A **compulsory shift to sugarcane** was not in the El Nino plan — option **(2)**.
The plan had a **control room** advising via **RSKs**, a shift from paddy to **red gram, black gram, castor**, and **One Mobile Rythu Bazaar per district**.
xa: Kharif 2026: **653 of 685** mandals affected; opposition sought a drought emergency.
All **28 districts** were in rainfall deficit.
PMDS in **Kurnool** on **92,000 acres** due to El Nino.

120.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's aquaculture sector:
1. It supports more than five lakh families.
2. It is regarded as the core of the State's Blue Economy.
3. Its markets are completely independent of foreign demand.
4. High input and electricity costs are among the concerns associated with the sector.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: More than five lakh families depend on aquaculture, which is central to the Blue Economy, and high input and electricity costs are concerns. Statement 3 is false because the sector has dependence on foreign markets, including the US market.
120.tq: Identify the false absolute statement while retaining the three sectoral facts.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct — option **(2)**.
Statements 1 and 2: more than **5 lakh families** depend on aquaculture, the core of AP's **Blue Economy**.
Statement 4: **high input and electricity costs** are a concern.
Statement 3 is wrong: the sector depends on the **US market**.
xa: Record seafood exports: **₹73,890 cr** (2025-26).
Aqua power tariff: **₹1.50/unit** inside notified aqua zones.
AP = **~75%** of India's cultured-shrimp exports.

121.s:
Consider the following pairs (Agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh — Districts covered):
1. Godavari Zone — East Godavari and West Godavari
2. Krishna Zone — Krishna, Guntur and Prakasam
3. Southern Zone — Chittoor, YSR Kadapa and Kurnool
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
121.x: Pair 1 is correct: the Godavari Zone covers East and West Godavari. Pair 2 is correct: the Krishna Zone covers Krishna, Guntur and Prakasam. Pair 3 is wrong: the Southern Zone covers Chittoor, YSR Kadapa and SPS Nellore; Kurnool belongs to the Scarce Rainfall Zone. Hence '1 only' is incomplete, '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include pair 3; the answer is '1 and 2 only'.
121.tq: Southern Zone = Chittoor, Kadapa, Nellore (PYQ 2023: Southern → Nellore); Kurnool and Anantapuramu are Scarce Rainfall.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2)**.
Pair 1: **Godavari** = **East and West Godavari**.
Pair 2: **Krishna** = **Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam**.
Pair 3 is wrong: Southern = **Chittoor, YSR Kadapa, SPS Nellore**; **Kurnool** is in the **Scarce Rainfall** zone.
xa: PYQ **2023** pair: Southern Zone → **Nellore**.
Scarce Rainfall = **Kurnool, Anantapuramu**.
Godavari RARS = **Maruteru**; Krishna RARS = **Lam (Guntur)**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's agro-climatic zone listing:
1. The zones continue to be listed against the 13 old districts.
2. They have been fully re-cut according to the April 2022 district reorganisation.
3. Andhra Pradesh now has 28 districts according to the cited current reference.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
121.x: The zones remain listed against the 13 old districts and have not been re-cut after the April 2022 reorganisation. The cited current reference states that Andhra Pradesh has 28 districts; therefore statement 2 is false.
121.tq: Spot the reversed claim about whether an old classification was updated.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: zones are still listed against the **13 old districts**.
Statement 2 is wrong: they were **not re-cut** for the **April 2022** reorganisation.
Statement 3: AP now has **28 districts** (Aug 2026).
xa: The Survey lists **pre-2022** districts for each zone.
⚠ Agro-climatic zones ≠ the **six** public employment zones under **Art. 371-D**.

121.s: The High Altitude and Tribal Areas agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh includes mainly the hill and tribal parts of which districts?
o: Chittoor, SPS Nellore and West Godavari
121.x: The High Altitude and Tribal Areas zone consists of the hill and tribal parts of Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam and East Godavari.
121.tq: Apply the location-based classification rather than matching entire districts indiscriminately.
xs: The **High Altitude & Tribal Areas** zone covers hill/tribal parts of **Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam and East Godavari** — option **(1)**.
**Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam** form the Krishna zone; **Kurnool, Anantapuramu** the Scarce Rainfall zone.
xa: It has **hill soils**; coffee and other plantation crops.
RARS: **Chintapalle**.
⚠ Hill/tribal parts of these districts form this zone; their plains fall in North Coastal and Godavari zones.

121.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh has six agro-climatic zones.
2. These six agro-climatic zones are the same as the six public employment zones under Article 371-D.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: AP has six agro-climatic zones (North Coastal, Godavari, Krishna, Southern, Scarce Rainfall, High Altitude & Tribal). Statement 2 is wrong: the six zones under Art. 371-D are administrative zones for public employment, unrelated to the agro-climatic classification. So '1 only'; '2 only', 'both' and 'neither' all misjudge one statement.
121.tq: Six agro-climatic zones (farming) are not the six Art. 371-D zones (jobs).
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: AP has **six** agro-climatic zones.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **six** zones under **Art. 371-D** are **administrative** zones for public employment.
xa: The six agro-climatic zones: **North Coastal, Godavari, Krishna, Southern, Scarce Rainfall, High Altitude & Tribal**.
India has **15** agro-climatic zones; **Karnataka** has **10**.

121.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Scarce Rainfall — Red and black soils
High Altitude and Tribal — Deltaic alluvium
North Coastal — High rainfall and laterite soils
121.x: High Altitude and Tribal areas are characterised by hill soils, not deltaic alluvium. Fertile deltaic alluvium is associated with the Godavari zone.
121.tq: Find the soil-setting mismatch using the physical character of each zone.
xs: "**High Altitude and Tribal — Deltaic alluvium**" is wrong: this zone has **hill soils** — option **(3)**.
**Deltaic alluvium** belongs to the **Godavari** zone.
**Scarce Rainfall** = red and black soils; **North Coastal** = high rainfall, **laterite** — correctly matched.
xa: Krishna zone: **deltaic and coastal plains**.
Southern zone: **varied**, plains to hills.
RARS: High Altitude = **Chintapalle**; North Coastal = **Anakapalle**.

121.s: Which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh is popularly associated with the description 'rice bowl' and is also an aquaculture hub?
121.x: The Godavari zone, characterised by fertile deltaic alluvium, is described as a rice bowl and an aquaculture hub.
121.tq: Link a well-known regional description with its geographical zone.
xs: The **Godavari** zone is the **"rice bowl"** and **aquaculture hub** — option **(2)**.
It has **fertile deltaic alluvium**.
xa: Godavari zone = **East Godavari, West Godavari**; RARS **Maruteru**.
Godavari delta paddy land is shifting to **aquaculture**.
India's first Mega Aqua Food Park is at **Tundurru** (**West Godavari**).

121.s: Paddy, chillies and cotton are the principal crops associated with which zone?
121.x: The Krishna zone, consisting of deltaic and coastal plains, is associated with paddy, chillies and cotton.
121.tq: Use the crop combination to identify the corresponding zone.
xs: **Paddy, chillies and cotton** belong to the **Krishna** zone — option **(4)**.
It has **deltaic and coastal plains**; districts **Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam**.
xa: RARS: **Lam (Guntur)**.
**Guntur** is the chilli centre and has the **Tobacco Board**.
AP lies in the **Southern cotton zone**.

121.s: In India's cotton geography, Andhra Pradesh is placed in the:
o: Eastern cotton zone with West Bengal and Odisha
Northern cotton zone with Punjab and Haryana
Western cotton zone with Gujarat and Rajasthan
Southern cotton zone with Telangana and Karnataka
121.x: Andhra Pradesh belongs to the Southern cotton zone along with Telangana and Karnataka.
121.tq: Use the neighbouring-state combination to identify the correct cotton region.
xs: AP is in the **Southern cotton zone** with **Telangana and Karnataka** — option **(4)**.
So the Eastern, Northern and Western cotton zones are wrong for AP.
xa: Cotton is grown mainly in the **Krishna** zone with paddy and chillies.
ANGRAU researches **pest-resistant cotton**.
Cotton (**"white gold"**) is the commercial crop that expanded most (PYQ 2022).

121.s:
Match the agro-climatic zones of Andhra Pradesh with their zonal headquarters:
List-I (Zone)
 a. North Coastal
 b. Godavari
 c. Krishna
 d. Southern
List-II (Zonal HQ)
 i. Lam, Guntur
 ii. Tirupati
 iii. Maruteru
 iv. Anakapalle
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
121.x: The North Coastal, Godavari, Krishna and Southern zones have their zonal headquarters at Anakapalle, Maruteru, Lam–Guntur and Tirupati respectively.
121.tq: Start with the distinctive Lam–Guntur and Tirupati pairs, then complete the code.
xs: **a–iv, b–iii, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
North Coastal → **Anakapalle**; Godavari → **Maruteru**; Krishna → **Lam, Guntur**; Southern → **Tirupati**.
xa: Scarce Rainfall → **Nandyal**.
High Altitude & Tribal → **Chintapalle**.
⚠ Trap: Godavari = **Maruteru**; Krishna = **Lam**.

121.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Agro-climatic zone)
 a. Godavari
 b. Krishna
 c. Scarce Rainfall
 d. High Altitude and Tribal

List-II (Headquarters)
 i. Chintapalle
 ii. Lam, Guntur
 iii. Maruteru
 iv. Nandyal

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
121.x: Godavari is headquartered at Maruteru, Krishna at Lam, Scarce Rainfall at Nandyal and High Altitude and Tribal at Chintapalle.
121.tq: Start with the distinctive headquarters and complete the code by elimination.
xs: **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
Godavari → **Maruteru**; Krishna → **Lam, Guntur**; Scarce Rainfall → **Nandyal**; High Altitude & Tribal → **Chintapalle**.
xa: North Coastal → **Anakapalle**; Southern → **Tirupati**.
⚠ ICAR **IIOPR** is at **Pedavegi** — a different institute.

121.s: Which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh is chronically drought-prone?
o: High Altitude and Tribal Areas Zone
121.x: The Scarce Rainfall Zone, covering Kurnool and Anantapuramu, is the chronically drought-prone zone of Andhra Pradesh.
121.tq: Match the descriptive label with the climatic condition it directly signifies.
xs: The **Scarce Rainfall Zone** (Kurnool, Anantapuramu) is **chronically drought-prone** — option **(3)**.
Godavari is the deltaic "rice bowl"; North Coastal and High Altitude get the most rain.
xa: The highest rainfall is in the **North Coastal** zone and the **tribal highlands**.
Crops: **groundnut** and dryland crops.
**PMDS** uses residual soil moisture in drought-prone areas.

121.s: Which areas receive the highest rainfall among the agro-climatic zones of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Krishna zone and Scarce Rainfall zone
North Coastal zone and tribal highlands
Scarce Rainfall zone and Southern plains
Southern zone and Godavari delta only
121.x: The North Coastal zone and the tribal highlands receive the most rainfall among the zones.
121.tq: Compare extremes in rainfall rather than confusing fertile areas with wettest areas.
xs: **North Coastal** and the **tribal highlands** get the highest rainfall — option **(2)**.
**Scarce Rainfall** (Kurnool, Anantapuramu) is the chronically drought-prone zone.
xa: North Coastal has **laterite** soils.
State normal rainfall: **860.0 mm**.

121.s: What was the total actual rainfall in Andhra Pradesh during 2024-25, and how did it compare with normal rainfall?
o: 960.3 mm, an excess of 11.7 per cent
718.2 mm, an excess of 11.7 per cent
860.0 mm, a deficit of 16.5 per cent
960.3 mm, a deficit of 2.3 per cent
121.x: Total rainfall in 2024-25 was 960.3 mm against the normal of 860.0 mm, an excess of 11.7 per cent.
121.tq: Read the total and its deviation together rather than mixing seasonal figures.
xs: 2024-25 rainfall: **960.3 mm**, an **excess of 11.7 per cent** over normal — option **(1)**.
Normal is **860.0 mm**; **-2.3%** was the North-East monsoon deviation.
xa: South-West monsoon: **681.6 mm** vs **574.7 mm** normal (**+18.6%**).
North-East monsoon: **278.7 mm** vs **285.3 mm**.
**Kharif 2026**: all **28** districts in deficit.

121.s: A district in a drought-prone area adopts pre-monsoon dry sowing under natural farming using residual soil moisture. This practice is known as:
121.x: Pre-monsoon dry sowing is referred to as PMDS and uses residual soil moisture, particularly in drought-prone areas.
121.tq: Apply the abbreviation to a practical drought-management scenario.
xs: **PMDS** = **pre-monsoon dry sowing**, using residual soil moisture — option **(1)**.
**NBSS&LUP** is the soil survey bureau; **RARS** are research stations.
xa: PMDS is used under natural farming in **drought-prone** areas (Jul 2026).
Zones decide **region-specific interventions**.

121.s: Which institution prepares district agricultural contingency plans?
121.x: District agricultural contingency plans are prepared by ICAR-CRIDA.
121.tq: Identify the responsible agricultural institution rather than a classification agency.
xs: District contingency plans are prepared by **ICAR-CRIDA** — option **(3)**.
**NBSS&LUP** divides India into agro-ecological regions; ANGRAU runs zonal research stations.
xa: Zones decide **region-specific interventions** such as **PMDS** and alternative crops.
Kharif **2026**: all **28** districts in deficit.

121.s: An agro-ecological zone is formed from an agro-climatic zone by superimposing which factor?
121.x: An agro-ecological zone is a land unit carved out of an agro-climatic zone by superimposing landform, which modifies climate and the length of the growing period.
121.tq: Distinguish the additional physical layer used in agro-ecological classification.
xs: An agro-ecological zone superimposes **landform** on an agro-climatic zone — option **(3)**.
Landform modifies climate and the **length of growing period**.
xa: **NBSS&LUP**: **20** agro-ecological regions + **60** sub-regions.
India has **15** agro-climatic zones.

121.s: The National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning (NBSS&LUP) has divided India into:
121.x: NBSS&LUP divides India into 20 agro-ecological regions and 60 sub-regions. 15 is the number of agro-climatic zones (Planning Commission), not agro-ecological regions; '20 and 15' mixes up the two; '60 and 20' reverses the regions and sub-regions.
121.tq: NBSS&LUP: 20 regions, 60 sub-regions; agro-climatic zones of India: 15.
xs: **NBSS&LUP** divides India into **20 agro-ecological regions** and **60 sub-regions** — option **(2)**.
**15** is India's number of **agro-climatic** zones; option (4) reverses regions and sub-regions.
xa: An agro-ecological zone = agro-climatic zone + **landform**.
AP has **six** agro-climatic zones; **Karnataka** **10**.

121.s:
Assertion (A): Andhra Pradesh has regional disparities in irrigation and farm income.
Reason (R): Its six agro-climatic zones are associated with uneven water distribution.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
121.x: Both statements are true, and uneven water distribution across the six agro-climatic zones contributes directly to disparities in irrigation and farm income.
121.tq: Check whether the reason explains the stated regional disparity.
xs: **Both A and R are true** and R is the **correct explanation** of A — option **(1)**.
AP's regional disparities in irrigation and farm income follow its **six** zones and **uneven water distribution**.
xa: India is moving to **state-wise agricultural roadmaps** (Apr 2026).
Drought-prone: **Scarce Rainfall Zone**; highest rainfall: **North Coastal** + tribal highlands.

121.s: Which State has ten agro-climatic zones, in contrast to Andhra Pradesh's current six-zone classification?
121.x: Karnataka has 10 agro-climatic zones, whereas the current Andhra Pradesh classification has six.
121.tq: Use the numerical comparison without confusing neighbouring-state classifications.
xs: **Karnataka** has **10 agro-climatic zones** — option **(2)**.
AP has **six**.
xa: India has **15** agro-climatic zones.
NBSS&LUP: **20** agro-ecological regions.

121.s: India's agro-climatic zones, which differ in soils and rainfall and are the basis for moving towards state-wise agricultural roadmaps, number:
121.x: India has 15 agro-climatic zones. Six is Andhra Pradesh's number of zones, 10 is Karnataka's, and 20 is the number of NBSS&LUP agro-ecological regions.
121.tq: India 15, AP 6, Karnataka 10, agro-ecological regions 20.
xs: India has **15** agro-climatic zones — option **(3)**.
**6** = AP's zones; **10** = Karnataka's; **20** = NBSS&LUP agro-ecological regions.
xa: India is shifting to **state-wise agricultural roadmaps** (Apr 2026).
NBSS&LUP also has **60** sub-regions.

122.s: Under which provision of the Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Societies Act, 1964, is the Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Tribunal constituted?
122.x: The Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Tribunal is constituted under Section 75 of the Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Societies Act, 1964.
122.tq: Test the exact statutory section rather than the name of the Act alone.
xs: The **AP Cooperative Tribunal** is constituted under **Section 75** of the **AP Cooperative Societies Act, 1964** — option **(2)**.
The 1964 Act is AP's **main cooperative law**.
xa: The Tribunal is chaired by a **judicial officer**.
It is the **appellate forum** under the 1964 Act and has **original jurisdiction** over **MACS Act 1995** disputes.
**APHOUSEFED** was registered under the 1964 Act in **1966**.

122.s: Which one of the following best describes societies formed under the AP Mutually Aided Cooperative Societies Act, 1995?
o: Societies administered directly by the AP Cooperative Tribunal
Societies dependent on government share capital and extensive state control
Societies confined exclusively to long-term agricultural credit
Self-reliant societies without government share capital, managed by members with minimal state control
122.x: The MACS Act, 1995 provides for self-reliant societies without government share capital, run by members with minimal state control.
122.tq: Discriminate between the member-driven MACS model and state-dominated cooperative structures.
xs: MACS Act **1995** societies are **self-reliant**, **without government share capital**, run by members with **minimal state control** — option **(4)**.
Disputes under it go to the **AP Cooperative Tribunal** in its **original jurisdiction** — the Tribunal does not administer them.
xa: MACS Act was asked in a **PYQ 2008**.
⚠ **1964 Act** = main law, Tribunal under **Section 75**; **MACS Act 1995** = no government share capital.
**National Cooperative Policy**: **2002**.

122.s:
With reference to the 97th Constitutional Amendment, consider the following statements:
1. It added Article 19(1)(c) relating to the right to form cooperatives.
2. It inserted Article 43B as a Directive Principle of State Policy.
3. It added Part IXB relating to cooperative societies.
4. The Supreme Court retained Part IXB in its entirety for State cooperatives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
122.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the 97th Amendment (2011) added Art. 19(1)(c), Art. 43B and Part IXB. Statement 4 is wrong: the Supreme Court struck down Part IXB for State cooperatives and kept it only for multi-State societies.
122.tq: Identify the constitutional additions and reject the reversed effect of the Supreme Court judgment.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1)**.
The **97th Amendment** (**2011**) added **Art. 19(1)(c)**, **Art. 43B** (DPSP) and **Part IXB**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the **Supreme Court** struck down Part IXB for **State** cooperatives, keeping it for **multi-State** societies.
xa: Art. 19(1)(c) = **right to form cooperatives**.
**National Cooperative Policy** came in **2002**.
Nehru called cooperatives one of **three pillars of democracy**.

122.s:
Consider the following statements about the cooperative movement in India:
1. The Cooperative Credit Societies Act, 1904 started the cooperative movement.
2. The Cooperative Societies Act, 1912 allowed non-credit societies to be formed.
3. The National Cooperative Policy was announced in 2011, the year of the 97th Amendment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
122.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 1904 Act started the movement. Statement 2 is correct: the 1912 Act allowed non-credit societies. Statement 3 is wrong: the National Cooperative Policy came in 2002; 2011 is the year of the 97th Amendment. So '1 and 2 only'; the other options include statement 3 or leave out a true statement.
122.tq: 1904 start, 1912 non-credit, 2002 policy, 2011 97th Amendment.

122.s: The Task Force on revival of cooperative credit (2004) and the Expert Committee on short-term cooperative credit structure (2013) were chaired, respectively, by:
122.x: The 2004 Task Force was chaired by A. Vaidyanathan and the 2013 Expert Committee by Prakash Bakshi. Option B reverses them; B. Sivaraman's committee led to NABARD; A.D. Gorwala did not chair the 2013 committee.
122.tq: Earlier (2004) = Vaidyanathan; later (2013) = Bakshi.

122.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Tribunal:
1. It is chaired by a judicial officer.
2. It is an appellate forum under the AP Cooperative Societies Act, 1964.
3. It has only appellate, and no original, jurisdiction over disputes under the AP MACS Act, 1995.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
122.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Tribunal is chaired by a judicial officer and hears appeals under the 1964 Act. Statement 3 is wrong: the Tribunal has original jurisdiction over disputes under the MACS Act, 1995. So any option containing 3 is wrong.
122.tq: Tribunal: appellate for the 1964 Act, original for the MACS Act 1995.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: the Tribunal is chaired by a **judicial officer**.
Statement 2: it is the **appellate forum under the 1964 Act**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it has **original jurisdiction** over disputes under the **MACS Act 1995**.
xa: Constituted under **Section 75** of the **1964 Act**.
MACS societies have **no government share capital**.

122.s: India has approximately how many cooperative societies and members, respectively?
o: 8.5 lakh societies and over 30 crore members
122.x: India has about 8.5 lakh cooperatives with over 30 crore members.
122.tq: Keep the society count and membership count in their correct order and scale.
xs: India has about **8.5 lakh cooperatives** with **over 30 crore members** — option **(1)**.
Option (4) swaps the units.
xa: Figure reported on **7 Jul 2026**.
**2 lakh** new multipurpose PACS/dairy/fishery societies planned; **24,417** set up.
The Ministry of Cooperation counts **114** initiatives (2026).

122.s: Compared with 2001-02, the number of cooperative societies in Andhra Pradesh has:
122.x: The number of cooperative societies in AP has decreased compared with 2001-02 (PYQ 2008); defunct labour contract and joint farming societies are being wound up. It has not increased, stayed the same or doubled.
122.tq: AP cooperative societies: falling in number since 2001-02.
xs: The number of cooperative societies in AP has **decreased** since **2001-02** — option **(2)** (PYQ 2008).
Defunct bodies are being wound up: **1,756** labour contract societies and **210** joint farming societies.
xa: About **one-third of PACS are inactive** despite registration (audits in MP and UP).

122.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the three-tier cooperative credit structure in Andhra Pradesh?
122.x: The structure consists of APCOB at the State level, DCCBs at the district level and PACS at the village level.
122.tq: Identify the institutional tier before considering the numerical details.
xs: **APCOB — State**, **DCCBs — District**, **PACS — Village** — option **(3)**.
The other options jumble the tiers.
xa: APSES 2024-25: APCOB **18 branches**; **13 DCCBs** with **442 branches**; **2,042 PACS**.
APCOB **refinances DCCBs** for long-term credit.
APCOB is the **CBBO** for PACS as FPOs.

122.s: According to APSES 2024–25, which of the following is the correct numerical composition of the cooperative credit structure?
o: APCOB: 18 branches; DCCBs: 13 with 436 branches; PACS: 2,024
APCOB: 13 branches; DCCBs: 18 with 442 branches; PACS: 2,042
APCOB: 13 branches; DCCBs: 18 with 436 branches; PACS: 2,024
APCOB: 18 branches; DCCBs: 13 with 442 branches; PACS: 2,042
122.x: APSES 2024–25 gives 18 APCOB branches, 13 DCCBs with 442 branches and 2,042 PACS.
122.tq: Read the figures across the State, district and village tiers without transposing them.
xs: APSES 2024-25: **APCOB 18 branches**; **13 DCCBs** with **442 branches**; **2,042 PACS** — option **(4)**.
**436** branches and **2,024** PACS are the **SES 2025-26** counts, so option (1) mixes sources.
xa: ⚠ **2,024** may be a transposition of **2,042**.
⚠ **2,037** PACS are being computerised.
Production credit 2024-25 via PACS/DCCBs: **Rs 5,933.92 crore**.

122.s: PACS primarily provide which of the following services?
o: Crop and short-term loans and supply of agricultural inputs
122.x: PACS provide crop and short-term loans and supply inputs such as fertilizers, pesticides, seeds and cattle feed.
122.tq: Distinguish the core credit and input-supply functions from the wider non-credit activities of PACS.
xs: PACS give **crop and short-term loans** and **supply inputs** — option **(3)**.
Inputs: **fertilizers, pesticides, seeds, cattle feed**.
xa: Non-credit: paddy & maize procurement, seed processing, **PDS**, insurance, RO water, petrol bunks, rice mills, warehousing.
Model bye-laws allow **25+ non-credit activities**.
**NABARD** supports turning PACS into **Multi-Service Centres**.

122.s: NABARD supports the transformation of PACS into:
o: Agriculture and Rural Development Banks only
122.x: NABARD supports turning PACS into Multi-Service Centres.
122.tq: Match the supporting institution with the institutional transformation it promotes.
xs: **NABARD** supports turning PACS into **Multi-Service Centres** — option **(2)**.
Liquidation applies to Labour Contract federations; **ARDBs** are the separate long-term credit arm; the **Tribunal** is a dispute forum.
xa: Model bye-laws let PACS take up **25+** non-credit activities.
PACS in **207 blocks** are eligible for **NCDC** equity grants as **FPOs**.
NABARD's **Sahakar Sarathi** is a new body.

122.s: Which institution provides long-term investment credit nationally, while APCOB performs the corresponding refinancing role in Andhra Pradesh?
o: ARDBs nationally and APCOB in Andhra Pradesh
DCCBs nationally and PACS in Andhra Pradesh
PACS nationally and NABARD in Andhra Pradesh
APCOB nationally and ARDBs in Andhra Pradesh
122.x: Agriculture and Rural Development Banks provide long-term investment credit nationally. In Andhra Pradesh, APCOB refinances DCCBs for long-term credit.
122.tq: Separate the national institutional arrangement from the Andhra Pradesh refinancing arrangement.
xs: **ARDBs** give long-term investment credit nationally; in AP, **APCOB** refinances DCCBs — option **(1)**.
ARDB = **Agriculture and Rural Development Bank**.
xa: Long-term agricultural credit via PACS/DCCBs: **Rs 1,345.51 crore** (2024-25).
AP has **13 DCCBs** with **442 branches**.

122.s:
Consider the following statements about PACS functioning as Farmer Producer Organisations:
1. PACS in 207 blocks are eligible for NCDC equity grants.
2. APCOB acts as the CBBO.
3. The arrangement is confined to PACS in 13 districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
122.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: PACS in 207 blocks are eligible for NCDC equity grants as FPOs, with APCOB acting as the CBBO (2024-25). Statement 3 is the trap: the scheme is defined by the 207 eligible blocks, not confined to PACS in 13 districts.
122.tq: Reject an unsupported limitation while retaining the two stated institutional details.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: PACS in **207 blocks** are eligible for **NCDC** equity grants.
Statement 2: **APCOB** is the **CBBO** (2024-25).
Statement 3 is wrong: eligibility is defined by the **207 blocks**, not **13** districts.
xa: **1,246 of 1,490** PACS became **PM Kisan Samruddhi Kendras**.
NABARD supports PACS as **Multi-Service Centres**.

122.s: Which of the following statements regarding the wider adoption of digital and non-credit functions by PACS is correct?
o: ERP software covers 2,037 PACS nationally, and model bye-laws permit only two non-credit activities.
ERP software covers about 80,000 PACS nationally, and model bye-laws permit more than 25 non-credit activities.
ERP software covers about 80,000 PACS only in Andhra Pradesh, and model bye-laws prohibit non-credit activities.
ERP software covers about 1,490 PACS nationally, and model bye-laws permit 13 non-credit activities.
122.x: Nationally, ERP software covers about 80,000 PACS, while model bye-laws allow PACS to undertake more than 25 non-credit activities.
122.tq: Match the national scale figure with the corresponding scope of model bye-laws.
xs: ERP covers about **80,000 PACS** nationally; model bye-laws permit **25+** non-credit activities — option **(2)**.
**2,037** is AP's computerised PACS, and **1,490** the PACS assigned to fertilizer companies.
xa: National PACS computerisation outlay: **Rs 2,925.39 crore**.
AP: **6,000+** banking touch points via **B@ncs24**.

122.s: How many PACS in Andhra Pradesh are being computerised under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme?
122.x: 2,037 PACS in AP are covered by the computerisation scheme. 1,490 is the number of PACS assigned to fertilizer companies (for PM Kisan Samruddhi Kendras), 1,553 completed pre-migration, and about 80,000 is the national ERP coverage.
122.tq: AP PACS computerisation: 2,037 PACS, on B@ncs24.
xs: **2,037 PACS** are being computerised in AP — option **(1)**.
**1,490** = PACS assigned to fertilizer companies; **1,553** = completed pre-migration; **80,000** = national ERP coverage.
xa: Data signed off for **98%** of PACS.
⚠ **2,037** computerised vs **2,042** PACS (APSES) vs **2,024** (SES).

122.s: The Ministry of Cooperation was established in which year under the vision “Sahkar se Samriddhi”?
122.x: The Ministry of Cooperation was set up in 2021 under the vision “Sahkar se Samriddhi”.
122.tq: Use the year-based direct-recall method and distinguish the Ministry’s formation from later initiatives.
xs: The **Ministry of Cooperation** was set up in **2021**, vision **"Sahkar se Samriddhi"** — option **(3)**.
The **97th Amendment** (**2011**) and **National Cooperative Policy** (**2002**) are the other year traps.
xa: Its **fifth Foundation Day** was on **6 Jul 2026**.
**114** initiatives counted (2026).
Flagship: "**World's largest grain storage programme in cooperatives**".

122.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the decentralised grain storage plan:
1. It is described as the world’s largest grain storage programme in cooperatives.
2. It envisages construction of storage facilities at the PACS level.
3. It is implemented through the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund, the Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure scheme and other schemes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
122.x: All three statements are correct. The programme is a cooperative-based, PACS-level storage initiative supported through AIF, AMI and other schemes.
122.tq: Test a programme through its description, implementation level and funding channels.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: it is the "**World's largest grain storage programme in cooperatives**".
Statement 2: storage is built at the **PACS level**.
Statement 3: it uses **AIF**, **AMI** and other schemes.
xa: AMI subsidy raised from **25% to 33.33%** (**6 Sep 2026**).
AP: AIF-funded storage at **Rythu Seva Kendras**.

122.s:
Consider the following statements about the financing of the decentralised grain storage plan in cooperatives (Sep 2026):
1. The AMI subsidy was raised from 25% to 33.33%.
2. The margin money was raised from 10% to 20%.
3. With the 3% AIF interest subvention, PACS pay an effective interest of 1%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
122.x: Statement 1 is correct: AMI subsidy went from 25% to 33.33%. Statement 2 is wrong: margin money was cut from 20% to 10%, not raised. Statement 3 is correct: with 3% AIF subvention PACS pay about 1%. So '1 and 3 only'; the other options include statement 2.
122.tq: Subsidy up, margin money down, effective interest 1%.

122.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the cooperative initiative or institution?
o: Tribhuvan Sahakari University — India’s first national cooperative university
National Cooperative Organics Ltd — urban cooperative bank development body
NABARD’s Sahakar Sarathi — national cooperative university at Anand
122.x: Tribhuvan Sahakari University at IRMA, Anand, is India’s first national cooperative university. NUCFDC is associated with urban cooperative banks, while National Cooperative Exports Ltd and Sahakar Sarathi have different roles.
122.tq: Use the correctly matched pair and reject swapped institutional identities.
xs: **Tribhuvan Sahakari University** is India's **first national cooperative university** — option **(2)**.
**NUCFDC** is for **urban cooperative banks**, not exports; the university is at **IRMA Anand**, not Sahakar Sarathi.
xa: New bodies: **National Cooperative Exports Ltd**, **National Cooperative Organics Ltd**, NABARD's **Sahakar Sarathi**.
Ministry of Cooperation: **2021**, "**Sahkar se Samriddhi**".

122.s: Political capture of cooperative boards tends to produce which combination of effects?
o: Higher deposits and professional management in every PACS
Automatic conversion of PACS into Multi-Service Centres
More impartial credit allocation and faster recovery from all defaulters
Distorted credit allocation, protection of politically connected defaulters and increased overdues
122.x: Political capture distorts credit allocation and shields politically connected defaulters from recovery, thereby feeding overdues.
122.tq: Trace the cause-effect chain from political interference to recovery problems and overdues.
xs: **Political capture** distorts credit allocation, **shields politically connected defaulters** and **feeds overdues** — option **(4)**.
