139.s: The constitutional amendment that provided compensation to States for GST revenue loss was the:
139.x: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 provided for compensation to States for revenue loss arising from GST implementation.
139.tq: Match the constitutional provision with its exact amendment number and year.
xs: The **101st Amendment (2016)** provided **GST compensation** to States — option **(4)**.
It compensates States for **GST revenue loss**.
The other amendments are not linked to GST compensation in the notes.
xa: **BRGF** (launched **2006-07**) is now **defunct**.
**Aspirational Districts Programme**: **NITI Aayog**, **Jan 2018**.
**Sec 94(1)** incentives notified in **2015**.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about the Backward Region Grant Fund (BRGF) and its successor approach:
1. BRGF was launched in 2006-07.
2. BRGF was delinked from central support from 2015-16.
3. The Aspirational Districts Programme, seen as the successor approach, was launched by the Finance Commission in January 2018.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct (launched 2006-07). Statement 2 is correct (delinked from 2015-16). Statement 3 is wrong: the Aspirational Districts Programme was launched by NITI Aayog, not the Finance Commission, in January 2018. So B; A omits 2, C and D include the false 3.
139.tq: BRGF 2006-07 to 2015-16; ADP = NITI Aayog, Jan 2018.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**BRGF** was launched in **2006-07** and **delinked from central support from 2015-16**.
Statement 3: wrong — the **Aspirational Districts Programme** was launched by **NITI Aayog**, not the FC, in **Jan 2018**.
xa: ADP has **5** themes; motto "**Convergence, Collaboration, Competition**".
BRGF aimed to **redress regional imbalances**; now **defunct**.
States now use own incentive policies (capital subsidies, power-tariff concessions).

139.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the features associated with the Aspirational Districts Programme?
139.x: The three stated themes of the Aspirational Districts Programme are Convergence, Collaboration and Competition. Compensation is not one of them.
139.tq: Find the odd policy term among three closely associated themes.
xs: **Compensation** is not an ADP feature — option **(4)**.
ADP motto: "**Convergence, Collaboration, Competition**".
Launched by **NITI Aayog** in **Jan 2018**, with **5** themes.
xa: ADP is the **successor approach** to the defunct **BRGF**.
**ASR** ranked **1st in India** on **Basic Infrastructure** (**March 2026**).
⚠ "Compensation" belongs to **GST compensation** (**101st Amendment**).

139.s: Rayalaseema has a low population density primarily because of:
o: Absence of Eastern Ghats hill tracts
139.x: Recurring droughts and famines are identified as major reasons for Rayalaseema's low population density.
139.tq: Match the regional demographic feature with its stated cause.
xs: Low density is due to **recurring droughts and famines** — option **(3)**.
Rayalaseema lacks industry (no **anchor industries**), so (2) is wrong.
Groundwater stress is highest in **Sri Sathya Sai (57.44%)** and **Chittoor (55.16%)**.
xa: Region has **8 districts**.
**Sri Bagh Pact (16 Nov 1937)** promised irrigation priority for **10 years**.
Strength: **Horticulture Hub** — **43%** of AP's horticulture area.

139.s: The Godavari–Penna link, Phase I, is intended to transfer:
o: 73 TMC of Godavari flood water to the Pennar through a five-stage lift
71.5 TMC of Krishna water through a three-stage lift
3.283 lakh acres of irrigation water from the Krishna to Gundlakamma
24.20 TMC of Pennar water to the Godavari through a two-stage lift
139.x: Phase I of the Godavari–Penna link proposes to carry 73 TMC of Godavari flood water to the Pennar through a five-stage lift.
139.tq: Keep the source river, destination river, quantity and lift stages together.
xs: **Godavari-Penna link Phase I**: **73 TMC** of Godavari flood water to the **Pennar** via a **5-stage lift** — option **(1)**.
It is about **21%** done.
**71.5%** is **Veligonda's** completion; **3.283 lakh acres** is Veligonda Phase II; **24.20 TMC** is **Handri Neeva**.
xa: **Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link** is proposed to carry Godavari surplus to Rayalaseema.
Veligonda: **Rs 768 crore** paid to **6,206** displaced families.
Handri Neeva: seasonal use of **24.20 TMC**.

139.s: Which project has been proposed to carry surplus Godavari water to Rayalaseema?
139.x: The Polavaram–Nallamala Sagar link has been proposed to carry surplus Godavari water to Rayalaseema.
139.tq: Identify the project by its stated source, destination and purpose.
xs: The **Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link** is proposed to carry Godavari surplus to Rayalaseema — option **(4)**.
**Vamsadhara Phase-II** and the **Nagavali-Suvarnamukhi** link are **North Coastal** projects.
**Handri Neeva Sujala Sravanthi** uses **24.20 TMC** seasonally.
xa: **Godavari-Penna Phase I**: **73 TMC** via **5-stage lift**; about **21%** done.
**Veligonda** (Krishna to Gundlakamma): **71.5%** complete.
Vamsadhara Phase-II: **93.5%** complete.

139.s: The Sri Bagh Pact, which promised Rayalaseema priority in irrigation for ten years, was concluded on:
139.x: The Sri Bagh Pact was concluded on 16 November 1937 and promised Rayalaseema irrigation priority for ten years.
139.tq: Use the exact historical date attached to the regional development promise.
xs: The **Sri Bagh Pact** was concluded on **16 November 1937** — option **(1)** is correct.
The other dates (**1935**, **1947**, **26 January 1937**) are not the date of the Pact.
It promised Rayalaseema **irrigation priority** for **10 years**.
It is the **historical root** of Rayalaseema's grievance.
xa: Today Rayalaseema has **8 districts**.
**Godavari-Penna** Phase I: **73 TMC** to the Pennar.
**Veligonda**: **71.5%** complete.

139.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of Rayalaseema districts?
o: Nandyal, Annamayya and Sri Satya Sai
139.x: Nandyal, Annamayya and Sri Satya Sai are Rayalaseema districts. Palnadu, Bapatla and NTR are coastal districts.
139.tq: Classify every district in a set and reject sets containing coastal or Uttarandhra districts.
xs: **Nandyal, Annamayya and Sri Satya Sai** are all Rayalaseema — option **(4)**.
**Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Anakapalli** are **Uttarandhra** districts.
The 8 Rayalaseema districts: Kurnool, Nandyal, Anantapur, Sri Satya Sai, YSR, Annamayya, Tirupati, Chittoor.
xa: ⚠ Package covered only **4** Rayalaseema districts.
Highest groundwater withdrawal: **Sri Sathya Sai (57.44%)**.
Uttarandhra has **6** districts.

139.s: The Veligonda project, reported to be 71.5% complete, is designed to carry water from:
139.x: Veligonda takes Krishna water to the Gundlakamma. Godavari to Pennar is the Godavari-Penna link (73 TMC), Godavari surplus to Nallamala Sagar is the proposed Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link, and Nagavali-Champavathi is the North Coastal link via Thotapalli barrage.
139.tq: Veligonda = Krishna -> Gundlakamma (Prakasam side).
xs: **Veligonda** carries water from **the Krishna to the Gundlakamma** — option **(1)**.
Godavari to Pennar is the **Godavari-Penna link**; Godavari to Nallamala Sagar is the **Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar** link.
Nagavali-Champavathi is the North Coastal link via **Thotapalli barrage**.
xa: Veligonda is **71.5%** complete; **Rs 768 crore** paid to **6,206** displaced families.
**Phase II** adds **3.283 lakh acres** (CDCA **Aug 2026**).
**Handri Neeva**: seasonal use of **24.20 TMC**.

139.s: Which of the following is the correct list of districts of Uttarandhra?
o: Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam
Alluri Sitharama Raju, Eluru, Anakapalli, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam and Srikakulam
Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Prakasam, Nellore, Tirupati and Chittoor
Kurnool, Nandyal, Anantapur, Sri Satya Sai, YSR and Chittoor
139.x: The six Uttarandhra districts are Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam.
139.tq: Use elimination by checking every district in the regional list.
xs: Uttarandhra's **6** districts: **Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) wrongly adds **Eluru** and **Kakinada**; option (4) lists Rayalaseema districts.
Uttarandhra is also called "**Kalinga Andhra**".
xa: Tribes on the Srikakulam side: **Savara and Jatapu**.
Lowest literacy: **ASR (44.67%)**.
The package covered **3** North Coastal districts.

139.s: Which of the following pairs of tribal communities and areas is correctly matched?
o: Kotia and Porja — coastal Krishna delta
Khond and Jatapu — Bhogapuram urban area
139.x: Savara and Jatapu communities are associated with the Srikakulam side. Gadaba, Bagata, Kotia, Porja and Khond are associated with the Araku/Visakhapatnam agency.
139.tq: Start with the sure geographical pair and reject misplaced tribal groups.
xs: **Savara and Jatapu — Srikakulam side** — option **(1)**.
The notes link no other tribe pair to an area.
Srikakulam is part of **Uttarandhra**.
xa: **Srikakulam and Vizianagaram** lack **anchor industries** → **distress migration**.
Lowest literacy in Uttarandhra: **ASR (44.67%)**.
Uttarandhra = "**Kalinga Andhra**", **6** districts.

139.s: Which district has the lowest literacy among the indicators specified for Uttarandhra?
139.x: Alluri Sitharama Raju district has the lowest literacy among the specified indicators, at 44.67%.
139.tq: Link the lowest indicator with the correct district and percentage.
xs: **Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR)** has the lowest literacy — **44.67%** — option **(4)**.
Vizianagaram and Srikakulam are noted for **distress migration**, not lowest literacy.
⚠ Lowest urbanisation (**2.84%**) and density (**54**) belong to the **new Polavaram district**.
xa: ASR ranked **1st in India** on **Basic Infrastructure** in ADP (**March 2026**).
**Vamsadhara Phase-II**: **93.5%** complete.
Uttarandhra has **6** districts.

139.s: The lack of anchor industries in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram is associated with:
o: A decline in horticultural output across Rayalaseema
139.x: The absence of anchor industries in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram contributes to distress migration.
139.tq: Connect the industrial gap with its stated migration outcome.
xs: No **anchor industries** in **Srikakulam and Vizianagaram** → **distress migration** — option **(2)**.
It is not linked to urbanisation or industrial concentration.
Rayalaseema has the same problem plus an **agrarian crisis**.
xa: Tribes on the Srikakulam side: **Savara and Jatapu**.
**Bhogapuram airport** (Vizianagaram): operations targeted **June 2026**.
AP Cabinet tracked **Rs 8.55 lakh crore** investments for North Andhra and Rayalaseema.

139.s: Bhogapuram airport is located in which district, with commercial operations targeted for June 2026?
139.x: Bhogapuram airport is located in Vizianagaram district, and commercial operations were targeted for June 2026.
139.tq: Match the infrastructure project with its district and stated timeline.
xs: **Bhogapuram airport** is in **Vizianagaram** — option **(2)** — operations targeted **June 2026**.
It is a **planned project** for North Coastal AP.
Vizianagaram lacks **anchor industries** → **distress migration**.
xa: Thotapalli barrage link: **Nagavali-Suvarnamukhi-Vegavathi-Champavathi**.
**Visakhapatnam Economic Region**: **10** districts, launched **13 Nov 2025**.
Vizianagaram was a **North Coastal** package district.

139.s: In the March 2026 rankings of the NITI Aayog Aspirational Districts Programme, ASR ranked first in which theme?
139.x: ASR ranked first in the Basic Infrastructure theme of the NITI Aayog Aspirational Districts Programme in the March 2026 rankings.
139.tq: Match the district ranking with the precise development theme, not with another Aspirational Districts indicator.
xs: **ASR** ranked **1st in India** on **Basic Infrastructure** — option **(1)** (**March 2026**).
This is under NITI Aayog's **Aspirational Districts Programme**.
ASR also has the **lowest literacy (44.67%)** in Uttarandhra.
xa: ADP launched **Jan 2018**; **5** themes.
Motto: "**Convergence, Collaboration, Competition**".
Lowest urbanisation: **new Polavaram district (2.84%)**.

139.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Visakhapatnam Economic Region covers 10 districts and was launched on 13 November 2025.
2. In January 2026, the AP Cabinet tracked investments of Rs 8.55 lakh crore for North Andhra and Rayalaseema.
3. The Visakhapatnam Economic Region was launched by NITI Aayog under the Aspirational Districts Programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct (10 districts, 13 Nov 2025). Statement 2 is correct (Rs 8.55 lakh crore, Jan 2026). Statement 3 is wrong: VER is a region-specific growth plan, not part of NITI Aayog's ADP (launched Jan 2018). So B; A omits 2, C and D include the false 3.
139.tq: VER = 10 districts, 13 Nov 2025; ADP = NITI Aayog, Jan 2018.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **VER** covers **10 districts**, launched **13 Nov 2025** — correct.
Statement 2: AP Cabinet tracked **Rs 8.55 lakh crore** for **North Andhra and Rayalaseema** (**Jan 2026**) — correct.
Statement 3: wrong — VER is a **region-specific growth plan**, not part of NITI Aayog's ADP.
xa: ADP: **NITI Aayog**, **Jan 2018**.
**Tirupati Economic Region** is VER's Rayalaseema counterpart.
ASR ranked **1st** on **Basic Infrastructure** in ADP (**March 2026**).

140.s: Under the Thirteenth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, within what period were the Indian Railways required to examine establishing a new railway zone in the successor State of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Three months from the appointed day
Two years from the appointed day
One year from the appointed day
Six months from the appointed day
140.x: The Act required the Indian Railways to examine establishing a new railway zone in Andhra Pradesh within six months from the appointed day.
140.tq: Fix the exact statutory time limit instead of confusing examination with establishment.
xs: **Indian Railways** had to examine a new zone within **six months from the appointed day** — option **(4)** is correct.
The provision sits in the **Thirteenth Schedule (Infrastructure)** of the Act.
xa: It only obliged Railways to **examine** and take an **expeditious decision** — a feasibility promise.
The same Schedule asks Railways to examine a **Rail Coach Factory** for **Telangana**.
Exam angle: "which body", "within what period" (**six months**), "**examine**" vs "establish".

140.s: Which one of the following most accurately describes the obligation relating to the proposed railway zone in Andhra Pradesh under the Thirteenth Schedule?
o: Railways was required to examine establishing the zone and take an expeditious decision
The State Government was authorised to establish the zone independently
The Union Cabinet was required to establish the zone through a constitutional amendment
Railways was required to establish the zone within six months
140.x: The statutory wording created a feasibility-oriented obligation to examine the establishment of a zone and take an expeditious decision; it did not itself establish the zone.
140.tq: Distinguish the legally precise word 'examine' from the stronger word 'establish'.
xs: Railways had to **examine establishing the zone** and **take an expeditious decision** — option **(1)** is correct.
It did not mandate establishment within six months, nor did it give the State or a constitutional amendment any role.
xa: Railways = **Union subject** (**Entry 22, List I**).
A zone is created by **executive decision** + **gazette notification** of the Ministry of Railways.
The same "examine" wording is used for the **steel plant, refinery, airport** items.

140.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Thirteenth Schedule also asks Railways to examine a Rail Coach Factory for Telangana.
2. The Rail Coach Factory provision is the same as the new railway-zone provision for Andhra Pradesh.
3. The railway-zone provision concerns the successor State of Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the Rail Coach Factory provision for Telangana must not be confused with the railway-zone provision for Andhra Pradesh.
140.tq: Separate two similar Thirteenth Schedule provisions by their State and subject.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1: Railways must examine a **Rail Coach Factory** for **Telangana** — correct.
Statement 2 is wrong: the coach factory (Telangana) is a different item from the **railway zone** (AP).
Statement 3: the zone provision concerns the **successor State of AP** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **Trap**: AP = **railway zone**; Telangana = **Rail Coach Factory**.
Both are "examine" (feasibility) promises.

140.s:
Consider the following statements about creating a new railway zone:
1. Railways is a subject in Entry 22 of List II (State List).
2. A railway zone is created by an executive decision and a gazette notification of the Ministry of Railways.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
140.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Railways is a Union subject, Entry 22 of List I (Union List). Statement 2 is correct: a zone is created by executive decision plus gazette notification of the Ministry of Railways. So B; A and C accept the wrong List, D rejects the correct statement 2.
140.tq: Railways = Entry 22, List I; no Act of Parliament needed for a zone.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(2) 2 only**.
Statement 1 is wrong: Railways is a **Union subject**, **Entry 22, List I** — not the State List.
Statement 2 is correct: a zone is created by **executive decision** + **gazette notification** of the **Ministry of Railways**.
xa: SCoR's **gazette notification** came on **4 May 2026**.
Without it, the GM appointed in **Mar 2026** had **no powers**.

140.s: The Railway Board note of 14 May 2026 attributed the staffing gap in the new railway zone mainly to:
o: The cancellation of the Gazette notification
Poor cooperation from existing railway zones
140.x: The Railway Board note blamed poor cooperation from existing zones for the staffing gap.
140.tq: Match the administrative problem with the stated institutional cause.
xs: The Railway Board note (**14 May 2026**) blamed **poor cooperation from existing zones** — option **(2)** is correct.
The notification was not cancelled; a GM was appointed; land disputes were resolved in April.
xa: HQ: only **183 of 526** posts filled.
**Rayagada**: **47 of 191** posts filled.
Staff shortage is listed among the zone's criticisms.

140.s: The establishment of South Coast Railway was described as significant because it was:
o: A demand pressed for over four decades and a statutory promise made in 2014, but notified only after a decade
A constitutional obligation implemented within six months of bifurcation
A demand raised for the first time in 2019 and implemented immediately
A proposal made only after the 2026 Gazette notification
140.x: The demand had been pressed for over four decades, while the statutory promise dated from 2014; the zone was notified only after about a decade.
140.tq: Compare the duration of the demand with the delay between statutory promise and notification.
xs: The zone was a **demand pressed for over four decades** and a **statutory promise of 2014**, **notified only after a decade** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was not implemented within six months, and it was announced in **2019**, not first raised then.
xa: CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu** hailed it as a "**promise kept**".
Gazette notification: **4 May 2026**.
Criticism: a **decade of delay**.

140.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. South Coast Railway becomes fully operational
B. South Coast Railway is announced
C. Gazette notification of South Coast Railway
D. The Act requires Railways to examine a new zone
140.x: The correct sequence is 2014 statutory provision, 2019 announcement, 4 May 2026 Gazette notification and 1 June 2026 full operationalisation.
140.tq: Fix the earliest statutory event first, then place announcement, notification and operation.
xs: Order: **D** Act (**2014**) → **B** announced (**2019**) → **C** Gazette notification (**4 May 2026**) → **A** fully operational (**1 June 2026**) — option **(1) D, B, C, A**.
The other sequences misplace the 2014 Act or the 2019 announcement.
xa: GM appointed in **Mar 2026** without powers.
Land disputes resolved in **Apr 2026**.
⚠ **2019** = announced; **4 May 2026** = gazette notification.

140.s: What was the principal administrative fate of the Waltair division after the formation of South Coast Railway?
o: Its Andhra part became Visakhapatnam division of South Coast Railway and the rest became Rayagada division of East Coast Railway
It was abolished without creating any successor division
It remained wholly under East Coast Railway
It was transferred wholly to South Central Railway as Guntakal division
140.x: Waltair was split: its Andhra portion became the truncated Visakhapatnam division of South Coast Railway, while the remaining portion went to East Coast Railway as the new Rayagada division.
140.tq: Track the split of one old division into two new administrative units.
xs: Waltair's **Andhra part** became the truncated **Visakhapatnam division** of **SCoR**; the rest became **Rayagada division** of **ECoR** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was not abolished, kept whole by ECoR, or sent to SCR.
xa: Rayagada sits alongside **Khurda Road** and **Sambalpur** divisions in ECoR.
**ECoR** HQ: **Bhubaneswar**.
**SCR** shrinks to **three divisions**.

140.s: The Kottavalasa–Kirandul line became a major point of dispute mainly because it was regarded as:
o: The principal suburban line of Vijayawada
The only passenger line of Guntakal division
The headquarters route of South Central Railway
The revenue lifeline of Waltair division
140.x: The Kottavalasa–Kirandul line was described as the revenue lifeline of Waltair division and therefore became the central flashpoint in the reorganisation dispute.
140.tq: Identify the functional significance of the disputed asset before considering competing claims.
xs: The **Kottavalasa-Kirandul (K-K)** line is the **revenue lifeline of Waltair** division — option **(4)** is correct.
That is why it became the **flashpoint** of the split.
xa: **Odisha** claims the **entire K-K line**; the Centre favoured moving it to **Rayagada**.
ECoR **keeps K-K line revenue** via Rayagada division.
AP: Waltair earned more than **Vijayawada, Guntur and Guntakal combined**.

140.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kottavalasa-Kirandul (K-K) line dispute:
1. Odisha claimed the entire K-K line.
2. The Centre favoured moving the entire K-K line to the new Rayagada division.
3. Andhra Pradesh leaders offered the entire line to Odisha without reservation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
140.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: AP leaders offered only the Odisha stretches (Koraput-Kirandul, Kuneru-Theruvali, Koraput-Rayagada). So B; A omits 2, C and D include the false 3.
140.tq: Odisha wanted all, the Centre agreed; AP offered only the Odisha stretches.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Odisha** claimed the **entire K-K line**; the **Centre favoured** moving the whole line to **Rayagada**.
Statement 3 is wrong: AP leaders offered **only the Odisha stretches** — **Koraput-Kirandul, Kuneru-Theruvali, Koraput-Rayagada**.
xa: AP objects that **backward Uttarandhra** areas go to Rayagada.
Criticism: K-K line and Waltair revenue **ceded to Odisha**.

140.s: Andhra Pradesh leaders argued that Waltair division had earned more revenue than which combination of divisions?
140.x: The Andhra Pradesh position was that Waltair had earned more than Vijayawada, Guntur and Guntakal combined.
140.tq: Use the revenue comparison to distinguish the disputed division from the three divisions named alongside it.
xs: AP argued Waltair earned more than **Vijayawada, Guntur and Guntakal combined** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Khurda Road, Sambalpur and Rayagada** are **ECoR** divisions.
xa: Waltair's revenue lifeline is the **K-K line**.
AP offered only Odisha stretches of the K-K line.
Vijayawada division earned **~₹4,894 crore** in SCoR's first four months.

140.s: The proposed Amaravati rail link is associated with which of the following projects?
140.x: The proposed Amaravati rail link is the new Errupalem–Namburu broad-gauge line.
140.tq: Identify the project by matching its stated purpose with the correct railway line.
xs: The **Amaravati rail link** is the new **Errupalem–Namburu** broad-gauge line (~**57 km**) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kotipalli-Narsapur** is another new line; **Ramayapatnam-Kadapa** is the steel plant line.
xa: It includes a ~**3 km bridge over the Krishna**.
Farmers of **Tadikonda/Mothadaka** opted for land pooling.
A **100-m** buffer for the line is built into Amaravati **Inner Ring Road** land pooling.

140.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the high-speed rail proposals is correct?
o: The 2026–27 Budget named seven high-speed rail growth connectors, including Hyderabad–Bengaluru, Hyderabad–Chennai and Chennai–Bengaluru.
The 2026–27 Budget named five high-speed rail growth connectors, excluding all southern corridors.
Amaravati–Hyderabad was proposed as a seven-hour high-speed rail journey.
Only Amaravati–Hyderabad was identified as a high-speed rail growth connector.
140.x: The 2026–27 Budget identified seven high-speed rail growth connectors, including the three listed southern corridors. Amaravati–Hyderabad was proposed to be covered in 70 minutes, not seven hours.
140.tq: Separate the complete list-based statement from options that alter the count or travel time.
xs: Budget **2026-27** named **7 HSR "growth connectors"**, incl. **Hyderabad–Bengaluru, Hyderabad–Chennai, Chennai–Bengaluru** — option **(1)** is correct.
Amaravati-Hyderabad is proposed in **70 minutes**, not seven hours; it is not the only connector.
xa: Amaravati rail link: **Errupalem-Namburu** (~**57 km**).
AP rail outlay: **₹10,134 crore (2026-27)**.
AP network is **100% electrified**.

140.s: What was the status of electrification of the railway network in Andhra Pradesh as stated for 2026?
140.x: The railway network in Andhra Pradesh was stated to be 100% electrified.
140.tq: Test the completion status directly and avoid confusing it with the length commissioned.
xs: AP's rail network is **100% electrified** — option **(1)** is correct.
So the partial-electrification options (**75%**, **50%**, **25%**) are wrong.
xa: AP rail outlay: **₹10,134 crore** (2026-27).
**42** projects, **4,768 km**, **₹77,855 crore** sanctioned (1 Apr 2026).
**74** AP stations are under **Amrit Bharat**.

140.s: Which of the following new railway lines in Andhra Pradesh is a dedicated line approved for a steel plant?
140.x: The dedicated Ramayapatnam-Kadapa steel plant line has been approved. Kotipalli-Narsapur is another new line, Errupalem-Namburu is the Amaravati rail link, and Kottavalasa-Kirandul is the disputed Waltair revenue line.
140.tq: Steel line = Ramayapatnam-Kadapa; capital line = Errupalem-Namburu.
xs: The dedicated **Ramayapatnam-Kadapa** steel plant line has been approved — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kotipalli-Narsapur** is another new line; **Errupalem-Namburu** is the **Amaravati** link; **Kottavalasa-Kirandul** is the disputed **Waltair** revenue line.
xa: AP rail outlay: **₹10,134 crore** (2026-27).
**42** projects worth **₹77,855 crore** sanctioned.
A dedicated zone is expected to **cut freight costs** for **VCIC**.

140.s: The South Coast Railway (SCoR) became India’s 18th railway zone on:
140.x: SCoR became India’s 18th railway zone on 1 June 2026.
140.tq: Distinguish the formation date from the dates associated with Metro Railway and Sullurupeta station.
xs: **SCoR** became India's **18th zone** on **1 June 2026** — option **(4)** is correct.
**29 Dec 2010** is when **Metro Railway, Kolkata** became the **17th** zone; **22 May 2025** is Sullurupeta's opening.
xa: **Gazette notification**: **4 May 2026**.
SCoR = **newest** zone.

140.s: Which one of the following was identified as the 17th railway zone before SCoR became the 18th zone?
140.x: Metro Railway, Kolkata, was the 17th zone and dates from 29 December 2010, before SCoR became the 18th zone.
140.tq: Use the first-and-last comparison to identify the immediately preceding zone.
xs: The **17th** zone was **Metro Railway, Kolkata** (**29 Dec 2010**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**South Central** and **East Coast** Railways are older zones.
xa: **SCoR** = **newest (18th)** zone, on **1 June 2026**.
ECoR HQ: **Bhubaneswar**.
SCR shrinks to **three divisions** after SCoR.

140.s: A dedicated railway zone in Andhra Pradesh is expected to support the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor primarily by:
o: Increasing passenger fares and reducing industrial traffic
Transferring all railway revenue to Odisha
Replacing electrified railway lines with road transport
Cutting freight costs and improving port connectivity
140.x: The dedicated zone is expected to cut freight costs for the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor and improve port connectivity.
140.tq: Link the institutional reform to its stated economic and logistics outcomes.
xs: A dedicated zone is expected to **cut freight costs** for **VCIC** and **improve port connectivity** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is described as a "**multimodal logistics hub**".
xa: Schedule XIII also mentions a **Vizag-Chennai corridor** study.
**₹300-crore** Visakhapatnam station yard remodelling approved.
Dedicated **Ramayapatnam-Kadapa** steel plant line approved.

141.s:
Match the Thirteenth Schedule commitment with its associated location or status:

a. Integrated steel plant
b. Crude oil refinery and petrochemical complex
c. New railway zone
d. Metro rail

i. Kakinada region
ii. South Coast Railway with headquarters at Visakhapatnam
iii. Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada–Guntur–Tenali region
iv. YSR Kadapa district

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
141.x: The steel plant is associated with YSR Kadapa, the refinery and petrochemical complex with Kakinada, the railway zone with Visakhapatnam headquarters, and metro rail with the Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada–Guntur–Tenali region.
141.tq: Start with the distinctive railway-zone and steel-plant locations, then complete the remaining pairs.
xs: **Steel plant — YSR Kadapa**, **refinery — Kakinada region**, **railway zone — SCoR, HQ Visakhapatnam**, **metro — Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada–Guntur–Tenali** — option **(1) a–iv, b–i, c–ii, d–iii**.
The other codes shuffle these locations.
xa: ⚠ Act named **SAIL**, actual plant = **JSW**; Act named **IOC or HPCL**, actual refinery = **BPCL**.
**SCoR** became operational on **1 Jun 2026** (announced **2019**).
The metro feasibility was to be done **within one year**; Vizag metro is still before the Centre (2026).

141.s: Which of the following Thirteenth Schedule commitments was dropped as non-feasible?
o: Examination of a new railway zone
New major port at Duggirajupatnam with Phase I by the end of 2018
Expansion of Visakhapatnam airport to international standards
141.x: The proposed new major port at Duggirajupatnam, for which Phase I was envisaged by the end of 2018, was dropped as non-feasible.
141.tq: Identify the commitment whose status is cancellation rather than delay or completion.
xs: The **new major port at Duggirajupatnam** (**Phase I by end-2018**) was **dropped as non-feasible** — option **(3)** is correct.
The railway zone is operational, all three airports are international, and the Vizag metro is still before the Centre — none was dropped.
xa: The site is now a **VPA-APMB greenfield port + shipbuilding cluster** (2026).
The State built **Ramayapatnam** as a substitute greenfield port.
⚠ Duggirajupatnam was the only port the Act said GoI "**shall develop**".

141.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Greenfield refinery-petrochemical complex — BPCL refinery near Ramayapatnam
2. VCIC — ADB-funded project with slow progress
3. New railway zone — SCoR operational from 1 June 2026
4. Metro rail in Visakhapatnam — Already operational throughout the city

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
141.x: The first three pairs are correct. The Visakhapatnam metro project was still before the Centre in 2026 and was not operational throughout the city.
141.tq: Reject the completed-status trap attached to an ongoing project.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Refinery → **BPCL** near **Ramayapatnam**; **VCIC** → **ADB-funded**, slow progress; railway zone → **SCoR** operational **1 Jun 2026**.
Pair 4 is wrong: the **Vizag metro** is **still before the Centre** (2026).
xa: VCIC is modelled on the **DMIC**.
Vizag metro: **4 corridors**, **76.70 km**, **₹11,498 crore**.
BPCL refinery final clearances pending (Sep 2026).

141.s: Which set of airports was specifically identified for expansion to international standards?
141.x: The commitment covered the airports at Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati. All three are described as international airports in the stated status update.
141.tq: Recall the complete three-airport set rather than a partial list.
xs: The Act named **Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati** airports for expansion to international standard — option **(1)** is correct.
All three are now **international airports** (ES 2025-26).
xa: The new **Bhogapuram** airport was dedicated on **1 Aug 2026**.
Other Schedule XIII items: **Duggirajupatnam** port, **YSR** steel plant, **refinery**, **VCIC**, **railway zone**, **metro**.
The Vizag metro is still before the Centre.

141.s: The new airport dedicated on 1 August 2026 is:
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram
141.x: The Bhogapuram airport was dedicated on 1 August 2026 as the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport.
141.tq: Match the new airport with its official name and location.
xs: The new **Bhogapuram** airport was dedicated on **1 Aug 2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Visakhapatnam**, **Vijayawada** and **Tirupati** were existing airports expanded to international standard.
xa: The Act asked for expanding **Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Tirupati** airports.
**SCoR** became operational on **1 Jun 2026**.
JSW Kadapa plant works were launched on **3 Jul 2026**.

141.s:
Under the educational commitments associated with the Thirteenth Schedule, which of the following was NOT included as one of the institutions proposed for Andhra Pradesh?

1. Indian Institute of Technology
2. National Institute of Technology
3. Indian Institute of Management
4. National Institute of Fashion Technology

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
141.x: The educational commitments included one each of an IIT, NIT, IIM, IISER, Central University, Petroleum University, Agricultural University and IIIT, besides an AIIMS-type hospital, Tribal Universities and NIDM. National Institute of Fashion Technology was not listed.
141.tq: Find the institution outside the specified commitment list.
xs: Only **4** — the **National Institute of Fashion Technology** — was not included — option **(3) 4 only**.
The list: one each of **IIT, NIT, IIM, IISER, Central University, Petroleum University, Agricultural University, IIIT**.
xa: Also an **AIIMS-type** super-specialty hospital, a **Tribal University** in each State, and **NIDM** in AP.
They were to come up in the **12th and 13th Plan** periods.
**11** premier institutions are now functional.

141.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to higher educational institutions in Andhra Pradesh:

1. IIT Tirupati — Yerpedu
2. IIM Visakhapatnam — Gambheeram
3. NIT Andhra Pradesh — Tadepalligudem
4. IISER Tirupati — Kurnool

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
141.x: IIT Tirupati is at Yerpedu, IIM Visakhapatnam is at Gambheeram and NIT Andhra Pradesh is at Tadepalligudem. IISER Tirupati is also at Yerpedu, not Kurnool.
141.tq: Use location discrimination among closely related institutions.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
**IIT Tirupati — Yerpedu**; **IIM Visakhapatnam — Gambheeram**; **NIT AP — Tadepalligudem** (West Godavari).
Pair 4 is wrong: **IISER Tirupati** is also at **Yerpedu**; **Kurnool** hosts the **IIITDM**.
xa: IIT Tirupati campus: **548 acres**; IIM Visakhapatnam: **241 acres**.
**AIIMS Mangalagiri**: **183 acres**, started **2018**.
**NIDM** Southern Campus: **Kondapalli** (near Vijayawada).

141.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
141.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri is associated with the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY), not the IIM Act, 2017. NIT Andhra Pradesh and IISER Tirupati are linked with the NITSER Act, while IIPE is linked with the IIPE Act, 2017.
141.tq: Spot the swapped legal basis among similar institutional entries.
xs: "**AIIMS Mangalagiri — IIM Act, 2017**" is wrong — so option **(1)** is the answer.
AIIMS Mangalagiri (**2018**) is under **PMSSY**; the **IIM Act, 2017** covers **IIM Visakhapatnam**.
The others are correct: **IIPE — IIPE Act, 2017**; **IISER Tirupati** and **NIT AP — NITSER Act**.
xa: AIIMS Mangalagiri: **183 acres**.
IIPE is at **Visakhapatnam** (2016).
NIT AP is at **Tadepalligudem**.

141.s:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Central Universities (Amendment) Act, 2019 created both the Central University of AP and the Central Tribal University of AP.
2. The Central University of AP is located at Janthaluru.
3. The Central Tribal University of AP was first proposed near Visakhapatnam and later moved to Vizianagaram.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: All three statements are correct. The 2019 Amendment Act created both universities; CUAP is at Janthaluru, while the proposed location of CTUAP shifted from near Visakhapatnam to Vizianagaram.
141.tq: Combine the establishing law, present location and relocation history.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **Central Universities (Amendment) Act, 2019** created **both CUAP and CTUAP** (APPSC 2018 key); CUAP is at **Janthaluru**; CTUAP moved from near **Visakhapatnam** to **Vizianagaram**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap**: the **Central Universities Act, 2009** is the **parent Act** it amended.
CTUAP: **Marrivalasa/Chinamedapalli**, **Dattirajeru** mandal (**490 acres**).
CUAP is in **Anantapuramu** district.

141.s:
Consider the following statements about national institutions in Andhra Pradesh:
1. IIITDM at Kurnool is an Institution of National Importance under the Ministry of Education.
2. The NIDM Southern Campus at Kondapalli, near Vijayawada, is under the Ministry of Education.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
141.x: Statement 1 is correct: IIITDM Kurnool is an INI under the Ministry of Education. Statement 2 is wrong: the NIDM Southern Campus at Kondapalli is under the Ministry of Home Affairs. So A; B and C accept the wrong ministry, D rejects the correct statement 1.
141.tq: Disaster management = Home Affairs; the place is right, the ministry is the trap.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **IIITDM Kurnool** is an **INI** under the **Ministry of Education** — correct.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **NIDM Southern Campus** at **Kondapalli** is under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
xa: The IIITDM is the "**IIIT**" promised in Schedule XIII.
**11** premier institutions are now functional.

141.s:
Consider the following statements about the education commitments in the Thirteenth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. The institutions were to be set up during the 12th and 13th Plan periods.
2. A Tribal University was promised in each of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
3. Eleven premier institutions are now functional in Andhra Pradesh.
4. The NIDM campus was promised for Telangana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: 12th and 13th Plan periods, a Tribal University in each State, 11 institutions functional. Statement 4 is wrong: NIDM was promised in AP (Southern Campus at Kondapalli). So B; A omits 3, C and D include the false 4.
141.tq: NIDM in AP; Tribal University in both States.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Institutions in the **12th and 13th Plan** periods; a **Tribal University** in **each of AP and Telangana**; **11** institutions now functional.
Statement 4 is wrong: **NIDM** was promised in **AP** (Southern Campus at **Kondapalli**).
xa: AP's Tribal University: **CTUAP**, **Vizianagaram** (started **2019**).
NIDM is under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.

141.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, the Steel Authority of India Limited was required to examine, within six months, the feasibility of an integrated steel plant in:
141.x: The Act required SAIL to examine within six months the feasibility of integrated steel plants in YSR district of Andhra Pradesh and Khammam district of Telangana.
141.tq: Recall both locations attached to the statutory feasibility requirement.
xs: **SAIL** was to examine, within **six months**, integrated steel plants in **YSR district** (AP) and **Khammam district** (Telangana) — option **(4)** is correct.
The other district pairs are not in the notes.
xa: ⚠ Act named **SAIL**; the actual plant is by **JSW**.
The State formed its own SPV, **AP High Grade Steels Ltd** (**2018**).
JSW plant works launched **3 Jul 2026**.

141.s: On 3 July 2026, construction was launched for the JSW Rayalaseema Integrated Steel Plant at:
141.x: Construction was launched at Sunnapurallapalli and Peddandluru villages in the Jammalamadugu constituency of Kadapa on 3 July 2026.
141.tq: Recall the two construction-site villages as a pair.
xs: JSW plant works were launched at **Sunnapurallapalli and Peddandluru** villages, **Jammalamadugu** constituency, Kadapa (**3 Jul 2026**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Marrivalasa/Chinamedapalli** = CTUAP; **Gambheeram** = IIM; **Kondapalli** = NIDM; **M. Kambala Dinne** = 2018 stone; **Yerpedu** = IIT/IISER.
xa: Plant name: **JSW Rayalaseema Integrated Steel Plant**.
Technology: **scrap-based Electric Arc Furnace** green steel.
Water: **2 tmc ft**/year from **Gandikota** via a **15-km** pipeline.

141.s:
Consider the following statements about the JSW Rayalaseema Integrated Steel Plant in Kadapa:
1. Its developer is AP High Grade Steels Ltd.
2. It is a scrap-based Electric Arc Furnace green-steel plant.
3. It is to draw 2 tmc ft of water a year from Gandikota.
4. Its cost is Rs 16,350 crore in two phases (Rs 4,500 crore in Phase I and Rs 11,850 crore later).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the developer is JSW Andhra Pradesh Steel Ltd; AP High Grade Steels Ltd was the State's 2018 SPV. Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct (scrap-based EAF, 2 tmc ft from Gandikota, Rs 16,350 crore = 4,500 + 11,850). So B; A leaves out 4, C and D include the false 1.
141.tq: AP High Grade Steels (2018 SPV) is not the JSW developer.
xs: Statements **2, 3 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: the developer is **JSW Andhra Pradesh Steel Ltd**; **AP High Grade Steels Ltd** was the State's **2018** SPV.
**Scrap-based EAF** green steel; **2 tmc ft** from **Gandikota**; **₹16,350 crore** = **₹4,500 crore** + **₹11,850 crore**.
xa: Land: **1,100 acres**.
Commercial production targeted **2028**.

141.s: In December 2018, the foundation stone for the Kadapa steel plant was laid by CM N. Chandrababu Naidu at:
141.x: The Dec 2018 stone was laid at M. Kambala Dinne in Mylavaram mandal (APPSC 2018 key). Sunnapurallapalli is where JSW construction began on 3 Jul 2026, Gandikota supplies the plant's water, and Yerpedu hosts IIT and IISER Tirupati.
141.tq: 2018 stone = M. Kambala Dinne; 2026 JSW = Sunnapurallapalli/Peddandluru.
xs: The **Dec 2018** stone was laid at **M. Kambala Dinne, Mylavaram mandal** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC 2018 key).
**Sunnapurallapalli** is the **2026 JSW** site; **Gandikota** supplies water; **Yerpedu** hosts IIT/IISER Tirupati.
xa: It was laid by CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu**.
Stones were laid again in **2019 and 2023** by CM **Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy**.
⚠ 2018 = **M. Kambala Dinne**; 2026 = **Sunnapurallapalli**.

141.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, which port was specified for development as a new major port by the Government of India?
141.x: The Act states that the Government of India shall develop a new major port at Duggirajupatnam. It was the only port named in the Schedule for this purpose.
141.tq: Directly identify the exact name appearing in a statutory commitment.
xs: The Act said GoI "**shall develop**" a new major port at **Dugarajapatnam** (Duggirajupatnam) — option **(3)** is correct.
It was the **only port named** in the Schedule; **Ramayapatnam** was the State's later substitute.
xa: It was later **dropped as non-feasible**.
Revived in **2026** as a **greenfield port + shipbuilding cluster** in **Tirupati district**.
⚠ "Shall develop" (port) vs "examine" (other items).

141.s: Which port was developed by the State of Andhra Pradesh as a substitute greenfield port after Dugarajapatnam was found non-feasible?
141.x: After Dugarajapatnam was dropped on feasibility grounds, the State developed Ramayapatnam as the substitute greenfield port.
141.tq: Test the replacement relationship between two closely associated projects.
xs: The State built **Ramayapatnam Port** as the substitute greenfield port — option **(2)** is correct.
**Mulapeta** and **Machilipatnam** got Phase-II approvals alongside Ramayapatnam, but were not the substitute.
xa: Developer: **Ramayapatnam Port Development Corporation Ltd (RPDCL)**.
Progress: **81%** (Aug 2026).

141.s:
With reference to the proposed Dugarajapatnam greenfield port and shipbuilding cluster, consider the following statements:
1. The SPV is a 50:50 joint venture of the Visakhapatnam Port Authority and the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board.
2. About 3,500 acres have been identified for the project.
3. The cluster is estimated to be worth ₹30,000 crore.
4. Andhra Pradesh is the only State selected for a national shipbuilding cluster.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the project is one of five national cluster sites; the others are in Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Odisha and Maharashtra.
141.tq: Find the incorrect membership statement in a list-based question.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
SPV is a **50:50 JV of VPA and APMB**; ~**3,500 acres** identified; cluster worth **₹30,000 crore**.
Statement 4 is wrong: it is **one of five** national cluster sites (others: **TN, Gujarat, Odisha, Maharashtra**).
xa: SPV name: **National Shipbuilding and Heavy Industries Park Andhra Pradesh Ltd**.
Under the **Shipbuilding Development Scheme (SbDS)**.

141.s: Dugarajapatnam, identified for a greenfield port and shipbuilding cluster under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme, is in:
141.x: The greenfield port and shipbuilding cluster at Dugarajapatnam is in Tirupati district.
141.tq: Match the named project location with the correct district.
xs: Dugarajapatnam is in **Tirupati district** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Prakasam** is the present district of **Ramayapatnam**.
xa: G.O. of **2 Jan 2026** revived it as a greenfield port + shipbuilding cluster.
It is one of **five** national cluster sites.
Cluster worth **₹30,000 crore**.

141.s: Ramayapatnam Port is presently located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
141.x: Ramayapatnam Port is presently in Prakasam district. Earlier material placed it in SPS Nellore district before district boundaries were redrawn.
141.tq: Separate the current district from the earlier district classification.
xs: **Ramayapatnam Port** is now in **Prakasam** district (2026) — option **(4)** is correct.
2024-25 data placed it in **SPS Nellore** district (**Ulavapadu** mandal) before boundaries were redrawn.
xa: Location: **93 km** north of **Krishnapatnam**; **5 km** east of **Thettu** on **NH-16**.
Nearest station: **Thettu**.
The **BPCL** refinery is proposed near it, between **Prakasam and Nellore**.

141.s: The State Special Purpose Vehicle responsible for developing Ramayapatnam Port is:
o: Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Ltd
141.x: Ramayapatnam Port is being developed by the State SPV Ramayapatnam Port Development Corporation Ltd, permitted in February 2020.
141.tq: Identify the project-specific developer rather than the supervising authority.
xs: Ramayapatnam is developed by the State SPV **Ramayapatnam Port Development Corporation Ltd (RPDCL)** — option **(3)** is correct.
**APMB** and **VPA** are partners in the **Dugarajapatnam** SPV, not Ramayapatnam.
xa: Permitted **Feb 2020**; contract signed **30 Jul 2021**.
**₹354.23 crore** variation works cleared (Cabinet).

141.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, IOC or HPCL was required to examine within six months the establishment of a:
o: Greenfield crude refinery and petrochemical complex
Gas-based power plant and LNG terminal
141.x: The Act required Indian Oil Corporation or Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited to examine, within six months, a greenfield crude refinery and petrochemical complex.
141.tq: Identify the precise statutory obligation and its implementing entities.
xs: **IOC or HPCL** was to examine, within **six months**, a **greenfield crude refinery and petrochemical complex** — option **(1)** is correct.
The other facilities are not in the Act.
xa: ⚠ Act named **IOC or HPCL**; actual refinery = **BPCL**.
BPCL complex: near **Ramayapatnam**, **9 MTPA**, ~**₹1.45 lakh crore**.
**Kakinada** lies in the **Visakhapatnam-Kakinada PCPIR**.

141.s: The BPCL greenfield refinery-cum-petrochemical complex is proposed near Ramayapatnam Port between which districts?
141.x: The BPCL complex is proposed near Ramayapatnam Port, between Prakasam and Nellore districts, in the villages of Chevuru and Ravuru.
141.tq: Test the location by pairing the project with its two neighbouring districts.
xs: The **BPCL** complex is proposed near **Ramayapatnam** port, **between Prakasam and Nellore** districts — option **(3)** is correct.
Villages: **Chevuru and Ravuru**.
xa: Capacity **9 MTPA**; ~**5.4 MT** of Euro-6 fuels.
**75%** of **6,000 acres** handed over.
Final environmental clearance expected **end-Sep 2026**.

141.s: Which statement regarding the proposed Kakinada petrochemical facility is correct?
o: It lies outside the Visakhapatnam-Kakinada PCPIR and has received central viability-gap funding.
Its MoUs were cleared by the State pollution board, and Kakinada lies in the Visakhapatnam-Kakinada PCPIR.
It is the BPCL refinery located between Prakasam and Nellore districts.
It was established under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme.
141.x: MoUs for a greenfield petrochemical facility near Kakinada were cleared by the State pollution board. Kakinada is located in the Visakhapatnam-Kakinada PCPIR; the available information does not specify viability-gap-funding figures.
141.tq: Reject options that merge the Kakinada facility with the separate BPCL refinery project.
xs: **Kakinada** MoUs were **cleared by the State pollution board**, and Kakinada lies in the **Visakhapatnam-Kakinada PCPIR** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option 1 contradicts the PCPIR fact; option 3 describes the **BPCL** refinery; **SbDS** is the shipbuilding scheme.
xa: The Act's refinery item named **IOC or HPCL**.
BPCL's complex is near **Ramayapatnam** (**9 MTPA**).
The refinery commitment's location in the Act table: **Kakinada** region.

141.s: Which organisation is the implementing agency for the metro rail projects in Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada?
o: Andhra Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Ltd
141.x: The implementing agency for the metro rail projects in both cities is Andhra Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.
141.tq: Identify the designated implementing agency rather than an earlier consulting or project arrangement.
xs: The implementing agency is **Andhra Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (APMRCL)** — option **(3)** is correct.
**UMTC** prepared a DPR under an older, **superseded** IL&FS JV arrangement.
xa: Vizag metro: **4 corridors**, **76.70 km**, **₹11,498 crore**.
A **double-decker** metro-cum-road corridor on **NH-16** is being surveyed.
The Act asked for metro feasibility **within one year**.

141.s: Which of the following correctly expresses the industrial-cluster linkage in southern Andhra Pradesh?
o: Kadapa steel, Machilipatnam Port and Visakhapatnam Metro are linked by a new rail line.
Kadapa steel, Ramayapatnam Port and the BPCL refinery are linked by a new rail line.
Ramayapatnam Port, Mulapeta Port and Bhogapuram airport are linked by a new rail line.
Dugarajapatnam Port, Bhogapuram airport and Kakinada PCPIR are linked by a new rail line.
141.x: Kadapa steel, Ramayapatnam Port and the BPCL refinery are linked by a new rail line, forming a southern Andhra Pradesh industrial cluster.
141.tq: Recognise the infrastructure linkage that defines the regional industrial cluster.
xs: **Kadapa steel**, **Ramayapatnam port** and the **BPCL refinery** are linked by a **new rail line** → a **southern AP industrial cluster** — option **(2)** is correct.
The other combinations include sites (Bhogapuram, Machilipatnam, Kakinada) outside this cluster.
xa: The JSW plant draws water from **Gandikota**.
BPCL refinery lies between **Prakasam and Nellore**.
Ramayapatnam: **81%** progress (Aug 2026).

142.s: Under the Thirteenth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Government of India was required to examine the feasibility of which industrial corridor within six months?
142.x: The Thirteenth Schedule directed the Government of India to examine the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor within six months.
142.tq: Identify the specific statutory obligation and avoid confusing the proposed corridor with its model corridor.
xs: The **Thirteenth Schedule** asks GoI to examine the **Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor** within **six months** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The VCIC was to be examined **on the lines of the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC)**: DMIC is the model, not the corridor to be examined.
**CBIC** and the **Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor** are the other two AP corridors, not the Schedule's six-month item.
xa: ⚠ The Act only says "examine within **six months**" — it fixes **no deadline for completion** of the corridor.
The same Act asks GoI to **take steps** for **rapid rail and road connectivity** from AP's new capital to **Hyderabad** and other Telangana cities.
The State law for corridors is the **A.P. Industrial Corridor Development Authority Act, 2017**, which creates **AP-ICDA**.

142.s: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor was proposed to be developed on the lines of which corridor?
142.x: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor was to be examined on the lines of the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor.
142.tq: Distinguish the parent corridor from the model on which the project is based.
xs: The VCIC was to be developed **on the lines of the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC)** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **East Coast Economic Corridor (ECEC)** is the VCIC's **parent** corridor (VCIC is its first phase), not its model.
**CBIC** and the **Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor** are fellow AP corridors, not the template.
xa: Exam trio: VCIC **funded by ADB**, **part of ECEC**, **modelled on DMIC**.
⚠ **DMIC** runs on the **Western DFC** with **Japanese aid**; VCIC is **ADB**-funded and port-led.
The VCIC is about **800 km** long.

142.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor:
1. It is approximately 800 km long.
2. It constitutes the first phase or segment of the East Coast Economic Corridor.
3. It is linked with the Act East and Make in India initiatives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All three statements are correct. The corridor is about 800 km long, forms the first phase of the East Coast Economic Corridor, and is linked with Act East and Make in India.
142.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the VCIC is **~800 km** long — correct.
Statement 2: it is the **first phase/segment** of the **East Coast Economic Corridor (ECEC)** — correct.
Statement 3: it is linked with **Act East** and **Make in India**, connecting India with **ASEAN/East Asia** — correct.
xa: The **ECEC** is **India's first coastal economic corridor**, running **Kolkata to Tuticorin**.
AP has **three industrial corridors**: **VCIC**, **CBIC** and the **Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor**.
⚠ **CBIC** has Japanese (**JICA**) support, while VCIC is **ADB**-funded.

142.s: The East Coast Economic Corridor, of which the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor is the first phase, extends from:
142.x: The East Coast Economic Corridor is described as extending from Kolkata to Tuticorin; some descriptions refer to its southern end as Kanyakumari.
142.tq: Test the geographical endpoints directly and distinguish the parent corridor from its first phase.
xs: The **East Coast Economic Corridor** runs from **Kolkata to Tuticorin** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes give the southern end as **Kanyakumari**, but most say **Tuticorin**; option (4) adds "only", which makes it wrong.
**Visakhapatnam to Chennai** is just the **VCIC**, the ECEC's **first phase** — not the whole corridor.
xa: The ECEC is **India's first coastal economic corridor**.
VCIC (**~800 km**) is modelled on the **DMIC** and funded by the **ADB**.
The corridor ties in with **Act East** and **Make in India**.

142.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the East Coast Economic Corridor?
o: A corridor confined to Andhra Pradesh
A corridor developed only for the automobile sector
India's first exclusively inland freight corridor
142.x: The East Coast Economic Corridor is described as India's first coastal economic corridor.
142.tq: Use the defining descriptor and reject options that narrow the corridor without support.
xs: The **East Coast Economic Corridor** is **India's first coastal economic corridor** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It stretches **Kolkata to Tuticorin**, so it is neither confined to AP nor an inland freight corridor.
Its first phase is the **Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC)**.
xa: VCIC links to **Act East** and **Make in India**, connecting India with **ASEAN/East Asia**.
⚠ ECEC end-point: **Tuticorin** in most notes, **Kanyakumari** in some.
The **Budget 2026-27** also mentions an **East Coast Industrial Corridor**.

142.s: The policy-based loan component of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor financing is intended for:
o: Land acquisition and steel-cluster expansion only
Ease of doing business and institutional reform
Construction of the East Coast railway network
142.x: The USD 125 million policy-based loan, entirely from the ADB, funds ease of doing business and institutional reform.
142.tq: Link the loan type with its policy purpose rather than with physical infrastructure.
xs: The **Policy-Based Loan** funds **ease of doing business (EoDB)** and **institutional reform** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is **USD 125 mn**, **100% ADB**, with **nil** GoAP share.
Physical works (₹**5,000 crore**) are backed by a separate **₹3,300 crore ADB loan in two tranches**, not by this loan.
xa: Whole programme: **USD 840 million** = ADB **$625 mn** + GoAP **$215 mn (25.6%)**.
Tranche-I and the Policy-Based Loan were signed on **23 Feb 2017** by **DEA, ADB and GoAP**.
⚠ Some notes (Jan 2026) name **JICA** for VCIC; most say **ADB** — follow ADB.

142.s: Which of the following statements best reflects the reported implementation status of the industrial corridor?
o: Development was described as rapid, with no further funding demand from industry.
Development was cancelled because ADB withdrew its entire loan.
Development was described as slow, and industry sought a special fund for VCIC and HBIC plug-and-play infrastructure.
Development was completed, and industry sought funds only for new expressways.
142.x: Implementation was described as slow, while CII sought a special fund for VCIC and HBIC plug-and-play infrastructure before the 2026–27 Budget.
142.tq: Combine the progress assessment with the industry’s funding demand.
xs: VCIC progress is described as **slow**, and industry sought a **special fund for VCIC and HBIC plug-and-play infrastructure** — option **(3)**.
The demand came from **CII** before **Budget 2026-27**.
ADB did not withdraw: Tranche-I works (~**₹2,300 crore**) are at an **advanced stage**.
xa: "**VCIC slow**" is listed among the criticisms and debates on the topic.
The **BHAVYA** scheme (**2026-27 to 2031-32**, **₹33,660 crore**) plans **100 plug-and-play parks**.
Six **BHAVYA** parks are proposed in AP, with **APIIC** as nodal agency.

142.s: Which pair of Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor nodes was identified for long-term phased development?
142.x: Donakonda and Machilipatnam were identified for long-term phased development.
142.tq: Match the special status of the nodes with the correct pair.
xs: **Donakonda** and **Machilipatnam** are slated for **long-term phased development** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The ADB-identified nodes are **Visakhapatnam, Machilipatnam, Donakonda** and **Srikalahasti-Chittoor**.
**Kopparthy** and **Visakhapatnam** are among the three nodes now being developed (over **33,000 acres**).
xa: **Kopparthy** (YSR Kadapa) Phase-1 is **2,596 acres**, with CCEA approval on **28 Aug 2024**.
**Visakhapatnam** node: **Rambilli + Nakkapalli** clusters give about **49%** of corridor output.
**30%** of the node area is developed first as a "start-up" area.

142.s:
Consider the following statements about the nodes of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor:
1. The Visakhapatnam node, with its Rambilli and Nakkapalli clusters, accounts for about 49% of the corridor's output.
2. The Chittoor node has a start-up area of 2,628 acres.
3. Trunk infrastructure at the Kopparthy node is funded through JICA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
142.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (Rambilli + Nakkapalli about 49% of output; Chittoor start-up area 2,628 acres). Statement 3 is wrong: Kopparthy's trunk infrastructure (about Rs 1,264 crore) comes through NICDIT; JICA backs CBIC, and VCIC itself is ADB-funded. So B; A omits 2, C and D include the false 3.
142.tq: VCIC = ADB, CBIC = JICA, node trunk infrastructure = NICDIT.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Rambilli + Nakkapalli** clusters of the Visakhapatnam node give about **49%** of corridor output — correct.
Statement 2: the **Chittoor** (Srikalahasti-Yerpedu) start-up area is **2,628 acres**, ₹463 crore — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: Kopparthy's trunk infrastructure (~**₹1,264 crore**) comes via **NICDIT**; **JICA** backs **CBIC**.
xa: ⚠ **2,002** acres = Bulk Drug Park (Vizag); **2,628** = Chittoor start-up area; **2,596** = Kopparthy Phase-1.
**Kopparthy** targets about **₹8,860 crore** of investment.
Visakhapatnam also has a **steel cluster** Phase-1 of **2,200 acres** (+4,000 planned).

142.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the three industrial corridors being implemented in Andhra Pradesh?
o: CBIC, East Coast Economic Corridor and Delhi-Mumbai Corridor
VCIC, CBIC and Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor
142.x: The three corridors are VCIC, CBIC and the Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.
142.tq: Use a complete list-recall question and reject lists containing corridors outside the stated set.
xs: AP's three industrial corridors are **VCIC**, **CBIC** and the **Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor** — option **(2)**.
**ECEC** is the parent coastal corridor of VCIC, and **DMIC** is the model it copies — neither is one of the three AP corridors.
xa: **VCIC = ADB**; **CBIC = JICA**; **DMIC = Japanese aid**.
CII sought a special fund for **VCIC + HBIC** plug-and-play infrastructure.
The **Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway** is a priority link of **CBIC**.

142.s: Which institution is the funding partner of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor?
142.x: The Asian Development Bank is the funding partner of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor.
142.tq: Use the funding-agency association rather than the country association of other corridors.
xs: The **Asian Development Bank (ADB)** is the VCIC's funding partner — so option **(4)** is correct.
ADB gives **$625 mn** of the **$840 mn** programme; GoAP adds **$215 mn**.
**JICA** (Japan) supports **CBIC**, not VCIC; some notes (Jan 2026) name JICA for VCIC, but most say **ADB**.
xa: The **World Bank and ADB** are named for **Amaravati capital** loans.
Exam trio: VCIC funded by **ADB**, part of **ECEC**, modelled on **DMIC**.
**DMIC** runs on the **Western DFC** with **Japanese aid**.

142.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the ADB-identified Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor nodes?
142.x: The ADB-identified nodes listed are Visakhapatnam, Machilipatnam, Donakonda and Srikalahasti-Chittoor. Orvakal is associated with the Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.
142.tq: Find the item belonging to another corridor by separating node lists.
xs: **Orvakal** is not an ADB-identified VCIC node — so option **(2)** is correct.
The ADB-identified nodes are **Visakhapatnam, Machilipatnam, Donakonda** and **Srikalahasti-Chittoor**.
**Orvakal** appears as a node whose trunk infrastructure **NICDIT** funds, along with **Kopparthy** and **Krishnapatnam**.
xa: **Donakonda** and **Machilipatnam** are for **long-term phased** development.
The three nodes being developed (APSES 2024-25) are **Visakhapatnam**, **Chittoor** and **Kopparthy**, over **33,000 acres**.
Chittoor node is also given as **Chittoor-South + Naidupeta**.

142.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with the institutional arrangement for the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor?
1. Executing agency — Department of Industries and Commerce
2. Project Management Unit — under the Commissioner of Industries
3. Project Implementation Units — four, including APIIC, APRDC and AP Transco
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All three statements correctly describe the institutional arrangement: the Department of Industries and Commerce is the executing agency, the PMU is under the Commissioner of Industries, and there are four PIUs including APIIC, APRDC and AP Transco.
142.tq: Match each institutional level with its designated agency or unit.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the **executing agency** is the **Department of Industries and Commerce** — correct.
Statement 2: the **PMU** is under the **Commissioner of Industries** — correct.
Statement 3: there are **four PIUs** — **APIIC, APRDC, AP Transco** and **GVMC** — correct.
xa: **AP-ICDA** is set up under the **A.P. Industrial Corridor Development Authority Act, 2017**.
**APIIC**, incorporated **1973**, is the State nodal agency for industrial parks and corridor land.
**NICDIT** funds node trunk infrastructure (Kopparthy, Krishnapatnam, Orvakal).

142.s: Which one of the following correctly describes NICDC?
o: It is the State nodal agency for industrial-park land in Andhra Pradesh.
It funds only road projects and has no role in industrial parks.
It was established under the A.P. Industrial Corridor Development Authority Act, 2017.
It was incorporated in January 2008 and was formerly known as DMICDC.
142.x: NICDC was incorporated in January 2008, was formerly known as DMICDC, and functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry through DPIIT.
142.tq: Use the incorporation date and former name to identify the correct institution.
xs: **NICDC** was incorporated in **January 2008** and was formerly **DMICDC** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It works under the **Ministry of Commerce & Industry (DPIIT)**, implements the **NICDP** and the new **BHAVYA** scheme.
The State nodal agency for park land is **APIIC**; the body under the **2017 Act** is **AP-ICDA**.
xa: ⚠ **NICDC** = Corporation (ex-DMICDC, 2008); **NICDIT** = **Trust** that funds trunk infrastructure.
NICDP: **11 corridors**; in **Aug 2024** the Centre approved **12 more projects**, total **20**.
**BHAVYA**: **₹33,660 crore**, **100** plug-and-play parks.

142.s: Which institution is responsible for funding node trunk infrastructure at Kopparthy, Krishnapatnam and Orvakal?
142.x: NICDIT funds node trunk infrastructure at the Kopparthy, Krishnapatnam and Orvakal nodes.
142.tq: Match the institution with its specific funding function and nodes.
xs: **NICDIT** funds node trunk infrastructure at **Kopparthy, Krishnapatnam** and **Orvakal** — so option **(1)** is correct.
NICDIT is the National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation **Trust**; it has **₹3,000 crore** in BE 2026-27.
**NICDC** is the corporation (ex-DMICDC); **APIIC** is the State land agency; **GVMC** is one of the VCIC's PIUs.
xa: ⚠ NICDC = **Corporation**; NICDIT = **Trust**.
Kopparthy trunk infrastructure via NICDIT: ~**₹1,264 crore**.
Under **BHAVYA**, the **100** parks are built through **NICDIT-State SPVs**.

142.s:
Consider the following statements about the AP Industrial Corridor Development Authority (AP-ICDA):
1. It was set up under the A.P. Industrial Corridor Development Authority Act, 2017.
2. Industrial parks under it are notified under Section 5 of that Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
142.x: Statement 1 is correct: AP-ICDA rests on the A.P. Industrial Corridor Development Authority Act, 2017. Statement 2 is wrong: parks are notified under Section 3 of the Act, not Section 5. So A; B and C accept the wrong section, D rejects the correct statement 1.
142.tq: AP-ICDA Act 2017, parks notified under Section 3.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **AP-ICDA** is created by the **A.P. Industrial Corridor Development Authority Act, 2017** — correct.
Statement 2 is wrong: industrial parks are notified under **Section 3** of the Act, not Section 5.
xa: **APIIC** (incorporated **1973**) is the State nodal agency for industrial parks and corridor land.
The VCIC's executing agency is the **Department of Industries and Commerce**.
**NICDC** is the national corporation (ex-**DMICDC**, **Jan 2008**).

142.s:
Consider the following statements about the BHAVYA park scheme:
1. It runs from 2026-27 to 2031-32 with an outlay of Rs 33,660 crore.
2. It is to create 100 plug-and-play parks through NICDIT-State SPVs.
3. Ten new parks have been proposed in Andhra Pradesh under it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
142.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (2026-27 to 2031-32, Rs 33,660 crore; 100 plug-and-play parks via NICDIT-State SPVs). Statement 3 is wrong: six new AP parks are proposed, not ten. So B; A omits 2, C and D include the false 3.
142.tq: BHAVYA: 100 parks nationally, six proposed in AP.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **BHAVYA** runs **2026-27 to 2031-32** with **₹33,660 crore** — correct.
Statement 2: it creates **100 plug-and-play parks** through **NICDIT-State SPVs** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: **six** new AP parks are proposed, not ten.
xa: BHAVYA is implemented by **NICDC** under **DPIIT**.
**APIIC** is the nodal agency for the BHAVYA parks in AP.
NICDIT has **₹3,000 crore** in BE 2026-27.

142.s: Among the three industrial corridors in Andhra Pradesh, which one is supported by Japan (JICA)?
142.x: CBIC has Japanese (JICA) support. VCIC is ADB-funded ($840 mn programme); notes naming JICA for VCIC are a known conflict and ADB is followed. HBIC is the third AP corridor, and ECEC is the parent coastal corridor of VCIC, not a JICA project.
142.tq: VCIC = ADB; CBIC = JICA.
xs: **CBIC** (Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor) has Japanese (**JICA**) support — so option **(1)** is correct.
**VCIC** is **ADB**-funded (**$840 mn** programme); notes naming JICA for VCIC are a conflict — follow ADB.
**ECEC** is VCIC's parent coastal corridor; **HBIC** is the third AP corridor.
xa: ⚠ **VCIC = ADB**; **CBIC = JICA**; **DMIC = Japanese aid**.
The **Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway** is a priority link of **CBIC**.
**CBIC** is one of AP's **three** industrial corridors with VCIC and HBIC.

142.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway:
1. It is a greenfield expressway.
2. It is being developed under Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I.
3. It starts at Hoskote in Karnataka.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: The expressway is a greenfield project under Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I and starts at Hoskote in Karnataka.
142.tq: Combine project type, scheme and starting point before selecting the inclusive option.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: it is a **greenfield** expressway — correct.
Statement 2: it is under **Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I** — correct.
Statement 3: it starts at **Hoskote** in Karnataka — correct.
xa: It crosses **Chittoor district** through the **Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary** elephant corridor.
Status: Karnataka stretch open since **Dec 2024**; **AP and TN stretches** still under construction.
⚠ **Hoskote** = start point; **Koundinya** WLS = elephant corridor it crosses.

142.s: The Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway is regarded as a priority link of which industrial corridor?
142.x: The Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway is a priority link of the Chennai–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.
142.tq: Match the transport link with its associated industrial corridor.
xs: The Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway is a priority link of the **Chennai–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (CBIC)** — option **(1)**.
**DMIC** runs on the **Western DFC** with Japanese aid; **VCIC** is the ADB-funded east coast corridor.
xa: **CBIC** has Japanese (**JICA**) support.
The expressway is greenfield under **Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I**, starting at **Hoskote**.
The Budget 2026-27 HSR list includes a **Chennai-Bengaluru** high-speed rail corridor.

142.s: The proposed Raipur–Visakhapatnam greenfield expressway is to pass through which combination of States?
142.x: The Raipur–Visakhapatnam Expressway is described as a greenfield route through Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.
142.tq: Use the endpoint-to-State route sequence to eliminate neighbouring-State combinations.
xs: The **Raipur-Visakhapatnam** greenfield expressway runs through **Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh** — option **(2)**.
It is a **flagship Central project** for AP.
xa: Other proposals: DPR for **Kharagpur-Amaravati**; **Nagpur-Machilipatnam via Vijayawada**; **Raipur-Amaravati**.
The **Bengaluru-Kadapa-Vijayawada** Economic Corridor is to be finished by **2027**.
The Governor (Jan 2026) fast-tracked **Nagpur-Vijayawada** and **Kharagpur-Visakhapatnam-Amaravati**.

142.s: In Chittoor district, the Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway passes through the elephant corridor of which protected area, where 3,475 m of animal underpasses were cleared by the Standing Committee of the NBWL?
142.x: The expressway crosses Chittoor via the Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary elephant corridor; the SC-NBWL cleared 3,475 m of underpasses (1,400 m continuous). The other three protected areas are not on its route.
142.tq: Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway + elephants = Koundinya.
xs: The expressway crosses Chittoor via the **Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary** elephant corridor — so option **(1)** is correct.
**SC-NBWL** cleared **3,475 m** of animal underpasses, **1,400 m** of them continuous.
xa: ⚠ **Hoskote** = start of the expressway; **Koundinya** WLS = elephant corridor in Chittoor.
It is a greenfield **Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I** road, a priority link of **CBIC**.
Karnataka stretch open since **Dec 2024**; AP and TN stretches under construction.

142.s: Under the Thirteenth Schedule of the A.P. Reorganisation Act, the Government of India is required to take steps for rapid rail and road connectivity from the new capital of Andhra Pradesh to:
o: Delhi and other important cities of northern India
Visakhapatnam and all coastal cities only
Bengaluru and all cities of Karnataka only
Hyderabad and other important cities of Telangana
142.x: The Act provides for rapid rail and road connectivity from the new Andhra Pradesh capital to Hyderabad and other important cities of Telangana.
142.tq: Focus on the statutory destination and the additional regional connectivity specified.
xs: The Act asks GoI to take steps for **rapid rail and road connectivity** from AP's new capital to **Hyderabad and other important cities of Telangana** — option **(4)**.
⚠ It only says "**take steps**" — no completion deadline is fixed.
xa: The same **Thirteenth Schedule** asks GoI to examine the **VCIC** within **six months**.
Proposed **Amaravati-Hyderabad** bullet train: **70 minutes**.
Budget 2026-27 HSR corridors include **Hyderabad-Bengaluru** and **Hyderabad-Chennai**.

142.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the seven high-speed rail corridors identified as “growth connectors” in the Union Budget 2026–27?
142.x: The seven corridors include Pune–Hyderabad, Hyderabad–Chennai and Delhi–Varanasi; Amaravati–Visakhapatnam is not included in that list.
142.tq: Check every listed corridor against the complete seven-corridor set.
xs: **Amaravati–Visakhapatnam** is not among the **7 high-speed rail corridors** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The seven: **Mumbai-Pune, Pune-Hyderabad, Hyderabad-Bengaluru, Hyderabad-Chennai, Chennai-Bengaluru, Delhi-Varanasi, Varanasi-Siliguri**.
xa: Total cost: **₹16 lakh crore**.
**Hyderabad-Chennai** is to take **2 h 55 min**.
An **Amaravati-Hyderabad** bullet train is proposed at **70 minutes**.

142.s: Which one of the following is the nodal agency for industrial infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh, including IT, biotech and apparel parks and SEZs?
142.x: APIIC is the nodal agency for industrial infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh, including IT, biotech and apparel parks and SEZs.
142.tq: Identify the correct institutional authority by matching the body with its assigned function.
xs: **APIIC** is the nodal agency for all industrial infrastructure — **IT, biotech, apparel parks** and **SEZs** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It works through the **PPP** model and has **22 JVs**.
xa: APIIC was incorporated in **1973** (APPSC 2023).
APIIC manages **571** industrial parks (**264** APIIC + **283** UDL).
APIIC can allot land up to **50 acres directly** (Jun 2026).

142.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sri City — Tirupati district on the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu border
142.x: Sri City, a multi-product SEZ, is located in Tirupati district on the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu border. Mallavalli is associated with the Mega Food Park, while Kopparthi is in Kadapa.
142.tq: Eliminate location swaps by checking the district and border description together.
xs: **Sri City**, a multi-product SEZ, is in **Tirupati district on the AP-TN border** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Mega Food Park** is at **Mallavalli (Krishna)**, not Visakhapatnam.
**Jawaharlal Nehru Pharma City** is at **Visakhapatnam** (Parawada); **Kopparthi** is in **Kadapa**, not Krishna.
