xa: The **₹40,000 crore** electronics components allocation (Budget 2026-27) helps **Sri City**.
**Visakhapatnam SEZ** is a Central government SEZ at **Duvvada**.
APIIC clusters: **Gandrajupalle** (Chittoor), **Kopparthi** (Kadapa), **Makavarapalem** (Visakhapatnam), **Machilipatnam**.

142.s: Jawaharlal Nehru Pharma City is located at:
142.x: Jawaharlal Nehru Pharma City is located at Parawada in Visakhapatnam.
142.tq: Distinguish the named industrial city from the separate APIIC cluster locations in the same region.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru Pharma City** is at **Parawada** in **Visakhapatnam** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Makavarapalem**, **Gandrajupalle** and **Kopparthi** are **APIIC cluster** locations, not the Pharma City.
xa: Visakhapatnam also has a **Bulk Drug Park** of **2,002 acres** (GoI Dept. of Pharmaceuticals).
**Visakhapatnam SEZ** (Central government SEZ) is at **Duvvada**.
**Mega Food Park**: **Mallavalli (Krishna)**.

142.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes Sri City and Visakhapatnam SEZ?
o: Sri City is a central government SEZ, whereas Visakhapatnam SEZ is a multi-product SEZ.
Sri City is a multi-product SEZ, whereas Visakhapatnam SEZ at Duvvada is a central government SEZ.
Both are sector-specific SEZs located in Krishna district.
142.x: Sri City is a multi-product SEZ. Visakhapatnam SEZ, located at Duvvada, is a central government SEZ.
142.tq: Use the contrast in classification and location rather than treating both SEZs as identical.
xs: **Sri City** is a **multi-product SEZ**, while **Visakhapatnam SEZ** at **Duvvada** is a **Central government SEZ** — option **(2)**.
Sri City is in **Tirupati district** on the AP-TN border, not Krishna; Duvvada is in **Visakhapatnam**.
xa: The **₹40,000 crore** electronics components allocation (Budget 2026-27) helps **Sri City**.
**Mega Food Park**: **Mallavalli (Krishna)**.
SEZ incentives include **100%** stamp duty exemption and a **3%** interest subsidy.

142.s: The Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC), the nodal agency for industrial infrastructure in the State, was incorporated in:
142.x: APIIC was incorporated in 1973 (APPSC 2023). 1956 is the year of the formation of Andhra Pradesh, 1991 the year of liberalisation, and 2014 the year of bifurcation; none is APIIC's year of incorporation.
142.tq: APIIC = 1973; 22 JVs; PPP model.
xs: **APIIC** was incorporated in **1973** (APPSC 2023) — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is the **State nodal agency** for industrial parks and corridor land, working through the **PPP** model.
xa: APIIC has **22 JVs** and manages **571** industrial parks (**264** APIIC + **283** UDL).
⚠ **264 + 283 = 547**, not 571 — the notes' parts do not add up.
**APIIC** is one of the VCIC's **four PIUs**, with **APRDC, AP Transco** and **GVMC**.

142.s: AP Farmer Managed Groundwater Systems (APFAMGS) is best described as a project that is:
142.x: APFAMGS is FAO-executed and funded by the Netherlands.
142.tq: Test the direction of the execution–funding relationship rather than just recognising the agencies.
xs: **APFAMGS** (AP Farmer Managed Groundwater Systems) is **FAO-executed** and **Netherlands-funded** — option **(2)**.
**World Bank and ADB** are named for **Amaravati capital loans**, not APFAMGS.
xa: ⚠ **VCIC = ADB**; **CBIC = JICA**; **DMIC = Japanese aid**.
The VCIC **Policy-Based Loan** (**$125 mn**, 100% ADB) funds **EoDB** and institutional reform.

142.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Project)
a. AP Integrated Irrigation & Agriculture Transformation Project
b. Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor
c. AP Farmer Managed Groundwater Systems

d. Amaravati capital loans

List-II (Funding agency or arrangement)
i. FAO-executed and Netherlands-funded
ii. World Bank and ADB
iii. World Bank
iv. ADB with contribution from the Government of Andhra Pradesh

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
142.x: The Integrated Irrigation and Agriculture Transformation Project is funded by the World Bank; VCIC combines ADB and Government of Andhra Pradesh funding; APFAMGS is FAO-executed and Netherlands-funded; and Amaravati capital loans involve the World Bank and ADB.
142.tq: Begin with the distinctive FAO–Netherlands pair and then resolve the remaining funding relationships.
xs: Correct matching is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
b: **VCIC** — **ADB** with a **GoAP** contribution (**$625 mn** + **$215 mn**).
c: **APFAMGS** — **FAO-executed, Netherlands-funded**; d: **Amaravati capital loans** — **World Bank and ADB**.
a: so the **Integrated Irrigation & Agriculture Transformation Project** takes the remaining **World Bank**.
xa: VCIC total: **$840 mn** (APSES 2024-25).
The VCIC **Policy-Based Loan** of **$125 mn** is **100% ADB**.
⚠ **CBIC** is backed by **JICA**, not ADB.

142.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the total ADB funding arrangement?
o: ADB $715 million, GoAP $125 million and total $840 million
ADB $500 million, GoAP $215 million and total $625 million
ADB $625 million, GoAP $215 million and total $840 million
ADB $840 million, GoAP $625 million and total $215 million
142.x: The total arrangement comprises $625 million from ADB and $215 million from GoAP, making $840 million.
142.tq: Add the component contributions and verify the total.
xs: Total VCIC funding: **ADB $625 million** + **GoAP $215 million** = **$840 million** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **$125 mn** is the **Policy-Based Loan** (ADB only), not GoAP's share.
xa: Loan agreements (Tranche-I + Policy-Based Loan) signed **23 Feb 2017** by DEA, ADB and GoAP.
Works: **₹5,000 crore**, backed by a **₹3,300 crore** ADB loan in **two tranches**.
Progress is described as **slow**.

142.s:
Consider the following statements about DMIC and VCIC:
1. DMIC runs on the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor.
2. Japanese aid is associated with DMIC.
3. VCIC is ADB-funded and port-led.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All three statements are correct. DMIC is associated with the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor and Japanese aid, whereas VCIC is ADB-funded and port-led.
142.tq: Keep the two corridors separate by comparing their funding, freight-corridor and development characteristics.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statements 1 and 2: **DMIC** runs on the **Western DFC** with **Japanese aid** — correct.
Statement 3: **VCIC** is **ADB**-funded and **port-led** — correct.
xa: VCIC was itself modelled **on the lines of DMIC** (Thirteenth Schedule).
⚠ **CBIC** gets Japanese **JICA** support; VCIC does not.
VCIC financing: **$840 mn** (ADB **$625 mn**, GoAP **$215 mn**).

143.s: Special Category Status (SCS) was first introduced in India in 1969 on the recommendation of which body?
143.x: Special Category Status was introduced in 1969 on the recommendation of the Fifth Finance Commission. The National Development Council endorsed the Gadgil Formula (1968-69) for distributing Plan funds, but it was not the body that recommended SCS.
143.tq: Identify the recommending body rather than the institution that later endorsed the related formula.
xs: SCS was introduced in **1969** on the recommendation of the **Fifth Finance Commission** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **National Development Council** only endorsed the **Gadgil Formula** (1968-69) for Plan funds.
The **14th FC** (Y.V. Reddy) made **no distinction** between general and SCS states.
xa: SCS is **not** in the Constitution; it is an **executive/Planning Commission-era** classification.
First three SCS states: **Jammu & Kashmir, Assam, Nagaland**.
Plan transfers: **Gadgil formula** (1969) → **Gadgil-Mukherjee formula** (1991).

143.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Special Category Status:
1. It is expressly provided for in the Constitution of India.
2. It was an executive and Planning Commission-era classification.
3. It was associated with preferential Central assistance under Plan fund distribution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
143.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Special Category Status is not a constitutional category; it emerged as an executive and Planning Commission-era classification linked to preferential Plan assistance.
143.tq: Test whether the classification is constitutional or executive before considering its financial consequence.
xs: Statements 2 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is wrong: SCS is **not** in the Constitution.
Statement 2: it is an **executive/Planning Commission-era** classification — correct.
Statement 3: under the **Gadgil formula**, SCS states got **preferential central assistance** — correct.
xa: Debate: SCS is an **executive, not constitutional** category vs a **political promise made in Parliament**.
Introduced in **1969** on the **5th Finance Commission**'s recommendation.
SCS = status with automatic **90:10**; a special package = project-linked money.

143.s: Which formula was introduced in 1991 as the later version of the Gadgil Formula for Plan transfers to States?
143.x: The Gadgil Formula was later modified and became the Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula in 1991.
143.tq: Distinguish the original formula from its later modified version by the year of modification.
xs: The Gadgil formula (1969) later became the **Gadgil-Mukherjee formula** in **1991** — option **(3)**.
It governed **Plan transfers** to States.
xa: The **Gadgil Formula** was endorsed by the **NDC** in **1968-69**.
SCS states got a **reserved first share** of **Normal Central Assistance**.
SCS began in **1969** (5th FC); first three: **J&K, Assam, Nagaland**.

143.s: Which were the first three States to be given Special Category Status?
143.x: The first three SCS States were Jammu & Kashmir, Assam and Nagaland (1969). Manipur, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Mizoram, Meghalaya and Uttarakhand got the status later; Uttarakhand was the last of the 11.
143.tq: First SCS trio = J&K, Assam, Nagaland.
xs: The first three SCS states were **Jammu & Kashmir, Assam** and **Nagaland** — option **(1)**.
Manipur, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Mizoram, Meghalaya and Uttarakhand are among the **11** but came later.
xa: SCS began in **1969** on the **5th Finance Commission**'s recommendation.
**J&K** became a **Union Territory** in **2019**.
Never granted despite demands: **Bihar** (BPSC 2019 key), **Odisha**, **Andhra Pradesh**.

143.s: Which of the following was NOT a criterion associated with Special Category Status?
o: High population density and advanced infrastructure
143.x: High population density and advanced infrastructure were not criteria for Special Category Status. The criteria included difficult terrain, low population density or sizeable tribal population, border location, economic and infrastructural backwardness, and non-viable finances.
143.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated backwardness and population criteria.
xs: **High population density and advanced infrastructure** is not an SCS criterion — so option **(3)** is correct.
The criteria are the opposite: **low population density** and/or sizeable **tribal population**, and **economic and infrastructural backwardness**.
**Non-viable state finances**, **border location** and **hilly terrain** are genuine criteria.
xa: Five criteria: **hilly terrain**, **low density/tribal population**, **international borders**, **backwardness**, **non-viable finances**.
Rationale: a **larger tax share** to cover the gap.
Benefits include **concessional-interest** central loans and **tax breaks** for industry.

143.s: What was the rationale behind granting Special Category Status to States?
o: To give them exclusive legislative powers over Union List subjects
To give them a larger share of central taxes to cover the gap caused by geographic disadvantage and backwardness
To exempt them from the jurisdiction of the Finance Commission
To allow them to borrow abroad without central consent
143.x: SCS was meant to give such States a larger tax share to cover the gap arising from geographic disadvantage and economic and infrastructural backwardness.
143.tq: SCS = bigger share to bridge the gap.
xs: SCS gave states a **larger share of central taxes** to **cover the gap** from geographic disadvantage and backwardness — option **(2)**.
The gap comes from **hilly terrain**, **low density/tribal population**, **border location**, **backwardness** and **non-viable finances**.
xa: SCS loans come at **concessional interest**; industries get **tax breaks**.
Unspent SCS funds **do not lapse**.
The Centre argued the **14th FC**'s higher devolution **subsumed** SCS benefits.

143.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the benefits of Special Category Status:
1. Central loans to Special Category States carried normal interest, the same as for general States.
2. Industries in Special Category States received tax breaks and incentives of the income-tax/excise type.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
143.x: Statement 1 is wrong: SCS States got Central loans at concessional interest, while general States got normal terms. Statement 2 is correct: industries in SCS States got tax breaks and incentives (income tax/excise type). Hence '2 only'; the other options are wrong.
143.tq: SCS = concessional loans + industry tax breaks + non-lapsing funds.
xs: Only statement 2 is correct — option **(2) 2 only**.
Statement 1 is wrong: SCS central loans carry **concessional interest**; only general states get **normal** terms.
Statement 2: industries in SCS states get **tax breaks and incentives** (income tax/excise type) — correct.
xa: Unspent funds in SCS states **do not lapse**; in general states they lapse.
PMGSY covers habitations of **250+** in SCS states vs **500+** in plains.
GST exemption threshold is lower (**₹10 lakh**) for SCS.

143.s: What was the treatment of unspent funds in a Special Category State?
o: They lapsed at the end of the financial year
They did not lapse and could be carried forward
They were converted into Central loans
They were transferred automatically to general States
143.x: Unspent funds in Special Category States did not lapse and could be carried forward. In general States, such funds lapsed.
143.tq: Test the distinction between lapse and carry-forward treatment.
xs: Unspent funds in SCS states **did not lapse** and were **carried forward** — option **(2)**.
In **general** states, unspent funds **lapse**.
xa: SCS central loans: **concessional interest**.
Consumer Welfare Fund seed money: **90:10** for SCS vs **75:25**.
SCS industries get **income tax/excise-type** tax breaks.

143.s: Under PMGSY, habitations eligible for road connectivity in Special Category States have a population of:
o: 250 or more, against 500 or more in the plains
500 or more, against 1,000 or more in the plains
100 or more, against 250 or more in the plains
1,000 or more, against 500 or more in the plains
143.x: The PMGSY threshold is 250+ in SCS States against 500+ in the plains. The other options give the wrong thresholds, and the last one reverses the concession. A similar concession applies to Consumer Welfare Fund seed money (90:10 for SCS against 75:25).
143.tq: SCS concessions: PMGSY 250 vs 500; CWF 90:10 vs 75:25.
xs: Under **PMGSY**, SCS habitations of **250 or more** qualify, against **500 or more** in the plains — option **(1)**.
Option (4) reverses the concession; the SCS threshold is the **lower** one.
xa: ⚠ Consumer Welfare Fund seed money: **90:10** for SCS vs **75:25** (2026).
GST exemption threshold is **₹10 lakh** (lower) for SCS.
SCS central loans carry **concessional interest**.

143.s:
Consider the following States:
1. Bihar
2. Odisha
3. Andhra Pradesh
4. Uttarakhand
Which of the above were never granted Special Category Status despite demands or claims for it?
143.x: Bihar, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh were never granted Special Category Status. Uttarakhand was among the States that received it.
143.tq: Classify each State before selecting the coded combination.
xs: **Bihar, Odisha** and **Andhra Pradesh** asked but were never granted SCS — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Uttarakhand** is one of the **11** states granted SCS.
The Centre feared that SCS for AP would bring identical demands from **Bihar and Odisha**.
xa: **Bihar** never getting SCS was a **BPSC 2019** key.
⚠ **Telangana** was never granted SCS, though some notes wrongly list it.
First three SCS states: **J&K, Assam, Nagaland**.

143.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the 11 States listed as having been granted Special Category Status?
143.x: Telangana has never been granted Special Category Status. Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and Tripura are included among the 11 SCS States.
143.tq: Find the State wrongly inserted into an otherwise genuine list of SCS recipients.
xs: **Telangana** has never been granted SCS — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh** and **Tripura** are among the **11** SCS states.
⚠ Some notes (UPSC Economy notes) wrongly list Telangana among SCS states.
xa: The **11**: Assam, Nagaland, J&K, Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Uttarakhand.
Never granted (asked): **Bihar, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh**.
**J&K** became a Union Territory in **2019**.

143.s: Who chaired the Fourteenth Finance Commission, whose award covered the period 2015-20?
143.x: Y.V. Reddy chaired the Fourteenth Finance Commission, whose award covered 2015-20.
143.tq: Match the Finance Commission number and award period with its chairperson.
xs: **Y.V. Reddy** chaired the **14th Finance Commission** (award **2015-20**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Arvind Panagariya** chairs the **16th FC**; **Manmohan Singh** was the PM who gave the 2014 SCS assurance; **Manickam Tagore** is a Congress MP who raised SCS in 2026.
xa: 14th FC raised the states' share from **32% to 42%** — the **largest increase ever**; accepted **24 Feb 2015**.
It made **no distinction** between general and special category states.

143.s: Which one of the following correctly states the Fourteenth Finance Commission’s position concerning general and Special Category States?
o: It abolished all Central assistance to general States
It maintained a separate devolution formula exclusively for SCS States
It made no distinction between general and Special Category States
It reduced the States’ share of the divisible pool to 32 per cent
143.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission made no distinction between general and Special Category States in the higher tax devolution arrangement. The Centre argued that the increased devolution subsumed SCS benefits.
143.tq: Watch for the reversal of the Commission’s uniform treatment and the direction of devolution change.
xs: The **14th FC** made **no distinction between general and Special Category states** — option **(3)**.
It **raised** the share from **32% to 42%**, so option (4) reverses it.
The Centre said this higher devolution **subsumed** SCS benefits.
xa: In **2015**, the Centre used the 14th FC award to deny SCS to AP.
AP argued the **42%** applied to all states and ignored its loss of **Hyderabad**.
14th FC chair: **Y.V. Reddy**; award **2015-20**.

143.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Fourteenth Finance Commission — 42 per cent
2. Fifteenth Finance Commission — 41 per cent
3. Sixteenth Finance Commission — 41 per cent and a Contribution to GDP criterion
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
143.x: All three pairs are correct. The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended 42 per cent, while the Fifteenth and Sixteenth Finance Commissions retained 41 per cent; the Sixteenth also added a 10 per cent Contribution to GDP criterion.
143.tq: Track the changing devolution percentages across successive Finance Commissions.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**14th FC — 42%** — correct.
**15th FC — 41%** — correct.
**16th FC — 41%** plus a **"Contribution to GDP"** criterion (**10%** weight) — correct.
xa: 16th FC chair: **Arvind Panagariya**; award **1 Apr 2026-31 Mar 2031**.
⚠ **32%** was the share before the 14th FC.
The **5th FC** recommended SCS (**1969**).

143.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission arrangement mentioned, the weight assigned to the ‘Contribution to GDP’ criterion was:
143.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission added Contribution to GDP as a criterion with a 10 per cent weight.
143.tq: Focus on the exact weight assigned to the newly added criterion.
xs: The **16th FC** gives **"Contribution to GDP"** a **10 per cent** (**10%**) weight — so option **(2)** is correct.
It keeps the states' share at **41%**.
xa: 16th FC chair: **Arvind Panagariya**; award **1 Apr 2026-31 Mar 2031**.
The 16th FC also **ends revenue deficit grants**.

143.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission was chaired by ____ and its award covers ____.
143.x: The 16th FC is chaired by Arvind Panagariya, and its award runs from 1 Apr 2026 to 31 Mar 2031; it keeps the share at 41%. Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th FC (2015-20). 2021-26 was the 15th FC period, and N.K. Singh chaired the 15th FC, not the 16th.
143.tq: 14th = Y.V. Reddy 42%; 16th = Panagariya 41% + 10% GDP.
xs: The **16th FC** is chaired by **Arvind Panagariya**, with an award from **1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031** — option **(1)**.
**Y.V. Reddy** chaired the **14th FC** (2015-20).
xa: The 16th FC keeps **41%** and adds **"Contribution to GDP"** (**10%** weight).
It also ends **revenue deficit grants**.
14th FC: **32% to 42%**, accepted **24 Feb 2015**.

143.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2014 assurance on Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh:
1. It was given by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on 20 February 2014.
2. It was given on the floor of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
143.x: Statement 1 is correct: PM Manmohan Singh gave the assurance on 20 February 2014. Statement 2 is wrong: the assurance was given in the Rajya Sabha, not the Lok Sabha. Hence '1 only'; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
143.tq: Remember the trio: 20 Feb 2014 - Manmohan Singh - Rajya Sabha - five years.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: PM **Manmohan Singh** gave the assurance on **20 February 2014** — correct.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was given in the **Rajya Sabha**, not the Lok Sabha.
xa: ⚠ Assurance in the **Rajya Sabha** (2014); TDP's no-confidence motion in the **Lok Sabha** (2018).
SCS was promised for **five years** (APPSC-GS 2018 key).
It was **not written into the Reorganisation Act**, so the Centre treated it as non-binding.

143.s: For how long was Special Category Status assured to Andhra Pradesh in the Rajya Sabha in 2014?
143.x: The assurance concerned Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh for five years.
143.tq: Test the exact duration rather than the date or the person associated with the assurance.
xs: SCS was assured to AP for **five years** — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2018 key).
PM **Manmohan Singh** gave it in the **Rajya Sabha** on **20 February 2014**, calling it "a solemn assurance".
xa: It was **not written into the Reorganisation Act**.
In **Sep 2016**, a **Special Assistance Package** was offered instead.
AP argued a commitment on the **floor of Parliament** carries constitutional weight.

143.s: Which one of the following was a reason for the Centre later treating the assurance on Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh as non-binding?
o: It was rejected by the Fifth Finance Commission
It was not written into the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act
It was applicable only to Union Territories
It was withdrawn by the Rajya Sabha on the same day
143.x: The assurance was not incorporated into the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, enabling the Centre later to treat it as non-binding.
143.tq: Identify the legal consequence of an assurance not being incorporated into the governing statute.
xs: The assurance was **not written into the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act** — so option **(2)** is correct.
So the Centre later treated it as **non-binding**, and in **2015** used the **14th FC** award to deny SCS.
The **5th FC** recommended SCS in **1969**; it had nothing to reject.
xa: AP's argument: a commitment on the **floor of Parliament** carries constitutional weight.
The promise was made by PM **Manmohan Singh** in the **Rajya Sabha** on **20 February 2014**.
SCS has been the **central plank of AP politics** since **2014**.

143.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Special Assistance Package was offered to Andhra Pradesh
B. Prime Minister gave the Rajya Sabha assurance on SCS for five years
C. Fourteenth Finance Commission award was used to deny SCS
D. TDP broke from the NDA
143.x: The correct sequence is 2014 assurance, 2015 Fourteenth Finance Commission award, September 2016 Special Assistance Package, and 2018 withdrawal of TDP from the NDA.
143.tq: Fix the earliest event first and then place the 2015 and 2016 financial-policy developments before the 2018 political event.
xs: Correct order: **B, C, A, D** — option **(1)**.
B: **Rajya Sabha** assurance — **20 February 2014**.
C: **14th FC** award used to deny SCS — **2015**.
A: **Special Assistance Package** offered — **Sep 2016**; D: **TDP broke from the NDA** — **2018**.
xa: In **2019**, SCS became an "**emotional referendum**"; YSRCP branded the package a "**betrayal**".
In **2026**, Manickam Tagore, Botcha Satyanarayana and Y.S. Sharmila revived the demand.
In **2018**, TDP moved a **no-confidence motion** in the **Lok Sabha** (July), which was defeated.

143.s: Which political development took place in 2018 in the context of Andhra Pradesh’s Special Category Status demand?
o: TDP broke from the NDA and moved a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha
YSRCP joined the NDA and withdrew the demand
The Rajya Sabha enacted SCS through a constitutional amendment
The Centre granted SCS to Andhra Pradesh for ten years
143.x: In 2018, the TDP broke from the NDA and moved a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha in July; the motion was defeated.
143.tq: Match the year with both linked political actions and avoid replacing a motion with a constitutional amendment.
xs: In **2018**, the **TDP broke from the NDA** and moved a **no-confidence motion** in the **Lok Sabha** — option **(1)**.
The motion (July 2018) was **defeated**.
xa: ⚠ Assurance in the **Rajya Sabha** (2014); no-confidence motion in the **Lok Sabha** (2018).
In **2019**, SCS became an "**emotional referendum**".
In **2026**, the demand was revived during the **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill** debate.

143.s: Why did Andhra Pradesh argue that the 42 per cent devolution recommended by the Fourteenth Finance Commission did not resolve its SCS-related concerns?
o: It applied to all States and did not address Andhra Pradesh’s asymmetric loss of Hyderabad
It replaced the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act entirely
It was available only to States with international borders
The 42 per cent devolution applied only to Andhra Pradesh and excluded all other States
143.x: Andhra Pradesh argued that the 42 per cent devolution applied uniformly to all States and therefore did not compensate for its asymmetric loss of Hyderabad.
143.tq: Test whether a general fiscal measure addressed the State-specific consequence of bifurcation.
xs: The **42%** devolution **applied to all states** and did not address AP's **asymmetric loss of Hyderabad** — option **(1)**.
The Centre said this higher devolution **subsumed** SCS benefits; the 14th FC made **no distinction** between general and SCS states.
xa: 14th FC (chair **Y.V. Reddy**): **32% to 42%**, the **largest increase ever**.
In **2015**, the Centre used the 14th FC award to deny SCS.
AP also argued a commitment on the **floor of Parliament** carries constitutional weight.

143.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Special Category Status from a special package?
o: Special Category Status is project-linked, whereas a special package provides an automatic 90:10 funding pattern.
Special Category Status provides a status-related automatic 90:10 funding pattern, whereas a special package involves project-linked financial assistance.
Both Special Category Status and a special package provide identical automatic 90:10 assistance.
Neither Special Category Status nor a special package involves financial assistance.
143.x: Special Category Status is associated with an automatic 90:10 funding pattern, while a special package consists of project-linked financial assistance.
143.tq: Split the comparison into status-based assistance and project-linked assistance before judging the options.
xs: SCS is a **status** with an **automatic 90:10** funding pattern; a **special package** is **project-linked** money — option **(2)**.
Option (1) swaps the two.
xa: AP was offered a **Special Assistance Package** in **Sep 2016** instead of SCS.
⚠ **90:10** = SCS vs **75:25** general (Consumer Welfare Fund seed money).
YSRCP branded the package a "**betrayal**" in **2019**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Special Assistance Package for Andhra Pradesh:
1. It was announced in September 2016 by Union Finance Minister Arun Jaitley in place of SCS.
2. It is also called the Special Assistance Measure (SAM).
3. It was announced by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Statement 1 is correct: FM Arun Jaitley announced it in September 2016 in place of SCS. Statement 2 is correct: it is also called the Special Assistance Measure (SAM) or 'Special Package'. Statement 3 is wrong: Manmohan Singh gave the 2014 Rajya Sabha assurance on SCS, not the package. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
144.tq: Don't mix the 2014 SCS assurance (Manmohan Singh) with the 2016 package (Arun Jaitley).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: Union FM **Arun Jaitley** announced the package in **September 2016** in place of SCS — correct.
Statement 2: it is also called the **Special Assistance Measure (SAM)** or "Special Package" — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Manmohan Singh** gave the **2014** Rajya Sabha assurance on **SCS**, not the package.
xa: The package covers **2015-16 to 2019-20**, matching the promised **five-year** SCS period.
SAM total: **₹24,350 crore**, including a **₹3,979 crore** revenue deficit grant.
The **2016-17** special assistance was **₹4,058.04 crore** (APPSC-G1 2017 key).

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the components of the Special Assistance Package:
1. The special-assistance component was intended to equal the additional central share that Andhra Pradesh would have received as an SCS State.
2. Polavaram was treated as a national project under Section 90.
3. The Centre was to bear 100% of the remaining irrigation-component cost of Polavaram from 1 April 2014.
4. Industrial incentives were linked to Section 94(1).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All four statements correctly describe the special-assistance and Polavaram provisions and the Section 94(1) industrial incentives.
144.tq: Verify the monetary equivalence, project status, effective date and statutory reference together.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Statement 1: special assistance equals the **extra central share** AP would get as an SCS state (**90% grant**) — correct.
Statements 2 and 3: **Polavaram** is a national project under **Sec 90**; Centre bears **100%** of the remaining irrigation cost from **1 Apr 2014** — correct.
Statement 4: industrial incentives come under **Sec 94(1)** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **Sec 90** = Polavaram; **Sec 94(1)** = tax incentives; **Sec 46(2)** = backward areas; **Sec 46** = revenue deficit.
The special assistance is routed through **Externally Aided Projects**.
The promised **10-year tax holiday** was delayed, diluted or subsumed in **GST**.

144.s: Which of the following statements regarding the package is NOT correctly stated?
o: The package included a special development package for Rayalaseema and North Coastal districts.
Support was provided for specified capital institutions and buildings.
The Centre was to bridge the resource gap of Andhra Pradesh for 2014-15.
A ten-year tax holiday was implemented fully and without dilution through the package.
144.x: The promised ten-year tax holiday was delayed, diluted or subsumed in the GST framework; it was not implemented fully and without dilution.
144.tq: Identify the over-absolute claim about tax incentives.
xs: A **ten-year tax holiday implemented fully and without dilution** is wrong — so option **(4)** is the answer.
The promised **10-year tax holiday** under **Sec 94(1)** was **delayed, diluted or subsumed in GST**.
The package does include a package for **Rayalaseema and North Coastal** districts (**Sec 46(2)**) and bridging the **2014-15** resource gap (**Sec 46**).
xa: **₹2,500 crore** was promised for the **capital**.
The **7** backward districts = **4 Rayalaseema + 3 North Coastal**; releases stalled.
The **2014-15** revenue deficit grant was **₹3,979 crore**.

144.s: The Special Assistance Package covered which period?
144.x: The package covered five years, from 2015-16 to 2019-20, corresponding to the promised SCS period.
144.tq: Test the exact five-year span rather than just the duration.
xs: The package covered **2015-16 to 2019-20** — so option **(4)** is correct.
These **five years** match the promised SCS period.
xa: It was announced in **September 2016** by FM **Arun Jaitley**.
PM **Manmohan Singh** had promised SCS for **five years** in **2014**.
⚠ **2016-17** is the year of the **₹4,058.04 crore** special assistance, not the start of the package.

144.s: Under the Externally Aided Projects route, which of the following best describes the repayment mechanism?
o: The State repays only the principal and the Centre bears no interest liability.
The State borrows from multilateral agencies, while the Centre repays loan and interest up to the SCS-equivalent amount.
The Centre directly funds every project without any State borrowing.
The State gives up all borrowing and receives an unrestricted capital grant.
144.x: The State borrows from agencies such as the World Bank and ADB, and the Centre supports repayment of loan and interest up to the SCS-equivalent amount.
144.tq: Ask who borrows, who repays and whether the support is a grant or repayment mechanism.
xs: The State **borrows from multilateral agencies** and the **Centre repays the loan and interest** up to the **SCS-equivalent amount** — option **(2)**.
The lenders are agencies such as the **World Bank** and **ADB**; there is **no open grant**.
The share is the **SCS-equivalent 90%**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say "Centre to bear **40%** cost for EAPs"; the fuller account gives **90%**.
AP complains of **long approval cycles** and **heavy compliance** — red tape and delays.
**₹15,000 crore** for **Amaravati** is raised via multilateral lenders.

144.s: Why has Andhra Pradesh criticised the Externally Aided Projects route?
o: It excludes multilateral agencies from project financing.
It requires long approval cycles and heavy compliance, creating red tape and delays.
It provides automatic tax concessions to industries.
It prevents the use of all external finance.
144.x: Andhra Pradesh has argued that long approval processes and extensive compliance requirements create red tape and delay project implementation.
144.tq: Link the administrative process to the stated consequence instead of confusing it with financing restrictions.
xs: AP says the EAP route has **long approval cycles** and **heavy compliance**, causing **red tape and delays** — option **(2)**.
The route actually depends on multilateral agencies (**World Bank, ADB**) — so options (1) and (4) are wrong.
xa: The Centre repays **loan and interest** up to the SCS-equivalent amount.
Criticism: package = **loans-and-projects** in place of a status; **fund lapses** + slow EAP approvals.
The State wants **grants**; the Centre prefers **loans and guarantees**.

144.s: The Centre cited which development as having already absorbed the benefits associated with Special Category Status?
o: The GST Council's abolition of all central assistance
The 13th Finance Commission's reduction of devolution to 32%
The 14th Finance Commission's removal of the general-special category distinction and increase of devolution to 42%
The 16th Finance Commission's restoration of revenue-deficit grants
144.x: The Centre relied on the 14th Finance Commission's removal of the distinction and increase of devolution to 42% as having absorbed SCS-related benefits.
144.tq: Use the institution, percentage and policy change as a combined identification test.
xs: The Centre cited the **14th Finance Commission**'s removal of the **general-special category distinction** and rise in devolution to **42%** — option **(3)**.
The Centre said this **absorbed** SCS benefits.
xa: Other reasons: "**constitutional and technical constraints**" and fear of demands from **Bihar and Odisha**.
Outcome: an "**equivalent**" monetary package instead of the status.
AP FM **Payyavula Keshav** (Aug 2026): AP lost up to **₹38,000 crore** after the **16th FC** dropped revenue deficit grants.

144.s: According to the Centre's stated position, extending Special Category Status to Andhra Pradesh was opposed because:
o: The 14th Finance Commission recommended tax concessions only for Andhra Pradesh.
The Constitution prohibited all assistance to newly formed States.
Constitutional and technical constraints prevented extending SCS to a new State and could trigger similar demands from Bihar and Odisha.
Andhra Pradesh had already received permanent statutory SCS.
144.x: The Centre referred to constitutional and technical constraints and feared that granting SCS to Andhra Pradesh would lead to similar demands from Bihar and Odisha.
144.tq: Identify the stated policy rationale and the likely precedent effect.
xs: The Centre cited **constitutional and technical constraints** for any new state and feared identical demands from **Bihar and Odisha** — option **(3)**.
It also said the **14th FC**'s **42%** devolution had absorbed SCS benefits.
xa: The result was an "**equivalent**" monetary package instead of the status.
The package was announced by **Arun Jaitley** in **September 2016**.
Opposition parties (**YSRCP, Congress**) still demand SCS.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Special Assistance Measure for Andhra Pradesh:
1. The total package announced under the measure was ₹24,350 crore.
2. ₹3,979 crore of this amount was towards the revenue deficit grant.
3. The remaining amount was intended for infrastructure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: The Special Assistance Measure was announced for ₹24,350 crore, including ₹3,979 crore as revenue deficit grant, with the balance meant for infrastructure.
144.tq: Test the total, component and balance together; the all-inclusive combination is correct.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: SAM total announced was **₹24,350 crore** — correct.
Statement 2: **₹3,979 crore** of it was the **revenue deficit grant** (2014-15) — correct.
Statement 3: the **rest** went to **infrastructure** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **₹4,058.04 crore** = 2016-17 special assistance; **₹3,979 crore** = 2014-15 revenue deficit grant; **₹24,350 crore** = SAM total.
**₹2,500 crore** was promised for the capital.
AP revenue deficit: **₹16,000 crore (2014-19)** → projected **₹48,000 crore (2025-26)**.

144.s: From 2024-25 onward, the amounts specified for Amaravati and Polavaram were respectively:
144.x: The specified assistance was ₹15,000 crore for Amaravati and ₹12,157 crore for Polavaram.
144.tq: Split the options by checking the correct project-to-amount pairing.
xs: From **2024-25** onward: **₹15,000 crore** for **Amaravati** and **₹12,157 crore** for **Polavaram** — option **(2)**.
Option (3) reverses the two figures.
⚠ **₹2,500 crore** was the old promise for the capital; **₹8,226 crore** is AP's 2026-27 SASCI ceiling; **₹7,900 crore** its 2024-25 SASCI loans.
xa: Amaravati's **₹15,000 crore** is raised via **multilateral lenders**.
~**₹4,000 crore** is to come from the **Urban Infrastructure Development Fund**.

144.s: The special assistance released to Andhra Pradesh for 2016-17 under the Special Assistance Measure was:
144.x: ₹4,058.04 crore was released as special assistance for 2016-17 (APPSC-G1 2017 key). ₹3,979 crore was the 2014-15 revenue deficit grant, ₹24,350 crore the total SAM package, and ₹2,500 crore the amount promised for the capital.
xs: **₹4,058.04 crore** was released as special assistance for **2016-17** (APPSC-G1 2017 key) — option **(1)**.
**₹3,979 crore** = **2014-15** revenue deficit grant; **₹24,350 crore** = SAM total; **₹2,500 crore** = promised for the capital.
xa: The rest of the **₹24,350 crore** after the deficit grant was for **infrastructure**.
The package was announced in **September 2016** by **Arun Jaitley**.
Package period: **2015-16 to 2019-20**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI):
1. It is run by the Ministry of Finance.
2. It began in October 2019.
3. Line ministries run sub-schemes under it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Statement 1 is correct: SASCI is run by the Ministry of Finance. Statement 2 is wrong: SASCI began in October 2020, not 2019. Statement 3 is correct: line ministries run sub-schemes; the loans are 50-year interest-free and for capital works only. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
144.tq: SASCI: MoF, Oct 2020, 50-year interest-free, capital works, outside the 3% GSDP ceiling.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **SASCI** is run by the **Ministry of Finance** — correct.
Statement 2 is wrong: SASCI began in **Oct 2020**, not 2019.
Statement 3: **line ministries** run sub-schemes — correct.
xa: SASCI gives **50-year interest-free** loans, over and above the net borrowing ceiling.
It lies outside the 16th FC's **3% of GSDP** deficit ceiling and funds **capital works only**.
AP can get up to **₹8,226 crore** under 2026-27 SASCI.

144.s: Loans under the Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) are:
o: 50-year interest-free loans for capital works, over and above the net borrowing ceiling
10-year concessional loans for revenue expenditure within the borrowing ceiling
grants routed only through externally aided project repayments
loans counted within the 16th FC's 3% of GSDP deficit ceiling
144.x: SASCI (Ministry of Finance, since Oct 2020) gives 50-year interest-free loans for capital works only, over and above the net borrowing ceiling and outside the 3% of GSDP deficit ceiling. They are not for revenue expenditure and not EAP repayments.
144.tq: SASCI = 50-yr, interest-free, capex only, outside the ceiling.
xs: SASCI gives **50-year interest-free loans** for **capital works**, **over and above the net borrowing ceiling** — option **(1)**.
They are not for revenue spending, not EAP repayments, and sit **outside** the **3% of GSDP** deficit ceiling.
xa: SASCI is run by the **Ministry of Finance** and began in **Oct 2020**.
2026-27 reforms tied to SASCI include **AgriStack** (**₹1,450 crore**) and **mining** (**₹950 crore**).

144.s: In August 2026, AP Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav said the State lost up to ₹38,000 crore because:
o: the 16th Finance Commission dropped revenue deficit grants
the 14th Finance Commission raised devolution to 42%
SASCI loans to the State were withdrawn
the Special Assistance Package ended in 2019-20
144.x: The loss of up to ₹38,000 crore came from the 16th FC dropping revenue deficit grants, with the revenue deficit rising from ₹16,000 crore (2014-19) to a projected ₹48,000 crore (2025-26). The 42% devolution was the 14th FC's, SASCI continues, and the package period simply ended.
144.tq: ₹38,000 cr loss = 16th FC ending RD grants.
xs: The loss of up to **₹38,000 crore** came because the **16th Finance Commission dropped revenue deficit grants** — option **(1)**.
**Payyavula Keshav** (AP FM) said this in **Aug 2026**.
⚠ **42%** devolution was the **14th FC**'s; SASCI loans continue (~**₹3,430 crore** so far in 2026-27).
xa: AP revenue deficit: **₹16,000 crore (2014-19)** → projected **₹48,000 crore (2025-26)**.
The 2026-27 SASCI ceiling for AP is **₹8,226 crore**, with **₹3,486 crore** received by Sep 2026.
AP's memorandum sought **higher devolution** + **capital-city weightage**.

144.s: Which one of the following correctly compares CSS funding under SCS and the Special Assistance Package?
o: SCS: 90:10 grant and automatic; Package: equivalent money only through EAP repayments
SCS: equivalent money only through EAP repayments; Package: 90:10 grant and automatic
Both provide automatic 90:10 grants for all schemes
Neither provides any central assistance for CSS
144.x: Under SCS, CSS funding was a 90:10 grant and automatic. Under the package, the equivalent amount was available only through externally aided project repayments.
144.tq: Compare both sides of the table rather than checking only one arrangement.
xs: **SCS**: **90:10 grant**, **automatic**; **package**: equivalent money **only through EAP repayments** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps them.
xa: SCS funds work **across all schemes**; package funds are **tied to approved external projects**.
Under EAPs, the Centre repays **loan and interest** up to the SCS-equivalent amount.
AP's complaint: similar money on paper, but SCS = **automatic flows and tax breaks**.

144.s: Which of the following benefits was associated with SCS but not provided in the same strength under the Special Assistance Package?
144.x: SCS included tax concessions for industry, whereas the package offered only the weaker Section 94(1) incentives.
144.tq: Focus on the benefit that changes in character rather than merely in delivery route.
xs: **Tax concessions for industry** came with SCS but are weaker under the package — option **(4)**.
The package has **only Sec 94(1)** incentives; the promised **10-year tax holiday** was delayed, diluted or subsumed in **GST**.
Amaravati support, multilateral repayment and project-linked borrowing are features **of** the package itself.
xa: SCS industry benefits are **income tax/excise-type** tax breaks.
SCS = **recognised category**, automatic yearly flows; package = **executive**, no statutory permanence.
CSS funding: **90:10** automatic under SCS.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. SCS had a recognised category status with automatic yearly flows.
2. The Special Assistance Package was an executive package without statutory permanence.
3. SCS funds could be used across all schemes, whereas package funds were tied to approved external projects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: SCS had recognised and automatic features, while the package was executive in nature and tied to approved externally aided projects.
144.tq: Test legal footing and use-of-funds differences together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **SCS** is a **recognised category** with **automatic yearly flows** — correct.
Statement 2: the package is an **executive package**, **no statutory permanence** — correct.
Statement 3: SCS funds work **across all schemes**; package funds are tied to **approved external projects** — correct.
xa: SCS duration: promised **5 years**; package: **2015-16 to 2019-20**.
Tax concessions: **yes** under SCS; only **Sec 94(1)** under the package.
Comparative note: SCS = status with **automatic 90:10** flows vs package = money tied to projects.

144.s: Which of the following is regarded as the principal criticism of the package provided in place of Special Category Status?
o: It provides only revenue grants and excludes capital works.
It consists entirely of automatic tax devolution without project conditions.
It is viewed as loans and projects in place of a status, with fund lapses and slow EAP approvals.
It abolishes all Central assistance to Andhra Pradesh.
144.x: The package has been criticised as a loans-and-projects arrangement instead of a status-based framework. Fund lapses and slow approvals for externally aided projects are also concerns.
144.tq: Find the option that combines the stated criticisms without reversing the nature of the package.
xs: The package is criticised as **loans-and-projects in place of a status**, with **fund lapses** and **slow EAP approvals** — option **(3)**.
It is **project-linked**, not automatic devolution, and it does fund **infrastructure**.
xa: SCS = status with automatic **90:10** flows vs package = equivalent money tied to projects.
The State wants **grants**; the Centre prefers **loans and guarantees**.
SCS vs package decided the **2019 election narrative**.
